name: Abductor Virgin
description:
Abductor Virgins, also known as Iron Virgins, are Bosses and Enemies in. They are Bosses in.

Overview:
Abductor Virgins are automatons affiliated with the Volcano Manor. Originally designed with the intent of capturing and transposing victims for interrogation, they can be found strewn around the Lands Between. Though the majority have lost their powers of transposition, they will still attempt to fulfill their original directive if approached.

To aid in their task, Abductor Virgins have been outfitted with heavy weaponry on both arms that alter how they approach each target. When a Virgin has approached a target, they will open their chest cavity and attempt to pull them in with serpentine tendrils. Given the loss of their transposition ability, the target will be constricted instead. If they survive this, they will be spat back out. 

They are weak to Lightning damage and all damage taken is greatly increased if attacked when their chest cavity is opened during a charge or attempted grab. 

Wheel=

Variant Description:
A model with arms that end in great iron wheels, based on the device used by Inquisitor Ghiza. One such model lies at the bottom of the big waterwheel of Raya Lucaria, its transpostitional powers still fully intact.

These variants will often use their wheels by pressing them down on the ground. When placing both wheels at their sides, they will either perform a small spin in place, or a larger spin where they gradually spiral outwards. When there is distance, the Virgin will place both wheels in front and rapidly accelerate forward. Sometimes they will stop before reaching the target and open their chest cavity in an attempt to grab them.

Moveset:

Can include a separate table for a specific instance of this variant's moveset.

Scythe=

Variant Description:
A model with arms that end in great scythes on chains that it can extend and retract at will. Though they only have one spin attack, they will often use it to get some distance between them and their target. At the very end, they may throw their scythes at the target. This is something that they will do whenever there is sufficient distance. It is important to be careful after dodging the initial throw, as the scythe may hit when it is being retracted. This is especially true when near the Virgin, as the scythe will spin back around behind it upon return.

It's important to note that the Scythe can sometimes go through walls.

Moveset:

Mixed=

Variant Description:
A unique model of the Iron Virgin that has both the scythe and wheel devices installed. They are capable of using a mixed move-set, often consisting of using the wheel to spin and close distance and the scythe to attack from far away.

name: Academy of Raya Lucaria
image: ER Official Gameplay Reveal Trailer Raya Lucaria.png
description: The Academy of Raya Lucaria is a both a faction, and a legacy dungeon located in Liurnia of the Lakes.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The founding of the Academy of Raya Lucaria was credited to the primeval sorcerers Azur and Lusat. Their study of the Primeval Current shook the academy when they began to transfigure fledgling sorcerers into Graven Masses—the seeds of stars.

Long ago, Rennala charmed the Academy with her lunar magic. She became the Academy's master and established the house of Caria as royalty. When Rennala assumed governorship over the Academy, she heavily limited the study of the primeval current due the dangers it presented and subsequently exiled Azur and Lusat. This change outraged Sorceress Sellen, who began to transform her peers into Graven Schools. Though the Academy expelled Sellen and denounced her methods, they shared her core sentiment, and their thirst for knowledge would eventually lead to the downfall of the Carians influence over the Academy.

The combined forces of the Knights of the Cuckoo: the Cuckoo Knights, the Raya Lucaria Soldiers and their Foot Soldiers were hired by the Academy at some point. As payment for their service, the Academy taught them martial Glintstone techniques like Scholar's Armament and Scholar's Shield. The design of the Cuckoo bird upon their armor is mused to represent the Cuckoo's refusal to be mere servants of the Academy. The Cuckoo were given free reign to wage war as they pleased by the Academy, and became known for their rapacious ways.

When Rennala's husband Radagon left her to become the second Elden Lord, Rennala's heart went with him. With Rennala a grieving shell of her former self, the Academy then realised that she was no champion after all. She still clutches the amber egg given to her by Radagon, which contains the Great Rune of the Unborn. No longer in any state to defend herself, the Academy took the opportunity to lock Rennala in their Grand Library and staged a rebellion against the Carians, so that they could pursue unlimited study once more. The resulting conflict between the Acadamy's forces, and those of the Carians, waged across Liurnia, becoming an effective Liurnian civil war. Ultimately, the Acadamy would achieve their goals. Without their queen, and her successors absent, the Carians fell into decline, and their influence in the Academy's policies dissipated.

After the Shattering of the Elden Ring, the Academy declared neutrality in the ensuing war and cast repelling seals upon its entrances, blocking outside access to anyone not in possession of a Academy Glintstone Key. Such a key may be found on an island west of the Academy, guarded by Glintstone Dragon Smarag.

sections.heading: Sites of Grace
sections.body:
There are four Sites of Grace in the Academy of Raya Lucaria:
Church of the Cuckoo
Schoolhouse Classroom
Debate Parlor
Raya Lucaria Grand Library

Church of the Cuckoo= 

The Church of the Cuckoo is found near the entrance to the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Go through the doorway on the left from the chapel-like room at the start, and turn left again immediately.

Schoolhouse Classroom = 

The Schoolhouse Classroom Site of Grace is found after passing through the graveyard and riding the waterwheel.

Debate Parlor = 

The Debate Parlor is the Red Wolf of Radagon's boss room. It appears after defeating the boss.

Raya Lucaria Grand Library = 

The Raya Lucaria Grand Library Site of Grace will appear in Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon's boss room after defeating her. It is accessed by taking the elevator guarded by Moongrum, Carian Knight.

name: Adel, Baron of Night
image: ERN Boss Adel, Baron of Night (1.1) Tornado.png
description: Adel, Baron of Night, also known as Gaping Jaw, is a Nightlord boss in, encountered on the third night of the Gaping Jaw Expeditions.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Adel was a marvel of the natural world—immense, regal, and unrivaled atop his perch. But when the Night's Tide drenched the old island in azure rain, all life withered and perished. Starved of prey, Adel was consumed by an insatiable, ravening hunger that grew into madness.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
He is a monstrous black dragon with a sideways jaw and a bottomless appetite. He harnesses the power of violet-purple lightning during his second phase. As an Everdark Sovereign, Adel moves at light speed and whips up a massive cyclone.

Adel deals Standard damage on all moves during the first phase. During phases two and three, he can also deal Lightning damage. He inflicts heavy Blood Loss buildup on its biting grab attack. 

Adel is resistant to Fire, Lightning, and Blood Loss, and fully immune to Madness. He is vulnerable to Scarlet Rot, Frostbite, and Sleep; however, he is particularly affected by Poison damage. When the effect is procced, Adel receives the full sum of the damage-over-time upfront, and the next round of status buildup can be applied sooner than usual. However, Adel creates a Poison hazard by vomiting up the contents of his stomach.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body:
Night of the Baron (first victory)
Random Relics
Murk
Sovereign Sigils (Everdark Sovereign)

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.body:
Damage Types 
+0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
A positive value indicates bonus damage. 
A negative value indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type. 

Resistances 
A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect. 
The symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body:
Phase 1: No lightning, staggered by Poison
Phase 2: Lightning, not staggered by Poison

Everdark Sovereign:

The Everdark Sovereign version of Adel, Baron of Night begins with Phase 2 and transitions to an empowered "Phase 3" fight. Adel gains jagged purple horns on his left and right jaws and is more challenging, utilizing a fully-upgraded moveset.
This version of the boss does not have the scripted weakness to Poison because it starts in Phase 2.
When he reaches 60% HP, Adel teleports uncontrollably, then strikes the earth in a flash of lightning, creating a raging tornado and starting Phase 3.
Tornado deals Lightning damage to players outside its ring; the eye of the storm is only safe zone.
The tornado can be passed through, but it deals damage; use Spiritstreams to jump in unscathed.
Tornado lasts 60 seconds, and has a 60-second cooldown; it can be activated once every 120 seconds.
The hurtbox of several attacks is expanded during Phase 3.
Prefers the triple ground pound over single ground pounds during Phase 3.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
Stack Lightning damage negation.
Eat nine Stanching Boluses to gain a +9 Resistance to Blood Loss.
Hurl Fetid Pots from behind, never near the mouth.
During the second phase, watch for and avoid spots where the lightning will strike.
Jump right before the delayed lightning eruption to avoid all earthquake attacks.
When fighting the Everdark Sovereign, use the Spiritstream jumps to enter the eye of the storm from above. They appear simultaneously with the tornado.
One of Adel's attacks displaces him far from his target. If he leaves the tornado ring, avoid chasing after him.
Allies can be freed from Adel's biting grab attack by breaking his stance 
Guardian, Raider, and Wylder can survive the full grab attack.
During Phases 2 and 3, Adel gains access to a variation of the grab that lasts longer and deals additional damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This Nightlord can be challenged after defeating Gladius, Beast of Night for the first time. The Everdark Sovereign Gaping Jaw Expedition is unlocked by beating Adel for the first time.
Dark Night of the Baron is purchased from the Collector Signboard after defeating the Everdark Sovereign.
The standard Gaping Jaw Expedition typically features Gaping Dragon or the Crucible Knight and Golden Hippopotamus duo as the second Night bosses. The Everdark Sovereign Expedition has an Ancient Dragon (Phase 1 & 2).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: DragonTyranno.
Everdark Adel, Baron of Night was the first Everdark Sovereign to debut, appearing from June 19, 2025, 09:00 UTC through June 26, 2025, 08:59 UTC. He was followed by Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow.
Adel is a name of European origins that means "Noble" or "Elite".

sections.body: The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of flames, dealing Fire damage equal to 169% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e., 507% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonfire. 
Compared to Dragonfire, this spell deals 17% more damage but also consumes 38% more FP. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless. 
This is the third strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 0.5% less damage than Ghostflame Breath and 10% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased. 
The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Ailment Talisman provides ~+350 resistance to a specific status effect after being afflicted.
Poison / Scarlet Rot resistance lasts for 120 seconds.
Frostbite resistance lasts for 45 seconds.
Hemorrhage, Sleep, and Madness resistance last for 30 seconds.
Death Blight is not affected, as its onset kills the player.
The buildup or duration of the triggering ailment is immediately reduced by a certain amount.
This talisman is especially useful in areas or encounters where specific ailments are prevalent.

sections.body:
Unlike Ash of War: Gravitas, which deals entirely Magic damage, this weapon's skill mostly Physical damage with some Magic damage, with roughly the same damage ratio as the weapon itself.
The shortest among all greatswords.
The 2-handed charged heavy attacks of this weapon deals damage on par with that of a Colossal Sword while draining much less Stamina than any other greatsword's. 1-handed charge attacks have similar bonuses but much less of a damage increase.
To be precise, the 1-handed charged heavy attacks have a roughly 10% higher damage multiplier while the 2-handed charged heavy attack has a 34% damage multiplier, and both cost only 18 points of Stamina where the average stamina cost for greatswords for both is between 35 and 42 points of Stamina for the 1-handed ones and between 38 and 48 for 2-handed ones.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Limgrave (Stormhill)
(Optional) Alexander can first be found in Stormhill, stuck in a pothole atop a cliff southwest of the Saintsbridge Site of Grace. He will call out once you get close. After talking to him, agree to help him and then stand behind him and hit him. Once you have dealt sufficient damage, he will burst free of the hole. Exhaust his dialogue again to receive an Exhalted Flesh.
Limgrave (Gael Tunnel)
(Optional) Alexander can next be found near the Rear Gael Tunnel Site of Grace, accessible via the Limgrave entrance. By progressing through the dungeon from the Caelid entrance, you will be able to unlock the door blocking Alexander's path. Exhaust his dialogue to continue his questline.
Caelid (Redmane Castle) 
(Optional) Alexander will be standing in the plaza as long as you have triggered the Radahn Festival. He is also available as a summon during the Starscourge Radahn boss fight.
Caelid (Redmane Castle)
After defeating Starscourge Radahn, Alexander can be found near the Site of Grace in the Wailing Dunes. Exhaust his dialogue to progress his questline.
Liurnia of the Lakes
(Optional) Alexander will be in a pothole on the cliffs above Jarburg, south of the Artist's Shack (Liurnia of the lakes). He will once again ask you to hit him, however doing so will not free him. You must throw an Oil Pot at him, talk to him again, and then hit him several more times to free him. Speak to him again to receive three Exalted Flesh.
Mt Gelmir
Alexander can be found in a pool of lava south of Fort Laiedd, near a Magma Wyrm encounter. To speak to him without taking damage from the lava, ride Torrent to a sloped rock in front of him and dismount. Speak to him to receive the Jar helmet.
Mountaintops of the Giants
(Optional) Alexander can be summoned during the Fire Giant boss fight. His summon sign is just inside the arena.
Crumbling Farum Azula
Alexander will be standing on a floating platform close to the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace. He will request a duel. After defeating him, exhaust his dialogue and pick up Alexander's Innards and a Shard of Alexander.
Alexander's Innards can be given to Jar-Bairn at the end of his own questline.

name: Ancestor Spirit
description: The is an optional boss in. It also appears as a field boss in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The antler-like horns of a long-lived stag continued budding long after death, over and over again, until the beast became an Ancestor Spirit. Ancestral Spirits are a phenomenon that exists beyond the purview of the Erdtree, following the principle that life sprouts from death, just as it does birth, granting power. Its horned remains are found at the southern Hallowhorn Grounds on the bank of the Siofra River, where it lies beneath the false night sky. Its large, antler-like horns sprouted small leafy plants that shone with light, infusing nearby Ancestral Followers with profound spirituality.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body:
13,000 runes
Ancestral Follower Ashes

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
The horned remains of this Ancestor Spirit are found at the Hallowhorn Grounds in the lower section of the Siofra River, accessible via the Siofra River Well in Limgrave. This ruined structure is situated southeast of the Siofra River Bank Site of Grace. 

In order to face this boss, the player must first light eight beacons scattered throughout the area. Each beacon corresponds to a pillar flanking the staircase to the Hallowhorn Grounds. Once all signals are lit, the following message displays: Power gathers somewhere in horned remains. The horned remains will burned with blue spectral flames, and agreeing to Touch horned remains will grant a supernatural encounter with the spirit.

sections.heading: Stats
sections.body:
HP: 4,393
Defense: 107
Stance: 120
This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
Cannot be parried
Ancestor Spirit is scripted to absorb the souls of nearby animal spirits, gaining a new attack based on the aspect. It periodically die, rebirthing itself, losing the move.

Resistances:

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body: The Ancestor Spirit is able to jump up and hop while mid-air. It can produce a jet of blue spirit vapor from its mouth, both while on the ground and in the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: During the early Age of the Erdtree, Gransax attacked Leyndell, breaching the walls of the Royal Capital and triggered the War of the Ancient Dragons. During his assault, the knights of the Erdtree employed Golden Lightning Fortification, an Erdtree Worship incantation, to shield themselves from his red lightning. In the aftermath, a faction of Tree Sentinels concluded that the only way to protect the Erdtree was to transform into dragons themselves, becoming the malformed Draconic Tree Sentinels.

description: Ancient Dragon-Man is an Invader and optional Enemy boss in.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body:
Wields the Dragon-Hunter's Great Katana and Dragon Communion Seal.
Uses the Magma Breath and Dragonmaw Incantations.
Prefers two-handed jumping attacks and Dragonwound Slash.
Has transformed using a Rock Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Ancient Dragon-Man has a single Flask of Crimson Tears.
He has 0 Poise and 0% Damage Negation for each Damage Type.
Draconic Tree Sentinels also became dragons to better fight dragons.

Strategy:
It is possible to defeat the Ancient Dragon-Man without having leveled up or upgraded one's Weapons, Flasks and even Scadutree Blessings with relative comfort through the use of spamming the crouching light attack from Whips. As its long reach, fast attack-speed, low stamina-consumption and early stamina-regeneration, combined with the Ancient Dragon-Man's non-existent poise, allows the player to consistently harass him from a relatively safe distance without needing to worry about him trying to excessively dodge and then rush the player down like conventional projectiles from spells or bows would.

The player can increase their un-upgraded weapon's damage-output through the use of Blood Loss, Frostbite and Poison procs that are then immediately followed by the use of the Skill, The Poison Flower Blooms Twice as a third source of blood loss-like burst-damage. 

The most efficient set-up for this would be to have two different whips they can alternate between. Hoslow's Petal Whip and Thorned Whip are excellent choices as they can both have their Affinities changed through the use of Ashes of War, while at the same time preserving their innate blood loss buildup no matter what affinity is chosen. So one Poison whip with Ash of War: The Poison Flower Blooms Twice and a Cold whip with almost any ash of the user's choosing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: His humanoid appearance is that of a bald, middle-aged man with a wide jaw-line, while also carrying many visual traits distinctive to the Draconian race, such as their stone-black skin and eyes with grey irises and blood-red sclera.

name: Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear
image: ER Icon Spell Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear.png
description: Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 8,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Ancient Dragon Prayerbook.
Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Calls on a red, crackling spear from above that is then slammed into the ground, hitting with Lightning Attack Power equal to 360% of Incantation Scaling in a small 0.2 meter radius, and creating a shockwave with a 3 meter radius that hits with Lightning Attack Power equal to 285% of Incantation Scaling.

From the point of impact, waves of red lightning are sent out directly ahead and behind, and to the left and right of the caster with Lightning Attack Power equal to 122% of Incantation Scaling in a 2 meter radius from the center of each wave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Casting the spell costs 29 points of Stamina. 
Deals 17 Stance damage on a direct or shockwave hit and 5 Stance damage on a wave hit. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
The "direct" hit and the initial area attack cannot hit the same target, though the smaller, weakest waves can hit an enemy that has already been hit if they are either quick or large enough to also be where those are. 
The "spear" is actually flung downwards, meaning it can be used to hit the ground beneath a cliff if the caster is standing on its edge. 
Casts faster than Fortissax's Lightning Spear, but is much weaker overall and per hit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them. 
Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
FP cost was decreased from 30 to 25. 
Only the direct hit had its Stamina Attack Power increased against guarding enemies, from 100 to 140. 
Separate Stamina Attack Power values were added for guarding players: for a direct hit, it was increased from 140 to 175; for a near hit, it was increased from 100 to 125; and for a far away hit, it was increased from 60 to 75. 
Patch 1.04 included an undocumented change which reduced the FP cost of this incantation.
FP cost was decreased from 42 to 30.

name: Ancient Ruins
description: The ancient ruins (古遺跡, Furui Iseki), also known as giant ruins (巨大な古遺, Kyodai na Furui Iseki), are recurring structures found throughout the Lands Between in. They were seemingly built by the ancient civilization associated with the ruins at Rauh (ラウフ, Raufu, possibly Lauf).

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The ancient ruins are remnants of a prehistoric empire that spanned the entire Lands Between. The Rauh civilization predated the hornsent and was one of the earliest in the realm, rivalling the Ancient Dynasty and Farum Azula. According to hornsent scholars, the inhabitants of Rauh practised a form of spiritual manipulation, with their most well-known artifact being the Spritestone, which could manipulate the moment when a spirit vanished. These were crafted from Rauh Burrows, stones with small, nest-like holes meant to be inhabited by tiny spirits called 'sprites', enabling them to function as ritual implements. The Rauh people also used Dewgems as an ingredient in sprite medicine. These secrets were thought lost to time until their rediscovery at Rauh by hornsent archaeologists.

Statues of a mysterious woman with a great octagonal crown are prominently featured throughout the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to this goddess-like figure. The Verdigris Discus can be found under one of these statues. The Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook 2 and the Bondstone are located beneath another, held by the corpse of a hornsent. In addition, female figures with pointed headpieces and long side veils are represented in other artistic reliefs at the Rauh ruins.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
Highroad Cave — a Guardian Golem protects black stone structures buried in the earth. These structures are built at the junction where the inland sea meets the Murkwater river that runs south through Agheel Lake and feeds into the sea via another set of Rauh arches.

Limgrave — structures are found along the southwest coast of Limgrave, bridging the chasm that separates the region from the Weeping Peninsula.

Weeping Peninsula — a row of black stone structures cross through Tombsward Ruins in western Weeping Peninsula.

Wailing Dunes — large arches of black stone emerge from the plateau, running east into the sea. This structure was likely once continuous with the corresponding sections at the Mohgwyn Palace deep underground.

Ruin-Strewn Precipice — appears to be a great dam positioned at the point where the Altus Plateau meets Liurnia of the Lakes. It is connected to the Seethewater river, which originates in Gelmir and floods the lower region.

Mountaintops of the Giants — black stone megastructures are present along the stretch of the frozen river that crosses the Mountaintops of the Giants and a valley in the Consecrated Snowfield where a large number of Guardian Golems protect it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Rauh civilization created colossal golems from stone and lava. These Guardian Golems are commonly found near their ruins. Their great arrows are imbued with ancient magic and generate tempestuous gusts of wind.
Flowing water is a persistent motif in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The location features numerous Dewgems and waterfalls, and irrigation channels bisect its paved roadways.
The Guardian Golem at Highroad Cave drops the Blue Dancer Charm related to the blind swordsman who defeated the ancient rot god.
The giant stone arches may have been constructed to divert rivers or regulate water flow, possibly to mitigate the impact of erosion or prevent the accumulation of stagnant water.
The Rauh civilization used heftiness to represent the burden of the strong to protect others.
"Heft" was later used to describe the Giant's Red Braid, Thorned Whip, Prelate's Inferno Crozier, and Giant-Crusher, among others. The Fire Prelates, who revered the Fire Giant, used heftiness to symbolize the weight of their duty. Many Fire Monks later abandoned their posts to serve the "weighty" Black Flame.
Rauh is internally referred to as モヘンジョダロ, Mohenjo-Daro, an ancient ruin of the real-world Indus Valley Civilization, one of the earliest cities ever built.

name: Ancient Ruins of Rauh
description: The Ancient Ruins of Rauh (ラウフの古遺跡, Raufu no Furui Iseki, possibly Lauf), also known as the Rauh Ruins, is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The ancient Rauh civilization predated the hornsent, and rivaled the Ancient Dynasty and Farum Azula as one of the earliest cultures to emerge in the Lands Between. The primordial Crucible of life flourished and likely originated in Rauh, and, according to legend, the "mother of all Crucibles" first appeared on the Giants. Its influence mutated the local wildlife to grow aspects of other creatures, such as horns and feathers. The area was suffused with such potent spirituality that an acrid Spirit Calculus formed on its inhabitants over time. 

According to hornsent scholars, the inhabitants of Rauh practiced a form of spiritual manipulation. Their most well-known artifact was the Spritestone, also known as "bondstone," which could manipulate the moment when a spirit vanished. These spritestones were crafted using Rauh Burrows, oval-shaped stones modeled with small, nest-like holes at their center to be inhabited by spirits, enabling them to function as ritual implements. Bondstones were large burrowstones with a white gem obtained from polishing a special crystal. These were used to control the explosions of spiritual powers, thus determining the moment when the bond with the spirit would be broken. 

For unknown reasons, the civilization of Rauh collapsed, and the city fell into ruin. It was split in two by a great chasm and became flooded and densely overgrown with vegetation. The secrets of spiritual bonding were lost to time.

Hornsent:
After their rise to power, the hornsent made expeditions to the Rauh ruins. They sought to understand the secrets of antiquity because these ruins were strongly associated with the Crucible that they held sacred. They erected the Church of the Bud in the Rauh ruins. The structure was known for its flowers and featured a large ornamental bud and stone platform for viewing adjacent Belurat and Enir-Ilim. Whether intentional or not, it was constructed atop a divine element. Later, hornsent archaeologists rediscovered the process for making spritestones and other forgotten spiritual arts.

Age of the Erdtree:
During Messmer's Crusade, his army marched toward Enir-Ilim through the ruins of Rauh. They razed the Church of the Bud and installed the Sealing Tree on the stone platform. However, the ruins were preserved due to the intervention of Fire Knight Salza, who defied orders to burn them. Messmer's forces collected large horned beasts and tanglehorned giants from the ruins for the Specimen Storehouse instead.

As the Church of the Bud burned around her, Romina sat on the ground, clutching the bud in speechless silence. She discovered a twisted divine element in the ashes and modified it into the scarlet rot. After the Battle of Aeonia, Romina summoned and soothed Malenia's unwanted butterflies, who allowed her to practice an ancient purification ritual once lost to time. Her actions imbued the church's flowers with scarlet rot, caused local Spider Scorpions to grow in size, and transformed the landscape surrounding the Church of the Bud into a scarlet rot swamp.

Game events:

The ruins are a lush oasis of green in the dour Realm of Shadow. Their sanctity is ensured by Fire Knight Salza, who guards the west entrance to the city. The eastern section of the complex is home to many Bloodfiends and horned beasts. The subterranean structures are excavated by Shadow Undead in search of the secrets of Rauh. The western half of the ruins are dominated by a Servants of Rot cult led by Romina, Saint of the Bud. The waters in this section are stagnant, festering pools of rot. Like the Scarlet Buds of the Church, the bodies of the Kindred of Rot have turned bright scarlet, indicating their acceptance by Romina. The ruins are also home to many Spider Scorpions and other creatures touched by the Crucible.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Internal Name: モヘンジョダロ, Mohenjo-Daro, an ancient ruin of the real-world Indus Valley Civilization.
A small portion of this area is accessible early by traveling through the Sending Gate at the Fifth Belfry, located behind Castle Ensis on the Scadu Altus.
Statues of a mysterious woman wearing a great octagonal crown are prominently featured throughout the ruins. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to the "Rauh goddess" figure. The Verdigris Discus can be found under one of these statues, while the [[Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook 2|Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook [2]]] and the Bondstone are located beneath another, held by the corpse of a hornsent. In addition, female figures with pointed headpieces and long side veils are represented in other artistic reliefs in the architecture.

Retail=
Retail:
Guaranteed Drop: Auriza Hero's Grave
Drops from the three teleporting Chariots found within the Hero's Grave of Capital Outskirts in Altus Plateau. 
The player has to navigate the side section that begins in the pit towards the end of the dungeon and trigger a Flame Pillar found at the end of said side section. This will move a statue of Rosus perched on top of said pillar that projects a teleporter sigil into the middle of the hallway where the two chariots patrolling side by side can be found. Causing the third chariot to teleport in the middle of their path, initiating a mass collision that destroys all of them in the process. The player will automatically receive this item (along with the complete Tree Sentinel Set) in their inventory once the final chariot collides.
The player can also more easily trigger this flame pillar without needing to explore the side section. The moment they enter the hall with the two chariots, the player can use Margit's or Mohg's Shackle (as despite doing no direct damage, both of these items sport enormous hitboxes that ignore walls) allowing them to trigger the flame pillar without needing direct line of sight with said pillar.
Once this item has been obtained, it can be duplicated by trading in Lost Ashes of War to Smithing Master Hewg.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Volcano Manor
Located on a corpse in an isolated room of Volcano Manor, near the shortcut door back to the entrance of the manor (Stonesword Key is required).
To reach it, the player must start from the Temple of Eiglay Site of Grace and take the elevator up to the upper level of the manor (where the Man-Serpent with Magma Blades patrol). Head northwest, past the Man-Serpent with the Magma Whip Candlestick, into the building and then rightwards into the throne room. Take either of the first sets of stairs up, followed by the second set of stairs that go away from the throne itself. Up on the second floor there will be a door that leads to another, locked by an Imp Statue. Unlock the statue and head through until a large room filled with hanging cages that can be used to descend downwards. Once the player has reached the bottom, they can head to the door opening on the northeastern wall of the room which will eventually lead to this item.
Once this item has been obtained, it can be duplicated by trading in Lost Ashes of War to Smithing Master Hewg.

name: Asimi, Silver Tear
description: Asimi, Silver Tear, later known as Asimi, Eternal King, was a Silver Tear character that was cut from. They asked to enter the player's body to aid them on their quest. Information about them is limited and may no longer be canonical.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Asimi was located at the Artist's Shack in Limgrave.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Asimi was a silver tear that gained sentience and the ability to speak, living in fear of death. An arcane creature of mimicry, they came from a mother chalice in the Eternal City—the cradle of their kind—with dreams of one day becoming Sovereign Eternal.

sections.heading: Asimi's Quest
sections.body:
Asimi would have identified the Tarnished as the one fated to become Elden Lord, offering power in exchange for protection. Should the player accept, Asimi was inhaled through a kiss, living inside their new host.

Upon hearing the great underground rivers of their home, Asimi would have urged the player to visit the Eternal Cities, where special chalices could be found. Asimi wished to quench their thirst by drinking from these cradle chalices to become a more perfect whole. After collecting the tears from each chalice, Asimi likely exited the Tarnished to follow their footsteps.

Asimi likely morphed into the Tarnished and attacked them, much like the Mimic Tear and Stray Mimic Tear bosses.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
A unique "kissing" animation would have triggered when the player accepted Asimi inside.
Melina offered unique dialogue if Asimi was present inside the Tarnished.
They likely dropped or granted the Mimic Tear Ashes.
The mother chalice was the most sacred to Asimi, and the cradle of their kind. It was suffused with the blessings of the stars.
Radagon of the Golden Order also sought to become a perfect whole and reign for eternity.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Asími (ασήμι) is a Greek word for "silver".

name: Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom
image: ER Icon Spell Aspects of the Crucible Bloom.png
description: Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom is found in the upper sections of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. From the Rauh Ancient Ruins, East site of grace, head across the bridge just to the west, then drop down to a slightly lower bridge section at the end.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Sprouts a flower from the user's chest, creating a rain of light around them that lasts for 4 seconds and has Holy Attack Power equal to 80% of Incantation Scaling per hit.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power per hit to 100% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 26 points of Stamina.
Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 44%.
Can deal decent damage against large foes such as Dragons, but more mobile or smaller foes will likely only be hit once or twice for minimal damage.
There is about a 2-second delay before the rain of light begins after casting the spell.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This spell is very similar to the light spell used by Miranda Blossoms, Melina, and the cut Miranda's Prayer tool. However, this spell creates a flower at the beginning of its cast.
Patch 1.14 increased attack speed, increased the size of the hitbox, and shortened the recovery time between using this incantation and follow-up actions.

variant.effect: Creates a miranda flower on chest to summon rain of light

name: Aspects of the Crucible: Breath
image: ER Icon Spell Aspects of the Crucible Breath.png
description: Aspects of the Crucible: Breath is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Aspects of the Crucible: Breath is acquired upon defeating Tanith's Knight, which can be fought after killing Tanith in Rykard's arena in the Volcano Manor, at the end of her questline.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Creates a large pouch on the caster's neck before breathing out tongues of flame with Fire Attack Power equal to 98% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast.
Attack Power is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
Doesn't immediately start to consume FP for the upkeep cost, instead only starting after about 2-3 seconds. This seems to coincide with the initially created throat pouch shrinking to roughly the width of the character's torso.
The caster must always move forward at a walking pace as long as this spell is being channeled.
Decent in PvP as a "wake-up" attack (i.e., after an attack that has knocked down an opponent, such as a Critical Attack), since it has a relatively short start-up animation and a wide attack area, which can cause the additional damage needed to finish off a target.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This spell is used by Crucible Axe Knights (except for the two found in Limgrave).
Aspects of the Crucible: Breath creates a throat pouch similar to those of the basilisks.

name: Aspects of the Crucible: Horns
image: ER Icon Spell Aspects of the Crucible Horns.png
description: Aspects of the Crucible: Horns is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Aspects of the Crucible: Horns is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight in Stormveil Castle, down the outer western rampart. From the Rampart Tower Site of Grace, head north to the walkway with the Warhawks, and drop down to the left at the guard tower. Continue dropping down until you reach a breakable cliff and fall through it to arrive on a cliffside with the Crucible Knight.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
The caster crouches slightly and creates a horn on their shoulder before dashing a few steps forward, hitting with Standard Attack Power equal to 277% of Incantation Scaling upon contact with the horn.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 327% of Incantation Scaling and greatly increases the distance charged, to about three times the previous amount, launching any human-sized foes that are hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 38 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 49 points of Stamina.
Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 18%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 36%.
Deals 16 Stance damage when uncharged and 30 Stance damage when charged.
The charged version of the spell is generally much better than the uncharged version, primarily due to the increased distance traveled and the ability to launch smaller foes into the air.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This spell is used by Crucible Tree Knights, though they summon it on their arm.
Despite this, the spell is dropped by a Crucible Axe Knight.
Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
FP cost was reduced from 20 to 18, and damage to Stamina of guarding enemies was increased from 200 to 240 for the uncharged version and from 260 to 300 for the charged version.
Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost, increased cast speed, increased the distance traveled when not charged, and made it easier to cause enemies to flinch when charged.
FP cost was reduced from 30 to 20.

variant.effect: Creates shoulder horn to gore foes from a low stance.

name: Aspects of the Crucible: Tail
image: ER Icon Spell Aspects of the Crucible Tail.png
description: Aspects of the Crucible: Tail is an incantation spell in. It is an Erdtree incantation.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Aspects of the Crucible: Tail is acquired by defeating the Crucible Knight trapped in the Stormhill Evergaol, located in Stormhill.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Creates a tail that swings in front of the caster with Standard Attack Power equal to 202% of Incantation Scaling.

If charged, it adds a second, larger swing, dealing Standard Attack Power equal to 274% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 42 points of Stamina to cast, whether charged or uncharged.
Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 36%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 56%.
The first swing deals 13 Stance damage, and the second swing deals 39 Stance damage.
This means that the charged version of the spell can deal up to 52 Stance damage, greater than even a hammer-type Colossal Weapon's charged heavy attack, allowing it to break the stance of many enemies within two hits.
The spell goes through obstacles, making it decent for ambushing foes by using thin walls as cover.
It is a bit slow to cast and has about a second of recovery time after the spell finishes casting.
Launches smaller foes backward if it hits them.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This is the spell used by Crucible Axe Knights.
Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
FP cost was reduced from 22 to 20, and stamina damage to guarding enemies was increased from 180 to 200 on the first swipe and from 240 to 270 on the second swipe.
Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost.
FP cost was reduced from 32 to 22.

variant.effect: Creates supple tail to sweep area before caster

name: Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns
image: ER Icon Spell Aspects of the Crucible Thorns.png
description: Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Aspects of the Crucible: Thorns is acquired by defeating the Golden Hippopotamus boss found just inside the main gate of Shadow Keep on Scadu Altus.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Sprouts spines from the back and rolls sideways on the ground, throwing them around the user, dealing Pierce Attack Power equal to 45% of Incantation Scaling per hit, hitting up to 10 times (450% of Incantation Scaling in total).

The spell can be charged to spin twice, increasing the maximum number of hits to 15 and moving forward. These extra attacks deal Attack Power equal to 120% of Incantation Scaling per hit (600% of Incantation Scaling for the extra hits or 1000% of Incantation Scaling in total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 29 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 38 points of Stamina.
Attack Power is boosted by wearing pieces of the Crucible Set (4% per piece, 17% for the whole set because 1.04^4 = 1.17).
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 122%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 156%.
The very low height of the user when casting this spell means that high-centered thrusting or horizontal attacks can easily miss them.
The charged version's increased forward momentum makes it even better at evading attacks.
Since this Incantation deals Pierce damage, it will occasionally deal a Counter Hit against an attacking foe, increasing the Attack Power of that specific hit by 30%.
Note that this will most likely result in an overall 2-3% damage increase per Counter Hit since each is only a portion of the total damage.
Since this isn't a weapon, it does NOT benefit from the Spear Talisman.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.14 increased attack power and stamina attack power against guarding enemies. The close-range hitbox now follows the movement of the player.
The attack power was increased from 40% of Incantation Scaling to 45% for the uncharged hits and most of the charged hits, while the increase was from 70% to 120% of Incantation Scaling for the stronger charged hits.
Stamina attack power against guarding enemies was only increased for the charged hits, going from 50 to 85 against PvE enemies and from 62 to 106 against other players.

name: Assassin's Approach
description: Assassin's Approach is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Starting spell for the Confessor origin.
Sold for 2,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Assassin's Prayerbook.
Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Assassin's Approach applies a Buff that silences footsteps and prevents all non-lethal fall damage for 30 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 15 FP per cast.
Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
Non-lethal fall damage is only negated for falls between 16 and 20 meters, meaning this incantation does not prevent guaranteed deaths from falls of 20 meters or more.
Overrides and is overridden by Soft Cotton.

Strategies:
Generally outclassed by Soft Cotton, which is an easy-to-acquire consumable tool that costs no FP to activate. However, Soft Cotton lasts only 20 seconds and cannot be crafted during combat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Update 1.03 (undocumented) increased FP cost from 12 to 15.
Update 1.07 extended the duration of this spell from 20 seconds to 30 seconds.

name: Astel
description: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void and Astel, Stars of Darkness are Bosses in. Naturalborn of the Void is a Boss in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Far beyond the Lands Between, within the Greater Will's lightless abyss, the many-colored debris of ancient stars coalesced into a malformed creature. A falling star of ill omen, Astel arrived long ago. It assailed the Eternal Cities with a barrage of meteors, sealing them deep underground, away from the true night sky. It destroyed the Nameless Eternal City and Noklateo, the Shrouded City.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: A procession of multi-colored orbs, Astel is an aberrant, cosmic entity that resembles a Great Dragonfly. It has a humanoid skull with large mandibles and a large blue eye emerging from a crack in its forehead. It has four translucent insect wings and six skeletal arms that end in human-like hands, the forelimbs each possessing six fingers. Its long tail ends in a spiny scorpion stinger, wielded as a flail. It also casts gravity-based magic and can warp to other parts of the arena.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Astel, Naturalborn of the Void=

This is an optional boss, but is required to reach Moonlight Altar and achieve a certain ending.
Moveset:

Astel, Naturalborn of the Void is encountered in a cavern beyond the Lake of Rot, accessed via a coffin in the Grand Cloister. It makes use of a variety of gravity-based attacks, and can warp to other parts of the arena.

Astel, Stars of Darkness=

This is an optional boss.
Moveset:

Astel, Stars of Darkness is encountered in Yelough Anix Tunnel in the Consecrated Snowfield. It fights much like in the other encounter, however it also gains a grab attack once its health goes below half, in which it spawns several copies of itself to grab the player.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The Fallingstar Beasts are likely another variant of Astel. They have the same head and tails, but the ferromagnetic beasts are covered in stone and iron filings.

Astel has an unused animation in which it fell from the sky, crashing to the earth like a meteor. This move is used by Starscourge Radahn.

description: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void is an optional Boss in.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is encountered within a secluded, starlit cavern somewhere along the underground Ainsel River, beyond the Lake of Rot. This area is accessed by entering the Transportation Coffin overlooking a chasm at the Grand Cloister. The elevator Astel blocks is the only path to the hidden Moonlight Altar, a necessary step for Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Defeating Astel, Naturalborn of the Void for the first time unlocks the "Astel, Naturalborn of the Void" achievement.
Defeating this boss is optional, though it is mandatory for the "Age of the Stars" ending.
Astel resembles a Great Dragonfly.
Astel, Naturalborn of the Void, is the boss of the Grand Cloister, an area populated by insect-like Kindred of Rot.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This boss was named Astel, Misbegotten of the Void in. At the time, the Misbegotten were referred to as "Aberrations."
Astel has an unused animation in which it fell from the sky, crashing to the earth like a meteor. This move is used by Starscourge Radahn.
The internal data Astel's boss arena includes spawn markers for an Ancestor Spirit and its spirit animals, suggesting the Grand Cloister boss was reassigned to Astel from a third Ancestor Spirit encounter.
It is also possible that one of the Ancestor Spirit boss rooms was duplicated and used as a template.

description: Axe Talisman is a talisman in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Mistwood Ruins, eastern Limgrave. A Runebear lies very close to the entrance.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Increases the damage of charged heavy melee attacks by 10%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Doesn't enhance the Dark Moon Greatsword's charged heavy attacks when they're buffed by its Unique Skill: Moonlight Greatsword.
Doesn't work with the projectiles launched by the charged heavy attacks of the Frozen Needle or Wing of Astel. 
Has strong synergy with the Roar Medallion if using a skill that boosts heavy attacks. 
Skill compatible with both are Barbaric Roar, Braggart's Roar, Shriek of Milos, and War Cry. 
Synergy with the Spear Talisman with weapons that have charged heavy attacks that deal Pierce damage. 
Weapon types that primarily have thrusting heavy attacks are Great Spears, Spears (except for the Death Ritual Spear, Partisan, and Spiked Spear), Heavy Thrusting Swords (except for the Great Épée), Thrusting Swords (except for the Estoc), and Straight Swords (except for the Broadsword, Cane Sword, Carian Knight's Sword, and Lazuli Glintstone Sword). 
Other notable weapons are the Claymore, Lucerne, Nagakiba, Pickaxe, Rusted Anchor, Warpick, and the Zweihander and Troll's Golden Sword. 
Works well with the unique charged heavy attack of the Iron Cleaver and Celebrant's Cleaver, since while they are weaker than the usual Axe charged heavy attack they also include a run-up that potentially let's them be used from a safe distance to close in.

name: Azur's Glintstone Staff
image: ER Icon weapon Azur's Glintstone Staff.png
description: Azur's Glintstone Staff is a Glintstone Staff and catalyst found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Found in a secluded room on the highest level of the Church of the Cuckoo. The level can be accessed via the rooftops of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.

From the Debate Parlor site of grace, go outside to the left until you meet two Raya Lucaria Sorcerers. Jump down on the stairs next to them. Continue forward until you can jump onto the rooftops. Then, proceed further and go up the ladder at the end of said rooftops.

After the sorcerer, go down on the rooftops again, until you can see a dome-like structure that has windows. Go through one of the windows, and descend onto the lower floor. One of the exits leads to a enclosed bridge, with a High Page guarding the secluded room. The staff is in the room behind him, in front of the inactive School of Graven Mages.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Increases FP cost of Sorceries by 20%, in exchange for speeding up their casting time even more than the Radagon Icon.
Casting speed is decreased for any spell cast when this staff is held in one of a character's two active hands, even if this staff isn't used to cast it. 
Adds 40 "virtual" Dexterity for the purpose of improving casting speed. 
The casting speed decrease applies to both Incantations and Sorceries but the FP cost increase only applies to Sorceries. This means that Incantation users can keep this Staff in the off-hand with no penalty aside from its weight and taking up an active hand-slot. 
A +10 Azur's Glintstone Staff gains 254 Sorcery Scaling with minimum stats (52 Intelligence), 279 Sorcery Scaling at 60 Intelligence, 320 Sorcery Scaling at 70 Intelligence, and 362 Sorcery Scaling at 80 Intelligence.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: Banished Knight Engvall
image: ER Icon Ash Banished Knight Engvall Ashes.png
description: Banished Knight Engvall is a spirit ash in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Dropped by Grave Warden Duelist in Murkwater Catacombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts. 
Summons a Banished Knight that wields a halberd with a more mobile variant of the Stormcaller skill on it.
Deals Standard and Pierce damage.
A slow, tanky summon that can hit decently hard and is available very early on, Engvall's main drawback is his huge FP cost which puts him out of range of most early builds that aren't focused on magic. This makes him an ideal companion for a caster that doesn't mind devoting all or most of a cerulean flask to him.
Though he is quite durable, he is quite expensive, FP-wise, to summon. His halberd gives him wide-sweeping attacks for cleaving through crowds, while his Stormcaller has good AOE and can knock many enemies flat. Still, he is greatly outclassed by Banished Knight Oleg due to the latter's greater damage potential: Oleg tends to move and attack faster with in longer combos, while Engvall is a bit slower and also isn't quite as good at keeping foes staggered.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In versions prior to Patch 1.03 this Spirit Ash was unobtainable, as the boss would instead drop a Battle Hammer. 
The Japanese name of these knights is 失地騎士 (shicchi kishi); knights who have lost their land to an enemy. The implication is they are "Banished Knights" because they have been driven from their homeland by force.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Magic damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for caster and allies within a 6 meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 13 points of Stamina to cast. 
Overall a very strong defensive incantation, if one that comes a bit late and will most likely come after the Magic-heavy area of Liurnia of the Lakes, with only the Astels and Loretta being the major Magic damage bosses left. 
Since it doesn't actually apply a flat increase to damage negation, just the damage taken, the actual effective new damage negation (the one shown on the character screen) can be calculated with the following formula: 1 - (1 - (current Magic damage negation)/100) * (1 - 0.60). 
As an example, if Magic damage negation before casting the incantation is 25.000 the result becomes this: 1 - (1 - 25.000/100) * (1 - 0.60) = 0.7, or 70.0% Magic damage negation.
Against other players, simply replace the 0.60 with 0.20 for a new end result of 40.0% Magic damage negation. 
Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher Magic damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell the less effective it may appear to be in the statistics.

name: Base Serpent
description: The base serpent or abyssal serpent is a character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Long ago, the abyssal serpent was a powerful snake in the Lands Between. It was separated from its light, although it is unclear by whom, when, or why. If it was not so already, it henceforth became a wicked entity.

Messmer, son of Queen Marika, was born cursed with the essence of the base serpent stirring within him. His mother's fear drove her to suppress its power, so she replaced his right eye with a golden Scarseal of Grace. Later, she trapped him within the Realm of Shadow on an endless crusade against those stripped of her Grace. The abyssal serpent slowly consumed Messmer's Kindling, but its influence was limited by his constant companions, the winged serpents.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Information regarding this character is limited.
If the base serpent did not possess Messmer from birth, then it was placed there by Marika herself.
It is unclear whether the shed snakeskin near the Bonny Village belonged to the base serpent.
The skin is adjacent to the O Mother statue, implying a connection to Messmer. However, its appearance more closely resembles the flayed snake found in the Temple of Eiglay than the attacks of Base Serpent Messmer.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Messmer refers to the Base Serpent as "光無き、深淵の蛇が" that can be translated as "the Lightless, Serpent of the Abyss", without the idea that it was "shorn of light" but rather that it had always been lightless (光無, Hikarina, lit. "Without light").
Messmer unleashes the base serpent by divesting himself of his mother's light.
Marika's actions ironically led to the base serpent's unsealing.
In the Japanese version, the "base serpent" is called 邪な蛇 ("Wicked Snake" or "Evil Snake").
The English word "base" is used to express a deficiency in character or status (ignoble, baseborn, base instincts).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Has a 20% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies. 
As a Flail, this weapon can't be parried. 
Scales strongly with Intelligence. 
This weapon's version is a bit different than the one used with Wing of Astel, instead being a swing that launches the wielder forward while spreading out a cloud that explodes a second later.
The Bastard's Stars weapon design is loaded with symbolic imagery.
Astel formed in the Greater Will's lightless abyss, and the icon depicts a skeletal finger protruding from a void. The finger bones extend from a starry, knot-like cluster of blue, green, and purple orbs. Wispy white filaments trail from the clump, and a small bony spur sprouts from its surface like a horn. A procession of stars follows from the mass, culminating in dark concentric rings.
The orange-hued stars likely represent primordial gold and amber-hued stars, which dictate the fates of the gods.
"Many-colored" is otherwise only used to describe the flowers adorning the Dominula Celebrants' weapons and Festive Hoods.

name: Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statue
image: ER Statue Ancient Dynasty Mohgwyn Closeup.png
description: Bearded Ancient Dynasty Statues, unofficially referred to as Elden John, Fellden John, Ancient Dynast, Ancient Dynasty God, Bearded Elder, Uhl King, Uld King, and other names in the community, are objects in. All information about the statues and unseen character they depict is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The old statues portray a bald-headed elder with a long, braided beard and a missing right eye, dressed in a hooded robe and holding a stone tablet to his chest with elongated arms, though individual examples vary. Those on stone-coffin ships show him in his most human form, flanked by maiden-and-lord pairings, and may be among the earliest. Works attributed to the Ancient Dynasty give him a damaged right eye and arboreal traits—most notably a root-like beard—and depict him embracing one half of a broken tablet with tightly crossed arms, the discarded half placed at his feet; the held fragment bears a tree, while the other contains a ringed world map or sun. Statues at the Cocoon of the Empyrean omit the rejected tablet and replace his legs with roots. The figures at The Four Belfries, likely the most recent, emphasize his emergence from dense roots or dead branches. His robes have extended sleeves, and he raises his hands to his chest. His legs and both tablets are absent.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A bearded man was revered in the Ancient Dynasty that existed long before the age of the Erdtree. His heroic followers were sent off with Great Grave Glovewort in great stone coffin ships for burial at sea, drifting towards the Lands Between. When the massive arks finally washed up on the Cerulean Coast, their contents had putrified into a viscous sludge of bruise-colored putrescence. Though tainted and impure, the Deathbirds nonetheless cleansed the putrid remains in their ghostflame kilns, until they one day stopped.

His followers established a series of palaces along the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers, where claymen priests used crude weapons made from shards of fallen meteorites, which also arrived from outside the realm. They constructed the Hallowhorn Grounds, Uhl Palace Ruins, Uld Palace Ruins, Lake of Rot, Grand Cloister, and Mohgwyn Palace, and later The Four Belfries. At some point, their ancient dynasty collapsed, and the tablet-clutching god's name was forgotten.

The Ancestral Followers later worshipped Ancestor Spirits among the dynastic ruins. Their ritual implements evoked the power of horns, trees, and Deathbirds. The followers' faith existed beyond the influence of the Erdtree, asserting that new life arises from death, and from Death, one gains power.

After the outer god of Rot was sealed away in the Grand Cloister, the Kindred of Rot prayed toward scarlet rot-infested statues of the bearded man.

The Mohgwyn Dynasty worshipped a large statue of the bearded man at the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum, which faced the Cocoon of the Empyrean, where eight smoldering statues of the bearded man portray him without legs, rising upward.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.body:
Ancient Dynasty
Claymen
Mohgwyn Dynasty
Putrescence (formerly)
Putrescent Knight (formerly)
Sanguine Nobles
Sanguine Albinaurics

sections.body:
Cerulean Coast
Lake of Rot

Mohgwyn Palace

Stone Coffins
Stone Coffin Fissure

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Some Ancient Dynasty stelae depict him tending tall trees.
Rugs and folding screens in Leyndell, Royal Capital depict clones of the bearded elder growing like fruit on a tree, suggesting a link between the Ancient Dynasty and the Golden Lineage. It also indicates that the statues may not all depict the same individual.
He may be related to the Suppressing Pillar because of its similarity to ancient dynasty architecture.
His context connects him to various outer gods, including Death, Night, the Fell God of Fire, the Formless Mother, and even the Greater Will.
He has only one eye, but plenty of facial hair, similar to the Fell God.
His likeness seemingly appears with and without the hood on the Winged Scythe, linking him to Ancient Death. This weapon symbolizes white-winged maidens, who are said to be Death's gentle envoys.
The Putrescent Knight's head seems to contain starlight.
Mohg, whose Omen blood was aflame by the Formless Mother, seeks to establish a Mohgwyn Dynasty within the Ancient Dynastic ruins. 
After the crusade ravaged the hornsent, they found the Formless Mother in the shadow of their ancestor, and transformed into Bloodfiends. Some sought out eternal rest from St. Trina in the Stone Coffin Fissure.
He may be related to Metyr, Mother of Fingers, who once communed with the Greater Will through her bubble-like microcosm, as Claymen Sorceries produce Magic bubbles within which oracles were once found, and Oracle Envoys use holy bubbles to herald the arrival of a new god. Maris, Fathom of Night, also known as the Augur and "master of bubbles," is another likely candidate.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The discarded tablet texture is sourced from the Babylonian Map of the World (also known as the Imago Mundi or Mappa mundi)—the earliest known world map—which depicts ancient Mesopotamia, often dubbed the “cradle of civilization,” as a sun or star-shaped region with two major rivers.
Both tablets display a tree on one face, and a map on the other, but their reverse sides are not visible in regular play; they most likely share textures for performance and storage efficiency.
The Bearded Elder shares many traits with Odin, the All-Father from Norse mythology. Most notably are his association with trees, missing right eye, and role as a psychopomp.
The figure and his paired tablets also allude to Moses, who received two stone tablets inscribed by the Finger of God. His appearance on stone coffins also likens him to Noah because "Noah's Ark" are their filenames.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Knight Bernahl's nameless Finger Maiden threw herself into the Forge of the Giants. According to unused concept she had detailed appearance and failed to become a kindling maiden. In full release, she only be mentioned in Beast Champion Set’s description and her ritual is presumed successful, considering that Bernahl's golden summon sign in the Crumbling Farum Azula requires no prerequisites.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Her presumed charred remains kneel in Dejection at the Shack of the Lofty on the Mountaintops of the Giants. Looting them grants the Traveling Maiden Hood, Traveling Maiden Robe, Traveling Maiden Gloves, and Traveling Maiden Boots. This finger maiden is also suspected of being Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood‘s maiden.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
An NPC version of Bernahl's Finger Maiden was planned for the Smoldering Church in Caelid, but was ultimately scrapped prior to the and may no longer be canonical.
Only her face data, equipped armor, initial location, and Japanese dialogue subtitles made it into the game; information about this version of her character is based on an unofficial translation of the Japanese script and may contain inaccuracies. An official English source text has yet to emerge or does not exist.
She wore the Bloodsoaked Mask, Finger Maiden Robe (Altered), Traveling Maiden Gloves, and Traveling Maiden Boots. She was bald with golden eyes and burns covering her face.
She asked to be burned with various flames to become a Kindling Maiden, but was ultimately unfit. The Giants' Flame would not find purchase within her in the way it does Melina, whose story she paralleled.
This NPC was replaced with Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater, a false Finger Maiden who invades at the Smoldering Church. Anastasia also invades near the Volcano Manor, which was where Bernahl went after his maiden perished.
Bernahl's Finger Maiden described the Fire Monks as giant.

description: Black Blade is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Trade the Remembrance of the Black Blade, dropped by Maliketh, the Black Blade, with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Summons a red, spectral version of Maliketh's Black Blade, then jumps and spins forwards with the blade to hit for Holy Attack Power equal to 225% of Incantation Scaling while also sending out a wave with Holy Attack Power equal to 162% of Incantation Scaling. 

If the incantation is used again immediately afterwards, the second sword's Attack Power is increased to 232% of Incantation Scaling while the beam's Attack Power is increased to 169% of Incantation Scaling for the second cast.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 44 points of Stamina to perform, with the follow-up costing the same amount of Stamina for a total of 88 points of Stamina if both parts are used. 
The sword part deals 9 Stance damage and the beam part deals 4 Stance damage. 
Both the sword itself and the wave it sends out can hit the same target at melee range, meaning that the first cast effectively can have Attack Power roughly equal to 387% of Incantation Scaling while the follow-up cast can have Attack Power equal to 401% of Incantation Scaling. 
The beam attack applies two debuffs: the first deals damage equal to 0.1% of the target's maximum HP + 1 every 0.1 seconds for 2 seconds (total damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20) while the second debuff lowers the target's maximum HP by 10% for 15 seconds, signified by a part of their health bar being blocked out with grey. 
The debuff that lowers maximum HP doesn't stack with the Maliketh's Black Blade's skill Destined Death similar debuff, but it does stack with the one inflicted by the Black Knife's skill Blade of Death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.08 fixed a bug that prevented the follow-up attack from occurring when the Black Sword Incantation was activated with a Sacred Seal in the left hand.
Black Blade is incorrectly referred to as Black Sword in this patch note. 
Patch 1.07.1 the incantation Black Blade is currently missing its follow up attack when cast from the left hand. This issue will be corrected in a future update.
The issue was fixed with Patch 1.08. 
Patch 1.07 reduced stamina consumption, improved turning performance and shortened recovery time, the sword and the wave attack have been changed so that they hit at the same time. Attack power, stamina attack power, and poise damage of each part have been decreased, decreased the number of times the wave part hits large enemies.
Prior to this only either the sword attack or the beam attack could hit an enemy. 
The Attack Power of the first sword and beam was decreased from 290% of Incantation Scaling and 252% of Incantation Scaling to 225% and 162% of the same respectively, and the Attack Power of the follow-up sword and beam was decreased from 297% of Incantation Scaling and 260% of Incantation Scaling to 232% and 169% of the same respectively. 
The Stamina damage to guarding opponents for the first sword and beam was decreased from 190 and 150 to 145 and 115 respectively, and the same for the follow-up sword and beam was decreased from 220 and 150 to 160 and 125 respectively. 
The Stamina damage to guarding players was split from the PvE values and increased at the same time, going to 181 and 143 for the first sword and beam, and to 200 and 156 for the follow-up sword and beam. 
The Stance damage of sword attacks and beam attacks were decreased from 10 and 7 to 9 and 4 respectively. The Poise damage of sword attacks and beam attacks meanwhile was actually increased, not decreased, going from 100 and 70 to 243 and 108 respectively. 
Patch 1.04 decreased Stamina consumption and decreased recovery time.

Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 23%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 41%. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Godslayer's Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
An very strong yet simple spell due to a combination of fast casting speed and percentage-based damage. 
Since it deals at least 2% of a target's health per cast it can kill anything damageable in 50 casts, though most often much quicker due to the Fire damage it also deals. 
All bosses in are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Quickly sheathe the right-hand weapon with Blackflame, granting Fire Attack Power equal to 85% of the seal's Faith-based Incantation Scaling and inflicting an effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds. 

Lasts for 7 seconds and counts as a Weapon Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 10 points of Stamina to cast. 
Despite being one of the Godslayer Incantations, this spell, like other spell-based weapon buffs, does not get bonus damage from its associated seal (the Godslayer's Seal for this one).
Can have its extremely short duration extended by 30% by the Old Lord's Talisman, to 9.1 seconds. 
The Blackflame effect is also applied to target's hit by Skills of the buffed weapon, even if those skills don't involve the weapon, such as with Skill: Thunderbolt or Skill: Flame of the Redmanes. 
Casts considerably quicker if used immediately after a roll, jump, or attack, or when sprinting, letting the user get more out of its short duration. 
The additional damage from the Blackflame effect will at most be 9% of target's maximum HP + 90 (11.1% + 110 if the Old Lord's Talisman is used). Practically though, the bonus damage will probably be around 5% + 50, presuming the user is able to keep on the offense. 
It's important to note that the duration of Blackflame effects doesn't stack, instead the duration is reset if another hit is landed during an ongoing burn. 
Due to the extremely short duration of this buff, it's important to keep on the offensive if possible after casting the spell. 
Should ideally be cast just before an opening in a boss's attacks happens. 
Outmatched in added Fire Attack Power (i.e. not counting the added Blackflame effect) by Drawstring Fire Grease below 170 Incantation Scaling and by Drawstring Messmerfire Grease below 208 Incantation Scaling. 
Note that both of these consumable items last considerably longer than Black Flame Blade, even if the Old Lord's Talisman is equipped. More specifically, Drawstring Fire Grease lasts for 10 seconds and Drawstring Messmerfire Grease lasts for 25 seconds. 
Can be used with a quick weapon such as the Dagger, even if it's unupgraded, to deal heavy damage to high-health bosses. 
All bosses in are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Uses the same casting animation as Drawstring Greases, and also share their very short duration (though Black Flame Blade's duration is shorter than even theirs).
