The ring can hit an enemy up to 4 times, effectively granting it Attack Power equal to 424% of Incantation Scaling (436% if charged), not accounting for flat defence, and dealing additional damage equal to 5% of target's maximum HP + 20 (since hitting with a new Blackflame effect will just reset the duration of the debuff). 
This makes the incantation surprisingly usable for attacking, at least against large opponents such as Trolls, since enemies can be tricked into standing inside of the flames. 
An older instance of Black Flame Ritual isn't removed when a new is cast, though their damage won't stack as efficiently against opponents compared to when their casts are more separated. 
Significantly harder to use against other players, being primarily useful for forcing them to stay away from the caster or to obscure the caster's other attacks. Be wary of opponent's jumping over the flames or simply running through them, as well as the fact that the charged version's pillars being further out means it's possible to stand close to the caster without being damaged. 
All bosses in are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Physical damage taken by 35% (15% in PvP) while also decreasing all healing received by 20% for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 30 FP per cast.
Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces Physical damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where PhysicalFortification represents the effect magnitude:
TotalPhysicalReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {PhysicalDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {PhysicalFortification}) )
For example, if physical damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
PhysicalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 36.25%:
TotalPhysicalReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.15) ) = 36.25%

Strategies:
The reduction in healing effective lowers the effectiveness of this spell to only lowering Physical damage taken by 18.75% (and increasing the effective damage taken in PvP by 6.25%), assuming that healing will be used and not accounting for it helping the player survive hits that otherwise would have killed them. 
Effectively still has its full PvP strength of 15% in no-healing scenarios such as semi-formal duels in the open world or via a Duelist's Furled Finger, and the Duel Arena Combat mode available through the Royal Colosseum in Leyndell, Royal Capital or via Roundtable Hold. 
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as physical damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple physical negation sources.
This incantation is valuable whenever available since the vast majority of areas will have most of the damage inflicted by enemies as various types of Physical damage. The biggest exception is Liurnia of the Lakes, where Magic damage shares the spotlight. 
Black Flame's Protection offers greater physical protection than Boiled Crab (35% vs. 20%) and has a slightly longer duration (70 vs. 60 seconds). This spell requires 30 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 30 FP to cast, while the Crab only requires 600 Runes per piece bought.
The Boiled Crab is preferable for PvP encounters, as Black Flame's Protection's effect is reduced to 15%. 
Though Boiled Crab (and the slightly weaker Boiled Prawn) are potentially accessible much earlier, it's possible to not gain access to them should Blackguard Big Boggart be killed before any of either has been bought from him. 
The reduction in healing for the Flask of Crimson Tears specifically can be countered with either the Crimson Seed Talisman or Crimson Seed Talisman +1, setting healing effectiveness to 96% and 104% respectively. 
Note that this only helps with the flask, as the Heal spells are not affected by either talisman but is affected by the healing reduction.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Scions of the Eternal Cities, the Black Knife Assassins were a group of women with close ties to Queen Marika the Eternal. Led by Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader, they were coconspirators of Ranni the Witch, who robbed the Rune of Death from Maliketh, the Black Blade. She imbued it into Blades of Calling, fashioning a set of god-slaying Black Knives. The Assassins carried out the Night of Black Knives, carving Cursemarks of Death into Ranni and Godwyn the Golden. They wore silent, silver scale armor and used Concealing Veils to mask their presence, rendering them effectively invisible.

Presently, they are scattered throughout the Lands Between, and can be found in many different regions.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
Twenty Black Knife Assassins appear in Elden Ring.
x2 Malefactor's Evergaol (Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader and Black Knife Tiche)

x1 Sainted Hero's Grave
x1 Black Knife Catacombs

x4 Ordina, Liturgical Town (spectral, inside evergaol)
x3 Kingsrealm Ruins (slain by War Counselor Iji during his quest)
x4 Ranni's Rise (slain by Blaidd the Half-Wolf during his quest)
At least four Assassins appear around Limveld in. Two stalk the streets of Noklateo, the Shrouded City, one roams near the easternmost evergaol, and another acts as the central castle boss.

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.body:
Deathtouched Catacombs=

Background:
This assassin sustained a grievous wound, retreating deep within the Deathtouched Catacombs. Uniquely, her health bar has already been partially depleted before the player arrives so that she starts at 60% HP. She is the only wounded Black Knife Assassin. Although red blood stains her armor, she bleeds darkness on hit.

She drops the Assassin's Crimson Dagger, a Talisman which allows the player to recover HP after performing a critical hit.

Black Knife Catacombs=

Background:
An assassin hiding in a small chapel within the Catacombs, concealed behind an illusory wall. As well as dropping the Assassin's Cerulean Dagger, which allows the player to recover FP from critical hits, she also leaves behind a Black Knifeprint, which can be given to Sorcerer Rogier to progress his questline.

D, Hunter of the Dead can be summoned for this fight.

Sage's Cave=

Background:
This assassin is invisible, save for the ripples she makes in the water in her boss room. Using the Sentry's Torch will render her visible.

Sainted Hero's Grave=

Background:
A Black Knife Assassin blocks the entrance to the Sainted Hero's Grave, located in central Altus Plateau. 

Alecto, Black Knife Ringleader=

Background:

The ringleader of the Black Knife Assassins is currently imprisoned in an Evergaol in the Moonlight Altar area of Liurnia of the Lakes. Tiche, Alecto's daughter, died protecting her mother during their flight from the Capital after the assassination of Godwyn.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Black Knife Assassin enemies are unmarked bosses that do not respawn once defeated.
Their bodies are invisible.
They float when they backstep, as if manipulated by unseen strings.
Melina uses the Black Knife Assassin model and animations, noticeable when summoned as a cooperator against Morgott, the Omen King. She wields the Blade of Calling, and may cast Minor Erdtree and Miranda's Prayer.
Black Knife Assassins have immunity to all Status Effects except Frostbite, corroborating Destined Death's vulnerability to the Eclipse.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The black moon of Nokstella once hung above the Eternal City, guiding countless stars. It possessed potent magic, earning the reverence of the Nox. 

At some point the black moon was lost and its fragments ended up scattered across the Lands Between. These Memory Stones were coveted by glintstone sorcerers, who crafted them into necklaces to enhance their magical prowess and mental capability.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The moon of Nokstella was immortalized in a legendary talisman. This blue silver artifact depicts the beguiling black moon encircled by four blue jewels, each one forming a crescent at a cardinal direction. A sequence of eight secondary gemstones separates the darker primary gems. 
Two Cuckoo birds crowns the symbolic lunar cycle, implying the Academy of Raya Lucaria's hands in the crafting of the talisman.
The black moon may be related to the Eternal Darkness spell of Sellia, Town of Sorcery.
It is possible the large hole in Nokstella's ceiling was once filled by the black moon.

description: Blackflame, also known as, is a type of flame in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Blackflame was weighty, alluring fire conjured by Godslayer incantations. Drawn from faith and the power of the Rune of Death, its black-and-white flames could burn away the very gods in ancient times.

Following the War Against the Giants, the beguiling blackflame enthralled Amon and other Fire Monks loyal to the Giants' Flame. Those who fled their duties formed the Blackflame Monks, aligning themselves with the Empyrean Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Godskin Apostles. Together, they launched a violent god hunt, during which the black flame was their armor within. However, Queen Marika commanded her Shadowbound Beast and half-brother, Maliketh, to defeat the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles. She removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it in his black blade. The Golden Order was born, and the true power of the black flame was lost.

sections.heading: Users of Blackflame
sections.body:
Blackflame Guilty
Blackflame Monks
Blackflame Monk Amon
Gloam-Eyed Queen
Godskin Apostles
Godskin Nobles
Vargram the Raging Wolf

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
All offensive Black Flame attacks deal Fire damage and apply a special effect that inflicts additional damage equal to 20 + 2.0% of the target's maximum HP over 2 seconds.
The effect does not stack, though further hits refresh its 2-second timer.
All bosses in the Realm of Shadow resist this percentage-based damage, taking only 10 + 1.0% of their maximum HP over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler (Base Serpent Messmer), Bayle the Dread, and Promised Consort Radahn (Radahn, Consort of Miquella) take even less: 7 + 0.7% of their maximum HP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen channeled Black Flames through her Godslayer's Greatsword.
The flames of Destined Death are red, indicating blackflame may be drained of its former color. That said, the Blackflame Monk's Seal is a colorless Giant's Seal and other Godskin paraphernalia likewise reflect the current color of blackflame.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Liurnia of the Lakes (Boilprawn Shack)
Head north-west from the Site of Grace to find Rya the Scout inside a gazebo and talk to her.
Move to north-west again from here to find Blackguard Big Boggart at the Boilprawn Shack and talk to him: select Give me the necklace and then Deal to be able to buy Rya's Necklace from him for 1000 Runes.
After purchasing the item, he'll start selling an infinite supply of Boiled Prawns. Purchase at least one to progress his questline: you'll receive the "Spread Out" gesture and, in turn, Boggart's summon sign will appear at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook to aid you against Magma Wyrm Makar.
Altus Plateau
After resting at a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, Boggart will move to the outer moat along the northern wall of Leyndell, Royal Capital in the Capital Outskirts (due west from the Capital Rampart Site of Grace).
You may now purchase an infinite supply of Boiled Crabs.
Exhaust Boggart's dialogue about Dung Eater. After freeing Dung Eater from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning Grounds, Boggart will have some additional dialogue.
Altus Plateau
After hearing Boggart's final piece of dialogue about Dung Eater, warning you that Dung Eater is lurking nearby, reload the area to find Boggart bound to a chair. Speak to him to trigger an invasion from Dung Eater.
Defeat Dung Eater and return to Boggart, who is now dead. Loot his equipment, as well as the Seedbed Curse.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Forbidden Lands
Hidden within a room that you can only reach during the elevator ride that leads down to the Forbidden Lands grace, alongside the Official's Attire. 

Jump from the southwestern part of the elevator to a doorway just above the bottom floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While its Faith-scaling is technically the strongest its Dexterity-scaling is effectively almost equal to it because the dagger's Physical base Attack Power is higher than its Holy base Attack Power. 
An equal split between Dexterity and Faith will give the most Attack Power (AP), though a pure Dexterity build or a pure Faith build will get only about 5% less AP. 
Since the skill scales with weapon upgrade level and Faith but not Dexterity or Strength, it can be beneficial to lean into the pure Faith build, or even a 45/45 or 30/60 Dex/Fth split. 
A pure Faith (80) build gives 1138 Holy Attack Power, 13% more Attack Power on the skill than hybrid Dexterity/Faith (45/45) build's 1010 Holy Attack Power and 5.5% more Attack Power than the skill of a Faith-leaning Dexterity/Faith (30/60) build's 1079 Holy Attack Power. 
Unfortunately generally outclassed by the Black Knife. While this weapon is 0.5 units lighter, has better scaling, and its skill deals more outright damage at a lower FP cost, the Black Knife will always have more AP due to higher base Attack Power, is attainable much earlier in the game, and the skill is often more damaging due to part of its damage being percentage-based. 
Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword. 
This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2 due to hitting twice.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base Attack Power while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base Attack Power: red for Fire Attack Power, yellow for Lightning Attack Power, orange for Holy Attack Power, and cyan for Magic Attack Power. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This dagger belonged to Melina. Curiously, another copy is wielded by Polyanna, one of Millicent's Sisters. 
The cost of the skill was reduced from 20 FP to 17 FP at an unknown point as an unlisted change.

name: Blaidd the Half-Wolf
description: Blaidd the Half-Wolf is an NPC character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A guarded and boorish yet fiercely loyal half-wolf, Blaidd was a shadowbound beast, created by the Two Fingers to serve Lunar Princess Ranni when she was chosen as an Empyrean. The wolf was the beast of the Carian royal covenant and irrefutably symbolized the moon's pride, and so he was approved and raised by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon as Ranni's stepbrother. 

Blaidd was Ranni's unwavering blade. Like all shadowbound beasts, he could not truly die and was incapable of treachery against his master, compelled to enact her will. Unbeknownst to him, however, an accursed failsafe within shadows overrode this directive should their master turn against the Two Fingers; should Ranni rebel against her prescribed fate, Blaidd’s unwavering loyalty would twist into madness, becoming a Baleful Shadow—a dire threat to Ranni herself.

When Blaidd swore an oath to serve no master other than Ranni the Witch and her Dark Moon, a cold frost magic graced his Royal Greatsword. The cold bothered him, nonetheless.

Game Events:
Blaidd searched the Mistwood Ruins for a traitor named Darriwil, and the passage to Nokron, Eternal City, a long-lost ruin said to be banished underground by the Greater Will. He travels to Redmane Castle to participate in the Radahn Festival.

sections.heading: Blaidd's Quest
sections.body:
Quest Items:

Questline Progression:
Limgrave (Mistwood Ruins)
Blaidd can be heard howling in Mistwood. After hearing the howl, speak to Merchant Kalé and select "About the howling in Mistwood." This will unlock the "Finger Snap" gesture.
Use Finger Snap at the Mistwood Ruins near the ruined tower adjacent to the slumbering Runebear to cause Blaidd to jump down. Talk to him and exhaust his dialogue.
Limgrave (Forlorn Hound Evergaol)
Enter the Forlorn Hound Evergaol in Limgrave and defeat Bloodhound Knight Darriwil. Blaidd will be available as a summonable cooperator during this fight.
After defeating Darriwil, Blaidd appears outside the Forlorn Hound Evergaol. Speak with him to earn a [[Somber Smithing Stone 2|Somber Smithing Stone [2]]].
Liurnia of the Lakes (Ranni's Rise)
After entering Ranni's service, a projection of Blaidd appears in Ranni's Rise and offers dialogue. This step is skipped if Starscourge Radahn has already been defeated.
Siofra River
Blaidd moves to the base of an enormous ruined bridge on the bank of the Siofra River, located between the Siofra River Bank and Worshipper's Woods Sites of Grace. He will suggest asking Preceptor Seluvis about how to reach Nokron, Eternal City. This step is skipped if Starscourge Radahn has already been defeated.
(Optional) After speaking to Seluvis about Nokron and then speaking to Sorceress Sellen, return to Blaidd and exhaust his dialogue. He will move to Redmane Castle afterwards.
Caelid (Redmane Castle)
Blaidd will appear in the Redmane Castle Plaza when the Radahn Festival begins. He also appears as an optional summon in the fight against Starscourge Radahn.
Caelid (Wailing Dunes)
(Optional) After defeating Radahn, speak to Blaidd next to the Starscourge Radahn Site of Grace. He will mark the location of the Starfall Crater—entrance to Nokron, Eternal City—on your map.
Limgrave (Forlorn Hound Evergaol)
(Optional) Interact with the Forlorn Hound Evergaol to speak to Blaidd. Either choose to release him or leave him.
Liurnia of the Lakes (Three Sisters)
After giving Ranni the Dark Moon Ring, Blaidd will appear as a hostile NPC outside Ranni's Rise, surrounded by the bodies of slain Black Knife Assassins. Defeat him to receive his armor and weapon.
Liurnia of the Lakes (Kingsrealm Ruins)
(Optional) Speak to War Counselor Iji to deliver the news of Blaidd's death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Wields the Royal Greatsword and wears Blaidd's Armor, Blaidd's Gauntlets, and Blaidd's Greaves.
Similar to the Beast Eye, Blaidd’s eyes are violet. His left eye is partially shut.
Blaidd revives himself if killed prematurely because he is a Shadowbound Beast; however, he remains hostile until the player uses Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows. 
Blaidd is friends with Merchant Kalé.
Blaidd rarely interacted with Tarnished before meeting the player.
During Ranni’s questline, the Tarnished confronts a Baleful Shadow in Nokstella, Eternal City, one of the assassins dispatched by the Two Fingers. This shadow takes Blaidd’s form, though it is not actually him.
Blaidd kills several Black Knife Assassins during an offscreen ambush at the Three Sisters, which triggers when the player gives Ranni the Dark Moon Ring.
Baleful Shadows sent after Ranni assume Blaidd's form and appearance.
A corpse near Ranni's Rise holds a Black Wolf Mask, nearly identical to Blaidd’s head. The mask likely belonged to an assassin who attempted to approach Ranni by impersonating Blaidd.
The eyes of the Black Wolf Mask differ from Blaidd’s: the right is silver or white with a large golden splotch (alternatively, gold and partially drained of color), while the left is shut.

sections.body:

The name Blaidd is Welsh for "Wolf."
The Black Wolf Mask was known as Blaidd's Lupine Visage in.

Costs 30 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to equip.

description: The was an unseen character mentioned in.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Blind Swordsman invented the Guard Counter technique, the art of allowing one's opponent to strike to leave them vulnerable to a well-timed reply.
The Prosthesis-Wearer Heirloom depicts the Blind Swordsman clasping left hands with Malenia; both figures wear prosthetic right arms.
Wore the Blue Cloth Set, which is used by the Warrior starting origin. This armor set bears a striking resemblance to the Blue Dancer Charm fairy.
The blue color of the set symbolizes brisk waters, emphasizing flow, and stresses the need to remain ever drifting. As such, the Blind Swordsman may be related to the nomadic warriors who wear the Blue Cloth set.
The hero's Flowing Curved Sword is housed within a Great Coffin in the Consecrated Snowfield. 
The Blue Dancer Charm and Shamshir are found among ancient ruins in Highroad Cave.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The fairy that bestowed the flowing sword on the blind swordsman is sometimes speculated to have been the spirit of the Siofra River, 'Síofra' being an Irish name meaning "elf" or "changeling," derived from síobhra, the older Gaelic word for "elf" or "fairy".

name: Bloodhound Knight Floh

description: Bloodhound Knight Floh is a spirit ash in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Defeat the Red Wolf of the Champion boss in Gelmir Hero's Grave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts. 
Summons a Bloodhound Knight with a curved greatsword and claws. 
Deals Slash damage and inflicts slight Blood Loss build-up with both weapons. 
As a red-eye Spirit Ash, this knight will remain at the spot where they are summoned and pursue any encroaching enemies aggressively. Quite fitting for the masterless knight known as the Rabid Stray. 
Like other, hostile Bloodhound Knights, Floh is quite fragile and reliant on being able to chain staggers and Blood Loss to burst down foes without being killed. Due to this, Floh is best used by a build that can keep attention away from them and that can take advantage of the additional Blood Loss build-up to more easily cause the status themself.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The name Floh seems to stem from the name of the prehistoric Floian period, a trait shared with Bloodhound Knight Darriwil, who in turn seems to be named for the Darriwilian period. 
The only other enemy with this etymological origin are the three named Crucible Knights: Ordovis, Siluria, Devonia.
Crucible Knight Floh was the boss of the Erdtree-Gazing Evergaol in early development. This location was renamed Forlorn Hound Evergaol and now contains Bloodhound Knight Darriwil.

The "Rabid Stray" seeking a lord of true caliber may reference the ancient Greek philosopher Diogenes the Cynic—known for his futile search for a wise (honest) man and later dismissal of Alexander the Great, the most powerful man in the world.
Diogenes was nicknamed a “barking dog” for his Cynic philosophy and austere lifestyle. Some accounts claim he died from a dog bite.
"At the approach of so many people, Diogenes sat up a little and fixed his eyes on Alexander. When the king greeted him and asked if there was anything he wanted, Diogenes replied, 'Yes, that you should stand a little out of my sun'. It is said that Alexander was so impressed by this—and by the arrogance and grandeur of spirit of a man who could treat him with such disdain—that he said to his courtiers, who were laughing and joking about the philosopher as they walked away, 'But I'll tell you this: if I were not Alexander, I would be Diogenes!'" — Plutarch, Alexander, XIV

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
2% drop rate from Fierce Demi-Humans aka Demi-Human Chiefs. 
One can point asleep next to the bridge west of the South of the Lookout Tower Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Strong Strength- and Arcane-scaling. 
Surpasses all daggers except the rather unusual Wakizashi for raw damage on a Heavy affinity and has the highest Strength-scaling of them all, just short of an S-rating. 
Second or third strongest dagger on the Occult affinity, though it will only slightly outmatch the Reduvia (only by 1 point) and the latter will have more Blood Loss build-up. 
Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
Despite this its Heavy affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy). 
The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult). 
While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage. 
The only dagger with a Strength focus on its Cold affinity instead of a Dexterity focus.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.body:
Quest Items:

Questline Progression:

(Optional) Limgrave
The following two steps can be completed in either order. His dialogue will vary depending on where he is met first.
Yura can be found under a fallen Azula ruin near the Seaside Ruins site of grace, southwest of Agheel Lake. Exhaust his dialogue and his summon sign will appear in Agheel Lake to assist against Flying Dragon Agheel. Speak to him again after defeating Agheel for further dialogue.
Enter the Murkwater River, the ravine north of Agheel Lake, and head towards Murkwater Cave. Bloody Finger Nerijus will invade you. After fighting Nerijus for a while, Yura appears to assist you. After defeating Nerijus, continue along the ravine to find Yura under a bridge. Exhaust his dialogue. 
Liurnia of the Lakes
A red summon sign can be found northeast of the Raya Lucaria Main Gate. Interact with it to assist Yura in defeating Bloody Finger Ravenmount Assassin. After defeating the foe, Yura can be found on the bridge near where the summon sign was. Speak to him to receive a [[Smithing Stone 5|Smithing Stone [5]]].
Altus Plateau
Travel to the Second Church of Marika, located northwest of the Altus Highway Junction site of grace, where Yura lies on the ground. Speak to him, and then pick up the Nagakiba. Shortly after, Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger will invade. Defeat her to receive Eleonora's Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear.
Mountaintops of the Giants
Once you travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, Yura's quest will be locked regardless of which steps have been completed. Shabriri will be waiting near the Zamor Ruins site of grace, in possession of Yura's reanimated body. The Nagakiba can be found on the ground in whichever location he would have been at, depending on how far into his questline you have progressed.

Yura can be found under a fallen Azula ruin near the Seaside Ruins site of grace, southwest of Agheel Lake. Exhaust his dialogue and his summon sign will appear in Agheel Lake to assist against Flying Dragon Agheel. Speak to him again after defeating Agheel for further dialogue.

Enter the Murkwater River, the ravine north of Agheel Lake, and head towards Murkwater Cave. Bloody Finger Nerijus will invade you. After fighting Nerijus for a while, Yura appears to assist you. After defeating Nerijus, continue along the ravine to find Yura under a bridge. Exhaust his dialogue.
Liurnia of the Lakes

A red summon sign can be found northeast of the Raya Lucaria Main Gate. Interact with it to assist Yura in defeating Bloody Finger Ravenmount Assassin. After defeating the foe, Yura can be found on the bridge near where the summon sign was. Speak to him to receive a [[Smithing Stone 5|Smithing Stone [5]]].
Altus Plateau

Travel to the Second Church of Marika, located northwest of the Altus Highway Junction site of grace, where Yura lies on the ground. Speak to him, and then pick up the Nagakiba. Shortly after, Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger will invade. Defeat her to receive Eleonora's Poleblade and the Purifying Crystal Tear.
Mountaintops of the Giants

Once you travel to the Mountaintops of the Giants, Yura's quest will be locked regardless of which steps have been completed. Shabriri will be waiting near the Zamor Ruins site of grace, in possession of Yura's reanimated body. The Nagakiba can be found on the ground in whichever location he would have been at, depending on how far into his questline you have progressed.

name: Bloody Finger Nerijus
description: Bloody Finger Nerijus is a mini-boss NPC invader in.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.body:
Nerijus will spawn in Limgrave along the riverbed beneath the bridge where the Night's Cavalry spawns at night, just as one nears the Murkwater Cave entrance. Like other NPC invaders, when he arrives, the Tarnished will be unable to use Torrent, leave the immediate vicinity, or enter the cave. He'll spawn at the far end of the riverbed and start running towards the player.

It's recommended to either clear out all Those Who Live in Death near the bridge before spawning Nerijus, as they can be a nuisance while fighting him, You can also avoid them by keeping to the other end of the riverbed, closer to where Nerijus spawns in.

Nerijus is aggressive and armed with a pair of Reduvia daggers that give him a mix of quick ranged and melee attacks that all inflict bleed buildup. However, he is fairly easy to knock around with a two-handed or heavy weapon; his poise is low due to his light armor set. If needing assistance, run back towards the bridge area to buy some time for Bloody Finger Hunter Yura to spawn in, who'll help assist in fighting Nerijus, though he can still be killed by Nerijus. The two of you together can keep him stunlocked with ease.

name: Boc's Mother
image: ER Icon Tool Prattling Pate You're Beautiful.png
description: Boc's mother or Mum was an unseen character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Boc's mother was a highly skilled demi-human seamstress whose dedication to her craft left a lasting impact on her son. Her ability to create garments from scratch surpassed even the royal seamsters of the Erdtree capital. Among the sewing tools Boc inherited, her curved needle—shaped like a fang—stood out as a cherished symbol of her craft and the deep bond they shared. She taught him the art of tailoring, inspiring his deep desire to follow in her footsteps.

Though Boc struggled with his appearance, his mother was the only one who called him beautiful, giving him a sense of self-worth that he clung to throughout his life. Her memory drove him to perfect his skills, always striving to live up to the talent and kindness she embodied.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: Boc's mother was a demi-human with deft hands. Her compassionate voice was recorded by a Prattling Pate, which can be found in the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Her unconditional affection for Boc was immortalized in the wistful Prattling Pate, which captured her tender words: "You're beautiful."
Boc's mother was likely a member of nobility. She possessed specific knowledge of the royal seamsters, who repaired the clothes of the demigods.
The lattice ornamentation featured on her sewing needle is identical to the stitching on the Mask of Confidence. Both designs are simplified version of the trellis of Radagon's Rune, and the seals on the Academy of Raya Lucaria gates and the Erdtree itself. The lattice design represents the threaded needlework both characters are known for.
Boc later trades in his mother's needle for the golden sewing needle once owned by Radagon of the Golden Order.

name: Boc the Seamster
description:
Boc the Seamster or Demi-Human Boc is an NPC in. He offers the player the ability to modify their garments, free of charge.

Overview:
Boc is a demi-human seamster from Limgrave. He was very close to his mother, a seamstress, until her passing. Inspired by her, Boc aspired to follow in her footsteps and inherited her sewing kit. He lived with a demi-human tribe in a Coastal Cave on the western coast of Limgrave, but at some point, he was cast out by his kin. Lost and isolated, Boc was transformed into a bush by a spell.

A Tarnished came across Boc and broke the spell, freeing him. Grateful, Boc offered to sneak back into the cave where he had been exiled to retrieve something precious with which to repay his champion. However, his former tribe discovered him and beat him mercilessly. When the champion found Boc again, he warned them not to enter the cave. Ignoring his warning, the champion avenged Boc and recovered his mother's cherished sewing needle. Moved by their kindness, Boc vowed to become a seamster like his mother.

Boc next encounters the champion in Liurnia of the Lakes, where he humbly offers his services as the champion's personal seamster. He will trace the champion's footsteps, following them to the Altus Plateau and the Royal Capital. Boc remains in awe of his master, and as the Tarnished champion draws closer to the throne of the Elden Lord, Boc will begin to refer to them as a lord. 

Even though Boc is given a golden needle worthy of a master seamster, allowing him to perform modifications to the grab of the demigods themselves, Boc remains terribly self-conscious and bothered by his appearance. He asks his master whether they think he is ugly and expresses an interest in being reborn by Queen Rennala. Should the Tarnished champion aid Boc in fulfilling his wish to be reborn, Boc will travel to the Academy of Raya Lucaria and will be reborn a human through her powers. However, like many of those reborn by Rennala, the process goes awry, and Boc dies shortly thereafter.

Instead, the Tarnished champion may find a Prattling Pate which speaks with the voice of Boc's deceased mother, and tells him he's beautiful. Upon hearing this, Boc will be contented and will continue faithfully serving his lord.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Limgrave
Boc can be found in the form of a small tree near Gatefront Ruins. He will call out until you attack or roll into the tree, reversing the illusion and causing him to transform back.

(Optional) Boc will ask if he can call you Lord at this point if he has already been given the Gold Sewing Needle. Agreeing will unlock the "My Lord" gesture.
Leyndell, Royal Capital (East Capital Rampart)
If Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon has been defeated, Boc will ask for a Larval Tear.
Giving him a Larval Tear will move him to Raya Lucaria Grand Library. He will appear kneeling on the ground in human form, unresponsive. Upon reloading the area, he will be dead.
Refusing to give him a Larval Tear will unlock the dialogue option "What do you really think?". Selecting this option will cause him to die just outside Raya Lucaria Grand Library.
Instead of selecting either option, using Prattling Pate "You're Beautiful" in front of him will prevent him from dying. He will remain at East Capital Rampart for the rest of the game.

description: Bols, Carian Knight is an optional boss in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: A hulking troll knight clad in heavy armor and wielding a massive greatsword, Bols was one of the Trolls called into service by the Carians, fighting as a true enchanted knight alongside human comrades. Bols was imprisoned within the Cuckoo's Evergaol in western Liurnia of the Lakes by the Knights of the Cuckoo during the Liurnian Civil War.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: A towering troll knight with slow, sweeping greatsword attacks that create shockwaves. His size makes it easy to pass between his legs and circle to his back. He can summon Greatblade Phalanx blades overhead.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Cuckoo's Evergaol (Liurnia of the Lakes)

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body:
Greatblade Phalanx
184,600 Runes

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body: Bols, Carian Knight deals Standard damage, Slash damage, Pierce damage, and Magic damage.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
Use his size: dodge between his legs and stay on his back side.
Keep him in view; he can pivot quickly into a follow-up.
Stay close even for ranged builds; create distance only to reset spacing.
When he casts Greatblade Phalanx, sprint toward him so the blades pass overhead.
Shockwaves from slams fan out in front; positioning behind him mitigates most follow-ups.

| Stomp || Raises one leg and stomps repeatedly. Roll toward the leg that did not stomp and punish.
| Swing || Horizontal or vertical greatsword swings. Roll into horizontal; roll away from vertical.
| Arm Sweep || Low arm sweep along the ground. Roll into the arm.
| Arm Slam || One or both arms slam, producing a shockwave. Get behind him or jump the wave.
| Downward Stab || Drives the blade into the ground, large shockwave. Get behind him during the wind-up.
| Sword Wrench || Rips the sword free to his right after Downward Stab. Stay on his left.
| Kneeling Swing || Kneels and performs a wide counter-clockwise sweep. Roll toward the weapon.
| Mega Slam || Long hold overhead slam with huge shockwave. Safe spot is directly behind; or jump the wave.
| Jumping Slam || Leaps and lands with a shockwave. Roll on descent.

| Dragging Slash || Long wind-up dash dragging the blade, then slash and follow-ups ending in a slam. Slip between his legs or get behind him; luring him into the arena edge can stop and stun the charge.
| Greatblade Phalanx || Summons three blades above his head that fire after a delay. Run toward him so the blades overshoot; avoid pairing attempts since only one blade can be parried at a time.
| Roar || Shockwave roar that buffs his damage by 20% for ~15s. Get behind him if close; otherwise create distance.

name: Borealis's Mist
description: Borealis's Mist is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Dragon Communion: Caelid / Jagged Peak
Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of frozen mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 158% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 110 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. 474% of Incantation Scaling and 330 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonice. 
Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Dragonice, and Ghostflame Breath), this is the most expensive one, but it effectively combines the high Frostbite build-up of Dragonice with the higher Magic damage of Ghostflame Breath. 
Compared to Dragonice, this spell deals 17% more damage but also consumes 38% more FP. 
Compared to Ghostflame Breath, this spell deals 6% less damage and consumes 17% more FP but causes 100% more Frostbite build-up. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 168 FP: 2*48 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 91 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
This is the second weakest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 16% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath and 7% less damage than Agheel's Flame (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals only 2% more damage than Ekzykes's Decay. 
However, the Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

name: Borealis the Freezing Fog
description: Borealis the Freezing Fog is an optional Great Enemy boss in.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Borealis the Freezing Fog is located in the Mountaintops of the Giants, patrolling the frozen lake southeast of the Freezing Lake Site of Grace. The nearest Grace is Spiritcaller Cave.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body: Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will award one Dragon Heart, 100,000 Runes, and will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body:
Instead of flames, Borealis exhales Dragonice and Borealis's Mist.
Borealis inflicts Frostbite with his breath attacks and roars. His attacks include:
Frost Breath: Borealis exhales a cone of freezing fog, which lingers and applies Frostbite.
Frost Stomp: Stomps on the ground, creating a shockwave of ice that deals AoE damage and builds Frostbite.
Frost Wing Sweep: Swings his massive wings, releasing icy projectiles that track players in the area.
Roar: Releases a deafening roar that briefly staggers players and applies frost buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Borealis the Freezing Fog counts as a Dragon-type enemy and is vulnerable to anti-dragon effects.
Furled Fingers and Spirit Ashes are allowed in this encounter.
Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Borealis is the only ice dragon in the game.

Costs 9 FP per cast or recast.

This spell has a long range and can scale walls and other obstacles.
This spell will track and home in on its target.
This spell utilizes the Briars of Sin.

Boosting:
Alberich's Bracers, Alberich's Robe, Alberich's Pointed Hat, and Alberich's Pointed Hat (Altered) each boost the effectiveness by 6%, up to a maximum of 18%.
Staff of the Guilty boosts the Attack Power by 20%.

name: Briars of Sin
image: ER Render Shield of the Guilty.png
description: The Briars of Sin, also known as the thorns of sin and the thorns of punishment, are supernatural vines in.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
The Briars of Sin are creeping, thorned vines that draw blood by impaling sinners from below or by squeezing them in their tight embrace. They could even enter the body, dismembering their victims in the process. Thorny, stake-like trees grew from the corpses of Fire Giants killed by the Briars.

By offering their own blood in sacrifice, practioners of thorn sorcery can manifest the Briars as crimson bloodthorns.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Briars of Sin punishing criminals and sinners in the Lands Between by crushing their eyes, permanently branding them as the Guilty. These crimson thorns inflicted Blood Loss and shared ancient ties with the Giants' Flame and blood star. During the War Against the Giants, Queen Marika's forces used the briars to impale and destroy the Fire Giants, swiftly ending the conflict with the fell god at the dawn of the age of the Erdtree.

Those who survived the briars were exiled from the Altus Plateau. A group of Guilty maidens dwelled in eternal darkness before beholding the heretical blood star, which revealed the aberrant secrets of Faith-based thorn sorcery. They produced bloodthorns by impaling sacrifices with smoldering, withered saplings, turning blood into red glintstone. They revered a maiden whose eyes were crushed by Briars of Sin before her rebirth in the Lands Between, and integrated with the Fire Monks, whose Prelates cracked crimson Thorned Whips to incite religious fervor. Horned Sanguine Albinaurics produce bloodthorns during their cartwheels.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.body:
Blackflame Sorcerers (formerly) 
Elemer of the Briar (Bell-Bearing Hunter)
Fire Monks
Fire Prelate
Guilty (Thorn Sorcerers)
Mad Tongue Alberich

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Only visual and contextual evidence supports their role in the War Against the Giants. It is unclear who wielded the briars, though the Trolls' betrayal was a noted turning point in the war.
The "thorn trees" seen impaling Fire Giants also appear near Fire Monk camps and Guardians' Garrison. 
Every Fire Giant slain by the Briars of Sin has white hair, as if drained of their iconic flame-red color. It is unclear whether this change was directly caused by the thorns or if their hair is drained of its color upon their deaths.
The Briars of Sin may be linked to the Impenetrable Thorns of the Erdtree and Scadutree, as well as the mottling thorns afflicting Exile Soldiers and the ruins of Stormveil Castle. 
Both Guilty and Exiled Soldiers drop Smoldering Butterflies, which are associated with Melina and the flame of ruin.
Elemer of the Briar, also known as the Bell-Bearing Hunter, hailed from Eochaid, an ancient realm of the Lands Between. 
Criminals marked for death by the Erdtree were bound in iron briars, while those accused of lesser crimes wore wreathes of sharpened branches.
Although Maliketh, the Black Blade sinned in the past and has gouged-out eyes, it is unclear whether the briars blinded him.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The maiden represented on the Shield of the Guilty was explicitly a goddess in; however, the item did not mention the Briars of Sin at the time. Her identity is unknown, though she may be Melina, the Gloam-Eyed Queen, the Fell God, or someone else. She is unlikely to be Queen Marika because "maiden" specifically refers to an unmarried young woman, and Godfrey was Marika's Lord by the time of her decree at the First Church of Marika.

name: Broadsword
description: Broadsword is a straight sword found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Starting equipment for the Confessor class. 
Nomadic Merchant southeast of Coastal Cave, beneath the collapsed structure.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
Always has the highest Attack Power (AP) of all regular Straight Swords, with the exception of the Quality Affinity, primarily due to its high base damage being able to compensate for its somewhat mediocre scaling. 
Since it's acquirable extremely early, as soon as the tutorial is completed, this weapon is a useful tool for potentially the entire game. 
Surprisingly, compared to its predecessors from previous game, this weapon isn't short but merely of average length. 
Leans towards Strength for Cold and Blood/Poison affinities. 
Despite having the highest damage and scaling on its Heavy affinity it actually gives slightly weaker Strength-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Heavy, Quality, or Fire affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Ground Slam, Storm Blade, and Flame of the Redmanes (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Heavy). 
Has a unique heavy attack and rolling attack, shared with the Cane Sword, replacing the usual thrusts with a broad, sweeping strike and an upward cut specifically. 
This is mostly a disadvantage. While the unique heavy attack is mostly good, it lacks the Pierce damage of the usual Straight Sword heavy attack and thus can't counter-hit attacking foes, while the unique rolling attack is very lacking in reach.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Basic Info:

Equipment:

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Roundtable Hold
Corhyn can be found in the central chamber of Roundtable Hold, where he will offer to teach you several Incantations. His shop inventory can be increased by giving him prayerbooks.
Roundtable Hold 
After reaching Altus Plateau, Corhyn will express an interest in searching for Goldmask.
Altus Plateau
Corhyn can be found north of the the Altus Highway Junction Site of Grace.
Talking to him here after finding Goldmask will allow you to reveal Goldmask's location to him.
Altus Plateau (Forest-Spanning Greatbridge)
Corhyn will now appear next to Goldmask. The pair will now travel together.
Leyndell, Royal Capital
Corhyn and Goldmask can be found near the colosseum. Corhyn will express frustration at Goldmask's current obsession with Radagon.
After using Law of Regression in front of the Radagon statue past the lift near Erdtree Sanctuary, talk to Goldmask to reveal Radagon's secret and then talk to Corhyn.
Mountaintops of the Giants
Corhyn and Goldmask will move to the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins. Corhyn can be offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, which will affect the end of his questline.
If offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, Corhyn will remain in this location after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade after Goldmask leaves. After reloading the area, he will have disappeared, leaving behind his flail, robe, and bell bearing.
Leyndell, Ashen Capital 
If Corhyn was not offered the Tonic of Forgetfulness, he will appear in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, close to the giant Bolt of Gransax after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade. After exhausting his dialogue and resting at a Site of Grace, he will be gone.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Corhyn will refuse to take the Tonic of Forgetfulness if offered to him and it will remain in your inventory. Despite this, the act of offering it to him will influence the outcome of his questline. This choice will not affect the outcome of Goldmask's questline, however.

description: Butterflies are a concept and.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Butterflies were thin-feathered insects known for their large, often brightly colored wings and fluttering flight. An aspect of the primordial Crucible, they held divine significance for the denizens of the Lands Between, and were used in purification rituals at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh in antiquity.

Each connected to a Demigod child of Queen Marika and Radagon, four strains of sacred butterfly appeared during the age of the Erdtree: Black Pyrefly (Messmer), Smoldering Butterfly (Melina), Nascent Butterfly (St. Trina and Miquella), and Aeonian Butterfly (Malenia).

When Malenia unleashed the scarlet rot at the Battle of Aeonia, scarlet butterflies emerged and became her wings, granting immense strength. Despite this, she later rejected them, just as she did the Servants of Rot. Only upon her transformation into Malenia, Goddess of Rot—when the Scarlet Aeonia blooms a second time—do butterflies return as her wings. The forsaken scarlet butterflies were left to roam the Swamp of Aeonia or were taken in by Romina, Saint of the Bud, who summoned scarlet rot after Messmer's crusade reached the Church of the Bud. Like the Kindred of Rot, these butterflies turned bright pink when they were embraced by Romina.

sections.body:

Nascent Butterflies boost Status Resistances, and cure Ailments in.

Romina, Saint of the Bud, has grown her own set of insect wings; the scarlet butterflies do not serve as her wings.
Similar to Aeonian butterflies, the Servants of Death collectively form the wings of Death Rite Birds.

description: Cane Sword is a straight sword found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found next to the stairs just south of the West Capital Rampart Site of Grace in Leyndell, Royal Capital and Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
The weakest of all Straight Swords in the game, and of below average length on top of that. Slightly stronger on Dexterity-leaning affinities such as Keen. 
Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
Has the same unique sweeping heavy attack and rolling attack as the Broadsword, and as such lacks attacks that deal Pierce damage when used on its own, only having the dual-wield backstep attack for that. 
The rolling attack does come out slightly quicker than the regular version.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Held by a Carriage located in the northwest region of Liurnia of the Lakes, between the Northern Liurnia Lake Shore and The Four Belfries Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The locked, innate skill, Carian Grandeur, while not unique and reliant on its weaker Intelligence-scaling, is still very strong if it can hit. Best used as a replacement for a Critical Attack or while lying in ambush since it charges somewhat slowly. 
Gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Intelligence build (616 AP from having 45 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 45 Intelligence), a bit less from a pure Strength build (609 AP from 80 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 18 Intelligence), and far less from a pure Intelligence build (576 AP from 10 Strength, 10 Dexterity, and 80 Intelligence). 
Note that since the skill's damage is entirely reliant on the character's Intelligence and the weapon's Intelligence-scaling, the skill will be weaker on the pure Strength build compared to the other two builds. 
Since the Carian Knight's Sword innate Intelligence-scaling is fairly poor, strengthening the skill and the sword's Attack Power together is somewhat difficult, with only the ease of upgrading weapons with Somber Smithing Stones over those needing Smithing Stones keeping it in front of regular Magic affinity weapons with this skill equipped. 
Has a unique blocking heavy attack, shared with the Lazuli Glintstone Sword. While this can make attacking into an attacking foe a bit less punishing, the resulting Stamina damage that will be taken if hit can prevent the user from attacking or rolling away. 
While the brief hit-stun taken by shields isn't suffered when hit, the low Stability means that using the unique heavy attack is highly likely to result in a stun from being guardbroken. 
Stability can be increased by 10% via two-handing and then further by the Greatshield Talisman. 
While the uncharged unique heavy attack deals the same amount of Stance damage as a normal uncharged heavy attack, the charged version only deals 1.5 times more Stance damage instead of the regular straight sword charged version which deals 3 times more Stance damage.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.body:
For both versions of the area, the greatest danger will be dangerous ranged Magic attacks, so bringing some way to counteract that (such as Spellproof Dried Liver, Magic Fortification, or Spelldrake Talisman) is useful. 

Normally only the Standard version is accessible but both versions can be freely switched between after acquiring the Carian Inverted Statue. 

Standard version:
From the only Grace, ignore the altar and walk around it. Take the elevator up to a split with stairs to a bridge on the left and a sidepath on the right. At the end of the sidepath is a Golden Rune [3] and picking up spawns two puppet Estoc variant Wandering Nobles. 

Walking up the stairs spawns two more puppet Nobles and Preceptor Miriam. Hitting Miriam once or twice causes her to teleport further away, a behavior that will continue for the rest of the area until she is killed (though do note that she can skip over spots if enough damage is inflicted in one go). On the bridge itself 5 more Nobles will spawn as you approach Miriam on the other side, while she will snipe at you with Loretta's Greatbow. 

The stairs at the other side of the bridge has Miriam and another puppet Noble and 2 more Nobles will spawn upon approaching a small raised stone section with the Carian Glintstone Staff. Further along and to the right is an elevator to the second floor. 

The first level of the second floor is essentially a circular balcony where you play a game of ring-around-the-rosie with Preceptor Miriam and occasionally spawning puppet Nobles, now also with the sorcerer variant. Miriam will alternate between either using Loretta's Greatbow or Magic Downpour while teleporting clockwise around the area if you approach closely while she isn't charging a spell, so try to either attack her as the spell is being charged up or use a ranged weapon like a Bow. Since the puppets don't respawn until resting at a grace one may want to focus their first lap in killing them. Killing her gives the Magic Downpour sorcery and a Golden Rune [4] can be found on the ring. 

To the left of the elevator used to come up and two lengths of the railing along is a ladder to the lower rafters. There is no item on the lower level but there are to Giant Rats, one straight ahead and one far to the right. Additionally there is another ladder up to the upper rafters, with 3 more Giant Rats and also the Cerulean Seed Talisman. 

Inverted version:
Using the Carian Inverted Statue on the altar instead changes the path behind it. The elevator well is now fall onto a ledge around a hole in the floor, and beyond it is a thin hole with 1 small Fingercreepers with another 2 flanking it on the walls. 

Entering into the bridge room, which is now a set of walkways with a platform in the middle. Take a left to drop down to a nook with the Mask of Confidence while dropping down on the right takes you to 2 small Fingercreepers. Since Preceptor Miriam will be standing on the central platform and bombard you with Loretta's Greatbow and Magic Downpour, stick close to the wall when approaching. Two more small Fingercreepers are on the same platform and a spear-wielding Raya Lucaria Soldier puppet hides around a corner to support her. Reducing Miriam to half health causes her to teleport further away. 

The Preceptor will stand across the gap, now unrestricted by cover, so keep an eye on her while dealing with the new enemies. Moving forward and to the right is a bridge with 2 Fingercreepers on it and a nook with a Fingercreeper to the right. Guarding Miriam final location will be 2 sword-wielding Raya Lucaria Soldiers that may have to be dealt with first. Defeat her to get Lucidity. 

Since there are no more doors forward you instead have to either drop down to either the middle chandelier below you and then one below that or fall of the right side to the wooden walkway around the area. Either way lets you drop down to the rafters and some Giant Rats. The lower level of the rafters holds some Glintstone Fireflies on the central ring and a few Holyproof Dried Livers one the lower left offshoot beam (seen from Miriam's last spot). 

Drop down into the elevator and use it to go down to access the door to Divine Tower of Liurnia.

name: Castellan Jerren
description: Castellan Jerren, also known as Witch-Hunter Jerren, is an NPC character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Jerren is the elderly castellan of Redmane Castle. In the past, Jerren was a nomadic warrior who became a guest of the Carian Royal Family. There, he became acquainted with General Radahn, the son of Radagon and Rennala, the Carian queen, who would later challenge the stars and arrest their movements, halting fate. He was considered an eccentric by Smithing Master Iji, the troll war counselor of the Carians. During this time, Jerren made a promise to kill Sellen, the Graven Witch, a sorceress who had long been a hindrance to the Carians.

After spending time as a guest of the Carians, Jerren served as a guest commander under General Radahn, and the two swore an oath of honourable death to one another. During the Shattering, Radahn fought Malenia, Blade of Miquella in the Battle of Aeonia, and in the aftermath was driven mad by Malenia's rot, cursed to wander the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike. Jerren convened the Radahn Festival to give Radahn a warrior's death.

Game events:
He attracted champions from across the Lands Between to participate in a battle against the Red Lion General and a chance to claim his Great Rune. Among the champions who converge upon Redmane Castle to participate in the festival is the Tarnished who succeeds in defeating Radahn, giving him an honourable death.

With Radahn dead, the stars are once again set into motion, and Sellen is dispossessed of her immortality. Finally able to uphold his old promise, Jerren travels to Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, where Sellen is bound by the Academy's shackles. When he arrives, he finds her as a husk, her soul having seemingly already fled. Suspecting Sellen to still be alive somewhere, Jerren continues his hunt, eventually tracking her down to the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He vows to kill her and crush her Primal Glintstone, which facilitated her survival. Should the Tarnished aid him in defeating Sellen, he will thank them before departing, promising to meet them again at the next tournament.

name: Castle Morne
description: Castle Morne is a location in. Found at the southernmost point in the Lands Between, it overlooks the southeastern shore of the Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Castle Morne once belonged to the Stormveil faction that later fell to the Erdtree long ago. A clan of warriors rose against Queen Marika, only to be vanquished. The lone survivor, burdened by anger and regret, collected their swords and reforged them into a single Grafted Blade Greatsword. Morne was the site of their legendary showdown with Godfrey, First Elden Lord, commemorated by a nearby Sword Monument. Although the hero swore an Oath of Vengeance, they were ultimately defeated by the Elden Lord, and their sword became a treasure of the keep.

After the Shattering, this fortress fell under the control of Godrick the Grafted, a distant scion of the Golden Lineage, who ruled Limgrave from Stormveil Castle. He appointed Castellan Edgar to oversee the castle and its Godrick Soldier garrison; however, by the time the player arrives, it has fallen to an uprising by its maltreated Misbegotten servants. Edgar's blind daughter, Irina of Morne, fled the castle, but her Great Coffin escort was overtaken by Misbegotten on the road near the Bridge of Sacrifice. Edgar is bound by duty to maintain his post until the sword of Morne is reclaimed from the Leonine Misbegotten.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The treasured Grafted Blade Greatsword of Castle Morne is one of the Legendary Armaments. Its hilt guard features the fierce golden lion of the Golden Lineage.
The armory is stocked with armaments of Exile Soldiers and Banished Knights.
Castellan Edgar wears an incomplete Banished Knight Set and wields a Banished Knight's Halberd (Skill: Spinning Slash) and Dragon Communion Seal, though he casts Erdtree Incantations. Following his daughter's murder, he continues Morne's legacy by hunting Misbegotten as Edgar the Revenger.
The large Moangrave may represent the revenger or their clan.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In heraldry, morné (or morne) describes a beast, typically a lion, depicted standing fiercely on one hind leg with its forepaws elevated, without teeth, claws, or a tongue. The term derives from the Old French morner ("to blunt"), representing a defanged, defeated, or stripped-down state. The name "Castle Morne" likely describes the castle's recurring themes of loss and diminished power, including the golden lion emblazoned on the vanquished revenger's Grafted Blade Greatsword, the rebellion of the oppressed Leonine Misbegotten who seized that weapon, the prior conquest of the castle by Godfrey, and the suppression of Godfrey's true ferocity by Serosh, Lord of Beasts. It may also allude to Stormveil stormhawks or Elder Lions, whose respective talons and horns were amputated by Godfrey's Golden Lineage. Although stormhawks are absent from the castle, their likeness appears on palisades throughout its grounds.
Mentioned in Dark Souls III, Morne was a knight who served the goddess of tears.

name: Castle Sol
description: Castle Sol is a landmark in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Castle Sol was an old fortress built on the northernmost tip of the Lands Between, belonging to those who later became Banished Knights. These drake hunters would gift an Icerind Hatchet, made from a scale of Borealis the Freezing Fog, to Liurnia of the Lakes as part of their diplomatic relationships.

In the distant past, a frigid, awe-inspiring eclipse mesmerized the knights of Castle Sol. Drained of its color, the lusterless sun repelled Destined Death and granted life to the soulless. The castle's inhabitants gathered at its Church of the Eclipse, where they used the storied Eclipse Shotel in worship of the dreadful celestial event.

In a later age, when veteran Commander Niall and his men were garrisoned at Sol, another force defeated them in battle even though they wielded storm and lightning-clad weapons. In exchange for the captured lives of his fallen men, Niall offered his right leg. Unable to die, and with nowhere to fade to, Niall eternally led the summoned spirits of his army of no nation. 

Following the Night of Black Knives, Sol's inhabitants fervently prayed for another eclipse, hoping to call a spirit into the soulless demigod interred with their mausoleum. The Mausoleum Knights, who beheaded themselves to protect their masters as spirits, displayed the Eclipse to ward off the Destined Death of Godwyn the Golden. 

Later, Miquella the Kind visited to castle and petitioned the master to return the life of his comrade. He bestowed half of a secret medallion to the master that would allow him to access the then-upcoming Haligtree if he had succeeded in his task. However, the awaited eclipse never came to pass, making the master of the castle unable to visit the Haligtree as he wasn't able to fulfill his duty, thus he lost hope and perished. Niall, the commander of Castle Sol, left alone in the castle to protect his long-passed master, continue commanding the nationless spirits of his Banished Knight army.

sections.body: Castle Sol is situated on the northern edge of the Mountaintops of the Giants, north Snow Valley Ruins Overlook. It is accessed from the east, after traveling down from the graveyard with Giant Skeletons. The path is guarded by a Tibia Mariner and Death Rite Bird.

name: Catch Flame
description: Catch Flame is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 600 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
Starting equipment for the Prophet Origin.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Conjure a small burst of flames from the hand, that has Fire Attack Power equal to 225% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 10 FP per cast.
Costs 17 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot. 
Deals 7 Stance damage. 
Can be chain-cast continuously, provided the player has sufficient amounts of FP.
Casting this incantation directly after a roll, jump, or backstep makes the casting time slightly shorter, making it much more dynamic than many other, slower spells. 
Moves the caster slightly forward with each use.
Despite using the Giants' Flame, this spell does not generate a spell sigil when cast, making it ineligible for a boost from the Giant's Seal.

Boosting:

Strategies:
With its rapid casting time, Catch Flame excels as a quick, close-range option for dispatching enemies. However, its small area of effect and short range make it less reliable against agile or fast-moving targets.
A potent damage-dealing spell throughout the game thanks to its more than decent damage and extremely quick casting time, and available on a lot of Incantations build with only a minimal amount of Faith. 
It is especially potent as an early-game tool for players who can manage the low FP cost compared to their meager FP pool.
Highly efficient as a melee spell for pure Faith builds.
Casting Catch Flame immediately before Magma Breath significantly reduces the cast time of the latter, enabling quicker execution in combat.
When chained into Magma Breath mid-air, Catch Flame modifies the casting animation into a faster, more fluid spray, allowing players to seamlessly chain another Magma Breath cast.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like Fire's Deadly Sin and Flame Sling, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.
Brother Corhyn was one of the prophets exiled for glimpsing the forbidden flame of ruin, a transgression that led to banishment.
Catch Flame closely resembles the Combustion spell from the Dark Souls series.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The cathedral's architecture matches the Church of Vows and the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, implying all three buildings were constructed by the Nox.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The name "Manus Celes" means "Hidden Hand" or "Celestial Hand" in Latin, though Celes is not a standard Latin word. It is derived from manus ("hand") and cēlēs ("to conceal, cover, or hide"), caeles ("deity, god; heaven-faring"), or caelestis ("heavenly, celestial").
Cælestial is an archaic spelling of celestial.
Its meaning may be intentionally ambiguous, as multiple interpretations supported by contextual evidence.
The "Hidden Hand" reading may allude to the hidden presence of the Two Fingers beneath the cathedral.
The "Celestial Hand," "Heavenly Hand," and "Hand of God" interpretations are supported by the abundant Starlight Shards in the area and the Two Fingers' association with Metyr, Mother of Fingers and the Greater Will.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This weapon is wielded by the young maidens who play a central role in the festival.
Grants 10 Runes every time an enemy is hit. 
The strongest dagger for the Keen affinity, with its A being just on the verge of an S-scaling. Otherwise somewhat subpar or average when it comes to damage, including the otherwise Dexterity-scaling Lightning and Cold affinities. 
Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
Pairs well with non-physical affinities such as Magic since those are usually already only partially negated by guarding and the ignored guarding damage negation applies to all forms of damage, not just Physical. 
As a dagger it will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

description: The Cerulean Coast is a subregion of the Realm of Shadow in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: A somber field of ephemeral blue lilies blooms among beached coffin-ships from beyond the Lands Between. These stone vesels house the Congealed Putrescence of ancient, tainted life, once purified in ghostflame by the deathbirds long ago. The blue flowers are contrasted by a sea of luminous crimson lilies on the plateau above, said to be the home of the Tibia Mariners and the hidden grave of Charo. Deep underground, below both fields, wilts St. Trina's Garden of Deep Purple.

name: Chair-Crypt Mummies
description: The Chair-Crypt Mummies, also known in the community as Nox Giants or Nox Gods are deceased characters and.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The chair-crypt mummies are not referenced in any item description or dialogue, leaving their nature and origins open to interpretation.
The symbol depicted on their robes is the same used by the Nox on the capes of their Night Maidens and Swordstresses
These bodies are of similar size and proportions to the Rauh giant mummy at Specimen Storehouse and Giant Skeleton enemies, possibly making these bodies contemporaries/descendants of the giants inhabiting the ancient civilization of Rauh.
Both Nox descendants and Marika's tribe, the Shamans, are Numen, hinting at a common ancestry.
Their fresh robes and mummified bodies are reminiscent of the shugendō practice of sokushinbutsu, wherein the mummified bodies of shugendō practitioners are enshrined and regularly given fresh robes. 
This same practice is found in the Tutelary Deities and Curseblades of Hornsent society, the latter being explicitly referred to as shugendō practitioners in the Japanese script. Notably, Hornsent society is heavily focused on the study of Rauh, which could indicate a shared origin between the Crypt-Chairs and Tutelary Deities in the customs of the ancient civilization.

image: ER Custom Sub-Menu Icon Man Front.png
description: Charo was an character mentioned in:.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The final resting place of Charo was concealed on the southern shore of the Gravesite Plain, among a hallowed field of crimson lilies overlooking the solemn Cerulean Coast.

Charo's Hidden Grave was shared with the wizened Tibia Mariners, first of all grave keepers, who guided Those Lost in Death long after withering away. A rare gravesite flower was also said to blossom there into cold ghostflame. The silent-burning, barely-tangible ghostflame bloom was sister to the spirit-calling grave violet.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: It can be inferred that Charo was the founder or patron of the Tibia Mariners. His may also be the first grave they were keeping.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Charo's name is a corruption of Charon, the ferryman of the dead in Greek myth. Charon was said to transport the souls of the dead down the River Styx in the underworld.

sections.heading: Basin of Atonement
sections.body:
At the back of the church stands a Nox Swordstress statue and an ornate Basin of Atonement. It is said that Radagon repented his territorial aggression by cleansing himself with dew in this pool. The player may replicate this act here by offering up Celestial Dew, performing an Absolution.

It will not render passive any characters that are hostile by default, nor will it revive those who have died. It will not restore Melina as a traveling companion, even if the Frenzied Flame has been suppressed with Miquella's Needle.
