Gurranq, Beast Clergyman, also known as Maliketh, the Black Blade, wields the Cinquedea, affirming its connection to Shadowbound Beasts and the Two Fingers.

name: Cleanrot Knight
image: ER Cleanrot Knight w Halo Scythe.jpg
description: are Enemies and Bosses in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Cleanrot Knights were fierce warriors who remained devoted to Malenia, Blade of Miquella, even as her scarlet rot consumed their bodies. Their winged helms and sword insignias embodied the unyielding resolve of their Empyrean master. They stood in arms with Miquella's followers within Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

They fought under Malenia's command throughout her undefeated campaign in the Shattering, which culminated in the fateful clash against General Radahn's Redmane army in Caelid. A majority of the knights fell at the Battle of Aeonia, their spirits locked in eternal combat in the War-Dead Catacombs. The few survivors wandered the resulting Swamp of Aeonia, while others traced the footsteps of Cleanrot Knight Finlay, who bore the sleeping Malenia all the way back to the Haligtree, passing through the Shaded Castle along the way.

sections.heading: Chacteristics
sections.body: All Cleanrot Knights wear golden armor and wield a Cleanrot Knight's Sword as a secondary weapon to complement their polearms. This allows them to land multiple attacks in quick succession, triggering the Talisman's blessing to strengthen them even further. Most Cleanrot Knights wield a Cleanrot Spear, which bears a small shield on its shaft. They will imbue their spear with gold before performing their more deadly attacks, such as grabbing their enemy with the spear tip and infecting them with Scarlet Rot, and summoning forth a golden palisade from the ground. They can also brace their spear with their sword to absorb an incoming blow and quickly retaliate with their own. Cleanrot knight commanders wield the Halo Scythe. They prefer ranged combat, repeatedly firing rings of Miquella's light from a distance. In close quarters, they may vomit Scarlet Rot.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.body: Cleanrot Knights are resistant to Slash and Holy damage, taking 35% and 40% less damage from these types. They receive flat damage from Pierce and Lightning damage, but take 20% extra damage from Fire attacks; however, the scythe-wielding variant can nullify this vulnerability by casting an incantation.

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.body:
Stillwater Cave=

Background:
A lone Cleanrot Knight, encountered in an alcove at the very end of Stillwater Cave that has been partially flooded in poisonous waters.

Strategy:
Most of the room is full of poisonous water, so it's advisable to quickly run to the small island of safety just left of the boss, in the middle left to far left section of the room. 

Since this boss is the spear-wielding variant and this fight will most likely happen early in the game, it's critical to avoid its Scarlet Rot-inducing, charging grab attack (signified by its spear glowing a bright gold). This is most easily accomplished by rolling diagonally forward to reach the other side of the boss. Since the boss is vulnerable to backstabs

Abandoned Cave=

Background:
A Cleanrot Knight and its commander, both encountered in an alcove at the very end of Abandoned Cave that has been partially flooded by scarlet rot. The remains of numerous Abudctor Virgins lay scattered around the arena. 

Strategy:
As the fight starts, only the spear-wielder is present, with the scythe-wielding commander rising from the rot pool to the left within 12 seconds of starting the battle. As such, it is best to spend that opening either summoning a Spirit or rushing down the spear knight to try and at least severely wound it before the scythe knight can join the fray. 

Of the two combatants, the spear knight is more aggressive and will try to restrict player movement with its Sacred Phalanx and inflict Scarlet Rot with its charge. In contrast, the scythe knight will harass from afar with Miquella's Ring of Light and buff both of them with a unique combination of health regeneration and extra Fire resistance to cover for one of their weaknesses. 

If fighting alone, try to pull the spear knight to the right so that the hill blocks the light rings and buys extra time to kill it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The emphasis placed on the Cleanrot Knight's gait and cone-shaped helmet in concept art draws similarities to the Kindred of Rot.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Cocoon of the Empyrean rests within an enormous pelvic girdle and contains the Empyrean body of Miquella.
After the Battle of Aeonia long ago, Miquella placed a powerful charm on the Demigod Mohg. cut Miquella from the roots of the Haligtree and stole him from the city of Elphael. Mohg carried him across the Consecrated Snowfield and brought him to his Mohgwyn Palace in the ruins of the Ancient Dynasty. Mohg has been sharing his accursed blood with Miquella in an attempt to ascend the dormant Empyrean into godhood and take his side as the next Elden Lord.

Sir Ansbach, commander of the Pureblood Knights, challenged Miquella in an attempt to dispel the charm cast on Mohg. Although he managed to wound the fearsome Empyrean, he, too, fell under his spell.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: The Coded Sword can be found on the upper floor of the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital, in the room that mirrors the one that the Two Fingers of the Roundtable Hold can be found it. This weapon cannot be acquired once the Tarnished has defeated Maliketh.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
As the name suggest, the skill, Unblockable Blade, will pierce through all the damage negation from a blocking shield or weapon. It also has a very wide reach since it's a sweeping attack and deals Stance damage on par with a Straight Sword's charged heavy attack, meaning it can break the Stance of most enemies within 2 hits and most bosses within 3 or 4 hits. 
Unlike all other weapons, this weapon doesn't bounce away from any shield when wielded one-handed, not even when hitting the Ant's Skull Plate or sturdy enemies such as Miners. 
Since this weapon has no Physical damage and instead is fully elemental, and its skill fully ignores all the damage negation of a block, it's not very wise to try to block it. 
Since this weapon deals pure Holy damage it benefits fully from Holy-Shrouding Cracked Tear but is also heavily weakened if the fought enemy has high Holy Damage Negation, something that becomes increasingly common among Bosses after entering Leyndell, Royal Capital, with most of them having 40% Holy damage negation and 3 (technically 2) late-game bosses having 80% Holy damage negation.

Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: Colossal Dragon
description: The colossal dragon is an object in.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Unlike modern drakes, the colossal dragon has featherless, leathery wings.
Dragon Communion Harpoons are embedded in the dragon's wings.
The verdigris rod that killed the colossal dragon is covered in fulgurite, implying it was delivered with lightning.
The nearby Dragon Communion Priestess implies Dragonlord Placidusax felled the colossal drake and devoured its dragon heart. However, the Dragonlord does not utilize metal rods in combat against the player.
The dragon does not show signs of decomposition.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: At an estimated 392 meters in length, the Colossal Drake is the largest FromSoftware dragon to date, a title previously held by Ancient Dragon Gransax (~328m).

name: Colossal Remains
description: Colossal remains, also known as giant skeletons, titans, and other unofficial names, are objects in.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Only the upper torso and skulls are exposed.
The skeletons found in Caelid are much larger than those on the Mountaintops.
The cause of the colossal giants' extinction remains unknown.
Due to the enormity of their size, it's possible these colossal giants were the original architects of the ancient ruins like the Rauh Ruins along with other landmarks that share the same architectural style, such as the Forge of the Giants and the Divine Towers.
The giants are the only known creatures large enough to have used the arrowhead that became the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword. It is possible they were the old gods.
Shadowy titans of similar proportions appear in Limveld on the second Noontide. These colossi appear to be formed from woody vines, and lack bones and upper skulls. Heolstor the Nightlord can reincarnate as one of these arboreal Night Giants.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In Norse mythology, the jötunn Vafþrúðnir claims the earth was formed from the body of Ymir.
In the Elden Ring Closed Network Test, heads of similar proportions were present in Limgrave when viewed from Stormveil Castle. Deep lacerations were carved into their stone flesh, which burned like coals.
A cut dialogue from Enia describes Radahn solely as "the slayer of giants." It is possible the remains in Caelid may once have been related to this cut aspect of his character.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: The caster channels for 3 seconds before releasing a torrent of energy that deals Magic damage, with an Attack Power equal to???% of Sorcery Scaling per second. The beam continues as long as the casting button is held, consuming additional FP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 46 FP per cast and drains 10 FP per sustained increment.
Costs 34 Stamina per cast.
Requires 3 Memory Slots to equip.
Can be channeled until FP is depleted.
Deals low Stance damage, but the beam's end deals more.

Boosting:
Azur's Glintstone Crown boosts attack power and FP cost by 15%.
Azur's Glintstone Staff reduces casting time and increases FP costs by 20%.
Cerulean Hidden Tear removes FP costs for 15 seconds.
Glintstone Scarab reduces FP cost by 15%.
The Graven-School Talisman and Graven-Mass Talisman boost attack power by 4% and 8% respectively, stacking for a total of 12%.
Magic Scorpion Charm boosts attack power by 12% (8% in PvP).
Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear boosts attack power by 20% (15% in PvP).
Primal Glintstone Blade reduces FP cost by 25%.
Radagon Icon reduces casting time by??%.
Terra Magica boosts attack power by 35%.

Strategies:
The beam has long range and can pass through enemies.
The beam’s direction cannot be adjusted once cast.
Casting time is reduced by Dexterity, up to a maximum of 70 Dexterity.
If cast immediately after applying the Cerulean Hidden Tear, it can be channeled without FP drain for up to 12 seconds.
This spell is easily interrupted due to its long casting time.
Most bosses and enemies will dodge when the spell is initially cast, not when the beam is released.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Despite the academy's ban on primeval sorceries, Comet Azur is used by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon.

name: Commander Gaius
description: Commander Gaius is an optional boss in encountered outside the backdoor of the Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Commander Gaius was a noted warrior and military strategist who rode a giant boar as his steed. Gaius studied gravitational magic from an Alabaster Lord. He was a fellow student of Radahn, a future demigod. He also befriended Messmer the Impaler, as both had in common that they were cursed from birth. The pair were as elder brothers to Radahn, with whom Gaius had formed a friendly rivalry.
When Messmer embarked on the purge of the Land of Shadow on Queen Marika the Eternal's orders, Gaius would join him and serve as the commander of his soldiers. He was never without his boar. Even when Marika abandoned Messmer, Gaius remained steadfast, guarding the backdoor of Shadow Keep. It was here that he would meet his end at the hands of a Tarnished champion.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.body: Commander Gaius is an albinauric without legs who rides a heavily armored, great-tusked boar. Gaius wears black iron armor patterned to represent fallen seeds and wields the Sword Lance. He was cursed by his Albinauric heritage and as such was doomed to lose the use of his legs.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body: Commander Gaius will charge with his boar to try to run you over. This can be dodge by jumping over with torrent or dodging at a very exact moment. He also uses gravity magic to attack enemies that are too far away.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Wears Gaius's Helm, Gaius's Armor, Gaius's Gauntlets, and Gaius's Greaves
Wields Sword Lance
Casts Blades of Stone
Gaius serves as a foil to Royal Knight Loretta, who hid her Albinauric nature from her compatriots.

moveset: Commander Gaius will charge with his boar to try to run you over. This can be dodge by jumping over with torrent or dodging at a very exact moment. He also uses gravity magic to attack enemies that are too far away.

name: Commander Niall
description: Commander Niall is an optional boss in. Defeating him will unlock the Commander Niall achievement.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body: At the beginning of the fight, Niall summons the spirits of two Banished Knights, one with a sword and shield, and the other wielding dual swords. Niall will be relatively passive while the knights are alive, instead buffing them until they have both been defeated or his health has been reduced to half. Both Banished Knights will inflict Frostbite with their attacks. Niall himself uses a mixture of lightning and frost-based attacks. He can imbue his prosthesis with lightning and perform kicks and stomps, and he can use his halberd to generate frost.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:

The Japanese description for Veteran's Prosthesis states Niall offered his leg, rather than his prosthetic, in exchange for his knights.

name: Count Ymir
description: Count Ymir, High Priest, later known as the boss Ymir, Mother of Fingers, is a character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Count Ymir was a master glintstone sorcerer renowned for his understanding of the cosmos. During the time of Elden Lord Godfrey, he served the Carian Royals and taught glintstone sorcery to Rellana, Twin Moon Knight. With a wizened hand gently gripping a glintstone, he often inspired his students, saying, "One need only envision the romance of the stars above with adoration for stardust in one's heart to become a great sorcerer. Do so, and you will know love." Although he originally held allegiance to the moons, he eventually dismissed them in his pursuit of deeper cosmic truths. 

Ymir uncovered secrets of the Greater Will during expedition into the hallowed Finger Ruins in the eastern Realm of Shadow. He studied the lamprey that dwelled within and mastered their Finger Sorcery, becoming a Finger-Weaver. Below the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, he found the Finger Ruins of Miyr concealed the Finger Birthing Grounds, where Metyr waited in vain.

Ymir learned that Metyr's true power and the guidance of the Two Fingers had been broken long ago. He became the high priest of Manus Metyr and acquired the service of the Swordhands of Night. After his child, Yuri, died at a tender age, Ymir's grief drove him to find a way to bring him back. He decided he would succeed Metyr as the next mother of Fingers. He began ingesting Fingerprint Nostrum and birthing Fingercreepers of his own. 

Game events:
Ymir shares the wisdom of the cosmos and a Hole-Laden Necklace with the Tarnished champion. He directs them to sound the ominous hanging bells at the Finger Ruins of Dheo and Rhia. Once both bells are rung, Ymir reveals the location of the Ruins of Miyr. Ringing the third and final bell will leave one's fate guided by the stars—and face-to-face with Metyr. If the Mother of Fingers is defeated, Ymir's hope is rekindled but the prospect of achieving his dream drives him mad. He achieves a partial transformation and fails to birth Yuri anew, instead creating more Fingercreepers.

name: Crescent Moon
description: The Crescent Moon was a celestial body mentioned in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The Crescent Moon was defined by a broad, curved arch that widened at the center and tapered at its ends. This half-wheel moon held nostalgic, religious, and scholarly significance for various peoples across the Lands Between. Its arcane power was associated with Night, Death, and Fate, and it stood in natural opposition to Holy power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Queen's Crescent Crown worn by Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon depicts a crescent moon.
The young Albinaurics wielded crescent moon-shaped weapons that evoked partial or whole ripples, which were said to be the Arcane origin of their artificial species. They formed crescent shapes with their bodies as they cartwheeled.
Royal Knight Loretta, who served the moon-worshipping Carian royal family, guards the path to the Young Albinauric Ashes.
Like the other Albinaurics, Rennala's reborn Juvenile Scholars cannot use their legs.
The legless Putrescent Knight wielded a crescent-shaped cleaver formed from bone and putrescence that scaled with Arcane. Its rider arched its spine backwards to execute series of spinning, guillotine-style chops.
Curved greataxes wielded by Exile Soldiers inspired nostalgia, and were called Crescent Moon Axes.
Bandits that ran free during the Shattering wielded crescent-shaped curved swords.
Some Abductor Virgins swing crescent moon-shaped blades.
Finger Reader Crones refer to Grand Lift medallions as half crescents.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The crescent moon appears during the second (waxing crescent) and seventh (waning crescent) phases of the lunar cycle.

name: Crossed-Tree
description: The Crossed-Tree is a concept in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The Crossed-Tree was an ancient symbol of an interleaving tree once used in the Lands Between. Its image was emblazoned in green on large iron greatshields designed to protect the entire body. Prior to entering the Realm of Shadow, Miquella the Kind handcrafted golden crossed-trees and distributed them to his Needle Knights, who decorated themselves in its image.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The Crossed-Tree depicts a symmetrical double helix formed by two entwined trunks rising from a shared base. As they ascend, the trunks curve inward and outward in alternating arcs, framing a series of almond-shaped enclosures. Eight broad, spade-like leaves grow from their limbs, while short branches sharply jut outward like thorns. A single, flame-shaped briar emerges from the base between the two trunks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Most information about the Crossed-Tree is conjectural, based on its visual details and context. The English and Japanese versions may differ in its characterization.
The English wording unambiguously asserts the importance of the Crossed-Tree image, implying it may have been a great tree that grew—or was expected to grow—in the distant past. Japanese lacks an equivalent for "interleaving" that carries its botanical connotations. It instead uses neutral language to describe an artistic symbol, without extra connotation implying the existence of an actual Crossed-Tree (古い交差樹の意匠が描かれている Furui kōsaju no ishō ga egakarete iru, An old crossed/intersection tree design/pattern is depicted/drawn on it).
The Crossed-Tree Towershield is sold by a Nomadic Merchant on the Forest-Spanning Greatbridge overlooking the Woodfolk Ruins in the Altus Plateau. This merchant also offers the Tree Surcoat, Red Crest Heater Shield, Scorpion Kite Shield, and various items tied to the Ancient Dragon Cult.
The Crossed-Tree design resembles the Spiraltree, but grows without the central supporting stake seen in the latter.
Miquella's crossed-trees are partially supported by a short pole, likely representing his needle.
In the 1.0 version of the game, this design is simply described as "Rune symbols;" this may reference Runes tendency to manifest in the form of golden trees, such as those dropped by the player on death.

name: Crucible
description: The Crucible (坩堝, Rutsubo), also known as the crucible of life (生命の坩堝), the golden Crucible (黄金の坩堝), or primordial crucible, was the primordial matter in which all life was blended together and the prior form of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The aspects of various creatures, such as feathers, scales, and knots, once grew on the bodies of humanoids. Ancient legends from the tower of Enir-Ilim claim that the "mother of all Crucibles" first appeared among the giants long ago. 

At some point, a group of people made contact with the Crucible, only to have their bodies mutated, becoming the chimeric Misbegotten, humanoid creatures with different aspects of other lifeforms like fur, scales, wings, tails and beast fangs. Identified as the mark of the Crucible, their presence was a signifier of divinity in ancient times. Of the Crucible's gifts, the Hornsent considered the tangled horn to be the most significant sign of primacy.

As Queen Marika's society advanced, signs of the Crucible were increasingly disdained as impurities. The Crucible Knights were shunned, the Omen were banished, and the Misbegotten were enslaved by the Erdtree, which deemed their corrupted appearance to be a punishment for their act. Perfumers like Tricia attempted to heal the Omen and Misbegotten, but were unsuccessful in curing these conditions. Rarely, budding horns and overlapping fangs still sprout on herbivorous and carnivorous beasts that typically would bear no horns, as a recessive trait considered a vestige of the Crucible's influence.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from a corpse in Auriza Hero's Grave in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. Make your way to the area where two chariots ride side-by-side, up and down a slope. At the bottom of this slope is a corpse, hanging off of a ledge above a pit. Drop into the pit from where this corpse lies to land on a beam, and continue dropping down into this pit, until landing on the top of a thin stone archway. Walk to the end of this archway and climb a ladder to reach another ramp, guarded by a single chariot. While it is possible to reach the bottom of this ramp without dying, it is extremely difficult, as it involves either taking a hit from the chariot without dying, or using a movement ability, like Bloodhound Step, along with excellent timing. The far easier thing to do is to proceed up the ramp until reaching a moving, fire-breathing pillar, which can be raised by hitting it. After raising the pillar, die or teleport to return to the ramp with two chariots. The raised pillar will now be shining a chariot-spawning circle of light onto the middle of this ramp, which will cause a chariot to spawn that collides with the others, destroying them all. The door at the bottom of the ramp leading to the corpse can now be safely reached.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
According to the Closed Network Test description for Ordovis's Greatsword, there were 16 Crucible Knights of Godfrey. Though the description has been changed, this is still the case for the final version of the base game. However, additional Crucible Knights were introduced and.
The Crucible Knights are meant to be a relic of the prehistoric era of the Crucible, which came long before the Age of the Erdtree, and their names are a deliberate reminder of their ancient origins. The names of the Crucible Knights all find their roots in the naming conventions of Earth’s prehistoric periods, specifically during the Paleozoic Era:
Ordovis is named after the Ordovician, which lasted from 485.4 million years ago to 443.8 million years ago.
Siluria is named after the Silurian, which followed the conclusion of the Ordovician and lasted until 419.2 million years ago. 
Devonia is named after the Devonian period, which was about 419.2 million to 358.9 million years ago
This is not a trait wholly unique to the Crucible Knights: Bloodhound Knight Floh and Bloodhound Knight Darriwil seem to be named after the Floian period and the Darriwilian period, respectively, both of which are stages of the Ordovician period. Unlike the Crucible Knights, there doesn't seem to be any particular reason why they are named after these periods.
The Crucible Knight with the spear was named Crucible Knight (Great Spear) in.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Devonia using a hammer reinforces the Crucible's connection to smithing.
Devonia calls upon an unnamed Aspect of the Crucible that transforms their lower body into a pachyderm centaur with six limbs. Its four back legs resemble those of even-toed ungulates, while the front legs terminate in large hands with opposable thumbs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Devonia's name is a reference to the Devonian period (from 419.2 to 358.9 million years ago).
The Crucible Knights are named after three sequential geological periods from the Paleozoic Era. From oldest to youngest, they are Ordovician (Ordovis), Silurian (Siluria), and Devonian (Devonia).
Although Devonia was the longest-serving member, they are named for the youngest period.
"Trees" evolved leaves, true roots, and seeds during the Devonian period.
Wattieza, the earliest known genus of trees, existed during the Devonian period. They were closely related to ferns, had fronds instead of leaves, and reproduced via spores.
The period that followed the Devonian was the Carboniferous, during which pentadactyly (five-fingers) evolved.

name: Crusade
description: The Crusade is an event in, referring to Messmer's endless war against the hornsent in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
After her ascension at their Gate of Divinity, the goddess Marika betrayed the hornsent—ruthless horned oppressors of her people—and secured dominion over the Lands Between. Guided by her Two Fingers, she planted a Golden Seed that transformed the primordial Crucible of life into the Erdtree and Scadutree. This ushered in an age of Plenty, glistening with abundance, in which Marika denied the tower folk the Grace of Gold. Horns and other aspects of the Crucible, traits previously considered divine, were gradually seen as impurities as Marika's civilization advanced.

The use of flame was traditionally prohibited to those who served the Erdtree, but Marika desired the Land of the Tower to be set aflame. She commanded her Demigod son Messmer to wage war against the Hornsent, and he became an agent of fear on her behalf. Marika previously stripped the Hornsent of Grace, and now they were to perish in Messmer's flame.

Leyndell's aristocratic elite strongly opposed the war; esteemed noble families disowned scions who pledged themselves as Fire Knights, driving them from their homes. Rellana, Twin Moon Knight, disavowed her Carian birthright to follow Messmer, and entered ritual combat in a show of faith to the Erdtree. The mighty Black Knights, who channeled the powers of the Crucible, remained devout followers of Messmer after his flight from Leyndell, and formed the backbone of his army. Messmer conscripted criminals from penal battalions amongst the common ranks, supported by perfumers preparing new incendiary scents.

Marika personally granted immense grace to champions who joined Messmer's army, and then veiled them in the realm of shadow for a cleansing purge in which there would be no honor nor mercy.

sections.heading: The Crusade
sections.body:
Messmer engaged many foes in battle, including the Divine Beasts, whom the Hornsent revered as messengers of the heavens. A majority of the Divine Beasts were killed in the Crusade, and were gored and impaled on Messmer's spears alongside many other victims before being burned, earning Messmer the infamous epithet, "the Impaler", and his undertaking of the Crusade made him a symbol of fear as his mother wished. As the Crusade raged on, Messmer's army came across the church of Romina, Saint of the Bud. It was put to the torch, leaving Romina in stunned silence as she held a bud in her hands amidst the burning ruins of her church.

Messmer's forces razed Prospect Town, Bonny Village, the Scorched Ruins, the Ruins of Unte, the Temple Town Ruins, the Church of the Bud, and Belurat, Tower Settlement. Messmer claimed the Shadow Keep, and the Gate of Divinity was veiled in shadow and inaccessible. Marika the Eternal sealed Messmer in the Realm of Shadow, ceased all communication, and condemned him to endless war. At the same time, she severed all history related to the Crusade so nobody could know of the original sin and her origins.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.body:
The Crusade had a lasting, heavy impact on the Realm of Shadow, especially on the Hornsent, whose civilization was destroyed to the point of beyond recovery, and its survivors developed a deep grudge, vowing vengeance against the people of the Erdtree for the suffering inflicted upon their clan. The immense suffering and resentment of all the Hornsent who were killed or who lost dear ones led to them to invoke the "curse of the omen" upon Marika's children each and all. Others discovered the Formless Mother in the scorched shadow of their ancestor, and were transformed into Bloodfiends. 

Messmer waited for his mother to end the crusade and bring him home, but the sign never came. Those in the Realm of Shadow felt the shattering of the Elden Ring, and the indefinite conquest lead to the deterioration of morale among Messmer's forces, which in turn led to internal rebellion and desertion.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
POWER (uncharged): 13.5% SS per bolt, 6 shots total (81% full barrage)

POWER (charged): 13.5% SS per bolt, up to 23 shots total (310.5% at 48 FP full barrage)

An astoundingly poor spell in PvE, without charging it has a terribly high cost for utterly miserable damage that's barely over half that of a single Glintstone Pebble, and if waiting to charge it this is extremely slow; simply spamming other spells will heavily outdamage it over time. Charging the attack does not increase the damage, it merely extends it for more shots at an additional 2 FP per shot, up to 17 extra bolts total.

The one notable exception would be in Invasion situations, both players and NPC Bloody Fingers. Such highly evasive opponents would find it rather difficult to evade the entire barrage of a fully charged shot.

name: Crystal Knife
description: The Crystal Knife is a Dagger.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found in a chest inside the Raya Lucaria Crystal Tunnel located in Liurnia of the Lakes. After taking the first elevator after the Site of Grace down and walking across a wooden beam it is inside the second room on the right, guarded by two distracted Marionette Soldiers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed.
The scaling favors an equal split between Strength and Intelligence, with the higher Physical base damage making the Strength-scaling more equivalent to the technically higher Intelligence-scaling. 
Surprisingly only 20 points/5% of total Attack Power behind when focused purely on Strength or Intelligence, or hybridizing Strength/Intelligence, Strength/Dexterity, or Dexterity/Intelligence. 
Decent raw damage but the unusual, for a dagger anyway, lack of a critical multiplier means it ends up being outclassed by all of the other daggers, especially the Dagger and the Miséricorde, for the purpose of critical hits. 
Pairs well with a Magic or Cold affinity Bloodstained Dagger due to its also scaling well with Strength.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

The skill, Spinning Slash, is potentially quite damaging, especially if it catches another player offguard and with low Poise, though it's somewhat hampered by the lack of reach on Straight Swords. 
Does best as a pure Strength weapon, as Dexterity and Intelligence are somewhat hampered by having much lower scaling numbers and being based off the lower Magic base damage respectively. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 652 Attack Power (AP), 45 Strength and 45 Intelligence grants 632 AP, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 624 AP, and 80 Intelligence grants 560 AP.
A good offhand weapon for those wishing to dual-wield Straight Swords on a Strength build with some Intelligence, due to the ease of upgrading weapons reliant on Somber Smithing Stones and its somewhat mediocre skill not mattering there.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Crystalians are humanoid beings with inorganic, crystalline bodies. Chiseled from pure blue glintstone, they wear red capes and wield crystal weaponry.

In combat, Crystalians are initially highly resistant to attacks; however, breaking their stance will lower their defense, rendering them significantly more susceptible to all forms of attack, and prevent most weapons from bouncing of them. Keep in mind that backstabs are still available even if the Crystalians are armored so dashing in for a Critical Attack with a Strike weapon is very useful to make sure one dies as quickly as possible. 

Putrid Crystalians are infected by Scarlet Rot. Although their movesets are identical to the standard variations, they also inflict Scarlet Rot buildup.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Crystalians cleave close to the ideals of the primeval current and are regarded as guests by the sorcerers. They possess a form of cognition known as the "wisdom of the stone", and bear the sole purpose of safeguarding their crystals until the end. They wield weaponry fashioned from crystal, a deed impossible for a human, and are believed by some to await the return of their creator who will craft them new brethren.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
An ascetic of the tower, Labirith renounced mortal comfort and trained her body through harsh discipline to ascend as a tutelary deity. She donned a masked crown of tangled horns to heighten her spirituality and dampen her focus, enabling the Divine Beast to take hold. She performed crazed, ritualistic dances using circular backhand blades with sharp, wave-like pointed edges, spilling her own blood in frantic spiritual fervor.

The other hornsent disdained and shunned the Curseblades as a scourge. Labirith's own people captured her and sealed her deep in the freezing Bonny Gaol among the jars, where she ultimately failed to become a tutelary deity. In this subterranean prison, she met Curseblade Meera. When Meera died, Labirith fell into a devastating darkness.

name: D, Beholder of Death
description:
D, Beholder of Death is an NPC in Elden Ring.

He is also possible to summon as a co-operator for the Valiant Gargoyles boss.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Devin, more commonly known as "D", is the twin-brother of Darian, who is also known as D. The two twins had separate minds and bodies, but shared a single soul. For this, they were reviled as accursed beings, but found solace in the Golden Order, which accepted them both.

Travelling deep below ground, to the very roots of the Erdtree, Devin came face to face with the Prince of Death himself. The encounter appears to have nearly shattered Devin's mind, as he came to dwell in the Siofra Aqueduct, barely able to speak.

When Devin's twin was murdered by Fia, a servant of the Prince of Death, a Tarnished champion delivered Darian's armor to Devin. Seemingly acknowledging that Darian had died, but still barely able to speak, Devin gathered himself, and if requested, helps the Tarnished champion clear the way to the Deeproot Depths.

After Fia is given the other half of the Cursemark of Death, allowing her to lay with the Prince of Death in order to produce a Rune of Death, Devin will finally find her, and kill her. The Tarnished champion can find Devin gloating and taunting the Prince of Death, cursing him and the murdered Fia. Having avenged his brother, Devin declares he has no more regrets and prays for the honeyed rays of gold to deliver his spirit, so that he may once again look his brother in the eye.

name: D, Hunter of the Dead
description:
D, Hunter of the Dead is an NPC in Elden Ring. 

He is also possible to summon as a cooperator in Black Knife Catacombs.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Darian, more commonly known as D, Hunter of the Dead is an undead hunter and an ally of Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Darian has a twin brother by the name of Devin, who was also called D. While Darian and Devin had different minds and bodies, they shared a single soul, and were reviled as cursed beings. The twins found sanctuary in the Golden Order, the only institution to accept them.

Darian befriended the spellblade Rogier, with whom he shared an interest in Those Who Live in Death. The two friends eventually parted ways, each coming to their own conclusion about the undead.

Darian became a proponent of Golden Order fundamentalism and a hunter of Those Who Live in Death, seeking to stamp out defilement and preserve the perfection of the Golden Order. Darian encountered and became an ally of Gurranq, who bid him to weed out Deathroot, a plant which caused the emergence of Those Who Live in Death, so that he might feed it to him.

Following the traces of death, Darian came upon Summonwater Village, where a Tibia Mariner had set up shop. In the outskirts of the village, he encounters a Tarnished champion and warns them to stay away from the village. After the champion defeats the Mariner and weeds out the Deathroot, Darian offers them a deal; to take his place as Gurranq's servant, in exchange for Gurranq sharing with them the strength of beasts.

With other matters to attend to, Darian relocates to Roundtable Hold. After the Tarnished takes him up on his offer, he declares them brothers-in-arms and teaches them the fundamentalist techniques wielded by the hunters of the dead. Another resident of Roundtable Hold and associate of the Tarnished champion is Fia, a deathbed companion and servant of the Prince of Death. Fia gives the Tarnished a dagger, asking them to find its rightful owner. After the Tarnished shows Darian the dagger, he offers to return it to its owner.

Shortly thereafter, Darian is murdered by Fia. The Tarnished champion may retrieve Darian's armor and find his twin. Devin will don the armor, and avenge his brother, finding Fia at the foot of the Prince of Death and murdering her.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Together with the Rapier this weapon has the second strongest critical multiplier at 130 (the Miséricorde has the highest, at 140). 
Has low enough requirements to be used with any starting class's default attributes and is fairly common, making it a decent secondary weapon for backstabbing and other critical hits, especially for those who don't have the stats to wield the Miséricorde. 
Generally Dexterity-leaning on its affinities and performs best on a Keen affinity (having scaling just short of S-tier scaling) but also works surprisingly well with the Occult affinity, even if it lacks any of the innate Status Effects required to truly take advantage of this. 
Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen). 
The shortest of all daggers.

name: Dark Moon
description: The Dark Moon is a celestial body in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Dark Moon first appeared to Lunar Princess Ranni in her youth, during an encounter arranged by her mother, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. Later, a heretical snowy witch who once tutored Ranni deep in the woods warned her of its occult influence, but the young Empyrean disregarded the warning. Moons were traditional symbols of the Carian Royal Family, and the Dark Moon came to embody Ranni's power and authority. Her vassals, too, swore fealty to the cold Dark Moon.

Game events:
If Ranni succeeds Queen Marika, she will usher in an age of the Stars, guided by the wisdom of the Dark Moon. It manifests at the Stone Platform when she inherits the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: It may be related to the Black Moon of Nokstella, Eternal City, but that moon was shattered into pieces long ago.

The Dark Moon Greatsword is Elden Ring’s version of the Moonlight Greatsword, which has appeared in multiple other FromSoftware games. Additionally, the name of the sword’s Unique Skill also alludes to this.
The Chinese and Korean release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "A greatsword of guidance bestowed on Ranni the Witch by the Two Fingers. The very Rune of Mind that will lead the next generation." The role of Carian matrimonial sword was instead filled by the Sword of Night and Flame.

name: Death (outer god)
image: ER Icon Key Item Rune of Death.png
description: Death is a concept and outer god mentioned and.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
All manner of Death drifted the Lands Between, washing up on its old shores from unknown and far-off origins. The outer god of Death held great sway over these lands, long before the age of the Erdtree. The first grave keepers were Tibia Mariners, who guided the dead long after withering away. Since antiquity, Death was brought to the Gravesite Plain, where the oldest gravestones turned into spiritgraves before fading away.

The Ancestral Followers believed winged envoys reaped the lives of those who did not bud new life. According to pagan belief, white-winged maidens were Death's gentle messengers, delivering death in holy light. Another envoy, the two-headed Twinbird, likely representative of the sun and its soul-granting eclipse, mothered the wicked Deathbirds, keepers of the violet ghostflame. These black-winged raptors cremated corpses within their kilns, raking ashes to release vengeful spirits. Even the impure, tainted putrescence of heroes was given equal treatment in death upon reaching the Cerulean Coast in stone coffin arks.

Some Servants of Death clung to life in hopes of offering up a death worth taking, while others achieved favor and glory by confronting death with courage. If their end came in battle, they were ushered through the spirit world by the red lamplight of the Helphen—a phenomenon akin to the Erdtree's grace. The Servants of Death revered the malevolent Deathbirds as deities, and entered the rite of Death to aid them. In return for serving as the Death Rite Birds' wings, they secured their eventual resurrection.

At some point the Suppressing Pillar in the Gravesite Plain was created to indicate the center of the Lands Between and the region where Death converged and was quelled.

Age of the Erdtree:
Death was suppressed when Queen Marika established the Golden Order; the Rune of Death was sealed in Maliketh's Black Blade. However, a shard was later stolen on the Night of Black Knives and used to slay both Godwyn the Golden and Lunar Princess Ranni. Godwyn, whose soul was killed while his body lived, was buried beneath the Erdtree, where he transformed into the Prince of Death. This event marked the spread of Deathroot through the Greattree's roots, giving rise to Tibia Mariners and Those Who Live in Death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Charo and Tibia are associated with Death.
At some point, the Lands Between were ruled by a soulless lord named Ensha, a champion of the lost and desperate. He was likely brought to life by the eclipsed sun, which granted life to soulless bones.
Enir-Ilim practiced hexes for spirit-calling in ancient times. The tower is guarded by Gravebirds enwreathed in Rings of Spectral Light.
Death is somewhat associated with St. Trina's Eternal Sleep.
Death is opposed to Scarlet Rot, which is the cycle of decay and rebirth. Like the Crystalians who follow the primeval current, Those Who Live in Death are particularly troubled by Scarlet Rot.
Destined Death likely slays the Lord of Frenzied Flame to maintain the fated death of the One Great.

name: Death Rite Bird
description: Death Rite Birds are optional recurring bosses in. They only appear at night and are a more powerful version of the deathbirds.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.body:
The Death Rite Bird often spawns from a giant ball of Ghostflame up in the sky.

It is possible to lock onto either the boss's head or the spine. It takes extra damage when hit in the head, but due to how much it moves, it can disorienting and result in getting dead-angled when blocking, so it's usually safer to lock into the spine or not at all.

While it is possible to fight this boss on horseback, it is not recommended. The safest place to be in melee range is behind its legs, where neither the weapon swings, nor the beak can hit you.

This boss can be staggered when dealt enough damage, giving you a window to land a Critical Attack on its head.

Weaknesses:
As they count as Those Who Live in Death they are weak to Holy damage and extremely weak to specific anti-undead weapons. Ash of War: Sacred Blade and Holy Water Pots are useful tools to make short work of these enemies, even if the user doesn't have a lot of Faith. 

Moveset:

The first phase is very similar to a normal Deathbird fight, with the difference that its melee attacks deal both physical and ghostflame damage, making shields somewhat less effective although blocking is still preferable to receiving the damage directly.

moveset: Deathbirds usually rely on melee attacks, which can be either dodged or blocked, except for their peck and grab attacks. It's recommended to avoid being under its head to avoid getting pecked.
| Melee Attack || Many of this boss's swipe attacks have it move backwards, meaning rolling towards it tends to result in getting hit.
| Peck || If the player is directly under the bird's head, it will do a peck attack from above.
| Grab || When the player is at mid range (not close enough to melee but not extremely far away), the bird can try a grab attack that can be dodged. If not dodged, it will inflict heavy damage.
| Screech || A short screech that inflicts Death Blight if close. Will follow up with a grab attack if the player is at mid-range.
| Ghostflame Ignition || Uses its Death's Poker to cast Unique Skill: Ghostflame Ignition, spreading lingering ghostflame. Deals Magic damage and inflicts Frostbite.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Demi-Humans are typically small in stature and bestial in appearance, often possessing fur, canine faces, and pointed ears. Although they are intelligent and capable of speech, as exemplified by Boc the Seamster, they are typically violent and brutish, particularly at night when their blood boils and they turn feral.

Demi-Humans wield a variety of weapons, such as falchions, daggers, and clubs. Those considered to be the toughest wield spiked clubs, which they believe to be a badge of honor.

Demi-Human society appears to be hierarchical, with the lesser Demi-Humans following much larger Demi-Human Chiefs. Demi-Humans lose hope if their leader dies, causing them to panic and stop attacking. At the top of the Demi-Human hierarchy are the Queens, who are capable of wielding rudimentary sorceries via their staves. 

Despite their violent demeanour, Demi-Humans are capable of fostering diplomatic relations with humans, with Kenneth Haight building an alliance with a group of Demi-Humans in Fort Haight.

sections.heading: Appearance

sections.heading: Notes

image: ER Boss Demi-Human Swordmaster Onze profile.png
description: Demi-Human Swordmaster Onze is an optional boss in. He is encountered at the Belurat Gaol.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
In a bygone era, when beasts were granted intelligence, the demi-human swordsmen were bequeathed Star-Lined Swords by their queens. Their royal blades were encrusted with shards of crude glintstone, symbolizing the procession of the stars. Each swordsman swore an oath to unveil the secret that awaited at the end of the line of stars.

Onze was a master swordsman who devoted himself to the Star-Lined Sword. When Onze realized that only ruin awaited at the end, he imprisoned himself in order to forestall it. His devoted apprentice, Yosh, defied him and spent the remainder of his days in hermitage by his side.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.body: Onze is an elderly demi-human swordsmen, small in stature with mottled, pale skin. He wears a filthy loincloth and a tattered cape clasped with rope. He has five fingers. His milky eyes are fully clouded over and thin wisps of white hair hang from his scalp and chin. Despite his withered appearance, he is nimble and deadly with his magical sword.

Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
St. Trina
Starscourge Radahn

The Golden Lineage:

The first Demigods were Godfrey, First Elden Lord and his descendants, known as the Golden Lineage. The confirmed members of the Golden Lineage are Morgott, the Omen King, his twin Mohg, Lord of Blood, Godrick the Grafted, Godefroy the Grafted, and the Grafted Scions. Godwyn the Golden's name, title, and the pattern on his clothing suggests his descendancy from the Golden Lineage. 

Godrick the Grafted was only a distant relation, his divine blood linking him to Marika sorely diluted, indicating unseen generations of Golden Lineage demigods. According to Kenneth Haight, Godrick is the last of the Golden Lineage, but the Grafted Scions are also suggested to be the dregs of the Golden Lineage. 

When Godfrey was divested of his Grace, he became Tarnished, and lost his demigod status.

Carian Royal Family:

After Godfrey was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon became King Consort and second Elden Lord by marrying Queen Marika. This led to the children he conceived with Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon becoming demigod stepchildren, including Starscourge Radahn, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and Ranni the Witch.

Messmer and Melina:
Messmer and Melina are both children of Marika.
It is often speculated that the Kindling Maiden Melina may be a demigod, as she is called "DaughterMarika" internally and states her mother is inside the Erdtree. Furthermore, she is bound by Grace, quotes ancient words of Marika, and implied to be the younger sister of Messmer the Impaler. Like Messmer, Melina is associated with a butterfly and is fated to fulfill a purpose.

Twin Prodigies:
The union of Radagon and Marika led to the birth of at least two more demigods, the twins Miquella of the Haligtree and Malenia, Blade of Miquella, however they suffered afflictions from birth; the former was born with a curse of eternal childhood, and the latter harbored Scarlet Rot within.

Soulless Demigods:

The Wandering Mausoleums found throughout the Lands Between cradle the corpses of soulless demigods. At least eight demigods became these soulless demigods, and at least one of them is an unwanted child of Queen Marika's. They are guarded by the Mausoleum Knights, who watch over a soulless demigod until their resurrection.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
According to Finger Reader Enia, the demigods are each and all the direct offspring of Queen Marika.
According to the Overview Trailer, the demigods are "those who have inherited the blood of Queen Marika the Eternal."

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
According to game director Hidetaka Miyazaki, the main demigod bosses of the game were initially written by George R. R. Martin. As part of the creative process, Martin wrote the initial characters as grand heroes, and FromSoftware took them developed the way in which their Great Runes misshaped and distorted them.
Localisation Notes
Rather than "unwanted child", the soulless demigod(s) of the mausoleum is referred to as Queen Marika's "ugly bastard" or "ugly spawn." (醜い落とし子, Minikui otoshi-ko.)

description: Discus of Light is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 11,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Goldmask's location in Altus.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation after moving to Goldmask's location, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: If Corhyn dies before this incantation appears in his inventory then it will become unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Throws out a ring of light with Holy Attack Power equal to 150% of Incantation Scaling and going through foes, stopping when it reaches its maximum range or hits an object. 

The ring begins to return to the caster shortly after arriving at its destination, having the same Attack Power for its attack against all foes it passes through.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. 
Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case). 
Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%. 
Effectively has Attack Power roughly equal to 300% of Incantation Scaling per cast since it will very often hit the main target on the way back. 
Several rings can be out at the same time, making the spell very spammable. 
Pairs well with the Erdtree Greatshield's skill Golden Retaliation and the Ash of War: Carian Retaliation since the timing of the returning ring is very predictable and will trigger the spell-parry-into-projectile part of those skills. 
Can be cast while riding Torrent, further extending the incantation's usability and ability to be spammed. 
The caster takes a short step forwards each time the spell is cast. While many steep falls prevent a character from stepping over them from movement caused by Skills, Spells, and Weapons, it's still good to be a bit careful. 
Though it goes through all enemies it will not ignore the damage reduction from an enemy that is keeping its guard up if they are guarding in the direction it's flying from. 
Note that it will still fly through said guarding enemy and will hit their unprotected back when returning unless said enemy turns around in between the two hits.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 reduced FP and stamina consumption, increased the range, speed, and duration of the halo, and increased casting speed.
Decreased FP cost from 9 to 3. 
Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost, increased damage, and cast speed.
Decreased FP cost from 11 to 9. Attack Power was increased from 114% of Incantation Scaling to 150% of Incantation Scaling.

name: Divine Beast Dancing Lion
image: Shadow of the Erdtree promotional screenshot 7.jpg
description: The Divine Beast Dancing Lion is an optional boss in. The Remembrace variant may be encountered in the Belurat, Tower Settlement. The lion dancer at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh may be fought on Horseback.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The divine beasts were messengers of the heavens. The sculpted keepers are representations used to perform the ritual of the lion dance during the tower festival in Belurat, Tower Settlement. Only the greatest of horned warriors became divine beast warriors, and few became sculpted keepers.

When Messmer the Impaler's army assailed the tower, the lion dance was turned towards martial ends.. By the end of Messmer's Crusade, only two divine beasts remained: one inside of Belurat, and another in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The one in Belurat was under the control of Hornsent Grandam, who directed the divine beast to rest until the Impaler's forces returned so it could exact vengeance for her people. When a Tarnished Champion happened upon the divine beast's resting place, Grandam assumed them to be one of Messmer's prodigies and ordered the divine beast to slay the Tarnished. It failed to do so, however, and was slain. The Tarnished can also encounter and slay the other divine beasts while exploring Rauh, thereby putting an end to them.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
The Divine Beast will fight normally in its first phase. Around 70% health, it will switch between three storm-based elements on a timed basis: Lightning, Frost, and Wind.

The Divine Beast Dancing Lion at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh also has access to Death Blight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: If the player opted to kill Hornsent Grandam before confronting the Divine Beast in Belarut, it will be shown that she survived the assault, resulting in a change to a more desperate and weary voice acting in the Divine Beast's introduction cutscene.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Swirls around twice to gather winds, then throws them forwards in a storm to create a tornado at the endpoint, hitting with Standard Attack Power equal to 220% of Incantation Scaling along the way and at the end.

Can be charged to increase Attack Power to 275% of Incantation Scaling and to launch hit foes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 26 points of Stamina. 
Deals 8 Stance damage with the tornado itself, and 3 Stance damage with the staggering winds cast when starting the incantation. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25%, the total Attack Power increase is 44%. 
Deals much more damage if an enemy is hit at the edge of this spell's range, where the tornado lingers, since they will be hit by the traveling hitbox and the end hitbox. 
Note that there is no hyperarmor when casting this spell, and the hitbox from the start-up animation will only stagger very weak enemies. This, combined with the greatest damage happening at the edge of its range, means that this incantation should be cast when far away from enemies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This incantation, much like Catch Flame, Divine Bird Feathers, Fire's Deadly Sin, and Flame Sling, doesn't create a subtype sigil when cast. 
Patch 1.13 increased attack power; enemies hit by the tornado will now be launched upwards, and the tornado will be less likely to disappear due to collision with the terrain. 
Only the fully charged version launches enemies. 
The Attack Power of the uncharged version was increased from 160% of Incantation Scaling to 220% of the same, and from 200% of Incantation to 275% of the same for the charged version.

description: Divine Fortification is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed Drop: Weeping Peninsula
Divine Fortification is obtained upon defeating the Teardrop Scarab found atop a fallen ruin near the Tombsward Ruins.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Divine Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Holy damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 FP per cast.
Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces holy damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where DivineFortification represents the effect magnitude:
TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {HolyDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {DivineFortification}) )
For example, if holy damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

Strategies:
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as holy damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple holy negation sources.
Divine Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Holy damage in the game, particularly when facing enemies like Cleanrot Knights, Erdtree Avatars, Miranda Blossoms, and Oracle Envoys, especially while exploring Miquella's Haligtree.
Divine Fortification offers the same holy protection as Holyproof Dried Liver (35%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
The Holyproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.

name: Dragon
description: Dragons, also known as drakes, are enemies and bosses in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Dragons are the mortal descendants of the Ancient Dragons, who once ruled the Lands Between during a prehistoric era. Unlike their predecessors, their fleshy hides bore no Gravel Stone scales. They possessed fewer limbs and flew on feathered wings. Their snouts were more narrow and terminated in diminutive maxillary beaks.

The dragons were idolized by humans for their sheer strength and sublime beauty. However, the ancient dragons viewed them as lowborn, paltry imitations. While the drakes inherited the fiery breath of their forebears, they could not channel their red lightning. Yet, their vivacious red hearts were covered in sacred gravel stones.

Dragon Communion:
]]

In a long bygone age, the progenitor of mortal drakes assailed Dragonlord Placidusax in a failed bid for power that left both dragons grievously wounded. On that day, the traitor, Bayle the Dread, and his entire bloodline were sentenced to death. Many lesser dragons were hunted and devoured in retaliation for Bayle's treachery.

The ancient dragon Florissax assumed mortal form to introduce the practice of Dragon Communion to humans. The drakes became prey for landbound warriors, who pursued their power with Gravel Stone weapons and consumed their hearts. To drake warriors, no flesh was finer than the heated essence of dragons, and their bottomless hunger became a vehicle for the Dragonlord's wrath.

Later events:, ready for grafting]]
Well before the first astrologers and the Erdtree, ice dragons held dominion over the Mountaintops. Some time later, they were defeated by the Fire Giants, who drove them the Flame Peak.

Many dragons in the current age descend from Elder Dragon Greyoll, a mother drake of colossal size. Following the Battle of Aeonia, Greyoll and her offspring fled the Scarlet Rot by settling on a plateau in the northern reaches of Caelid, later known as Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.

sections.heading: Variants

Dragons who settled in northern Caelid with their mother, Elder Dragon Greyoll.

There are six red-eyed Flying Dragons surrounding Greyoll. Greyoll will lose 20% of her health with each Dragon killed, meaning that killing five will cause Greyoll to die.

Glintstone Dragon=

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.body:
Flying Dragons:

Flying Dragon Agheel=

Flying Dragon Agheel Overview
Wandering Nobles in the ruins around the lake chant Agheel's name, praying that it will burn them to ash. Flying Dragon Agheel is encountered in Agheel Lake in southern Limgrave, northwest of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins. It appears by flying down from above, torching a congregation of Wandering Nobles with dragonfire.

Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is available as a summon for this fight, after speaking to him under the ruin south of the lake.

After taking a critical hit, the target receives an additional 20% standard damage for the remainder of the fight.

Defeating Flying Dragon Agheel will unlock Agheel's Flame, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

Moveset

Flying Dragon Greyll=

Flying Dragon Greyll Overview
A Flying Dragon encountered on the Farum Greatbridge (bridge south of Bestial Sanctum), on the northern peninsula of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Greyll is identical to Agheel in both appearance and ability. However, the bridge gives the player much less room to maneuver. 

Moveset

Glintstone Dragons:

Glintstone Dragon Smarag=

Glintstone Dragon Smarag Overview
A devourer of sorcerers, whose body gradually became corrupted by the glintstones of those he ate. Smarag is encountered near an island west of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and north of the Temple Quarter, guarding a corpse that holds the Academy Glintstone Key. Note that it is not necessary to kill this dragon to get the Academy Glintstone Key; it can be retrieved by either sneaking behind it or rushing beyond it before it's fully awakened to get at the corpse.

Smarag is able to fire Glintstone Cometshards from his mouth, and can also unleash magic breath, akin to the fire breath of other Dragons.

Defeating Glintstone Dragon Smarag will unlock Smarag's Glintstone Breath, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts. 

Moveset

Glintstone Dragon Adula=

Glintstone Dragon Adula Overview
A devourer of sorcerers, whose body became corrupted by glintstone. Adula was once bested by Ranni the Witch and subsequently swore a knightly oath to her Dark Moon.

Adula is first encountered outside Ranni's Rise in the Three Sisters, north of Caria Manor. After a brief fight, it disappears, only to reappear at the Moonlight Altar outside the Cathedral of Manus Celes. 

Adula can use magic breath, much like Smarag. However, it can also utilize Adula's Moonblade, conjuring a magic blade in its maw mid-flight and unleashing a wave that inflicts Frostbite.

Moveset

Decaying Ekzykes:

A Dragon plagued by scarlet rot, encountered north-west of the Cathedral of Dragon Communion. Also known as the Dragon Communion Revenger, Ekzykes did not forget his hatred even as he succumbed to the rot.

Instead of flames, Ekzykes breathes toxic clouds that inflict Scarlet Rot, covering a large area and taking a few seconds to dissipate. Its stomps also produce a small cloud of Scarlet Rot.

Defeating Decaying Ekzykes will unlock Ekzykes's Decay, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts. 

Borealis the Freezing Fog:

One of the ice dragons, who were lords of the Mountaintops before the Fire Giants chased them from the peak. Borealis is encountered on the frozen lake in the northeast of the Mountaintops, emerging from a thick white fog.

Borealis exhales clouds that inflict Frostbite. Its stomps also produce small clouds of Frostbite.

Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts. 

Elder Dragon Greyoll:

Greyoll is known as the mother of the lesser dragons. She is a massive but stationary dragon encountered in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, just south of Fort Faroth. She is immobile, either having grown too weak to move or as a result of having fused with the surrounding rocks, but can still let loose fearsome roars to weaken her enemies. 

Defeating any of the six lesser dragons surrounding her will cause large amounts of damage to her, and killing them all will kill her. 

Defeating Elder Dragon Greyoll will unlock Greyoll's Roar, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for three Dragon Hearts.

name: Dragon Communion
description: is a historical practice in. It involves the hunting of drakes, the descendants of Ancient Dragons, in pursuit of their gravel stone-covered hearts. Specifically, Dragon Communion is the act of consuming dragon hearts to acquire the draconic powers within. The hearts are consumed at a Dragon Communion Altar, which is usually in the presence of a fallen dragon.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
In the distant past, the lord of the ancient dragons, Placidusax, was attacked by the great drake, Bayle the Dread. Their clash ended in a stalemate and left both gravely injured, with Bayle fleeing the field of battle. As vengeance for Bayle's transgression, Placidusax had some of his followers take mortal forms as humanoid priestesses and travel to the lands of men, where they would beckon human warriors to their cause. They established the practice of dragon communion to hunt down and punish Bayle and his descendants, the drakes. The human warriors were lured to this cause with the promise of great power, which could only be acquired by consuming the heart of a drake.

As time passed, the practice continued without the priestesses' influence; however, many practitioners forgot the original purpose of these hunts and continued consuming hearts for personal gain. Many practitioners develop a hunger for hearts as they hunt, which gradually intensifies the more hearts they devour. This leads many to commune without restraint, an act that has dire consequences for their humanity, as their bodies and minds gradually become increasingly draconic. The result is transformation into Magma Wyrms, dragon-like creatures with pitifully small wings, incapable of flight, and cursed to crawl the earth on their bellies until the end of their days. Ironically, this end often comes at the hands of their fellow communers as their own hearts are now a sufficient target for dragon communion as well.

sections.heading: Dragon Communion Altars
sections.body:
]]
Dragon Communion can be performed at Dragon Communion Altars, though certain powers may only be redeemed at specific Altars. There are three Dragon Communion Altars in the Lands Between:
Church of Dragon Communion
Cathedral of Dragon Communion
Grand Altar of Dragon Communion

sections.heading: Known Practitioners of Dragon Communion
sections.body:
Ancient Dragon-Man
Ancient Dragons
Drake Knights
Drake Warrior Igon
Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger

Nameless Magma Wyrm at Mt. Gelmir

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Some drakes have become aware of this practice, such as Ekzykes the Decaying, who even after succumbing to Malenia's rot would never forget his hatred and thus keeps himself stationed at the entrance of the Cathedral of Dragon Communion, so that he may kill or deter any would-be practitioners before they can reach the altar.
Yura, Hunter of Bloody Fingers abstains from consuming dragon hearts to avoid the risk of losing himself, though it's possible he once did, and bargained with Shabriri to escape his fate.
The ultimate form of Dragon Communion is consuming the Heart of Bayle.
Feasting on Rock Hearts was the ancient, original form of Dragon Communion, transforming oneself into an Ancient Dragon.

name: Dragon Communion Seal
image: ER Icon weapon Dragon Communion Seal.png
description: The Dragon Communion Seal is a Sacred Seal in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Dropped by a spectral Banished Knight located in the Fringefolk Hero's Grave in Limgrave. To find it, start at the Stranded Graveyard Site of Grace and head down the first two ramps in the Grave, then head right in the split to go up another two ramps. The Knight is inside a small room at the end of the ramp and is quite tough for the early game. The Chariot in the dungeon can be used to help kill it, though that comes at considerable risk to the player as well.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This Sacred Seal is best used for split Arcane/Faith builds, with an even split being slightly more favorable over one more biased towards Arcane. It can also be used for a pure Arcane build but that alternative is slightly weaker, by about 7-8%. 
For comparison: a 45/45 Arc/Fth split gives 336 Scaling at +10, a 60/30 Arc/Fth split gives 333 Scaling at +10, and a 80/10 Arc/Fth split gives 310 Scaling at +10. 
Holding a Dragon Communion Seal (DCS) in one of your active hands will boost the damage of directly damaging Dragon Communion Incantations by 15%.
Holding a DCS in each active hand (that is, two Seals that are each held in separate hands) will increase the damage boost to 32.25% (1.15*1.15=1.3225). 
The damage boost is still granted if the other piece of equipment is two-handed. 
This bonus stacks with the 20% damage boost granted when reactivating the Rock Heart. 
Any incantation that inflicts Poison (except for Poison Armament), Madness, or non-bloodflame Blood Loss build-up and is cast using this Seal will have their Status Effect scale with the wielder's Arcane stat. 
This status build-up bonus is equivalent to a fifth of the regular Weapon Scaling bonus from Stat Scaling, meaning that with a +10 DCS's scaling with Arcane being at 2.25 this caps at 45% (0.2*2.25=0.45). 
Of the Blood Loss-inflicting incantations only Swarm of Flies inflicts any direct Blood Loss-build up (70 build-up out of its total 150 build-up) as direct status build-up instead of as part of a non-scaling bloodflame effect. 
It would theoretically also scale the amount of Sleep build-up of any incantation that inflicts such a Status Effect. However, no incantation that inflicts that status effect exists. 
Curiously Scarlet Rot build-up doesn't scale with Arcane, even though the spell type can inflict that status effect. 
The weight being 0 means and the existence of Physical Dragon Communion Incantations such as Dragonmaw and Rotten Breath means this Seal works well with the Blue Dancer Charm weight-based increase to Physical damage. 
This synergy is further enhanced by the existence of the Rock Heart, essentially a 0 weight armor set that can increase the damage of Dragon Communion Incantations even further. 
This Seal is very unsuitable for casting Weapon Buff or direct healing spells as those depend entirely on the Faith portion of the used Seal's scaling, and this Seal only have about a third of the Faith scaling that pure Faith scaling Seals such as the Finger Seal and Erdtree Seal have.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.04 decreased the scaling of status effect build-up from spells and incantations of Albinauric Staff and Dragon Communion Seal.
Previously both of these casting implements full Arcane-scaling would apply to the Status Effects build-up of spells cast with them. For a +10 Dragon Communion Seal, this meant that almost the full S (2.25) would be applied thus resulting in roughly 3 times the Status Effect build-up on builds with high Arcane which would often result in instant or near instant application of Madness with spells such as Frenzied Burst.

description: Dragon King's Cragblade is a melee armament found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Trade the Remembrance of the Dragonlord, gained by defeating Dragonlord Placidusax, with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This weapon's Guard Counters become Thrusting Counterattacks.
Has a 30% damage boost against Dragons and a 15% damage boost against Ancient Dragons. 
Since this weapon primarily deals Pierce-type damage, which is most dragons weakness, it is well suited to this anti-dragon role. Be aware that Borealis, the Freezing Fog, is a Pierce-resistant dragon and that all Ancient Dragons resist the secondary Lightning damage. 
The Dexterity-scaling is responsible for increasing both the Physical damage and the Lightning damage. 
The Physical/Lightning split is roughly 60%/40%. 

Scales best with Dexterity, up to the 80 point softcap. 
The skill is chargeable, benefiting from the Godfrey Icon. 
Has a unique heavy attack, shared with the Bloody Helice. In comparison with the default one, found on the Godskin Stitcher, the regular heavy attack has longer reach, the charge heavy attack is a lunging thrust instead of a short-ranged double thrust, and the feint (done by dodging when charging a heavy attack).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.04 decreased the skill's cost from 35 FP to 28 FP, decreased its recovery time, and decreased the damage of the uncharged version of the skill. Also increased skill cast speed.
