name: Dragonbolt Blessing
description: Dragonbolt Blessing is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Altus Plateau
Dragonbolt Blessing is found in a treasure chest within Stormcaller Church.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Summons a crackling aura that increases the resistance to all Status Effects by 30 and causes the one-handed light attacks of non-Great or Colossal weapons to be deflected. This also reduces the caster's Lightning Damage Negation by 35% and counts as a Body Buff, and lasts for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
Deflects the one-handed regular light attacks of Daggers, Throwing Blades, Straight Swords, Thrusting Swords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Curved Swords, Backhand Blades, Katanas, Great Katanas, Twinblades, Axes, Spears, the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear Great Spear, Halberds, Reapers, the Katar and Pata Fists, Claws, and Beast Claws. 
Unarmed attacks are also deflected. 
One-handed regular light attacks from Staves, Sacred Seals, Torches, and Small Shields are also deflected. 
Fists besides the Katar and Pata aren't deflected. 
For Daggers, Thrusting Swords (except the Estoc and Noble's Estoc, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Heavy Thrusting Swords (except the Sword Lance, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Twinblades, Axes (except the Iron Cleaver and Celebrant's Cleaver, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Spears, the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear, Reapers, the Katar and Pata, Claws, and Beast Claws, one-handed regular heavy attacks and running light attacks are also deflected. 
For Katanas, running light attacks are also deflected. 
For Light Greatswords, one-handed regular heavy attacks are actually deflected. 
For Thrusting Swords, running heavy attacks, rolling light attacks, and backstep light attacks are also deflected. 
For Heavy Thrusting Swords, rolling light attacks and backstep light attacks are also deflected. 
Combines well with the Skill: Raptor of the Mists since that skill will also make the user dodge an attack that would have hit them, thus preventing the damage, while the slight stun of the Dragonbolt Blessing can make it easier to land the attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: This incantation actually deflects all weapon attacks with an AttackRepel value below 70.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Quest Item: Jagged Peak
Given by the Dragon Communion Priestess at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion after giving her Thiollier's Concoction at night and waiting for her to wake up (and then repeatedly talking to her), and then finally defeating Bayle the Dread. 
This item is mutually exclusive with the Priestess Heart and Flowerstone Gavel. 
Continue talking to her and both confess to be the one that put her to sleep and accept her into your service to receive the Ancient Dragon Florissax Spirit Ash. 
Since this requires Thiollier's Concoction, make sure to get that item by giving him the Black Syrup from Moore at Belurat, Tower Settlement (obtained by speaking to both of them several times) and then giving the Syrup to Thiollier BEFORE defeating the Putrescent Knight or approaching Shadow Keep too closely.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Increases the Damage Negation by 10% (5% in PvP) for the user and allies within 7 meters, and also decreases damage taken when Guarding by 20%. 

Counts as an Aura Buff and lasts for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. 
Since this is an Aura Buff, it has to compete with the Golden Vow spell, which it compares rather unfavorably towards as that one grants a stronger Damage Negation bonus and a Damage bonus, and takes considerably less Faith to use. 
The reduction to damage taken through blocking is applied after the damage has already been reduced by the blocking equipment's own Blocking Damage Negation. 
Also used by Ancient Dragon Florissax, though a new Journey must be started to attain both on the same character. 
Be wary that Florissax can overwrite a possibly more beneficial Aura Buff cast by someone else.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from a corpse that lies on the ground, near Bestial Sanctum, in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Equipping the Longtail Cat Talisman here, or using Soft Cotton is very helpful, as there are several parkour drops coming up that will deal unavoidable damage, and there are Bat enemies in the area. From the front door of the sanctum, head southwest around the side of the sanctum, until reaching a cliff that overlooks a large tree root, close enough to drop to. Drop from here to the branch, to another branch, to a domed rooftop, and then to the first of 3 ring structures, jutting out from the cliffside. Jump up to the ledge surrounding the nearby pillar, walk across the buttress to the next pillar, drop to the lower ledge, jump to another lower ledge on the first pillar, and drop down to the second ring. Jump to the next-lower ledge on the outer pillar, walk across the buttress, and jump to a ledge that sticks out from the wall below. At this point, it is recommended to mount Torrent, as the final jump is extremely difficult to make on foot, while almost trivial to make with Torrent's double-jump ability. The third ring below is just barely beyond the instant-death threshold for falling, so instead, aim for the ledge on that outer pillar, just a few feet above the ring. After finally reaching the third ring, head northeast along it to find the corpse.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, or the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Creates a dragon head before breathing out a wave of flames, dealing Fire damage equal to 144% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e., 432% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast, with an additional 40 points required upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Agheel's Flame. 
Compared to Agheel's Flame, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 30% less FP. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 104 FP: 2*28 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 53 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath, and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains, as it will continue casting regardless.
This is the second strongest "default" dragon breath attack, dealing 9% less damage than Glintstone Breath if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation are equal. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:

The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: Effects

Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of frozen mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 135% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 110 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 405% of the same and 330 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. 

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 48 points of Stamina to cast, and another 48 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
This spell can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast in midair, unlike Borealis's Mist and Ghostflame Breath. 
Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Borealis's Mist, and Ghostflame Breath), this is the most cost-effective for inflicting Frostbite, but causes less damage than the other two breaths. 
Compared to Borealis's Mist, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 29% less FP. 
Compared to Ghostflame Breath, this spell deals 20% less damage but consumes 17% less FP and causes 100% more Frostbite build-up. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 120 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running. 
Only 65 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless. 
This is the second weakest "default" dragon breath attack, dealing 15% less damage than Glintstone Breath and 6% less damage than Dragonfire (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals only 3% more damage than Rotten Breath. 
However, the Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

name: Dragonlord Placidusax
description: Dragonlord Placidusax is a Remembrance Boss in, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Dragonlord Placidusax is a quadrupedal dragon with two wizened heads and a grievously wounded gravel stone body. The scales protecting his head and back are drained of color, while those on his underbelly are vibrant gold. Each of his craggy, horn-strewn faces has yellow eyes, paired crown horns, and a large horn on the snout. They both have long strands of white hair that continue down the full length of their necks. In his prime, Dragonlord Placidusax had five heads, each emerging from the vortex-like swirl at the base of his neck, though now only two remain. He also had two pairs of wings in the past, but has since lost the rear set. His exposed flesh is red and gold.

Placidusax summons Red Lightning and can assume the form of a storming thundercloud. He can fire beams of golden flame from his both mouths.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
In the prehistoric era, eons before the age of the Erdtree, the Lands Between were ruled from Farum Azula by Dragonlord Placidusax, the Elden Lord and many-headed king of the beastmen and undying Ancient Dragons. However, after he lost a head and his god fled, but likely before the meteorite struck his flying royal city, Placidusax retreated to the storm beyond time to dream in eternal anticipation of his god's return. He required his followers to render up their sleep and remain ever-awake, so that he might find solace in slumber. The timeless ancient dragons, to whom the passing of many lifetimes had rendered notions of ambition, hunger, and fierceness of spirit as utterly unfathomable, received his blessings and grace in return.

In time, the drake dragons—paltry, mortal offspring of the ancient dragons—rebelled, and Placidusax was betrayed by one of his own: Bayle the Dread. The old dragons formed a living wall of rock to protect their Dragonlord, but not before Bayle inflicted mutual, dire wounds upon the Dragonlord, claiming two of his heads and fleeing to the Jagged Peak. In retaliation, the Dragonlord marked Bayle and his bloodline for death. He reportedly slew the colossal drake and devoured its Dragon Heart, consummating the first Dragon Communion. He sent his followers to introduce Dragon Communion to mankind, within whom he recognized the mad hunger and fiery drive necessary to destroy Bayle.

Farum Azula became a mausoleum enshrining Placidusax, guarded by his chosen beasts. Despite his severely weakened condition, Placidusax continued to grant blessings to his followers. Several of Placidusax's Gravel Stone scales were disseminated throughout the world. They were used as smithing stones, said to allow for the creation of god-slaying weapons by lightly twisting time.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
Dragonlord Placidusax can be found in the storm beyond time at Crumbling Farum Azula. The nearest site of grace is Beside the Great Bridge, from which it can be reached by traveling north and down the slope. The player needs to jump down from a broken section of the bridge to reach his mausoleum complex. Once inside, activate the empty beastman to lie down. The storm rewinds time, and the Dragonlord appears.

The arena is a large, circular platform with pillars around its perimeter. These can be destroyed by Placidusax's attacks. The size of the arena gives ample room to avoid his area of effect or dodge his divebomb attacks.

Defeating Dragonlord Placidusax unlocks the Dragonlord Placidusax site of grace, which appears inside the arena.

runes
Remembrance of the Dragonlord

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Phase 1:

Placidusax will begin the fight by summoning a storm of red lightning bolts which rain down on the arena for a few seconds. During his first phase, he will primarily use lightning claw attacks if the player is in front, a slam attack with his wings if they are to either side, and a tail sweep if they get behind him. He also has fire breath attacks which cover a large area in front of or around him. He has an area of effect attack which involves summoning a large lightning bolt and thrusting it into the ground, creating a massive explosion after a short delay. When he performs this attack, the music will briefly get quieter and red waves will emanate from where the lightning bolt hits, providing an indicator for the range of the explosion.

Phase 2:
Placidusax now gains the ability to disappear in a cloud of fog. If he floats into the air before doing so, he will reappear in a stationary or moving thundercloud above the arena, before emerging and diving down at the player. He also gains the ability to disappear and reappear in quick succession, unleashing attacks with his lightning claws in between. 

Moveset:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Defeating Dragonlord Placidusax for the first time unlocks the "Dragonlord Placidusax" achievement.
Dragonlord Placidusax is not classified as a Dragon or Ancient Dragon for the purpose of Anti-Dragon effects because he is the origin of Dragon Communion. Unlike Dragon Communion Incantations, Placidusax's Ruin does not scale with Arcane.
According to the Remembrance of the Dragonlord, Placidusax was an Elden Lord before the era of the Erdtree, making him the earliest known Elden Lord.
Placidusax's five heads once corresponded with the five-fingers of intelligence granted to beasts in ancient times.
One of Placidusax's heads was lost prior to Bayle's betrayal. The Old Lord's Talisman depicts him with four heads and both sets of wings. Four fingers were seen as a sign of good luck.
Two of the Dragonlord's lost heads, as well as parts of their respective necks, can be found on the body of Bayle the Dread, still biting into the drake's neck.
Part of a dragon’s body (an arm, wing, and head) resembling Placidusax can be seen sticking out of a body of rock in Farum Azula prior to reaching his arena. These were the old dragons who protected him as a living wall of rock in the prehistoric era.
The Dragon Communion Priestess implies Placidusax felled the colossal drake at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion and consumed its heart, but Placidusax does not wield metal rods against the player.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Placidusax's design is most likely modeled after King Ghidora from the Godzilla franchise.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: The caster lifts up into the air and creates a large dragon head to bite down hard.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Deals Physical damage.
Damage is boosted by holding a Dragon Communion Seal in an active hand.
The spell actually has two separate hitboxes: the more damaging mouth and the weaker neck.
This incantation is surprisingly capable of, however rarely, landing headshots, increasing direct and Stance damage by 50%.
While extremely slow, taking around 4 seconds to cast, this spell deals heavy damage and has an excellent turning radius until the bite happens, making it a powerful and often worthwhile gamble if used correctly.
Deals a massive 55 Stance damage, slightly more than a fully charged heavy attack from hammer-type Colossal Weapons.
For context, most bosses have between 80 and 120 Stance (the greatest exception is Starscourge Radahn at a whopping 200 Stance).

sections.heading: Trivia

name: Dung Eater
description: The Dung Eater is an character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Dung Eater envisioned an Order that would place a "pox upon life itself." He murdered and defiled countless victims in a reviled ritual that produced Seedbed Curses, severing the dead souls from the Erdtree and binding them to his own flesh. Those cursed in this way were doomed to be reborn as Omen, passing the curse to their descendants for all eternity. With each pox, the Dung Eater nourished and grew his own Seedbed Curse. He personally cultivated thousands of these horn-strewn tumors across the realm. The art was among the most vile things in the entire Lands Between.

The Dung Eater was caught and imprisoned for his unspeakable crimes, but his work continued unperturbed, much to the horror of fellow inmate Blackguard Big Boggart. Then, he was publicly hanged in front of an angry crowd beneath the sun. Upon his death, the Dung Eater received Queen Marika's grace. The Dung Eater visited Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, the Volcano Manor and Leyndell, Royal Capital after his revival. He was jailed with the noble Omen in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and eventually lost sight of his guiding grace.

Game events:

The Dung Eater's red phantom appears at the Roundtable Hold when the Tarnished reaches the Altus Plateau. He sits on the floor among a pile of bodies in the room adjacent to Sir Gideon Ofnir's study. Though he does not respect his fellow Tarnished, he abides by the pact of non-aggression. Roderika, Spirit Tuner senses the spirits trapped by the Dung Eater and warns the Tarnished of the curse.

If the player collects a Seedbed Curse and speaks to the Dung Eater, the Dung Eater detects its presence. He produces a Sewer-Gaol Key and asks the Tarnished to release his corporeal body from the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. If he is released, the Dung Eater attacks and defiles Blackguard Big Boggart. When the player discovers the evidence, the Dung Eater invades them as well. If repelled, Dung Eater exclaims something unexpected happened. Despite the curse stirring within, his blessing was warded off by the protagonist—a feat none had succeeded in before.

The Dung Eater has a revelation: he was not the one who could curse the world as in his vision. He was just the means to get there; his flesh is the one that must receive the blessing. He asks to be killed and defiled by the Seedbed Curse until his gestated Mending Rune of the Fell Curse coalesces. If this Rune is added to the Elden Ring, it curses Order itself and ushers in the Blessing of Despair.

The Tarnished may also choose to simply kill him, leave him in his jail, or turn him into a puppet with Seluvis's Potion.

sections.heading: Quest
sections.body:
Completing the Dung Eater's quest unlocks the "Blessing of Despair" ending.
His quest intersects with Blackguard Big Boggart and Roderika, Spirit Tuner.

Quest items:

Questline progression:

Liurnia of the Lakes (Laskyar Ruins)
Head north-west from the Site of Grace to find Rya the Scout inside a gazebo and talk to her.
Move to north-west again from here to find Blackguard Big Boggart at the Boilprawn Shack and talk to him: select Give me the necklace and then Deal to be able to buy Rya's Necklace from him for 1000 Runes.
After purchasing the item, he'll start selling an infinite supply of Boiled Prawns. Purchase at least one to progress his questline: you'll receive the "Spread Out" gesture and, in turn, Boggart's summon sign will appear at the Ruin-Strewn Precipice Overlook to aid you against Magma Wyrm Makar.
Roundtable Hold
After touching any Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, the Dung Eater will appear in the western quarter of the Roundtable Hold, past Gideon's study. Talk to him with at least one Seedbed Curse in inventory to receive the Sewer-Gaol Key.
(Optional) Talking to Roderika, she'll now have a new dialogue option "There's something you should know" to warn you of the danger of the new arrival.
Leyndell, Royal Capital (Underground Roadside)
Drop down the open grate to the left exiting the room and follow the path past the Miranda Flowers to reach the Dung Eater's cell, which is guarded by a Large Fingercreeper hidden underground and some smaller ones hanging from the ceiling. Open the cell and talk to him, selecting Leave your gaol!.
Leyndell, Royal Capital (Forsaken Depth)
(Optional) The Dung Eater can now be summoned to aid you against Mohg, the Omen.
Leyndell, Royal Capital (Queen's Bed Chamber)
(Optional) Alongside Melina, the Dung Eater can now be summoned to aid you against Morgott, the Omen King.
Roundtable Hold
(Optional) The Dung Eater has disappeared from the Hold, leaving behind on his spot a message that reads: "I'll defile you next. Come to the outer moat."
(Optional) Talking to Roderika, she'll now have a new dialogue option "About the spirits' voices" to express her relief for the Dung Eater's departure.
Leyndell, Royal Capital (Outer Wall Battleground)
Visit the moat to the south-east below the capital's ramparts to meet again with Boggart, who now sells an infinite supply of Boiled Crabs too. Talk to him and select About the Dung Eater.
Reload the area to find Boggart moribund and, after talking to him, collect Seedbed Curse, Blackguard's Bell Bearing, Iron Ball, and Blackguard's Iron Mask from his cadaver. Shortly after, the Dung Eater will invade you and, once defeated, will drop his Sword of Milos.
Roundtable Hold
The Dung Eater will have now returned to the Hold. Talking to him, he'll instruct you to defile his corpse with the Seedbed Curse.
(Optional) Talking to Roderika, she'll now have a new dialogue option "About the spirits' voices".
Leyndell, Royal Capital (Underground Roadside)
(Optional) If you don't intend to follow his questline, you can select Administer Seluvis' Potion to turn the Dung Eater into a puppet. After his screams have ceased, you're free to kill him to collect his loot without failing the Preceptor's questline.
After collecting all five Seedbed Curses, return to him and select Use the Seedbed Curse, then collect the Mending Rune of the Fell Curse from his body. Reloading the area, you'll be able to collect the Omen Set too.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Roderika cautions the spiritual harm done by the Dung Eater's Seedbed Curse is worse than Godrick's grafting.
The Dung Eater possesses a fate.
During the intro cinematic, the Dung Eater is hung by an iron chain in a gallows, silhouetted against the bright Erdtree or sun. A faint golden Grace near his chest illuminates the sun medallion, visually linking it to the haloed backdrop.
He was confined to the same prison as nobleborn Omen beneath the streets of Leyndell. Like the Omen, his body also contains cursed spirits.
Two Seedbed Curses are found at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, regardless of whether he is freed. This suggests he was among (or descended from) the Tarnished who remained in the Lands Between.
The Dung Eater's right eye is visible through the gash in the Omen Helm in the Dung Eater concept art.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like all human NPCs, the Dung Eater has a custom face. He has wild red hair and eyes that are spaced too widely apart, giving him an almost deformed appearance. He is the only character who looks this way.
The Fell God is described as being "malformed," and is also associated with giants, horns, red hair, and the sun. It was ousted by Queen Marika during the War Against the Giants.
Milos is also described as grotesque.
The Dung Eater’s name and methods may draw inspiration from an old Japanese myth in which a person’s soul was believed to reside in a special organ located inside the anus. Known as the shirikodama (尻子玉), this mythical sphere was said to be extracted by demons to steal their victim’s soul. The Dung Eater’s grotesque ritual may symbolically mirror this act, as he seizes the souls of his victims by defiling them to their core.
The Headless can steal the shirikodama in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. These enemies are physically similar to Omen, though they are bloated and hornless. Like the Dung Eater, they were previously executed for great crimes.

name: Ekzykes's Decay
description: Ekzykes's Decay is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Dragon Communion: Caelid
Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Decaying Ekzykes in Caelid.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a heavy, rotting mist, dealing Standard damage equal to 155% of Incantation Scaling and causing 65 Scarlet Rot build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 465% of the same and 195 build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. 

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Note that while the Dragon Communion Seal scales with Arcane, Scarlet Rot will not scale with that so Ekzykes's Decay gains no innate benefit except for the damage boost.
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
Compatible with the Blue Dancer Charm, even more so since its two primary boosting items, the Dragon Communion Seal and Rock Heart, are weightless.
The Scarlet Rot deals damage roughly equal to 1170 + 29.7% of the target's maximum health over the course of 90 seconds.
Deals 20% less damage against other players. 
The total Scarlet Rot build-up is 390 if using both breaths, enough to afflict many vulnerable enemies and bosses with the Status Effect and most non-resistant ones within two full casts.
This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Rotten Breath.
Casting this spell until it stops costs 168 FP: 2*48 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 91 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Compared to Rotten Breath, this spell deals 18% more damage but also consumes 40% more FP.
This is the weakest "named" dragon breath attack, but it's also the only one that deals Physical damage.
Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased. Reduced Scarlet Rot status effect buildup.
The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%. 
The status build-up per hit was decreased from 130 to 65 (total build-up reduced from 780 to 390).
Prior to Patch 1.07, this amount of build-up was twice as much, 780 in total, letting it Rot most non-resistant enemies and bosses in one full cast.

name: Elden Beast
description: The Elden Beast is the final Boss of, encountered on the Stone Platform inside the Erdtree at Leyndell, Ashen Capital, fought directly after Radagon of the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: A long-necked, aquatic creature, the Elden Beast is a living constellation of shimmering Amber Starlight suspended in a translucent silhouette. Its narrow head lacks a traditional face, instead containing a single ball of glowing white light. It has a golden spine, an elongated body, and, along its back, long, tapering fins flare outward like fingers of radiant gold. Behind the torso trails a long, tapering tail that ends in a rich golden rootstock. The Elden Beast has two arms and two legs, with five-fingered hands. A glowing crack like shattered glass graces its chest.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Sent upon a golden star by the Greater Will, the arrival of the Elden Beast was one of the earliest events known to have occurred in the Lands Between. It was the vassal beast of the Greater Will and the living incarnation of the concept of Order. At some later point in the primordial past, the Elden Beast was forged into the great Elden Ring. The Empyrean consort of Dragonlord Placidusax became its vessel, becoming a god and making the ancient dragon the first known Elden Lord.

After untold ages, the Numen Marika, an Empyrean, became the new goddess and the vessel of the Elden Ring. Her Golden Order established her as the one true god to rule over the Lands Between. However, Marika eventually shattered the Elden Ring, leading to her imprisonment at the Stone Platform within the Erdtree. 

The Tarnished enters the Erdtree where they find the shackled Marika, and face Radagon, Marika's male other self and the reigning Elden Lord, the two of them sharing the same body. After his defeat, the Elden Beast emerges from Radagon, transforming his defeated body into a large sword. The Elden Beast reverts to the Elden Ring upon defeat.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
Nearest Site of Grace: Elden Throne

The Elden Beast appears immediately after Radagon of the Golden Order is defeated. If you die to the Elden Beast, you are required to fight Radagon again before rechallenging it.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
HP: 22,127
Defense: 121
Stance: 150
This boss cannot be Parried.
This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
Deals Standard and Holy damage
Immune to all Status Ailments

Elden Beast is the second half of the final boss fight with Radagon of the Golden Order. The Elden Beast uses a combination of physical sword attacks and golden Holy attacks.

The arena is a large, flat body of shallow water. Although it appears endless, the arena does have invisible walls surrounding it. The Elden Beast will regularly swim away from the player, or disappear underwater before emerging, meaning that the fight often requires one to chase or wait for it. Unlike the previous fight, it is possible to summon Torrent. 

When its health reaches around 80% it will fly up into the air and create a golden ring which closes in on the player before exploding. This can be avoided by jumping over the ring as it closes in. It will also begin to use additional attacks, such as Elden Stars or Spear Showers. At around 30% health, it will perform the Golden Ring attack again, but this time it will generate three rings that each close in on the player.

Resistances:

Moveset:

Strategies:
Its normal sword attacks are fairly easy to dodge, with perhaps the repeating stabs being an exception. The Golden Rings can be jumped over to preserve your momentum and get out of them quicker, while the Spear Showers can be avoid by running while zig-zagging. 

Elden Stars, if it cannot be interrupted by a stagger, is quite dangerous due to the consistent damage over time it can inflict and because it will gain speed to chase if allowed to travel with minimal turning. A way to fairly easily dodge it is to circle the Elden Beast counter-clockwise (that is, heading around it to your right before circling left to run out the duration.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
It is heavily implied that the Elden Beast was the being who imprisoned Marika inside the Erdtree based on one of its attacks where it attempts to grab the player and lift them up in the air to crucify and then pierce them with a barrage of golden spears, similar to how Marika was seen in the cutscene before the final boss battle.
Its tail resembles a network of golden roots and is comparable to those of Astels and Fallingstar Beasts.
The properties and appearance of the Elden Beast may have differed when it contained the Rune of Death and various Great Runes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The Elden Beast is internally referenced as the "NebulaDragon".
It resembles the dragon associated with the alchemical Rebis, paralleling Marika and Radagon. The Rebis represents a single entity split into male and female halves, later reunited as a transcendent being empowered by a dragon.
It was not possible to summon Torrent when facing the Elden Beast prior to Version 1.12.

name: Elden Ring (concept)
description: The Elden Ring (エルデンリング, Eruden Ringu) is a mysterious artifact that defines the world of itself. It is the source of the Erdtree, and its various interlocking runes represent and establish Order, the fundamental laws of the world.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The Elden Ring itself is made up of various interlocking shapes, known as runes, which appear as ethereal rings and arches made of light. These runes have power over fundamental concepts that dictate reality in the Lands Between, such as "Death." Under the Golden Order, the runes represent the concepts of order and discipline enforced on the physical world.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Long ago, the Greater Will sent a golden star bearing its vassal Elden Beast far across the cosmos to the world of the Lands Between. The beast was the living embodiment of the concept of Order, and later became the Elden Ring. 

Special beings known as Empyreans are able to become vessels of the Elden Ring, housing it within their bodies to become gods. The consort of an Empyrean takes the title of Lord, and the consort of an Empyrean who has become the Elden Ring's vessel is known as an Elden Lord. The vessels can alter the runes that make up the Elden Ring itself, changing the fundamental laws of the world, as Marika did when she removed the Rune of Death and began the Age of the Erdtree. The Elden Ring has taken different appearances in the past in accordance with the laws of previous ages. The oldest known configuration of the ancient Elden Ring can be found in Crumbling Farum Azula, dating to an age long before the Erdtree when Dragonlord Placidusax reigned as Elden Lord.

The most recent configuration of the Elden Ring was the Golden Order, founded by its divine vessel, Queen Marika the Eternal, who later remove it from her body and 
shattered it with her Numen hammer. Despite her other half Radagon's attempts to repair the Ring, many of its shards scattered across the realm, the largest and most powerful of which claimed by Marika's Demigod offspring. Corrupted by the strength of their newfound Great Runes, the Demigods fought a grueling Shattering War, a crucible from which no Lord arose.

sections.heading: Types of Runes
sections.body:
Several of the runes that make up the Elden Ring have particular names. These include:

Runes - Countless tiny fragments of the Elden Ring that spread throughout the Lands Between. These runes can be collected by the Tarnished to gain strength with the help of a Finger Maiden.
Rune Arc - The lower arches of the Elden Ring act as basins in which its blessings pool. There appear to be three Rune Arcs in the current configuration of the Elden Ring.
Great Runes - The large circular shapes that make up the central form of the Elden Ring. The Great Runes hold tremendous power, and the Demigods fought over them after the Elden Ring was shattered.
Anchor Rings - The Great Runes inherited by Godrick the Grafted, and Morgott, the Omen King, are both described as anchor rings. Godrick's Great Rune is the anchor ring found in the center of the Elden Ring. Morgott's Great Rune is the anchor ring that houses the base of the Elden Ring, and proves both that he is born of the Golden Lineage, and that he is the rightful Lord of Leyndell.
Since Mohg, Lord of Blood is Morgott's twin, his Great Rune is naturally similar to Morgott's, but it is unknown if his Great Rune can be considered an anchor ring as well.
Elden Runes - Elden Runes are not given a strict definition. The seals of Queen Marika and King Consort Radagon are both described as Elden Runes. Queen Marika's Elden Rune appears at the bottom of the Elden Ring, as the lower arch where the central vertical line of the Elden Ring ends, and it was said to be where the blessings of the Elden Ring would gather. Lord Radagon's Elden Rune is the crosshatch lattice pattern visible behind the central rings of the Elden Ring. It is unknown if there is a difference between Great Runes and Elden Runes.
The Rune of Death - Also known as Destined Death, it was originally a part of the Elden Ring, but was removed by Queen Marika in order to found the Golden Order. It governs the deaths of the inhabitants of the Lands Between. The Rune of Death was once harboured within the sword of Queen Marika's shadowbound beast, Maliketh, the Black Blade, until a fragment of the Rune was stolen in the Night of the Black Knives. Maliketh subsequently sealed the rest of the Rune's power within his own flesh in order to prevent Death from being stolen again. How the Rune of Death should be categorized is unclear: it may be a Great Rune, an Elden Rune, or something else entirely.
Mending Runes - Mending Runes are special runes that are envisioned and gestated by certain people, which can be added to the Elden Ring by the player. Mending runes both repair the Elden Ring and embed new ideas and natural laws into it, and thus into the world itself. It is unknown whether any Mending Runes had ever been added to the Elden Ring prior to the player's journey.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The Elden Beast is the Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The shape of the Elden Ring may have been inspired by various runes from RuneQuest, which Miyazaki has cited as an inspiration for his games in the past, including Elden Ring.
Notably, the Plant Rune, Truth Rune, and possibly the Fertility Rune from RuneQuest.
Cut and removed content suggests that additional Great Runes have proper names.
The cut versions of the Euporia (Abundance Twinblade, Abundance and Decay Twinblade) reference the "Rune of Abundance" and the "Rune of Decay" in their descriptions, belonging to Miquella and Malenia respectively.
In the Chinese 1.00 text, the Grafted Blade Greatsword referred to a "Rune of Grafting" (“接肢”的卢恩, Jiē Zhī de Lú'ēn), likely Godrick's Great Rune. The description for Helphen's Steeple, Golden Order Greatsword, and Icon Shield mentioned a "Rune of Life" (生命卢恩, Shēngmìng Lú ēn), and the Korean 1.0 Dark Moon Greatsword refers to a "Rune of Mind" ("정신의 룬, jeongsin-ui lun).
The Japanese talkmsg files refer to a "Mind Rune" (精神ルーン, Seishin Rūn) and a "Life Rune" (生命ルーン, Seimei Rūn).

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: This spell sends out a golden orb that tracks its target while shooting out small projectiles with Holy Attack Power equal to 20% of Incantation Scaling. Upon making contact with a surface or enemy, the orb explodes, dealing Holy Attack Power equal to 199% of Incantation Scaling and hitting a 4.2-meter radius around the point of impact.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 47 FP per cast.
Costs 48 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
Deals 14 Stance damage with the explosion and 0.5 Stance damage per mini-projectile that hits.

Strategies:
The small projectiles sent out by the main orb deal extremely low damage and are mainly useful for harassing other players with constant incoming damage ticks.
The reason that the damage is so much lower than the difference in Attack Power suggests is because defense reduces the damage of attacks with relatively lower Attack Power much more than those with relatively high Attack Power.
Generally a rather ineffective spell that is mostly useful for pressuring other players in PvP scenarios.

sections.heading: Trivia

Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption from 47 to 41.
Patch 1.04 increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

sections.body: Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, just south of Fort Faroth.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While the intended method of defeating her is by killing the surrounding lesser dragons, killing Greyoll herself directly through another method, such as Blood Loss, will also kill these smaller dragons.
This method will grant all 67,350 Runes at once, making this an excellent place to use a Gold-Pickled Fowl Foot for more Runes early on.

Defeating Elder Dragon Greyoll unlocks Greyoll's Roar, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for three Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
While the English localization claims that Greyoll was the mother of "all" dragons, the Japanese description simply claims she was a "great mother of dragons" (竜の大母).
This same term, 大母, is also used for the Grandmother.
Elder Dragon Greyoll was originally intended to be fought more directly. However, attempting to view this moveset results in heavy lag and slowdown which is presumably why it wasn't implemented.
Greyoll was initially conceived as an Ancient Dragon, with her concept art depicting her as such and the Chinese CNT version of Greyoll's Roar describing her as an "ancient dragon" and a stony mountain. It's likely that this late-stage script revision is the reason she uses a scaled up drake model rather than having a unique design.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Grants the right-hand weapon a Weapon Buff giving bonus Lightning Attack Power equal to 75% of the Faith-based Incantation Scaling of the Sacred Seal used to cast it for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 10 points of Stamina to cast. 
Despite being a Dragon Cult Incantation, this spell, like other spell-based weapon buffs, does not get bonus damage from its associated seal (the Gravel Stone Seal for this one). 
This is generally the strongest Faith-based weapon buff: Order's Blade requires a light Intelligence investment and grants the more often resisted Holy, Black Flame Blade has a very short duration of 7 seconds (9.1 seconds with Old Lord's Talisman) even with it dealing damage based on the target's maximum HP, and Bloodflame Blade only grants Fire Attack Power equal to 40% of Incantation Scaling. 
Like with all spell-based Weapon Buffs, it can only be cast when a weapon is held in the right hand and the casting implement in the left hand. 
Outmatched by Lightning Grease and Skill: Lightning Slash below 114 Incantation Scaling and by Dragonbolt Grease below 160 Incantation Scaling. 
Though they cast much quicker and last for a shorter duration, Drawstring Lightning Grease is stronger below 147 Incantation Scaling while Drawstring Dragonbolt Grease is stronger below 180 Incantation Scaling. 
Lightning Slash has the advantage of also being usable for weapons with the otherwise unbuffable (not counting other skills) Lightning and Sacred Affinity weapons.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Summons a lightning bolt down onto the user, damaging nearby enemies with Lightning Attack Power equal to 213% of Incantation Scaling. 

For 45 seconds, the user is granted a Body Buff that has Lightning Attack Power equal to 45% of Incantation Scaling in a small area around the user every 1 second. 

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the initial bolt to 262% of Incantation Scaling and the Attack Power of the Body Buff's pulses to 59% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast. Cost is increased to 36 points of Stamina if charged.
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged. 
Since charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the bolt by 23% and the Attack Power of the lingering effect by 31%, this leads to a total Attack Power increase of 41% and 51% respectively. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn. 
The initial bolt deals surprisingly good damage, if only in a very small area around the user, while the buff deals minuscule amounts of damage. 
While the damage over time is very small, it is still somewhat useful for things that only require any amount of damage without having to "waste" a hit, such as killing Skeletons before they can resurrect or breaking the damage-reducing bubble from Opaline Bubbletear or a Uplifting Aromatic (including the one used by Perfumers). 
Annoyingly enough, this lingering damage effect will not prevent the Stance of any enemy from recovering. 
The lingering damage effect from the Buff completely ignores Guarding, fully piercing through Guarded Damage Negation. 
Since this incantation grants a Body Buff, it will remove many strong defensive buffs such as Barrier of Gold and Fireproof Dried Liver. While there isn't a lot of overlap between these spells' uses (Electrocharge is more suited for use against many smaller enemies, while most defensive buffs are better against tougher foes), this is still a downside to trying to use the initial bolt offensively.

name: Elemer of the Briar
description: Elemer of the Briar is a reoccurring boss in.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body:
Try to stick close to him as his ranged sword swipes are much wider and generally harder to predict. 
It is possible to bait him into a cycle of repeated shield slams by getting behind him and only landing one attack (lighter weapons can possibly use an uncharged heavy attack and some skills are quick enough to also be used) after each slam. Be aware that he can also follow up with an explosion sometimes, so take a moment to see if the shield begins to glow red as he is about to pull it up. 
The grab is rather hard to dodge and very delayed. Wait until his hand begins to move towards you before dodging. It is also possible to dodge by running far enough away or by being behind him. 
The blade drill is hard to avoid if rolling to the right and has some reach so try to roll forward and to the left. 
His shield charge is very quick so try to stay relatively close as to not provoke it.

Elemer is encountered in the hall at the top of the Shaded Castle. He can channel energy through his sword, allowing him to send it towards the player and control it at a distance, or fire a red beam by rotating it quickly.

The Bell Bearing Hunter appears at night, in the Hermit Merchant's Shack in the Capital Outskirts. The Hermit Merchant (Capital Outskirts) will disappear for the duration of the fight, but will reappear if the player dies or if they defeat the boss. 

This version is actually stronger than Elemer's own fight.

This version is actually the strongest of all the Bell-Bearing Hunter encounters and has twice the health of Elemer's own, named encounter.

name: Empyreans
description: are special Demigods with the potential to reach full godhood and forge a new Order. They are hand-selected by the Two Fingers to succeed the current god as vessel for the great Elden Ring. As such, they are important characters in the world of.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Empyreans can ascend to godhood through different methods. Marika was able to ascend using the Gate of Divinity, gathering the Runes of thousands of hornsent sacrificed to form it. Miquella was also able to use the Gate after divesting his physical body and Great Rune before performing a secret rite involving Radahn as his Lord. Malenia could ascend by letting her Rot bloom three times. while Ranni finds her Order by "[going] to the night sky." They fully consummate their godhood by becoming the vessel of the Elden Ring. Their chosen consort confers Great Runes and brandishes the Elden Ring, becoming the Elden Lord.

Empyreans are served by warrior vassals of unerring loyalty, which may come in the form of wolves. Shadowbound beasts, sometimes simply referred to as "shadows," are custom-tailored by the Two Fingers to ensure the Demigod follows the right path. Though incapable of treachery towards their Empyrean, should their master resist the will of the Two Fingers, they will descend into madness, becoming a curse rather than a protector. The three known shadowbound beasts are: Maliketh, who serves Marika; Blaidd, who serves Ranni; and the Baleful Shadow, which had no Empyrean master and served the Two Fingers directly. There are also many aspects that an Empyrean can possess.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The most prominent Empyrean was Queen Marika, a golden-haired Numen from the Shaman Village. A descendant of denizens of another world, she was selected and guided by the Two Fingers toward true godhood. Through seduction and betrayal, Marika ascended at the Gate of Divinity, located atop the tower of Enir-Ilim. There, she acquired threads of the Elden Ring, became its vessel, and created her Order. She later used a Golden Seed to transform the Crucible into the Erdtree, and eventually shattered the Elden Ring. Her shadow was Maliketh and her consorts were Lord Godfrey and Serosh, and later her other half, Lord Radagon.

Another Empyrean, known as the Gloam-Eyed Queen, wielded the god-slaying black flame and raised the Godskin Apostles. She challenged Marika's established Order by leading her followers on a god hunt. However, she was defeated in battle by Marika's shadowbound beast, Maliketh, the Black Blade. Marika then extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and Maliketh sealed it within his Black Blade. This act severed the source of the Gloam-Eyed Queen's power and created the Golden Order. The identities and deeds of her shadow and consort remain unclear.

During the Age of the Erdtree, three Empyreans were named as Marika's potential successors: Miquella, Malenia and Ranni. Miquella and Malenia were twins born of a single god, being the children of both Marika and her second consort Radagon. Their powerful lineage made them prime candidates for Empyrean. Ranni, on the other hand, was the daughter of Radagon and his former wife, Queen Rennala of the Full Moon, prior to his union with Marika. This demonstrates that being the child of two full gods is not a strict requirement to become an Empyrean, as Ranni herself was only a demigod. Miquella saw a tender kindness in General Radahn and made a vow to select him as his future consort.

Game Events:

Miquella himself was able to ascend to godhood, but was defeated by the Tarnished before he could reach Fractured Marika and bring about his envisioned Age of Compassion. Unlike her brother, Malenia rejected her destiny and abandoned the Servants of Rot. However, she would briefly ascend as the Goddess of Rot during her battle with the same Tarnished warrior but was similarly defeated, yet fated to bloom once more. As for Ranni, she has the potential to bring about her Age of Stars with the assistance of the Tarnished, who she makes her consort. The Tarnished can become Marika's third consort, using her imprisoned form to bring about the Ages of Fracture, Order, Age of the Duskborn, or introduce the Blessing of Despair.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Each Empyrean typically bonds with their Lord consort near their ascension to godhood.
Whether all Empyreans are granted a Shadow is unclear, as there is no concrete evidence of Miquella, Malenia, nor the Gloam-Eyed Queen receiving shadowbound beasts.
Mohg, Lord of Blood wished to be Miquella's consort but was used to house the soul of Radahn instead.
Dragonlord Placidusax's unnamed god is presumed to be an Empyrean who was once a vessel to the Elden Ring, apropos to his own title as Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
"Empyrean" refers to the highest heaven in ancient and medieval cosmology, usually consisting of fire or light. It can also refer to the firmament (the heavens) or an ideal place or state. In Japanese, Empyreans are referred to as 神人 (Shinjin; lit. "Divine Person", "God-like Person").
Miquella has cut dialogue phrased similar to the speech given by Ranni the Witch during her Age of Stars ending.

name: Ensha (lord)
image: ER Icon Armor Royal Remains Helm.png
description: Ensha, also known as the soulless king, was a character mentioned in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
King Ensha was a soulless champion with golden bones who claimed lordship over the Lands Between in ancient times. He was regarded as a hero to Those Lost in Death, who were always in desperate need of leadership. He held such masterful control over life energies that a single punch rendered his foes unconscious, stealing their vitality. His royal remains were likewise graced with potent restorative power, and so they were forged into armor.

The king's bones were later acquired by Ensha of the Royal Remains, the unspeaking associate of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Ensha's golden royal remains are set in bronze armor and decorated with crimson, cerulean, gold, and viridian gemstones, including a prominent red jewel on his forehead. His faded hair is worn in a ponytail and melted candlewax covers the besagew affixed to his right pauldron.

His golden bones are similar to Blessed Bone Shards, human bones imbued with the gold of the Scadutree—a blessing said to be the greatest honor that could be granted to the dead. Like the royal remains, these golden bones possessed healing properties similar to sunlight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Most information about Lord Ensha is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.
Lord Ensha appears to be from an earlier batch of Those Who Live in Death, possibly granted life during an Eclipse.
The Gold Skeletons that arise from graveyards on the Altus Plateau may have been followers of Ensha in the past.
Gold Skeletal Knights were Sun Realm warriors who wore red cloaks depicting a bright sun.
The Altus Bloom may also be related to Ensha.
The crimson jewel on his forehead mirrors the red gem atop Helphen's Steeple, which is acquired from a Tibia Mariner outside Castle Sol.
Ensha of the Royal Remains ambushes the player to obtain one half of the Haligtree Secret Medallion, which is required to reach Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. Its counterpart lies in Castle Sol.
He may be connected to the soulless Prince of Death, who can be reborn as the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince to usher in the age of the Duskborn.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Concept art for Ensha of the Royal Remains included two unused elements: a candle sconce besagew resembling a small hand holding a Site of Grace, and a "Royal Remains Sword." In the final game, Ensha instead wields two hardened skeletal arms, the Clinging Bones of old Lord Ensha.

description: Eochaid was an unseen location mentioned in. Little is known of its people and customs.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Eochaid was a lesser foreign kingdom located outside the Lands Between. Its people were proud ascetics who practiced a distinct form of magic and lived solitary lives. By using copper as a conduit, those from Eochaid willed their blades to pirouette through the skies. The state of Eochaid and its people vanished long ago.

After the Shattering war subsided, a man in iron armor from Eochaid began amassing Bell Bearings, stalking numerous merchants and instructors and killing them with violent corkscrew attacks. When captured, the Bell Bearing Hunter’s crimes warranted the death sentence, and he was bound in winding, rusted iron thorns. Before his execution at The Shaded Castle, Elemer of the Briar seized the ceremonial copper Marais Executioner's Sword, furnishing it with battle skills from his homeland, and drove Castellan Maleigh Marais from the castle, claiming both for himself.

Likely associated with the Briars of Sin and guilty criminals

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Extremely good on the Faith-scaling Flame Art and Sacred affinities and below average on the rest. Can have an over 100 point lead in Attack Power compared to other affinities. 
Since the Faith-scaling by default applies to the Physical damage for all affinities, these two affinities allow for double-dipping for damage, even more so if stacked with the flat damage bonuses from Flaming Strike and Sacred Blade.
The double-dipping effectively pulls it B-scaling on Faith-scaling affinities to the equivalent of an S-scaling.
Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Fire Knight's Shortsword. 
This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.
If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats. 
In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities is only shared with the Clayman's Harpoon while the DLC adds the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, Fire Knight's Greatsword, and Fire Knight's Shortsword, weapons which all have the same quality.
Due to a bug this weapon actually doesn't have an actual Arcane-scaling on Poison, Blood, and Occult affinities.

name: Erdtree
description:
The Erdtree (黄金樹, Ōgonju; lit. "Golden Tree") is a giant, gold-colored
tree that towers above the Lands Between in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Crucible of life was the primordial matter that became the Erdtree and the place where all life was once blended together. It was said to be close in nature to life itself, and was represented by gold with a reddish tint—primordial gold. Queen Marika transformed the Crucible into the Erdtree under the guidance of the Two Fingers.

Age of the Erdtree:

The birth of the Erdtree coincided with the War Against the Giants. Following the defeat of the Fire Giants and their Fell God, and the confinement of the Flame of Ruin, Queen Marika declared the beginning of a new epoch, glistening with life, known as the Age of the Erdtree.

Although the Erdtree came from a blending of all life, many cultures were deemed vulgar under Marika's regime. In the time of Lord Godfrey, everything once stood in opposition to the Erdtree. Through countless victories in war, it became the embodiment of Order, and defeated were eradicated, enslaved, or banished to the fringes.

Age of Plenty:

When the new age began, the Erdtree flourished with abundance. It secreted primordial life energy in the form of sacred sap, which hardened into an amber that was treasured as the most precious of jewels. These blessings fell like golden tears from its boughs, pooling in flasks or large collection basins. Queen Marika herself personally bestowed them to her Elden Lord and chosen few. These Sacred Tears were worshipped and used to spread the faith in churches across all lands.

During these early days, the Erdtree radiated the gentle warmth of the sun and healed all who basked in its golden glow. Its bark at this time was brown, much like the Minor Erdtrees.

It was thought that the blessed sap of the Erdtree would drip from its boughs forever, but that era of blind belief swiftly came to an end. It was only for a fleeting moment, as is the course of all life. Over time, the Erdtree became more an object of faith.

Erdtree Burial:

Erdtree burial was an honor awarded to heroes as a proper death meant returning to the Erdtree. The remains of such champions were deposited within the catacombs built around the Greattree roots that once connected to the Erdtree. Indeed there were once heroes abundantly blessed by the Erdtree who upon earning their honors simply died. Statues of Rosus, Usher of Death, were erected in order to guide the dead who lose their way during their return to the Erdtree roots.

Age of the Elden Ring:

On the Night of Black Knives, a stolen fragment of the Rune of Death was used to murder Godwyn the Golden. As a hero and the first demigod to die, Godwyn's body was buried deep beneath Leyndell in the Deeproot Depths overlooking the Nameless Eternal City. Although his soul has perished, his body did not, and his Erdtree burial enabled the Rune of Death to spread throughout the great tree roots, sprouting in the form of Deathroot across the Lands Between. Deathroot violated the catacombs and gave rise to Those Who Live in Death, who refused the Erdtree's call to return. At some point, either before or after the Elden Ring was shattered, the connection between the Erdtree and the great tree roots was severed.

The Shattering:
s were released when the Elden Ring was shattered]]

Minor Erdtrees were considered to be the offspring of the Erdtree. After the Elden Ring was shattered, golden seeds flew from the Erdtree and scattered across the Lands Between, as if life itself knew that its end had come. It used to be believed that Erdtree seeds could not exist, as the Erdtree was once perfect and eternal. Erdtree Avatars emerged following the shattering of the Elden Ring, determined to protect the withering Erdtree's offspring. Illusory trees, or phantom trees, also grew from the scattered golden seeds. Additionally, the Wrath of Gold incantation was discovered, and feared as a sign of the Erdtree's wrath.

Queen Marika was imprisoned inside the Erdtree after she shattered the Elden Ring. At some point following the shattering of the Elden Ring, the entrance to the Erdtree was blocked by impenetrable thorns, emblazoned with the seal of King Consort Radagon, which prevent access to anyone outside. The Flame of Ruin was capable of burning the Erdtree and destroying the impenetrable thorns, but doing so was long held to be the first cardinal sin.

Game events:
]]
After the defeat of Morgott, the Omen King, The Tarnished attempted to enter the Erdtree to repair the Elden Ring, become Marika's consort, and ascend as Elden Lord. However, they were unable to enter due to the impenetrable thorns. The Tarnished then traveled to the Mountaintops of the Giants to rekindle the Flame of Ruin and burn the Erdtree, either by sacrificing Melina (as was her duty as the kindling maiden) or by using the Frenzied Flame. This journey eventually led them to Crumbling Farum Azula, where the defeat of Maliketh, the Black Blade unbound the Rune of Death, enabling them to enter the burning Erdtree.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The fate of the Erdtree is dependent on the player's ending choice.
The Scadutree is the "shadow of the Erdtree."
Miquella's Haligtree was meant to succeed the Erdtree.
The Erdtree's presence facilitates interaction and harmony with Demi-Humans.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In the Japanese version of, the Erdtree is called 黄金樹 (Ōgonju), which simply means "Golden Tree." Additionally, Finger Reader Enia refers to the Erdtree as 世界樹 (Sekaiju), meaning "World Tree" or "Yggdrasil."
The Erdtree is evidently inspired by the World Tree motif found in various mythologies around the world.
It may have also drawn inspiration from the Two Trees of Valinor featured in Tolkien's Legendarium.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Besides its full physical blocking, this Greatshield also has very good Holy and Magic damage reduction. 
The skill's damaging portion can be activated from ANY lasting "magical" effect. This means that, besides parrying enemy Sorceries and Incantations, it can be used much more easily through the wielder's own items and spells. 
Discus of Light's returning disc and the Wraith Calling Bell's newly launched spirit are two cheap and easy to use sources of fodder for the skill. 
The skill can only block a single projectile per activation.
The Erdtree Greatshield portrays an elder and a maiden beside a tree. The elder reaches his right arm into the boughs, his left hand resting on the pommel of a sword that serves as a cane. This scene condenses two frames from ruins left by the Ancient Dynasty, possibly depicting the Bearded Elder.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: orange for Holy damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Erdtree Seal is the strongest Faith-only Sacred Seal when the stat is above 68. 
Gets 353 Incantation Scaling at 80 Faith when the seal is at +10. The other seals are in the 310 to 330 range at that point. 
If using only a single Seal, other Faith-only Seals will still outmatch the Erdtree Seal when using the type of incantations that they boost. However, since this boost also applies to other Seals when a spell-boosting seal is held in an active hand, wielding two Seals at the same time makes the Erdtree Seal once again the stronger alternative unless two copies of the same spell-boosting seal are obtained. 
Though it won't quite catch up with the Godslayer's Seal (the strongest Seal beforehand) until the Faith stat reaches the 60s, the ease of upgrading it because it requires Somber Smithing Stones (versus the unfortunately generally much rarer Smithing Stones that the Godslayer's Seal needs) means it can still see good use beforehand. 
Besides increasing the Seal's Incantation Scaling, the Faith-scaling also increases the its own meager base Physical and Holy damage.

name: Eternal Cities
description: The Eternal Cities are landmarks in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
]]

The Eternal Cities were built by the Nox, who were devoted to the starry night sky. These cities contained massive stone Chair-Crypts that seated giant maidens. The Nox used weapons forged from the liquid metal of Silver Tears, which could mimic other forms. They used these Mimic Tears in an attempt to create their own Lord.

Long ago, the Nox conspired against the Greater Will. They donned Nox Mirrorhelms to repel its light and used the Fingerslayer Blade to inflict a grievous wound upon a vassal of the Greater Will. As punishment for their blasphemy, they were banished deep underground. The Black Moon that hung over Nokstella was shattered into Memory Stones, and Astel, Naturalborn of the Void was unleashed upon one of their cities and it stole its false night sky. Although the nameless Eternal City was completely leveled, the others were left mostly intact. Although the efforts of the Nox all ended in failure, they continued to believe a Lord of Night would one day come to usher in an Age of the Stars.

Eternal City architecture also appears in Sellia, Town of Sorcery, Ordina, Liturgical Town, Leyndell, Royal Capital, and the Ainsel River Main.

sections.heading: Inhabitants
sections.body:
The Eternal Cities were home to the Nox clergy, which included Nox Monks, Nox Swordstresses, and Night Maidens.
Silver Tears are found throughout Nokron and Nokstella.
The Fallen Hawks now wander Nokron and the Siofra Aqueduct.
The Dragonkin Soldiers, who wielded ice lightning, were born in the Eternal Cities after they were sent underground.
The Nox of the nameless Eternal City crafted Valiant Gargoyles with Corpse Wax.
War Counselor Iji wears a Mirrorhelm, the description of which either implicates his involvement in the plot to use the Fingerslayer Blade or his knowledge of it and his blasphemous desire to use it for Ranni's plans.
The nameless Eternal City is populated by Basilisks, Mausoleum Knights and Mausoleum Soldiers and Gargoyles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Many of the buildings constructed by the Nox, such as the Siofra Aqueduct, appear inverted, hanging like stalactites from the cavern ceiling. It is unclear whether these were built after their banishment.
The Carian Study Hall was built with a similar design.
Eternal City ruins are strewn about the Ainsel River Main near Nokstella. This area is red with scarlet rot and prowled by a Baleful Shadow during Ranni the Witch's questline. An aqueduct drains water from the Ainsel into the stagnant lake.
Sellia, Town of Sorcery was founded in Caelid. Many notable glintstone sorcerers came from Sellia, including Primeval Sorcerer Lusat, who went on to found the Olivinus conspectus at the Academy of Raya Lucaria. The Sellians were known assassins who utilized night sorceries to hunt their peers. The secret chair-crypt at this location is vacant.
The Eternal Cities were likely buried after the ancient dynasty ended, as they are found surrounded by their underground ruins.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The nameless Eternal City is the only one without a chair-crypt.

name: Fell God
description: The fell god, also known as the one-eyed god, is a character mentioned in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The fell god of fire has been around for a long time and predates the Erdtree. It was a malevolent figure in the old hornsent legends of Enir-Ilim. The Fire Giants were its followers, and tended the god's undying flames housed within the great black Forge anchored to the Flame Peak atop the Mountaintops of the Giants. Though it was feared, the sparks of its flame could fertilize even frozen lands, leading to the growth of half-ashen and smoldering flowers called Fire Blossoms.

The Fire Giants considered smithing a divine ritual, and even the Trolls, their descendants, wielded hammers as ceremonial tools for smithing, crafted with the same pattern of the fell god's eye. The connection of smithing to divinity dates back to the Forges of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh, where Anvil Hammers were shaped like altars and used in ancient divine rituals.

The fell god was also considered evil by Queen Marika, as its Flames were capable of burning her Erdtree. Thus, she waged a bloody War Against the Giants for the sake of her new Age of the Erdtree. However, during this conflict her priests would be forced to use the very power they were fighting against to protect the champions of the Erdtree from the flames of the Fire Giants, creating the first incantation of the Fire Monks.

It is said that Queen Marika personally slew the fell god, but once the Fire Giants were defeated, she realized the flame of their forge could not die and thus sealed it away, reducing its once formidable fire into mere embers and cursing the last surviving Fire Giant to keep them so for all eternity. The power to fully burn the Erdtree was lost when the Rune of Death was sealed in Maliketh's Black Blade.

However, the fell god was not destroyed. Though dormant, it continued to lurk within its subjects, on the cusp of being awakened at any moment with a sufficient sacrificial offering. The fell god's allure swayed even the Fire Monks that were tasked with keeping watch over the Flame.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.body:
Fire Giant
Fire Monks
Adan, Thief of Fire
Birac
Chief Guardian Arghanthy
Fire Monk
Fire Prelate
Flame Guardian
Guilty (Thorn Sorcerer)
Blackflame Monk (formerly)
Blackflame Monk Amon (formerly)
Blackflame Sorcerer (formerly)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
a concentric ring of eight dots surrounding a larger central dot]]

It is unclear whether the fell god is one of the outer gods. Though the power of their flames can certainly be described as divine and they operates like one, it is never explicitly stated to be an outer god.
Erdtree prophets glimpsed its flame within their faith, implying this power currently exists within the Golden Order.
This can be explain by the fact that the forces of the Erdtree were forced to create incantations that channeled the flame of the fell god through faith to protect themselves from that power, thus integrating the laws of another god into the Order. This is something that, according to Sorcerer Rogier, the Golden Order of the past was already capable of doing.
In addition, the Erdtree was once as warm as the gentle sun, a power possibly related to those of the fell god
It currently manifests as a grotesque face on the torsos of Fire Giants.
In addition to the Fire Giants, the Fell God dwells within the Flame of the Fell God. This spell is a massive ball of fire, not unlike a sun. This ability is most similar to the Messmer's Orb.
The inhabitants of the Lands Between have produced a number of objects that invoke the fell god's image.
The Furnace Golems are colossal wickermen filled with burning bodies. Their faces are Furnace Visages—stone masks depicting the fell god as a bronze sun, with a mane of eight curled horns. It looms high above the Fire Giant faces attached to the golems' knees.
Its opens one or both eyes when taking damage or during certain attacks.
The sun medallion on the Dung Eater's Omen Armor resembles the Furnace Visage.
The leader of the Fire Monks, Chief Guardian Arghanthy, uses a One-Eyed Shield that expels flame from its mouth. The large swirl along below the barrel is flanked by eight smaller swirls.
The Fire Monk Armor portrays a cyclopian face on the torso in imitation of Fire Giants.
The fell god is represented by a ring of eight small circles surrounding a larger central circle.
This pattern appears on the One-Eyed Shield, Furnace Visage, Verdigris Armor, and Verdigris Greaves.
This distinctive pattern appears on the Divine Towers, with some pillar reliefs featuring central cavities filled with glowing meteorite ore.
The Troll's Hammer, used by giants during an age when smithing held divine significance, also features eight circles orbiting a central circle.
The Verdigris Discus shares this pattern with the fell god's eye. Verdigris, believed to be a gift from an outer god, also appears on the talismans and great dish carried by the Fire Giant. 
St. Trina's prophesied adult form shared many physical traits with the fell god.
The fell god's red hair grows on its followers, such as the Fire Giants, Monks, and Prelates.
Radagon, Messmer, Rykard, Radahn, Ranni, Malenia, Millicent, and Millicent's Sisters all have the same red hair. Melina's hair is much more faded than the rest.
Red hair also appear on every single Fire Knight, those who had received inside them the flame of Messmer, who had visions of the Flame burning the Erdtree and the kindling inside him.
Radagon resented his own red hair, which was a curse of the giants.
Misbegotten, especially Misbegotten Warriors, have red hair and fur.
Red is a color strongly associated with life and the Crucible, and is the color of the horned Great Red Bears.
Red hair appears to seep from the severed Omen horns protruding from the Dung Eater's armor. The only opening in the Omen Helm is a large crack near the right eye.
Although inaccessible through normal gameplay, the Dung Eater has faded red hair and is only character modeled to have a deformed facial appearance.
The blind Lamenter has horns, red hair, and a dormant face resting on its back. Though its blissful state was a true form of enlightment, the fearful horsent refused to accept it and foolishly buried it deep underground in the Lamenter's Gaol.
It is commonly referred to as being "grotesque," "corrupt," "malformed," "fell," and "evil."
Milos the giant was also seen as malformed.
Fire Sprites are naturally the most boisterous of their kind.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In the Japanese localization for Burn, O Flame!, the Fire Giant is singular rather than plural, implying the fell god did not curse them prior to the War Against the Giants, rather it was the curse that Queen Marika the Eternal imposed on the last of their kind, as confirmed in the Remembrance of the Fire Giant's description.
While the English localization claims that the Hornsent's sagas were "haunted" by the Fell God, the Japanese description simply claims it was "An evil god of fire of the legends of the horned people" (角人たちの伝承にある、火の悪神である). The Hornsent were aware of the Formless Mother and Shadow Undead at the Abandoned Ailing Village cast Swarm of Flies, an incantation associated with the Formless Mother, they used Rot for purification rituals through Romina, Saint of the Bud and kept Gravebirds inside Belurat and Enir-Ilim, golems crafted as kindreds to the Deathbirds. The god of fire being considered as "fell" (evil) could be attributed to Messmer's soldiers who built the Furnace Golem, as the people of Erdtree viewed all deities other than Marika negatively and had a tradition of addressing the deity as "fell" through multiple artifacts.

name: Fia, Deathbed Companion
description: Fia, Deathbed Companion is an NPC character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Fia was once a Deathbed Companion. She would receive the warmth and vigor from champions, and then lay with the remains of an exalted noble, to grant him another chance at life. This was the sole purpose of Fia's existence, and was considered a sacred act in her homeland. 

However, before Fia could bear the noble into new life, she was awakened by the guidance of grace, and chased from her birthplace, travelling to the Lands Between. At some point she met a chivalrous knight by the name of Lionel the Lionhearted. Upon meeting the exiled Fia, Lionel declared himself to be her father, and became her loyal companion.

Fia found herself in Roundtable Hold, where she continued to perform her role as a Deathbed Companion. Here, she encountered Rogier, a spellblade obsessed with Those Who Live in Death, and a Tarnished champion seeking to become Elden Lord. Rogier began an investigation into the events surrounding the Night of Black Knives, which had led to the death of Godwyn, aided by the Tarnished champion. Fia subtly aided the pair in their investigation, pointing them towards the Black Knifeprint, and granted her services to the Tarnished champion, taking their warmth and vigor in exchange for her blessings.

Unbeknownst to the other Tarnished of Roundtable Hold, Fia was the companion of Godwyn, the Prince of Death, and wished to become a mother to Those Who Live in Death. After asking the Tarnished to return a Weathered Dagger to D, Hunter of the Dead, Fia kills D, who was in possession of one half of the Cursemark of Death, and returns the Cursemark to the malformed corpse of Godwyn in Deeproot Depths. She then solicits the assistance of the Tarnished in retrieving the other half of the Cursemark, which she uses to gestate a Mending Rune that can embed the principle of Life in Death into Order.

D, Beholder of Death, seeking revenge for his brother, D, kills Fia after she creates her Mending Rune.
