sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Fia's questline ties into the questlines of several other NPCs, and is required in order to achieve the Age of the Duskborn ending.
Roundtable Hold
Fia can be found in her room in Roundtable Hold. Initially she will be available to provide a Baldachin's Blessing.
After Rogier comes to Roundtable Hold and discusses the Night of Black Knives, Fia will provide a Knifeprint Clue. The Black Knifeprint must be obtained and given to Rogier.
Roundtable Hold
After triggering the Radahn Festival, Fia will ask you to return the Weathered Dagger to its rightful owner. You must give this to D, Hunter of the Dead, and reload the area.
Fia can now be found in a previously locked room, standing over D's corpse. Exhaust her dialogue and she will disappear.
Deeproot Depths
Defeat Fia's Champions and rest at the Site of Grace. Fia will be sitting in front of Godwyn's corpse. She will offer you the opportunity to kill her. To continue her questline, select "No, I want to be held." Selecting "That's right" will not lock you out of the rest of the questline, and you can change your mind by speaking to her again.
While being held, choose "Talk in Secret" to learn about the Cursemark of Death.
Divine Tower of Liurnia
In order to access the Divine Tower of Liurnia, you need to have progressed Ranni the Witch's quest and received the Carian Inverted Statue. Use the statue on the pedestal in the first room of the Carian Study Hall and progress through the area to the Divine Tower. 
Retrieve the Cursemark of Death from the top of the tower.
Deeproot Depths
Speak to Fia again and select "Talk in Secret" until you receive the option to hand Fia the Cursemark of Death.
Exhaust her dialogue once again and reload the area to find her sleeping. 
Deathbed Dream
Interact with Fia's body to enter the Deathbed Dream. Defeat Lichdragon Fortissax to return to Deeproot Depths.
Deeproot Depths
Loot the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince from Fia's body. This will allow you to achieve the Age of Duskborn ending.
Reload the area to find Fia dead, with D, Beholder of Death standing over her.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Fia will not fight you if attacked, however skull-like projectiles resembling those summoned when casting Rancorcall will spawn above her head and target you. Her dialogue when attacked implies that Godwyn is the source of these projectiles.

description: The Finger Reader Crones are a set of eight characters in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The eldery Finger Reader Crones were immortal oracles who divined messages from the Greater Will and its vassals, the Two Fingers, speaking on their behalf. They perceived the Fingers' formless language of light, interpreting their motions into speech. Finger Readers congregated in Leyndell, Royal Capital during the age of the Erdtree. One was rumored to have served as wet nurse to Godwyn the Golden.

When the Two Fingers atop the Divine Towers fell inert during or after the Shattering, many Finger Readers became dormant. Those who remained active continued to seek fingers to read.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
Altus Plateau (Forest-Spanning Greatbridge)
Caelid (Smoldering Wall)
Capital Outskirts
Deeproot Depths
Forbidden Lands (Grand Lift of Rold)
Liurnia of the Lakes (Academy Gate Town)
Liurnia of the Lakes (east Raya Lucaria gate, near Bellum Highway)
Stormhill
Many dead or dormant Finger Readers can be found between the Erdtree Sanctuary and Queen's Bedchamber in Leyndell, Royal Capital, presumably dormant or having died of unnatural causes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The only named Finger Reader is Enia, found in the Roundtable Hold, and she is the only one who still interprets the words of her Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Two of the nameless eight nameless crones have internal names that do not display on the in-game HUD.
Keeper of Forbidden Lands - the Finger Reader at the bottom of the Grand Lift of Rold in the Forbidden Lands.
Godwyn's Wet Nurse - one of them was said to serve as a wet nurse to royalty; presumably the one in Deeproot Depths lamenting the fate of Godwyn, as she is also the only finger reader who does not specifically ask to read fingers. Their voice actress was also credited as Wet Nurse. 
Keeper of Forbidden Lands was named Keeper of Borders in.

description: The Finger Seal is a Sacred Seal and catalyst in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 800 Runes.

Obtained by default if selecting the Confessor or Prophet origins.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Used to cast Incantations. No bonus to any spells, including Two Fingers Incantations.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
At 249% Faith scaling this Seal is technically the third strongest in the game, and the strongest if your Faith is between 10 and 26. Do note that it is outclassed by any Sacred Seal with a bonus to certain spells if those spells are being cast. 
At 10 Faith it has 126 Incantation Scaling. 
At 20 Faith it has 156 Incantation Scaling. 
At 30 Faith it has 188 Incantation Scaling. 
At 40 Faith it has 221 Incantation Scaling. 
At 50 Faith it has 254 Incantation Scaling. 
At 60 Faith it has 286 Incantation Scaling. 
At 70 Faith it has 305 Incantation Scaling. 
At 80 Faith it has 329 Incantation Scaling. 
Consistently 3-5 points behind the Godslayer's Seal after reaching 27 Faith and above, making it quite viable to keep the Finger Seal upgraded for regular use if you have already invested in it and are somewhat lacking in regular Smithing Stones. 
Actually stronger than the Erdtree Seal until 66 Faith, and thereafter it becomes outclassed, which in combination with the latter requiring the much more common Somber Smithing Stones makes the latter option much more favorable. 
No bonus to any incantations, not even the ones granted by the Two Fingers, a trait shared only with the Erdtree Seal among the Sacred Seals

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.body: Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.

name: Fingerslayer Blade
image: ER Icon Key Item Fingerslayer Blade.png
description: The Fingerslayer Blade is a Key Item in. It is part of Ranni the Witch's questline.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
The Fingerslayer Blade must be given to Ranni the Witch at Ranni's Rise to advance her questline.
In exchange, Ranni will reward the player with the Carian Inverted Statue, which opens the path from the Carian Study Hall to the Divine Tower of Liurnia.
Grants access to the Cursemark of Death and the Stargazer Heirloom.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Location: Night's Sacred Ground
The Fingerslayer Blade is found inside a treasure chest at the base of the Chair-Crypt in Nokron, Eternal City. The chest is guarded by a Mimic Troll and multiple Silver Mimic Tears.
The locked Nox treasure chest containing the Fingerslayer Blade only opens for Ranni's followers. "You are not destined to open this" displays if the player tries to open it before agreeing to serve Ranni the Witch at Ranni's Rise.
Nokron, the upper Eternal City section of the Siofra River, becomes accessible after defeating Starscourge Radahn at the Wailing Dunes. The death of the Red Lion General releases certain stars from his gravitational grip, resuming fates held in stasis since the Starscourge Conflict. A falling star crashes to the earth in Limgrave, setting Ranni's Empyrean destiny back into motion. The starfall crater enables passage to the long-lost Eternal City.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The misshapen Fingerslayer Blade has a spiraling, crescent-shaped blade that faintly glows at its tip. Its crossguard bends in a downward arch, similar to the Rune of Death.
It strongly resembles the Sacred Relic Sword fashioned from the extracted remains of Radagon of the Golden Order, suggesting it was once a vessel that held the Elden Ring.
As per its reveal, only the Elden Beast can transform gods into armaments.
The Fingerslayer Blade is unlikely to originate from among the known cast.
Nox conspirators who wore Nox Mirrorhelms wielded the Fingerslayer Blade, likely against Metyr, Mother of Fingers, the daughter of the Greater Will who retreated beneath the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. This act triggered the invasion of Astel and the downfall of the Eternal Cities.
Later, Ranni the Witch can use the Fingerslayer Blade against her Two Fingers, hidden beneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes.
The Fingerslayer Blade, an item with which treacherous War Counselor Iji is well-versed, is guarded by a Troll.

name: Fire Giant
description: The is a boss in. He is encountered at Flame Peak on the Mountaintops of the Giants. This encounter is not optional as it must be completed to unlock Crumbling Farum Azula and advance the main storyline.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Alexander, Warrior Jar is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been met at Mt. Gelmir. His summon sign is just inside the western boss gate. Torrent can also be used during this fight.

The arena is a large snowfield with craggy, uneven terrain. The field slops upwards from the entrance, and the Giant begins the fight at the top of the slope. Torrent can be called during this fight, and is useful for covering distance and avoiding the avalanche by jumping.

Resistances:

Moveset:

Phase 1:

During phase 1, the Fire Giant will fight using a large, circular dish. Although he is fairly slow-moving, he is able to cover distance using his roll. He also possesses the ability to launch an avalanche straight towards the player. Initially, the majority of his attacks involve slamming the dish into the ground.

The objective initially is to attack the red braids wrapped around his left leg. After enough damage has been dealt, the braids will fall off, uncovering his injured ankle. At this point he will roll three times in succession, and then reach into the mouth on his abdomen, coating his hand in flames. He now gains the ability to use two fire-based abilities- a fast-moving fireball, and a large, slow-moving fire orb that homes in on the player.

Phase 2:

Once his health drops below 47%, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. The Fire Giant has now lost the large dish as well as his left leg, and is forced to kneel on the ground. He is less mobile during this phase, however he can still roll. He now has a greater variety of fire spells. He may summon pillars of fire that erupt from the ground around him, breathe fire, or spew molten rocks that rain down on the arena. His weak spot is now on his left forearm.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Fire Giants came in a range of sizes. Some were smaller than the Fire Giant, while others were larger. Even the largest known Fire Giants were smaller than the skulls of the colossal remains.
Each Fire Giant killed in the War Against the Giants is tangled in the Briars of Sin and has white hair rather than red, as if drained of color. It is unclear whether this change was caused by the thorns or occurs naturally upon a Fire Giant's death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: Giant (ID: c4760)
The Fire Giant is voiced by Shaun Dooley, who also voiced Shabriri, Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, and the Kaiden Sellswords.

name: Fire Knight's Shortsword
image: ER Icon weapon Fire Knight's Shortsword.png
description: The Fire Knight's Shortsword is a dagger melee armament found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: 4% chance to be dropped by dual dagger-wielding Fire Knights.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Generally leans towards Dexterity-scaling over Strength-scaling.
Despite the description this dagger actually has higher Faith-scaling and raw Attack Power (AP) on a Sacred affinity than on a Flame Art affinity. It's also outclassed in raw AP by a Flame Art affinity Erdsteel Dagger.
However, the Fire Knight's Shortsword's Flame Art affinity usually has higher effective damage than the Sacred affinity due to only having to bypass 2 flat defences rather than 3, and the Fire damage will be higher on its own than either the Sacred affinity's Holy damage or the Flame Art Erdsteel Dagger's Fire damage.
Surprisingly enough, since this weapon is themed after Faith and Fire, it actually has the strongest Intelligence-scaling of all Daggers on the Magic and Cold affinities. 
Though the innate Fire damage is low on all but the Fire and Flame Art affinities, simply having it means it will immediate reset fully applied Frostbite on the next hit if on a Cold affinity or using Frostbite-causing skills such as Chilling Mist. It will also stun enemies that are extremely vulnerable to fire, such as Fingercreepers and Miranda Sprouts and Blossoms
Has a unique double-hitting heavy attack shared with the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger. 
This unique attack grants 4 points towards the scaling of the Winged Sword Insignias instead of the usual 2, due to hitting twice.
If choosing any of the Magic, Cold, Blood, Poison, or Occult affinities this is one of the few weapons that can scale with four separate stats. 
In the base game the ability to scale with four different stats via affinities was only held by the Clayman's Harpoon and the Erdsteel Dagger, while the DLC added the Black Steel Greathammer, Bloodfiend's Arm, and Fire Knight's Greatsword, weapons which all have the same quality.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Slam down on the ground do hit with Fire Attack Power equal to 183% of Incantation Scaling with a 3 meter radius and gain a Body Buff that hits 4/s with 45 Fire Attack Power with a 2 meter radius while ignoring Guarding. Lasts for 40 seconds and damages the caster for 6/s (240 damage total). 

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power of the initial fire explosion to 212% of Incantation Scaling and the Body Buff's Attack Power per tick to 59. Self damage is increased to 8/s (320 damage total).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 10 FP per cast.
Costs 28 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 36. 
Requires 1 Memory Slot. 
The initial fire explosion deals 7 Stance damage while the ticks from the Buff deals 0 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage of the initial explosion to 10. 
The self damage is technically 3/0.5 seconds for the uncharged version and 4/0.5 seconds for the charged version. 

Boosting:

Old Lord's Talisman increases the duration of this spell from 40 to 52 seconds.
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 16% for the explosion and by 31% for the ticks, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 33% for the explosion and by 51% for the ticks.

Strategies:
The Attack Power is too low to reliably defeat most enemies without additional sources of damage.
Fire attacks cleanse targets of their Frostbite buildup, resetting the status effect. This spell synergizes particularly well with Frostbite builds by allowing them to trigger Frostbite damage more frequently than usual.
The constant HP drain from this spell can be mitigated by using the Blessing of the Erdtree or Blessing's Boon incantations, the Crimsonburst Crystal Tear; the Blessed Dew Talisman, the Icon Shield, or the Royal Remains Armor. Equipping the full Royal Remains Set will completely offset the damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like Catch Flame and Flame Sling, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.

In a prior version of, this spell could guarantee the activation of the Erdtree Greatshield's Golden Retaliation skill, triggering its golden projectile whenever used.
Additionally, this spell used to inherit the on-hit effects of active Weapon Buffs. Most notably, this included the Blood Loss buildup from Bloodflame Blade and the Death Blight effect from the Eclipse Shotel's Death Flare skill, resulting in devastating consequences.
Patch 1.03: Fixed a bug which causes Fire's Deadly Sin incantation to have different effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged. 
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 21%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total 39%. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Fire Knight Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Attack Power is boosted by 3% when the Messmer's Helm is worn. 
Attack Power is boosted by 4% when the Fire Knight Armor is worn. 
Excellent tracking before it begins to move, able to launch even at targets that have managed to get between the caster and the flame. The tracking remains fairly good after launching. 
Has roughly 17% less Attack Power than Flame Sling with a similar casting time and the exact same FP cost. However, Flame Sling has no specific equipment that boosts only it, while Fire Serpent has several and stacking all of those means it will do roughly 1-3% more damage. 
The range is fairly mediocre. This, in combinations with the strong tracking, makes this more of a short to medium range spell.

sections.body:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 14 FP per cast.
Costs 10 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot.
The reason that Frostbite is only removed when fully applied instead of also when it's building up is because the flat HP damage is considered to be Fire damage, and an effect of that damage type is that it removes applied Frostbite. 

Strategies:
This incantation is considered vital for navigating swamp areas filled with Poison and Scarlet Rot.
This is especially true for Scarlet Rot areas as other means of removing it is either in limited supply (Preserving Boluses) or only get one use without resting at a Site of Grace again (Speckled Hardtear). 
While technically only the Prophet and Confessor origins have enough Faith to use this incantation by default, it can still be used by any starting Origin's at base Faith by using the Two Fingers Heirloom (a Prisoner will need another point in Faith, easiest gained with either Marika's Scarseal or a Commoner's Garb or Commoner's Simple Garb).
All Origins also start with enough FP to cast this incantation at least 3 times without using a Flask of Cerulean Tears, provided they haven't used any FP for anything too expensive.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Flings 12 balls of fire each with Fire Attack Power equal to 115% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 140% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 16 FP per cast.
Costs 40 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 52 points. 
Technically the Stamina cost is 10 points for the uncharged version and 13 for the charged version, but the cost is taken 4 times. 
Requires 1 Memory Slot.
Deals 4 Stance damage per hit (12 at most). Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 6 (18 at most).
The initial fireball will split into 12 after traveling a short distance.
At most 3 of the small fireballs can damage a single target. This limits the effective maximum Attack Power of this spell towards a singlet target to roughtly 345% of Incantation Scaling, or 420% of the same when charged. 
When charged, the fireballs will explode on impact to deal area-of-effect (AoE) damage.
Inflicts additional Stamina damage to blocking targets.

Boosting:

Godfrey Icon increases the Attack Power of charged attacks by 15%.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 22%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of??%.

Strategies:
Each fireball deals individual damage, and hitting with multiple fireballs can greatly increase damage output.
This spell is highly effective against large targets, as most or all fireballs can hit, and works well for groups due to its solid AoE damage, low FP cost, and quick casting.
At close range, only the initial fireball may hit before splitting, so midrange is ideal for landing multiple hits.
The wide spread and AoE of the fireballs can catch evasive enemies, making it useful against invaders or invisible Teardrop Scarabs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Update 1.07: Decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
The FP cost was decreased from 18 to 16.
Stamina Attack Power against Guarding enemies was increased from 25 to 34 per hit for the uncharged version and from 34 to 42 per hit for the charged version. 
Against players the Stamina Attack Power was increased from 25 to 42 per hit for the uncharged version and from 34 to 52 per hit for the charged version. 
Update 1.04: Decreased the damage of single cast and improved the performance so that it hits the enemy multiple times. Decreased FP cost.
The Attack Power of the uncharged version was reduced from 245% of Incantation Scaling to 115% of the same, and the Attack Power of the charged version from 286% of Incantation Scaling to 140% of the same. 
The hit limit per enemy per cast was increased from 1 to 3.

description: Flame Fortification is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants

Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Flame Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Fire damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 FP per cast.
Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces fire damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where FlameFortification represents the effect magnitude:
TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {FireDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {FlameFortification}) )
For example, if fire damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

Strategies:
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as fire damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple fire negation sources.
Flame Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Fire damage in the game, especially against dragons, fire monks, and Radahn soldiers, as well as while exploring Mt. Gelmir.
Flame Fortification offers greater fire protection than Fireproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
The Fireproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.

name: Flame, Protect Me
image: ER Icon Spell Flame, Protect Me.png
description: Flame, Protect Me is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Fire Monk incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Mountaintops of the Giants
Flame, Protect Me can be found in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave in the Mountaintops of the Giants. It is located behind an imp statue fog wall right next to the dungeon's grace. One Stonesword Key is required to access it.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Flame, Protect Me applies a Body Buff that increases Fire Damage Negation by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 30 FP per cast.
Costs 20 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot.

This incantation reduces damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total Fire damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where FlameProtect represents the PvE/PvP effect multiplier:
TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {FireDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {FlameProtect}) )
For example, if Fire damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 70%:
TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.60) ) = 70%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 40%:
TotalFireReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.20) ) = 40%

Boosting:
Old Lord's Talisman extends the duration from 70 to 91 seconds.

Strategies:
Acquired very late, most often after every significant Fire-heavy area and boss except for Mountaintops of the Giants itself and the Fire Giant, and perhaps Dragonlord Placidusax. 
If doing the Volcano Manor questline to access Praetor Rykard, then he can be fought after acquiring this incantation since the last assassination also takes place in Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave
This is the only improved elemental defense buff that doesn't also apply to nearby allies. 
The only way to also buff nearby allies with Fire Damage Negation is Protection of the Erdtree, which also increases Holy, Lightning, and Magic Damage Negation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: This incantation is one of the oldest known techniques among the Fire Monks.

description: Flame Sling is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Flame incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:

Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Fling a small ball of fire with Fire Attack Power equal to 202% of Incantation Scaling.

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 255% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 11 points of FP to cast.
Costs 22 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 29 points. 
Requires 1 Memory Slot.
Deals 5 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 9.25. 

Boosting:

Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon. 
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 26%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of 45%. 
Although this spell utilizes the Giants' Flame, its power is not boosted by the Giant's Seal.

Strategies:
An easy to use spell with very early availability that'll provide very good damage throughout the game. 
Doesn't hold up as well late game since more damaging spells such as Giantsflame Take Thee and Black Flame (especially the latter's maximum HP-based bonus burn damage) will be more useful when FP isn't as precious and kill speed becomes more important.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like Catch Flame and Fire's Deadly Sin, this incantation does not produce a spell sigil when cast, indicating that it technically doesn't belong to the Giants' Flame subtype and isn't boosted by the Giant's Seal.
Flame Sling was formerly known as "Feast Upon Flame" during the Closed Network Test.
Similar to the Fireball spell from the Dark Souls franchise.
Patch 1.07: Increased attack power when charged.
The Attack Power of the charged version was increased from 240% of Incantation Scaling to 255% of the same.

name: Forge of the Giants
description: The Forge of the Giants is a location in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
An ancient artifact of the Rauh civilization, the Great Forge contained the ever-burning power of the nameless fell god. The Fire Giants later claimed the forge when they invaded the Mountaintop, driving the Ice Dragons from their icy, windswept home. Sparks from the Forge of the Giants showered the frozen mountaintops, fertilizing the land with Fire Blossoms.

Long ago, Queen Marika ordered Lord Godfrey and his warriors to wage a war against the Giants, whose flame of ruin threatened her burgeoning age of the Erdtree. Marika's forces defeated the giants and confined the Flame, but it could not be fully extinguished. Marika cursed the last Fire Giant to tend it for all eternity. 

Game events:
Melina instructs the Tarnished awaken the flame of ruin and commit the first Cardinal Sin. After either she or the Tarnished burns the Erdtree, the Tarnished is transported to Crumbling Farum Azula, where the Rune of Death is hidden.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: The Forge of the Giants is accessible via Flame Peak after defeating the Fire Giant. The player teleports to Crumbling Farum Azula following a one-time cutscene at this location.

sections.heading: Sites of Grace
sections.body:
Forge of the Giants = 

The Forge of the Giants Site of Grace is found on the eastern lip of the forge. If Melina has not left the player, the option to burn the Erdtree will be present. The "Listen to the flames" option will be present if not. Both options will cause the Erdtree to burn and transport the player to Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Characters
sections.body: Melina

sections.heading: Items
sections.body: Smoldering Butterfly

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Alexander, Warrior Jar believes the flame of ruin can repair the crack he sustained in his duel with Starscourge Radahn.
The Forge shares architecture motifs with the Divine Towers and Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
The decoupled chains suggest the Lands Between was once part of a larger island. Whatever missing landmasses they connected to may be sealed or have drifted away.
Statues from the Ancient Dynasty show a bearded man holding half of an engraved tablet, with the other half at his feet. The tablet texture was sourced from the Imago Mundi, the earliest known world map.
Alternatively, the Forge may have once been a portable smithery, suspended by chains like a hanging cauldron.
The titan skeletons here are smaller than those in Caelid.
Forge of the Giants is visible from the First Step in Limgrave.

name: Formless Mother
description: The Formless Mother (姿なき母, Sugata-naki Haha), also known as Mother of Truth (真実の母, Shinjitsu no Haha), is an Outer God and.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Formless Mother is omnipresent and can be stabbed from anywhere in the Lands Between by using a ritual spear.
Although never directly stated, many details point to the Land of Reeds being under the influence of the Formless Mother. Descriptions of Reedlanders as having "succumbed to a blood-soaked madness" and their clear favoritism for weapons that cause Blood Loss all point towards the work of the Outer God. The magical enhancement granded by the forbidden Reedlander combat technique, Seppuku, may very well be a blessing from the Formless Mother, with the technique acting as a form of offering. Additionally, both Okina and Eleonora join Mohg's Bloody Fingers.
The entity responsible for the Thorn Sorceries, Briars of Punishment and Briars of Sin, referred to as the blood star, the may have some connection to the Formless Mother. It is entirely possible due to their perceived values of spilling blood and inflicting wounds, that the Formless Mother and "the blood star", could be one in the same.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The Mother's designation as "Formless" resembles the title of a Great One (conceptually similar to an Outer God) that is indirectly featured in the FromSoftware game Bloodborne, called "Formless Oedon" (姿なきオドン, Sugata-naki Odon). In fact, both entities are strongly associated with blood.

name: Fortissax's Lightning Spear
image: ER Icon Spell Fortissax's Lightning Spear.png
description: Fortissax's Lightning Spear is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Trade the Remembrance of the Lichdragon, gained by defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, with Finger Reader Enia.
Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Calls on two red, crackling spears from above that is then slammed into the ground, hitting with Lightning Attack Power equal to 367% of Incantation Scaling in a small 0.2 meter radius, and creating a shockwave with a 3 meter radius that hits with Lightning Attack Power equal to 288% of Incantation Scaling.

From the point of impact, waves of red lightning are sent out directly ahead and behind, and to the left and right of the caster with Lightning Attack Power equal to 122% of Incantation Scaling in a 2 meter radius from the center of each wave. 

The second spear is slammed down as the first spear's waves are spreading, repeating the process but with the power of the direct hit increasing to 374% of Incantation Scaling, the shockwave hit to 292% of the same, and the wave hit to 123% of the same.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Casting the spell costs 42 points of Stamina. 
Deals 16.8 Stance damage on a direct or shockwave hit and 5 Stance damage on a wave hit. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
The "direct" hit and the initial area attack cannot hit the same target, though the smaller, weakest waves can hit an enemy that has already been hit if they are either quick or large enough to also be where those are. 
The "spears" are actually flung downwards, meaning they can be used to hit the ground beneath a cliff if the caster is standing on its edge. 
Has a much longer casting time than Ancient Dragons' Lightning Spear due to having two spears, but each hit is stronger.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them. 
Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
FP cost was reduced from 45 to 35. 
Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 100 to 140 on the direct hit with the first spear and from 120 to 160 with the second spear. 
Separate Stamina Attack Power values for guarding players: for the first spear the direct hit was increased from 140 to 175, the shockwave hit was increased from 100 to 125, and the wave hit was increased from 60 to 75, while for the second spear the direct hit was increased from 160 to 200, the shockwave hit was increased from 120 to 150, and the wave hit was increased from 60 to 75. 
Patch 1.04 decreased FP and Stamina cost, increased cast speed and decreased recovery time, and allows caster to withstand enemy attack while casting more easily.
FP cost was reduced from 65 to 45.

name: Frenzied Flame
description: The Frenzied Flame (狂い火, Kurui Hi), also called Yellow Flame of Frenzy (黄色い狂い火, Kiiroi Kurui Hi) and Yellow Flame of Chaos (混沌の黄色い火, Konton no Kiiroi Hi), is a force that manifests in the eyes of those stricken by maddening grief and suffering. It is feared by many for its uncanny ability to destroy individuality, capable of melting away even eternal spirits. Those deeply stricken by its folly develop an insatiable need to spread its influence further, willingly seeking to infect others with it. These afflicted, known by some as Chaos Followers, yearn for the arrival of their lord so that they may incinerate all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The flame's ability to blend minds together may have been more apparent in an earlier version of. As the brotherhood of Nomadic Merchants that can be encountered throughout the world would mention that they fear going to sleep, as while asleep, they would feel as if their minds would rapidly drift and switch between each other, leaving all of them bewildered and confused on who they really are when they wake up.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Jump up and create blue, icy lightning spear which is then slammed down to create two slightly overlapping fields of lightning, one after the other. The slam and each field has Lightning Attack Power equal to 307% of Incantation Scaling and inflict 120 Frostbite build-upw.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:

Deals 5 Stance damage per hit.

The second is where the first lightning field ends and the second one begins, which is roughly at the halfway points of the incantation's reach.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Fulghor was a gallant and pious centaur who, in ancient times, undertook an arduous quest in service of radiant gods that cloaked themselves in thunder. When his left arm was severed from behind, he realized his comrades had betrayed him and the gods they served.

Fulghor later encountered and embraced the Night, but his holy zeal did not falter. He channeled a sacred form of the Night's power and was consumed by battle, becoming a Nightlord and the champion of Nightglow.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: Centaurus.
Fulghor was the second Everdark Sovereign to debut.
Among the Nightlords, Fulghor is the only one whose title is not simply just "of Night", rather "of Nightglow".
During the Everdark fight, Fulghor's glowing cross bears some resemblance to Miquella's Cross.
Also in his Everdark form, Fulghor is able to air-walk, not unlike Spirits such as Torrent and the Ancestor Spirit.
Fulghor shares some characteristics with Gundyr from the Dark Souls series:
Their heavy build, armor, and helmet design.
Their transformation with an oversized, left arm of darkness.
Their alternate encounter, with both as their non-afflicted selves.

name: Fulgurbloom
description: Fulgurbloom is a crafting material in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Fulgurbloom grows abundantly in spots where lightning strikes regularly. These spots can be found in every major area. 
The earliest accessible spot of 14 Fulgurbloom is in Limgrave, on the hill just north of the Agheel Lake North site of grace. 
In Weeping Peninsula a group of 8 can be found east from the MInor Erdtree in a small ravine accessible via Tombstones embedded in the side of the cliff. 
In Altus Plateau, the largest collection, with 3 groups, can be found near the Rampartside Path site of grace, east of the Sainted Hero's Grave. Head west from the Grace for the first group of 10 and then head south for the second group of 8. Go northeast to get up on the hill just south of the Grace itself for the third group of 10. Be aware that Ancient Dragon Lansseax spawns very close to the route.
In Liurnia of the Lakes, directly northeast from the Island Testu's Rise is located on a group of 14 can be found. 
In Caelid, more specifically Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, a group of 10 can be found along the way between the Minor Erdtree and the Farum Greatbridge. 
At Castle Sol in Mountaintops of the Giants, the largest collection of two groups can be found. Just west of the Castle Sol Main Gate site of grace first a group of 13 and the of 15 is located. 
In Consecrated Snowfield, east from the Ordina, Liturgical Town site of grace up the hill in the most north-eastern part of the area a group of 27 can be found around a rock pillar formation. 
Also dropped by certain lightning-infused enemies found in Altus Plateau and Leyndell, Royal Capital. Specifically Lightning Sheep (20%), and lightning pot-throwing Imps (10%) and Leyndell Soldiers (5%).

name: Furious Blade of Ansbach
image: ER Icon Spell Furious Blade of Ansbach.png
description: Furious Blade of Ansbach is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Blood Oath Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Enir-Ilim
Complete Sir Ansbach's questline while siding with him against Needle Knight Leda and defeat Promised Consort Radahn and then this Incantation (as well as Ansbach's Set and the Obsidian Lamina) can be found on his body, just to the right after entering the boss arena again.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
User dashes forward slightly before slashing twice in wide arcs with a bloodflame dagger to deal Fire damage equal to 97% of Incantation Scaling twice, before a wave of fire follows the path of the last slash to deal another burst of Fire damage equal to 154% of Incantation Scaling. 

For the charged version, there are now three dagger slashes that deal damage equal to 98% of Incantation Scaling and the final burst deals damage equal to 163% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 37 points of Stamina to cast, whether charged or uncharged.
Inflicts Blood Loss build-up, 180 for the uncharged version and 250 for the charged version. 
Since all of the Blood Loss comes from bloodflame effects the build-up doesn't scale with Arcane, even if the Dragon Communion Seal is used. 
For context, most enemies have a default resistance to Blood Loss of roughly 400 to 500, meaning the uncharged spell will most likely cause the Status Effect in 2-3 casts and the charged version will usually cause it within 2 casts, provided they are cast somewhat quickly after the other. 
Damage is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon when charged. 
Since the damage of the dagger slashes already are increase by 1% the total increase is 16% for them, while the final burst has its damage increase by 6% and thus gets a total increase of 22%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.13 increased attack power, fixed a bug where the “Furious Blade of Ansbach” Incantation did not apply Hemorrhage status build up.
For the uncharged spell the dagger slashes had their damage increased from 90% of Incantation Scaling to 97% of the same, and the final burst had its damage increase from 145% of Incantation Scaling to 154% of the same. The charged spell's dagger slashes had their damage increased from 90% of Incantation Scaling to 98% of the same, and its final burst had its damage increase from 145% of Incantation Scaling to 163% of the same. 
Patch 1.14 cancelling this incantation into rolls will now take less time, increased poise damage, increased enemy knockback distance.
For the dagger hits the poise damage was increased from 4 (68 against other players) to 5 (85 against other players) and for the wave of fire the poise damage was increased from 2 (34 against other players) to 3 (51 against other players).

name: Gatekeeper Gostoc
description: Gatekeeper Gostoc is an NPC and merchant in.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Basic Info:

Quest Items:

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Stormveil Castle 
Gostoc can be found in the gatehouse to the left of the main gate. He will offer you the choice of taking the main gate or using the side entrance. Choosing "No, I'll use the main entrance" will cause the main gate to open when you approach it. This will not prevent you from taking the side entrance, however.
Stormveil Castle
(Optional) Upon entering a dark room in the western section of the castle, Gostoc will close the door, locking you in with a Banished Knight enemy. To leave, grab the Rusty Key and return to the door to open it. If you die in this room, you can return to it and loot the item without being locked in again.
(Optional) Gostoc will now appear in several locations around the dungeon. Speaking to him in one of these locations for the first time will reward you with a Grace Mimic. The locations are as follows:
Stormveil Cliffside. He will appear on a ledge above the Site of Grace, only if you enter the castle via the wooden scaffold and head straight back.
Western Wall ground floor. He will appear here after you have gone up the ladder past the door unlocked with the Rusty Key.
Chapel roof. He will appear on the roof of the chapel where you meet Rogier, after visiting the roof with the Grafted Scion and returning.
Rampart Tower. He will appear in the elevator tower, on a wooden platform that needs to be jumped to.
While he is in any of these locations, he will take 30% of the Runes you drop if you die in the dungeon. In order to get him to stop, talk to him at any one of the first three listed locations, and then at the fourth location. Then, return to his location at the gatehouse and talk to him again. He will no longer steal any Runes.
Additionally, he will become available as a merchant if you return to him after he begins stalking you.
Stormveil Castle (Godrick's arena)
After defeating Godrick the Grafted, Gostoc will appear in the room. After exhausting his dialogue his shop will be open once again. He will also stop stealing your Runes if you skipped the previous part.
Stormveil Castle (Throne Room)
After completing Nepheli Loux's questline, Gostoc will appear in the back of the throne room. After exhausting his dialogue, his shop will become available again, now with an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone available to purchase.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Cut dialogue suggests Gostoc was to be revealed a son of Godrick and, by extension, the Golden Lineage.
Much of his questline and content was cut from the game. He was able to compete with Nepheli Loux for lordship of Stormveil Castle after Godricks defeat. He would succumb to the process of grafting himself, however.

name: Ghostflame Breath
description: Ghostflame Breath is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak
Acquired from the altar at the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 3 Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of deathly mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 168% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 55 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. 504% of Incantation Scaling and 165 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Dragonice.
Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Dragonice, and Borealis's Mist), this is the most cost-effective for Magic damage, but causes considerably less Frostbite build-up.
Compared to Dragonice, this spell deals 25% more damage but also consumes 20% more FP and causes 50% less Frostbite build-up.
Compared to Borealis's Mist, this spell deals 5% more damage and consumes 15% less FP but causes 50% less Frostbite build-up.
Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Despite not being a named dragon breath, it behaves like one. This means that the caster floats in midair and that it cannot be cast when riding Torrent.
This is effectively the second strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 11% less damage than Smarag's Glintstone Breath and only 0.6% less damage than Agheel's Flame (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals 8% more damage than Rotten Breath. 
However, the, admittedly low, Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks. 
Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

variant.effect: Channels dragon to spew ghostflame breath

name: Ghostflame Dragon
description: Ghostflame Dragons are optional bosses in. They are weak to both Holy damage and anti-dragon effects.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
There are three Ghostflame Dragons in the Realm of Shadow:

Gravesite Plain
Location: Near the Greatbridge, North Site of Grace.
Details: Found asleep in the center of a swamp upon first encounter. During phase 2, it gains the ability to summon Skeletons to assist it in battle.

Scadu Altus
Location: In a clearing near the Moorth Highway Site of Grace.
Details: This Ghostflame Dragon is engaged in a skirmish with a battalion of Messmer Soldiers, Messmer Foot Soldiers, and Black Knights.

Cerulean Coast
Location: South of the Cerulean Coast Site of Grace.
Details: This dragon dramatically swoops down from the sky during its initial encounter. It summons several Skeletons each time it uses its Ghostflame Bellow attack.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body: All Ghostflame Dragons drop a Dragon Heart and a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body: Ghostflame Dragons utilize a modified version of the standard Dragon movepool. Compared to other Dragons, they prefer to fight within melee range. Their Ghostflame breath attacks deal magic damage and apply Frostbite buildup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Ghostflame Dragons count as both Dragon and Undead enemies.
Ghostflame dragons are weak to both Holy damage and anti-dragon effects.
Defeating a Ghostflame Dragon will unlock Ghostflame Breath when performing Dragon Communion.
Multiplayer and Spirit Ashes are allowed in all Ghostflame Dragon encounters.

name: Giants' Flame
image: ER Icon Spell Flame of the Fell God.png
description:
The Giants' Flame (巨人の火, Kyojin no Hi), also referred to as the Flame of Ruin (滅びの火, Horobi no Hi) and the Flame of the Fell God (悪神の火, Akujin no Hi), is a divine element in.

The flame of ruin is an ancient and inextinguishable fire capable of burning even the Erdtree itself. This power of the fell god is wielded as Giants' Flame incantations by Fire Giants and Fire Monks.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
]]

The flame of ruin has burned within the great black cauldron atop Flame Peak since prehistoric times. Sparks from the Forge of the Giants rained upon the frozen Mountaintops of the Giants, fertilizing the land with half-ashen blooms called Fire Blossoms. Its embers even reanimated the dead. The Fire Giants borrowed this Flame from their fell god. 

The flame of ruin long plagued the hornsent, and ultimately threatened the emerging Age of the Erdtree. To eradicate the threat of the first Cardinal Sin, Marika ordered Godfrey and her unified army to annihilate the Fire Giants and seal the Flame. The Fire Giants were defeated, and, according to legend, Queen Marika vanquished the fell god herself. Though victorious, Queen Marika could not extinguish the flame of the forge. Instead, she cursed the last Fire Giant to tend to it for eternity.

Age of the Erdtree:

The fell god's Flame was a forbidden subject during Queen Marika's reign. Although its presence was a native part of the Golden Order, it was anathema to Erdtree Worship. The Fire Monks were appointed to guard the Flame, and the path to the Mountaintops became Forbidden Lands. However, the Erdtree was fated to catch flame, and prophets who foresaw the cardinal sin were branded heretics and banished. The Fire Monks eventually succumbed to the Flame's allure, and worshipped it out of reverence and fear. The secrets of the Giants' Flame were documented in a Giant's Prayerbook and kept hidden by the Prelates. The Flame's ability to consume the Erdtree was later suppressed when Maliketh sealed the Rune of Death.

After the Shattering, Adan stole the Flame of the Fell God from Chief Guardian Arghanthy, and Fire Monks crusaded as far as Liurnia to reclaim it.

Game events:

The flame of ruin continues to smolder within the forge on the northern mountaintops. It can be rekindled to burn the Erdtree and its impenetrable thorns. This unlocks the road to Crumbling Farum Azula and Destined Death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Some Fire Monks were captivated by the Black Flame, becoming Blackflame Monks.
Only Melina or a Lord of Frenzied Flame may awaken the Giants' Flame.
The fell god is said to inhabit the Giants' Flame.
The champions of the Erdtree used Flame, Protect Me to bolster themselves during the War Against the Giants.
A Flame within strengthens the body and cleanses poison and scarlet rot.
Flame grants life to Burning Corpses.
Giants' Flame is emulated by the Flame Chariots.
The Furnace Golems use a variant of Flame.
Messmerfire is closely related to the Giants' Flame.
Both resurrect Putrid Corpses
Messmer's Orb is nearly identical to the Flame of the Fell God.
Messmer's Kindling burns the Sealing Tree that shrouds Enir-Ilim.
Flare, O Serpent! follows the naming schema.
Black Flame is closely related to the Giants' Flame.
In the Chinese and Korean 1.0 version of the Sword and Night of Flame, Radagon is symbolized by Giants' Flame."

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: NocturnalCerberus.
Gladius was first revealed in the initial trailer and was the only Nightlord featured in the network test.
Among the Nightlords, Gladius is:
The first to be fought.
The last Everdark Sovereign to debut.
The name Gladius derives from the Latin word for "sword," referring to the short, double-edged blades used by Roman soldiers from the 3rd century BC to the 3rd century AD.
Its design draws heavily from Cerberus, the three-headed hound of Greek mythology that guards the gates of the underworld to prevent the dead from leaving. This makes Gladius a fitting choice as the first Nightlord to be fought.
In Maliketh, the Black Blade's boss area at Crumbling Farum Azula, there is a statue of a young girl surrounded by three wolves below a prehistoric depiction of the Elden Ring.
Gladius' story is similar to that of the spirits of the Lone Wolf Ashes summon. This item, alongside the Spirit Calling Bell, were delivered to the Tarnished by Ranni the Witch, who was entrusted to do so by Torrent's former master.
Curiously, the Tricephalos' expedition's description compares Gladius to shadows, a term similar to the Shadowbound Beasts.
One of Everdark Gladius' attacks is the exact same used by Heolstor the Nightlord, hinting that the latter was the swordsman in Gladius' backstory.
Gladius is reminiscent of Sif from the Dark Souls series:
Both are massive wolves who wield great swords for their boss fights.
They each have a bond with a swordsman, whose sword they utilize.
Their names may have ties with the word "sword", with Gladius' being of Latin origin and Sif's arguably sounding similar to saif of Arabic origin.
Gladius might also hold ties to the Red Wolves. Interestingly, Gladius is weakest to Holy, which instead deals the least damage to the red wolves.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of blue flames, dealing Magic damage equal to 159% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e. 477% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 40 points of Stamina to cast, and another 40 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Smarag's Glintstone Breath. 
Compared to Smarag's Glintstone Breath, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 30% less FP. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 104 FP: 2*28 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 53 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
This is the strongest "default" dragon breath attack, though as it only does 10% more damage than Dragonfire, if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation is lower than its Magic Damage Negation that will change. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Skill

Unique Skill: Glintstone Dart

Compared to Skill: Glintstone Pebble, an uncharged Glintstone Dart has 13% higher base damage on the projectile and the charged version has 39% more base damage. This is on top of the Dart having roughly 6% stronger scaling for the bullet.

name: Gloam-Eyed Queen
description: The Gloam-Eyed Queen is a unseen character mentioned in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by the Two Fingers long ago. She had a special eye and an affinity for god-slaying Rune of Death, manipulating its black flames in her palm and into her Godslayer's Greatsword. She embraced the highborn Godskin Nobles, needle-bearing servants of Destined Death, and cradled newborn Godskin Apostles in a swaddling cloth sewn from supple skin. Like their predecessors, the apostles assimilated serpentine physiology in a manner akin to the Crucible, and grew to bring death to the gods. Several Fire Monks abandoned their posts to swear fealty as Blackflame Monks.

The Gloam-Eyed Queen led the Godskin Apostles during a victorious god-hunt, however, she was defeated by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast of Queen Marika. Afterward, Marika removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it away within his Black Blade, creating the Golden Order and suppressing the true power of the Godslayer incantations. The Gloam-Eyed Queen's sword was locked away at the bottom of the Divine Tower of Caelid and her Godskin Swaddling Cloth is in Spiritcaller's Cave on the Mountaintops of the Giants, guarded by a Spiritcaller Snail that summons the spirits of Godskin Apostles.

sections.heading: Followers
sections.body:
The Godskin Apostles were the followers of the Gloam-Eyed Queen:
Blackflame Monk
Blackflame Monk Amon
Blackflame Sorcerer 
Godskin Apostle
Godskin Noble

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen is connected to the Dominula Festival, which involves flaying people to obtain their skins and runes. The blue capes worn by chosen maidens are embroidered with the design that appears on Godskin Noble Robes.
Her fate remains unclear.
She may be connected to Melina, an amnesiatic daughter of Marika with a special sealed eye and an association with Destined Death. Melina's quest to burn the golden Erdtree enables the defeat of Maliketh and upends the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In, this character was referred to as the Dusk-Eyed Queen and the Queen in Black in English and 女骑士 (horsewoman/female knight) in Chinese.
"GloamEyedKnight" and 宵眼の女王の騎士 (Yoime no Joi no Kishi, lit. Gloam Eyed Queen Knight/Horseman) are internal names for the Putrescent Knight, which gained eternal rest by imbibing St. Trina's nectar in the Garden of Deep Purple.

name: God-Devouring Serpent
description: The God-Devouring Serpent, also known as the elder serpent, great serpent, and Serpent King, is an optional Demigod boss in. The God-Devouring Serpent is the first phase of the fight against Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy. Defeating this boss triggers a cutscene that initiates the battle with Rykard. It must be defeated to advance Tanith's questline.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The great serpent is an enormous blue snake with arms and an affinity for both lava sorceries and poison. This boss is weak to the Serpent-Hunter's Great-Serpent Hunt, the true power of which activates during this encounter.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Hated for its tremendous and insatiable gluttony, the elder serpent of Mt. Gelmir is an immortal terror that seeks to one day consume the entire world. It has been repelled by the white light of the Serpent-Hunter since ancient times. A cult on Mt. Gelmir practiced hexes and performed human sacrifices in reverence to a heretical serpent god. Over time, these practices ceased, and their Gelmir Sorcery was lost. 

During the reign of Queen Marika, it was rediscovered by the Demigod Rykard. During the Shattering, Praetor Rykard willingly allowed the great serpent to devour him. Although his Gelmir Knights obtained the legendary Serpent-Hunter weapon, they failed to defeat their former lord. Now, the great serpent and Rykard share a single body as the Lord of Blasphemy, engaging in an appalling birthing ritual that spawned the Man-Serpents. They devour countless champions with the ultimate goal of consuming the gods and the world itself.

sections.heading: Location

name: God Hunt
image: ER Icon Armor Godskin Noble Robe.png
description: The God Hunt was an event mentioned in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Rune of Death, also known as Destined Death, was once part of the Elden Ring until it was removed by Queen Marika to give shape to her Golden Order. 

The Gloam-Eyed Queen was an Empyrean chosen by her own Two Fingers, and individual with the potential to succeed Marika as vessel of the Elden Ring. At some point between the War Against the Giants, after the order Fire Monks was established to watch over the Flame of Ruin and the end of the Age of Plenty, when the Erdtree's blessed sap was still abundant she managed to get her hands on the Rune of Death, wielding it to empower the black flame she channeled from her spiral greatsword

sections.heading: Battles
sections.body:
The Gloam-Eyed Queen raised her Apostles, childrens with serpentine tails that had assimilated inhuman physiology like the Crucible that had created the Erdtree and cradled the newborns in swaddling cloths made of skin. The Queen taught them incantations of the black flame and they used Godslayer's Seals made with obsidian and representing the manipulation of her power.. She raised her children to became the servants of Destined Death and the death of the gods. The Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles thus started their hunts against the gods. Dozens of "gods" would be killed and flayed, and their divine hides were stitched into clothing for their hunters, thus giving them the title of "Godskin" Apostles 

The Godskin Apostles wielded twinblade peelers that featured a sickle on one end and a spike for flesh piercing in the other, requiring high skill while the Godskin Nobles, the most ancient apostles, possessed incredible skill with the stitcher swords and wore aprons with seven faces They also stole a power that once represented the gods' wrath, and wielded it as a trophy in the form of a shockwave manifested from their bellies.

At some point during the conflict, some Fire Monks deserted their eternal duty of guardians of the Forge of the Giants and the Giants' Flame contained therein, their long watch having eroded their resolve as they started to succumb to the allure of the Flame's taboo. The first to abandon his post as guardian was Amon, who swore allegiance to the black flames of the gods' hunts and became the first Blackflame Monk. Many more would become traitors of their order, letting themselves be seduced by the black flames of the Gloam Eyed Queen and its apostles.

The God Hunt ended when the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Apostles were defeated by Marika's shadowbound beast, Maliketh.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.body:
After the defeat of the Gloam Eyed Queen, Marika's only need for her shadow was to serve as a vessel. On her orders, Maliketh sealed away the Rune of Death, binding it within his Black Blade. Marika's offspring thus obtained a form of immortality owing to the removal of their fated deaths from the Elden Ring, however Maliketh continued to instill fear in the demigods thanks to his blade containing the only power that could still kill them.

As a result of the Rune of Death being sealed, the true power of the black flame of the Godskins was also lost but, despite their Queen's defeat, her surviving Apostles and Nobles continued to remain hidden along with some Blackflame Monks. One Apostle and some Monks managed to flee to the fringes and continued to protect the Godslayer's Greatsword of their Queen deep inside the Divine Tower of Caelid. A Noble and an Apostle would die in the Spiritcaller Cave, still holding onto the swaddling cloth of their Queen.

Following the Shattering, many agents of the Gloam-Eyed Queen would reappear in the Lands Between with the apparent goal of continuing to seek the power of Death or to act against the gods. One Noble would try to infiltrate the Divine Tower of Liurnia where the Cursemark of Death left on Ranni's corpse is found. One Apostle would lead the skinning festivities of Dominula, Windmill Village. One Noble and a Blackflame Monk would protect the Temple of Eiglay, seemingly in serving of the God-Devouring Serpent. A Noble and an Apostle would manage to find their way into Crumbling Farum Azula, where Maliketh continued to protect the Rune of Death sealed inside his flesh.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The God Hunts could be the conflict in which the God-Devouring Serpent and serpents in general were branded as "traitors" by the Erdtree, implying a previous alliance.
A Godskin Apostle and Blackflame Monk can be found defending in the Temple of Eiglay where the shed skin of the deity can be found. 
The Godskin Apostles have serpentine tails and share the ability to stretch their torso with Gelmir Man-Serpents, the children of the God-Devouring Serpent. 
The robes of the Godskin Apostles were decorated with obsidian, also inlaid in their Godslayer's Seals, a natural product of volcanos, with Mt. Gelmir thus implied to be the main lair of the Godskin.
The Gelmir Hero's Grave implies a major conflict in the location that involved the forces of the Erdtree.
The Two Fingers may have sanctioned the god hunt.
Like the Godskin's emphasis on skinning their divine victims, flaying was the hallmark of the delightful festival of Dominula, Windmill Village, an old tradition tacitly tolerated by Queen Marika.
The design embroidered on the Blue Festive Garbs' cape used by the maidens selected to play a key role in the festivities of the Dominula Dancers matches the symbol on the Godskin Noble Robe.
One Godskin Apostle is found leading the skinning festivities of Dominula, Windmill Village.

name: Godefroy the Grafted
description: Godefroy the Grafted is an optional mini-boss in found in the Altus Plateau at the Golden Lineage Evergaol.

sections.heading: Lore
sections.body:
A member of the Golden Lineage, he is a descendant of Godfrey, First Elden Lord, and Queen Marika the Eternal. Much like his kinsman Godrick the Grafted, Godefroy has practised the grotesque act of grafting. 

At some point while the alliance of the Shardbearers still ruled over Leyndell, Royal Capital, Godefroy plotted to seize control of the capital. The demigod apparently managed to recruit an army that assumed strong enough for the attack. Godefroy also made use of the special characteristic of his Shaman flesh, grafting into his body parts of corpses in an attempt to gain more strength.

Godefroy would lead his men into what would become known as the First Defense of Leyndell, but ended up fighting around the Second Church of Marika, in the middle of Altus and well distant from even the outer walls of the capital.. The demigod and his soldiers would suffer a complete defeat at the hands of soldiers of Leyndell with their leader captured by Knight Kristoff, a member of the Ancient Dragon Cult of the capital.

Godefroy was imprisoned in the Golden Lineage Evergaol with only his axe in a secluded area close to the Grand Lift of Dectus and guarded by Vulgar Militia men. Though he was defeated, the demigod's attack would precipitate the deterioration of the sovereign alliance between the Shardbearers caused by the traces of the Night of Black Knives still lingering. This would eventually lead to the demigods clashing against each other and the following wars of the Shattering.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Godefroy possessed the Godfrey Icon, a legendary talisman depicting Godfrey and Serosh, the patriarch and guide the Golden Lineage even during his imprisonment.
Godefroy had access to the corpses of Trolls and Banished Knights with the power of the storm to graft to his body.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.body:
Players who encounter Godefroy have most likely already defeated his relative, Godrick the Grafted. The same strategies used to defeat Godrick can be used here, since Godefroy uses the same moveset as Godrick's first phase, but without the second phase.

Be aware that he is considerably tankier, having twice as much HP as Godrick (12.5k vs 6k) and not being able to summon anything or anyone in his arena. He will also deal much more damage, even for his location. 

Upon defeating Godefroy, he drops the Godfrey Icon.
