name: Godfrey, First Elden Lord
description: Hoarah Loux, Warrior, also known as Godfrey, First Elden Lord and the Lord of the Battlefield, is a mandatory boss in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Lord Godfrey was once known as Hoarah Loux, a simple, yet ferocious warrior with a ceaseless lust for battle. He was an unmatched champion who earned his right to Lordship through sheer strength. Later, he took the name Godfrey when he took the spirit of Serosh upon his back. The Lord of Beasts suppressed his rage,allowing him to conduct himself in a manner befitting Marika's first Elden Lord.

Age of the Erdtree:

Before it came to be an embodiment of Order, everything was in opposition to the Erdtree. Godfrey led Marika's golden armies in the War Against the Giants, a decisive conflict thay ended with the Giants' defeat and the confinement of the Fell God's Flame of Ruin. This war heralded the birth of the Erdtree, and the beginning of an age of Order ruled over by Marika and her Elden Lord.

The age of the Erdtree began amidst conflict, and Godfrey was regarded as the "Lord of the Battlefield." He fought the Storm Lord alone and emerged the new lord of Stormveil. Later, during the siege of Castle Morne, Godfrey bested a lone hero who wielded a grafted blade and fought for vengeance. Godfrey was commander of the Crucible Knights, and Ordovis and his men honored their master by wearing the crest of the axe, a symbol of Godfrey's.

Godfrey and his offspring with Queen Marika were the first Demigods, known as the Golden Lineage. His bond with Serosh became an emblem of this lineage, guiding them as they conquered the Lands Between. Godfrey's double-headed axe symbolized his warrior's vow of conduct and would later become a symbol of the Golden Lineage.

The Long March:

At the end of his campaign, Lord Godfrey's golden armies remained unvanquished and unbowed. When his last enemy fell, it was said that the golden hue of Godfrey's eyes faded. He found his Grace lost, tattered, and faded.

Godfrey and his warriors were then informed by Queen Marika that she had divested them of their Grace. She drove them from the Lands Between to wage war in a distant land, where they would live and die. Marika promised Godfrey and his men that after their deaths, they would regain what she had taken from them. They would return to the Lands Between with the strength required to brandish the Elden Ring.

Thus, Godfrey and his kinfolk became the Tarnished. They left the Lands Between together on a pilgrimage known as the Long March, at the end of which Godfrey divested himself of kingship and became a simple warrior once more.

Godfrey became a chieftain of the Badlands under the name of Hoarah Loux. The head of his axe had been broken in a battle fought during the Long March. His loyal warriors honored him by wielding axes of their own, and they became the weapon of choice for Badlands chieftains.

Return to the Lands Between:

At some point, Hoarah Loux died. However, when the Elden Ring was shattered following the death of his son Godwyn the Golden, the Tarnished that died outside the Lands Between were returned to life by the call of their long-lost Grace. The Tarnished, who had grown strong in the face of death, crossed the fog and returned to the Lands Between, to stand before the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. Godfrey was among those who made their way back to the Lands Between. 

The Ashen Capital:

After the Tarnished champion has claimed the Great Runes, burned the Erdtree, and unbound the Rune of Death, they return to the city of Leyndell and approach the Erdtree. At the Elden Throne, they find Godfrey, Serosh on his back, mourning the death of his son Morgott, whom the Tarnished had previously slain. 

Godfrey rises to his feet and addresses the Tarnished. He acknowledges their effort; however, he declares his intention to seek an audience once again. The two Tarnished do battle, and Godfrey finds himself overpowered. The former Elden Lord grabs the head of Serosh, thanks him for his service, and then tears him from his back. Drenched in the blood of his loyal regent, Godfrey resumes the fight, now as the savage Hoarah Loux. Nevertheless, the Tarnished defeats Hoarah Loux, who declares that their strength befits a crown.

sections.heading: Encounters
sections.body:
Leyndell, Royal Capital=

Moveset:

This is a boss fight against a golden, spectral version of Godfrey. He is fought within the Erdtree Sanctuary, accessed by climbing up a large root south of the West Capital Rampart Site of Grace. This battle is not optional as he must be defeated to progress Leyndell further and continue the story. Compared to the later encounter, this version of Godfrey has a greatly reduced moveset, mainly consisting of close-range axe swings. He can create areas of effect by stomping or smashing his axe into the ground, and he may also throw his axe at the player from a distance.

Environment:
Godfrey is fought in a long, fairly spacious room. There is a narrower, lower section to the left of the entrance, as well as various pillars which may restrict movement or allow one to gain distance from the boss.

Leyndell, Ashen Capital=

Nepheli Loux, Warrior and Shabriri are both available as summons for this fight, provided their questlines have been completed. Like the first battle, this fight is not optional and must be defeated to reach the final bosses of the game.

Moveset:

Phase 1 - Godfrey, First Elden Lord:
Godfrey will usually initiate the fight by throwing his axe at the player and then dashing after it. 

Godfrey has a stomp attack similar to that of the Crucible Knights, causing spikes to come out of the ground that are easier to dodge by jumping than to i-frame with a roll. He will generally follow up on the spike stomp with a series of axe swings, but can do a second stomp at any time, even repeatedly.

Godfrey's primary offense will be axe swing combos. They can be dodge rolled safely and involve enough delays for the player to sneak in a hit before having to dodge again.

He retains his moves from the earlier fight, with the addition of more close-range axe attacks and some abilities that generate earthquakes.

Phase 2 - Hoarah Loux, Warrior:

After his health drops below 50%, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Godfrey no longer has Serosh or his axe, and has an almost entirely new, grappling-based fighting style.

Phase 2 always starts with him rushing towards the player with a delayed command grab. He will always briefly go into slow-motion mid-jump, which can roll-catch. He will attempt to grab the player like this multiple times over the course of phase 2. Properly rolling out of the way of it gives you one of the largest time windows to attack him out of his entire phase 2.

He will do many other grab attacks, ground-slams, leap attacks, delayed kicks and delayed stomp attacks. Panic-rolling and blocking is not recommended.

When he begins to crack the ground after a leap attack by smashing his hands into the ground, the player must run away from him as far as they can, otherwise they will get blown up by an explosion that is very difficult to roll through. He often announces this attack by knocking the player away from him with a roar.

Environment:
The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles. It is the same arena where Morgott, the Omen King was fought previously.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Defeating the golden Godfrey, First Elden Lord at Leyndell, Royal Capital for the first time unlocks the "Godfrey, First Elden Lord" achievement.
Defeating Hoarah Loux, Warrior at Leyndell, Ashen Capital for the first time unlocks the "Hoarah Loux, Warrior" achievement.
Godfrey wears the Elden Lord Set (Elden Lord Crown, Elden Lord Armor, Elden Lord Bracers, Elden Lord Greaves).
Godfrey's lordly posture is maintained by Serosh, whose teeth sink into his left shoulder for the fight. These actions help suppress Godfrey's bloodlust.
How Serosh is anchored to Godfrey is similar to how Miquella attaches himself to Promised Consort Radahn. Their entwinement also parallels twin stalks of the Scadutree.
Serosh's crown bears an uncanny resemblance to the Elden Lord crown.
The Axe of Godfrey was unbroken when he gained Serosh and vowed to become a Lord.
The axe wielded by the golden phantom version of Godfrey is unbroken and features twin blades, suggesting it represents Godfrey before the Long March.
Statues of Godfrey with Serosh and an undamaged axe are found at the Roundtable Hold and in the Stormveil Castle throne room.
There is a portrait of Godfrey with a broken axe in Stormveil Castle's main hall, which is guarded by a Grafted Scion. This was likely painted after Godfrey returned to the Lands Between.
The Axe of Godfrey strongly resembles the Beastman's Cleavers made by Azula Beastmen.
Hoarah Loux, Warrior is a highlander.
Highlanders are mighty warriors capable of subduing beasts with sheer strength. While most wore blue, only the greatest bear hunters were permitted to wear red. Lord Godfrey is draped in blue, while Hoarah Loux is soaked in red beast blood.
The Highland Axe is found directly beneath a large portrait of Godfrey in the main hall of Stormveil. Godfrey’s kinfolk wielded these axes during the Long March.
Both Hoarah Loux and the highlanders begin battle by shouting their names.
Hoarah Loux roars like a Runebear and Ash of War: Hoarah Loux's Earthshaker is used by Great Red Bears.
Just as Godfrey discards the golden lion to become Hoarah Loux, a nameless Redmane forsook the red lion to become Red Bear. Both cover themselves in red after besting savage beasts with their bare hands.
The Brave's Battlewear, once the traditional garb of Godfrey's kin, was later repurposed into the Gloried Attire.
Nepheli Loux, Warrior shares the surname "Loux" with Hoarah Loux, implying a familial or clan relationship.
If her questline is completed in her favor, Nepheli may be summoned as a cooperator against Godfrey and Serosh.
Although her exact relation is unclear, her age and warrior culture likely make her Godfrey's daughter or a close descendant born after he reverted to Hoarah Loux. Her relationship with Sir Gideon Ofnir may indicate that Godfrey was recalled to the Lands Between when she was young.
Godfrey became the lord of Stormveil Castle after defeating the Storm Lord in single combat, establishing the Golden Lineage as the rightful rulers of Limgrave. After the Stormhawk King bonds with Nepheli, Kenneth Haight recognizes her as part of Hoarah Loux’s bloodline, and declares Nepheli the rightful heir to Limgrave.
Nepheli Loux claims she swore an oath when she became a warrior. Godfrey also made a vow upon becoming Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Godfrey has a wide range of dialogue lines that cut from the game. At one point, he would have directed the player to cross the Sea of Fog to reclaim the Elden Ring.
Godfrey had a few differences in.
He had two health bars.
He delivered an extra line upon defeating the player in phase one: "Tarnished Warrior. 'Twas nobly fought. Thy rest is well deserved."
Upon death, Hoarah Loux laughed heartily after saying, "Brave Tarnished. Thy strength befits a crown."
Much of Godfrey's character shares ties with the mythical Greek hero, Heracles. Godfrey possesses earthshattering strength, endured harsh trials to earn his godhood, slew the mightiest of the Giants, has a connection with lions through Serosh, and he even enters a berserker state.
There are also parallels between Godfrey and Arthur, the legendary King of Britain, with both being great warriors once presiding over a lost golden age, and with Arthur himself being away - but prophesied to one day return, reclaim his rule and save his people. Other parallels include the round table seen at the Roundtable Hold, and his chief Crucible Knights, Ordovis and Siluria, being named for ancient Celtic tribes in Pre-Roman Britain.

name: Godrick the Grafted
description: is a Boss. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer encountered in Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Godrick is a descendant of the Golden Lineage, the bloodline that began with Queen Marika the Eternal and her first consort Godfrey. Only a distant relation of Marika's line, his divine blood was sorely diluted, and he was viewed as the runt of the litter. Godrick idolized the first Elden Lord, desiring his ancestor to witness his feats. He wielded an axe emblazoned with a lion, a symbol of Godfrey, and furnished his army with the Erdtree and Serosh emblems of the Golden Lineage. Though he styled himself “lord of all that is golden,” he commanded far less respect than his forebear and was despised by many of his own servants.

After the Elden Ring was shattered, Godrick inherited the Great Rune from the center of the Elden Ring, referred to as the anchor ring. During The Shattering, he was hounded from Leyndell, Royal Capital. He claimed a multitude of treasures, including the Mimic's Veil, and hid among the womenfolk to flee the city. Godrick made his way south, settling in Limgrave with an army of soldiers who had fled Leyndell. He took up residence in Stormveil Castle, using it as a refuge to hide from General Radahn. When Malenia marched southward, Godrick insulted her, leading to a confrontation that left him beaten and humiliated, forced to beg for mercy.

Godrick again retreated to Stormveil Castle to practice grafting, the forbidden art of attaching the parts of other beings to oneself to gain power. When the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between, Godrick sent his soldiers on Tarnished hunts, seeking new subjects to graft. He also produced Grafted Scions; abhorrent beings comprised of many different limbs, seemingly grafted onto children.

Game events:
The Tarnished journeys to Stormveil Castle in search of Godrick's Great Rune, on the advice of White Mask Varré and Melina. The castle shows many examples of his grafting: severed limbs hanging in the dining hall, a dismembered Troll over a courtyard, and piles of corpses, including the companions of Roderika. Eventually the Tarnished finds Godrick in a graveyard, addressing a dead dragon impaled on a statue. He grafts the dragon's head to his own arm mid-fight, but is defeated, and his Great Rune is claimed.

Later, Nepheli Loux can become the lord of Limgrave at the appointment of Kenneth Haight.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Overview:
HP: 6,080
Defense: 105 (increased during Phase 2)
Stance: 105
Cannot be Parried
Vulnerable to a Critical Attack after his Stance is broken
Deals Standard and Strike damage during Phase 1; Phase 2 adds Fire damage via the Grafted Dragon.

Nepheli Loux, Warrior may be summoned if spoken to in Stormveil; her Summon Sign is outside the arena.

Resistances:

Moveset:

Phase 1:
The fight begins after a cutscene. Godrick primarily uses his axe and enlarged left arm, generating cyclones and quakes for area-of-effect damage. He rolls to reposition and uses a homing wind projectile.

Phase 2:
At roughly 60% HP, a cutscene plays, and he grafts the dragon's head to his arm. He gains ranged and area fire attacks layered onto his Phase 1 kit.

Environment:
The arena is a narrow, paved approach flanked by graveyards, with a wider entrance near the steps. Movement through gravestones is possible, but it can hinder dodging.

name: Gods
description: Gods are among the most powerful characters in the world of.

sections.heading: List of gods
sections.body:
Queen Marika the Eternal:

Queen Marika the Eternal is the divine sovereign of the Lands Between. She was a Numen woman hailing from a Shaman Village in the Hinterland. As an Empyrean, Marika traveled to the Gate of Divinity atop Enir-Ilim where she ascended to godhood and became the vessel of the Elden Ring. Marika is further known as the mother or step-mother of the demigods, grower of the Erdtree, founder of the Golden Order, slayer of the Fell God as well as the spouse of the Elden Lords Godfrey and Radagon. Although she vanished after the Shattering, Marika influences the Tarnished and her chosen through the golden Guidance of Grace.

Miquella the Kind:

After Godfrey was Tarnished, the demigod Miquella the Kind was born to Queen Marika and Lord Radagon. Despite his eternal youth, he was selected as an Empyrean like his twin sister, Malenia. He was the master inventer of Unalloyed Gold, the grower of the sacred Haligtree, and a coercive charmer. After divesting himself of his flesh, his eye, his fears, his vacillation, and St. Trina—his love and fate—Miquella, like Marika, ascended to godhood at the Gate of Divinity. He used the body of Mohg to resurrect his promised consort, Radahn, in a failed attempt to succeed his mother as sovereign and usher in an Age of Compassion.

Malenia, Goddess of Rot:

Malenia, the undefeated Blade and twin sister of Miquella the Kind, was born afflicted with baleful Scarlet Rot. However, she managed to suppress it with the help of the Blind Swordsman and Miquella's Unalloyed Gold Needle. During her legendary duel with Radahn at the end of the Shattering, she reluctantly unleashed the Scarlet Aeonia. Following this bloom, the Swamp of Aeonia manifested in Caelid, producing the Kindred of Rot. If the Empyrean Malenia is confronted and defeated at the Haligtree, she will blossom for a second time. Her third and final bloom is prophesied to complete her transformation into a true Goddess of Rot. Unlike her twin, Malenia has no interest in establishing her own Order.

Fell God:

The red-haired, one-eyed Fell God of fire is an ancient deity worshipped by the Fire Giants. It is regarded as an malevolent entity that opposes and threatens the Erdtree and the Golden Order. Queen Marika allegedly slew the Fell God during the War Against the Giants, and cursed the last survivor of their race to eternally tend the Flame.. However, the Fell God's still lingers within the giants.

Ancient Dragon God:
Dragonlord Placidusax waited for his fled god to return.

Old Gods:

The old gods ((古い神々, Furui Kamigami) were colossal giants who wielded ancient meteoric ore that contained explosive white light. An excavated shard of one of their arrowheads was the treasure of a ruined forge that came after them.

Radiant Gods:
 Fulghor, Champion of Nightglow worshipped radiant gods (光を放つ神々, Hikariohanatsu Kamigami, lit. Light-Emitting Gods) cloaked in the roar of thunder. It is possible that they are one and the same with the Old Gods, as both are referred to as kamigami in the Japanese script, both produce light (their radiance is written with the same kanji as the Old Gods white light, 光), and the legends of them concealing themselves in thunder are reminscent of the thunderstone folklore which provided the real-world inspiration for the Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword.

Serpent-God:

The ancient inhabitants of Mt. Gelmir made sacrifices in the name of a Serpent-God. It is likely connected to one of the god-like snakes, such as the Abyssal Serpent and God-Devouring Serpent.

sections.heading: Divine entities
sections.body:
Demigods: 

Demigods are powerful beings with the divine blood or power but without possessing true godhood. In the Lands Between most demigods are children or step-children of Queen Marika and the Elden Lords. After Marika shattered the Elden Ring, many demigods acquired Great Runes and became Shardbearers. The Tarnished are guided by Grace to challenge the demigods and claim their Great Runes.

Empyreans:

Empyreans are beings capable of becoming gods. During the Age of the Erdtree, Empyreans were chosen by the Two Fingers. Examples of Empyreans are Marika, Miquella, Ranni, Malenia and the Gloam-Eyed Queen.

Greater Will:

The Greater Will is a mysterious entity or force known for fracturing the One Great, thus creating life and souls in the Lands Between. It once sent the Elden Beast to the Lands Between, which would eventually become the Elden Ring itself. The Greater Will also had other vassals like Metyr and her children, the Two Fingers, who selected Empyreans to become gods. The Greater Will is speculated to have imprisoned Queen Marika after she shattered the Elden Ring. Due to the Greater Will's power to rupture the One Great, create and imprison gods, it can effectively be seen as the supreme being of the Elden Ring universe.

Outer Gods:

Outer Gods are extremely powerful entities that exist outside of the Lands Between, the current Order of the Elden Ring or on an higher plane. Examples of outer gods are the Formless Mother, the God of Rot, the Twinbird's God, and the Frenzied Flame.

Tutelary Deities:

A tutelary deity is a god or spirit regarded as the guardian, patron, or protector of a specific location, natural feature, individual, lineage, nation, cultural group, or profession. The term "tutelary" derives from roots associated with safety and thus of guardianship.

Hornsent aspired to ascend as tutelary deities by engaging in severe ascetic training. Some became Curseblades or Divine Beast Warriors. Withered corpses of successful tutelary deities, enshrined across the Realm of Shadow, quietly gather Revered Spirit Ash in their palms.

sections.heading: Potential Gods
sections.body:
Ancient Dynasty:

A nameless bearded man with a bald head and one eye may have been the god of the Ancient Dynasty, which existed long before the age of the Erdtree. Once served by the claymen in Underground Ruins, he is now revered at the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum and Grand Cloister.

Nox Gods:

The Nox once revered mummified giants seated upon Chair-Crypt thrones, often honored them with Great Ghost Glovewort and other treasures.

Rauh:

The Ancient Ruins of Rauh feature large statues of a woman wearing an octagonal hat. She is associated with the Verdigris Discus and Bondstone. Both the hornsent and Kindred of Rot offer their prayers to the "Rauh goddess" figure. The Golden Crucible originated in Rauh.

name: Godskin Duo
description: Godskin Duo is a boss battle where you have to battle against a Godskin Apostle and Godskin Noble at the same time. They can be found in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is not an optional boss as they must be defeated to advance further in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
The Godskin Duo share one health bar of around 24000 HP (NG), but also still have their own HP. If one is killed, it will either respawn automatically after ~15 seconds or the other Godskin will reanimate them. They will also still enter phase 2 if dropping close to 50% in individual HP.

The pillars within the arena are an effective way to separate them, although their phase 2 attacks will demolish the upper portion of them. In addition, both of them can be parried. 

Sleep Pots can serve as a way to buy time as both bosses can be rendered temporarily paralyzed by sleep status.

name: Godwyn the Golden
description: Godwyn the Golden, also known as the Prince of Death, and First of the Dead, is a character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Godwyn was born during the Age of the Erdtree to Queen Marika the Eternal and her first consort, Godfrey, making him a scion of the Golden Lineage. He emerged as a hero of the Erdtree after the end of Age of Plenty when the Ancient Dragon Gransax breached the walls of Leyndell, triggering the War of the Ancient Dragons. Godwyn played a pivotal role during the final battle with Fortissax outside Leyndell. He prevailed, but spared the dread dragon, forging a friendship that ended the war and founded the Ancient Dragon Cult.

The dragon cult worshiped the ancient dragons and studied their lightning incantations. These practices were sanctioned by the Golden Order, as lightning and Gravel Stones were imbued with gold. Godwyn learned to channel Fortissax's power to summon a storm of golden lightning. His inner circle of elite ancient dragon knights formed his personal guard, who received the largest amber medallions ever bestowed.

Death:

Godwyn was the first Demigod to die, in recorded history, on the Night of Black Knives. His stepsister, Lunar Princess Ranni, orchestrated the plot by stealing a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh and imbued godslaying daggers with Destined Death. The Black Knife Assassins infiltrated the royal capital and struck Godwyn, carving the half-wheel centipede into his flesh while a matching mark was etched into Ranni. The ritual caused both to suffer an incomplete death: Ranni's soul endured while her flesh destroyed; Godwyn's body remained, but his soul was gone.

Prince of Death:

The soulless body of Godwyn the Golden was buried below Leyndell at the base of the Erdtree's roots, located in the Deeproot Depths. However, his spirit could not return to the Erdtree because he did not experience a true death. Godwyn's soulless body then grew and transformed into an unrecognizable, piscine aberration known as the Prince of Death. Ancient Dragon Fortissax entered Godwyn's Deathbed Dream to fight against the Death within him, but was ultimately corrupted by the Death Blight.

Through Godwyn, the Rune of Death seeped into the Greattree roots and spread throughout the Lands Between. Soon after, the Death-Prince's distorted visage manifested itself across the realm. His eyes peered out of tendrils and vines, and even his distorted face materialized in places of Erdtree burial. This corruption sprouted Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death. Later, the roots of the Erdtree were disconnected from those below.

Wandering Mausoleums prowled the lands to recall the spirits of the soulless Demigod. Many lordsworn warriors protected these great Spirit Calling Bells, and willingly beheaded themselves in a Death rite to guard them eternally as Mausoleum Knights. Though the earth shook when the Mausoleums tolled, the spirit of Godwyn never returned. In contrast, Godwyn's innermost circle embraced his death and became the Death Knights, who quested for a cadaver surrogate to bring about the Age of the Duskborn.

Godwyn's downfall catalyzed the shattering of the Elden Ring and the subsequent Shattering War of the Demigods. Later, the knights of Castle Sol and Miquella worked toward achieving an eclipse they believed would restore Godwyn's soul to his body. Despite their efforts, the failure of the plan contributed to the doom of the Haligtree.

Game events:
Fia, Deathbed Companion was the guardian of Those Who Live in Death. After recovering the half-wheel centipede taken from Godwyn's body, she makes her way to the Prince of Death's Throne. If Fia acquires the cursemark from Ranni's body, she sleeps with Godwyn to transfer to him the strength of countless heroes and grant him a second life as the Prince of Death. As a result of their union, Fia conceived the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince. She requests it be used to mend the shattered Elden Ring and usher in an Age of the Duskborn, introducing the principle of Life within Death into the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
Godwyn's main body rests at the Prince of Death's Throne, located in a shallow pool of purple water at the base of a tainted root in the Deeproot Depths.
Godwyn's cadaver surrogates are found at Fog Rift Catacombs, Scorpion River Catacombs, and Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Although the Prince of Death is the source of the Death Blight, the Prince of Death's Throne is harmless to the player.
Like his mother Marika, Godwyn is strung up and called a martyr.
Godwyn was protected by a personal entourage in addition to the royal palace guard.
After his death, Godwyn's closest allies did not agree on which Godwyn to aid. The golden knights served the Prince of Death, but Fortissax fought to stop it.
Godwyn's cadaver surrogates are thought to be his larger manifestations found at Fog Rift Catacombs, Scorpion River Catacombs, and Stormveil Castle.
His eyes appear upon objects in areas touched by Deathroot, such as Summonwater Village, Tombsward Catacombs, and Wyndham Ruins.
Corpses clump together to form certain Prince of Death objects. Similar to the gravestone accretions, and they are likely a form of Regression.
The Prince of Death's Pustule and Prince of Death's Cyst depict the duplication of his facial features.
His cystic visage grows on the backs of Crabs and Giant Crabs living in tainted waters.
If Lichdragon Fortissax is defeated in the Deathbed Dream, Fia is free to transfer the spiritual warmth and vigor of her champions into the Prince of Death. This process produces the Mending Rune of the Death-Prince.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: His grotesque, semi-circular face is reminiscent of polypore fungi—also known as bracket or shelf fungi—that grow on dead and dying trees.

name: Golden Epitaph
description: Golden Epitaph is a straight sword and melee armament in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found at the entrance of Auriza Hero's Grave. Requires a Stonesword Key to access and is guarded by a Basilisk.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The skill, Last Rites, functions as an Aura Buff and adds 25 Holy damage and a universal 10% (5% for PvP) damage bonus, as well as a 100% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death. While being an Aura Buff does mean it will stack with a lot of other buffs, it also places it in competition with Golden Vow (especially the spell version), which also adds a strong boost to damage negation on top of its damage boost, and the Golden Epitaph being Faith-leaning means meetings its requirements are easy. 
However, Last Rites is generally quicker to use and doesn't require a Sacred Seal to use, making it possibly more convenient in combat.
Since the flat damage bonus is applied to all attacks used by the player, this means it's also applied to effects that tick repeatedly or hit several times, such as Volcano Pots and Bestial Sling.
This weapon has an innate 30% damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death (Skeletons, Deathbirds and such), on top of dealing the Holy damage that they are usually vulnerable to.
Has the most Attack Power (AP) on a hybrid Strength/Faith build or a hybrid Dexterity/Faith build, with a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build being a bit weaker, and a pure Faith build being weaker still. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength or 45 Dexterity and 45 Faith grants 602 AP, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 591 AP, and 80 Faith grants 581 AP.
The hybrid Strength/Dexterity build has the advantage of not competing with the spell version of Golden Vow and, with 2 more points in Faith, serves as a good offhand weapon to the Miquellan Knight's Sword (though that weapon is acquired much, much later than the Epitaph).

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
An epitaph is "a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone" (Cambridge Dictionary), which in this case would be the phrase "O brother, lord brother, please die a true death." in the description. 
This weapons resembles the Rune Sword from Demon's Souls.
Patch 1.12 fixed a bug that caused damage to the player and friendly summons when using the "Last Rites" Skill under specific circumstances.
Prior to the fix, Last Rites would be applied to non-damaging, persistent effects such as Terra Magica, making them deal the flat 25 Holy damage to any friendly players standing on it.
Patch 1.07 increased effect duration, increased attack power, effect against Those Who Live in Death has been revised upward. 
The skill's duration was increased from 45 seconds to 60 seconds, the universal 10% damage buff was added (limited to 5% in PvP), and the damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death was increased from 50% to 100%.
Patch 1.04 increased cast speed.
For the skill, that is.

image: ER Icon Spell Golden Lightning Fortification.png
description: Golden Lightning Fortification is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed Drop: Crumbling Farum Azula
Drops from a Scarab south of the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, near an Ancient Dragon.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Grants a Body Buff that decreases Lightning damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for caster and allies within a 6 meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. 
Overall a very strong defensive incantation, and one that comes just before the final Lightning-heavy area in the game, Crumbling Farum Azula, and the Dragonlord, one of the more Lightning-focused bosses in the game. 
Since it doesn't actually apply a flat increase to damage negation, just the damage taken, the actual effective new damage negation (the one shown on the character screen) can be calculated with the following formula: 1 - (1 - (current Lightning damage negation)/100) * (1 - 0.60). 
As an example, if Lightning damage negation before casting the incantation is 25.000 the result becomes this: 1 - (1 - 25.000/100) * (1 - 0.60) = 0.7, or 70.0% Lightning damage negation. 
Against other players, simply replace the 0.60 with 0.20 for a new end result of 40.0% Lightning damage negation. 
Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher Lightning damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell the less effective it may appear to be in the statistics.

description: The Golden Order Greatsword is a Greatsword, a melee armament. It is one of the Legendary Armaments.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Received upon defeating the Misbegotten Crusader in Cave of the Forlorn, located in the Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While a pure Faith build would be expected to be strongest investment in terms of pure Attack Rating (AR) for this weapon, after Faith reaches 50 Dexterity will grant roughly equal AR until it also reaches 50. The first option will grant stronger casting, more damage from the skill and potentially also higher melee damage if an enemy has lower or equal Holy defence to its Physical defence. The second option grants slightly quicker casting and potentially slightly better damage if an enemy has higher Holy defence than Physical defence. 

This is one of the few weapons that deal 20% bonus damage to Undead enemies such as Skeletons and Death Rite Birds and will also prevent the former from resurrecting without needing an extra hit to finish them off.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Despite its description saying it is made of pure light it is actually of average weight among the Greatswords and is not one of the game's two weightless weapons, the Coded Sword and the Cipher Pata.
The Chinese and Korean release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "A greatsword guided by the one and only Rune of Life. The overflowing golden light became a blade without substance. The embodiment of the power of the Erdtree itself." The role of Carian matrimonial sword was instead filled by the Sword of Night and Flame.

name: Golden Order Seal
image: ER Icon weapon Golden Order Seal.png
description: The Golden Order Seal is a Sacred Seal and catalyst in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found inside the Minor Erdtree Church, located between the two ramparts of Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Enhances Golden Order Fundamentalist incantations by 10%.
Scales equally well with Intelligence and Faith for the purpose of casting Incantations, and boosts the effect of directly damaging Golden Order Incantations if held in an active hand (does not need to be used for casting the spell).

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.body: Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Only the Faith portion of its scaling applies to Healing and Weapon Buff incantations, most notably making it rather unsuitable for casting Order's Blade.
The strongest faith scaling of the hybrid seals at 159%, though that is barely over half of the faith only seals (averaging 250%). 
Incantations boosted by 10% when this seal is held in an active hand (not necessarily cast through) is Discus of Light, Triple Rings of Light, and Radagon's Rings of Light. Most notably, Law of Causality and Order's Blade is not boosted. 
Like most of the weightless seals, it lacks a Strength scaling for its Physical damage. 
Scales best with an equal split of Intelligence and Faith. 
A 17/17 split (minimum requirements) gives 150 Incantation Scaling. 
A 45/17 or 17/45 split (reaching one middle softcap) gives 244 Incantation Scaling. 
A 80/17 or 17/80 split (reaching one of the highest softcaps) gives 270 Incantation Scaling. 
A 45/45 split (reaching both middle softcaps) gives 338 Incantation Scaling, comparable to an Erdtree Seal gaining 353 Incantation Scaling at 80 Faith. 
For casting Incantations with a faith requirement below 17, the Frenzied Flame Seal is potentially better due to much lower Attribute requirements (none at all) but is attainable only later, and requires completing Lightseeker Hyetta's questline and at least partially committing to her Ending.

name: Golden Vow
description: Golden Vow is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree Worship Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Mt. Gelmir
Located inside the Corpse-Stench Shack east of the broken stone bridge on the Road of Iniquity. Anastasia, Tarnished-Eater will also invade at this same spot.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Grants an Aura Buff to the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius that increases all damage dealt by 15% (7.5% in PvP) and decreases all damage taken by 10% (5% in PvP) for 80 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 50 points of Stamina to cast.
Can be held indefinitely if the caster wants to wait for their allies to step into range of the buff.
Generally considered the strongest of all Aura Buffs due to having the second strongest universal attack and defense bonuses (highest against other players) after the unique skill Rallying Standard while also having the longest.
The only real disadvantage is that the cost is relatively high (though low for the very good duration) and the moderate Faith requirement.
The Rallying Standard skill does have the advantage of higher bonuses (though not in PvP), while the Shared Order skill at the cost of having no defense bonus, a lower attack bonus, and a slightly shorter duration of 60 seconds has no requirement beyond being able to wield an infusible weapon such as the Dagger and a lower FP cost of 20.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
While most things in-game only gained different values against other players after Patch 1.07, this incantation seems to have gained its PvP values with or prior to Patch 1.03.
Patch 1.09.1 fixed a bug where the effects of some Skills, Incantations, Items, and Weapons that increased attack power were not applied to Spells and Incantations.
After this patch, the effect of Golden Vow applied to Spells again.
Patch 1.09 fixed a bug that reduced the power of some skills while under the Golden Vow effect.
This update also introduced a bug where Golden Vow's effect was not applied to Spells.
The bug that was fixed appears to be the same one as the one that was fixed with Patch 1.05, below, which was apparently reintroduced with Patch 1.07.
Patch 1.05 fixed a bug that caused the attack power of some skills to be reduced when using the "Golden Vow" skill.
The bug would cause some skills, such as Storm Blade, to deal no damage, while others, like Waterfowl Dance, would deal heavily reduced damage.
This bug appears to have been introduced with one of the 4 updates from Patch 1.03 to Patch 1.03.3.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Basic Info:
Goldmask cannot be made hostile, and will disappear if attacked, giving no Runes or item drops. He will reappear in his last location after resting at a Site of Grace.

Equipment:

Quest Items:

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Altus Plateau (Forest-Spanning Greatbridge)
Goldmask can be found at the end of the broken bridge, facing the Erdtree. Interact with him to progress.
Altus Plateau (near Altus Highway Junction) 
Speak to Corhyn to reveal Goldmask's location.
Altus Plateau (Forest-Spanning Greatbridge) 
Return to the bridge and exhaust Corhyn's dialogue.
Leyndell, Royal Capital
Goldmask and Corhyn can be found near the colosseum. Corhyn will express frustration at Goldmask's current obsession with Radagon.
After using Law of Regression in front of the Radagon statue past the lift near Erdtree Sanctuary, talk to Goldmask to reveal Radagon's secret and then talk to Corhyn.
Mountaintops of the Giants
Goldmask and Corhyn will move to the bridge south of Stargazer's Ruins.
Leyndell, Ashen Capital
After defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, Goldmask's corpse can be found on a slope near the colosseum. Loot his corpse to receive the Mending Rune of Perfect Order, which will unlock the option to complete the Age of Order ending.
After reloading the area, return to Goldmask's corpse to retrieve Goldmask's Rags, Gold Bracelets, and Gold Waistwrap.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Goldmask is among the Tarnished listed in the game's intro. He is depicted splayed on the ground across a carving of the Erdtree Incantation sigil, alongside a book and a container leaking a golden fluid. Grace can be seen gleaming in front of him.

name: Grafted Blade Greatsword
image: ER Icon weapon Grafted Blade Greatsword.png
description: The Grafted Blade Greatsword is a Legendary melee armament found in.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
The Attribute boosts from this weapon's unique skill, Oath of Vengeance, is especially useful early on, as it will boost your durability by increasing your Defense and HP, and also increase your Equip Load by roughly 8.0 (about 5.6 if accounting for the 70% threshold for Medium Load) letting you carry it easier. 
Do keep in mind that while the bonuses to Strength and Dexterity can increase the damage dealt by this weapon's attacks it cannot be used to meet the Attribute requirements as the skill itself is not usable without meeting those requirements.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Location: Castle Morne
The Grafted Blade Greatsword is obtained upon defeating the Leonine Misbegotten at the Morne Moangrave behind Castle Morne at the southern tip of the Weeping Peninsula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This weapon does not accept weapon buffs. 
The Grafted Blade Greatsword is one of the nine Legendary Armaments.
This is the renowned sword of Castle Morne mentioned by Castellan Edgar. He stresses that this sword must not fall into the hands of the Misbegotten.
The fighting lion motif associated with the Golden Lineage appears on the guard, though this detail is difficult to see in-game.
While the Dexterity scaling is a good bit stronger than expected it will only exceed the benefits of the Strength scaling when the final softcap of 80 (54 if using both hands) Strength is reached.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This weapon received several buffs in patch 1.04. Its base damage (+0) was increased from 157 to 162 and its guard rating increaed from 64/48/48/48/48/43 to 80/48/48/48/48/53. 
This is one of the earliest available Colossal Swords or Weapons and most likely the second acquired after the Zweihander, also found on the Weeping Peninsula. 
The Chinese and Korean release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "A special greatsword created by joining together the swords of warriors who once served Godfrey. It is imbued with the power of the Rune of Grafting."

name: Grafted Scion
description: The Grafted Scion is an Enemy and a Boss.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: Grafted Scions are grotesque, spider-like creatures with youthful faces, silver hair, and a wide array of grafted limbs. They are clad in green cloaks and wield Ornamental Straight Swords and Golden Beast Crest Shields—armaments symbolic of the Golden Lineage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The scions were the dregs of the Golden Lineage, their power amplified by Godrick's loathsome grafting technique. Many Tarnished were sacrificed to create Grafted Scions, including the vassals who accompanied Roderika.

A Grafted Scion encountered outside the Chapel of Anticipation. This is the first boss encountered in the game, however killing it is not mandatory. If the Grafted Scion is not defeated during the first encounter, it is possible to return to defeat it by returning to the Chapel of Anticipation via one of the sending gates at the Four Belfries, at the cost of one Imbued Sword Key.

name: Grandmother
description: The Grandmother (大母, Taibo) was an unseen character in.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While her Japanese name, 大母, is rarely used to refer to the mother of ones parents, it can be more literally read as "Great Mother;" the same term is used to refer to Greyoll. 
Her features strongly resemble those of the tortured Jar Dwellers found in Bonny Gaol and elsewhere.
The headless statue found outside Bonny Village resembles the Grandmother.
The Grandmother may have embedded herself into the tree to water it with her blood in the way Miquella did his Haligtree.
The Grandmother may have been a Numen.
Fractured Marika is found in a statuesque form at the Stone Platform within the Erdtree.
Her eyes are obscured, which implies blindness.
One of her eyes is open while the other is closed, though this cannot be seen under normal gameplay.

description: Gravel Stone Seal is a Sacred Seal in. It is a catalyst for casting Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Dropped by a specific spear-wielding Leyndell Knight, found just to the left when standing outside of the front gate to the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Boosts Dragon Cult Incantations by 15%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Consistently only a few points behind the currently strongest pure Faith Sacred Seal until the low 70's, where the Erdtree Seal begins to greatly out-scale all other Seals. 
If only one Seal is wielded, this Seal is always the strongest one for the purpose of casting damage-dealing Dragon Cult Incantations due to its damage boost. 
Holding a Gravel Stone Seal in one of your active hands will boost the damage of directly damaging Dragon Cult Incantations by 15%. 
Holding a GSS in each active hand (that is, two Seals that are each held in separate hands) will increase the damage boost to 32.25% (1.15*1.15=1.3225). 
Note that Electrify Armament is not among the spells boosted, as it is not directly damaging and only cares about the caster's Faith and the used Sacred Seal's Faith scaling.

Tragoth is reminiscent of Havel the Rock, a recurring character in the Dark Souls series:

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Starting equipment for the Bandit class.
2% drop chance from Small Demi-Humans.
The earliest farming spot is just inside Lakeside Crystal Cave, where once can be found hiding inside of a bush next to another, regular Demi-Human.
The most efficient farming spot is just north of the Craftsman's Shack Site of Grace on Mt. Gelmir, where four of them are hiding amongst a flock of Sheep.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Leans more towards the various Dexterity- and Arcane-scaling affinities. 
Pairs well with the similarly Dex/Arc-leaning Reduvia as an off-hand weapon for dual wielding. 
Pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
Its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen). 
The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult). 
While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage. 
Curiously, the Strength-scaling of the Keen affinity is actually stronger than that of the Standard affinity, despite the Keen affinity usually greatly decreasing the Strength-scaling of the weapon.
On the shorter side of daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Carnivorous feral beasts touched by the Crucible's influence, the Great Red Bears naturally sprouted horns suffused with spirituality. These red-haired Runebears prowled the Land of Shadow and took special pleasure in hunting and devouring other horned creatures.

They often clashed with local Highlanders, whose warriors also sought glory by subduing savage beasts and proving their own strength in battle. The fiercest Highlanders fixated on the bears' primal power, believing that hard-earned victory against such dangerous creatures revealed an inner, self-made divinity. A former Redmane warrior who slew a Great Red Bear in a blood-soaked duel became consumed by its unadorned power, wielding its claw without alteration and abandoning all desire except to be a Red Bear himself.

name: Great Runes
description: The are Key Items in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Great Runes are the shards of the Elden Ring, currently making up the Golden Order, and represent the concepts of order and discipline that the demigods enforced on the physical world. They were inherited by some of the demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal following the shattering of the Elden Ring. The mad taint of the newfound strength granted by the Great Runes precipitated the Shattering, wherein the demigods fought for control of the Lands Between. The demigods who inherited Great Runes were known as Shardbearers.

The Tarnished, upon returning to the Lands Between, were compelled by the Two Fingers to seek out demigods to relieve them of their Great Runes in order to become Elden Lord. The Tarnished required one Great Rune to be granted audience with the Two Fingers in the inner chamber of the Roundtable Hold. They also required enough Great Runes to repair the Elden Ring before the Two Fingers would permit them to enter Leyndell, Royal Capital to have an audience with Queen Marika to become Elden Lord. During the course of the game, this is two Great Runes, however since the Shardbearer Morgott, the Omen King guards the entrance to the Erdtree and must be killed to access it, they will have at least three when granted audience. Finger Reader Enia has only ever seen two Great Runes together once before this.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
When initially obtained by the player, a Great Rune (except the Great Rune of the Unborn) would be devoid of any benediction, and had to be taken to the Divine Tower mentioned in its description, whereupon it would be restored by interacting with the image of the Great Rune above the inert Two Fingers at the summit of the tower. Further, a Rune Arc was required for The Tarnished (Protagonist) to be granted the blessing of a Great Rune after restoring it. 

The Great Runes acquired by The Tarnished were used to repair the Elden Ring in at least one ending.

It is unknown if the Rune of Death is considered a Great Rune or an Elden Rune.

The Great Runes reflect the demigods that inherited them. For example, Morgott's Great Rune was proof that he was born of the Golden Lineage, and the rightful Lord of Leyndell. Mohg, Lord of Blood's Great Rune was soaked with accursed blood from his devout love for the wretched mire he was born into. Morgott's and Mohg's Great Runes were naturally similar due to their bearers being twins. Malenia, Blade of Miquella's Great Rune was half-rotted but infused with Malenia's spirit of resistance.

Miquella of the Haligtree and Ranni the Witch are the only Shardbearers known to have discarded their Great Runes. The whereabouts of Ranni's Great Rune remain unknown. Miquella relinquishes and breaks his Great Rune after the Tarnished crosses into one of three areas of the Land of Shadow: the eastern half of Scadu Altus, the Rauh Base region, or Shadow Keep.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
"Great Rune" (GR) was the developmental codename for Elden Ring.
Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice contained Project "GR" assets.
Proper names for various Great Runes were cut before release.
Rune of Life - In the Chinese and Korean 1.0 text Helphen's Steeple, the Golden Order Greatsword, and Icon Shield make reference to the Rune of Life, which provides the Erdtree's power and places a curse upon heroes of the Lands Between. It is presumably Marika's own Great Rune.
Rune of Abundance — The cut Abundance Twinblade and Abundance and Decay Twinblade, weapons make reference to "the Rune of Abundance" and the "the Rune of Decay" in their descriptions belonging to Miquella and Malenia respectively.
Rune of Decay 
Rune of Grafting — In the Chinese 1.0 text, the Grafted Blade Greatsword refers to "the Rune of Grafting" (“接肢”的卢恩, “Jiē Zhī” de Lú'ēn), presumably Godrick's Great Rune.
Rune of Mind — In the Korean 1.0 text, the Dark Moon Greatsword refers to "the Rune of Mind" ("정신의 룬, jeongsin-ui lun), presumably Ranni's Great Rune.
In English, Enia calls the player a Shardbearer after they acquire a Great Rune, while in Japanese she calls them.

name: Greater Will
image: ER Icon Armor High Priest Hat.png
description:
The Greater Will is an unseen character in. It is a mysterious entity hailing from the lightless void and serving as the dominant force in Elden Ring and the history of the Lands Between. Its vassals and envoys are central to the Golden Order. Its image boosted Intelligence and Arcane.

Background:
Long ago, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, creating births and souls. The adherents of the Three Fingers consider this action to be a mistake, because it resulted in torment, despair, affliction, sins, and curses.

The Greater Will sent a star bearing its gleaming daughter to the Lands Between. It communicated with Metyr, Mother of Fingers, through the microcosm held between her tail fingers. Soon, a second, golden star containing an Elden Beast arrived in the Lands Between. This Elden Beast was the Greater Will's vision for Order, and it would later become the Elden Ring. This beast was its vassal, and the living incarnation of the concept of Order. The Greater Will has other vassals and envoys known as the Two Fingers, who speak in a cipher sign language of light.

Eternal Cities:
Before the age of the Erdtree, the denizens of the Eternal Cities rebelled against the Greater Will. To shield themselves from its influence, the Nox donned ritual mirrorhelms to block its intervention and that of its vassals. In an act of blasphemy, they drew the ire of the Greater Will by wielding the Fingerslayer Blade against one of its vassals. In response to this transgression, the Greater Will unleashed Astel, whose destruction of the Eternal Cities condemned them to an existence underground.

Age of the Erdtree:
During the age of the Erdtree begun by Queen Marika the Eternal and at least the era immediately preceding it, the Greater Will's envoy Two Fingers selected Empyreans as candidates to become the God of the coming age. Queen Marika was one such candidate, and created the Golden Order by confining the Rune of Death. However, Marika would eventually shatter the Elden Ring, leading to her demigod offspring inheriting the Great Runes which in turn would trigger a war known as the Shattering. The Greater Will abandoned the demigods following the Shattering, as none managed to claim title of Elden Lord.

According to the Two Fingers, the Greater Will has not abandoned the realm, nor the life that inhabits it, proclaiming this is why the Tarnished have been extended the Guidance of Grace. After the Tarnished returned to the Lands Between following the Shattering, the Two Fingers, at the behest of the Greater Will, bade them kill the demigods in order to claim their Great Runes to become Elden Lord by becoming Marika's consort, as the Greater Will had long since renounced the demigods. 

In the time of The Tarnished (Protagonist), it was discovered that the entrance to the Erdtree was blocked by impenetrable thorns, preventing anyone from becoming the Elden Lord. This caused the Two Fingers to commune with the Greater Will in search of answers, which may take thousands or tens of thousands of moons. When The Tarnished (Protagonist) suggested burning the Erdtree, which would unbind Destined Death and slay the world itself, Finger Reader Enia exclaimed that the Fingers and the Greater Will would never allow it.

After The Tarnished (Protagonist) caused the Volcano Manor's recusants to disband following the defeat of Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, the recusant known as Knight Bernahl declared himself the inheritor of his comrade recusant's will. He declared their refusal to become the Greater Will's pawns and swore it would fall by his blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Greater Will is never directly referred to as an Outer God in the game. Instead the Two Fingers selected both Ranni and her Dark Moon and Malenia and her Rot as potential candidates for godhood and to forge a new Order through the Elden Ring
The Nox Mirrorhelms presumably worked by reflecting the Greater Will and the Two Fingers' language of light.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Decreases Stamina damage taken from attacks when Guarding by 20%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Since the decrease to Stamina damage when guarding is a percentage of the Stamina damage otherwise taken it sees diminishing returns when paired with equipment with high Guard Boost, such as Greatshields. 
This means it overall pairs better with equipment that has Guard Boost in the 40 to 60 range, such as Greatswords, Colossal Weapons, and Medium Shields. 
Effectively increases Guard Boost by an amount equal to 100 subtracted by the equipment's actual boost and then divided by 5 (i.e. (100-(Guard Boost))/5). 
For a piece of equipment with 40 Guard Boost wearing this talisman would effectively give it 40 + (100-40)/5 = 40 + 12 = 52 Guard Boost. For comparison, something with 60 Guard Boost would effectively get 60 + (100-60)/5 = 68 Guard Boost and something with 80 Guard Boost would effectively get 80 + (100-80)/5 = 84 Guard Boost.
Before Patch 1.04 this talisman could bring the then-not-yet-nerfed Fingerprint Stone Shield to 100 Guard Boost, decreasing Stamina damage taken to 0 and making it near impossible to deal with unless using anti-block weapons such as Reapers or the Shotel, skills such as Piercing Fang and Impaling Thrust, or by managing to circle around the shield-wielder for a Backstab.

sections.heading: Trivia

The effect was actually changed, from a 10% increase to Guard Boost to a 20% decrease to Stamina damage taken while guarding. 
Patch 1.04 decreased the effect of Greatshield Talisman for weapons with high block rate.
While all other pieces of equipment received a 10% increase to Guard Boost this update made it so that Greatshields received a lesser increase to Guard Boost.

name: Greattree
description: The Greattree is an unseen location in. It is mentioned only in a few item descriptions.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The vast network of Greattree roots spreads throughout the Lands Between. The various catacombs and hero's graves of the region were built specifically around these roots. The Greattree roots begin where those of the Erdtree end: the Deeproot Depths—the source of the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers. The two root systems were once connected, which enabled Erdtree Burial.

After Godwyn the Golden received Erdtree Burial at the base of the Erdtree's roots, his soulless body transformed into the Prince of Death. Over time, fragments of the Rune of Death leaked from his body and spread through the roots of the Greattree, giving rise to Deathroot and, ultimately, Those Who Live in Death. Sometime after the Shattering, the two root systems ended up disconnected through the Deathroot corruption, impeding the Erdtree ability to recover bodies and souls through Erdtree Burial.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The roots of the Greattree secrete a special Root Resin used for making various greases.
Elden Stars, the most ancient of all Erdtree Incantations, is placed near the Great Waterfall Basin Site of Grace at the Deeproot Depths.
The Elden Beast's tail resembles golden roots.

Oak leaves litter the area around the large hollowed-out tree protected by Crucible Knight Siluria.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Several references to the Greattree were not present in the English version 1.00 of. The relevant items instead used placeholder descriptions until a subsequent update.
The "Greattree roots" are referred to as 大樹根 (taijune) in the Japanese version of Elden Ring. The term can be translated literally as "big/great tree roots", "great treeroots", or "Great Roots".
The Japanese version of Elden Ring does not appear to use a distinct proper noun corresponding to "Greattree". Instead, it uses the descriptive term taijune ("great tree roots"). Compound names such as Erdtree and lampwood follow a naming convention often associated with Old English literature (e.g., Beowulf) and modern fantasy works inspired by it.
The Finger Reader Crone in the Capital Outskirts refers to the Erdtree as a great tree in her dialogue; "Surely you see it, too? The gold that enshrouds the heavens. The great tree which begets the pillars of light. O Tarnished, hasten to the foot of the tree. And whatever you might face... The Fingers will surely guide you...". The Erdtree is also referred to as a great tree various more times in the Japanese text, such as with the name of the Tree-and-Beast Surcoat. 大樹と獣のサーコート translating to Great Tree and Beast Surcoat.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: A Guardian Golem found at the end of Highroad Cave, having most likely fallen down from the bridge to the Divine Tower of Limgrave.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
Damage types: mainly Standard damage, with some Pierce damage from its thrusts and Fire damage from its flame breaths. 

It's immune to all Status Effects and has 40% negation to all non-Physical damage types except for Magic, where it has only 20% resistance. It is somewhat weak to Strike damage, having 0% negation towards it, and a mild 10% negation against all other Physical damage types. 

Since it starts out lying on the ground and will take a few seconds to get up once alerted, it's easy to get in some opening hits on its ankles. It has the range advantage and can hit most of the cave thanks to the length of its weapon. 

The simplest strategy is to do the same as with a regular, non-boss halberd golem by sticking behind its ankles and backing away when its starts hitting the ground with the butt of its weapon or if it breathes fire.

sections.heading: Character Information

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
(Optional) Speak to D, Hunter of the Dead, after obtaining a Deathroot and he will advise you to visit Gurranq. This can either be done at the start of D's questline in Limgrave, or in Roundtable Hold.
Travel to the Bestial Sanctum at the north-eastern point of Caelid. The sending gate marked on your map by D if you showed him a Deathroot will lead you straight there. Speak to Gurranq. If you have at least one Deathroot, Gurranq will give you a Clawmark Seal and Beast Eye. The Beast Eye will notify you whenever you are close to another Deathroot.
Hand over each Deathroot you find to Gurranq in exchange for rewards. After you have given him four Deathroot, reload the area and Gurranq will attack you. After depleting 30% of Gurranq's health, he will be subdued- speak to him and reload the area so that he returns to his original position.
After giving him the ninth Deathroot, he will give you an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone before disappearing.
Gurranq will reappear at the end of Crumbling Farum Azula, under the name Beast Clergyman. After reducing his health to 50% he will enter phase 2, under the name Maliketh, the Black Blade. 
Maliketh can be fought before completing Gurranq's questline. Doing so will not affect the questline, and Gurranq will remain in the Bestail Sanctum even after Maliketh has been defeated. Likewise, killing Gurranq in the Bestial Sanctum will not affect the fight against Maliketh.
Maliketh will have unique dialogue if you complete Gurranq's questline before fighting him in Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes

Gurranq can occasionally be found outside the Bestial Sanctum at night, howling in the direction of the Erdtree.

name: Haligtree
description: The Haligtree (聖樹, Seiju) is a great tree in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Long ago, the Empyrean Miquella abandoned Golden Order Fundamentalism upon realizing it could not cure his twin sister Malenia's scarlet rot. Seeking to create a new order of Unalloyed Gold, he settled on the Haligtree as his sanctuary. 

After the Battle of Aeonia, Miquella watered the sapling with his own Empyrean blood. He later embedded himself within a cocoon in the tree's roots to nurture it, attempting to grow it into an Erdtree. However, his efforts were interrupted when Mohg, the Lord of Blood, abducted him from the Haligtree. Under Miquella's charm, Mohg zealously sought to elevate the Empyrean to godhood and establish the Mohgwyn Dynasty as Miquella's consort. Without Miquella, the Haligtree began to wither.

Afterward, Cleanrot Knight Finlay carried Malenia's slumbering body to the Haligtree, placing her at its roots. There, Malenia awaited her brother's return while slowly corrupting the tree with the scarlet rot.

Nevertheless, the Haligtree became a refuge for societal outcasts, including the Misbegotten and Kindred of Rot. Loretta, a former Knight of Caria, established a sanctuary for the Albinaurics within its boughs, turning the area into a sacred haven for their kind.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The form of a young person with a hole in their torso can still be seen in the roots of the Haligtree where Miquella's cocoon once rested within it.
The current Haligtree appears to have grown from the stump of the older tree originating from Miquella's cocoon.
Haligtree game area has two sets of roots that often appear alongside one another. The larger, wider, and darker ones are older than Miquella's.

The master of Castle Sol holding half of the Medallion required to access the Haligtree would have been allowed to enter it depending on the success of the Eclipse in reviving a soulless Demigod. 
Gideon Ofnir sought the path to the Haligtree, sending his shadow, Ensha, to retrieve the secret medallion from the Village of the Albinaurics. In the process, Ensha killed Lattena's wolf companion, Lobo, but ultimately failed in his mission.
The Haligtree Secret Medallion depicts it with green or viridian amber.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Haligtree is a combination of the Old English word hālig (holy, sacred; healthy, sound) and tree. A literal translation would be "holy tree".
In cut dialogue lines, Old Albus referenced a chalk city of Miquella called "Eburion". This area may have been reworked into Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Equipped:
Heal is a starting spell for the Prophet origin. 

Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
The caster kneels in prayer, healing HP equal to 230% of their Faith-based Incantation Scaling, and heals nearby allies for 115% of the same.

Nearby Revenants and Revenant Followers take damage equal to 50% of their maximum HP plus an additional 300 HP. This attack also breaks their Stance, causing them to become staggered.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 32 FP per cast.
Costs 35 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
Restores HP equal to 7.19% of Incantation Scaling for each FP spent.
The healing effect can be delayed indefinitely by holding the casting button, which is helpful if an ally is not yet within range.

Strategies:
Heal is generally outclassed by the more efficient Great Heal and the significantly stronger Erdtree Heal.
The healing amount is based on the Faith scaling of an equipped sacred seal. Seals that scale with other attributes will result in reduced healing effectiveness compared to those that focus solely on Faith.
This spell breaks the stance of Revenants and Revenant followers, allowing you to quickly cast it again for a potential quick kill. This is the most FP-efficient way to quickly kill Revenants.
While technically only the Prophet and Confessor origins have enough Faith to use this incantation by default, it can still be used to kill a Revenant with any starting Origin's base Faith by using the Two Fingers Heirloom (a Prisoner will need another point in Faith, easiest gained with either Marika's Scarseal or a Commoner's Garb or Commoner's Simple Garb).
All Origins have enough FP to cast this incantation at least 3 times without using a Flask of Cerulean Tears, provided they haven't used FP for anything too expensive.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This spell is tied with Urgent Heal for the lowest healing effectiveness per FP spent.
This incantation was included among the starting equipment for the Prophet class during the Closed Network Test.

name: Heal from Afar
image: ER Icon Spell Heal from Afar.png
description: Heal from Afar is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Scadu Altus
North of Moorth Ruins there are two small bodies of water. At the northern edge of the southern body of water is a small cave tunnel with a Miranda Blossom and three Perfumers, with the incantation lying under a glowing tree at the end.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Throws out a golden orb that detonates on impact with a surface or character. 

If the caster is caught in the blast, they are healed for 420% of their Seal's Faith-based Incantation Scaling, while any allies affected are healed for 336% of the Faith-based Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Effectively heals the user as much as Lord's Heal while costing 10 less FP, healing allies for 60% more, and having far greater range. 
Heals roughly as much HP per FP as Erdtree Heal. 
Like all Incantations that can heal others, if this spell hits a Revenant or Revenant Follower, they will take damage equal to 300 + 50% of their maximum HP, and their Stance will break immediately. 
Unlike all other incantations that can do this, Heal from Afar has far greater range and thus can be used for this purpose much more safely (other healing incantations require the user to stand almost adjacent to the Revenant for this to work). 
Since it also detonates on impact with an object, aiming it into the ground or a nearby wall makes it usable as a personal heal. 
Combined with either high Dexterity or moderate Dexterity and Radagon Icon, it can be easily used for self-healing mid-combat. 
Has a fairly large area of effect that makes firing it into a large foe such as a boss a good method for healing Cooperators or Spirit Ashes. 
Can't be cast when riding Torrent, unlike most healing spells.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Though the description calls this an Erdtree Incantation, the sigil created on the ground when casting (two rings, one smaller and one larger, with script-like decorations on them) is that of a Two Fingers Incantation. 
This has no mechanical effect as neither Incantation category has their spells strengthened by wielding a specific Sacred Seal.

name: Helphen
description: The Helphen, also known as the lampwood, is an unseen location mentioned in, believed to be a great tree in another world.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The legendary lampwood tree was the source of the lamplight that beckoned the dead of the spirit world. Just as the Grace of Gold guided the Tarnished to the Erdtree, the Helphen's rays of light appeared only to those slain in battle, ushering them toward its black steeple. It was connected to the Deathbirds' cold-burning ghostflame and the Tibia Mariners, who led Those Lost in Death from spectral vessels.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The Helphen's Steeple renders the lampwood as a black coniferous tree with needles and excurrent, tapered branches. A prominent crimson gem inlaid at the apex of the black steeple design implies the Helphen's sap and lamplight are red in appearance. Lamplight is presumed to shine in the eyes of those it graces.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Most information about the Helphen is conjectural, based on visual details and contextual clues.
The game uses present-tense to describe the Helphen, implying it is still operational.
Its name suggests a connection to the great tree stump at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.
The Tibia Mariners, also psychopomps, likely produce lamplight when they emit red light from a sacred seal held in their left palm, conferring glowing red light to the eyes nearby Those Who Live in Death, who once fell in battle.
The discordant red lights seen in the Forbidden Lands are speculated to be rays of lamplight.
The Shadow Keep, Church District may have a connection to the Helphen due to the presence of Tibia Mariner boats and the appearance of its many spires. Two Scorched Tree Spirits in the flooded courtyard protect an unusual tree whose branches appear to grow downward like roots. This area contains the only path to the Scadutree Base.
Usher of Death, Rosus fulfills a similar role by lighting the path to catacombs.
While coniferous trees are found throughout the Lands Between, spirit conifers only appear on the Mountaintops of the Giants.
The Spirit Shelter, known in the Japanese script as the 霊樹 (Reiju, lit. Spirit Tree) is another tree with a strong connection to spirits. It is possible that the Helphen's black steeple served a similar purpose to the Divine Tower which supports the Spirit Shelter; an artificial structure for their respective spirit trees to grow around.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The requirements for receiving the lamplight are similar to those for entering Valhalla in Norse mythology.

name: Helphen's Steeple
description: Helphen's Steeple is a Greatsword, a melee armament.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Dropped by a Tibia Mariner on the Mountaintops of the Giants, near Castle Sol, not far from the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook grace and where you fight the Death Rite Bird.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The Chinese and Korean release of the game preserve a very different earlier draft of this item description, roughly translating to "Greatsword in the shape of the jet-black memorial spire which comforts the spirits of heroes who died under the Rune of Life's curse. This sword hosts the black flame that embodies the spirits." It is worth noting that the term "black flame" included Ghostflame and the flames of Destined Death in earlier drafts, rather than exclusively referring to Godslayer incantations.

name: Heolstor the Nightlord
description: Heolstor the Nightlord (夜の王、ナメレス, Yoru no Ō, Nameresu, lit. Lord of Night, Nameless) also known as the Night Aspect (夜を象る者, Yoru o Katadorumono), the Primordial Nightlord (原初の夜の王, Gensho no Yoru no Ō), and The Shape of Night (夜の輪郭, Yoru no Rinkaku), is the primary antagonist and final boss of.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
According to its Relic, Heolstor was once a man and a knight who was beaten by some nameless hero, along with countless other warriors. The country they fought for was destroyed, and they were left in a massive mound of corpses. He was the only one whose willpower allowed him to cheat death and rise from the pile, only to curse the world forever.

The Night Lord became the ruler of the Lands Between after the Shattering. It wields the power to summon monsters and champions from other worlds, and is responsible for the Night's Tide. The Nightfarers of the Roundtable Hold work together to overthrow the Nightlord and save Limveld. Its realm is accessible by entering a petrified tree in the Spirit Shelter at the end of the second day.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.body:
Damage Types 
+0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
A positive value indicates bonus damage. 
A negative value indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type. 

Resistances 
A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect. 
The symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Heolstor can be fought on the Third day or the Final Day during the Night Aspect expedition. Like all the other Nightlords, its boss fight can be accessed through the Spirit Shelter.

Its arena is the same as with all Nightlords.
