sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Night Aspect Expedition.
This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
This boss has Parriable attacks.
This boss is vulnerable to Holy damage, with which it gets crippled and debuffed by in both phases.
Heolstor cleaves open rifts in the sky to draw power from other realms. Each rift reveals the skybox of a different Nightlord's arena and grants a corresponding elemental Affinity.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: Nameless. 
The identity of the Nightlord was leaked early when the Nightreign Achievements were published.
The Nightlord may be connected to the Lord of Night awaited by the Nox of the Eternal Cities.
The Wylder can be reborn into a new Nightlord using a Silver Tear.
He wields what appears to be the next iteration of Fromsoftware's iconic Moonlight Greatsword. Lore clues indicate that this was his original sword, and is not a Carian blade like other Moonlight Swords in Elden Ring's lore, as it does not channel the freezing power of the Moon. It instead channels the abyssal power of Heolstor's Night. 
Heolstor's story shares some similarities with that of the Revenger of Castle Morne, slayed by Godfrey.
They both lost their life to a "hero".
It said that "[...] from the sky poured down a great rain", matching the constant rain of the castle's location, Weeping Peninsula.

Localization:
His Japanese name, ナメレス or Nameresu (pronounced nah-may-ray-su) is a somewhat unusual transcription of the word Nameless, which would normally be written ネームレス or Nēmuresu; seemingly prioritizing similarity between a romaji transcription of the name to the English word over phonetic matching.
The word Heolstor is Old English for "darkness, veil".

name: Hero's Graves
description: Hero's Graves are Landmarks in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Hero's Graves housed the remains of fallen champions whose heroism and valor earned them the privilege of Erdtree Burial. Followers of Queen Marika constructed or repurposed these catacombs during the age of the Erdtree, selected for their proximity to Greattree roots. The process facilitated and prioritized the heroes' spiritual return to the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
The surface entrances to Hero’s Graves are multi-tiered stone mausoleums with precise ornamentation. Each is crowned by a statue of a headless undertaker draped in a heavy shroud, cradling a pale, limp form as it proceeds toward the Erdtree. The dying figure reaches weakly for the golden tree in rigid, almost supplicant surrender—depicting the moment of death before the spirit’s return to the Erdtree.

Inside, the catacombs contain statues and shrines honoring a handless maiden, and banners corresponding to the factions the interred heroes served. The remains are typically guarded by imps and Merciless Chariots.

sections.heading: List of Hero's Graves
sections.body: There are five Hero's Graves in the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The statues are orientated to directly face the Erdtree.
The anonymous, faceless undertaker likely represents solemn impartiality toward the dead it receives.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Location: Stormveil Castle
The Highland Axe is found directly beneath a large painting of Elden Lord Godfrey and Serosh at Stormveil Castle.
This area contains a Grafted Scion and may be reached by from the Rampart Tower Site of Grace by descending the nearby elevator.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Boosts the strength of roar attacks (such as the enhanced heavy attacks of Barbaric Roar, or the projectile from Beast's Roar) by 10%. Do note that while this effect is very similar to the boost granted by the Roar Medallion, unlike that Talisman this Axe does not boost the damage of the breath and roar Incantations such as those found among the Dragon Communion Incantations. 
Similar to how the damage boosts to spells from certain casting implements work, the Highland Axe only grants this boost while held in one of the active hands (left or right, the currently "shown" equipment). The other active piece of equipment can still be two-handed, as the other hand slot will still count as active in the meantime (so having a Highland Axe in the active left hand slot while two-handing a Greatsword in the right hand slot will still grant a damage boost to the Greatsword's War Cry skill. 
Unlike many other such boosts, wielding two Highland Axes will not stack the boost and it will instead remain at 10%.
This item is depicted on the Axe Talisman.
This item's proximity to the painting and the description of the Axe Talisman posits Godfrey (Hoarah Loux) and the Tarnished as highlanders.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Increases Holy damage negation by 35% (10% in PvP) upon consumption. This counts as a Body Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Unlike the other Liver items, the Holyproof Dried Liver has a much stronger effect that is on par with the associated elemental fortification Incantation instead of weaker than it. 

This means that it is almost strictly superior to Divine Fortification in both PvE and PvP due to having the same effectiveness, greater duration (120 seconds vs 90 seconds), much lower FP cost (0 FP vs 20 FP). The only downside is that Divine Fortification can be used infinitely after acquiring it as long as you have a Sacred Seal and 10 Faith while the Liver has to be repeatedly crafted for that, which may require you to run out of the way to grab crafting materials.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Hit with a bolt from above with Lightning Attack Power equal to 205% of Incantation Scaling. 

Follow-up casts are quicker than the initial one.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina. 
Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies. 
Also deals 2 Stance damage. 
Actually works by sending out an invisible bullet, which then creates the lightning bolt from above when it hits an opponent. This is also why Honed Bolt very often seems to hit far behind the target when it misses, as the bullet has hit its maximum range and automatically performs the attack. 
Combines well with other incantations due to its quick casting speed.

name: Horned Giant
description: The horned giants are characters in:.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The horned giants bore haloed crowns of tangled horns, an aspect of the primordial Crucible that originated in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The presence of such horns was regarded as a mark of divinity and an irrefutable sign of primacy. Hornsent scholars who studied the ancient ruins collected and archived the giants' remains at the Shadow Keep's Specimen Storehouse. 

After Queen Marika's rise to power and the end of the Age of Plenty, however, aspects of the Crucible and horns on humans were deemed impurities. During the Crusade, Fire Knights Hilde and Salza refused to burn down the ruins, urging instead for the preservation of the horned specimens, even at the risk of their own lives. They succeeded in convincing Messmer, ensuring the specimens survived the cleansing fire. Messmer's Army continued this work, safeguarding both the Storehouse and its mission.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The "Horned Giant" name is conjectural.
They are most likely the remains of the ancient inhabitants of the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.Alternatively they could be ancient tutelary deities of the hornsent, or may have inspired the practice in hornsent culture.
According to the hornsent, the "mother of all Crucibles" grew on the giants of Rauh in ancient times.
They are strung up in a rigid crucifixion pose, similar to Queen Marika and the Prince of Death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Horned Giant are similar in stature to the giant mummies seated in the Chair-Crypts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In the Japanese text of the game, it is said that the people within the jars are put there to be reborn as "good people" / "righteous people" (善き人). It lacks the religious connotations of the word "saint" or "sainthood" used in the English version. This applies to the following texts:
"I swear—a living saint I'll surely be!" Stranded Souls -> 天に誓う。善き人になる
"Nigh-sainthood itself awaits you within." Stranded Souls -> そして、善き人になりなさい 
"This is what becomes of the condemned, who get sliced up and stuffed into jars to become saints instead." Innard Meat -> 善き人になるために 切り刻まれ、大壺に詰め込まれた罪人どもの なれの果てである
"They offer their prayers to the innards of the greatjars, such that they might be reborn one day into sainthood." Greatjar -> その祈りは大壺の中身に捧げられる いつか、善き人として生まれ変わるように それは、人の手による輪廻である

name: Igon
description: Igon is an NPC character in.

sections.heading: Character information
sections.body:
Locations:

Summon sign:

Equipment:

Quest items:

Questline progression: 
Gravesite Plain
Find Igon by following his screams; he is on the floor near the Pillar Path Waypoint Site of Grace outside the Dragon's Pit. Talk to him until you exhaust his dialogue.
Foot of the Jagged Peak
After climbing the Jagged Peak and defeating the Jagged Peak Drake he starts screaming again, he is in the middle of the road that advances to the next area. Exhaust his dialogue until he gives you Igon's Furled Finger and asks you to summon him. 
Jagged Peak
After Bayle the Dread appears in his arena, Igon can be summoned to fight him. His summon sign is right in front of the fog wall (on your very first fight against Bayle, the summon sign won't appear until the boss spawns).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Igon is missing his left leg. This is the reason he can't walk.
Both Igon's legs are functional when his soul is summoned against Bayle the Dread.
Dragon Communion Harpoons may be purchased for 1,000 runes each from the Twin Maiden Husks after donating Igon's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Igon is a reference to Captain Ahab, who hunted the great white whale Moby Dick in the novel of the same name: both lose their leg in the process and use it as motivation to continue, both use harpoons as weapons against their respective quarry, and both are utterly and insanely dedicated to their hunt.
Igon is referred to in some internal files as "Dragon Communion Ahab" showing that this was an intentional comparison.
Another, perhaps intentional or perhaps not, link between the two is that "Bayle" and "whale" rhyme. 
Igon's character model is the only one that is missing a leg.

Crumbling Lands: Leads to an isolated section of Crumbling Farum Azula, where the Pearldrake Talisman is found.
Night Sky Unceasing: Leads to an isolated section of Nokron, Eternal City, where the Mottled Necklace is found.
Precipice of Anticipation: Leads back to the game's starting area, allowing a rematch with the Grafted Scion. Also contains Stormhawk Deenh, The Stormhawk King, and the corpse of the Tarnished's former Finger Maiden for progressing White Mask Varré's questline.
A fourth Sending Gate is found at the Fifth Belfry in the Realm of Shadow, located behind Castle Ensis, on a small island north of the Castle Ensis Checkpoint Site of Grace. This area is part of the Scadu Altus.

description: The Inseparable Sword is a Greatsword, a melee armament.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Obtained after the death of D, Beholder of Death, meaning there are two ways to obtain this weapon. 
The first way is the regular one, which is slower and require that the questlines of both D's and also Fia, Deathbed Companion, is completed, whereafter it is found where Fia sat in Deeproot Depths. 
The second is to kill D, Hunter of the Dead (only possible during the first encounter with him, in Limgrave, and impossible thereafter) to obtain the Twinned Set from him and then give this armor to D, Beholder of Death. This results in the second D becoming hostile at the spot where he was sitting after reloading the area, and killing him then awards the weapon (and the Twinned Set once more).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Uses a unique, more vertical Greatsword light-attack moveset derived from Dark Souls 2's Mirrah Greatsword and share with the Banished Knight's Greatsword and the Knight's Greatsword. 
One of the stronger Faith-based Greatswords, at the cost of needing a modest investment in Strength and Dexterity to wield. 
Deals 20% bonus damage to Those Who Live in Death. Combined with the extra 100% bonus damage when buffed with its innate Skill: Sacred Blade for ridiculous damage against such foes. 
While it normally cannot be buffed it still gets the flat bonus damage after casting Sacred Blade.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.body: Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones and cannot be buffed or infused.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Has the unique trait (among Greatswords) of being sheathed on the wielder's hip rather than their back.

name: Irina's Necklace

sections.heading: Use
sections.body:
The intended functional purpose of Irina's Necklace in the is unknown. Given its item description and the woman's resemblance to Irina of Morne, the locket almost certainly portrays her mother, Castellan Edgar's wife. Like Irina's Letter, Irina's Necklace may have been delivered to Edgar at Castle Morne, or Edgar the Revenger at the Revenger's Shack—provided he was somehow spared—though no such quest stages exist. The item most likely had no purpose once received.
In, this item was Azure Insignia, and may have been connected to the Red Insignia that was replaced with the Volcano Manor Invitation in subsequent patches.

Although it was unobtainable, this item was retitled "Azure Insignia" in Elden Ring version 1.00, but its description remained the same. It was renamed "Rya's Necklace" in subsequent builds of the game.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Location: Village of the Albinaurics
The Ivory Sickle is looted from a stone coffin atop a hill at the Village of the Albinaurics, located beneath the Moonlight Altar in southwestern Liurnia of the Lakes. The item is near Old Albus and the Village of the Albinaurics site of grace. Beware the Depraved Perfumer.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While the skill, Quickstep, is rather generic for an innate, locked skill, it's still very useful for quicker traversal on surfaces that slow you down, like deep muck or water, and for getting around in combat aggressively. 
Due to this weapon's mild Intelligence requirement and light weight, it allows for exploiting the fact that Quickstep costs 0 FP if the weapon's requirements aren't met and 8 out of 10 Origins won't do so by default (only the Astrologer and Prisoner meet them). While this heavily limits the skill's in-combat usage (decreases amount of i-frames from 15 to 5) it does make it ideal for traveling over slowing surfaces. 
Unusually for a weapon upgraded with Smithing Stones, this weapon cannot be buffed or have its affinity changed. 
Though its Dexterity-scaling is slightly stronger than its Intelligence-scaling it gains the most Attack Power from a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence approach. 
Though the description may give the impression that this is a Faith-scaling weapon, it has not association with that stat. 
Overall a somewhat awkward weapon when it comes to how to best use it. A pure Intelligence build would do better with any other dagger with a Magic affinity while a hybrid Dex/Int build would probably prefer the Glintstone Kris. 
It does admittedly serve as a decent stand-in for the aforementioned Glintstone Kris before getting it since it requires defeating two specific bosses holding Great Runes while the Ivory Sickle can be gained without defeating any boss at all if Stormveil Castle is bypassed and is available a bit earlier than most Cold or Magic affinity Skills. It's also a decent off-hand weapon but is somewhat hampered by requiring the somewhat hard-to-get-enough-of regular Smithing Stones. 
All attacks ignore 50% of guarded damage negation, though the dagger's low original Attack Power may make it appear to be lower than that.
This applies to both the Physical damage and the Magic damage. 
As a dagger it will bounce away when hitting Medium Shields and Greatshields which means the weapon should preferably be used two-handed when attacking against those so that the guard-piercing can be fully exploited.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity or Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: Kaiden
description:
Kaiden is a mentioned location in. It is said to be located at the mountaintops of the wintry north and serves as the home settlement for a clan of hulking, fearless mercenaries who are adept at fighting on horseback. 

They primarily make use of a type of curved greatsword whose versatile design combines the blade of a scimitar with the heft of a hatchet. The mercenaries cover themselves in navy-blue cloth, chain-mail and scaly gray armor while insulating themselves from the blistering cold with the pelt of snow-wolves. They all take great care in maintaining their horses, carrying various types of Rowa Raisins to feed their animal companions.

__TOC__

While a decent amount of the Kaiden Sellswords can be unsurprisingly encountered in the snowfields of the Giant's Mountaintops, they are generally well traveled and can be encountered in more regions around the Lands Between, particularly in Limgrave where they have seemingly been hired to guard campsites, patrol shorelines or escort Wandering Nobles in the middle of transporting their excavated relics.

It could be possible that it is located even further north than the mountaintops, beyond the watery borders of the Lands Between.

name: Kenneth Haight
description: Kenneth Haight is an NPC in. He claims to be the next ruler of Limgrave but is in need of assistance as his fort has fallen.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Kenneth Haight is a nobleman and claims to be next in line as the rightful ruler of Limgrave. He resided in a fort known as Fort Haight, and is known for his considerable largesse, at least by his own account. Godrick the Grafted assumed control of Limgrave following the Shattering, and at some point sent a knight commander to seize Fort Haight.

Driven out of his home, Kenneth began searching for adventurers who might help him restore control of his fort. He was stumbled upon by a Tarnished champion, and despite some reticence in accepting the help of a Tarnished, bid them to retake his fort in exchange for a handsome reward, while also sharing with them his exceedingly low opinion of Godrick.

Upon the Tarnished's success, a joyous Kenneth Haight grants them a reward and thanks them profusely. In addition, he offers them the opportunity to be knighted and enter into his service. He tells them to meet him as his fort, where the ceremony shall be held.

However, upon seeing the sorry state of his fort, Kenneth becomes maudlin. Believing that Limgrave cannot remain without a proper ruler, he dedicates himself to finding a true and stalwart Lord of the proper lineage as soon as possible. He apologizes to the Tarnished, telling them he now lacks the authority to lift them to knighthood. 

After the death of Godrick, Kenneth eventually encounters a worthy lord; Nepheli Loux. Kenneth joins her in the throne room of Stormveil Castle to aid her in assuming the reins of the castle. When the Tarnished who had once aided him comes to visit, Kenneth tells him he intends to eventually return to his fort, where he can fulfill his old promise and raise them to knighthood at last. 

He may or may not be a reference to the real-life role-playing game designer Kenneth Hite.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Diallos Hoslow is a scion of House Hoslow and the younger brother of Juno Hoslow. From a young age, Diallos was all talk and no trousers, with an inability to commit to action. As a result, Juno inherited the Hoslow legacy without resistance. Juno loved his brother dearly and showered him with adoration. Diallos, in turn, admired his brother, a mighty warrior who lived up to the bloody legacy of House Hoslow. Diallos aspired to be like his older brother, knowing that pursuing the bloody legacy of their house would break his brother's heart.

Diallos had a servant by the name of Lanya and the two were companions since childhood. At some point, the two set out on a journey in the Lands Between, but Diallos lost track of the fickle Lanya, and the two became separated. He made his way to Roundtable Hold where he implored the Hold's visitors to keep an eye out for Lanya.

Diallos eventually managed to track Lanya down to Liurnia of the Lakes, where he found her dead. He deduced that the recusants of the Volcano Manor were behind her death and swore vengeance upon them. He tracked them down to their hideout on Mt. Gelmir, but when the proprietor of the manor, Lady Tanith, offered him a place among them, flattering him by telling him he had the stuff of champions, Diallos abandoned his vengeance and decided to join the manor as a recusant. 

Diallos pursued the path of a recusant, dirtying his hands time and again, but soon came to realize his folly. Having achieved nothing, he declared himself a complete fool, just as his brother had said, for abandoning the path of revenge and sullying the name of his house. 

Diallos left the Volcano Manor and travelled to Jarburg, a settlement for Living Jars. Diallos became Jarburg's new "Potentate" and devoted himself to caring for the jars. Diallos was at peace with his new calling, feeling for the first time in his life that he was on the straight and narrow. The jars enjoyed his soft, silky hands, but they were disappointed by his apparent lack of strength and courage.

When Jarburg was invaded by jar-poachers, Diallos took up arms to defend his charges. He was mortally wounded in the battle, but managed to drive off the poachers and saved most of the jars. Diallos died at peace, having finally proven his worth to his dear jars and to himself.

image: ER Icon Spell Knight's Lightning Spear.png
description: Knight's Lightning Spear is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Scorpion River Catacombs
After arriving in the room with a spiked falling roof, keep to the right to find a ladder in one of the small safe spots around the corner (in the second half of the room) and climb up it. Cross the bridge to the right and then, after waiting for the Death Blight build-up to subside, use a thin ledge to the left to cross to the side with the Death Blight inflicting statue to find a short tunnel with the Incantation at the end, guarded by two Imps wielding Greatswords.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Creates a spear of Lightning to hurl, with Attack Power equal to 138% of Incantation Scaling, accompanied by four sigils that create additional follow-up spear to hit twice with Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling per hit. 

Charging the spell creates two more sigils that each launch a new spear, and increases the first spear's Attack Power to 164% of Incantation Scaling, though there's still only two hits total from the follow-up spears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged. 
Though the initial Attack Power is boosted by 19% (37% with the talisman above) when charged, the additional spears do not do any extra Attack Power (though the two actual damaging hits do gain a 15% Attack Power boost with the talisman), making the overall boost 11% (28% with the talisman) when charged. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
Deals 27 Stance damage if it's charged and all projectiles hit, about on par with a Straight Sword's charged heavy attack but at range, making it very strong at opening enemies for Critical Attacks. 
A full uncharged hit deals 15 Stance damage. 
Enemies will not react to the casting of either the charged or uncharged version. This is unlike Lightning Spear, where only the uncharged version is not noticed by enemies. 
The sigils will always launch additional spears if created, even if the caster is interrupted before they can throw the first spear. 
Slightly stronger than Lightning Spear when it comes to the FP-to-damage ratio and deals considerably more damage per hit, but the uncharged version takes 0.3 seconds, or 55% more time, to cast. 
If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies. 
Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Knight's Lightning Spear was charged or not. 
This effect can be triggered up to 2 times per cast, once from the initial spear and then a second time from the follow-up spears hitting.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This spell is used by the Death Knights.
Patch 1.13 PvP-only adjustments: increased attack power of the initial lightning spear, decreased attack power of the spears launched after the first one, decreased Poise damage of all spears generated by this spell.
This increased the Attack Power of the first spear by 40% and decreased the Attack Power of the follow-up spears by 20% against other players, increasing overall Attack Power by 2% in PvP. 
The patch actually increased damage to Poise done by this spell, doubling it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In Game Version 1.00, there were no Kindred of Rot at the Grand Cloister, nor was the lonely Ancestral Follower Warrior present in the lake. Instead, the Grand Cloister featured a group of approximately six Rot Worshippers (rot-infused Ancestral Follower Warriors), and one rotten Ancestral Follower Shaman. The primary differences were that the Warriors had a stun-locking rot-breath ability, while the Shaman’s melee attacks inflicted Scarlet Rot. Additionally, the Putrid Tree Spirit at the far end of the area was always visible.
It seems that early on in development an Ancestor Spirit was intended to be fought where Astel is, as the spawn data for them and their spirit animals can be found in the area, which might be the reason the rot-infused Ancestral Followers where placed there.
Though Astel, Naturalborn of the Void was still there it was named Astel, Misbegotten of the Void (the Misbegotten were at the time referred to as Aberrations).

name: Land of Reeds
description:
The Land of Reeds (葦の地, Ashi no Chi) is a mentioned location in.

It is located outside the borders of the Lands Between and is said to be a place locked in a long and miserable civil war, which, over time, has caused its alienation from neighboring nations and left the entire land succumbed to a blood-soaked madness.

__TOC__

sections.heading: People
sections.body:
ER Base Template Type A Reedlander.png|Male Reedlander
ER Base Template Type B Reedlander.png|Female Reedlander

The peoples hailing from this land are referred to as "Reedlanders" and are select-able as a base template for the player character's appearance.

Known Reedlanders:
The Samurai Origin
Yura, Hunter of Bloody Fingers
Okina, the Bloody Finger
Inaba Clansmen

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Its history, weapons and mentioned customs are extremely reminiscent of the Sengoku (warring states) period of Japan, during the the 15th and 16th centuries.
One of the legendary names of ancient Japan was 葦原の中つ国 (Ashihara-no-Nakatsu-Kuni), which translates literally to "The Land Amongst the Reeds." (More idiomatically, it might be read "the land of abundant rice.")
Although never directly stated, many details suggest the Land of Reeds is under the influence of the Formless Mother. These include descriptions of Reedlanders as having "succumbed to a blood-soaked madness" and their clear favoritism for weapons that cause Blood Loss. The Outer God delights in the inflicting of wounds and the spilling of blood in all forms. The magical enhancement granded by Seppuku may very well be a blessing from the Outer God, with the technique acting as a form of offering. If the Formless Mother does preside over the Land of Reeds, it remains unclear if Reedlanders are willing to serve it, or if they are even aware of it.

name: Lands Between
description: The is the name given to the setting of. It is a vast realm formerly ruled by Queen Marika the Eternal.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
It is said that long ago, the Greater Will triggered a great rupture across the heavens, and the vitality of the stars rained down upon the Lands Between. The first star to arrive contained the daughter of the Greater Will: Metyr, Mother of Fingers. Later came a golden star bearing an Elden Beast, which later became the Elden Ring.

The Lands Between witnessed the rise and fall of many civilizations and their gods. In the prehistoric era, Dragonlord Placidusax served as the Elden Lord of the Ancient Dragons. During the Age of the Erdtree, Queen Marika, vessel of the Elden Ring, and her consort, the Elden Lord, ruled from Leyndell, Royal Capital, atop the Altus Plateau. Evidence of ancient cultures such as the Nox, Giants, Astrologers, Ancient Dynasty, and Hornsent remains scattered and buried throughout the realm.

The Lands Between was also home to the Primordial Crucible, where all life was once blended together. Under the guidance of the Two Fingers, Marika transformed the Crucible into the Erdtree during her rise to power. She later excised the heart of the Lands Between, creating a Realm of Shadow to conceal her secrets.

After Marika shattered the Elden Ring, the Lands Between became the site of The Shattering: a war between her Demigod offspring. Despite the power gained through their Great Runes, none of them succeeded in becoming Elden Lord. Grace was then extended to the Tarnished, who were called back to the Lands Between to seek the shards of the Elden Ring, so that one may become Elden Lord.

sections.heading: Nightreign
sections.body: is set in a parallel timeline where the Shattering War had a different outcome, featuring Limveld, a volatile and ever-changing region.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Sections of the Lands Between have been displaced, buried, or sealed away over the ages.
All manner of Death washes up on the Lands Between.
The Suppressing Pillar stands at the center of the Lands Between.
The various outer gods contest the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
George R. R. Martin invented the name "Lands Between" for the setting.
The Lands Between were once referred to as "The Riftlands" through an unnamed character's monologue from a leaked internal trailer initially meant for European shareholders.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Call down a glaive made of red lightning that is then swept horizontally, hitting for Lightning Attack Power equal to 325% of Incantation Scaling, and sending out a wave of red lightning with Attack Power equal to 167% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Casting the spell costs 45 points of Stamina. 
Deals 12 Stance damage on a direct hit. The wave deals 5 Stance damage. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
A bit too slow to be used against tough foes but very effective against crowds.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Like other red lightning incantations, this spell doesn't actually make the caster create a bolt of lightning in the hand, instead summoning the bolt from somewhere above them. 
Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption.
FP cost was reduced from 28 to 22.

name: Lanya
description:
Lanya is a character in. She is a servant of House Hoslow and childhood companion of Diallos Hoslow.

Described by Diallos as being "fickle as the wind," she has a habit of running off to unknown places, frequently requiring him to search for her whereabouts.

She would eventually meet her fate in the middle of one of her disappearances, having been murdered by an unspecified Recusant of Volcano Manor, and her body was left in a pool of blood at the northern edge of Academy Gate Town. This act that would put Diallos on a path of revenge; however, true to his nature, he was unable to commit to the act in the end, instead joining the Recusants himself as a prospective champion. He would still feel pain and sadness over Lanya's death, calling it cruel and unfortunate, but believed they were both simply laid hard roads by fate.

__TOC__

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.body:
Lanya has a slender figure and mild orange skin with faintly visible freckles covering her cheeks. Her eyes are light blue. She has messy, orange-blonde hair that reaches down to her shoulders, with some covering her left eye and some tied into a small ponytail at the top of her head.

She wears the Chain Armor, Chain Gauntlets and Chain Leggings.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While Layna's killer is unnamed, Patches, later revealed to be a Recusant, does appear in Liurnia not far south of Academy Gate Town at the Scenic Isle, provided the Tarnished hasn't reached Altus Plateau yet. However, she is nowhere near a cliff and has suffered a violent end, making it less likely (but not impossible) to have been Patches.
She may have been slain by Albinaurics, many of which roam the area, taking revenge on a lord's servant as a lord's men had raided their nearby village.
The chain mail she wears is described as standard issue wear for soldiers, meaning Lanya may have been a foot soldier for the Hoslows, although she may simply have worn men's armor in a common "tomboy" fashion.

image: ER Icon Spell Law of Causality.png
description: Law of Causality is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Given by Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing after defeating Mohg, Lord of Blood and choosing to talk "About the Lord of Blood's Cocoon". 

Can also be bought from the Twin Maiden Husks for 5,000 Runes after defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Grants a unique Buff that lasts for 120 seconds. If the buffed target is damaged 5 times within 7 seconds, they explode, hitting for 487 Holy Attack Power against all enemies within a 4-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. 
Deals 7 Stance damage. 
Since the buff caster has to take damaging hits to trigger the effect, shields with 100% Guarded Damage Negation can prevent the effect from activating. Shields with almost but not quite 100% Guarded Damage Negation (such as the Lordsworn's Shield and its 94% Guarded Damage Negation against Physical damage) can minimize the damage needed. 
The final hit for the buffed can be triggered during a roll or another effect that reduces damage taken to 0. If this happens, the explosion's damage is also reduced to 0. 
Does not scale at all with Incantation Scaling, meaning its damage can only be increased with effects that can buff general damage, incantation damage, and Holy damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 extended effect time.
Duration was extended from 60 seconds to 120 seconds.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Removes the Status Effects, Buffs, and debuffs from the caster and allies and enemies within a radius of 15 meters and also dispels all active spells within that effect radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 50 points of Stamina to cast. 
The requirements of the Sacred Seal don't need to be met to cast this spell, making it usable with no Faith investment. 
Surprisingly useful for crossing the Lake of Rot. While it's slower to cast than other spells and items, it's still somewhat useful for characters with high medium to high Intelligence but without the Faith needed for Flame, Cleanse Me or the materials for Preserving Boluses. 
Be careful when using it near allies so it doesn't remove their beneficial effects. 
Needed for Goldmask's quest: Reveals a secret referenced by Miriel when used while standing on top of the unknown artist's Wizened Finger message in front of the Radagon statue in Leyndell, Royal Capital, just outside of the Erdtree Sanctuary. Once you have revealed the secret message, you will be able to tell Goldmask about it to progress Brother Corhyn's quest.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The locked, innate skill, while not unique and reliant on its weaker Intelligence-scaling, is very strong for both the projectile bullet part and the weapon stab part. 
Gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Intelligence build (600 AP from having 45 Strength, 9 Dexterity, and 45 Intelligence), a bit less from a pure Strength build (579 AP from 80 Strength, 9 Dexterity, and 13 Intelligence), and even less from a pure Intelligence build (561 AP from 8 Strength, 12 Dexterity, and 80 Intelligence). 
Note that since the projectile part of the skill is a bullet-type it scales with associated stat, in this case Intelligence, meaning that the pure Intelligence build will deal the most damage with that part of the skill, and that the pure Strength build will most likely end up dealing somewhat less damage overall with the skill. 
Has a unique blocking heavy attack, shared with the Carian Knight's Sword. While this can make attacking into an attacking foe a bit less punishing, the resulting Stamina damage that will be taken if hit can prevent the user from attacking or rolling away. 
While the brief hit-stun taken by shields isn't suffered when hit, the low Stability means that using the unique heavy attack is highly likely to result in a stun from being guardbroken. 
Stability can be increased by 10% via two-handing and then further by the Greatshield Talisman. 
While the uncharged unique heavy attack deals the same amount of Stance damage as a normal uncharged heavy attack, but the charged version only deals 1.5 times more Stance damage, instead of the regular charged version which deals 3 times more Stance damage.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Despite Leonard's small and scrawny stature, Radahn continued to ride him even as he grew to an enormous size. Unwilling to abandon beloved steed, Radahn studied gravitational magic in Sellia under a master who was an Alabaster Lord.

Leonard served the Red Lion General in many battles during the Shattering. After Radahn's duel with Malenia at the Battle of Aeonia, Leonard remained by his lord's side as he was consumed by the baleful scarlet rot.

Unlike the steed of the Putrescent Knight, Leonard has no attacks of his own.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Starscourge Radahn's model is internally labeled as "RadahnAndLeonard."
Leonard is hidden underground directly below the player when Radahn uses his meteorite attack. Leonard remains below the player to ensure Radahn does not miss. He phases through the ground during the explosion and Radahn rides him once more.

moveset: The Leonine Misbegotten wields an Iron Greatsword and deals Standard damage on all attacks. The Leonine Misbegotten is highly aggressive and mobile, and it may be challenging to find openings to attack it. It can buff itself with Red Eyes when it uses Barbaric Roar.
| Barbaric Roar || Stands upright and raises its left arm, then unleashes a roar that damages a small area of effect. Gains Red Eyes at the start of the animation.
| Double Slash || Slashes counterclockwise, followed immediately by a clockwise slash.
| Double Swipe || Swipes forward, then backhands with its left paw.
| Ground Slam || Leaps while gripping the sword blade horizontally, then slams into the ground on all fours, producing a shockwave. May repeat once.
| Hop Slice || Performs a short hop and brings the sword down vertically.
| Lunging Slash || Drops to all fours, raises its haunches, then leaps forward to slash with its sword. Typically used from long range.
| Opener: Horizontal || Opens a combo with a single clockwise slash.
| Opener: Vertical || Raises the sword overhead and slams downward to begin a combo.
| Quickstep || Dashes in a direction on all fours. May be repeated or chained into another attack.
| Running Slash || Draws its sword behind the shoulder while sprinting, then delivers a wide slash. Used when at a distance.
| Slash || Swings its sword once in a clockwise arc.
| Sideswipe || Drops to all fours, dashes clockwise, then leaps a great distance forward, slashing during the pass. Used when at a distance.
| Slice & Leap || Strikes counterclockwise, then leaps high and plunges the sword into the ground.
| Slice & Slam || Slashes clockwise, pauses briefly overhead, then slams the sword straight down.
| Stamp (Sweep) || Stomps once, then spins with two full horizontal sword sweeps.

name: Libra, Creature of Night
image: ERN Boss Libra, Creature of Night.PNG
description: Libra, Creature of Night (夜の魔、リブラ, Yoru no Ma, Ribura), also known as Equilibrius Beast (調律の魔物, Chouritsu no Mamono), is a Night Lord boss in.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.body:
Damage Types 
+0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
A positive value indicates bonus damage. 
A negative value indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type. 

Resistances 
A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect. 
The symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This Nightlord is fought on the final day of the Equilibrious Beast Expedition.
This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
When Libra starts pummeling the ground and summoning a Madness aura, run around and collect as many false-gold pieces around the arena as you can. Each one heals you a bit but most importantly, alleviates Madness buildup.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: Baphomet.
His connection to dubious alchemy and counterfeit gold are likely a play on the fact that the Japanese word for western alchemy, 錬金術 (Renkinjutsu, lit. the art of refining gold) refers in modern parlance to hucksters making money through unethical means and scams. 
He wields his staff in his left hand. Making him the next unique left-handed character that Fromsoft puts in their games. There’s always at least one in each installment. That is, Iron Golem in Dark Souls 1, Fume Knight and Throne Watcher in Dark Souls 2, Old Demon King and Dancer of the Boreal Valley in Dark Souls 3, Ludwig in Bloodborne, and Messmer in Elden Ring. Artorias was also rumored to be left-handed, before his arm was shattered.
His name, Libra, is the same as a star sign in Astrology. Its unique symbol is that of a balance/scale, and its gemstone is an Opal. Its most prominent traits are that of Balance, Diplomacy, Charm, Intelligence, and Fairness. 
Libra is referred to as a Demon (悪魔, Akuma), making him the first of his kind in the universe.
The demons of the Demon's Souls and Dark Souls universes are known as デモン (Demon) in the Japanese script, a simple transcription of the English word Demon, while Libra uses 悪魔 (Akuma), a Japanese word which refers to demons such as the buddhist Mara and Christian devil, tying into its links to Baphomet, a medieval Christian garbling of the name of the Islamic prophet, which was later attached to Éliphas Lévi's Sabbatic Goat, an iconic depiction of a goat-headed figure which formed the basis for Libra's design.
Libra's title in Japanese (夜の魔) directly calls him "Demon of Night".

image: ER Icon Spell Light of Miquella.png
description: Light of Miquella is an incantation spell in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. It is one of Miquella's Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Trade: Remembrance of a God and a Lord

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Summons a circle of light that explodes after 3 seconds into a pillar of light for Holy Attack Power equal to 375% of Incantation Scaling over a 6-meter radius. 

1 second after the large pillar of light explodes, smaller pillars of light with a radius of 1 meter and with Holy Attack Power equal to 70% of Incantation Scaling are created in the affected area.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast. 
The large pillar of light deals 20 Stance damage, while the smaller ones deal 2 Stance damage per hit. 
Wearing the Circlet of Light increases the Attack Power by 10%. 
The incantation is guaranteed to complete after the circle of light is created, even if the caster is knocked out of the casting animation before the first pillar of light has time to explode.

name: Lightning Fortification
description: Lightning Fortification is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Altus Plateau.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: If the player lights the Forge of the Giants before this incantation appears in Corhyn's inventory, it will become unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Lightning Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Lightning damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 FP per cast.
Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces lightning damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where LightningFortification represents the effect magnitude:
TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {LightningDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {LightningFortification}) )
For example, if lightning damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
TotalLightningReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

Strategies:
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as lightning damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple lightning negation sources.
Lightning Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
This incantation is especially valuable against Leyndell Knights, Silver Tears, and Spark Orbs, particularly in Crumbling Farum Azula, where lightning damage is prevalent.
Lightning Fortification offers greater lightning protection than Lightningproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
The Lightningproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.

name: Lightning Spear
description: Lightning Spear is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 6,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Dragon Cult Prayerbook.
Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Creates a small, golden spear in hand to throw, with Lightning Attack Power equal to 234% of Incantation Scaling. 

Charging the incantation increases the Attack Power to 293% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Casting the spell costs 28 points of Stamina. Charging it increases the cost to 36 points of Stamina. 
Deals 5 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 9. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged. 
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 44%. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
Charging this incantation more than doubles the casting time. In fact, though Knight's Lightning Spear is a good bit slower when both are cast uncharged, if they are charged they take the same amount of time to cast. 
Non-player characters will not actively try to dodge the uncharged version of this incantation. This is especially useful when fighting against evasive foes such as Tarnished-type enemies, since they are otherwise near-perfect at dodging projectile attacks. 
If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies. 
Also deals 2 Stance damage regardless of if the original Lightning Spear was charged or not.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 increased attack power when charged.
This increased the Attack Power of the charged version from 273% of Incantation Scaling to 293% of Incantation Scaling. 
Patch 1.03 seems to have included an undocumented changed which increased the FP cost of this incantation. 
FP cost was increased from 14 to 18.

The stone platforms on either side of this can be used to descend safely. Note that it's surrounded by large bats and that lightning strikes constantly hit around this area.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Creates an uneven line of lightning strikes with Lightning Attack Power equal to 246% of Incantation Scaling per hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina. 
Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
If the incantation hits a watery surface or an enemy standing on such a surface, a small area of effect attack with Lightning Attack Power equal to 50% of Incantation Scaling will be created that can hit the target foes and any adjacent enemies. 
Also deals 2 Stance damage. 
Can hit multiple times per cast. 
Targeting may seem somewhat random due to the line that is being struck not being quite straight. However, the lightning bolts will always strike on the same intervals which means getting a feel for this and keeping a consistent distance will help with hitting greatly. 
This incantation does not work under low roofs. 
This is because the targeting is done by sending a projectile straight above the caster's head that then travels forward while sending down lightning bolts periodically. This projectile is destroyed if it hits a solid object.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 decreased FP consumption.
This reduced the FP cost of casting from 21 to 19.
Patch 1.04 decreased Stamina cost, increased cast speed and decreased recovery time.

description: Lightningproof Dried Liver is a craftable, consumable tool in.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Increases Lightning damage negation by 15% (10% in PvP) for 120 seconds upon consumption. This counts as a Body Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Compared to Lightning Fortification:
In PvE there is a tradeoff, the Liver has greater duration (120 seconds vs 90 seconds) and much lower FP cost (0 FP versus 20 FP) while the Fortification has greater Magic damage negation (35% versus 15%).
Unlike the other Liver items this item's cookbook is acquired far later in the game, making it unavailable for Leyndell, Royal Capital, one of the game's major Lightning-focused area. 
In PvP the Liver is stronger, since these effects have the same strength but the Liver has a greater duration and no FP cost.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Can be crafted after acquiring the Ancient Dragon Apostle's Cookbook [4] from a round building atop floating stone walls making a bridge upwards in Crumbling Farum Azula. It is found past the Dragon Temple Lift Site of Grace, straight across the courtyard and jumping atop two buildings on the right to get across a gap. Following across the ascending pseudo-bridge, it is guarded by 2 Giant Skeleton Beastmen. 
2 found in Leyndell, Royal Capital, on the stairs leading to the Fortified Manor. From the Avenue Balcony Site of Grace, head up the stairs and head right to see the stairs, which are guarded by 2 Leyndell Soldiers and 1 spear-wielding Leyndell Knight. 
1 found in Crumbling Farum Azula, near the Crumbling Beast Grave Site of Grace. Head right and look to the left at a hole in the wall as soon as the next room is entered to find it. 
1 found in Lake of Rot, to the side of an island near the place where the Dragonkin Soldier is fought in the eastern part of the fetid lake. 
1 found in Altus Plateau, on a high rock just south of Lux Ruins.

name: Lightseeker Hyetta
description: Lightseeker Hyetta, later known as Finger Maiden Hyetta, is an NPC in.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Basic Info:

Equipment:

sections.heading: Hyetta's Quest
sections.body:
Quest Items:

Questline Progression:
For Lightseeker Hyetta to appear, you must have completed Irina of Morne's questline, meaning Irina must be dead.

Lake-Facing Cliffs (Liurnia of the Lakes)
Hyetta first appears near the Lake-Facing Cliffs Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes. Exhaust her dialogue, and she shall request a Shabriri Grape.
Give her a Shabriri Grape, the nearest of which is south of Hyetta, found within the rear entrance to Stormveil Castle. However, the door is locked from the other side, accessible from the Stormveil Castle throne room.
Purified Ruins (Liurnia of the Lakes)
Hyetta moves to a spot close to the Purified Ruins. She again asks for a Shabriri Grape, the closest of which is east of Hyetta's location, within the Purified Ruins. It is in a secret cellar, hidden beneath some wooden planks.
Give her the Shabriri Grape and exhaust her dialogue.
Gate Town Bridge (Liurnia of the Lakes)
Hyetta will now appear just north of the Gate Town Bridge site of grace. She will ask for yet another Shabriri Grape. The final grape is dropped by Edgar the Revenger, who ambushes the player at the Revenger's Shack, found north of the Minor Erdtree in western Liurnia. 
After giving her the third grape, you will have the option to tell her that the grapes are human eyes. After hearing her dialogue following this revelation, reload the area and speak to her again in the same spot.
Bellum Church (Bellum Highway)
Hyetta is next found within the ruined Bellum Church, found along the Bellum Highway. After talking to her, she will ask you to bring her a special Fingerprint Grape. This item can be obtained by defeating Festering Fingerprint Vyke, who invades the player at the Church of Inhibition in eastern Liurnia.
Bring Hyetta the grape and exhaust her dialogue.
Frenzied Flame Proscription (Subterranean Shunning-Grounds)
Hyetta's final location is in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, deep below Leyndell, Royal Capital, at the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription. A seal at the Cathedral of the Forsaken restricts access to this location, available only after defeating Morgott, the Omen King. Exhaust her dialogue until she instructs you to unequip all Armor and interact with the burnt door at the end of the hall, past where she stands.
Remove all Armor and interact with the door to initiate a cutscene wherein the player meets the Three Fingers and inherits the Flame of Frenzy. (WARNING: this action permanently removes Melina as a companion and sets you on the path to the "Lord of the Frenzied Flame" ending, the latter of which can only be undone by using Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time to cheat fate.)
After the cutscene, return to Hyetta and exhaust her dialogue. After speaking to her twice, the Frenzied Flame burns her away, leaving behind the Frenzied Flame Seal and five Frenzyflame Stones.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Hyetta will not appear if the player kills Irina of Morne early.
Hyetta can be killed and her blood can be used to soak the Lord of Blood's Favor for White Mask Varré.
Hyetta has the same facial appearance and voice as Irina of Morne, and she will only appear if Irina's questline has ended and she has died. Hyetta is Irina, having experienced some form of resurrection or rebirth similar to Shabriri.
The player can meet the Three Fingers and commit the Cardinal Sin without meeting Lightseeker Hyetta, and her questline proceeds as usual if started after.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Voice actor: Clare Corbett
Lightseeker Hyetta had an additional quest stage at Bellum Church in the, but the dialogue and key item she gave were both cut from the game by the release. The context it provided offered insight into her transition from Irina of Morne and into the characters of Irina and Edgar. Hyetta gave Irina's Necklace after receiving the Fingerprint Grape, abandoning her long search for its owner.

name: Lion Greatbow
description: The Lion Greatbow is a Greatbow, a ranged armament. It fires equipped Great Arrows. It is General Radahn's secondary weapon.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Trade the Remembrance of the Starscourge, gained by defeating Starscourge Radahn, with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough either way).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Its Strength requirement is effectively always 15 as Greatbows can only be wielded two-handed.
Boosts the damage of Radahn's Spears by 20% when held in an active hand. Note that this remains true even if it isn't used to shoot them, as long as this weapon is in the other hand. 
Using two separate Lion Greatbows grants the boost twice, for a 44% damage increase.
Scales slightly better with Strength than with Dexterity, though a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build fares a bit better than a pure Strength build. 
A 45/45 split of the Attributes gives 501 Attack Rating (AR).
An 80/18 (minimum Dexterity) split gives 488 AR (effectively 120 Strength due to the 50% boost from two-handing).
A 54/18 (minimum Dexterity) split gives 470 AR (effectively 81 Strength due to the 50% boost from two-handing).
A 15/80 (minimum Strength) split gives 466 AR.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Patch 1.09 increased this weapon's scaling values.

sections.heading: Upgrading
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
Can't be buffed or be infused with Ashes of War.

passive_effects: Increases the power of Radahn's Spear by 20%.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body: Lionel's Equipment:

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body: Fia's Mist (as part of Fia's Champions)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
He has unique character data in Zullie the Witch's video "Elden Ring - Hidden Faces of Enemy NPCs" he is an older man, with somewhat unkempt and heavily greyed hair, beard, moustache, and bushy eyebrows, bright silver eyes and a heavily wrinkled face.
Wears the Lionel's Set, a very heavy armor set that provides exceptional protection particularly against slashing damage.
Wields a Great Épée with Ash of War: Repeating Thrust and a Prince of Death's Staff that is used to cast Fia's Mist and Rancorcall.
Lionel the Lionhearted uses a Carian Glintstone Staff when summoned as a Coooperator against Starscourge Radahn.
A corpse that can be presumed to be his, what with his armor being lootable from it, can be found in the Lower Capital Church inside of Leyndell, next to the Deathbed Dress.
Given his inclination for Death Sorceries, Lionel presumably relayed information regarding Black Knifeprints to Fia, specifically the Knifeprint Clue.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
His distinctive rounded armor set and chivalrous personality (inferred by his apparent attitude towards Fia) is likely a reference to the Knights of Catarina from the Dark Souls series, who are jovial people clad in onion-like rounded suits of armor. Unlike these knights, however, he cannot be interacted with or spoken to.
Based on other Fia's Champions being Tarnished such as other players when online and Sorcerer Rogier, it could be the case that Lionel is also a Tarnished.

name: Litany of Proper Death
image: ER Icon Spell Litany of Proper Death.png
description: Litany of Proper Death is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Sold by D, Hunter of the Dead for 2500 runes.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Causes the user to cross their arms before performing a T-like pose to unleash a medium-ranged wave of crossing lights on the ground with Holy Attack Power equal to 56% of Incantation Scaling. 

Has a massive 900% Attack Power bonus against Those Who Live in Death, effectively making it have Holy Attack Power equal to 560% of Incantation Scaling against them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast. 
Attack Power is increased by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%. 
Deals low damage overall against non-weak enemies, with only the massive Attack Power bonus against undead making it deal enough damage to actually be somewhat usable. 
The damage vector is very groundbound and can be stopped by changes in elevation. 
Skeletons defeated by this spell are immediately killed and cannot resurrect themselves. 
The reach is somewhat hard to judge visually, with the clear golden sheen ending after about one-third to one-half of the range.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Prior to Patch 1.02, the description and effect were different. 
Old effect: Deals holy damage especially potent against undead.
Old description:

variant.effect: Creates image of Order to deal holy damage

name: Longsword
description: Longsword is a straight sword in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Starting armament of the Vagabond origin.
Purchased from Twin Maiden Husks at the Roundtable Hold for 1,000 Runes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version. 
Consistently the second strongest of all regular Straight Swords, outmatched only by the Broadsword, almost matching it on a Keen affinity and outclassing it on a Quality affinity. 
This may be somewhat surprising since the Longsword's scaling values leans towards Strength more so than Dexterity, but it's primarily because the Broadsword scales rather less well on Keen. 
Quality affinity requires high stats to use properly, making this somewhat difficult to exploit before New Game Plus/Journey 2 and later. 
While not quite to the level of the Short Sword's unique heavy attack chain, since the first heavy attack in a chain is a Pierce damage attack as well as the heavy variant of its default skill and as such can hit for heavy counter damage with the Spear Talisman.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

This talismans original description said that it was made to look like Radahn's cat, though it was later removed from the description.
The old description states: "A brooch depicting a long-tailed cat, known to be the beloved pet of General Radahn. Reduces fall damage. This black cat was known to have enjoyed jumping down from great heights; it would leap from the great bell-tower of Raya Lucaria as a kitten, and once fully grown, from the great heavenward roots that twisted through the Erdtree Capital skies."

description: The Lord of Blood's Favor is a Key Item in.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
The Lord of Blood's Favor must be soaked in a Finger Maiden's blood to become Lord of Blood's Favor (Soaked). This can be done through the following options:
Interact with the corpse of the Tarnished's own Finger Maiden at the Chapel of Anticipation (requires an Imbued Sword Key to access the Sending Gate at the Four Belfries).
Interact with the corpse of Vyke's Finger Maiden at the Church of Inhibition near the Frenzied Flame Village Outskirts.
Kill Irina of Morne at the Bridge of Sacrifice in the Weeping Peninsula, or, if already deceased, kill Lightseeker Hyetta at any of her locations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Location: Rose Church, Liurnia of the Lakes
The Lord of Blood's Favor is a quest item given by White Mask Varré at the Rose Church in Liurnia after speaking with him and fulfilling one of the following requirements:
Invade and defeat Magnus the Beast Claw three times at the Writheblood Ruins in the Altus Plateau.
Use Festering Bloody Fingers to Invade actual players three times (online only).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Lord of Blood's Favor is removed from the inventory when used.
Prospective Pureblood Knights are required to renounce to the Two Fingers and soak this cloth in the blood of their own maiden.
This item is required to reach the Mohgwyn Palace in the early-game.

Interact with the corpse of the Tarnished's own Finger Maiden at the Chapel of Anticipation (requires an Imbued Sword Key to access the Sending Gate at The Four Belfries).
Interact with the corpse of Vyke's Finger Maiden at the Church of Inhibition near the Frenzied Flame Village Outskirts.
Kill Irina of Morne at the Bridge of Sacrifice in the Weeping Peninsula, or, if already deceased, kill Lightseeker Hyetta at any of her locations.

sections.heading: Notes

This blood-drenched Lord of Blood's Favor displays an emblem associated with the Mohgwyn Dynasty.
The ritual of soaking the favor in a sacrificial maiden’s blood is an initiation rite for the Pureblood Knights.

Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook, then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: The caster kneels in prayer to remove Poison, Blood Loss, and Sleep and their buildup from themselves and nearby allies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 9 FP per cast.
Costs 10 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
The healing effect can be delayed indefinitely by holding the casting button, which is useful if an ally is not yet within range.

Strategies:
Lord's Aid is an effective utility spell for removing status effects during general gameplay.
As the Status Effect removal niche is generally better covered by more specialized alternatives such as Flame, Cleanse Me or Bestial Constitution, this incantation instead serves much better as a way to cure some common Status Effects from partners in Co-Op, whether as a summoned Furled Finger or as a summoning Host of Fingers.
Lord's Aid is preferable to Law of Regression for helping allies in PvE encounters, as the latter also removes positive Buffs.
The caster crouches while casting this incantation, which may cause some attacks to miss due to the reduced height.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: This is one of only two spells in the entire game that removes Status Effects from nearby allies. The other is Law of Regression, an incantation with a high Intelligence requirement.

variant.effect: Alleviates poison / blood loss / sleep buildup for self and allies

name: Lord's Divine Fortification
image: ER Icon Spell Lord's Divine Fortification.png
description: Lord's Divine Fortification is a incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Quest Item / Purchase: Roundtable Hold
Received from Gideon after discussing the haligtree roots, once Malenia, Blade of Miquella has been defeated.
Can be purchased from the Twin Maiden Husks for 3,500 Runes if the player does not talk to Gideon about the roots before unleashing the Rune of Death.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Grants a Body Buff that decreases holy damage taken by 60% (20% in PvP) for 70 seconds for the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 30 FP per cast.
Costs 20 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces holy damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total holy damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where Lord'sDivineFortification represents the effect magnitude:
TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {HolyDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {Lord'sDivineFortification}) )
For example, if holy damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.60) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 40%:
TotalHolyReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.20) ) = 40%
Since it's effectively the damage taken that is reduced, the higher holy damage negation stat a character has before casting the spell, the less effective it may appear in the statistics.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as holy damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple holy negation sources.
Lord's Divine Fortification is a very strong defensive spell that can significantly protect against the ranged attacks of many of the more difficult bosses, such as Maliketh, the Black Blade; Radahn, Consort of Miquella; and Radagon of the Golden Order. 
This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Holy damage in the game, particularly when facing enemies like Cleanrot Knights, Erdtree Avatars, Miranda Blossoms, and Oracle Envoys, especially while exploring Miquella's Haligtree.
Lord's Divine Fortification offers greater holy protection than Divine Fortification (60% vs. 35%) but with a shorter duration (70 vs. 90 seconds). This spell requires 27 Faith, 1 Memory Slot, and 30 FP to cast, while Divine Fortification requires only 10 Faith and 20 FP.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: This is the only upgraded Fortification spell that is a Two Fingers Incantation.

variant.effect: Greatly increases holy damage negation including allies

name: Lore
description: The narratives and are built bit by bit and told mainly through context and environmental storytelling techniques. This page summarizes the main story and lists the major factions, characters, and events that define the Lands Between and broader Elden Ring setting. This page allows users to easily locate parts of the text that offer insight into each topic. Please refer to the Lore category for a complete list of articles.

sections.heading: Story
sections.body:
In the beginning, the Greater Will fractured the One Great, which led to divisions, births, and souls. It sent its daughter, Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and its golden vassal Elden Beast through the Primeval Current to the Lands Between, the place to which all Death inevitably drifts. The Elden Beast held the power of runes and was the living embodiment of Order, and it was later forged into the great Elden Ring. The Lands Between became the arena of champions vying to become the Elden Lord.

Prologue:
Long ago, in the Lands Between, the Two Fingers directed the Empyrean Marika to claim godhood at the Gate of Divinity and become the next vessel for the Elden Ring. Marika then waged a violent War Against the Giants to upend the Fell God and suppress the Flame of Ruin, using a Golden Seed to transform the primordial Crucible of life into the Erdtree. This act ushered in an age of Plenty. Empowered by soaring Grace of Gold, Godfrey, her first Elden Lord, and his warriors set out to conquer the entirety of the continent in her name. However, this age of abundance soon came to a swift, unforeseen end. Marika later removed the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring and commanded her loyal shadow, Maliketh, to seal it away. Thus, she, her Demigod offspring, and those blessed by her Grace of Gold would live forever, earning her the title of Queen Marika the Eternal.

Godfrey, by then known as the Lord of the Battlefield, fought until Marika's reign was absolute. When the last worthy enemy fell to his axe, the very same Grace that blessed him and his army was taken away by Marika, who instructed them to wage another war and die abroad, with the promise that life and Grace would be returned to them after death. All those who were stripped of their Grace, as well as their descendants, were Tarnished, and forced onto boats and across the Sea of Fog to carry out their Long March into the Badlands, though one vessel failed to leave. Queen Marika also sent her son Messmer and an army of outcasts on a crusade to destroy the hornsent, the old folk who dwelled in the Land of the Tower. She trapped them in the Realm of Shadow to protect herself from the Base Serpent and to conceal her shrouded origins. She later claimed Radagon of the Golden Order as her second Elden Lord, who was, in truth, her other self and a very part of her being.

After a time, Marika later instructed her children to rise as Lords or gods, or become sacrifices. She then shattered the Elden Ring, fracturing her Golden Order and releasing its Great Runes into the Lands for her children to claim. After that, Queen Marika was nowhere to be found—punished by the Elden Beast and imprisoned within the Erdtree. The Demigods were each corrupted by the power of their Great Runes, triggering the appalling Shattering, a war from which no victor arose, leading to their abandonment by the Greater Will. True to Marika's promise, it was then that the Grace of Gold returned to the Tarnished, and beckoning them back to the Lands Between so that one might repair the shattered Elden Ring and become the Elden Lord.

Nightreign:
 shares the same world and backstory as Elden Ring, but takes place on a parallel timeline that diverged after Marika shattered the Elden Ring. A Shattering War also took place between the Demigods; however, it had a different outcome: Heolstor the Nightlord, empowered by the Primordial Nightlord's Rune, ushered in the Night. An azure Night's Tide created the Nightlords and threatened to wash away the Lands Between. The Dreglord, a comparable threat, emerged soon after, driven by vengeance to smash the Night.
