name: Loretta
description: Royal Knight Loretta, also known as Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree, is a recurring, optional Great Enemy boss in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Loretta was once a royal Carian knight, and served as a personal guard for Carian royalty. Loretta's favored weapon was said to be the bow, and she developed sorceries imitating the power of a greatbow. 

Loretta eventually became concerned with the plight of the Albinaurics and embarked on a long and bloody journey searching for a haven for the Albinauric people. She determined that the Haligtree was their best chance for eventual salvation. It was rumored she was actually an Albinauric herself, due to the shape and symbolism associated with her Silver Mirrorshield. She would eventually find it at the Haligtree, in service to demigod Miquella, where she now remains. 

Loretta appears to have entered into Miquella's service, replacing the blue glintstone that once adorned her war sickle with unalloyed gold. Now she stands guard within the Haligtree, refusing to abandon her post although Miquella himself is long gone. Her lapis-lazuli blue cape is the emblem of the knightly pride that continues to guide her.

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.body:
Royal Knight Loretta=

Background:
Royal Knight Loretta is a boss in. She can be found at Caria Manor in the Royal Moongazing Grounds.

She appears to be an apparition of Loretta summoned to guard Caria Manor, just as the real Loretta presumably used to do before leaving her duty to help find sanctuary for the mistreated Albinaurics.

Defeating her disables the magical spell of warding that complicates the approach to the Manor.

Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree=

Background:
Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree is a mini-boss in found in Miquella's Haligtree and is required to progress to Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree. This boss is a stronger version of Royal Knight Loretta, found in Caria Manor.

It is possible to parry Loretta's halberd swings.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Defeating Royal Knight Loretta for the first time unlocks the "Royal Knight Loretta" achievement. Similarly, defeating Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree for the first time unlocks the "Loretta, Knight of the Haligtree" achievement.
Loretta is presumed to be an Albinauric Archer in disguise.
Rumored to be an Albinauric, she cares deeply for them, abandoning her duty to travel to the Haligtree.
This female character appears only on horseback and demonstrates unmatched skill with the bow.
Her naming scheme aligns with Latenna.
Loretta's War Sickle, Royal Knight Armor, and Silver Mirrorshield were crafted from silver.
The Carians were known to employ Albinaurics as servants.
Although she bleeds red when struck, so does Commander Gaius, a known First-Generation Albinauric. The red blood may be attributed to the mount and rider being coded as a single enemy, with red chosen over white because players are more likely to hit the horse or boar.

sections.heading: Trivia

name: Loretta's Greatbow

You need to be careful in aiming it: if, and only if, your character is fully facing the direction you want to fire it will shoot dead-center of your screen in a straight line.

Background:
A flail-wielding Pumpkin Head found in a cellar beneath Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave. The warrior obstructs the entrance to a second chamber, where Sorceress Sellen resides.

The room isn't very big but the boss also isn't that quick or good at turning. The left Pumpkin Head will be sitting with its back as you enter, so make sure to attack it quickly to try and reduce this 1v2 to a 1v1. 

It's possible to use Torrent in this fight, though it's unlikely to be useful due to how small the room is.

name: Magic Fortification
description: Magic Fortification is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 3,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Magic Fortification grants a Body Buff that decreases Magic damage taken by 35% (10% in PvP) for 90 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 FP per cast.
Costs 13 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces magic damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where MagicFortification represents the effect magnitude:
TotalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {MagicDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {MagicFortification}) )
For example, if magic damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
TotalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.35) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
TotalMagicReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

Strategies:
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as magic damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple magic negation sources.
Magic Fortification is a moderately effective defensive spell with low casting requirements, usable by most starting Origins when equipped with the Two Fingers Heirloom and a Finger Seal.
This incantation is valuable due to the prevalence of Magic damage in the game, particularly against sorcerers, Deathbirds, and Glintstone Dragons, especially in regions like Liurnia of the Lakes.
Magic Fortification offers greater magic protection than Spellproof Dried Liver (35% vs. 15%) but at a shorter duration (90 vs. 120 seconds). This spell requires 10 Faith and 1 Memory Slot to be equipped and 20 FP to cast, while the Dried Liver only requires crafting materials.
The Spellproof Dried Liver is preferable for PvP encounters, as both effects are reduced to 10%.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found inside of Shadow Keep. From the Main Gate Plaza Site of Grace, head up the western stairs and take a right after the first stair, then take a right again in the corridor to arrive in a small room with a Black Knight. The dagger can be found on a body in the left corner.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Though this is a dagger it counts as a Thrusting Sword when dual-wielding, meaning that except for another copy of itself it cannot be dual-wielded with another dagger. 
Uses the Thrusting Sword dual-wielding moveset if paired with itself.
Keep in mind that the second dual wield attack will only use the right-hand weapon, and hits 3 times.
Does more than a dagger usually would when dual-wielded, but not enough to truly compete with an actual Thrusting Sword.
If wielded in the left hand alongside some kind of Rapier in the right hand, significantly modifies the attack pattern of the Rapier into a faster combination with more strikes.
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Miséricorde, and the Scorpion's Stinger.
Compared to a Thrusting Sword with Parry equipped, this dagger will have the same amount of start-up frames and takes the same amount of time to complete but with twice as many active parry frames, with a slightly shorter recovery time to compensate.
Since only the Rapier and Rogier's Rapier have increased Critical Attack damage (130 and 110 respectively), having this weapon in the off-hand to another Thrusting Sword to then two-hand upon making an enemy vulnerable to a such an attack might increase such damage.

name: Malenia, Blade of Miquella
description: Malenia, Blade of Miquella, later known as Malenia, Goddess of Rot, is an optional remembrance Boss in. She is a Demigod Shardbearer who is encountered in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A Demigod daughter of Queen Marika the Eternal and her second Elden Lord, King Consort Radagon, Malenia was born during the age of the Elden Ring. Like her elder twin brother, Miquella, a dreadful curse afflicted her from birth. The Scarlet Rot, an incurable, radiating sickness, ravaged Malenia, threatening to consume her from within. Although her condition eventually claimed her eyes and several limbs, the Two Fingers identified her as an Empyrean, a candidate to replace her mother as the god of a new age.

Miquella worked to undo the curses they had both inherited. While unable to find a cure for his sister within the Golden Order, Miquella designed a needle of unalloyed gold to keep the rot at bay. He also crafted the prostheses that enabled her to continue fighting. At some point, Malenia encountered the legendary blind swordsman of the Flowing Curved Sword, who had long ago sealed away an Outer God of Rot. The swordsman became her master, enabling her to gain wings of unparalleled strength. Malenia eventually became a peerless warrior and her brother's sworn blade and protector.

The Shattering:
]]
After the Elden Ring was shattered, Malenia claimed a shard of the fractured Elden Ring. She attracted loyal Cleanrot Knights, who vowed to fight next to her, despite the inevitable, gradual putrefaction of their flesh. During the Shattering, Malenia led an army that marched south from the Haligtree down the Bellum Highway. She won many battles against the other Demigods, even humbling fellow Shardbearer, Godrick the Grafted, who groveled at her feet for mercy after first insulting her and then suffering defeat. 

Battle of Aeonia:

Malenia and her half-brother Radahn would eventually be the last two demigods left standing in the conflict. Their forces clashed in the Caelid Wilds, and the two fought the Battle of Aeonia, a bitter duel to fulfill an unhonored vow. In the midst of the combat with Radahn, Malenia unleashes Scarlet Rot, resulting in her first Scarlet Aeonia.

The rot did not kill Radahn but robbed him of his wits, turning him feral. Malenia herself was left slumbering in a coma. She was rescued by one of her Cleanrot Knights, Finlay, who carried her across the Lands Between. When Malenia and Finlay took refuge at the Shaded Castle, Maleigh Marais, the sickly-born head of House Marais, was naturally drawn to the unconscious Demigod. He saw in her his personal goddess. Finlay carried Malenia back to the Haligtree, far north of the Erdtree. 

The unleashed scarlet rot devastated Caelid, leaving it a rotting wasteland, and created the Swamp of Aeonia. Malenia inadvertently brought forth the Scarlet Butterflies and Kindred of Rot. The pests, including Sage Gowry, who worshipped her as a goddess and hoped to cause her to bloom once again, believing that she would usher in a new age of rot. However, Malenia rejected her fate and never embraced the Servants of Rot.

Miquella had encased himself within the Haligtree in an effort to create a new Erdtree of his very own, hopefully granting him the power to cure both his and his sister’s curses. However, during Malenia's absence, Miquella was ripped from the womb of the tree and taken away by Mohg, Lord of Blood before he could emerge from his cocoon. Malenia dreamt while awaiting Miquella's return, and the scarlet rot seeped out from her and began infecting the Haligtree.

Game events:

Malenia's slumber is eventually disturbed by a Tarnished, who found their way to the roots of the Haligtree. The two fight, and Malenia finally meets her match, but she suffers her first true defeat. However, in the end, Malenia succumbs to the Scarlet Rot and blossoms yet again, reborn as a nascent goddess. She unleashes her full fury against the invader, but falls short yet again, her dying words an apology to her vanished brother. Having bloomed twice, Malenia withdraws within her scarlet blossom.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Malenia is fought at the end of Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, in a large chamber beyond the Haligtree Roots Site of Grace. 

Her arena is an open cavern with a shallow pool of water at its center. There are no obstacles, so there is plenty of space to gain distance during some of Malenia's more devastating attacks.

Combat Overview:
HP: 33,251 (total)
Defense: 123
Stance: 80
She must be parried three times to trigger a stance break, enabling a Critical Hit.
Multiplayer is enabled
Spirit Ashes are enabled
She regains lost HP with every successful attack, even if they are blocked.
She gains +10 Fire negation (0 → 10) and -10 Lightning negation (20 → 10) while standing in water.

Drops:
480,000 runes
Malenia's Great Rune
Remembrance of the Rot Goddess

Moveset:

Phase 1 - Malenia, Blade of Miquella:
HP: 18,473
Deals Standard, Slash, and Pierce damage
In phase 1, Malenia will primarily make use of melee attacks using her sword. Her quick attacks, combined with her HP regeneration on hit, mean that she can rapidly recover from any damage dealt. However, she staggers easily, and her attacks can be cancelled by attacking during her wind-up animations. Frostbite and Blood Loss are especially good for staggering her.

Phase 2 - Malenia, Goddess of Rot:

HP: 14,778
Deals Standard, Slash, Pierce, and Holy damage; and inflicts Scarlet Rot buildup.
Once Malenia's health reaches 0, a transformation cutscene will play, wherein she embraces the rot, releasing a swarm of butterflies and initiating phase 2. Malenia, Goddess of Rot starts the second phase with 80% of her maximum health, but can recover it with her HP regeneration.

The phase always begins with a scripted Scarlet Aeonia attack, which can immediately end the fight if the player does not immediately get some distance. She flies on wings made from her hair and butterflies, and many of her regular attacks can now inflict Scarlet Rot buildup. She gains a variety of rot-based attacks and can also create phantom projections of herself, which vanish after attacking. The most dangerous attack in her arsenal is her signature Waterfowl Dance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Defeating this boss for the first time unlocks the Shardbearer Malenia achievement.
The "Demigod Slain" flyout is displayed upon defeating Malenia, Goddess of Rot.
Malenia has a prosthetic right arm, left leg, and right foot. These were added due to the infection of the scarlet rot. The rot has also visibly spread over her eyes, so she is presumably also blind. However, her disabilities do not handicap her battle prowess in the slightest.
According to the Scarlet Aeonia Incantation description, Malenia will become a true Goddess if her scarlet flower blooms three times. She first used this spell during the Battle of Aeonia. Malenia blooms a second time during her duel against the Tarnished.
Once defeated, she will leave behind a large, solid Scarlet Aeonia in her arena. If the player has the Unalloyed Gold Needle after completing Millicent's questline, it can be given to the Aeonia to receive Miquella's Needle and a Somber Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone.
Millicent and her four sisters are descended from Malenia in some way, but more as offshoots, or buds, of her Scarlet Bloom rather than actual daughters. Millicent seeks to return Malenia's sense of dignity.
They will be reborn as Malenia's Scarlet Valkyries if their deaths coincide with a great betrayal.
Malenia and Miquella are together known as the "twin prodigies" (天賦の双子, Tenpu no Futago).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In, this character was also known as Arbitress Malenia and Malenia, the Red Queen.
Malenia has unused dialogue.
Malenia, Blade of Miquella delivered a different line upon killing the player in.
Malenia has an alternative intro cutscene that was cut before release. Miquella was present in the tree, and Malenia calls the player her companion, indicating a cut third ending to Millicent's questline in which Malenia's pride is restored.

name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
description: Maliketh, the Black Blade is a boss in, encountered in Crumbling Farum Azula. This is not an optional boss as Maliketh must be defeated to unlock Leyndell, Ashen Capital and reach the endgame of Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Moveset:

Phase 1 - Beast Clergyman:
Phase 1 is much like combat against Gurranq. During this phase, the Beast Clergyman will make use of his Cinquedea as well as a variety of bestial incantations. His attacks are very fast, leaving few obvious spaces for the player to attack. He may use an earthquake attack, causing area of effect damage in a small circle around him. 

Phase 2 - Maliketh, the Black Blade:
At half health, a cutscene will play and phase 2 will begin. Maliketh now wields his Black Blade, and all of his attacks will cause rapid health loss overtime as well as temporary reduction of maximum health. Maliketh is a fast and acrobatic fighter, relying on quick slashes, spins and leaps. He will sometimes jump up and cling to the pillars around the arena, before either jumping at the player or jumping away and firing a ranged attack.

During this phase, the Blasphemous Claw can be used to deflect Maliketh's Black Blade attack, as well as the spin attack he performs after plunging his sword into the ground. Deflecting his attacks will stun him for a few seconds, creating a window during which to attack.

Environment:
The arena is a wide, circular room. It is possible to fall off the edges all around the perimeter of the room. There are several pillars around the centre of the room, which Maliketh may jump onto to perform certain attacks. These pillars can also be used to create distance between oneself and Maliketh, or to avoid his ranged attacks.

sections.body:
The area features pillars with the mummies of immured lupine beastmen. Much of its crumbling architecture floats as if frozen in time.
The young girl in the scene is presumed to be the first vessel for the Elden Ring and the God of Placidusax, confirming the old legends that claimed wolves were the first shadowbound Beasts. The statues have long muzzles like Red Wolves who serve Radagon, though they most resembled Azula Beastmen in their concept art.
The old Elden Ring strongly resembles the root-like tail of the Elden Beast.

name: Margit, the Fell Omen
description: Margit the Fell Omen is a boss in.

sections.heading: Encounters
sections.body:
Limgrave | (Castleward Tunnel)

As the Tarnished approaches the gates of Stormveil Castle, Margit will materialize on a nearby tower and jump down the courtyard to confront his opponent. This encounter will not take place if Morgott, the Omen King is defeated beforehand. 

Altus Plateau | (Outer Wall Battleground)

As the Tarnished treks through the Capital Outskirts, Margit will possess the body of a nearby Commoner to once again hunt down his enemy. This encounter does not count as a boss fight, and it is possible to run away when he appears.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Sorcerer Rogier is available as a summon for this fight.
Moveset:

Phase 1:
Margit is quick and relentless, his powerful combos and rapid follow-ups make it hard to find a window to punish him, but there are two types of attacks that leave him open amply: overhead strikes and ground stabs.

Since both can be easily evaded by running to the right, the key to victory is learning how to bait out these moves, which is generally done by dodging away from the first part of a combo, while remaining just in range for him to keep going through with it fully.

His jumping stab can also be exploited, as he always tells this move by tossing his holy dagger twice, while the player is far way: as he finishes throwing his weapons, walk towards him and dodge through the jump attack.

Without being particularly weak to anything, he still takes some additional damage from slashing and fire attacks, and he can also be poisoned and bled, which makes the Uchigatana a particularly favorable choice against this boss.

While standard light attacks won't impact him much, an aggressive playstyle made of jump attacks, charged attacks and Ash of War will see Margit repeatedly falling on his knees, leaving him open to a critical strike.

Margit's Shackle can be used during this phase to temporarily stun him, opening him to attacks. This will not work in phase 2.

Phase 2:

As his health drops to 60% or below, he will enter Phase 2 always executing the same hammer sweep plus jumping strike.

Even with the addition of some new moves, the bait-and-punish strategy of Phase 1 is still applicable.

While the moves made with his holy weapons cannot be parried, the majority of his regular weapon attacks are susceptible to interruption.

Environment:
Margit's arena is a narrow and long pathway with chasms on each side. While the boss himself cannot fall to his death, the player must constantly reposition himself to avoid having their back against the wall or the brink.

The area is also filled with obstacles and while the weapons scattered through out can be broken by dodging into them, the wooden barricades might just get in the way of a safety roll.

One must also not overestimate the length of the arena, as Margit's gap-closing attacks are fast and cover a long distance.

Used when his health reaches 60% or below to signal the start of Phase 2.
Dodge away from the first attack and through the second, but beware of the shockwave
caused by the impact of the jump attack on the ground.
| colspan="2" |Summons his holy hammer and swings his weapon right to left, following it immediately
after with the hammer; if the player runs away, throws a leaping horizontal slash left to
right and ends with a ground stab.
Dodge or run backwards to bait the leaping slash, then dodge through it and run to the
right to counter the final thrust.
| colspan="2" |With his hand over his right shoulder, summons his holy swords and quickly launches in
an open-arm spinning slash, swinging up to five times.
Dodge away as soon as the sword appears and keep running backwards, ready to dodge
| colspan="2" |Rapidly summons his holy sword and stabs, following up with a sword slash left to right,
and concludes with a ground stab; may replace the first stab with a quick sword swing
Dodge away as soon as the sword appears and keep walking backwards, then run to the
| colspan="2" |Slashes diagonally left to right from over his shoulder, then performs a slow charged
Dodge the first attack to the left and the second to the right.

Margit is quick and relentless, his powerful combos and rapid follow-ups make it hard to find a window to punish him, but there are two types of attacks that leave him open amply: overhead strikes and ground stabs.

Since both can be easily evaded by running to the right, the key to victory is learning how to bait out these moves, which is generally done by dodging away from the first part of a combo, while remaining just in range for him to keep going through with it fully.

His jumping stab can also be exploited, as he always tells this move by tossing his holy dagger twice, while the player is far way: as he finishes throwing his weapons, walk towards him and dodge through the jump attack.

Without being particularly weak to anything, he still takes some additional damage from slashing and fire attacks, and he can also be poisoned and bled, which makes the Uchigatana a particularly favorable choice against this boss.

While standard light attacks won't impact him much, an aggressive playstyle made of jump attacks, charged attacks and Ash of War will see Margit repeatedly falling on his knees, leaving him open to a critical strike.
Margit's Shackle can be used during this phase to temporarily stun him, opening him to attacks. This will not work in phase 2.
As his health drops to 60% or below, he will enter Phase 2 always executing the same hammer sweep plus jumping strike.
Even with the addition of some new moves, the bait-and-punish strategy of Phase 1 is still applicable.
While the moves made with his holy weapons cannot be parried, the majority of his regular weapon attacks are susceptible to interruption.

Margit's arena is a narrow and long pathway with chasms on each side. While the boss himself cannot fall to his death, the player must constantly reposition himself to avoid having their back against the wall or the brink.
The area is also filled with obstacles and while the weapons scattered through out can be broken by dodging into them, the wooden barricades might just get in the way of a safety roll.
One must also not overestimate the length of the arena, as Margit's gap-closing attacks are fast and cover a long distance.

name: Maris, Fathom of Night
image: ERN Boss Maris, Fathom of Night (1.1).png
description: Maris, Fathom of Night, also known as the Augur and the Master of Bubbles, is a Nightlord boss in. Maris, Fathom of Night is the Nightlord fought on the final night of the Augur Expedition. It is highly mobile, though it is quite passive and typically floats beyond the reach of melee attackers. It rams foes at great speeds and splashes bouncing waves of spirit water. Maris has hypnotic powers that lull its foes into a deep and deadly slumber. Maris deals Physical and Magic damage, and its attacks may inflict Sleep. Its weakness is Lightning damage, which easily staggers it during certain attacks.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: Maris is a gelatinous invertebrate with an otherwise featureless face that radiates a bright white light. Its elongated, blue body contains a network of constellations. It is wrapped in a transparent shroud like jellyfish’s exumbrella, lending a crustacean-like silhouette. It swims using flexible bilateral tentacles that end in green, fin-like structures. In its second phase, long dark green ribbons unfurl behind it, trailing like strands of drifting seaweed.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Like the Elden Beast, the Augur was an ancient stellar being that drifted through the skies. It camouflaged itself by transforming its surroundings into a vast ocean and blending with local lifeforms. For eons, it wandered the cosmos in a dream-like trance—until it encountered the immense and lonesome Night. For the first time, its curiosity stirred.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Maris, Fathom of Night deals Standard damage, Magic damage, and inflicts Sleep.
This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its stance is broken.
Maris creates additonal enemies throughout the fight that function like environmental hazards. It summons plants with long, flexible stalks and swarms of volatile violet Spirit Jellyfish that chase down Nightfarers and explode in Mists of Slumber. During phase two, Maris drops atomic slumber bombs. All these entities are targetable, and may be destroyed with sufficient damage. They release projectiles that chase after and damage Maris.

sections.heading: Resistances
sections.body:
Damage Types 
+0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.
A positive value indicates bonus damage. 
A negative value indicates that a boss is resistant to the damage type. 

Resistances 
A lower value indicates faster procs of the applicable status effect. 
The symbol denotes full immunity to the status effect. 

Moveset:

Augur Raid:
The Augur is a lesser version of this boss encountered during the Giant Bubbles raid in Limveld. It spawns bubbles around the map. Entering one transports the player directly to the Augur. It is more passive and uses a limited moveset. Defeating Augur yields 50,000 runes and grants the Unifying Fate boon, which causes the Flask of Crimson Tears to also restore FP.

Everdark Sovereign:
Everdark Maris spawns in as Phase 1
Defeat Phase 1 and loot a legendary Dormant Power containing the Nightfarers' starting weapon with the Storm Ruler Skill.
Maris respawns as Phase 3
Now vast, Maris floats out of reach of most attacks and no longer spawns minions; the Storm Ruler is almost required.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
Maris, Fathom of Night may initiate the encounter by slamming its tentacles to produce wide, sweeping waves that bounce like Fire Spritestones. The waves are best avoided by rolling into them, rather than backward or to the side. Depending on character height and the amplitude of the wave, dodge rolling may not even be necessary. When Maris executes a spiraling water rush, players can similarly evade by rolling into the boss as it charges forward. On occasion, Maris generates a localized cyclone; players should disengage until the vortex dissipates before resuming offense.

Maris periodically delivers swarms of jellyfish that pursue players before detonating. These can be destroyed from range or deliberately triggered near Maris to inflict damage on the boss. Maris also summons ground-based stalks from below. These plants are similar to Spirit Eels, and attack by flailing their bodies like tentacles. These can be evaded through repositioning or neutralized directly, as they are easily destroyed. They also deal damage after being destroyed.

Maris makes a siren noise, retreats and lands and curls into a suspended sphere to channel a hypnotic incantation that rapidly induces Sleep buildup. This move applies to the entire arena and cannot be avoided. Therefore, this move must be interrupted immediately by closing distance and applying pressure. Lightning-based attacks are particularly effective at disrupting the channel and avoiding Sleep accumulation.

At approximately half health, Maris enters its second phase, becoming significantly more aggressive. It summons larger swarms of explosive jellyfish, which may be countered through the same methods as before. Additionally, it releases large luminous droplets that descend from above and explode on impact, applying Sleep buildup. These can be intercepted before contact using ranged attacks or avoided entirely by sprinting beyond the blast radius. Despite the increased intensity, most attacks remain heavily telegraphed, allowing skilled players to time evasive maneuvers and counterattacks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The plants, jellyfish, and teardrop are coded like NPCs.
Plants and Jellyfish defeated by the Nightfarers release bubbles that chase and damage Maris. Destroying the slow-falling bombs releases larger bubbles that deal considerably more damage.
Maris is a mother because it births the Jellyfish.
Maris, the Master of Bubbles, may be related to the lost oracles of the Ancient Dynasty sought by Claymen.
The teardrop does not pass through player; players can balance them on their heads, delaying their detonation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: AbstractExistence.
An augur was a priest that practiced augury, the interpretation of the will of the gods by studying events observed within a predetermined sacred space (templum). The templum corresponded to the heavenly space above.
Like Metyr, Mother of Fingers and the Elden Beast, Maris, Fathom of Night is among the oldest entities in the universe.
Furthermore, Maris and the Elden Beast share a few similarities:
Transparent skin.
Glowing head.
Aquatic traits.
Sound emitted.
Among aquatic life, Maris appears to draw more inspiration from jellyfish in particular.
Because of said jellyfish inspiration, and the start of its Everdark fight involving a lesser Augur, it is inferred that Maris is not a singular entity, but several offshoots of the same being.
Unlike the other Everdark Sovereigns, Maris' fight does not begin from the base fight's second phase.
The Storm Ruler mechanic of Maris' Everdark fight calls back to the Demon's Souls series.

Localization:
Its Japanese title, 夜の深海, translates into "Deep Sea of Night".

name: Melina
description: Melina is a deuteragonist character in. She is a mysterious, spectral woman who offers an alliance with the Tarnished to help them on their journey to become Elden Lord. She may only be encountered when resting at specific Sites of Grace, though she may be summoned to help fight Morgott, the Omen King at the Elden Throne.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Melina has long observed the Lands Between. She was born at the foot of the Erdtree. She is a secret child of Queen Marika. Unlike Messmer or Morgott, Melina does not recall Marika with fondness.

At some point long ago, Melina bore a vision of fire. She was burned, leaving her bodiless; a drifting spirit bound to Grace.. Like her brother Messmer, she was assigned a purpose by Marika. However, she was unable to remember it. And so, Melina traveled with the spectral steed Torrent in search of the Tarnished who would lead her back to the foot of the Erdtree. There, she may ascertain her given purpose.

Game events:

Torrent identifies and selects a maidenless Tarnished, who recently washed up in the Stranded Graveyard, as one capable of brandishing the Elden Ring. Melina descends the spectral steed to grant the fallen champion a set of Sacred Flasks, choosing to aid them in violation of the Golden Order.

Sometime later, Melina approaches the Tarnished to offer them an accord: She could play the role of the missing Finger Maiden in return for a ride to the foot of the Erdtree. If the player desires the strength of runes, and, if they accept the accord, Melina entrusts them with the Spectral Steed Whistle and, therefore, Torrent. Melina advises them to follow the guidance of Grace and seek the shardbearer at Stormveil Castle.

Once the Tarnished defeats the demigod, Melina confesses that she was testing the Tarnished to see if they truly possessed the guidance of grace and if they were fit for the challenges to come. Satisfied with her new companion, Melina offers to take them to Roundtable Hold, a gathering place for Tarnished champions.

Throughout their journey, Melina also provides specks of guidance at certain sites of grace and, at churches dedicated to Queen Marika, she offers to reveal words spoken by Marika herself in the distant past.

Leyndell, Royal Capital:

Upon arriving at their destination, the Royal Capital at the foot of the Erdtree, Melina thanks the Tarnished for escorting her and leaves to ascertain her purpose, claiming that she can govern her movement more freely there. She entrusts the power of runes and Torrent to the Tarnished. She will also offer her aid should the Tarnished challenge Morgott, the Omen King, ruler of Leyndell and guardian of the Erdtree.

After defeating Morgott, the Tarnished finds the path into the Erdtree barred by impenetrable thorns refusing entrance to all. Melina, having ascertained her purpose and seeing the Tarnished stuck, rejoins the Tarnished to say that she can burn the Erdtree to gain entrance inside, provided that she can get ahold of the Giants' Flame. And hence, she asks to go on a new journey, this time to the flame of ruin, far above the clouds, upon the snowy Mountaintops of the Giants. and tells them she will take care of the "kindling" required to set the tree alight.

Defeating Morgott also unseals a path to the Three Fingers. If the Tarnished rests at the nearest grace from their entombment, Melina will warn against meeting them and insist against inheriting the Frenzied Flame, for it would end all lives and births, which she cherishes. If the Tarnished heeds her warning, Melina and the protagonist will continue their journey for the flame of ruin.

Cardinal Sin:

When making their way to the Forge of the Giants, Melina clarifies that she is now acting of her own volition, regardless of the purpose that her mother gave her. After defeating the guardian of the flame, Melina puts her plan into action. She takes the Tarnished's hand, narcotizing them by doing so, and proceeds to sacrifice herself to channel the flame of ruin, setting the Erdtree aflame. The Tarnished, maidenless once more, wakes up at Crumbling Farum Azula. There, they must confront the Black Blade Maliketh and recover the Rune of Death. In this, Melina fulfills her purpose: "The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death."

Destined Death:

If the player ignores her warnings at the Frenzied Flame Proscription, or just inherits the Frenzied Flame without speaking with her, she will say that The Tarnished is no longer fit, ending her accord, and forever leaving their side but threatening to kill them should they become the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

If Melina did not fulfil her purpose as Kindling Maiden, an additional cutscene will play after the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending. At the Stone Platform, a chorus of whistling guides a transformed Melina to the Spectral Steed Whistle. She retrieves the smoldering ring from a pile of ash and holds it in her open palm. As Torrent's final remnants are consumed by the Frenzied Flame, Melina reveals her unsealed left eye and vows vengeance upon the player in the form of Destined Death.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Summon sign:

Equipment:

sections.heading: Questline progression
sections.body:
Melina's questline runs parallel to the main story and is required to complete the game. It has two possible outcomes.
Stranded Graveyard
After fighting the Grafted Scion at the Chapel of Anticipation, Melina and Torrent appear during a cutscene. Melina grants the Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears before departing.
Sites of Grace (Limgrave)
After leaving the Stranded Graveyard, activate and rest at either the Agheel Lake North or Gatefront Ruins Sites of Grace. A cutscene will play and Melina will offer an accord.
Alternatively, activate at any two Sites of Grace in the overworld and then rest at one of the following eight Sites of Grace: Agheel Lake North, Agheel Lake South, Bridge of Sacrifice, Church of Elleh, Gatefront Ruins, Seaside Ruins, Stormhill Shack, or Third Church of Marika.
(Optional) If you refuse her accord, you cannot enter Leyndell, Royal Capital, even with two Great Runes. You can reconsider at any time by selecting "Talk to Melina" at any Site of Grace.
Accepting grants the Spectral Steed Whistle, allowing you to summon Torrent.
(Optional) Sites of Grace
Melina may appear when you rest at any Site of Grace, offering the dialogue options "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal".
Note: these options will no longer be available once you progress to the next step.
Melina offers to share the words of Queen Marika when the player rests at one of the following Sites of Grace: Church of Pilgrimage, First Church of Marika, Grand Lift of Dectus, Minor Erdtree Church, Outer Wall Battleground, Queen's Bedchamber, and Third Church of Marika. Select "Talk to Melina" and accept to hear them.
Sites of Grace
Rest at any Site of Grace outside Limgrave or fight Margit, the Fell Omen at least once to trigger another conversation in which Melina extends an invitation to the Roundtable Hold. Accepting this invite is mandatory for accessing Leyndell, Royal Capital later in the game.
(Optional) Sites of Grace
After progressing Boc the Seamster's questline, Melina may appear to discuss him.
If Boc moves to the East Raya Lucaria Gate, Melina will appear there to ask about him.
If Boc moves to the Altus Highway Junction, Melina will appear there to ask about him again.
(Optional) Sites of Grace (Altus Plateau or Capital Outskirts)
Speak to Melina at any Site of Grace on the Altus Plateau or in the Capital Outskirts. This step is missed if the player enters Leyndell, Royal Capital.
Leyndell, Royal Capital
Resting at a Site of Grace in Leyndell will trigger another interaction with Melina, after which she will leave you. Her dialogue options at various Sites of Grace will be temporarily unavailable.
Defeat Morgott, the Omen King.
(Optional) Melina may be summoned as a cooperator by activating her summon sign outside Morgott's boss room.
Approach the entrance to the Erdtree, turn back, and rest at the Elden Throne Site of Grace. Melina will appear and, after some dialogue, give you the Rold Medallion.
(Ending A) Mountaintops of the Giants
After defeating the Fire Giant and resting at the Forge of the Giants, you may talk to Melina. Speak to her and respond "I'm Ready" to commit the cardinal sin. Melina awakens the Giants' Flame, becomes its kindling, and burns the Erdtree. The player collapses and awakens in Crumbling Farum Azula.
Note: this ends Melina's questline, as her spirit. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.
(Ending B) Frenzied Flame Proscription
Visit the Frenzied Flame Proscription and interact with the Three Fingers. Melina will appear at the next Site of Grace you rest and will leave you permanently.
Note: this action cannot be reversed by using Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows or inserting Miquella's Needle at Dragonlord Placidusax. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.
Note: you will gain the option "Listen to the flames" when resting at the Forge of the Giants Site of Grace, allowing progression to Crumbling Farum Azula. This unlocks an additional cutscene in the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Melina uses the Black Knife Assassin animation set.
Attacks that produce lingering hazards can hit Melina when she sits at a Site of Grace, even applying Status Effects.
Melina is a child of Marika and has access to her most secret incantation.
This incantation will also be automatically cast when she dies, even as a cooperator, the only way to see this in-game without modding. 
Melina can be summoned to help fight against Morgott.
Melina wields the Blade of Calling, which is golden flame counterpart to the Black Knife. Additionally, she uses two unplayable incantations that resemble the effects of Minor Erdtree and Miranda's Prayer. 
Melina is not a Finger Maiden.
Melina is aware her agency will be restored if the Erdtree is destroyed.
If the player spares Melina and chooses the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending, she will be transformed after Marika and the Erdtree are destroyed.
Melina's purpose remains the same, but its context becomes flipped: "The one who walks alongside flame, Shall one day meet the road of Destined Death."

Speculation:
It is implied that Melina is another child of Radagon and Marika:
Naming Convention: Most siblings in the Lands Between share the first letter of their name. Messmer/Melina/Miquella/Malenia would be no exception to this rule.
Hair Color: Melina's hair color seems to be a combination of Radagon and Marika's hair colors.
Butterflies: There are four butterfly items in-game, each representing a cursed demigod: Nascent Butterfly (Miquella), Aeonian Butterfly (Malenia), Black Pyrefly (Messmer), Smoldering Butterfly (Melina).
Messmer had a younger sister who also bore a vision of fire and, like Melina, he possessed the kindling to burn the Erdtree It is unknown when in the timeline Melina was born exactly, but she knew Marika's secret incantation and Messmer was the older brother of Radahn.
The soundtrack for Messmer's boss fight shares a leitmotif with Radagon's boss theme.
Melina has an implied connection to the Gloam-Eyed Queen as she reveals her eye with a violet iris and inherits the power of Destined Death should the player spare her by using the Frenzied Flame as kindling.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Melina is internally named "MaricaOfDaughter" (ID: 2180).
There are several lines of Melina's dialogue that can be heard in pre-launch game trailers that end up not being used in the main game. Whether they were envisioned as Melina's own words or spoken echoes of Queen Marika is not known.
The Tarnished will soon return... guided by grace once lost.
The Golden Order is broken to its core.
They will fight. And they will die. In an unending curse.
For how else is champion, or a lord, to be born?
Brandish the Elden Ring... for all of us.

questline: Melina's questline runs parallel to the main story and is required to complete the game. It has two possible outcomes.
Stranded Graveyard
After fighting the Grafted Scion at the Chapel of Anticipation, Melina and Torrent appear during a cutscene. Melina grants the Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears before departing.
Sites of Grace (Limgrave)
After leaving the Stranded Graveyard, activate and rest at either the Agheel Lake North or Gatefront Ruins Sites of Grace. A cutscene will play and Melina will offer an accord.

Alternatively, activate at any two Sites of Grace in the overworld and then rest at one of the following eight Sites of Grace: Agheel Lake North, Agheel Lake South, Bridge of Sacrifice, Church of Elleh, Gatefront Ruins, Seaside Ruins, Stormhill Shack, or Third Church of Marika.
(Optional) If you refuse her accord, you cannot enter Leyndell, Royal Capital, even with two Great Runes. You can reconsider at any time by selecting "Talk to Melina" at any Site of Grace.
Accepting grants the Spectral Steed Whistle, allowing you to summon Torrent.
(Optional) Sites of Grace
Melina may appear when you rest at any Site of Grace, offering the dialogue options "The Rays of Grace" and "Melina's Goal".
Note: these options will no longer be available once you progress to the next step.

Melina offers to share the words of Queen Marika when the player rests at one of the following Sites of Grace: Church of Pilgrimage, First Church of Marika, Grand Lift of Dectus, Minor Erdtree Church, Outer Wall Battleground, Queen's Bedchamber, and Third Church of Marika. Select "Talk to Melina" and accept to hear them.
Sites of Grace

Rest at any Site of Grace outside Limgrave or fight Margit, the Fell Omen at least once to trigger another conversation in which Melina extends an invitation to the Roundtable Hold. Accepting this invite is mandatory for accessing Leyndell, Royal Capital later in the game.
(Optional) Sites of Grace
After progressing Boc the Seamster's questline, Melina may appear to discuss him.
If Boc moves to the East Raya Lucaria Gate, Melina will appear there to ask about him.
If Boc moves to the Altus Highway Junction, Melina will appear there to ask about him again.
(Optional) Sites of Grace (Altus Plateau or Capital Outskirts)
Speak to Melina at any Site of Grace on the Altus Plateau or in the Capital Outskirts. This step is missed if the player enters Leyndell, Royal Capital.
Leyndell, Royal Capital
Resting at a Site of Grace in Leyndell will trigger another interaction with Melina, after which she will leave you. Her dialogue options at various Sites of Grace will be temporarily unavailable.
Defeat Morgott, the Omen King.
(Optional) Melina may be summoned as a cooperator by activating her summon sign outside Morgott's boss room.
Approach the entrance to the Erdtree, turn back, and rest at the Elden Throne Site of Grace. Melina will appear and, after some dialogue, give you the Rold Medallion.
(Ending A) Mountaintops of the Giants

After defeating the Fire Giant and resting at the Forge of the Giants, you may talk to Melina. Speak to her and respond "I'm Ready" to commit the cardinal sin. Melina awakens the Giants' Flame, becomes its kindling, and burns the Erdtree. The player collapses and awakens in Crumbling Farum Azula.
Note: this ends Melina's questline, as her spirit. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.
(Ending B) Frenzied Flame Proscription
Visit the Frenzied Flame Proscription and interact with the Three Fingers. Melina will appear at the next Site of Grace you rest and will leave you permanently.

Note: this action cannot be reversed by using Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows or inserting Miquella's Needle at Dragonlord Placidusax. You will not be able to hear any dialogue you may have missed.

Note: you will gain the option "Listen to the flames" when resting at the Forge of the Giants Site of Grace, allowing progression to Crumbling Farum Azula. This unlocks an additional cutscene in the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: RedEyeGypsy
Merchant Kalé was among the earliest characters added to the game and has a substantial amount of cut content. Although he underwent multiple iterations before release, his personality, mannerisms, and association with Frenzied Flame were established from the start.

Great Caravan:
Merchant Kalé had a full questline in which he actively searched for the lost Great Caravan. After acquiring the Burial Crow's Letter, his journey would have brought him to the Frenzied Flame Proscription, where he expressed tremendous anger toward the people of the Erdtree for what they did to his ancestors. Kalé then attempted to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame, but failed and was burned by the Three Fingers.
This questline may have been replaced or cut to avoid conflict with Lightseeker Hyetta's questline, as both arrived at the Frenzied Flame Proscription after directing the player to seek the Three Fingers.

Cursed Red Eyes:
In his earliest known draft, Kalé and the Nomadic Merchants were conceived as a single being divided into many bodies. They bore the cursed red eyes, an early version of the Frenzied Flame that threatened to blend them back together.
This version of Kalé and his brothers actively rode their mules and roamed the map, much like the Great Coffins pulled by Trolls.
The brothers were telepathically linked and dreamed together, but yearned to extinguish the flame and separate.
Kalé gave the player St. Trina's Crystal Ball, buying any collected Dream Mist, which staved off their curse. 
St. Trina once becalmed the entombed Nomads with a lullaby, now played by Nomadic Merchants to calm themselves. Trina's cessation implies the Miquella-Trina abduction concept existed in early development.
In the final version of the game, Miquella's Needle serves as the means to quell the Frenzied Flame.
Frenzied Flame melted away that which divided and distinguished at this stage of development.
Killing Merchant Kalé or any of his brothers triggered Redeemer Guilbert to invade the player at several locations in Limgrave (then Tenebrae).
Kalé sold Note: Redeemers.

name: Messmer the Impaler
description: Messmer the Impaler (串刺し公、メスメル, Kushizashi Kō, Mesumeru), later known as Base Serpent Messmer (邪な蛇、メスメル, Yokoshimana Hebi, Mesumeru), is a mandatory remembrance boss in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Messmer was born to Queen Marika the Eternal prior to the Second Liurnian War. His birth was cursed by a dark entity, an evil serpent coiled within that threatened to subsume him. Known to Messmer as the Abyssal Serpent, this force was restrained only through Marika's intervention—she removed her son's right eye and replaced it with a seal of her Grace. Ever since his accursed birth, Messmer was in constant company of the winged serpents, friends who suppressed the base serpent.

Much like his younger sister, Messmer bore a vision of fire. and he despised the flame inside himself, and time and time again hoped to rid himself of it, but found that it ever burned. 

At some point, Messmer befriended Commander Gaius, an Albinauric who, like him, was cursed from birth and akin to an older brother to General Radahn, Gaius' fellow student in the art of gravitational sorcery. Gaius would go on to command Messmer's armies during the crusade.

The Crusade:

Toward the end of the Age of Plenty, Messmer was charged by his mother with carrying out a purge of the tower-dwelling hornsent of the Land of Shadow, who did not bear the light of grace. At some point during his Crusade, Messmer was abandoned in the Land of Shadow, but continued to zealously enforce the purge even though Marika used him as a scapegoat and ceased all contact with him. Messmer came to reside in a fort known as the Shadow Keep.

Key in his army were the Black Knights, commanded by Black Knight Commander Andreas and his son and second-in-command Black Knight Captain Huw. Although they remained devoutly loyal to Messmer despite his abandonment by Marika, they ultimately rebelled upon learning of his serpentine nature. The pair were imprisoned in an underground tomb, and despite his betrayal, Messmer mourned the loss of Huw, whom he had considered a brother-in-arms. His Fire Knights would also refuse to follow the orders of burning the Ancient Ruins of Rauh and the destruction of the specimens in the Specimen Storehouse.

Eventually, an intruder invaded Messmer's stronghold, the Shadow Keep, and was noticed by the demigod's serpents, who identified them as a Tarnished Champion and a pretender to the title of Elden Lord. Though surprised that a Tarnished had come to the Land of Shadow, Messmer nonetheless attacked them to continue enforcing the purge. However, the serpentine demigod struggled overcome the Tarnished. Unwilling to accept "a Lord devoid of light" and desperate to regain the upper hand, Messmer ripped out Marika's seal and unleashed the power of the Abyssal Serpent, allowing him to frequently transform into a massive serpent. Nonetheless, the Tarnished was able to land a fatal blow upon Messmer. Realizing that his mother had indeed forsaken him, Messmer used his dying breath to curse Marika.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Hornsent can be summoned for this boss. His summon sign is found inside of the boss room, and will appear if the player decides to side with him against Leda or ignore this part of Leda's quest.

Phase One:
The attacks of Messmer the Impaler are imbued with fire damage, making him a formidable opponent who relies heavily on his spear's reach and agility. To proceed in this boss fight, readiness for his swift movements is important. When fighting Messmer at a close range, you will have more chances of retaliating and chipping away at his health while he recovers. Engaging Messmer patiently is the best strategy to effectively take him down. When he finishes a string of attacks, focus on breaking his poise by pulling off heavy attacks for a chance to deal significant damage.

Because of his speed, Messmer can quickly transition between offense and defense by quickly disengaging with a leap after he finishes a move. Be aware that Messmer counters swiftly after sustaining damage, too. As his speed and precision in combat are his biggest asset, observation is required to avoid being overwhelmed. Once Messmer's health is half-depleted, a cutscene will trigger, which will start Messmer's second phase.

Phase Two:
During the second phase, Base Serpent Messmer remains at 50% HP and not only retains his original attacks, but also introduces a set of new and more lethal attacks with the help of the Abyssal Serpent. Among the fresh additions to his move set is the ability to transform into a large red serpent that rises up to the ground to throw a fireball or do bite attacks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Messmer was likely born earlier than the other Demigods. Exactly when he was born remains unknown, as all mention of him was erased by his mother after she abandoned him in the Land of Shadow.
He is older than Radahn, who was born before Miquella, Malenia, Trina, and Ranni.
Although not explicitly stated, Messmer is strongly implied to be an Empyrean child of Marika and Radagon, born of a single god.
Messmer has the red hair of Radagon and his children.
Messmer was cursed at birth by a threat to Marika's power.
Radagon's motif in The Final Battle is echoed in the soundtrack for Messmer's boss fight, Messmer the Impaler.
Messmer is linked to Black Pyreflies, one of four butterflies found in-game, two of which are associated with Empyreans born from a single god. The Smoldering Butterflies correspond with Melina.
Seals are placed on his eyes.
Messmer is the elder brother of Melina, as both she and his younger sister were daughters of Marika with visions of fire.
Melina serves as kindling to burn the Erdtree, and Messmer's Kindling can burn the Sealing Tree.
Melina, who has a corresponding butterfly and faded red hair, must also be an Empyrean child of Marika-Radagon because the game makes the distinction that Messmer and Radahn, his half-brother, are not brothers; Messmer acted like an elder brother to Radahn, but was not one.
Upon his defeat, Messmer denounces Marika and curses her with his dying breath. This is the only time he refers to his mother by name.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Messmer's name may be a nod to German physician Franz Mesmer, who theorized about the existence of "animal magnetism" (a universal, invisible force or "magnetic fluid" that he supposed connected all living things and was capable of curing diseases, later referred to as mesmerism). Mesmerism would eventually come to be associated with hypnosis and is today considered a synonym for the former (with the term "mesmerizing" coined after it).
Messmer's epithet is most likely inspired by Vlad III, commonly known as "Vlad the Impaler" (Romanian: Vlad Țepeș; rendered in Japanese as "串刺し公" (Kushizashi Kō)), who was one of the historical inspirations for Bram Stoker's novel Dracula. Like Vlad III, Messmer has a notable draconic motif: while "Dracula" means "son of the dragon" (Vlad's father was called Vlad Dracul), Messmer for his part wears a helm shaped like a dragon's head, dons armor resembling the Drake Knight set, and has a snake with dragon wings.
Messmer's visual design was likely inspired by the marble sculpture of Laocoön and His Sons, which depicts a pair of serpents winding circuitously around a priest and his sons, whose divine punishment for attempting to destroy the Trojan Horse and expose the trap is misinterpreted by the Trojans as proof that Laocoön was the real traitor and that the horse was trustworthy. This sculpture is famous for being one of the greatest examples of dynamic motion and emotion of its time.
Messmer has an unused voice line that would have played during the cinematic for his boss fight. He would have told the Tarnished, "Miquella spoke of thee..."

| colspan="2" |Leaps into the air and summons a fireball in hand before charging.
| colspan="2" |Will fly around while swinging his spear and suddenly stop to release a flurry of flaming spear attacks, ending with a spear slam to the ground.
| colspan="2" |Transforms into a big red serpent and slams a big fireball.

Another version is you can see him in the center of the pool of red liquid while three Serpent heads are visible. The Serpent heads will strike successively and after the third strike, Messmer will follow up with a Flaming Spear Lunge attack, where he flies up, pauses mid-air, and slams his spear onto the ground to create an explosive area around him.

The attacks of Messmer the Impaler are imbued with fire damage, making him a formidable opponent who relies heavily on his spear's reach and agility. To proceed in this boss fight, readiness for his swift movements is important. When fighting Messmer at a close range, you will have more chances of retaliating and chipping away at his health while he recovers. Engaging Messmer patiently is the best strategy to effectively take him down. When he finishes a string of attacks, focus on breaking his poise by pulling off heavy attacks for a chance to deal significant damage.

Because of his speed, Messmer can quickly transition between offense and defense by quickly disengaging with a leap after he finishes a move. Be aware that Messmer counters swiftly after sustaining damage, too. As his speed and precision in combat are his biggest asset, observation is required to avoid being overwhelmed. Once Messmer's health is half-depleted, a cutscene will trigger, which will start Messmer's second phase.

During the second phase, Base Serpent Messmer remains at 50% HP and not only retains his original attacks, but also introduces a set of new and more lethal attacks with the help of the Abyssal Serpent. Among the fresh additions to his move set is the ability to transform into a large red serpent that rises up to the ground to throw a fireball or do bite attacks.

name: Messmerfire
description: Messmerfire or Messmer's Flame (メスメルの火, Mesumeru no Hi), also known as Messmer's Kindling (メスメルの種火, Mesumeru no Tanebi), is an inextinguishable dark-red flame that is strongly associated with Messmer the Impaler and his Fire Knights. It holds the destructive power of burning the sealing tree that blocks the entrance to Enir-Ilim, where the mysterious Gate of Divinity is located.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Long ago, the demigod Messmer the Impaler was born with a dark flame that burned within him and is being eaten away at by a wicked and malevolent serpent called the Base Serpent whose essence stirred within his body. Messmer despises his own flame and often tried to rid himself of it again and again only to discover his folly; his flame will forever burn.

Later, Messmer's mother Marika, sends her son on an endless Crusade against the Hornsent, the tower-dwelling people inhabiting the Realm of Shadow, as they do not possess Marika's grace. During the Crusade, Messmer and his army cleansed the realm with fire, destroying everything in their path and putting them to the torch. This caused the surviving Hornsent to develop a strong hatred of Messmer and his followers to the point where they began to seek out vengeance for their betrayal.

name: Metyr, Mother of Fingers
description: Metyr, Mother of Fingers is an optional Remembrance Boss in, introduced in the expansion.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Metyr, the brilliant daughter of the Greater Will, was the first of all stars to fall upon the Lands Between. She possessed a microcosm which allowed her to receive messages from the Greater Will. Metyr gave birth to the Two Fingers that guided the empyreans and the Tarnished.

Long ago, Metyr was damaged and her Ringed Finger was removed. She would never again receive a signal from the Greater Will. The wisdom received by the Two Fingers was severed, and Metyr began birthing the aberrant Fingercreepers. Metyr concealed herself within the Finger Ruins of Miyr, below the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, and waited for an eternity in vain for another signal from her lord.

Although Metyr was broken, her Two Fingers continued guiding the empyreans without a word from the Greater Will. It is said they presided over the birth of Marika’s Erdtree as she created it from the primordial matter of the Crucible.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Metyr is a monstrous being made from fingers. Her head resembles an elongated thumb, and her face a pronounced thumbprint. At its center is a small, wart-like eye from which she blasts pink energy beams. Ridge-like wrinkles, forming fingerprint-like patterns, cover Metyr's head and neck. She moves about on four sets of four-fingered hands, 16 coordinated finger legs in total. Metyr has two long-reaching arms that terminate in four-fingered hands tipped with sharp nails painted red. She may use these to pry open her abdominal cavity when birthing new Fingercreepers. Her tail forks into two tail fingers which wrap each other like a spiral. Between them rests an orb containing a microcosm.

Metyr's body festers with unhealed wounds. Upon her right chest is a deep laceration, and her belly has been split wide open, revealing gore and the stillborn remains of malformed fingers. Several more protrude from large lesions on her neck and tail fingers, and her microcosm appears clouded like an eye with cataracts. The iris of her bloodshot eye is quartered into a quatrefoil.

To reach it, the player must ring the two hanging bells at the other Finger Ruins, return to the cathedral, examine Ymir's throne, and descend the newly revealed ladder to the ruins below. There, they must defeat Swordhand of Night Anna before ringing the final bell.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body:
Phase One:
Metyr crawls around and can fire a laser beam from her eye. Try fighting her head-on. She punishes flanking during this phase.

Phase Two:
Metyr summons her damaged microcosm and uses it to channel gravity magic. Be wary that she can fly during this stage, which can be troubling for some melee players.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Metyr is the only boss that does not fade away upon defeat, but instead disappears into the microcosm once held by her tail-fingers.
The Gazing Finger weapon is referred to as her head, but it should be noted that this item is made from a Remembrance.
The many fingers protruding from Metyr's wounds resemble Festering Bloody Fingers. There are several different models, but they typically only have one or two fingers.
Metyr's four-fingered hands each look like a pair of Two Fingers put together.
Metyr's pink, wart-like eye appears on Fingerprint Nostrums. 
Finger-Weavers like Count Ymir ingested this bean-shaped medicine to become fingers.
This phenomenon is similar to the Prince of Death's eyes, which appear in areas tainted by Deathroot.
The encounter with Metyr is foreshadowed by the Crimson and Cerulean Seed Talismans +1, which are obtained by ringing the finger bells at the Finger Ruins of Dheo and Rhea. Both talismans depict an orb held between a crux.
Metyr is not stated to be the mother of the Three Fingers.

Speculation:
The Nox of Nokron, Eternal City are strongly implied to have used the Fingerslayer Blade against Metyr.
The Ringed Finger was severed from the ancestor of Fingercreepers, which was Metyr. This item is hidden in the Gelmir Hero's Grave.
War Counselor Iji may have been involved in the attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Metyr is referred to as FingerNursery within the game files. Her microcosm, or special orb, is internally named Sun.
The soundtrack for the second phase of Metyr's fight is reminiscent of the first-ever recorded sound of a Black Hole.
Metyr is one of the few bosses to survive having their health depleted by the player. Others include Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, Morgott, the Omen King, and Gurranq, Beast Clergyman.

name: Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame
image: Shadow of the Erdtree promotional screenshot 11.jpg
description: Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame, also known as Sage Midra, is an optional boss.

sections.heading: Appearance
sections.body: A feeble man wearing a yellow or gold robe with a large clasp with green gems. A golden stake is driven through his eye that continues into his body. Its barbs emerge from his torso in the shape of an evergreen. He unseals the Frenzied Flame by removing the rod through his eye, decapitating himself to reveal a gazing fireball of Frenzied Flame. The barbs coil around the weapon to form his sword.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Pre-Phase:
You fight the feeble Lord. He is easily staggered and has low health compared to his actual fight, but can still prove dangerous with a scream AoE or grab attack if not dealt with quickly.
Phase One:
He pulls his head off and gets a fireball head of Frenzied Flame. He deals madness and swings at the player with his Greatsword, often with a mix of quick or delayed attacks.

Phase Two:
When Midra's health drops to about 65%, he will rise up above you and drop down for a massive explosion. After that, Midra will retain his original strings of attacks and will gain new ones that more frequently utilize madness.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Midra's wounds have stitches.
His brooch features green gems, indicating his need for Endurance.
Though Midra was able to endure the Unendurable Frenzy, he had not suffered enough to reach his fullest potential.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: KingOfChaos (IDs: 5050, 5051)
This boss is likely inspired by the "King in Yellow", a character created by Robert W. Chambers, appearing in his 1895 book of the same name as well as several short stories.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Summons an orb of Frenzied Flame that shoots out bolts of flame in front of the caster, dealing Fire damage equal to 75% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 30 Madness build-up per hit.

The caster suffers 6 Madness build-up 7 times per second, and any enemy within 5 meters of the orb takes 10 Madness build-up 2.5 times per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Inflicts a lot of Madness build-up on the caster, enough to fully inflict the status effect in less than 10 seconds, necessitating high amounts of Focus to use this spell effectively.
Madness build-up scales with the Arcane-scaling of the Dragon Communion Seal.
Damage is boosted by 20% per Frenzied Flame Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Very effective for keeping the damage boosts from Black Dumpling, Aged One's Exultation, and Madding Hand active during combat.
More effective when cast under foes that are large enough that the orb is summoned inside of them.
Drains FP much quicker when channeled than the additional cost of 5 would imply, as it drains 7 times per second (or 35 FP per seconds).
Can move when casting and can be cast while riding Torrent.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The summoned orb is similar to the orb that replaces The Tarnished's head during the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending.
Patch 1.14 increased attack speed, increased Frenzy status buildup range against enemies, decreased Frenzy status buildup when using this skill.
The self-Madness build-up was reduced from 7 build-up per tick to 6 build-up per tick.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Obtained from Millicent, after killing her, at almost any time after she equips the Valkyrie's Prosthesis given by the player.
The first location where she can be killed, and drop the talisman, is the Windmill Heights site of grace at Dominula, Windmill Village.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Increases Dexterity by 5 and also increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 4%/6%/11%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point. 

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hits towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive) also increasing the effect. 
These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land. 
For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive. 
For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count. 
Can be worn together with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia or the Winged Sword Insignia to stack the effect, but only the latter can be obtained in the same playthrough. 
Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy. 
An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice. 
This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

name: Millicent's Sisters
description:
Millicent's sisters are adopted daughters of Sage Gowry and siblings of Millicent. These red haired girls once sprouted as buds from the Scarlet Aeonia found within the heart of Caelid. They all wear the Traveler's Set and use weapons and skills associated with either aspects of their inadvertent mother Malenia, both her role as the unalloyed blade of Miquella and her looming transformation into the goddess of rot. They all seek to aid their adoptive father in cultivating Millicent into a Scarlet Valkyrie.
__TOC__

sections.heading: The Sisters
sections.body:
Polyanna, Youngest Sister=

Polyanna's Equipment:

Details:

Unlike her sisters Polyanna can be encountered long before the confrontation at Elphael. 

She can be summoned within the Swamp of Aeonia as a friendly cooperator against Commander O'Neil to help retrieving the snapped needle for Gowry. 

Her Summon sign can be found directly south of the Inner Aeonia site of grace, en-caved among the tall roots of the Aeonia flower that are erupting directly up from the ground.

Polyanna's Appearance:

Polyanna has a slender body, fair skin and the left half of her face is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

Her right eye is covered with a white eye-patch and her visible left eye reveal that they are slightly clouded with a golden-yellow iris and a darkened, near-black sclerae. 

She has faded orange-red hair tied into a bun at the back of her head, her forehead is covered with bangs that have been cut horizontally at the height of her eyebrows, along with thinner bangs on the sides reaching down to the height her chin.

Amy, Third Sister=

Amy's Equipment:

Amy's Appearance:

Amy has a slender body, fair skin and the upper half of her face from the top of her cheeks to her forehead, is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

She has small pursed lips and both of her eyes are covered with a white blindfold. Despite not being visible, her eyes share the same features as Polyanna. 

She has a faded orange-red, unkempt hair that reaches down to her shoulders, enveloping most of her whole head and even the right side of her face.

Maureen, Second Sister=

Maureen's Equipment:

Maureen's Appearance:

Maureen has a slender body, fair skin and the upper-left half of her face is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

Her left eye is covered with a white eye-patch and her visible right eye reveal that her sclerae is also darkened like her sisters however unlike them, her iris and pupils are almost completely clouded over. 

She has chin-length, curvaceous, faded orange-red hair covering most of her head. An opening revealing her face beginning on the right side of her forehead before curtaining out to the sides. where they eventually begin flowing back in towards the cheeks to then finally curve back outwards to the sides.

Mary, Eldest Sister=

Mary's Equipment:

Mary's Appearance:

Mary has a slender body, fair skin and the upper half of her face, from the top of her right cheek to the left-side top of her forehead is covered with a large, sickly birthmark.

She has both of her eyes are covered with a white blindfold. Despite not being visible, her eyes share the same features as Polyanna and Amy. 

She has long faded orange-red hair that reaches down to her collar bone, an opening beginning on the upper left side of her face before curtaining outwards into large fluffy bangs framing her face.

sections.heading: Tactics
sections.body:
Successfully assisting Millicent can be accomplished with relative ease even with a character that hasn't leveled any of their attributes or weapons yet, as Millicent herself is significantly more powerful than any of the sisters individually. Her damage is high but her health is relatively low, so Millicent's safety is at the most risk only when she's greatly outnumbered and the majority of her sisters are attacking her at once.

Due to Millicent's high damage (particularly from her Waterfowl Dance), the player can equip the Shabriri's Woe Talisman and/or any pieces of the Duelist Set or Rotten Duelist Set to make the majority of the sisters more easily prone to chase them around the environment, leaving Millicent to deal with a single sister one at a time.

]]
Since Polyanna can cast Pest Threads, she's the only one who can harm the running player from a distance and so it's preferable to leave her with Millicent first so she can eliminate Polyanna before she becomes a problem for the player.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Maureen's Treespear is unique and impossible to replicate by the player as it has Charge Forth. Instead the version the player has access to cannot be infused with Ashes of War and it has Sacred Order as it's default skill.
It's possible to infer that Millicent may be the fourth sister to sprout from the Heart of Aeonia due to the fact that Polyanna is still present in Caelid at the start of the questline while her older sisters are comparatively absent, due to them likely having a head start on their journey to the Haligtree as they would have been born earlier than both Millicent and Polyanna.
Since Malenia and Millicent can both blossom into giant flowers on death, it brings into question the large flower found in a chamber near the Haligtree Roots site of grace. It is unclear whether this is an earlier bloom from Malenia herself, as a copy of the Traveler's Set that can be found next to it may imply it is from one of the four sisters. However considering how much higher Gowry seems to value what Millicent's potential flower is likely going to be compared to her sisters, it may be from a sister we haven't heard of before.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Millicent's Sisters had different nameplates in: Amy, Third Daughter, Mary, Eldest Daughter, Maureen, Second Daughter, and Polyanna, Youngest Daughter.

Etymology:
Polyanna is derived from a combination of the names Polly (which in of itself has roots from the name Mary) and can mean "sea" and Anna (Derived from the Hebrew name Hannah, meaning "grace").
"Polyanna" has also been historically used as noun to describe an excessively cheerful or optimistic person. Stemming from the name of a character created by US writer of children's stories, Eleanor Hodgman Porter.
Amy stems from French and means "beloved" or "well-loved". It's derived from the Latin word "amare" which in of itself means "to love".
Maureen and Mary's names both stem from the same Hebrew name Miriam. It can translate to "drop of the sea", "bitterness", "beloved" and "wish for a child".
