name: Minor Erdtree (spell)
description: Minor Erdtree is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Scaduview
Found in Shaman Village, under a very, very small Minor Erdtree among a field of golden flowers. The path is guarded by a Tree Sentinel.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Creates a miniature Minor Erdtree at the caster's feet for 30 seconds. 

Caster and nearby allies are healed for 18 HP every 0.5 seconds (1070 HP total over the entire duration) as long as the effect remains active.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Area of effect is roughly 3-4 times larger than the visual effect, presumably due to the size of the spell's visual being changed before release (see trivia). 
Generally outclassed by other healing incantations such as Great Heal or Blessing's Boon, as those like the former heal immediately while those like the latter do not require characters to stay in a small area to be healed. 
Duration is NOT affected by the Old Lord's Talisman. 
Deals damage equal to 10 + 3% of their health to Revenants and Revenant Followers for every second they are in the effect radius of the spell. 
Compared to Warming Stones: same duration (30 seconds), more healing per second (effectively 36 HP per seconds vs 25 HP per seconds) and total healing (1070 HP vs 720 HP), costs more FP (30 FP vs 20 FP), and takes 70 Faith and 2 Spell slots instead of needing to be crafted. It also has the difference of not healing nearby enemies, unlike Warming Stones, and only 10 Warming Stones can be carried at a time. 
The comparison with Sunwarmth Stones is slightly closer as it increases slightly (30 HP per second, or 900 total HP over the duration), in exchange for taking slightly more FP to cast (24) and requiring more rare materials to craft. Duration and healing even enemies remain the same for Sunwarmth Stones.
Compared to Frenzyflame Stones: same duration (30 seconds), slightly more healing per second (effectively 36 HP per seconds vs 35 HP per seconds) and total healing (1070 HP vs 1050 HP), costs more FP (30 FP vs 15 FP), and takes 70 Faith and 2 Spell slots instead of needing to be crafted. The Frenzyflame Stones additionally only heal players that are attuned to the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.13 increased HP recovery amount.
Technically it lowered the amount of HP healed per tick, from 24 to 18, but since it also decreased the interval between heals from 1 second to 0.5 seconds the amount healed was effectively increased by 49%. 
A version of this spell that summons a significantly larger tree is used by Melina when summoned against Morgott, the Omen King.
The size of the summoned tree was greatly decreased from the preview of Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree, allegedly because its original size made it cause significant slowdown of the game when summoned. 
Has the second highest Faith requirement for an incantation, surpassed only by Light of Miquella.

name: Minor Erdtrees
description: Minor Erdtrees are Landmarks in.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: Gargantuan deciduous trees with dense canopies of golden leaves, visible from great distances. The bark of young Minor Erdtrees gives off a golden glow that apparently fades as they reach maturity.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Erdtree's offspring sprouted from its fabled Golden Seeds, scattered across the Lands Between when it sensed the end of its life for the first time.

Queen Marika the Eternal would plant developing Minor Erdtrees at the Minor Erdtree Church, where she would deliver a speech, demanding to abandon blind faith and declaring her intent of inquiring the depths of her Golden Order in an attempt to strengthen its grace through understanding. The order of the Erdtree Guardians would be established to protect the Erdtree's offspring through a pact with it. Talismans depicting the Erdtree seed, once believed as something that could not exist, were crafted to increase the powers of its blessed sap. Perfumers developed wondrous physicks using the crystal tears that were slowly collected in basins at the feet of the Minor Erdtrees. Catacombs for Erdtree Burial would be built close to Minor Erdtrees as their roots were once linked together with those of the Erdtree.

Upon the shattering of the Elden Ring, fearing its coming end again, the Erdtree would release new seeds that would start growing into Illusory Trees and deploy Erdtree Avatars to protect its already grown but withering offspring.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Crystalized Tears for the Flask of Wondrous Physick are commonly acquired at Minor Erdtrees.
Small collection basins are found at the base of most Minor Erdtrees. They collected hardened sap.
Teardrop Scarabs often linger near Minor Erdtrees.

name: Miquella of the Haligtree
description: Miquella the Kind, also known as Miquella of the Haligtree, Empyrean Miquella, and the Unalloyed, is a Remembrance Boss. He is an Empyrean and a son of Queen Marika the Eternal and King Consort Radagon. He is the older twin brother of Malenia, and together they are known as the Twin Prodigies (天賦の双子, Tenpu no Futago). His other self is St. Trina, whom he divested and cast into the depths of the Stone Coffin Fissure. He is encountered at the Gate of Divinity atop Enir-Ilim in the Realm of Shadow, where he fights alongside Radahn, Consort of Miquella.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Miquella and his twin sister were born with incurable afflictions, with Miquella's curse being perpetual youth. Miquella made a promise to Malenia and experimented tirelessly in an attempt to undo their curses. The twins were very close, and Malenia became Miquella's sworn blade and protector. Miquella was loved by many people and had a remarkable ability to compel affection from others. For this reason, many regarded him as the most fearsome Empyrean.

Just as his parents were two halves of the same person, Miquella also had another half—St. Trina—who held the power of Sleep. St. Trina was Miquella's fate, and she was his "love".

Miquella was chosen by his Two Fingers to become an Empyrean, destined to succeed Queen Marika. He was an adherent of Golden Order Fundamentalism, and developed new incantations as gifts to his father Radagon. However, Miquella abandoned Fundamentalism when it failed to treat Malenia's rot. He then began creating Unalloyed Gold, which he used it to craft needles that could ward away the meddling of outer gods and forestall Malenia's incurable rot. These needles could even be used to subdue the power of the Frenzied Flame. He also unsuccessfully sought a solution for his half-brother Godwyn's state of incomplete death.

The Haligtree:
 once cast powerful charms]]

At some point, Miquella started watering a sapling with his own blood in the hope that it would become a new Erdtree. The sapling was grown on top of the fortress of Elphael and became known as the Haligtree. Soldiers and Knights sworn to protect the Haligtree would use unalloyed gold to symbolize their loyalty and devotion to Miquella, wearing braided crowns made of the metal and creating shields embedded with it. 

Miquella was also said to favor the low and meek, and his Haligtree was intended to be the eventual salvation for the many. It became a hidden haven for the persecuted and the unwanted of the Lands Between, such as the Misbegotten and Albinaurics.

As Miquella pursued godhood, he knew that he would have to take a consort, to which his eyes fell upon his half-brother General Radahn, for he was strong but remained kind. He approached Radahn with his naive offer, to which the General vowed that he would become as such, in return for unspecified terms on Miquella and Malenia's behalf.

Malenia journeyed with her armies to Caelid to confront Radahn. The resulting Battle of Aeonia ended with Malenia unleashing her Scarlet Aeonia, whispering beforehand in Radahn's ear that "Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort." After using her last resort attack, Malenia entered a comatose state, and one of her knights took it upon herself to carry her leader's slumbering body back across the Lands Between to the Haligtree. Radahn had survived, albeit barely standing, and his mind was riddled by the Scarlet Rot. He was now little more than a howling beast aimlessly wandering the battlefield, devouring the corpses of friends and foes alike.

Following the Battle of Aeonia, Miquella embedded himself into the Haligtree to progress his ascension, but was kidnapped during his slumber. Another of Miquella's half-brothers was to blame: Mohg, who served an Outer God known as the Formless Mother. He took the sleeping Empyrean deep underground to the Mohgwyn Palace, where he aspired to raise Miquella to full godhood himself through blood offerings, and then to take on the role of Miquella's consort instead of Radahn, becoming the new monarch of a Mohgwyn Dynasty. Mohg urged his followers to render offerings of blood and drench Miquella's cocoon in order to facilitate his awakening.

Despite all of Mohg's efforts, Miquella remained completely unresponsive. At some point, Miquella had covertly placed an enchantment on Mohg, wishing to use the Omen to gain access to the Realm of Shadow. Sir Ansbach, a Pureblood Knight in service to Mohg, attempted to free his lord by challenging Miquella, only to succumb to an enchantment of his own.

Without Miquella's blood offerings, and Malenia no longer protected by her Unalloyed Gold Needle once she was returned, the Haligtree became a misshapen husk. slowly succumbing to the unmitigated Scarlet Rot. Malenia and the Haligtree's soliders desperately awaited Miquella's return to save their rotting home. 

The Realm of Shadow:

Making use of Mohg, Miquella entered the Realm of Shadow, the location of the Gate of Divinity. As Miquella traveled through the Realm of Shadow, he abandoned parts of himself, including his flesh, his eye, his doubt and vacillation, his love, and his fears. Golden Miquella's Crosses resembling a Great Rune appeared at each location where he abandoned something, akin to Miquella's footprints. Miquella's followers, who pursued him into the Realm of Shadow, used these crosses to trace his path through the realm. Miquella also discarded his other half, St. Trina, in the Stone Coffin Fissure. St. Trina, whose love for Miquella was boundless despite her abandonment, recognized that godhood would be a prison for the Empyrean, and desired for him to be killed out of mercy. 

Eventually, a Tarnished champion broke into Mohg's palace and slew the Lord of Blood for his great rune. Sir Gideon Ofnir suggested it might be safer to destroy the cocoon that Miquella remains asleep in. Instead, the Tarnished met Needle Knight Leda, a loyal follower of Miquella, who urged them to travel to the Realm of Shadow by touching Miquella's withered arm within the cocoon.

Within the Realm of Shadow, the Tarnished encounters several more of Miquella's followers, learns of his mission to ascend to godhood via the Gate of Divinity, and of the powerful charm that he had placed upon his disciples, which is broken when he discards his Great Rune. After gaining access to the tower of Enir-Ilim, the Tarnished is confronted by a resurrected Radahn, in a vessel made from the remains of Mohg. It is unclear whether Miquella always intended to use Mohg's body to resurrect Radahn. However, he needed a vessel, likely a hornsent or omen one due to their strong connection to the spiritual world, to bind to Radahn's soul. During the ensuing battle, Miquella steps out of the Gate of Divinity and embraces Radahn as his consort. The Tarnished triumphs over Radahn and Miquella, thus preventing Miquella's age of compassion.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Miquella's Lily is a delicate flower of Unalloyed gold, thought to be beloved by him in his youth. It signifies the faith in the Haligtree.
The Albinaurics, beings artificially created by human hands, view Miquella's Haligtree area as the chosen land.
The Haligtree is also inhabited by many unwanted and persecuted races, such as the Albinaurics, the Misbegotten, the Crystalians and the Kindred of Rot.
The success of Miquella's Haligtree was dependent on the Eclipse.
Even before Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree released, there are hints in-game about the connection between Miquella and St. Trina:
They are associated with their respective lilies, Miquella's Lily and Trina's Lily. Either is a rare drop from the Cleanrot Knights, who serve Malenia, Miquella's sister.
Similarly, the Albinauric Archers guarding the waygate to the Haligtree have lily motif armor and can drop St. Trina's Arrows.
A cookbook dedicated to St. Trina allows the player to create the Bewitching Branch, blessed by Unnalloyed Gold incantations.
The duality of Marika and Radagon, Miquella's parents.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
To "quell" is to suppress, put an end to, or calm something, like an uprising, fear, or strong emotion, often by force or authority.
Quella, a young boy whose emblem was a sacred tree, was the god of dreams in Dark Souls II.

Cut Content:
In earlier versions of, Miquella was the shardbearer of the Rune of Abundance.
In one version, Miquella was associated with the Abundance Twinblade, an item which was later released as Euporia in Shadow of the Erdtree.
In another build of the game, Miquella's consciousness would have been within the world of his dream. In a cut quest, Miquella acted as St. Trina of the Cradlesong, the saint of slumber. He would have sung a lullaby to soothe the Red-Eyed Merchants of their Frenzied Flame affliction and helped them to retain their personhood and prevent them from becoming "one".
A cutscene associated with Miquella was cut from the final version of., with associated materials including Leaf, Root, Root_Large, Soil_Blood_Stain, Seedling_Blood_vessel, Seedling_Blood_vessel_branch, and Seedling_Blood_vessel_MultColor_branch.
There is a cut dialogue most likely associated with this cutscene: "Young seedling, young seedling. Return to the bosom of earth. But remember well, Thou'rt mine. So shall I give of myself. This is for thee. Mine abundance, my drop of dew. Quench thy thirst, throughout thy frame. Blossom and burgeon, time and and time again. Grow larger, stronger. Until the day cometh. When thou canst share in my dream. Elden Ring, O Elden Ring. Beget Order most elegant, from my tender reverie." 
There is a separate dialogue, possibly related to the use of Miquella's Needle: "If thou covetest the throne, Impress my vision upon thine heart. In the new world of thy making, all things will flourish, whether graceful, or malign."
There is cut dialogue in which Miquella would have intervened in support of Malenia;
The phase one cutscene had her say: "Sweet Tarnished.. Dearest companion... Did you not heed my warning? Your greed knows no end. You would steal the last drop of warmth from his empty frame? After all you've taken, you still want more? Then you will have to kill me. I am Malenia, Sword of Miquella. And I have never known defeat."
During her second phase cutscene, Miquella would've said: "My dear twin, accept this gift. A gift of abundance, my last drop of dew. Let all things flourish, whether graceful, or malign." Presumably, this drop of dew would allow Malenia to ascend to her second phase, and would've been a prerequisite of some kind for Miquella's cut cutscene.
In Shadow of the Erdtree, there is an unused alternate set of dialogue for the Promised Consort Radahn cutscenes, sandwiched between the retail dialogue internally;
Radahn's phase 1 cutscene would have him say: " I am Radahn. Born of red-maned Radagon, and Rennala of the Full Moon. A lion bred for battle."
The phase 2 cutscene would have had Miquella say: "I hereby swear. To every living being, and every living soul. Now comes the age of our eden. A thousand year voyage guided by compassion. Beginning here, love encompasses all. No living thing will be denied, no deed censured. I am ready. To embrace the whole of it. Let us go together. Radahn, my promised consort."

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While the skill, Sacred Blade, is excellent, at this point of the game most bosses and tough enemies are resistant to Holy damage, and most tough Those Who Live in Death will have been defeated, making it far less useful than the much earlier acquisition of Ash of War: Sacred Blade is. 
Has a unique heavy attack that causes the user to step forward. This attack has good forward reach, and since the first attack in the charged version makes a short dash forward it's useful to catch opponents out of their roll and for landing the Stance-breaking charged heavy attack while not having to stand too close to enemies. 
This weapon gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, as the Faith-scaling is mostly useful for increasing the damage of the Skill. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 605 AP, 80 Strength or Dexterity grants 581 AP, 45 Strength (or Dexterity) and 45 Faith grants 566 AP, and 80 Faith grants 516 AP. 
In other words, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity is best if looking to maximize AP while 45 Strength and 45 Faith (Strength is slightly preferable over Dexterity due to the bonus from two-handing) is better for a mix of attack damage and skill damage. 
Pairs surprisingly well with the Golden Epitaph, another Holy sword that scales similarly well on a hybrid Strength/Dexterity or Strength/Faith build.

name: Miranda
description: Miranda was an unseen character that was cut from the retail version of. Information about Miranda is limited and may no longer be canonical. She was likely reworked into Miranda the Blighted Bloom, an afflicted Miranda Blossom whose sickly, yellowed petals are mottled with purple splotches. Her blight has spread throughout the miranda garden deep within the Perfumer's Grotto.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Miranda was the maiden of the Flower Crucible in an age long passed, presumably at the Church of the Bud in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. She was the first bud in a strain of carnivorous flowers that flourished into an aspect of the Crucible. 

Her offshoots were the Miranda Blossoms, poisonous, man-eating flowers with the ability to summon a downpour of holy light. They produced Poisonbloom and a pollen known for its bedeviling fragrance. The unscattered form of this Miranda Powder was prized by Perfumer apothecaries for its aromatic properties. It is said that the act of expelling miranda powder from one's mouth was once a restorative art.

Miranda took root within the Perfumer's Grotto and was later infected with a festering blight.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: Representations of Miranda depict her feminine form stretched in prayer, giving way to pink botanic features. Her inclusion would have further explained the mysterious origin of the man-eating Miranda Blossoms, and the budding power of certain Empyreans.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Miranda is still in the game but is more of an implied character. Although the human aspect of Miranda may no longer be canonical, personification is used to describe the sweet little Miranda Sprouts.

She may be connected to the female figure depicted wearing an octagonal crown at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh.
Miranda Blossoms are commonly found near ancient ruins built by the Rauh civilization.
Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom was uncovered deep within the forgotten Rauh ruins by Crucible Knight Devonia during her search for the true source of the Crucible. 
Devonia was the only known user of this technique, which reinforces its primacy.
The Kindred of Rot pray toward statues of this character.

Miranda may be connected to the outer god of rot.
Several scarlet butterflies flutter in the air around a lone Miranda flower in the Rotted Woods, a bud which grants the Favor of the Rotted Woods. Red specks of light swirl towards it like grace. This emphasizes the link between Miranda, Malenia, and the outer god of rot.
Poison is related to rot.
Rot Disciples appear to grow Putrid Mirandas in Abandoned Cave.
Romina, Saint of the Bud's rotten stinger attack named for a poisonous flower.

Marika, Miquella, Malenia, St. Trina, Prince of Death, and the Erdtree guardians are other characters who take on plant aspects.
Miranda fits the naming trend for Marika's bloodline.
If summoned for the Morgott boss fight, Melina uses an ability that closely resembles Miranda's Prayer that rains golden-hued light. She automatically casts Minor Erdtree on herself if defeated.
Malenia's Scarlet Aeonia ability is very similar to Aspects of the Crucible: Bloom, though it does not call down light.

The Miranda flowers flourish in a variety of hostile environments. There are six strains of Miranda flowers distributed throughout the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow.
Miranda flowers do not grow in the Consecrated Snowfield or on the Mountaintops of the Giants. They are particularly troubled by Fire damage.
Multicolored flowers play an important role in the delightful festival at Dominula, Windmill Village.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Daughters of Miranda are literal buds whereas offshoots of Malenia are metaphorical buds.
There were two Mirandas in Elden Ring version 1.00. The Miranda Blossom in Tombsward Cave, which drops a Viridian Amber Medallion, was called "Miranda the Blighted Bloom". This was changed and now there is only one Miranda the Blighted Bloom.

The miranda flowers are visually similar to real-life roses and sundews.
The forename Miranda comes from the Latin word mirandus, which means "worthy of admiration". It also derives from the Latin verb miror, which means "to admire" or "to wonder at".
William Shakespeare invented the name for a character in his play The Tempest in 1611. In the play, Miranda is the daughter of the magician Prospero. They were sent to die at sea on a "rotten carcass of a boat" but survived and found exile on an enchanted island.

name: Miséricorde
description: The Miséricorde is a dagger found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found behind a fog wall that requires 1 Stonesword Key to open, near the roaming Grafted Scion inside Stormveil Castle and the elevator shortcut back up to the Rampart Tower Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Has the highest critical multiplier in the game, at 140. 
Generally average or above average damage depending on the affinity used, but always the strongest dagger for Critical Attacks such as backstabbing or riposting. As such it's useful as a secondary weapon to be pulled out quickly, even when a build isn't focused on daggers. 
Deals damage equivalent to a Colossal Weapon, for comparison. 
This damage is strong enough that a riposte with a Fire affinity Miséricorde can oftentimes overwhelm the flat defences that often hold back split damage weapons, dealing strong damage (doesn't work as well on backstabs since the damage multiplier for them is lower). 
While it technically leans towards Dexterity it actually performs about as well on the Heavy affinity as the Keen affinity, technically better due to most daggers not working as well with Strength. 
Actually the strongest pure Dexterity dagger with the Cold affinity and the strongest dagger period on the Occult affinity, but lacks the support of other Status Effects that other daggers such as the Bloodstained Dagger and Great Knife have. 
Despite the general Dexterity tendency its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen). 
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard daggers moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, the Main-gauche, and the Scorpion's Stinger. 
Somewhat stronger on lower stats than other daggers due to its higher base damage but lower scaling. 
The longest of all daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: Mohg, Lord of Blood
description: Mohg, Lord of Blood and Mohg, the Omen are Bosses. Luminary Mohg is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and at the Mohgwyn Palace.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Mohg, also known as the Lord of Blood, was born of the Golden Lineage—the offspring of Queen Marika and Godfrey, First Elden Lord—and was the twin brother of Morgott. The twins were accursed Omen and, as a result, were confined and shackled to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell. 

Unlike his brother, Mohg embraced his Omen blood. Deep underground, Mohg made contact with an Outer God known as the Formless Mother, who ignited his accursed blood with bloodflame, granting him powerful magic.

Mohg escaped confinement in the wake of the Shattering, claiming a Great Rune of the Elden Ring. He began establishing his domain from Mohgwyn Palace and recruiting followers, including his Sanguine Nobles and a murderous Tarnished known as the Bloody Fingers. Among these followers was Sir Ansbach, commander of the Pureblood Knights, and Varré, a war surgeon who was able to successfully tame Mohg's accursed blood.

Miquella the Unalloyed later embedded himself within his Haligtree in an attempt to shed his affliction. In this vulnerable and unguarded state, Mohg seized the opportunity to abduct him from the tree. Miquella was an Empyrean, thus having the potential of ascending to godhood; Mohg intended to raise Miquella to full godhood so that he may rule at his side as consort and take the role of Elden Lord. At some point during or after the abduction, Mohg was unknowingly enchanted by Miquella. The circumstances and timeline of this enchantment remain unclear.

After abducting Miquella, Mohg hibernated with him within the Cocoon of the Empyrean, and had his followers render offerings of blood, drenching its chamber in order to facilitate Miquella's awakening. But no matter how much of Miquella's bloody bedchamber Mohg tried to share, he would receive no response from the young empyrean.

During this time, Mohg largely escaped the notice of the Roundtable Hold, who were searching for clues as to his whereabouts.

Game Events:
Eventually, the Tarnished came to learn the location of Mohg's palace, where he had hidden alongside the stolen Miquella. When the Tarnished stumbles upon his chambers, Mohg emerges from a pool of blood, holds Miquella's hand and apologizes for leaving him, ready to confront their "guests". Despite unleashing the full power of his accursed blood, Mohg is unable to overcome the Tarnished, falling at their hands.

Following his death, Mohg's corpse was stolen and transported to the Land of Shadow, where Miquella utilized it for an ancient ritual at the Gate of Divinity. Mohg's body became a vessel to house the revived soul of Radahn, Miquella's promised consort.

sections.heading: Encounters
sections.body:
Mohg, the Omen=

Mohg, the Omen:
Mohg, the Omen is projection encountered in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, within the Cathedral of the Forsaken that lies beyond the Forsaken Depths Site of Grace. The arena is a fairly small chapel, with pillars on the side that can be used to gain distance. The Dung Eater is available as a summon for this fight, provided he has been released from his cell.

Mohg's trident attacks have long delays, and cover a wide range. He uses a number of bloodflame-based attacks, which deal blood loss as well as fire damage. Mohg's Shackle can be used to stun him for a few seconds, allowing for some additional hits.

Defeating Mohg, the Omen unlocks the Cathedral of the Forsaken Site of Grace and grants Bloodflame Talons and 100,000 runes. He must be defeated in order to access the Frenzied Flame Proscription.

Moveset:

Mohg, Lord of Blood=

Mohg, Lord of Blood:
Mohg, Lord of Blood is encountered at the top of the Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum. The arena is reasonably wide and open, with some gravestones on each side that act as obstacles. 

This fight plays out much like the Mohg, the Omen fight, until the second phase, when he performs a Bloodboon Ritual and subsequently sprouts enormous black wings. During phase 2, many of Mohg's moveset expands and his attacks will cover large areas in fire.

Mohg, Lord of Blood must be defeated to unlock the Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and enter the Realm of Shadow.

Phase 1:
Phase 1 is largely the same as the fight against Mohg, the Omen. The key difference is the introduction of a countdown. When his health drops to certain levels, he will thrust his spear into the air and chant, causing a red ring to appear around the player. He will do this three times, and once his health reaches 50% he will perform Bloodboon Ritual, dealing huge amounts of damage for each ring and inflicting blood loss, while simultaneously recovering his own health. The Purifying Crystal Tear can be added to the Flask of Wondrous Physick to significantly decrease the amount of damage dealt by this move.

Phase 2:
After performing Bloodboon Ritual and recovering much of his health, Mohg will sprout wings and his spear will be imbued with bloodflame. The majority of his attacks will spray bloodflame on the ground, leaving patches of fire that last for a long time. He also now has abilities that utilize his wings to get out of range or to close distance easily.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Defeating Mohg, the Omen and Mohg, Lord of Blood for the first time unlocks the "Mohg, the Omen" and "Shardbearer Mohg" achievements, respectively.
Mohg's has five fingers on his right hand wielding the trident, but his left hand appears to have six. The finger, the third on his left hand, is actually a stiff, solid claw that sticks out when he summons his Bloodflame Talons.
Mohg's blood is possibly given to the Bloody Fingers invaders covenant. They have it injected into their finger after completing initiation, and it leads them to develop madness and bloodlust.
His death pose is visually identical to the "Heart Stolen" death animation the player can suffer during the Promised Consort boss fight; hinting even prior to Shadow of the Erdtree that Mohg was under Miquella's charm all along.
The specific timing of Mohg assuming the title of Lord of Blood and the exact sequence of his activities relative to the Shattering are not well-documented, making the precise timeline of these events unclear.

Bugs:
Summon Signs cannot send to the Summoning Pool at Mohgwyn Dynasty Mausoleum for the Mohg, Lord of Blood boss fight. Only manually placed Summon Signs appear in this area.

description: The Moons are celestial bodies in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Two moons hung over the Lands Between and Shadow Realm, fixed in the sky, unmoving in relation to the sun. The first was bright enough to be visible during the day, locked in a waxing crescent phase. The second, visible only from the Moonlight Altar, was due north and slightly to the right of the first, and was locked in a new moon phase. Beams of its blue moonlight touched the Moonlight Altar, an area rich with fallen Starlight Shards.

sections.heading: List of Moons

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The visible moons remain fixed in place and do not respond to the movement of the sun, suggesting they either emit their own light or reflect illumination from an unseen source in the east.
The Carian Royal Family requires their vassals to swear their allegiance to the moon.

name: Morgott, the Omen King
description: Morgott, the Omen King, is a remembrance boss in. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Leyndell, Royal Capital. He is not an optional boss and must be defeated to unlock Mountaintops of the Giants and progress the story.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Morgott was a direct offspring of Lord Godfrey and Queen Marika, and the rightful heir to their Golden Lineage. Despite his royal pedigree, he and his twin brother, Mohg, were born with accursed blood that caused tangled horns to sprout from their infant bodies. Once revered as divine aspect of the Crucible, these growths branded them as Omen spurned by the Erdtree and excluded from its grace. Though spared the painful excision of their horns, they were nonetheless banished to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital. A Regal Omen Bairn was made in secret to honor Morgott in a long-standing tradition.

Unlike his twin, Morgott's devotion to the Erdtree never wavered. He renounced his omen blood, extracted a portion of it, and sealed it away. The blood that formed Morgott's Cursed Sword caused it to shimmer in shifting hues, and so he encased it in stone and wielded it like a cane. Several horns were removed from his brow line.

The Shattering:
]]
When Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, Morgott claimed one of the Great Runes, which proved that he was indeed the Lord of Leyndell. With Leyndell in disarray, Morgott claimed the Erdtree capital for himself and defended it from the assault of his fellow demigods. While he succeeded in securing Leyndell against outsiders, he found that the Erdtree would not admit him, or anyone else, to claim the title of Elden Lord. Despite the fact that he had been reviled as an accursed fiend by the Golden Order, Morgott took it upon himself to become the Erdtree's protector.

He assumed the name Margit the Fell Omen during the Shattering, slaughtering champions who approached the Erdtree in the hopes of becoming Elden Lord. Under this pseudonym, he also lead the Night's Cavalry, who assisted him in the killing of great warriors, knights and champions. Simultaneously, he ruled Leyndell as the Veiled Monarch. He was able to project himself to various parts of the Lands Between. 

Game events:

When the Tarnished returned, Morgott and his Night's Cavalry hunted them throughout the realm. Morgott first encounters the Tarnished at Stormgate, where he tests their mettle as Margit before allowing them to challenge Godrick for his Great Rune. Later, he ambushes the hero again by disguising a commoner as himself in the war-torn Capital Outskirts.

The Tarnished gains entrance to Leyndell, Royal Capital and challenges Morgott at the Elden Throne after claiming two shards of the Elden Ring. Denouncing the Tarnished and his siblings as willful traitors, Morgott launches his assault. As he falters during the battle, he unleashes his sealed curse to aid him, though he feels unbearable shame in doing so. Despite his efforts, he is ultimately defeated and stripped of his Great Rune.

Without his Rune, Morgott is freed from his curse, and transforms into an enfeebled old man. He warns the Tarnished the impenetrable thorns would bar them from becoming Elden Lord, just as they rejected him. After the Cardinal Sin and the release of the Rune of Death, Morgott was finally able to truly die. At the Ashen Capital, Godfrey returned just in time to find his son in his final moments, cradling him tenderly as Morgott's body crumbled into golden dust.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Melina and Dung Eater are both available as summons for this fight. For Dung Eater to be available, the player must have released him from his cell in the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds.

Moveset:

Phase 1:
Morgott is a highly aggressive and fast-moving enemy, chaining together attacks in rapid succession while leaving few openings. His curved sword inflicts blood loss on impact, while the holy armaments he summons deal holy damage. He has ranged attacks, such as his throwing knives and spear, and utilises jumps, cartwheels, and dashes to close or create distance.

Phase 2:
Once his health drops to 50%, Morgott performs an area of effect attack in which his cursed blood erupts from the ground. His blade becomes infused with his cursed blood, and he gains a number of bloodflame-based attacks. He may also summon golden blades that rain down from the sky.

Environment:
The arena is a wide, circular platform with no obstacles, aside from the throne which will break if hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Though a common characteristic on Misbegotten, Morgott is the only Omen to display the tail Crucible aspect.
Morgott likely seized power during or in the aftermath of the First Defense of Leyndell. As Margit the Fell, he actively participated in the Second Defense of Leyndell.
Morgott was known as the Grace-Given, presumably awarded grace for his loyalty and dedication to the Erdtree, despite being an Omen born without it. Ironically, he dismisses the player as "graceless" before their battle.
His other title is the Veiled Monarch of Leyndell, an alias adopted to conceal his Omen heritage from the public. All of his appearances—whether participating in battle or hunting champions—were conducted under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.
Morgott can summon spectral weapons during his fights, including the Treespear, Giant-Crusher, Erdsteel Dagger, and Carian Knight's Sword.
While the first three weapons are associated with the Erdtree, its warriors, or its nobility, the Carian Knight's Sword originates with the Carian Royal Family, a curious choice given their shared ties to night. This may imply Morgott once observed Carian Knights—perhaps the guards of visiting diplomats—or that he mastered the sword sorceries during the Shattering.
Though he fought on the battlefield for the majority of his time as Elden Lord, Godfrey reveals he knew Morgott before their banishment. He likely made the tanglehorn bairn in secret to memorialize his son, an ancient hornsent practice.
The precious bairn has a tail and Morgott's general horn pattern. It is wrapped in a small cloak identical to the one he wears in game. It is obtained using the Remembrance of the Omen King and is the only Remembrance reward made to memorialize its subject.
Until his defeat, Morgott's seal at the Cathedral of the Forsaken prevents access to the Frenzied Flame Proscription.
Like Godrick the Grafted and other Demigods, Morgott remains alive after his defeat. He becomes an NPC that can be spoken to.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Morgott, the Omen King was named Morgott, Prince of the Omen in.
Morgott referred to himself as Elden Lord in a dialogue that was cut from the game.
There was a cut questline involving Shanehaight, a nobleman of the capital, who discovers the truth about their Veiled Monarch, much to their horror.
Morgott's name may be inspired by Morgoth, the alias of Melkor, the main and very first antagonist of Tolkien's Legendarium of Middle-earth.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Throws out a ring of light with Holy Attack Power equal to 200% of Incantation Scaling on impact. The ring stops and expands when it touches an enemy or an object, hitting with Holy Attack Power equal to 40% of Incantation Scaling 7 times over 2 seconds. 

Charging the incantation increases the Attack Power to 250% of Incantation Scaling on the initial hit and to 45% of Incantation Scaling for the smaller hits, while also increasing the number of follow-up hits to 9 over 3 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast. The cost increases to 36 points of Stamina if charged. 
Deals 8 Stance damage on the initial hit and 1.5 Stance damage per expanded hit (for a total of 18.5 Stance damage if both the initial hit and all expanded hits land). Initial Stance damage increases to 10 if charged, raising the total Stance damage to 23.5 if all hits land. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 25% for the initial hit and 12% for the follow-up hits (36% total), wearing this talisman raises Attack Power by a total of 44% for the initial hit and 29% for the follow-up hits (57% total).
Can deal damage equal to 480% of Incantation Scaling (655% of Incantation Scaling if charged), assuming no flat defense or damage negation on an enemy. Typically, it deals damage closer to 360% of Incantation Scaling (450% of Incantation Scaling if charged), assuming 0% damage negation due to flat defense having a disproportionate negative effect on the damage of the weaker follow-up hits.
Attack Power is not boosted by the Circlet of Light.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The nameless Eternal City was built by the Nox in a bygone age at the source of great underground rivers of the Lands Between. It was protected by the same Valiant Gargoyles made with the Corpse Wax of fallen champions that served as the guardians of Leyndell. 

The city would be destroyed by a falling star long ago after its inhabitants sinned against the Greater Will, a ruin that would be manifested by the eternal darkness conjured by Night Sorcery.

At some point, Astel, Naturalborn of the Void appeared suddenly and, after stealing its false night sky, devastated the city with bombardment of meteorites. The Eternal City was fully depopulated and the corpses of its inhabitants were left to drift along the path of the Ainsel river.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Nanaya was the lady of Midra and lived with him in his Midra's Manse during the golden age of the Hornsent. After Midra tried to become a Lord of Frenzied Flame, the Hornsent found out and damned him because the Frenzied Flame was forbidden. The Inquisitors broke into his house and used Golden Crux to impale him through the right eye with a Greatsword of Damnation, which spread open like Golden Arcs. When her husband was in agony after failing, like many others before him, to become Lord, Nanaya cradled what remained of him and told him to "endure" and so he did for a great long while. She passed away in a room across the hall, but it's unclear when or why. After she died, a Tarnished Champion came and drove Midra to abandon her guidance and give into the Frenzy Flame.

Many Tarnished champions believe Nanaya's smile looks like Shabriri's Woe, a starting item associated with Shabriri, the origin of the Shabriri Grapes.

name: Nepheli Loux, Warrior
description: Nepheli Loux, Warrior is an NPC in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Nepheli Loux is a Tarnished warrior from the Badlands. In her infancy, Nepheli lived through murder and pillage unchecked. At some point, she lost the guidance of grace, and was taken in by Gideon Ofnir, who became her foster father. Gideon promised Nepheli that if he became Elden Lord he would never allow the downtrodden to be cheated again, earning her loyalty and aid in his pursuit of the title of Elden Lord.

Game Events:
At the behest of Gideon, Nepheli infiltrates Stormveil Castle, the home of the demigod Godrick the Grafted. Here, she encounters a Tarnished, who aids her in defeating the decrepit demigod. With Godrick slain, she returns to Roundtable Hold, where she awards them with an Arsenal Charm she found in Stormveil, and encourages them to speak to her foster father.

Travelling to Liurnia of the Lakes, Nepheli comes upon the Village of the Albinaurics, where she witnesses the slaughter of the Albinauric inhabitants at the hands of her father's men. Reminded of the brutality she witnessed as a child, Nepheli vows to deliver justice to the oppressors, assisting the Tarnished in defeating the Omenkiller responsible for the slaughter.

For giving into her emotions and abandoning the mission, Nepheli is cast aside by Gideon. Without her estranged father's guidance, she becomes crestfallen, resigning to the lower levels of Roundtable Hold where she questions the faith she had in Gideon. 

The Tarnished obtains the ashes of The Stormhawk King in the Chapel of Anticipation, which they may choose to give to Nepheli. She can smell the ancient storm within the ash, and is reminded of her first hawk. Despite her inability to sense spirits within ash, she gladly receives them.

After claiming the Stormhawk King's ashes, Nepheli encounters Kenneth Haight, who recognises her as a worthy heir of Limgrave. Nepheli accepts the role, having been reminded by Limgrave of her own home. As the new lord of Limgrave, Nepheli pledges to aid the Tarnished should they become Elden Lord, pledging to call upon the storm to drive away the foulness that has settled on the winds.

sections.heading: <!--Background-->Overview
sections.body:
The Night is a darkness unending associated with the stars and fate. This god is identified by bones with a distinct lifelessness, which manifest in areas under its influence, such as the central castle and beyond the Spirit Shelter gate. The Iron Menial received one such Bone-Like Stone from the Nightlord in a dream, granting it to the Recluse when he awoke. Though it held the power to expunge divine essence, it could also be destroyed by it. It also held the power to alter fate, affirming a connection to the primeval current and stars. The "distinct lifelessness," "dead of night," and association with bones reveal its link to the outer god of death, which is already connected to Night and fate.

The Nox of the Eternal Cities worked toward bringing about age of the Stars, while the cutting-gifted tribe sought to prevent it. After Ensha of the Royal Remains massacred the Village of the Albinaurics at Sir Gideon's request, the Elder Albinaurics begged the night to punish the hateful world it condemned them to.

Nightreign:
An outer god of Night is the higher power behind the Nightlord in. Its power is the Night's Tide that threatens Limveld. The Night was ushered in by the man who became Heolstor the Nightlord after the Shattering in the Nightreign timeline. His version of the Night was a curse, and he was an enemy to the world.

name: Night Giant
description: The Night Giants, also known in the community as Titans, Tree Giants, or Shadow Giants, are characters in.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Although vaguely skeletal in appearance, the Night giants' mist-clad, wooden bodies lack actual bones. They are covered in concentric fingerprint whorls and enwreathed in woody vines that twist in swirling patterns. They have long, slender arms and clawed feet, but lack maxillae and upper skulls entirely.
Shining trees with blue branches and leafless violet twigs, housed within their hollow chest cavities, jut upward past their toothy wooden jaws.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Night Giants were colossal humanoids whose silent march toward the Lands Between marked the threatening final advance of the Night. They neared the shores of Limveld at noontide on the second day of the Expedition, visible as vast shadowy silhouettes in the distance, trudging across the Sea of Fog. Their bodies became corporeal as they drew nearer, continuing their slow, lumbering procession toward the growing Spirit Shelter tree as the Night's Tide swallowed the land.

In the "Dawn" ending, the Grace of Gold awakens a wooden titan whose head bears the contour of Heolstor the Nightlord's helm. By turning away from the Erdtree, this giant symbolically ended the Primordial Nightlord's dominion over the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The "Night Giant" name is conjectural.
The has all-blue slots, which may reflect the blue trees growing within the Night giants. Given this, it is possible that the term refers to them.
Night Giants appear on every Expedition.
Figures with similar tree-like features bow before the Primordial Nightlord in the opening cinematic.
Although likely golems, the root growth inside Trolls and the briars impaling dead Fire Giants suggest that the Night Giants' botanical nature marks them as true giants.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Night Giants are roughly two miles tall (3,450 meters, or ~11,319 feet), establishing them as the most enormous creatures to appear in. They are about five times larger than the Colossal Remains in Caelid, and about 1,000 meters shorter than the Erdtree (4,452 meters).
Their legs are modeled despite being submerged in water in-game.
The "Dawn" cutscene was pre-rendered, meaning the Nightlord Giant's unique 3D model cannot be viewed.

name: Night of Black Knives
description: The Night of Black Knives (黒き刃の陰謀の夜, Kuroki Yaiba no Inbō no Yoru) was an event mentioned in. It involved the theft of Destined Death and the assassination of Godwyn the Golden, a son of Queen Marika the Eternal. It would serve as the catalyst of the conflict known as The Shattering.

sections.heading: Prelude
sections.body:
Although the conspirators behind it remained unknown to the wider world, it was in fact orchestrated by Lunar Princess Ranni as she was looking for a way to free herself from the control of the Two Fingers.
Ranni, who sought to change her fate, stole a piece of the Rune of Death from Maliketh, who served as the guardian of the rune. With the stolen fragment, Ranni proceeded to imbue the Black Knives of Numen Assassins, all of them being women from the Eternal Cities with ties to Marika, with the powers of Destined Death.

On the same night, Ranni gifted her brother, Praetor Rykard, with the Blasphemous Claw, a rock engraved with traces of the Rune of Death, as a reward for helping her in the plot and to make Rykard able to challenge Maliketh on the day of his blasphemy.

sections.heading: Assassination
sections.body:
Wishing to shed her Empyrean body but preserve her spirit, she knew that the spirit of someone else had to die as well. On the night of the plot, the assassins arrived in Leyndell, the Royal Capital, and slew Godwyn the Golden, carving the Cursemark of Death into his flesh. The Cursemark was supposed to form a circle; however, as Ranni perished in the same moment as Godwyn, the mark was split into two half-wheels. Godwyn's soul alone perished, while Ranni became the first Demigod to die in the flesh.

Immediately following the assassination, the Black Knives fled the capital. Tiche, the daughter of the Black Knife Ringleader Alecto, died protecting her mother during the escape.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.body:
Godwyn's body was interred in the Deeproot Depths at the base of the Erdtree's roots, where he mutated and deformed into the being that would become known as the Prince of Death. Later, the traces of the Rune of Death used to slay him spread through the network of Greattree roots that span the Lands Between, taking the form of Deathroot, the source of Those Who Live in Death.

Ranni, whose Empyrean body perished upon the carving of the Cursemark, transferred her soul into a doll modeled after her mentor. She maintained a low profile following the Night of Black Knives, and it is unknown whether her death was widely known.

Following the Night of Black Knives, the Elden Ring was shattered by Queen Marika. As a result, the great war known as The Shattering ensued. 

In the aftermath of the Shattering, a Tarnished known as Fia, the Deathbed Companion, came into contact with the soulless body of Godwyn. Fia sought the two half-wheels, wishing to reunite them and produce a Mending Rune, which could introduce Those Who Live in Death to the Elden Ring. During this time, another Tarnished named Rogier began to study the Night of Black Knives, bringing him into contact with Fia.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Night's Cavalrymen were once led by Margit, the Fell Omen, delivering death to great warriors, knights, and champions. Their fond remembrances inspired the Phantom Slash battle art, which manifests an apparition of their former teacher. Presently, they can be found across the Lands Between, appearing only at night.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
The Night's Cavalry are knights in black armor with flowing black hair that only appear at night, riding atop funeral steeds. They fight using flails, which can inflict blood loss, or glaives, which allow them to perform wide, sweeping attacks.

The Night's Cavalry and its Funeral Steed have separate health bars. Defeating the horse dismounts the rider. The knight summons a new horse from a purple portal after a while, or after the player runs away.

name: Noble Presence
description: Noble Presence is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Godslayer incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed Drop: Volcano Manor
Noble Presence is acquired by defeating the Godskin Noble found at the Temple of Eiglay on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Noble Presence creates a repelling shockwave that knocks back human-sized enemies within a 1.3-meter radius, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 239% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting a Blackflame effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds. 

Charging the spell increases the radius to 2.3 meters and increases the Attack Power to 279% of Incantation Scaling, while also launching human-sized enemies into the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 FP per cast.
Costs 28 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 36 points. 
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
Deals 16.8 Stance damage. Increases to 21.84 Stance damage when charged. 

Boosting:
The Godskin Noble Robe boosts the effectiveness of this spell by 20%.
This spell is not strengthened by the Godslayer's Seal.

Strategies:
Noble Presence is fairly effective against groups of enemies, as its large area-of-effect shockwave can push back or launch multiple foes at once.
The knockback effect can be useful in controlling the battlefield by throwing enemies off cliffs or into hazardous areas.
Can be used defensively to break the Stance of incoming attackers, giving the caster time to heal or reposition.
Charging the spell for maximum potency is particularly effective against heavier foes and enemies with shields. 
The additional damage from the Blackflame effect is somewhat unreliable, as the invincibility given to launched foes will prevent it from being applied to human-sized foes. It is nonetheless 
All bosses in are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07: Increased stamina consumption and increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies. Shortened recovery time.
Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 180 to 200 for the uncharged version, while the charged versions Stamina Attack Power wasn't changed. 
The Stamina Attack Power against guarding players was increased from 180 to 250 for the uncharged version, while it was increased from 234 to 292 for the charged version.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The default skill is useful for breaking the guard of blocking enemies with the light attack version or for breaking their Stance with the heavy attack version.
The longest of all Straight Swords, with very good scaling but bad base damage making it a mostly good weapon, not counting how hard it can be to farm.
Performs best on the Keen affinity as it has the lowest damage deficit there and is usually only a dozen or fewer points behind in terms of pure Attack Power. 
Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
As the description implies, this swords sells for 10 times as much as most other Straight Swords.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: Nox Swordstress & Nox Monk
description:
The Nox Swordstress and Nox Monk are an optional duo Enemy bosses in.

Overview:
A duo boss consisting of a Nox Monk and a Nox Swordstress. They are found in a courtyard on the northern side of Sellia, behind a magical seal which can be broken by lighting three braziers atop towers throughout the town. Inside the courtyard is a large chair-crypt, reminiscent of those found in the Eternal Cities, albeit without a giant skeleton occupying it. 

Defeating the boss will unlock the Chair-Crypt of Sellia Site of Grace. A treasure chest beneath the chair, accessible only once the duo has been defeated, contains Lusat's Glintstone Staff.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 6,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Fire Monks' Prayerbook.
Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then that instructor die before purchasing this incantation, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Summons a large, short-ranged burst of flame in hand, with Fire Attack Power equal to 280% Incantation Scaling. 

Charging the spell increases Attack Power to 385% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 16 FP per cast.
Costs 24 Stamina per cast. Stamina cost increases to 31 when charged. 
Requires 1 Memory Slot.
Deals 10.175 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 14.4. 

Boosting:

Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 38%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 58%.

Strategies:
Effective in close-range encounters with groups of bunched-up enemies.
Potentially deals a lot of damage when charged, but is somewhat difficult to use to the moderate casting time and needing to be at melee range while lacking the flexibility and agility of Catch Flame.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
This spell was formerly titled "Oh, Flame!" during the Closed Network Test.
Patch 1.04: Increased damage. 
Attack Power of the uncharged version was increased from 257% of Incantation Scaling to 280% of the same, and the charged version was increased from 301% of Incantation Scaling to 385% of the same. 
Either Patch 1.03 or Patch 1.03.3 seems to have included an undocumented change that increased the FP cost of this incantation from 12 to 16.

name: Omen
description: Omen (忌み, Imi, or 忌み子, Imigo) are Enemies in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Newborn children bearing horns were considered divine in ancient times. A potent spirituality suffused their oversized horns, a blessing of the primordial Crucible believed by the hornsent to mark them as a chosen people. These and other Crucible aspects were later deemed impurities during the reign of Queen Marika, who excluded those who bore them from her Grace of Gold.

The Omen's horns are imbued with wraiths and their blood is tainted. Without the Grace of Gold, they were shunned from society, their souls barred from returning to the Erdtree. Royal Omen, including the twins born to Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey, were secretly banished to the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds below Leyndell, buried and shackled by golden magic for eternity. In contrast, the horns of commoners were severed, a brutal surgical procedure that few survived.

During times of war, conscripted Omen received curved cleavers that took advantage of their brute strength, though a worsening curse placed upon the blades ensured they would later be reclaimed. Additionally, wicked, horned elder spirits tormented Omen in their nightmares, and masked perfumers imitated these hideous spirits. Omenkillers mercilessly hunted and subdued Omen with blades decorated with amputated Omen horns. However, Perfumer Tricia and her partner instead provided aromatic treatments to the help Omen as they died.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Omen are hulking, blue-skinned brutes with small heads and silver hair. They have four fingers and toes, and twisted horns sprouting from their large bodies, though lowborn Omen bear bleeding stumps instead. Demigod Omen, such as Morgott, the Omen King and Mohg, Lord of Blood, have scales, tails, and even black-feathered wings.

Accursed Omen, born of royalty, possess some horn growth but are forced to live underground in secrecy. They harbor some amount of wraiths, which they can expel from their mouths at foes. The Strong Accursed Omen, capable of unleashing a barrage of wraiths in a fiery explosion, consequently imbuing their weapons with their power. In this empowered state, they can slam their weapons with explosive force to release more wraiths.

Omen wrapped in black cloaks aligned with Death-Serving Commoners in worship of the Prince of Death, who was once Godwyn the Golden.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.body:
Omen Cleaver =

Omen Cleaver:

Omen Cleaver:

The Omen wields an Omen Cleaver, a heavy-bladed, curved sword etched with a pattern that is the remnant of a deteriorating malediction. The swords have a deceptively long reach, which the Omen take full advantage of with their fighting style.

sections.body:
The Fell Twins duo boss encountered on the bridge leading to the Divine Tower of East Altus are both Omen. Other Omen bosses include Margit, the Fell Omen, Mohg, the Omen, Mohg, Lord of Blood, and Morgott, the Omen King.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal names: ShunnedChildSword (ID: 214000) and ShunnedChildAxa (ID: 214010)
Localization Notes
The Omen are called 忌み (Imi), which would mean "Abomination" in this context.
They are also occasionally referred to as 忌み子 (Imigo), which means "Abominable Child", "Unwanted Child", or "Shunned Child."
Margit's "Fell Omen" title is 忌み鬼 (Imi Oni), meaning "Abominable Demon."
The Mending Rune of the Fell Curse is called 忌み呪いの修復ルーン (Imi Noroi no Shūfuku Rūn) "Mending Rune of the Abomination Curse" or "Abominable Curse", where 忌み (Imi) is the same word localised as "Omen." Therefore, "Mending Rune of the Omen Curse" would be a localization in line with the rest of the text.
The Omen Bairn items are called 水子 (Mizuko), which can refer to a newborn baby, or an aborted, stillborn, or miscarried fetus.
水子供養 (Mizuko kuyō) is a Japanese Buddhist memorial service for those who have had a miscarriage, stillbirth, or abortion. The ceremony is meant to comfort parental grief, guilt, or the soul of the fetus, sometimes in fear of its vengeful spirit. Statues of Jizō, a Bodhisattva thought to protect children, are commonly offered by temples, which may be the inspiration for the Omen Bairns. 
Possibly inspired by the Shope papilloma virus that causes rabbits to form horn-like growths.

Village of the Albinaurics=

Background:
An Omenkiller found in the Village of the Albinaurics in Liurnia of the Lakes, across the bridge from the Site of Grace. This Omenkiller appears to be responsible for the slaughter of the Albinaurics on the orders of Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing. This Omenkiller is accompanied by three dogs. Nepheli Loux, Warrior is available as a summon for this boss, provided she was spoken to at the entrance to the Village of the Albinaurics.

A magic user with a guided bolt-like spell such as Glintstone Pebble has a particularly efficient tactical option for this Omenkiller: the area he is in also contains two cabins. The double-jump of Torrent can easily get you onto the lower cabin, and from there another double-jump can get you onto the roof of the taller one. From there, the Omenkiller will not be able to reach you with any of his attacks. He does often get rather close to the wall of the cabin which can be difficult for you to hit, and at longer range (usually after a fire-breath when he backs up a bit) he tends to dodge attacks, but carefully timing your shots should slowly but surely allow you to kill this enemy solo at little risk.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: In the beginning, everything was the One Great. At some point, it was fractured by the Greater Will, creating divisions, births, and souls. sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 10 points of Stamina to cast. 
Despite being a Golden Order Incantation, this spell, like other spell-based weapon buffs, does not get bonus damage from its associated seal (the Golden Order Seal for this one). Additionally, said seal is actually rather bad for casting this spell as its Intelligence scaling will not be used for the weapon buff's strength. 
The moderate investment in Intelligence required for this spell is somewhat inconvenient since it does not help its scaling. The best way to cast this in limited situations is to equip the Stargazer Heirloom with an innate Intelligence of 8-12. This is possible for every Origin without an Intelligence investment, except for the Hero and the Prophet, both of which have a 7 in that Attribute. 
Like with all spell-based Weapon Buffs, it can only be cast when a weapon is held in the right hand and the casting implement in the left hand. 
If you wish to buff two weapons at the same time, see below for similar skills. 
Outmatched by Holy Grease below 114 Incantation Scaling, by Skill: Sacred Blade below 120 Incantation Scaling, and by Golden Grease below 160 Incantation Scaling. 
Though they cast much quicker and last for a shorter duration, Drawstring Holy Grease is stronger below 147 Incantation Scaling while Drawstring Golden Grease is stronger below 180 Incantation Scaling. 
Sacred Blade has the advantage of also being usable for weapons with the otherwise unbuffable (not counting other skills) Lightning and Sacred Affinity weapons.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Dropped by the Grafted Scion at the Chapel of Anticipation, either by beating it first try when starting the game or when visiting again through The Four Belfries in west Liurnia of the Lakes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The skill, Golden Tempering, is the only way to buff the weapon directly, adding a flat 100 Holy damage, and grants access to unique heavy, charged heavy, and running heavy attacks that are comprised entirely of thrusts. 
These attacks always use both swords, even when using the weapon one-handed, so they can be performed even when something else is held in the left hand. 
This means that it pairs very well with a shield that has No Skill equipped. While most Greatshields are functionally out of reach due to these swords having quite low Strength-scaling, the Jellyfish Shield and its skill, Contagious Fury, is still somewhat accessible and usable, even if having to first use the sword's buff and then the shield's buff is somewhat finicky. 
This is a paired weapon, meaning it doesn't gain the effective 50% increase to Strength when wielded with two-hands but instead pulls out a second sword. 
Since this weapon has below average weight for a Straight Sword, this essentially allows for dual-wielding at half the weight and upgrade material that would otherwise had been required. 
Unlike how it usually is when dual-wielding, both light and heavy attacks will use both sword and blocking with the sword is still possible, if ill-advised. 
Almost entirely focused on Dexterity, but still about 10% weaker than the strongest infusable weapons on a Keen affinity (Longsword and Broadsword).

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The golden symbol displayed upon using the skill is the seal of the Erdtree, also displayed when casting Erdtree-associated incantations such as Erdtree Heal and Aspects of the Crucible: Horns.
Patch 1.07 added a timing for interrupting the attack during a series of strong attacks while under the effect, increased strong attack motion speed, poise damage, and stamina attack power against guarding enemies during the effect, increased the duration and attack power of the effect that grants the weapon a holy attribute, reduced time between the skill activation and being able to perform actions.
Increased the duration of the skill's weapon buff from 40 seconds to 60 seconds, and increased the amount of added Holy damage from 85 to 100. It also decreased the aftercast time where you are unable to do anything after performing the skill.
Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost and increased cast speed, and increased effect duration.
FP cost was reduced from 30 to 24, and the duration was increased from 20 seconds to 40 seconds.

name: Outer God
description: The are unseen, enigmatic entities wielding immense power and influence over the world of, often acting indirectly to reshape the Lands Between according to their inscrutable designs. They manifest through various natural or supernatural phenomena, often tied to one or more divine elements.

sections.heading: List of Outer Gods
sections.body:
Formless Mother:

The Formless Mother, also known as the Mother of Truth, is an arcane outer god associated with Omen, hornsent, blood, and bloodflame. She craves wounds and is said to bestow power upon those born with accursed blood. The Blood Oath incantations channel her divine element, accessed by puncturing her omnipresent body with ritual spears. It is believed that the eternal blood of the Formless Mother will never dry or turn to rot.

Her current followers are Mohg, the Lord of Blood; his Mohgwyn Dynasty; and the bloodfiends, former hornsent.

Outer God of Death:

An outer god of Death once held influence over the Lands Between. Its powers presumably included Death Blight, Spectral Light, and the Ghostflame wielded by the ancient Deathbirds and Gravebirds. This entity may also be connected to spirit-calling hexes.

The Twinbird and White-Winged Maidens are said to be the envoys of Death. After his burial at the roots of the Erdtree, Godwyn the Golden was transformed into the Prince of Death.

Outer God of Frenzied Flame:

This theoretical outer god is representated by the maddening, yellow Flame of Frenzy; however, it is unclear whether the Frenzied Flame itself embodies this divinity or is simply a manifestation of its power. Nonetheless, its purpose is to catalyze the reunification of the One Great by destroying the Lands Between and plunging the world into chaos. It presents profound danger to all life, possessing the ability to melt away even eternal spirits. The god is associated with the Eye of Yelough and contagious yellow embers in the eyes of its followers.

The Flame of Frenzy initially entered the world through impressions left upon the grave of an ancient god by the Readerless Fingers, likely in the Finger Ruins. Later, its use was forbidden and vehemently suppressed by the Hornsent, Queen Marika, and Melina. Its blind Finger Maiden later described its envoy as a "distant light," visible only after amassing numerous Shabriri Grapes.

The Three Fingers serve as the corporeal agents of the Frenzied Flame. Its Chaos Followers—Hyetta, Midra, Nanaya, Shabriri, Vyke, and the immured Great Caravan—await the Lord of Frenzy, who will ignite the Erdtree with the yellow flame.

Outer God of Night:

An outer god of Night is thought to be the 'greater being' behind the Nightlord in. Its power is the Night's Tide that threatens Limveld. This god is identified by bones with a distinct lifelessness, which manifest in areas under its influence, such as the central castle and beyond the Spirit Shelter gate. The Iron Menial received one such Bone-Like Stone from the Nightlord in a dream, granting it to the Recluse when he awoke. Though it held the power to expunge divine essence, it could also be destroyed by it. It also held the power to alter fate, affirming a connection to the primeval current and stars.

An eye appears in skybox for each Nightlords' arena, and is formed by the clouds above the final ring on both nights in Limveld.
The "distinct lifelessness," "dead of night," and association with bones may imply a connection to the outer god of death, who is already connected to Night. The Black Knifeprint is composed of starlight.

Outer God of Rot:

The outer god of Scarlet Rot whose essence was sealed away by a blind swordsman in the Lake of Rot. A great scorpion's tail, which was crafted into a dagger, is said to be a relic of this outer god. Miquella's Needle was crafted and inserted into Malenia, Blade of Miquella to ward off the affliction of the Scarlet Rot.

Its current followers include Romina, Saint of the Bud; Sage Gowry; and the Servants of Rot.

According to Gowry's understanding, the Laws of an Order of Rot would be those of "Decay" (腐敗の律) and "Rebirth" (輪廻の理).

sections.heading: List of Unconfirmed Outer Gods
sections.body:
This section lists the entities with a very similar role to the outer gods, but are never textually referred to as such.

Fell God:

The nameless god of fire is the source of the Giants' Flame and Giants' Flame incantations; however, it interferes with the Lands Between more directly. It is an ancient, malformed deity that was depicted with curled horns and thick braids of bright red hair. It is also tied to smithing and verdigris.

Blood Star:

The blood star is a mysterious entity responsible for Briars of Punishment and Briars of Sin, two aberrant Thorn Sorceries. These sorceries require Faith to use, which implies the blood star is something that can be worshiped, and is therefore an entity. The Guilty could only see the blood star after they were blinded.

Serpent-God:

The ancient inhabitants of Mt. Gelmir made sacrifices in the name of a Serpent-God. It is likely connected to one of the god-like snakes, such as the Abyssal Serpent and God-Devouring Serpent.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The term "outer god" may also refer to gods outside of the current order, the Golden Order.
The outer gods may be parts of the One Great that became independent when it fractured. Some language used to describe outer gods implies they were once holy, but became fractured or corrupted in the past.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
"Outer God" refers to cosmic entities in works by H.P. Lovecraft, alongside the "Great Old Ones." These "Other Gods" are vast, incomprehensible deities that often exist beyond human reach. The term "Outer God" was later coined by August Derleth to categorize these enigmatic beings in his expansion of the Cthulhu Mythos.
The Japanese term for was similarly pulled from Japanese translations of the Cthulu Mythos.

name: Parrying Dagger
description: The Parrying Dagger is a Dagger.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: 1 can be bought from Patches for 1,600 Runes in any of his locations (Murkwater Cave is the earliest).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The second strongest of all the regular non-Wakizashi daggers on a Keen or Quality affinity, after the Celebrant's Sickle and Bloodstained Dagger respectively. 
Despite this its Keen affinity actually gives it slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen). 
Otherwise pretty mediocre damage-wise, with a leaning towards Dexterity on most of its affinities. 
Having Parry as its skill gives early access to Parrying without having to buy Ash of War: Parry from Knight Bernahl or venture out of Limgrave and the Weeping Peninsula. It is however outclassed slightly by any Small Shield with the skill, especially the also-available-early Buckler. 
Decent off-hand weapon for those wishing to dual-wield daggers.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones. 
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

name: Patches
description: Patches is an NPC and boss in. He surrenders if you reduce his HP to 50% or less. From then on, he acts as a merchant and gives helpful advice to players.

sections.heading: Character Information
