sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Murkwater Cave
Pass through the golden fog into the boss room and loot the Cloth Garb and Cloth Trousers from the treasure chest to trigger Patches to jump down from above.
After reducing his health to 50%, he will stop attacking and grant the Grovel for Mercy gesture. He will now become available as a merchant after reloading the area.
Continuing to attack him will cause him to become hostile again. If he gets your health low enough, he will grant the Extreme Repentance gesture. Using this will cause him to stop attacking again.
(Optional) There will be another chest in his room after returning. Using this will trigger a trap which will teleport you to the Mistwood. It will not be possible to fast travel until you have rested at a Site of Grace. Patches will grant the Calm Down! gesture after returning to him.
(Optional) Liurnia of the Lakes
Patches can be found near the Scenic Isle Site of Grace. He will discuss Rya and the Abductor Virgin below the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
Clearing the Subterranean Inquisition Chamber and returning to Patches will unlock new dialogue, as well as the Calm Down! gesture if not received in the previous step.
(Optional) Mt. Gelmir
From the First Mt. Gelmir Campsite Site of Grace, go west past the siege tower and then north. Patches will advise you to follow a path of Glowstones leading to a ledge, which Patches will then kick you off. 
Volcano Manor
Patches can be found in the entrance corridor after entering Tanith's service. After completing Tanith's first request, Patches will give you a request to kill Great-Horned Tragoth.
Tragoth can be found in the Magma Wyrm Makar boss room in the Ruin-Strewn Precipice. Kill him and then return to Patches and exhaust his dialogue, then rest at a Site of Grace and speak to him again to receive the Magma Whip Candlestick.
After defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, return to Patches and exhaust his dialogue.
Shaded Castle
Patches can be found in the hallway leading to Elemer of the Briar. Talk to him to receive the Dancer's Castanets. 
Offer the Dancer's Castanets to Tanith in Rykard's boss room. She will refuse them, however they will be removed from your inventory.
Murkwater Cave
Return to Murkwater Cave and enter the boss room. Open the chest to trigger another fight with Patches. Attack him once to make him stop attacking, and he will give the Patches' Crouch gesture.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Patches is a reoccurring character in From Software's games, having appeared in Armored Core: For Answer, Demon's Souls, Dark Souls, Bloodborne, and Dark Souls III. Many of his recognisable traits, such as his physical appearance, use of a spear, and proclivity for tricking the player have been retained for his appearance in Elden Ring.
Patches can be summoned during the boss fight against Starscourge Radahn, however he will return to his world after a few seconds.

description: Phantom Bloody Finger and Phantom Recusant Finger are consumable tools in.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Using this item will make the Invader kneel for a second before teleporting to a random spawn location in proximity to the Host of Fingers of a recently invaded world.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Location: Varies
Phantom Fingers are temporary items acquired automatically upon invading another world. The Phantom Finger obtained depends on the invasion item used to invade the world.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The game uses the Host's current X and Z-coordinates to determine multiplayer spawn points; it does not take the Y-coordinate into account. This can lead to Invaders being placed at the top or bottom of a cliff, demanding an inappropriately lengthy detour. This item is helpful when the spawn point is less than ideal.
Phantom Fingers can be used to escape to another location when spotted or cornered.
Phantom Fingers can also be used to ambush an isolated Host of Fingers after luring their Furled Fingers far away.
The effectiveness of this item varies based on the platform and the drive the game is installed on, as the game enters a Loading Screen upon using this item. The quicker the Loading Screen, the faster the maneuver.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Despite the phantom fingers received from using the Bloody Finger and Festering Bloody Finger having the same name, they are technically different items with their own unique icons.
Despite technically being considered different items, their function and item descriptions are completely the same, including the Recusant version.
When there is an over-leveled Furled Finger in a world, the game will try to adjust their stats to improve balance; decreasing their survivability by lowering their HP, Stamina, and FP, while reducing their damage-output by increasing the defenses of everything else against them, specifically, this includes invaders. However, before version 1.09 was released, there was a consistent bug that completely removed the invader's defense bonus against these co-operators (always after one of the phantom fingers had been used in that session), effectively giving the over-leveled Furled Finger all of their original, unscaled damage-output back against the invader alone.

name: Pidia, Carian Servant
description: Pidia, Carian Servant is a merchant NPC in.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body: Basic Info:

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Carian Manor
If Ranni the Witch has not been given either the Fingerslayer Blade OR Seluvis' Amber Draught, the player can find Pidia on the second floor of the Manor Lower Level Site of Grace. However, he can only be reached from the building's rooftop. To gain access to him, the player must travel to the Three Sisters and follow the clifftop above Caria Manor southwest. Once there, the player can descend several platforms in order to safely reach the Manor rooftop below. When first talking with Pidia, he will offer to sell you a number of rare items from his storeroom.
Carian Manor
If Ranni the Witch has been given either the Fingerslayer Blade OR Seluvis' Amber Draught, the player will hear Pidia crying out in pain when approaching his location. Upon reaching him, the player will find Pidia lying dead, surrounded by the puppet soldiers he once maintained. The player can loot Pidia's Bell Bearing from his corpse, as well as one of two puppets depending upon certain conditions. If the player has already given Seluvis' Potion to Nepheli Loux, Pidia will drop the Nepheli Loux Puppet. If the player has not given Seluvis' Potion to Nepheli Loux, Pidia will drop Dolores the Sleeping Arrow Puppet, instead.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
He's in an area in which you can't fight, which means he can't be killed under normal circumstances. When it is revealed in Ranni the Witch's questline that Seluvis is a puppet, Pidia will subsequently be killed by his Raya Lucaria Soldier puppets before a The Tarnished (Protagonist) champion arrives.
He sells the Weathered Map to the Amber Starlight required for Seluvis's Amber Draught that he wants Ranni the Witch to drink so he can make her into a doll, even though she is already a doll.
If Seluvis dies before a puppet reward can be given by him, then dead Pidia will drop the puppet.
Pidia wears a Headband of the Golden Ones.
The reveal that Pidia controls Preceptor Seluvis is foreshadowed during Seluvis's introduction at Ranni's Rise when he pauses mid-sentence before stating that he lives at Seluvis's Rise.

name: Pike
description:
The Pike is a Spear, a melee armament. With its extreme length plus its attack pattern of long forward stabs, the Pike has absolutely excellent forward range compared to nearly every other melee weapon, and its Stat requirement is not very high making it an excellent early option for every class, including magic users.

When skill-refitted with something like Ash of War: Spinning Slash with a wide attack arc, it also becomes very effective against clustered groups of enemies. Another good choice is Ash of War: Impaling Thrust, allowing the player to punch clean through an enemy's shield block from a sizeable distance.

name: Placidusax's Ruin
description:
Placidusax's Ruin is a spell in. 

Though it may look similar, it's neither one of the Dragon Cult Incantations nor one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Aquisition
sections.body:
Trade the Remembrance of the Dragonlord, dropped by Dragonlord Placidusax, with Finger Reader Enia.

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Sends an electric burst almost immediately upon casting to deal Lightning damage and knock away players and lighter enemies, before sending out several sweeping, golden beams that deal Fire damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This spell does not belong to any school of incantations, and as such doesn't have its damage boosted by any Sacred Seals. 
The damage being split between Lightning and Fire damage makes it somewhat difficult to maximize the entirety of the spells through Crystal Tears and Talismans. 
This damage split somewhat ironically gives it great similarity to the Incantations associated with Placidusax's archenemy Bayle the Dread, whose spells have the same split in damage types. 
The initial burst of Lightning comes out very quickly and as such is surprisingly useful when fighting other players or player-type enemies such as NPC invaders.

name: Preceptor Miriam
description:
Preceptor Miriam is a hostile character in. 

Miriam can be fought twice in the Carian Study Hall, once before placing the Carian Inverted Statue and once after.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
She rather predictably wears the Preceptor Set, using the standard chest and head pieces. 
Wields an Academy Glintstone Staff which she uses to cast Carian Slicer, Greatblade Phalanx, Loretta's Greatbow, and Magic Downpour, of which the Greatbow spell is usually the most used. 
Can teleport to the next spot in her area upon taking sufficient damage, though she may skip over a spot in the Standard Study Hall if enough damage is taken at one spot. This cannot happen in the Inverted Study Hall unless killed in the first spot, as she only has two spots there. 
Can summon various puppets, Wandering Nobles in the standard area and Raya Lucaria Soldiers in the Inverted area.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.body:
Lucidity (only in the inverted version of the Carian Study Hall) 
Magic Downpour (only in the normal version of the Carian Study Hall)

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Pidia's questline becomes locked after giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade, regardless of any steps already completed.
Follow Ranni the Witch's questline and join her service in Ranni's Rise. Speak to the projections of Blaidd, Iji, and Seluvis, and then speak to Ranni once again.
Visit Seluvis's Rise, south of Ranni's Rise, and speak to Seluvis. Agree to his request to obtain Seluvis's Potion.
Perform any one of the following to proceed with Seluvis's questline:
Give Nepheli Loux the potion. In order to do this, you must have defeated the Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics and Nepheli must be in the lower level of Roundtable Hold. You will obtain Nepheli Loux Puppet from Pidia, Carian Servant at the end of his questline.
Give Dung Eater the potion. In order to do this, you must have obtained a Seedbed Curse, freed Dung Eater from his gaol, defeated his dark spirit in the Capital Outskirts, and made sure Dung Eater has returned to his gaol. You will be able to obtain Dung Eater Puppet from Seluvis after this.
Talk to Gideon Ofnir and give him the potion.
Return to Seluvis and exhaust his dialogue, regardless of the option chosen in the previous step. His shop inventory will now be available.
Travel to the ruins north-east of Ranni's Rise and pass through the illusory floor. Go down the steps into the cellar and interact with the message saying "Seluvis' puppet. Do not touch."
Return to Seluvis and select the "About your chambers" dialogue option. You will now be able to buy puppets from Seluvis in return for Starlight Shards. Buy any one of these puppets to continue.
Speak to Seluvis again and select the "About the scheme" dialogue option.
Obtain the Amber Starlight from Altus Plateau. This can be found in a small grotto north-east of the Altus Highway Junction Site of Grace, north of the giant staircase that leads to the Tree Sentinel boss fight.
Return to Seluvis and select the "Give Amber Starlight" dialogue option to obtain the Magic Scorpion Charm.
Reload the area and speak to Seluvis to obtain the Amber Draught.
You may attempt to give the Amber Draught to Ranni. Doing so will lock Ranni's questline, and it can only be resumed by seeking Absolution at the Church of Vows. Talking to her three times after trying to give her the draught will cause her to instantly kill you.
Seluvis will now be dead. His Bell bearing and armour set can be looted from his body, which can also be interacted with to access the puppet shop. Pidia will also die at this stage.
If Ranni is not given the Amber Draught, Seluvis will die in the same way after giving her the Fingerslayer Blade.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant are both voiced by Charles Dale, and Pidia's dialogue is found nested within Seluvis' dialogue in the game's files. Along with the pose Seluvis is found in at the end of his questline, being reminiscent of the puppets in his cellar, it is presumed that Seluvis himself is a puppet of Pidia. The reveal is foreshadowed during Seluvis's introduction at Ranni's Rise when he pauses mid-sentence before stating he lives at Seluvis's Rise.

name: Primal Glintstone Blade
description:
Primal Glintstone Blade is a talisman in.

Reduces FP consumed by spells by 25% and Maximum HP by 15%.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from a chest in the cellar of Stargazer's Ruins in central Mountaintops of the Giants. The cellar is locked by a seal, which can be dispelled by summoning the Spirit Jellyfish Ashes near the NPC jellyfish that speaks, near the center of the ruins. Note that the NPC jellyfish does respawn, if killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
25% FP reduction is roughly equal to an extra 33.33% FP when casting spells. This will vary a bit depending on the cost, decreasing slightly if 75% of a spell's cost isn't a whole number since the cost is rounded up. 
The 15% HP reduction is quite harsh, with 1900 HP (60 Vigor) being reduced to 1615 HP (roughly 46 Vigor), 1704 HP (50 Vigor) being reduced to 1448 HP (roughly 40 Vigor), and 1450 (40 Vigor) being reduced to 1232 HP (roughly 35 Vigor). Useful for low levels but since this items is only available quite late, it is best if you are quite mindful of the penalty. 
The FP boost means effective Mind becomes greater at higher levels of Mind without it. 221 FP (38 Mind, maximum recover of Flask of Cerulean Tears at +12 with no bonuses elsewhere) becomes 294 FP (roughly 49 Mind), 173 FP (30 Mind) becomes 230 FP (roughly 39 Mind), 121 FP (20 Mind) becomes 161 FP (roughly 28 Mind).

variant.effect: Spells consume less FP, but maximum HP is reduced

name: Primeval Current
description:
The Primeval Current, also known as the procession of stars, is an unseen location in.
The primeval current of glintstone sorcery is intrinsically tied to the cosmic vitality of the stars, shaping both the land and fate of the Lands Between. It is described as a torrent of glintstone flowing from a distant star cluster, often likened to a celestial procession of stars. However, its cosmic mysteries bewitch those who gaze into the current, often driving them to the brink of despair.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
]]
Long ago, the Greater Will triggered a great rupture in the One Great, scattering the ancient life of the stars across the cosmos. This celestial event is seen as the primordial causality that led to fractures, births, and souls.

The first star to arrive on the Lands Between carried Metyr, Mother of Fingers, daughter of the Greater Will. Later, a golden star descended, bearing the Elden Beast, which would become the Elden Ring. Later, many more of these shooting stars would become meteors that struck the Lands Between, giving rise to the Alabaster and Onyx Lords and lifting Farum Azula into the sky. During an age when Fire Giants ruled Flame Peak, an ancient astrologer on the Mountaintops of the Giants perceived the primeval current. Soon, the stars' amber rained down upon the Lands Between. This meteorological phenomenon introduced glintstone and glintstone sorcery to the world.

The Black Moon once hung over Nokstella, guiding countless stars. However, it was lost long ago. The Nox of Nokron used the Fingerslayer Blade against Metyr, a blasphemous act that enraged the Greater Will. In response, the Greater Will sent a malformed star from its lightless abyss through a portal to assault the Eternal Cities. In a hail of meteorites, Astel leveled the Nameless Eternal City and banished the Eternal Cities deep underground, disconnecting the Nox from the true night sky.

The Academy of Raya Lucaria was later founded by two glintstone sorcerers, Azur and Lusat, who sought to uncover the secrets of glintstone and the enigmatic crystalians. Both peered beyond the "wisdom of stone" into the primeval current and were irrevocably changed by what they saw. Azur was left bewitched and haunted by the abyss, while Lusat was shattered after witnessing the dying light of a star cluster. When the Carians, followers of the Moon and allies of the crystalians, gained control of the academy, they suppressed the study of the primeval current. However, Sorceress Sellen defied this ban, obsessively pursuing its secrets. She even transformed fellow sorcerers into Graven Masses—the seeds of stars. For her treachery, the Graven Witch was expelled from the academy.

Shortly after Miquella's vow, Queen Rennala's son Radahn harnessed Gravity Sorceries in defense of Sellia. In the ensuing Starscourge Conflict, Radahn stood alone against the stars—and prevailed. His victory halted their movement, thereby forestalling the fate of his sister, Ranni.

The Demi-Human Queens task their Demi-Human Swordsman with discovering what lies beyond the procession of the stars. Demi-Human Swordmaster Onze sealed himself in the Belurat Gaol to forestall the ruinous fate he perceived.

It is possible Astel used a wormhole to reach the Eternal Cities. or that the Nox unwillingly summoned it through the Eternal Darkness sorcery, the despair that brought about their ruin made manifest

name: Protection of the Erdtree
image: ER Icon Spell Protection of the Erdtree.png
description: Protection of the Erdtree is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree Worship incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed Drop: Altus Plateau
Protection of the Erdtree is obtained upon defeating a Teardrop Scarab located on a square platform upon a hill southeast of the Road of Iniquity Side Path Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Protection of the Erdtree grants a Body Buff that decreases Fire, Holy, Lightning, and Magic damage taken by 30% (10% in PvP) for 70 seconds for the caster and allies within a 6-meter radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 30 FP per cast.
Costs 50 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
This spell reduces damage taken rather than directly increasing damage negation. The total damage reduction can be expressed by the following formula, where ProtectionOfTheErdtree represents the effect magnitude:
TotalAffinityReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - {AffinityDamageNegation} \times 0.01) \times (1 - {ProtectionOfTheErdtree}) )
For example, if affinity damage negation is 25 at the time of casting, the total reduction against PvE enemies would be 51.25%:
TotalAffinityReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.30) ) = 51.25%
Against other players, the total reduction would be 32.5%:
TotalAffinityReduction = 100 ( 1 - (1 - 25 \times 0.01) \times (1 - 0.10) ) = 32.5%

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
The effectiveness of this spell diminishes as non-physical damage negation increases, offering less benefit when stacked with multiple non-physical damage negation sources.
Protection of the Erdtree is a versatile defensive incantation that protects both the caster and allies from multiple damage types, making it invaluable in varied combat scenarios. Due to its accessibility early in the game, it does not require extensive stat investments, allowing many players to utilize it effectively.
This spell is particularly useful against enemies that deal elemental damage, especially during encounters with groups or multi-phase bosses that utilize different affinities.
While it is the weakest defensive Body Buff incantation, it strengthens all non-Physical damage negations, making it useful as a Furled Finger for not having to carry multiple defensive incantations when summoned via Summoning Pools.
Opaline Pickled Liver

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Unlike other advanced defensive incantations, Flame, Protect Me only affects the caster. Therefore, Protection of the Erdtree is the only way to grant nearby allies protection specifically against Fire damage.
Protection of the Erdtree is accessible earlier than its counterparts.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The stars of the night sky influenced fate long ago, and so it was that the Eternal City gathered Starlight Shards in preparation of a special draught. Members of the Nox clergy imbibed cloudy, bluish-black tonics, yielding their bodies and souls to fate, becoming puppets. However, the practice nearly vanished after the Greater Will banished the Nox deep underground.

Crude, handmade dolls, such as the Marionette Soldiers and Avionette Soldiers, were created to serve sorcerers during the age of the Erdtree. They were turned towards martial ends during the Liurnian Wars instigated by the Erdtree. The avionettes swooped through the air with scythes, raining Fire Pots.

Certain puppets become vessels for the souls of others, such as Ranni the Witch and Sorceress Sellen. After the Night of Black Knives, Ranni acquired the puppet of her secret mentor, the Snowy Crone of the deep forest. Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant considered to be the greatest puppet ever created.

name: Putrescent Knight
description: The is a Boss in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Interred within stone coffins and buried at sea in an age long past, the stagnant, congealed remains of tainted heroes eventually drifted toward the Gravesite Plain of the Lands Between, where all Death converges. Though putrescence was once incinerated in ghostflame by Deathbirds, the contents of the vessels leaked and pooled at the bottom of the Stone Coffin Fissure, where they lingered in endless wait for true Death.

When St. Trina fell into the depths of the Fissure, her gentle sleep intensified into a deadly poison. Her nectar-like blood pooled, sprouting flowers, creating the Garden of Deep Purple. A mass of putrescence imbibed this nectar, finding salvation in her velvet, eternal sleep. From this, the putrescence reformed into a Putrescent Knight sworn to Trina.

The Knight is both rider and mount, each lacking functional legs. It wields a vast, crescent-shaped cleaver of human bone and hardened putrescence, its strength drawn from the Knight's arcane power. It conjures putrescence-born Death Sorceries, transmuting liquor into spiritual explosions of bruise-colored ghostflame.

name: Queen Marika the Eternal
description:
Queen Marika the Eternal is the central character in the world of. She is the divine ruler of the Lands Between and the current vessel of the Elden Ring, a god in truth. She grew the towering Erdtree, concealed the Realm of Shadow, and established the Golden Order. By the time of the game's events, she has long vanished from public view, though her influence persists through the Grace of Gold. Her Demigod offspring became shardbearers when they claimed Great Runes that dispersed when she shattered the Elden Ring.

Information about Marika is primarily provided by Melina, Finger Reader Enia, and various item descriptions.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Queen Marika was a tall Numen woman with fair skin and long, flowing golden hair gathered into two uneven braids, the right being longer. She typically wore a circlet, gold armbands, gold serpentine bracelets, and either a black dress or a robe patterned with golden floral motifs. Often depicted in cruciform poses with her head bowed, she simultaneously evoked divinity, fragility, regality, and martyrdom.

In the present era, her body appears as a stone-like, petrified husk, fractured and cracked like broken porcelain. She is shackled and suspended on a great Rune Arc with a red needle-like shard piercing her abdomen like a spear. During the final confrontation, her body transforms into Radagon of the Golden Order before the Elden Beast reveals itself. Following the player's victory, she ultimately reverts to a fractured, statuesque form.

Marika's Rune:
]]

Marika's Rune was the official seal of Queen Marika, used by her to control vassals, bestow grace, and seal away threats to her power.

Bearing a close resemblance to the Rune of Death, Marika's Rune is a Y-shaped Elden Rune with an upward crescent resembling the lower arc of the Elden Ring, believed to be the basin in which its blessing pool. Its shape parallels Marika's crucified form within the Erdtree. Variations of the Rune recur throughout the Lands Between, such as the Effigies of the Martyr, statues found in churches of Marika, and the numerous crosses found throughout Limgrave and Dominula, Windmill Village.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Queen Marika is found near the Fractured Marika site of grace on the Stone Platform within the Erdtree, accessible from Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
.]]

Marika came from the Shaman Village in the Scaduview. Her people had an affinity for trees and flesh that melded harmoniously with that of others. The hornsent tortured and sliced up shamans before stuffing them into the jars to be reborn as saints. The Two Fingers recognized Marika as an Empyrean and bestowed her a shadowbound beast in the form of her half-brother, Maliketh—a faithful follower, incapable of treachery. At some point during this period, Marika took the warrior Hoarah Loux as her consort, who later vowed to become Godfrey, her first Elden Lord. Through seduction and betrayal, she ascended to godhood at the Gate of Divinity atop the tower of Enir-Ilim, and became the vessel for the Elden Ring. This affair led to the birth of the Erdtree and Scadutree, and was considered a betrayal by the Hornsent. The Scadutree veiled the land of shadow upon its creation.

Eventually, Marika returned to the Shaman Village to find it abandoned, the people of her village were stolen away from their home, never to return. After cutting off a braid of her hair as an offering to the Grandmother, she bathed her home in the healing light of gold, knowing full well that there was no one to heal. She would never return again.

Age of the Erdtree:

In the early days, everything was in opposition to the Erdtree. With Godfrey’s aid, Marika waged a War Against the Giants atop the frigid northern mountains, where dwelled the Flame of Ruin capable of burning the Erdtree. Ultimately victorious, Marika was believed to have slain the Fell God of the Fire Giants. Upon learning that the Flame of Ruin would never die, however, she cursed the last of the giants to tend to it for eternity. Marika declared the path to the mountains as Forbidden Lands and excised details of the war from history.

Marika and Godfrey would rule together and have at least three children: Godwyn the Golden and the twins Morgott and Mohg. The twins were both born as accursed Omen and were hidden in the depths below the capital. Even so, Godfrey and his Golden Lineage would be counted as the first of the demigods. Godfrey went on to conquer many lands for the Erdtree.

At some point during Marika's rule, the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her Godskin Apostles wielded the power of god-slaying black flame to carry out a god hunt. Marika thus desired to seal the Rune of Death's power. Her Shadowbound Beast and half-brother Maliketh defeated the Gloam-Eyed Queen and her apostles, and then she extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring. Maliketh sealed it in his black blade, founding the Golden Order and establishing Marika as the one true god.

When the Erdtree sensed its mortality for the first time and released its Golden Seeds to spawn the Minor Erdtrees, revealing itself not as perfect and eternal as those who worshipped it believed it to be, Marika would abandon blind faith and declare at the Minor Erdtree Church her intent to inquire into the depths of her Golden Order in an attempt to strengthen its grace through understanding.

Queen Marika punished the cutting-gifted tribe for discovering the nature of her original sin.

Liurnian Wars:
Queen Marika desired to conquer Liurnia of the Lakes, the land of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and the Carian Royal Family. She declared war on the glintstone sorcerers and sent a golden host led by her secret other half: a red-haired champion named Radagon. The champions of the moon, led by Rennala, repelled the glorious warriors of the Erdtree for a time, but it ended in a draw. In the second Liurnian War, Radagon invades again, but this time, he uses the Celestial Dew at the Church of Vows in a ritual to recant his aggressions and seek absolution. The Carian Queen accepted, and their wrongdoings were washed away. The two were wed and produced three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni.

Crusade:
Marika sent her son Messmer away on a crusade into the lands of the Hornsent. Despite her precautions, her fear of the Abyssal Serpent sealed within him led her to trap him within the Realm of Shadow, where he would wage war to exterminate the Hornsent and devastate their lands. No matter how many of her enemies burned in his flame, however, Messmer received no sign from Marika to end his crusade. Marika kept these events and the land of shadow hidden away and removed from history.

Godfrey's Banishment:
With her rule secure, Marika announced her intention to search the depths of the Golden Order, declaring the early days of blind belief a thing long past. When Godfrey's last foe fell, it was said the hue of his eyes had faded. Marika banished him and his kinfolk from the Lands Between, robbing them of their grace, thus creating the first Tarnished, all in the hope that they would grow stronger by waging war in lands outside her rule, dying, and then eventually being revived with their guidance of grace returned. 

King Consort Radagon:
After Godfrey's banishment from the Lands Between, Marika took Radagon as her second husband and King Consort, elevating him to become the second Elden Lord. Radagon already had three children with Queen Rennala of the Carian Royal Family, and after his union with Marika, she would raise her new step-children, Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni to demigod status.

Marika and Radagon would go on to have two more children of their own, the twins Malenia and Miquella, who like Marika herself and Radagon's daughter Ranni, were Empyreans, and were thus potential successors to Marika. However, Radagon and Marika were in truth the same. Radagon was described as Marika's male "other self". Thus, the twins were the children of a single god, and they were both born afflicted: Malenia with rotting sickness and Miquella with eternal childhood.

Night of Black Knives:
On the Night of Black Knives, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen from Maliketh. For a long time, it was not known who was behind the plot, but it is finally revealed it was in fact Ranni who stole the fragment of the rune to forge god-slaying black knives through a fearsome rite. 

The Black Knife Assassins, Numen women purported to have close ties to Marika herself, used these knives to slay Godwyn the Golden, the first recorded death of a demigod in all history. Queen Marika is said to have been driven to the brink by the death of Godwyn, and she instructed her Demigod children to fight for the positions of Elden Lord and that of godhood.

The Shattering:

Some time after the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika used her Numen hammer to shatter the Elden Ring. Fragments of the ring splintered into Great Runes and spread across the Lands Between, starting a conflict between her demigod children. War after war was fought, but there was no victor. For her part, Marika would be imprisoned inside the Erdtree, possibly by the Elden Beast or the Greater Will itself. 

Game Events:
True to her promise to Godfrey and his warriors, grace was restored to the banished Tarnished. They would rise from their graves and journey to the Lands Between to once again brandish the Elden Ring. The Tarnished formed the Roundtable Hold, where they worked to realize the goal Marika had given them. They would be served by a Misbegotten blacksmith named Hewg, whom Marika herself had charged with smithing a "god-slaying weapon" before his imprisonment in the Hold.

Eventually, the Tarnished manages to fight their way into the Erdtree, where the shattered Marika lies imprisoned. Marika is suddenly released from her bonds, as Radagon asserts control over their shared body and confronts the Tarnished. After defeating Radagon and the Elden Beast itself, the Tarnished may choose what to do with the fractured body of Marika. Marika's head is restored to her frame if the Elden Ring is mended, either by itself or with a Mending Rune. If Ranni is summoned, she picks up Marika's head gently, peacefully dissipating along with the rest of her body. If the Tarnished is the Lord of Frenzied Flame, Marika's head breaks apart and crumbles into ash. 

By choosing to go down the Elden Lord path, whether the regular one or using any of the three Mending Runes to fix the Elden Ring within Marika, the Tarnished champion ushers in a new age. They become the third Elden Lord and effectively Marika's new consort in every one of them, except in the Age of the Stars (where they become consort to Ranni) and in the Lord of Frenzied Flame ending (where they make the whole world burn). However, Queen Marika remains shattered and unresponsive, with only the Elden Ring itself shining brightly within her body.<!--

sections.heading: Echoes of Marika
sections.body: At certain Sites of Grace found in churches, the very words of Queen Marika yet linger. Melina offers to share them with the Tarnished if she is traveling with them. The game does not establish a chronological order for the seven Echoes of Marika. They are as follows:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
When Marika transforms into Radagon, her dress seamlessly shifts into his skirt.
Queen Marika and Lord Radagon wear the same black outfit with gold floral patterns in their side profile paintings at the Roundtable Hold, teasing their secret at an early point in the game's narrative.
The Elden Beast crucified Marika upon a giant Rune Arc and imprisoned her within the Erdtree after she shattered the Elden Ring. The Elden Beast's grab attack similarly crucifies the player on a similar arc and pierces them with golden spears. However, the needle impaling Marika's abdomen is the same color as the Rune of Death.
After shattering the Elden Ring, Marika was punished by the Greater Will. It also is possible Maliketh became a Baleful Shadow, impaled Marika, and, released from the Two Fingers' spell, no longer remembers doing so.

Melina, the Kindling Maiden, is a secret daughter of Marika.
She reads the ancient words of Marika.
She is bound by Grace, states her mother is inside the Erdtree, and later gains freedom of movement upon reaching the base of the Erdtree.
She is associated with Butterflies, fated to fulfill a purpose, and implied to be the younger sister of Messmer the Impaler.
Furthermore, Melina is internally referenced as "MaricaOfDaughter" or "DaughterMarika".

After enduring an eternity of abandonment, Messmer disowns Marika as his mother and curses her with his dying breath.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Marika and Radagon mirror the alchemical White Queen and Red King—a being divided into male and female halves, later reunited as a hermaphroditic Rebis. This reunion symbolizes transcendent power, embodied by a dragon (Elden Beast). This concept represents the culmination of the alchemist's quest to achieve balance and perfection.
In, Marika's Rune was referred to as the "Life Rune."

name: Radagon of the Golden Order
description: Radagon of the Golden Order is a boss in. He is encountered inside the Erdtree in Leyndell, Ashen Capital, and is the first half of the final boss fight, with the Elden Beast as the second half.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Radagon is the first of two enemies that compose the final boss fight of, with the Elden Beast being the second. Players will have to fight Radagon again if they die to the Elden Beast.

Moveset:

Phase 1:
Radagon relies on very fast hammer swings, and some of his attacks will generate shockwaves. These shockwaves will either be immediate, or will occur after a brief delay- for the latter, golden cracks will appear in the ground moments before the explosion.

At range, Radagon can throw golden spears at the player. He will either leap into the air and throw a single, giant spear, or quickly hurl five spears in a loose fan. These spears will remain in the ground for a second before exploding. He also has a grab attack which he may perform at close- or mid-range. During the grab, his left arm will glow gold and he will wind it back behind him before lunging. The shockwave generated by the grab may still cause damage even if the grab itself misses. 

All of his gold attacks will inflict Holy damage.

Phase 2:
After his health has been lowered somewhat, he will leap into the air and perform a Gold Breaker attack, creating a large area of effect shockwave. During this phase, Radagon will sometimes teleport, generating an explosion when he reappears. In addition to the golden spear attacks used in the previous phase, he may now jump up and throw a volley of spears. His stomp will also now create a shockwave that deals Holy damage.

Phase 3:
Once his health is below half, Radagon will teleport into the middle of the arena and perform three rapid hammer strikes on the ground, each producing a large shockwave. He will now teleport much more often, and can perform two shockwave-inducing hammer strikes in quick succession.

Environment:
The arena is a featureless, oval platform with no obstacles. It is not possible to fall of the edges.

Strategies:
This boss can be cheesed by running up to him as soon as possible and blocking his way. The AI doesn't become aggressive until it has made a certain number of steps, so you can take him down with ease as long as you have a way to deal damage without moving (bows, damage dealing auras, etc). This can also be done by running up to him as soon as possible, performing a jump attack (so landing too low for his line of sight), and quickly sidestepping behind him. You are then most likely free to make multiple strong attacks on him until his guard is broken, perform a critical hit, charge a strong attack again while he's standing up, and start the fight proper at that point onward with roughly half his health already gone.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Radagon needs to be parried multiple times to trigger a stagger.
Radagon was said to have despised his own red hair, as it was perhaps the result of a curse by red-haired Fire Giants. Ironically, most of his children would inherit it, and some of them would even be proud of its heroic implications.
Radagon's rune can be seen in Radagon's Scarseal, Radagon's Soreseal, and in the thorns blocking the Erdtree. It resembles the criss-cross pattern seen in his statues, and is reminiscent of a sewing pattern, as he was also associated with sewing needles, perhaps symbolizing his need to keep things held together.
The Radagon Icon mentions how he studied sorcery as husband of Rennala, and incantations as husband of Marika, aspiring to be complete.
When Marika's body changes into Radagon, her dress becomes his skirt.
Queen Marika and Lord Radagon wear the same black outfit with gold floral patterns in their side profile paintings at the Roundtable Hold, teasing their secret at an early point in the game's narrative.
The Revenant's ghost stares at a Radagon painting at the Roundtable Hold in.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal name: MaricaOfDistorted (ID: 2190)
Radagon/Marika are reminiscent of the alchemical Red King and White Queen, who are often depicted as the two halves of the Rebis. In alchemy, the Rebis is a single being possessing both male and female qualities, also sometimes referred to as the divine hermaphrodite. It is said that the Rebis originated from a being that was divided into male and female halves, until it was unified again to form a transcendental being empowered by a dragon.
Lord Radagon prophesied the Tarnisheds' return in.

| colspan="2" |Imbues his hammer with golden light and swings it in an arc in front of himself. Golden cracks appear in the ground in front of him covering a large area which then erupt with golden energy.

| colspan="2" |Radagon's left arm turns gold as he pulls it back, and then lunges at the player in an attempt to grab them. If the grab is successful he strikes them with his hammer. If the grab misses, a small shockwave is created where his hand hits the ground.
| colspan="2" |Imbues his hammer with golden light and smashes the ground with it. This produces a small shockwave where the hammer hands, after a brief delay.
| colspan="2" |Thrusts his hammer straight forwards. May perform this after a stomp.
| colspan="2" |Closes distance by rushing towards the player, swinging his axe.
| colspan="2" |Leaps into the air and throws a golden spear at the player. The spear remains in the ground for a short amount of time before exploding.
| colspan="2" |Throws five small golden spears in a fan formation. The spears will dig into the ground and then explode. In phase 2 he will immediately throw another five spears.
| colspan="2" |Leaps into the air and hovers for a moment, before smashing into the ground with his hammer, creating a large shockwave around him.
| colspan="2" |Disappears and reappears somewhere else in the arena, creating an explosion when he reappears. Often performs an attack immediately after appearing.

| colspan="2" |Leaps into the air and produces a golden spear in his hand. Plunges the spear into the ground, creating a criss-cross pattern on the ground which drains the player's HP if they stand in it.
| colspan="2" |Leaps into the air and throws many golden spears at once.

| colspan="2" |Teleports to the centre of the arena and smashes his hammer into the ground three times, which each impact producing a larger shockwave. The third strike has a longer delay than the first two, and leaves an impression of the Elden Ring on the ground.
| colspan="2" |After teleporting, rushes the player and slams his hammer into the ground, creating a shockwave. Immediately follows with a second slam and shockwave.

Radagon relies on very fast hammer swings, and some of his attacks will generate shockwaves. These shockwaves will either be immediate, or will occur after a brief delay- for the latter, golden cracks will appear in the ground moments before the explosion.

At range, Radagon can throw golden spears at the player. He will either leap into the air and throw a single, giant spear, or quickly hurl five spears in a loose fan. These spears will remain in the ground for a second before exploding. He also has a grab attack which he may perform at close- or mid-range. During the grab, his left arm will glow gold and he will wind it back behind him before lunging. The shockwave generated by the grab may still cause damage even if the grab itself misses.
All of his gold attacks will inflict Holy damage.

After his health has been lowered somewhat, he will leap into the air and perform a Gold Breaker attack, creating a large area of effect shockwave. During this phase, Radagon will sometimes teleport, generating an explosion when he reappears. In addition to the golden spear attacks used in the previous phase, he may now jump up and throw a volley of spears. His stomp will also now create a shockwave that deals Holy damage.

Once his health is below half, Radagon will teleport into the middle of the arena and perform three rapid hammer strikes on the ground, each producing a large shockwave. He will now teleport much more often, and can perform two shockwave-inducing hammer strikes in quick succession.
The arena is a featureless, oval platform with no obstacles. It is not possible to fall of the edges.

This boss can be cheesed by running up to him as soon as possible and blocking his way. The AI doesn't become aggressive until it has made a certain number of steps, so you can take him down with ease as long as you have a way to deal damage without moving (bows, damage dealing auras, etc). This can also be done by running up to him as soon as possible, performing a jump attack (so landing too low for his line of sight), and quickly sidestepping behind him. You are then most likely free to make multiple strong attacks on him until his guard is broken, perform a critical hit, charge a strong attack again while he's standing up, and start the fight proper at that point onward with roughly half his health already gone.

description: Radagon's Rings of Light is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Liurnia of the Lakes / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 7,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn or Miriel, Pastor of Vows after giving either of them the Golden Order Principia.
Should the prayerbook be given to one of them and then have that instructor die before purchasing this Incantation, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them the respective tutor's Bell Bearing.
WARNING: Should both Corhyn and Miriel die before giving either of them the prayerbook then this incantation becomes unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Creates a halo of light above the caster's head, which is then thrown out as an expanding ring of light around them, with Holy Attack Power equal to 310% of Incantation Scaling. 

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 395% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 37 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 48 points of Stamina. 
Deals 10 Stance damage on a hit, increasing to 14 Stance damage if charged. 
Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 27%, wearing this talisman increases Attack Power by a total of 46%.
While its large hitbox would seem able to hit large targets multiple times, it can actually only hit a target once. 
This makes it less able to hit weak spots on large foes, since the large hitbox can fairly easily hit another, non-weak body part beforehand.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Actually consists of 16 separate but overlapping projectiles. 
Patch 1.07 reduced FP consumption and recovery time.
FP cost was reduced from 25 to 21. 
Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost, increased damage, and cast speed. Decreased recovery time.
FP cost was reduced from 29 to 25.
Attack Power was increased from 282% of Incantation Scaling to 310% of the same for the uncharged version and from 333% of Incantation Scaling to 395% of the same for the charged version.

name: Ranni the Witch
description: Ranni the Witch, also known as Lunar Princess Ranni and Renna the Witch, is a character in. She is one of the Demigods, and the focus of one of the game's most elaborate questlines.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A child born of the union between Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon and red-haired Radagon during the age of the Erdtree, Ranni embodied an alliance between Raya Lucaria and Leyndell. She had two older brothers, Radahn and Rykard. As a daughter of Carian royalty, she was a Lunar Princess, and raised in accordance with tradition. Led by the hand of her mother, young Ranni encountered her Dark Moon—cold, dark, and veiled in occult mystery. 

The Two Fingers named Ranni as an Empyrean, one with the potential to one day succeed Queen Marika as the divine ruler of the Lands Between, and granted her a Shadowbound Beast named Blaidd to be her vassal. He was approved of by Rennala and was raised as her foster brother. Ranni grew up playing with Blaidd, and they were often accompanied by Iji, a troll blacksmith who served the Carian royals. 

At some point, Ranni's father abandoned her mother to marry Queen Marika and assume the title of second Elden Lord. Although Ranni and her siblings were raised to Demigod status by their new stepmother, their heartbroken mother was left indisposed, cradling her Amber Egg in all-consuming grief.

Ranni later ventured deep in woods, where she encountered a snowy crone who became her secret mentor. She was an old witch well versed in cold-based sorceries, and she taught Ranni to fear the Dark Moon as she imparted her magic. The full Dark Moon, cold and leaden, would become Ranni's sigil and symbol of her power and authority. 

The Night of Black Knives:

Although the Two Fingers had chosen her as Marika's successor, Ranni did not wish to be a puppet for the Greater Will and resented her Empyrean fate. In order to escape it, Ranni stole a fragment of the Rune of Death from Maliketh, the Black Blade and, through a fearsome rite, imbued it into the blades of Numen assassins, who were said to be close to Queen Marika herself. She also gave a fragment to her brother Rykard as a last resort, so he could kill Maliketh if necessary. Ranni plotted for the assassins to kill another individual while she simultaneously killed herself, slaying her own body while the other person died in spirit, thus freeing herself from being an Empyrean. 

In what would become known as the Night of Black Knives, the assassins murdered Godwyn the Golden, killing him in spirit, while Ranni killed herself in body, transferring her spirit into a doll said to be modeled after the image of her mentor, the Snow Witch. This marked the step-siblings as the first demigod casualties in history. Ranni's fate and her involvement in the plot remained largely unknown by the denizens of the Lands Between. 

The Shattering:
At some point after the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring. Ranni claimed a Great Rune, but appears to have discarded it, and largely remained outside of the conflict that followed. As a consequence of her doll body, Ranni required extended periods of hibernation and withdrew from the world, hiding in the Carian Manor while her agents worked to bring about her plan of ridding the Lands Between of the influence of the Greater Will, allowing her to pursue her divine ascension on her own terms.

Game events:

After the Shattering, Ranni learned of a recently arrived Tarnished riding the spectral steed, Torrent. She approached them at the Church of Elleh, inquiring whether they possess the steed that once accompanied Melina. Upon confirming her suspicions, she bestowed upon them a Spirit Calling Bell and Lone Wolf Ashes, explaining that Torrent’s former master had entrusted her with delivering these items to its next owner.

Ranni later reunited with the Tarnished at her Rise in the Three Sisters, where she invited them into her service. She tasked the Tarnished with aiding Blaidd in uncovering a path into Nokron, Eternal City, to claim its treasure—a weapon capable of slaying the Two Fingers who had chosen her as an Empyrean. However, the path to Nokron would only reveal itself with the death of her brother, Starscourge Radahn, who had long held the stars—and thus Ranni's fate—in stasis with gravity magic.

After Radahn's defeat and the acquisition of the Fingerslayer Blade, Ranni descended to the Ainsel River Main, leading to Nokstella, Eternal City. There, she commanded her champion to rid her of the Baleful Shadows sent by the Two Fingers to assassinate her. Upon their victory, Ranni rewarded the Tarnished with a key to a Carian chest containing the Dark Moon Ring. Then, Ranni departed to fulfill her dark purpose. She traveled to the Cathedral of Manus Celes on the Moonlight Altar, where she slew the great Two Fingers beneath it and abandoned her doll body.

If the Tarnished retrieved the Dark Moon Ring and presented it to Ranni's doll, she accepted them as her consort, granting them the Dark Moon Greatsword as a symbol of their union. She revealed the full extent of her plan: to succeed Queen Marika as god and bring about the Age of the Stars. Ranni intends to remove the Elden Ring from the Lands Between and journey into the cosmos, freeing its inhabitants from the influence of the Greater Will and granting them true autonomy over their lives.

After defeating the Elden Beast, the Tarnished may summon Ranni, who ushers in the Dark Moon and her Age of the Stars, realizing her vision for a new Order.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: Ranni's disembodied spirit inhabits the woven puppet of a four-armed maiden with pallid blue skin and long, flowing blue hair. Her left eye—the doll's right—is sealed shut by an azure sigil, while both open eyes glow cyan. She wears an elegant white gown beneath a voluminous fur cloak, lined with two long brown braids. A massive, floppy-brimmed witch’s hat rests atop her head, crowned with a delicate silver filigree. Luminious blue veinwork runs throughout the frozen brim's cold underside.

sections.heading: Ranni's Quest
sections.body:
Completing Ranni's quest will result in the "Age of the Stars" ending.
Her questline intersects with the following NPCs: Blaidd the Half-Wolf, Castellan Jerren, Fia, Deathbed Companion, Pidia, Carian Servant, Preceptor Seluvis, Smithing Master Iji, and Sorcerer Rogier.

Quest items:

Questline progression:
(Optional) Church of Elleh
After meeting Melina and obtaining the Spectral Steed Whistle, use Torrent at least once. After that, rest on any Site of Grace. Then, fast travel to the Church of Elleh Site of Grace and find Ranni (using the pseudonym "Renna the Witch") sitting on a broken wall. Exhaust her dialogue to receive the Spirit Calling Bell and Lone Wolf Ashes for free.
If you miss this step, these items will be available for purchase at the Twin Maiden Husks in Roundtable Hold— 200 runes for the Lone Wolf Ashes and 1,000 runes for the Spirit Calling Bell respectively.
Caria Manor
Traverse Caria Manor in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes.
Defeat the apparition of Royal Knight Loretta at the Royal Moongazing Grounds, which unlocks the path to Three Sisters behind her.
Ranni's Rise
Ranni can next be encountered on the top floor of her Rise in the Three Sisters. This stage varies depending on whether you have met her before, defeated Starscourge Radahn, or given Sorcerer Rogier the Black Knifeprint.
Agree to become one of Ranni's vassals, and then head back down the tower to speak to the projections of Iji, Blaidd, and Seluvis. After speaking to all three, return to Ranni and speak to her again. After this point, if you return to Ranni, she will be sleeping and non-responsive.
(Optional) Administer Preceptor Seluvis's Amber Draught to Ranni. She will awaken. Speak to her three times, and she will banish you from her sight.
WARNING: This will permanently end Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant's quests.
WARNING: Ranni's questline will no longer progress; however, this can be undone by using Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows.
Caelid
Defeat Starscourge Radahn to resume the movement of the stars.
Nokron, Eternal City
Nokron can only be accessed via the Starfall Crater in east Limgrave after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
Proceed through the area to obtain the Fingerslayer Blade, which is in a chest northeast of the Night's Sacred Ground Site of Grace.
Three Sisters
Travel to Ranni's Rise and deliver the Fingerslayer Blade to Ranni, who will give you the Carian Inverted Statue.
This key item is required to progress Fia, Deathbed Companion's questline. However, it is not necessary to complete Ranni's quest.
WARNING: This will permanently end Preceptor Seluvis and Pidia, Carian Servant's quest.
Travel to Renna's Rise, which unseals after Ranni departs with the Fingerslayer Blade. Enter and climb to the top, and go through the Sending Gate to the upper portion of Ainsel River.
Ainsel River Main 
Pick up the Miniature Ranni near the spawn point and rest at the Ainsel River Main Site of Grace. Use the "Talk to miniature Ranni" option three times to get her to speak.
Nokstella, Eternal City
(Optional) Ranni will also have dialogue at the Nokstella, Eternal City and Nokstella Waterfall Basin Sites of Grace. These are not required to continue her questline.
Defeat the Baleful Shadow invader just past the Nokstella Waterfall Basin Site of Grace to obtain the Discarded Palace Key.
Academy of Raya Lucaria
Defeat Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon at the Raya Lucaria Grand Library.
Unlock the chest behind Rennala and obtain the Dark Moon Ring.
Lake of Rot
Ride the Transportation Coffin at the Grand Cloister. Defeat Astel, Naturalborn of the Void and then travel up the lift. However, this lift remains locked until the player obtains the Dark Moon Ring.
Moonlight Altar
Travel to the Cathedral of Manus Celes and descend through the tunnel near the altar to find Ranni sitting on the corpse of her Two Fingers. Interact with her to trigger a cutscene. After the cutscene, speak to her again, and she will disappear, bequeathing the Dark Moon Greatsword.
Stone Platform
After defeating the final boss, there will be a blue summon sign beside Fractured Marika. Interact with it to summon Ranni, allowing you to achieve the Age of the Stars ending.
WARNING: Ranni's summon sign will not appear if the player has met with the Three Fingers. This can be undone by defeating both Malenia, Goddess of Rot and Dragonlord Placidusax, and using Miquella's Needle in the latter's boss arena at Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Wears the Snow Witch Set: Snow Witch Hat, Snow Witch Robe, Snow Witch Skirt

Ranni cannot be killed but will vanish if attacked. She will reappear if the player uses Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows.

Ranni inhabits a doll body resembling the Snow Witch, her former master. She later inhabits miniature versions of it. It is unclear whether it was made by the Nox of the Eternal Cities, Ranni, or the snow witch herself.

Ranni's original Empyrean body can be found atop the Divine Tower of Liurnia and still possesses one-half of the Cursemark of Death.
Examining the blackened remains closely reveals hints of red hair on her head, which is characteristic of a daughter of Radagon.
Ranni's original body has two arms, while her doll body has four. It is thus similar to Miquella the Kind and the Marionette soldiers utilized by Sorcerers throughout the game.
The Stargazer Heirloom can be found on her body as well, a memento of her mother Rennala.

Certain stages of Ranni's questline trigger Seluvis to go inert and Pidia to die at the hands of puppets of Raya Lucaria Soldiers. This outcome occurs either if Ranni is offered the Amber Draught or after she receives the Fingerslayer Blade and departs from Caria Manor.
The Cuckoo soldiers participated in the Siege of Caria Manor but were defeated by the Carian's magic.

If the player administers the Amber Draught to Ranni, she will awaken and express her disappointment in them for indulging Seluvis before banishing them from her sight. Should the player persist in attempting to speak with her, Ranni will instantly kill them. This transgression may also be forgiven through absolution at the Church of Vows.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Ranni's body was imbued with frost magic, releasing a cold so intense that even Blaidd, that covered his armor with a pelt, was still bothered.
When in her doll form at Ranni's Rise, she is sitting on top of a bunch of books covered by a piece of fabric, making her seem taller than she appears. She also applies the same trick when introducing herself as "Renna", sitting on a low ruined wall at the Church Of Elleh.
Prior to the release of, Ranni narrated the Story Trailer and was referrer to as the Storyteller and the Snow Witch in promotional material.
The dialogue spoken by Ranni during the Age of the Stars ending differs between English and Japanese. Although it is not a direct translation, the overall message is maintained.
She was called Enchantress Ranni in cut content.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found inside Sage's Cave, located in Altus Plateau. They can be found inside a chest just beyond a room containing four skeletons, hidden behind an illusionary wall.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Raptor Talons are a pair of Claws that scale primarily with Strength and Dexterity, and attacks with Slashing and Piercing damage, as well as applying Blood Loss to enemies. As the in-game description suggests, the Raptor Talons also do increased damage with jump attacks (roughly 10% more).
While they have a somewhat short reach compared to other weapons, the Raptor Talons are fast, lightweight, and come in pairs, with the Tarnished brandishing one set of claws in each hand when wielding the Raptor Talons "two-handed".

sections.body:
Guide Stele (Map: Rauh Ruins): located west of the Ancient Ruins Base. Acquisition requires traversing a canyon corridor guarded by two Guardian Golems. Continuing southwest from the Guide Stele leads directly to the Temple Town Ruins site of grace. 
Spiritspring

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.body:
North of the Ancient Ruins Base, the roadway contains Messmer Soldier patrols and two loot Scarabs: one on the road yielding a [[Somber Smithing Stone 7|Somber Smithing Stone [7]]], and a second on a pillar containing Ash of War: Scattershot Throw. Beyond the archway lies a ruined structure that grants access to Taylew's Ruined Forge. 

A small lake west-southwest of the forge contains a gathering of Bloodfiends and a Bloodfiend Hexer, who bears the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear. Nearby cliff shadows hold a corpse with a [[Shadow Realm Rune 3|Shadow Realm Rune [3]]], and a small southern encampment contains the Pearl Shield Talisman. A Rauh Burrow can be reached by traveling west-southwest from the Ancient Ruins Base, positioned atop collapsed masonry. 

A locked Spiritspring east of the Temple Town Ruins Guide Stele can be activated by destroying a marked boulder south-southwest along the path. The spiritspring leads to the Northern Nameless Mausoleum, which houses a humanoid mausoleum boss that awards a distinct weapon and armor set upon defeat. 

Temple Town Ruins includes several notable items across its periphery: a [[Grave Glovewort 5|Grave Glovewort [5]]] to the west, [[Smithing Stone 3|Smithing Stone [3]]] deposits to the east, and a Revered Spirit Ash within a southern ruined dwelling. Entry into the central complex may be gained through a collapsed southern wall. Within the settlement, players can obtain Beast Blood, a [[Somber Smithing Stone 3|Somber Smithing Stone [3]]], a Scadutree Fragment located beyond the rooftop route, and the Two-Handed Sword Talisman stored in an upper structure guarded by a Horned Warrior. 

The northern ravine contains multiple spiritsprings and elevated ruins. A chest atop the first cliff holds Beast Horns, and a further ascent yields a [[Smithing Stone 7|Smithing Stone [7]]] and the ashes of Divine Bird Warrior Ornis within a small stone shelter. 

Continuing northwest along the river, an altar accessed via a ramp of avian Gravebird statues contains the Gravebird's Blackquill Armor. A nearby cave includes a poison trap and stores Fire Spritestones with [[Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook 1|Antiquity Scholar's Cookbook [1]]]. Additional items in the river include Preserving Boluses and Ash of War: The Poison Flower Blooms Twice. The Ravine North site of grace stands at the northern hilltop. 

Northwest of the Ravine North grace, a woodland inhabited by multiple Bears leads to the Gloried Highlander Set and the lair of Rugalea the Great Red Bear, who drops the Roar of Rugalea. At night, gravemarker fairy circle in the northern sector surrounds a Larval Tear. A nearby mound contains [[Greater Potentate's Cookbook 8|Greater Potentate's Cookbook [8]]]. 

The river west and south from Ravine North contains numerous Flying Spider Scorpions, and leads to a hazy area filled with coffins and statues. [[Ghost Glovewort 2|Ghost Glovewort [2]]] marks the approach to the Scorpion River Catacombs, its entrance guarded by Shadow Militiamen. The dungeon contains several unique items and culminates in a boss encounter with a Death Knight who wields the Death Knight's Longhaft Axe and drops the Cerulean Amber Medallion +3. Additional items in the catacombs include Black Knight Captain Huw, Imp Head (Lion), Knight's Lightning Spear, and [[Ancient Dragon Knight's Cookbook 2|Ancient Dragon Knight's Cookbook [2]]].

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Three Rosus Statues line the path to Scorpion River Catacombs, one for each Catacombs in the Realm of Shadow, though they all face towards the same area.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Situated at one of the Academy of Raya Lucaria's highest points, the Raya Lucaria Grand Library was the hub of knowledge in Liurnia of the Lakes during the age of the Erdtree. It was where Queen Rennala was sequestered following her abandonment by Radagon, and remained since the subsequent Liurnian Civil War that ignited when the Knights of the Cuckoo betrayed and invaded the Carians. Here, Rennala cradled an amber egg, the Great Rune of the Unborn Demigods—a final farewell present from Lord Radagon. She dedicated herself to the forbidden art of rebirth, producing countless Juvenile Scholars, her sweet children.

name: Redeemer Guilbert
description: Redeemer Guilbert, also known as Mercenary Swordsman, was an NPC character that was cut from the final version of. Information about Guilbert and his associated content may no longer be canonical.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Redeemer Guilbert was victimized as a child and nursed a deep-seated grudge. Powerless to exact his own revenge, he prayed to the God of Vengeance. Soon after, a do-gooder appeared and slew his tormentor.

In time, Guilbert became a Redeemer of vengeance. He fought on behalf of the meek and the weak, and claimed to sense acts of revenge as they occured.

After the Battle of Aeonia, Guilbert swore an oath to avenge General Radahn. He vowed to defeat Malenia the Rotted.

Game events:
Guilbert's first in-game target was Crucible Knight Ordovis, a boss trapped within the Erdtree-Gazing Evergaol. If summoned as a Cooperator for this fight, Guilbert later recounted a dream in which he fought alongside the Tarnished to avenge those wronged by Ordovis.

Afterward, Guilbert began to contemplate Radahn's grievances and declared Godrick the Grafted to be his next target. He traveled to Stormveil Castle, where he supposedly gave the player a Key Item. This item could be delivered to Roundtable Knight Vyke, then located beside the Rampart Tower Site of Grace, who would have given Neutralizing Boluses in exchange. Guilbert's mission was to slay Godrick to avenge those who had been grafted, and was summonable near the Secluded Cell Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Character information
sections.body:
Location:
Guilbert was initially located beneath a Fallen Ruin to the south of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins in the spot Bloody Finger Hunter Yura now occupies.

Summon sign:
Guilbert's summon sign (Mercenary Swordsman) was available when facing Crucible Knight Floh at the Erdtree-Gazing Evergaol (now Forlorn Hound Evergaol). This encounter was replaced with Blaidd the Half-Wolf and Bloodhound Knight Darriwil.

If Guilbert moved to Stormveil Castle, he would be summoned to fight Godrick the Grafted. Additionally, he was planned to give an item that would prompt Roundtable Knight Vyke to offer his summon sign as well.

Equipment:
Guilbert wore the Eccentric's Set and wielded the Claymore; however, he dropped the Flamberge upon death.

Quest items:

Questline steps:
(Optional) Limgrave and Stormhill
Redeemer Guilbert will Invade the player if they killed Merchant Kalé or any of his Nomadic Merchant brothers.
Dragon-Burnt Ruins

Stormveil Castle
Guilbert will stand in the throne room. There is no direct information about what he would do here.
(Optional?) Receive a nameless Key Item from Guilbert?
Give it to Roundtable Knight Vyke to receive Neutralizing Boluses and enable his summon sign for Godrick the Grafted. 
Defeat Godrick the Grafted.
(Optional) Summon Guilbert from his gold summon sign and defeat Godrick the Grafted.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Redeemer Guilbert's questline would have intersected with cut questlines for Roundtable Knight Vyke, Merchant Kalé, and the Nomadic Merchants. He would have provided foreshadowing for Smithing Master Hewg.
Defeating Guilbert's invasion would display "Redeemer Died" on the screen.
Having Redeemer Guilbert invade the murderous player incentivized using Celestial Dew to receive absolution at the Church of Vows. 
Only Guilbert's audio files seem to remain in the current build of the game.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Guilbert was likely reworked into a few different characters:
Bloody Finger Hunter Yura: they share a voice actor and use a similar manner of speech. Their initial friendly encounters are placed in the same spot beneath the Fallen Ruin outside Dragon-Burnt Ruins. They are both driven to bring justice to wrongdoers on behalf of the downtrodden (Yura is a Hunter of Bloody Fingers).
Castellan Jerren: other elements, such as the Eccentric's Set, Flamberge, and oath to General Radahn, are part of Witch-Hunter Jerren's character.
Edgar the Revenger, Hornsent, Revenger: they are each vengeance-obsessed Revengers.
In the Chinese version 1.00 of Elden Ring, the text description for the Flamberge referenced the Redeemers and the God of Vengeance.
Guilbert's dialogue places Smithing Master Hewg in Stormhill at Stormhill Shack (then Scavenger's Shack, a hub for NPCs) at this point of 's development. This location is now occupied by his counterpart, Roderika, Spirit Tuner.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Dropped by Bloody Finger Nerijus near Murkwater Cave once defeated.
Beware that progressing through the game can prevent this invasion from happening, more specifically by defeating all the major Limgrave bosses (Flying Dragon Agheel, Mad Pumpkin Head, Margit, the Fell Omen, Tibia Mariner, and Tree Sentinel).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Its skill, Reduvia Blood Blade, is essentially a version of the Blood Blade skill that costs twice as much FP and deals a little less Stance damage in exchange for not costing any HP to cast and having 50% more base Blood Loss (90 instead of 60). 
Since this skill hits with both the projectile and the blade, it deals much more damage and inflicts more Blood Loss build-up when used within the dagger's range.
Ultimately, Blood Blade will do about 4% more damage at half cost with equivalent Arcane and an Occult affinity, making it the stronger alternative if the user is willing to stomach the self-damage and the relatively lower Blood Loss isn't a problem. 
Not counting the Wakizashi this is the strongest dagger for a hybrid Dexterity/Arcane build and the second strongest dagger for a hybrid Strength/Arcane or pure Arcane build, after the Bloodstained Dagger.
However, the Bloodstained's advantage is rather slight, only 8 AP (Attack Power) for the Str/Arc build and a mere 1 AP for the pure Arc build and the Reduvia will consistently have 10 more points of Blood Loss build-up.
Since this weapon has innate Arcane-scaling its innate Blood Loss will scales with that stat. 
The Bandit starting Origin has enough stats to wield this quite strong weapon without any level ups or stat increases.

name: Regal Ancestor Spirit
description: The Regal Ancestor Spirit is an optional Remembrance boss in. It is encountered at the northern Hallowhorn Grounds along the Siofra River after lighting six bonfires.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Deer-like spirits found in Siofra River. They exist beyond the purview of the Erdtree, and follow the principle that life sprouts from death as it does from birth. This process is reflected by their horns, which sprout new growths even after the ancestor's death. Shamans of the Ancestral Followers don headdresses fashioned from horns with buds, mirroring the appearance of the ancestor spirits.

Ancestor Spirits appear emaciated, with exposed ribs, matted fur, and cavities in their chests. They have large, antler-like horns which glow and sprout small buds.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: An Ancestor Spirit is found in the upper part of Siofra River at the northern Hallowhorn Grounds, north-east of Night's Sacred Ground and the Ancestral Woods Site of Grace. Much like the other Ancestor Spirit, this one can only be fought after lighting flames- in this case six- in the surrounding area and then touching the horned remains.

sections.heading: Boss fight
sections.body:
Although it initially fights in much the same way as the standard Ancestor Spirit, once its health has been reduce to half it will start to heal itself by siphoning HP from the player, as well as from the spirit animals in the arena. It will also sometimes collapse and fade away, and then emerge from one of the other animals in the arena. It can also use abilities reminiscent of other animals- hopping like a springhare, charging like a boar, or curling into a ball and rolling like a goat.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Using this item will make the player-character brace themselves for a second before unleashing a close-ranged explosion that'll launch human-sized (or smaller) opponents away from them before sending out 10 long-ranged wraith projectiles that'll track any target that the user was locked on to as they were ejected from their body. These wraiths travel in three groups, the first two groups being comprised of 3 projectiles each and the final having 4, each group also have their own defined travel speed, leading to three distinct rolling windows whenever the player is fighting against this tool in PvP.

As it deals Holy Damage; any holy-boosting equipment or spell will further increase the damage from this item.
Each piece of the Omen Set will also increase the damage of this item by 5%, meaning wearing the full set will increase it by 20%.

description: Regalia of Eochaid is a straight sword in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: On a ledge at the beach bordering Caelid and Limgrave, to the east of the Third Church of Marika. It can be reached through the Gaol Cave or by using Torrent to perform some tricky jumps to ascend the cliff face onto its ledge.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The skill, Eochaid's Dancing Blade, is both chargeable (benefiting from the Godfrey Icon) and actually counts for repeated-hits boosters such as the Winged Sword Insignias and Thorny Cracked Tear, something many other repeated-hits skills such as the Ghiza's Wheel's skill Spinning Wheel or the Ornamental Straight Sword's skill Golden Tempering's special heavy attacks don't. 
It's however somewhat outclassed by the Marais Executioner's Sword when it comes to dealing damage with the skill, as the latter is a Greatsword and thus has greater Attack Power for the skill to be based off. 
Since the skill's damage is based entirely of off the weapon's base Attack Power, and about a third of the Regalia's damage is Magic damage, Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear and Terra Magica functionally give +7% damage and +12% damage respectively if they can be set up beforehand. 
Though both the Dexterity-scaling and the Arcane-scaling may appear equal, and technically are as both are valued at 0.66, the Arcane-scaling actually applies to BOTH the Physical damage and the Magic damage. This effectively places it as a mid-tier B-scaling (1.08 scaling instead of 0.66 scaling). However, due to scaling falling off around 54 points in a damage stat (see the Weapon Scaling page) a hybrid Dexterity/Arcane build holds up fairly well. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Arcane grants 631 Attack Power (AP), 45 Dexterity and 45 Arcane grants 618 AP, and 80 Dexterity grants 561 AP. 
With a pure Arcane build this weapon will outmatch Occult affinity Straight Swords by 90-100 AP. As this is largely due to the innate Magic damage, this can be somewhat misleading in its performance if enemies are resistant to that damage type.
