name: Rejection
description: Rejection is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Sold for 1,500 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this Incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Rejection produces a shockwave, knocking back enemies within a 2-meter radius and inflicting heavy Stamina damage to guarding enemies—180 in PvE and 220 in PvP—while also dealing 10 Stance damage.

Charging the spell increases the radius to 4 meters, Stamina damage to 220 in PvE and 275 in PvP, and Stance damage to 14.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 9 FP per cast.
Costs 24 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 31.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
Rejection has 0 Attack Power and deals no damage.
Knockback occurs in the direction the caster is facing.

Strategies:
The player model is just under 2 meters tall, making it a useful reference for measuring the spell's reach.
Although this incantation deals no damage, it can instantly kill enemies or other players by knocking them off edges.
This spell easily knocks down most flying or jumping foes and can be used to break the Stance of many enemies.
The knockback effect applies to Crystalians even while armored, breaking their Stance in 7 hits, or 5 hits if charged.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Rejection is one of the few offensive spells that deal no damage.
Although this spell is affected by the Godfrey Icon when charged, its 0 damage output makes the 15% damage boost irrelevant.
Patch 1.07: Increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies. 
This increased the Stamina damage against guarding enemies from 150 to 180 when uncharged and from 180 to 220 when charged.
Stamina damage against guarding players was instead increased to 220 when uncharged and 275 when charged.

name: Rellana, Twin Moon Knight
description: Rellana, Twin Moon Knight is a Boss in Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. She is encountered in Castle Ensis.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A scion of the moon-worshipping Carian royal family, Lunar Princess Rellana was the younger sister of Rennala, the Full Moon Witch. As young girls, the sisters encountered the twin moons, which overlapped, as if nestled against one another. Taught sorcery by the illustrious Count Ymir, Rellana later became an enchanted Carian Knight.

Rellana was drawn to Messmer. In the days leading up to the crusade, the gallant Twin Moon Knight disavowed her birthright, entering ritual combat at the colosseum to demonstrate her fidelity to the Erdtree. Her sister, by then Carian Queen, accepted her abdication and sanctioned her quest, bequeathing a length of her lustrous black hair. Rellana and a group of her Carian Knights joined Messmer's crusade, knowing full well that not even the brilliance of the moon could grant him succor.

After claiming Castle Ensis in the Realm of Shadow, Rellana's lunar sorcery shattered a linchpin stone at Moorth Ruins, triggering a landslide that sank much of the hornsent settlement into the earth. Before long, Rellana was known as the Sword of Messmer.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Rellana is an optional boss as she can be bypassed via the sealed Spiritspring in Gravesite Plain to enter Scadu Altus. 

Needle Knight Leda can be summoned to fight this boss. However, her summon sign will not be available after entering Shadow Keep Castle for the first time.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The Twin Moon Knight, Rellana's soundtrack, is musically similar to Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In the game's internal files, she is referred to as "SwordofMessmer".
Rellana has fully voiced cut dialogue.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
"Remembrance of the Elder Inquisitor" is a conjectural title for this item, which lacks an official English name.
This item was not fully implemented in the code. It lacks an item record; only the icon made it into the game.
It depicts Jori, Elder Inquisitor and a Large Inquisitor.
Presumably traded to Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold in exchange for the Barbed Staff-Spear and one of the Spiral Incantations, likely the Giant Golden Arc spell used by Large Inquisitors.

name: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
description: is a character in. She is a Shardbearer Boss encountered in the Academy of Raya Lucaria. While this encounter is not required to advance the story, Rennala must be defeated to unlock the ability to respec, Moonlight Altar, and "Age of the Stars" ending.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The young Lunar Princess was an astrologer who gazed at the night sky and chased the stars. In her youth, Rennala and her younger sister, Rellana, encountered moons that one day made them champions. Hers was an enchanting full moon. Later, she bewitched the Academy of Raya Lucaria with her lunar magic, becoming its master. She prohibited study of the primeval current at the academy, exiling its founders, Azur and Lusat. She established the house of Caria as royalty and anointed the enchanted Carian Knights, heroes of the highest honors.

When the sorceries of the Carians were still only the prototypes of the latter sword-phalanx sorceries., Rennala gifted a braid of her hair to Rellana, who disavowed her birthright to join Messmer the Impaler in his Crusade in the Realm of Shadow. 

In the age of the Erdtree, a champion known as Radagon led Queen Marika's armies against Liurnia of the Lakes. Rennala and the academy rallied forces to repel the invasion. She led her Glintstones Knights and, despite numbering fewer then twenty, their magic made them a match for even the champions of gold in battle. Two Liurnian Wars were fought, both of which saw no clear victor.

Radagon ended the Second Liurnian War by cleansing himself with Celestial Dew. Repenting his territorial aggressions, he swore his love to Rennala. They married at the Church of Vows, uniting the houses of the Erdtree and the Moon. As a Carian Queen, Rennala bestowed Radagon a Moon greatsword in accordance with a long-standing tradition. They had three children: Radahn, Rykard, and Ranni. Rennala led young Ranni by the hand to meet her Dark Moon.

Later, Radagon gifted an amber egg, the Great Rune of the Unborn, to Rennala, and left her side to become the second King Consort of Queen Marika, receiving the title of second Elden Lord. When Radagon left, Rennala's heart left with him.

Realizing their heartbroken queen was no champion at all, the Academy rebelled against the Carian Royal Family and Rennala was locked away in the grand library. Clutching the amber egg left to her by Radagon, she dissociated, devoting herself to the grim art of reincarnation. She would use it on Juvenile Scholars found around her, calling them her "sweetings", continuously rebirthing them in an imperfect process which would leave their memories fading into oblivion. The children born anew by Rennala were all frail and short-lived, imperfect beings, each and all.

Game events:
Rennala remained in the Grand Library throughout the reign of Lord Radagon and the ensuing Shattering war. She hovered idly in the air, clutching her egg, while her reborn Juvenile Scholars sang a lullaby that shielded her in a golden, moonlike bubble.

If the Great Rune separates from Rennala, a protective mechanism activates, releasing a dense black fog. The disembodied voice of Ranni the Witch warns intruders as an illusory image of Rennala emerges from the darkness to battle the player upon a moonlit sea. This apparition reflects Rennala as she once was, at the height of her power.

If the illusion is defeated, the present Rennala regains her egg and sits quietly in her bassinet at the center of the library, calling softly to her timid sweetings.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Overview:
HP: 3,493 (Phase 1)
HP: 4,097 (Phase 2)
Defense: 109
Stance: 0
Cannot be parried
Vulnerable to Critical Attacks after her Stance is broken
Deals Standard and Magic damage
This boss summons Juvenile Scholars during Phase 1. She summons Wolves, Troll Knights, Flying Dragons, and Bloodhound Knights during Phase 2.
Drops: 40,000 runes, Remembrance of the Full Moon Queen, and Great Rune of the Unborn

Throughout both phases, Rennala resists magic but is more vulnerable to physical attacks.

Moveset:

Phase 1: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon:

Rennala's first phase occurs in a circular room with an open inner area and a more narrow outer area, divided by bookcases. Rennala floats around the room encased in a golden sphere that prevents her from taking damage. The majority of her Juvenile Scholars congregate in the inner arena, however a few can be found hiding behind the bookcases. 

Rennala rarely attacks directly during this phase. Instead, the Juvenile Scholars lunge, breathe fire, and use telekinesis to assault the player with the books and globes. They also drop chandeliers from the ceiling if the player stands underneath them. However, Rennala periodically converts scholars to gravestones, which she sends flying towards the player. She also summons new Scholars to replace those the player has slain.

One of the Scholars sings, surrounded by a golden aura. The song grows louder as the player draws near. Hitting the singing Scholar at least once—without necessarily killing them—causes another to begin singing. Disrupt three singing Scholars to shatter Rennala’s sphere, dropping her to the ground and leaving her vulnerable. While she lies stunned, the Scholars cease their attacks, giving the player an opening to strike. After a few seconds, Rennala releases a golden explosion and rises again, her protective sphere restored. Repeating this process several times creates additional opportunities to damage her. 

Defeating Rennala triggers a cutscene, and advances the fight to Phase Two. A spell placed by Ranni the Witch on the amber egg activates, releasing a dense fog of darkness.

Phase 2: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon:

After the cutscene, the arena transforms into a vast, moonlit watery plane with no obstacles or clutter. Ranni's illusory Rennala engages the player directly with a full health bar. She relies primarily on ranged magical attacks but also swings her staff to strike if the player approaches too closely. 

When her health drops below 60%, she begins summoning spirits for assistance. Each time she summons, a glowing circle expands around her, dealing damage to anything within it. She can call forth a Bloodhound Knight, three wolves, a Flying Dragon, or a Troll Knight, each lasting only a few seconds before vanishing. During this phase, Rennala moves more evasively, making it difficult for melee fighters to land consistent attack chains.

Moving away from Rennala's homing attacks is simple, as there is nothing to get stuck on or blocked in by. However, there is nothing to separate Rennala from her summoned allies.

sections.heading: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (NPC)
sections.body:
After defeating her, Rennala becomes an NPC, remaining in the library where she was fought in phase 1. As an NPC she offers two services: Rebirth allows the player to reallocate levels to different stats at the cost of a Larval Tear, while Cosmetics allows the player to alter their character's appearance, which is the same function that the mirror in Roundtable Hold has.

When Sorceress Sellen moves to the Academy of Raya Lucaria during her questline, she will temporarily occupy Rennala's spot, while Rennala will move behind one of the bookshelves in the library. She will return to her usual place once Sellen's questline is completed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Wears the Queen's Set and wields the Carian Regal Scepter as her Glintstone staff. It is one of the best staffs in the game and it enhances full moon sorceries.
Rennala survives their fight and may interact with the player. She is always found in the Grand Library at the top of the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
After Rennala is defeated, she allows players to change their appearance or reallocate their stats using her Rebirth magic. The process requires Larval Tears. 
When Sellen takes over the Academy, Rennala can still be found in the Grand Library, hiding behind some bookshelves. When Sellen eventually turns into a Graven Mass, Rennala is back in her place while Sellen is moved to the side of the library where she remains for the rest of the game.
The approach to the Grand Library which houses Rennala is guarded by Moongrum, one of the last Carian Knights who once served the Lunar Queen. A Mad Pumpkin Head and Giant Silver Tear also protect the route.

image: ER Icon Key Item Revered Spirit Ash.png
description: Revered Spirit Ash is a Bolstering Material in.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Revered Spirit Ash are used at Sites of Grace to increase the Revered Spirit Ash Blessing level. The Blessing reduces the damage taken by Torrent while mounted and by summoned Spirit Ashes, while also increasing the damage dealt by Spirit Ashes. However, this effect is only active while within the Realm of Shadow.

Collecting all available ashes and reaching Blessing level 10 results in:
89% spell damage increase for Spirit Ashes.
75% spell damage increase for Spirit Ashes.
42.5% damage reduction for Spirit Ashes and Torrent.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
A total of 25 Revered Spirit Ashes are found throughout the Realm of Shadow:

Gravesite Plain: On a small altar northeast of the Gravesite Plain site of grace, past the white tree filled with hanging bodies. 
Gravesite Plain: Found at an altar located to the east of the Cliffroad Terminus site of grace, near a pond inhabited by turtles. 
Abandoned Ailing Village: Revered Spirit Ash can be looted from an altar surrounded by Man-Flies.
Temple Town Ruins: South of the Temple Town Ruins, near the edge, you will see the altar. 
Belurat, Tower Settlement: x2 Revered Spirit Ash can be found on the altar in a room infested by Spider-Scorpions. 
Belurat, Tower Settlement: After defeating the Divine Beast Dancing Lion, take the lift and proceed to open a large door; the altar is nearby. 
Belurat, Tower Settlement: Climb up after defeating the two Gravebirds, and spot a Shadow Pothead that drops x1 Revered Spirit Ash and x1 Golden Horn Tender. 
Belurat, Tower Settlement: After crossing the bridge with the Horned Warrior, turn left to find an altar with Revered Spirit Ash across from the central tree. 
Bonny Village: Fall from the broken bridge and follow the path north past the Stray to find the statue with Revered Spirit Ash at the end of the road. 
Moorth Ruins: East of the ruins, find a small shack containing the Revered Spirit Ash. 
Village of Flies: Found on a body laid on a pedestal upon entering the Village of Flies. 
Ancient Ruins of Rauh, West: Dropped by the Shadow Pothead in the area, along with x1 Silver Horn Tender, x1 Dewgem, and x1 Rauh Burrow. 
Ancient Ruins of Rauh (West): Found on the statue in the center of the area. Beware of enemies nearby. 
Enir-Ilim: Outside the First Rise site of grace, take the stairs and cross the bridge to defeat a Large Inquisitor for a Revered Spirit Ash. 
Enir-Ilim: x2 Revered Spirit Ash is located at the base of the statue in an indoor altar-like room with Man-Flies praying to an idol. 
Enir-Ilim: Found in a small room on an altar; be cautious of Gravebird enemies in the area. 
Ruins of Unte: Found on the altar near the stone wall southeast of the Ruins of Unte. 
Ellac River Cave: Found on an altar near the Ellac River Cave site of grace. 
Midra's Manse: In the library, jump across bookshelves to reach a Large Inquisitor; defeat it for a Revered Spirit Ash. 
Midra's Manse: Found on a body hanging from a chandelier near the Midra's Manse site of grace. 
Shadow Keep: Climb the statue’s feet and drop carefully onto the beast statue below to find the Revered Spirit Ash. 
Shadow Keep: From the Seventh Floor site of grace, jump onto the railings on the left to find this item on a hanging statue. 
Ancient Ruins of Rauh (East): Dropped by a Shadow Pothead west of the Viaduct Minor Tower site of grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Revered Spirit Ash Blessing affects both Ashes and Renowned Ashes.
The Mimic Tear Ashes does not receive the full benefits of the Blessing for balancing reasons.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained by defeating the Stonedigger Troll in Limgrave Tunnels in central Limgrave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Boosts the power of roar (including roar-boosted special attacks) and breath attacks. 
Boosts the direct damage by 15% for the skills Beast's Roar, Regal Roar, Starcaller Cry, and Troll's Roar, and the incantations Aspects of the Crucible: Breath, Howl of Shabriri, and Roar of Rugalea. 
Boosts the damage of the follow-up heavy attack granted by the skills Barbaric Roar, Braggart's Roar, Shriek of Milos, Troll's Roar, and War Cry by 15%.
Boosts the following incantations (mostly Dragon Communion Incantations) by 10%: Agheel's Flame, Borealis's Mist, Dragonfire, Dragonice, Ekzykes's Decay, Ghostflame Breath, Glintstone Breath, Greyoll's Roar, Magma Breath, Rotten Breath, Smarag's Glintstone Breath, and Theodorix's Magma, as well as Placidusax's Ruin. 
Stacks with the 10% roar damage boost of a Highland Axe. 
The Highland Axe only boosts skills, not incantations, and does not stack with itself (meaning two Highland Axes wielded together gives as much of a boost as one Highland Axe does).

name: Roar of Rugalea
image: ER Icon Spell Roar of Rugalea.png
description: Roar of Rugalea is an incantation spell in. It is the only Bear Communion Incantation.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed drop: Rugalea the Great Red Bear
Roar of Rugalea is received upon defeating Rugalea in the woods in the northern part of the Rauh Base, northwest of the Ravine North Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Creates a red bear's head to roar, causing Standard damage equal to 355% of Incantation Scaling in a forwards cone. 

Charging the spell lets out a weaker roar dealing Standard damage equal to 250% of Incantation Scaling, but will also let the user continue to roar for another 12 hits dealing damage equal to 30% Incantation Scaling each and finishing with a roar dealing damage equal to 200% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 17 points of FP to cast.
Costs 35 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases Stamina cost to 74 points. 
For the charged version, the first roar costs 35 points of Stamina while the remaining 13 roars cost 3 points of Stamina each (39 in total). 
Requires 1 Memory Slot.
Deals 14 Stance damage. Charging the spell increases Stance damage to 28. 
For the charged version, only the first and final roars deal Stance damage. 

Boosting:
Bloodboil Aromatic increases Standard Attack Power by 30% (20% in PvP) for 60 seconds as a Body Buff.
Blue Dancer Charm increases Physical Attack Power by up to 15% at low carried Equip Load values. 
Exalted Flesh increases Physical Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 30 seconds as a Body Buff.
Flame, Grant Me Strength increases Physical Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 30 seconds as a Body Buff.
Uplifting Aromatic increases Physical Attack Power 10% (7.5% in PvP) for 40 seconds as an Aura Buff.
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon. 
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 118%, this increases the Attack Power by a total of 162%. 
Be aware that since many of the hits are small, the effective damage increase will be much smaller due to enemy flat defences. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% if wearing the Pelt of Ralva. 

Strategies:
Surprisingly decent reach, especially when charged. 
The final roar of the charged version can launch human-sized enemies backwards. 
The weak hits of the charged version can lock lighter enemies in place with their stagger, potentially keeping them in range for the final hit. 
This is very useful since most of the damage of the charged version is in the first and final roars, even more so since the damage of the "mini roars" tends to end up heavily reduced by enemies' flat defences.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.13 increased poise damage and attack power. Fixed a bug that sometimes interrupted the cast of the “Roar of Rugalea” Incantation.
This increased the damage of the uncharged roar from 80% of Incantation Scaling to 355% of Incantation Scaling. For the charged version, the power of the final roar was increased from 160% of Incantation Scaling to 200% of Incantation Scaling. 
This also added an initial roar hit to the charged version of the spell, dealing damage equal to 250% of Incantation Scaling.

Roundtable Hold

Roundtable Hold

name: Romina, Saint of the Bud
image: ER Boss Romina Saint of the Bud.png
description: Romina, Saint of the Bud is a mandatory Boss in.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
Romina is not an optional boss as it must be defeated to burn the Sealing Tree and reach Enir-Ilim.

Phase One:
Romina is a distinctive opponent whose weaponry is her poleblade, centipede head, and scorpion stinger. It is essential to have a balanced strategy of both offense and defense, but it is advantageous to be more aggressive in battle.

Focus on her central human body as well as her centipede fangs and scorpion tail, which functionally serve as her arms. These parts move independently, allowing her to launch multiple simultaneous attacks, such as swinging her spear while her stinger strikes from another direction. Her attacks include Heavy Spear Thrusts, Sweeping Stinger strikes, and Biting Fangs.

Her most common opening move is her Centipede Sweep, where the centipede part of her body will swing from right to left. It can be dodged by rolling forward. This will let you get close to Romina to deliver a full heavy attack. However, you have to be aware that she may follow up by dashing and swinging her poleblade, which can be avoided by rolling to the left or backwards.

Stay as close as possible to Romina, as some of her sweep attacks won't hit you at point-blank range. Being near her also makes her attack pattern more predictable. For instance, after her usual opening attack, closing the distance with a dodge roll will cause her follow-up attack to miss if you are right beside her.

It is important to always look at Romina's poleblade, as when it glows red, this shows that it has become enchanted with Scarlet Rot. If hit with the enchanted weapon, it will cause a Scarlet Rot build-up. Always be wary of her weapon status. One of the combos that she does with her enchanted weapon is the Leap Combo where she starts with a poleblade sweep, an overhead attack, and then she jumps high in the air, and then plunges her weapon down. To dodge this, you can either:

Roll to your left for a sweep attack
Roll forward (slightly forward to your right) when she wings the overhead attack.
Pay attention when Romina's poleblade will flash pink for a brief moment, then roll forward at that exact moment.

When the leap combo is timed correctly, you can deliver a couple of free hits while she recovers. This combo also has a variation where Romina skips the 3rd part of the attack and does an enchanted weapon combo instead. She also has another basic move where she makes 3 quick sweepingmovements with her poleblade without enchantments. Finally, she can also do the Rolling Attack where she will curl up into a ball, and then roll around the arena. After she finishes rolling, she will slam the ground and then swing her pole blade. This can be initially avoided by getting out of her way, either by dodging or sprinting away. Lock the camera onto her to see where she is going. At the end of the roll, roll to the right to dodge both of her attacks. Then, you can retaliate with a heavy attack.

After she finishes a combo, quickly counterattack to take advantage of the time when she will be briefly vulnerable. While powerful, her attacks have high recovery times, allowing you to dodge and immediately counter. When she begins a combo, dodge her attacks by rolling to the side or towards her to close the distance. Immediately after dodging, counter with heavy attacks to break her poise. Frequent usage of jumping and heavy attacks is recommended as it can stagger her, leaving her open to further attacks. 

One of her special moves is the Double Spin 360 Combo, where she will lift up her human body as her weapon glows red, and will do two full spins while swinging her poleblade. After performing this move, she will pause to recover. This move can be dodged by rolling to the left, then dodging to the left again after a slight delay. This move usually causes Romina to end up at a far position from you, but she will take time to recover, and you can do at least one light attack or a jump attack if you sprint up to her.

Phase Two:
After her health drops to 50%, she will immediately transition to her second phase; her attacks remain the same, but she can now conjure Rotten Butterflies that will explode like bombs after a short period. She will be seen with pink butterflies circling her, and after a brief period, she will cause a whirlwind in the small arena. Romina then follows up this move with more butterflies in the outer area of the whirlwind that will randomly explode throughout the arena. To dodge this move, start sprinting away as her body lights up with a pink hue. Then, if you can outrun the AoE, you can stand at the edge, and you will not get hit. If you get caught, you can spam roll until you get out of the AoE. As the fight goes on, Romina will likely redo this move again, but with shorter preparation. So you will need to react quicker to get out of the exploding butterflies.

Romina at first seems like you must wait and punish with a typical melee build. She has a glaring weakness: she is vulnerable to animations that shift the player's hurt box down, particularly to low-profile common moves like her double glowing spear lunge and swipe. A perfect example I found was using Dryleaf Arts, where the Heavy attack naturally has low profiles for many of her spear-swiping moves. During my run, I found it more beneficial to be aggressive rather than defensive. Staying on her inner right side up front will negate a lot of her attacks with a dodge as needed. I ran Frost to add the slow to her animations, which was a plus, but not required in fighting her. The low profiling and staying on the offensive to break stance to heal as needed or deal significant damage was enough.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: The chanting in Romina's boss soundtrack is reminiscent of that of Malenia's in Phase Two.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In the game's internal files, she is named "ScarletCorruptionWarrior".
Romina's appearance is a possible call-back to arachnid-centaur women in previous FromSoftware games: Quelaag and Najka from the Dark Souls series. With her title of Saint, poleblade, and pale complexion, Romina is also reminiscent of Aldrich.
Romina has cut dialogue, which is fully voiced.
Romina is the only mandatory boss in Shadow of the Erdtree to have no cutscene or dialogue.

If you get caught, you can spam roll until you get out of the AoE. As the fight goes on, Romina will likely redo this move again, but with shorter preparation. So you will need to react quicker to get out of the exploding butterflies.

Romina at first seems like you must wait and punish with a typical melee build. She has a glaring weakness: she is vulnerable to animations that shift the player's hurt box down, particularly to low-profile common moves like her double glowing spear lunge and swipe. A perfect example I found was using Dryleaf Arts, where the Heavy attack naturally has low profiles for many of her spear-swiping moves. During my run, I found it more beneficial to be aggressive rather than defensive. Staying on her inner right side up front will negate a lot of her attacks with a dodge as needed. I ran Frost to add the slow to her animations, which was a plus, but not required in fighting her. The low profiling and staying on the offensive to break stance to heal as needed or deal significant damage was enough.

name: Rotten Breath
description: Rotten Breath is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Dragon Communion: Caelid / Jagged Peak
Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a heavy, rotting mist, dealing Standard damage equal to 131% of Incantation Scaling and causing 65 Scarlet Rot build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 393% of the same and 195 build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. 

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 48 points of Stamina to cast, and another 48 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Note that while the Dragon Communion Seal scales with Arcane, Scarlet Rot will not scale with that, so Rotten Breath gains no innate benefit except for the damage boost. 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
Can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast midair, unlike Ekzykes's Decay. 
Compared to Ekzykes's Decay, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 29% less FP. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 120 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
Only 65 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
This is the weakest "default" dragon breath attack, but it's also the only one that deals Physical damage. 
Compatible with the Blue Dancer Charm, even more so since its two primary boosting items, the Dragon Communion Seal and Rock Heart, are weightless. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players. 
The Scarlet Rot deals damage roughly equal to 1170 + 29.7% of the target's maximum health over the course of 90 seconds.
The total Scarlet Rot build-up is 390 if using both breaths, enough to afflict many vulnerable enemies and bosses with the Status Effect and most non-resistant ones within two full casts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 reduced the Scarlet Rot status effect buildup for Rotten Breath.
The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.
The status build-up per hit was decreased from 130 to 65 (total build-up reduced from 780 to 390).

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: In a treasure chest guarded by three Crystalians in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, behind some large tree roots right after the Ephael Inner Wall grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Effectively just the Crystal Sword but with slight Scarlet Rot build-up, much, much later acquisition, and lower damage from very slightly lower Strength-scaling and lower Physical and Magic base damage. 
The skill, Spinning Slash, is potentially quite damaging, especially if it catches another player offguard and with low Poise, though it's somewhat hampered by the lack of reach on Straight Swords. 
Does best as a pure Strength weapon, as Dexterity and Intelligence are somewhat hampered by having much lower scaling numbers and being based off the lower Magic base damage respectively. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 625 Attack Power (AP), 45 Strength and 45 Intelligence grants 607 AP, 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 599 AP, and 80 Intelligence grants 540 AP. 
Has on average 25 less AP
A good offhand weapon for those wishing to dual-wield Straight Swords on a Strength build with some Intelligence, due to the ease of upgrading weapons reliant on Somber Smithing Stones and its somewhat mediocre skill not mattering there.

The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: Rotten Winged Sword Insignia
description: Rotten Winged Sword Insignia is a talisman in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from Millicent after choosing to assist her in defeating her sisters, as part of her questline.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 6%/8%/13%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point. 

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hit towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive). 
These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land. 
For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive. 
For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count. 
Can be worn together with the Millicent's Prosthesis to stack the effect, but not with the Winged Sword Insignia. 
However, this talisman and the Prosthesis can't be obtained in the same playthrough, instead requiring a new cycle of New Game+ to obtain. 
Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy. 
An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice. 
This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.body: At some point between an unknown Patch and Patch 1.03.3, this talisman was apparently bugged, with the buff that is applied to attack power both increasing and decreasing with successive attacks. That is, in some scenarios, performing an additional attack within a sequence would cause attack power to decrease, rather than increase. This could be observed when using the Dagger and Short Sword weapons. This effect could be observed for the Winged Sword Insignia as well.

name: Roundtable Hold
description: The Roundtable Hold is the main hub area in. Entry to Roundtable Hold is locked until the player receives an invitation from Melina, achieved by resting at a Site of Grace in Liurnia of the Lakes or Caelid, or by defeating Margit, the Fell Omen. Afterward, the Roundtable Hold can be accessed via fast travel from the map.

sections.heading: Layout
sections.body:
Roundtable Hold consists of a main floor and a cellar, each comprised of several rooms. Certain rooms are inaccessible until certain requirements are met.

Lobby:
The central chamber of the Hold, containing the circular Table of Lost Grace site of grace, from which it gets its name. The player shall appear in this chamber every time they visit Roundtable Hold. Brother Corhyn, Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, and Knight Diallos can all be found here initially, later joined by Roderika, Spirit Tuner and D, Hunter of the Dead. A Marika statue by the fireplace can be used to access the Colosseums, once unlocked.

Northern Wing:

The northern wing, ahead and to the left upon arriving in Roundtable Hold, consists of a corridor which branches into Gideon's study and the Twin Maiden Husks' room. Ensha of the Royal Remains stands guard outside Gideon's study, and Nepheli Loux, Warrior briefly appears here after Godrick the Grafted has been defeated.

Gideon's Study:

A spacious room which has been adapted into a study by Gideon Ofnir, who can usually be found behind his desk. It will be locked upon first visiting Roundtable Hold, but will open either after claiming a Great Rune or talking to Gideon and reloading.

Twin Maiden Husks:

The Twin Maiden Husks can be found in a room through a door in the northern wing. Here, the player can buy and sell various items. They receive Bell Bearings, which allows them to sell the goods of dead merchants. Some of these Bell Bearings carry over into.

Library:

A small library behind a door in the Twin Maiden Husks' room, which will only open after touching a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau. The back of the library is piled with decaying corpses, and is occupied by the spirit of the Dung Eater.

Eastern Wing:

The eastern wing is a corridor which connects to Fia's room, the armory, and the cellar. Smithing Master Hewg resides here, and is later joined by Roderika.

Fia's Room:

A large bedroom occupied by Fia, Deathbed Companion. The Clouded Mirror Stand to the right upon entering can be used to open the Character Creation menu and alter one's appearance.

Balcony:

Situated between the northern and eastern wings, a balcony overlooks the great hall. Sorcerer Rogier retreats here after leaving Stormveil Castle.

Hall:

A large hall lined with banners and statues, accessed by dropping down from the balcony. Mad Tongue Alberich will invade when the player approaches the far end of the hall. After he has been defeated, a wisp of light will appear which allows the player to return to the balcony above.

Living Quarters:

A series of rooms connected to the hall, to the left after dropping down from the balcony. The Cipher Pata can be found on a corpse lying on one of the beds.

Armory:
A locked room at the far end of the eastern wing. It will only open after giving D the Weathered Dagger, received from Fia. 

Pantry:

A storage room on the lower level, at the bottom of a flight of stairs past Hewg in the eastern wing. It is initially empty, but Nepheli Loux will move here after the Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics has been defeated.

Dining Room:

A narrow room connected to the pantry, which requires a Stonesword Key to open. There is a treasure chest containing Crepus's Black-Key Crossbow and 20 Black-Key Bolts.

Kitchen:

A room connected to the dining room, requiring two Stonesword Keys to open. A treasure chest contains the Assassin's Prayerbook.

Audience Chamber:

A throne room connected to the lobby, wherein resides the Two Fingers and Finger Reader Enia. This chamber is locked until at least one Great Rune has been obtained. The player comes here to progress the main story and to trade in Remembrances for boss items.

description: The Royal Greatsword is a Colossal Sword, a melee armament.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from Blaidd, along with his armor set (except the Black Wolf Mask), when encountered at Ranni's Rise after Ranni the Witch's storyline has been completed. Killing him prior to this will award no items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Intelligence-scaling is actually slightly stronger than the Strength-scaling despite having the same letter grade. 
This means that a pure Intelligence build is the strongest way to build this weapon. However, because scaling values become less effective after reaching 40-50 in a stat and because wielding this weapon already requires a fair investment in Strength, a hybrid Str/Int build has almost as much AR while requiring much fewer Attribute points to do. 
The weapon itself does not cause Frostbite but both parts of the skill, the stab-jump and the explosion, do cause some build-up (60 on the stab and 100 on the explosion).

sections.heading: Upgrading

sections.heading: Trivia

Patch 1.04 increased the cast speed and decreased recovery time for the skill.
Patch 1.07 increased the poise when casting the skill.
Patch 1.09 increased the scaling values of the weapon.
As the description implies, this resembles a much more ornate version of the standard Greatsword.
Shares it name with a weapon from Dark Souls 2 (Royal Greatsword), which was a Greatsword-type weapon and Strength-based counterpart to that game's version of the Flamberge.

description: Royal Revenant is an enemy and boss in.

sections.heading: Bosses
sections.body:
Kingsrealm Ruins=

Background:
A Royal Revenant encountered in the hidden cellar of Kingsrealm Ruins in north-western Liurnia of the Lakes. It guards a chest containing the Frozen Needle.

Strategy:
Encountered in a very small room and without having to go through their signature lengthy spawning animation, this Revenant will turn aggressive quickly. 

If it leaps towards roll forwards to the left of it and get in a hit before backing away, being ready to roll. Should it start to use more short-ranged melee slams, back away to provoke more leaps. Sometimes it will start to chain these slams into one long combo, either try to keep as far away as possible from this or get behind it if already close. 

Occasionally it will start to emit a green color around its head which signifies that it's about to spit out a thin cone of Poison sludge. Potentially dangerous if caught in the middle of an action such as drinking a Flask of Crimson Tears but otherwise easily rolled or jumped away from. 

Sometimes it will slip through a portal underground to appear behind its target and spit poison before starting its attack routine again. 

Healing incantations:
One easy way to kill it is to find an opening to cast a cheap healing spell such as Heal and then cast it again immediately while it's stunned. Any class can do this as even a Prisoner has enough Faith with a Commoner's Garb/Commoner's Simple Garb and Two Fingers Heirloom. 

Another way to do this is to summon the Finger Maiden Therolina Puppet, though she's more unreliable in casting her healing incantation.

name: Ruins Greatsword
description: The Ruins Greatsword is a Legendary melee armament in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Obtained upon defeating the optional Misbegotten Warrior and Crucible Knight duo boss at the Redmane Castle plaza.
Note that this fight is only available whenever the Radahn festival isn't active. If it's currently active, it can be deactivated by defeating Starscourge Radahn and talking to Jerren once more in the chapel just before the lift down to Radahn and then reloading the area, preferably by teleporting to the Chamber Outside the Plaza Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Ruins Greatsword is one of eight Legendary Armaments required for completing the "Legendary Armaments" achievement.
Charged heavy attacks cost more stamina than usual but also deal with above-average damage thanks to a secondary hit with some extra area of effect. 

While this weapon scales with both Strength and Intelligence, it is borderline useless to invest in the latter anywhere beyond meeting the Attribute requirements. This is because the damage are incredibly minimal to both normal attacks (maxing out at +32 Magic damage with 99 Intelligence if the weapon is upgraded to +10) and because unlike how these sort of weapons scale normally, where Intelligence provides minimal weapon damage bonuses but great skill damage bonuses, both weapon upgrade level and Strength provide far greater bonuses to the skill's damage. 

Despite the appearance of its effects, it does not cause bonus damage to gravity-type enemies (e.g., Fallingstar Beasts), presumably because it is not extraterrestrial in origin.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The ruin that the rubble used to make this sword originated from was most likely Crumbling Farum Azula, giving its dilapidated state and nearby location. 
While the weapon resembles the Fume Ultra Greatsword from Dark Souls II and Dark Souls III, it even more so resembles the King's Ultra Greatsword from Dark Souls 2, especially because it resembles a statue wielded on a hilt. 
This weapon's guard rating was increased in patch 1.04, from 65/56/50/50/50/45 to 82/56/50/50/50/56.

name: Rune of Death
description: The Rune of Death (死のルーン, Shi no Rūn), also known as Destined Death (運命の死, Unmei no Shi), is an unobtainable Great Rune in that controls the fated deaths of the Demigods. Once part of the Elden Ring, it was removed by Queen Marika and sealed away when she established her Golden Order. It appears during the cutscene that plays when the player defeats Maliketh, the Black Blade at Crumbling Farum Azula.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Destined Death is a crimson, cross-shaped rune with tapered ends, resembling Marika's Rune with a downward arc. Smoke emanates from the rune as a jagged black fissure splits it vertically through its center. It manifests within a font of Darkness upon its unsealing.

Destined Death:
The Rune of Death can grant Destined Death, or true and fated death. When used to carve the Cursemark of Death in a full ring, it kills the recipient in both body and soul; however, incomplete rings can apply partial effects under specific circumstances. Known as half-wheels of the centipede, the waxing crescent burns away the flesh while the waning crescent destroys only the soul.

The Rune also produces crimson flames with golden motes that inflicts the Destined Death status effect, which reduces maximum HP and deals damage over time. The power of Destined Death could be repelled by the Blasphemous Claw or a depiction of the eclipsed sun.<!--

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Rune of Death was once embedded within the Elden Ring, empowering the black flames to deliver Destined Death to even gods. It was venerated by the Godskin Apostles and wielded by the Gloam-Eyed Queen, whose sacred Godslayer's Greatsword channeled black flames. The Queen, an Empyrean chosen by the Fingers, led the Apostles on their god hunt; however, she was ultimately vanquished by Maliketh, the shadowbound beast and loyal vassal of Queen Marika.

Golden Order:

With the Gloam-Eyed Queen defeated, Marika extracted the Rune of Death from the Elden Ring, and Maliketh sealed it within his Black Blade. This act was the foundation of the Golden Order and established Marika as the one true god. It exempted the Demigods from dying true deaths, granting them immortality, and also conferred a form of unending life to the Erdtree people. With the true lethality of Godslayer incantations suppressed, only Maliketh held the power to destroy the Demigods, and there was not one among them who did not fear him.

Night of Black Knives:
At a later point in history, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen from Maliketh by Ranni the Witch, who used it to create the godslaying Black Knives through a fearsome rite. On the Night of Black Knives, the Black Knife Assassins used these blades to murder Godwyn the Golden, the first Demigod to perish in all of recorded history. However, due to Ranni carving the Cursemark of Destined Death into her flesh at the same moment as Godwyn's death, he was unable to die a proper death and perished in soul alone. Meanwhile, Ranni's flesh perished and her soul continued to live, inhabiting a doll body. After the Night of Black Knives, Maliketh bound his sword within his own flesh in order to ensure that none would ever steal Death again.

Godwyn was given an Erdtree Burial at the Erdtree's roots in the Deeproot Depths beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital. However, his soulless body soon began a grotesque transformation into the blighted Prince of Death. Fragments of the Rune of Death began to spread through the underground Greattree roots connected to Godwyn's corpse, sprouting in the form of Deathroot, and leading to the rise of Those Who Live in Death.

Game Events:
 quivers in the presence of Deathroot.]]

As Gurranq, Beast Clergyman, Maliketh attempts to reclaim the stolen shards by consuming Deathroot, an endeavor he believes will restore the Golden Order and end his hunger. After devouring all nine Deathroots, his hunger persists and he realizes that the Golden Order cannot be restored. He was, in truth, betrayed by Marika.

Marika's daughter, Melina, aids the Tarnished knowing their quest will ultimately violate the Golden Order. Her purpose as the Kindling Maiden is to commit the Cardinal Sin and unlock the path to Maliketh and Destined Death. Although Maliketh unbinds the Black Blade, he is defeated. The Tarnished interacts with the Rune, unleashing a burst of crimson flame. The Erdtree is engulfed in crimson flames, and its impenetrable thorns are burned away.

If the Tarnished rises as the Lord of Frenzied Flame after using the Frenzied Flame to spare Melina, she gains or unlocks the power of Destined Death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Rune of Death might be an Elden Rune due to its similarity to Marika's Rune and its significance to the setting and story.
A power similar to Destined Death appears to be wielded by the Black Blade Kindred, certain Vulgar Militia, and the Baleful Shadow. However, it only inflicts damage over time, and does not reduce maximum HP like the effect of Maliketh's Black Blade, the Black Blade incantation, or the Black Knife.
The Rune of Death's fissure motif also appears on Maliketh's Black Blade, the Blasphemous Claw, and the Black Knives.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Maliketh's Destined Death attacks had purple particle effects in. They were replaced with the current crimson visuals in a subsequent patch.
Destined Death may have been inspired by the "Death Rune" from RuneQuest, which Miyazaki has cited as an inspiration for Elden Ring.

name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
description: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy is a boss in. He is a Demigod and a Shardbearer who is encountered in Volcano Manor.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Rykard was born the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala, head of both the Carian Royal Family and the Academy of Raya Lucaria. He had two siblings, Radahn and Ranni.

At some point, the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, was robbed of grace and hounded from the Lands Between. Rykard's father, Radagon, left Rennala to become Queen Marika's new consort and the second Elden Lord. Rykard and his siblings were thus raised to demigods by their new stepmother, Marika. 

Under the Golden Order, Rykard was a ruthless justiciar who commanded a company of inquisitors. His inquisitors persecuted and mercilessly tortured those considered heretics to the Golden Order, such as the Albinaurics. He spent time in the volcanic Mt. Gelmir, where he discovered the ancient magma hexes of a forgotten serpent-worshiping religion native to the region, which he brought back into practical use as new sorceries. Rykard also travelled to a foreign land where he encountered a dancer by the name of Tanith, who he would eventually take as his consort.

Rykard was also known for the construction of the Iron Virgins, automatons which were capable of both battlefield carnage and abducting victims to transport them to the Volcano Manor.

Rykard's budding blasphemous inclinations led him to assist his sister, Ranni, in orchestrating the Night of Black Knives. On the night of the plot, Ranni rewarded Rykard with a slab of rock engraved with the traces of the Rune of Death, which would allow him to challenge the black beast of Destined Death, should the coming trespass one day transpire.

The Shattering:
At some point following the the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, and her offspring acquired the Great Runes. The maddening taint of their newfound strength led to the Shattering, a war between Marika's demigod descendants, each seeking to become the new ruler of the Lands Between.

Rykard was indignant, and viewed the Erdtree and the gods demanding that the demigods fight over miserly scraps of power to be debasing. He launched a blasphemous campaign against the Erdtree and the Greater Will. When he turned to heresy, taking by force became the rule, the gods themselves being no different. Rykard's ambitions, though blasphemous, marked him a worthy sovereign, and drew many followers to his cause who admired his heroic aspirations. His rebels were known as the Recusants. 

Based in the Volcano Manor on Mt. Gelmir, his forces battled the armies of the Leyndell in what would become the most appalling battle of the Shattering, a wretched, unending war with no glory. Acts of cannibalism became a sickening reality across the battlefields, and some forces from both sides became afflicted with the Frenzied Flame sickness.

Blasphemy:
At some point during the Shattering, Rykard fed himself, Great Rune and all, to the blasphemous serpent that dwelled inside Mt. Gelmir, an ancient traitor to the Erdtree, merging with the creature. In the final moments before being devoured, he briefly had a vision of the future wherein he witnessed a serpent devouring the world. 

Following this, his lofty ambition degraded into gluttonous depravity. He fed on his greatest champions, and in the bowels of the serpent, they became the lord's family. Disturbed by what had become of their master and by the costly battles waged in his name, Rykard's forces abandoned him. Some attempted to put him to rest by searching for a mighty weapon capable of killing their lord. Such a weapon was found in the Serpent-Hunter, an enchanted spear crafted to hunt an immortal serpent in the distant past. However, all attempts made to take his life failed. The spear would come to reside in Rykard's chambers, left by a former Recusant who hoped a worthy champion might one day appear to wield it and spare the once-noble Rykard from further dishonor.

When Rykard gave himself to the elder serpent, the birth of the man-serpents followed, the deformed offspring of a repellent birthing ritual. One such man-serpent, known as Zorayas, would go on to be adopted by Tanith, and learn to assume an illusory human form in which she went by Rya. She was unaware of the origins of her birth, as Tanith concealed the truth of the Volcano Manor from her and insisted she was born of the grace of a king. It is implied that the woman known as Daedicar was one such woman subjected to the ritual, the biological mother of Zorayas and other man-serpents.

At some point before giving himself to the serpent, Rykard offered Tanith the Tonic of Forgetfulness to purge her memories of him. However, she refused, claiming "My Lord, there could be no greater distress than to forget you." Tanith was the only human known to stand with Rykard after he merged with the serpent of blasphemy; as in that moment, she was truly charmed by him. The Crucible Knight bodyguard of Tanith may have also served the Volcano Manor before Rykard was devoured, and as such, would have been the second human known to remain loyal, but this remains unknown. Tanith would continue her lord's legacy by leading a new force of Recusants, recruiting unsuspecting Tarnished after their return to the Lands Between following the end of the Shattering. The worthiest of these Tarnished champions would be granted an audience with Rykard, which ended with them being devoured by the serpentine demigod to increase his power further. 

Game events:
Eventually, a Tarnished champion managed to reach Rykard's chambers, and defeated the serpentine demigod to claim his Great Rune. Rykard took notice of this and awoke to confront the Tarnished, then pulled out a massive sword from the serpent's mouth, while boasting that they would join the Serpent King as family. After a hard battle, Rykard was ultimately slain by the Tarnished. Upon his death, he claimed "A serpent never dies", proven true when his initially vanished corpse began to regenerate. After Rykard is slain, Tanith suggested she planned to soon depart, having no reason to remain at Volcano Manor. However, afterwards she secretly journeyed to Rykard's chambers and attempted to eat his tremendous corpse, muttering her hopes that Rykard might live on within her, just as he had the serpent.

sections.heading: Boss Fight
sections.body:
The fight consists of two distinct phases, each with its own health bar. Phase 1 must be beaten each time to reach phase 2.

The Serpent-Hunter can be found sticking out of a pile of corpses near the entrance to the arena, and can be obtained without alerting the boss. This weapon makes the fight significantly easier, as it produces blades of light when swung that allow for long-distance attacks.

Defeating this boss will terminate Tanith's questline, regardless of how far one has progressed it. Any Volcano Manor targets not yet unlocked will also be missed.

Moveset:

Phase 1 - God-Devouring Serpent:
The God-Devouring Serpent is slow-moving, surrounded by a pool of magma. The magma makes it difficult to get close without taking damage, however the Serpent-Hunter allows for one to attack from a safer distance. It uses a combination of quick biting attacks and eruptions of magma, as well as a poison attack.

Phase 2 - Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy:
After reducing the Serpent's health to 0, a cutscene plays and phase 2 begins. Rykard, armed with a sword, moves around the arena similarly to the Serpent, however his moveset is almost entirely new.

Environment:
Rykard's arena is a spacious cavern, dotted with piles of corpses and tall corpse pillars, which can be broken by Rykard's attacks. The size of the arena is helpful for avoiding Rykard's Rancor and Rancor Rain, as one can run around the room until the attack ends.

sections.body:
The Blasphemous Claw mentioned a "" against the Two Fingers.
As seen in the opening cutscene and his paintings, Rykard appears to have light red hair or, arguably, blond hair, in contrast to his direct siblings.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Prevents the loss of Runes upon death (except for deaths cause by Death Blight). 

Breaks upon death (except for deaths caused by Death Blight).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Useful to equip when you are about to run into an area full of dangerous enemies, just keep in mind to unequip afterwards so as to not lose it unnecessarily. 
Like the Twiggy Cracked Tear, since it prevents you from dropping a Bloodstain with your runes upon death it will also prevent it from replacing your previous one and therefore gives you another chance to grab it.
This is especially useful around large drops since it makes the consequences around fall damage deaths much smaller, provided you are willing to risk losing a twig. 
Be careful when farming these, as the only enemies that drop them are also some of a few that can inflict Death Blight and therefore circumvent the protective effect. 
Can be used to transport out a bunch of Runes stuck inside of a boss room, especially when combined with quitting out to the main menu to reset the character to just outside of the boss room's fog wall.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Caelid (Sellia, Town of Sorcery) 
Gowry can be found in his shack near the entrance to Sellia. He will request that you find an Unalloyed Gold Needle in the swamp and bring it to him in exchange for a secret about Sellia.
Caelid (Swamp of Aeonia)
Travel to the Swamp of Aeonia and defeat Commander O'Neil to obtain the Unalloyed Gold Needle.
Caelid (Sellia, Town of Sorcery)
Give the Needle to Gowry. Reload the area and speak to him to obtain the repaired Needle.
Caelid (Church of the Plague)
Travel to the Church of the Plague and give Millicent the Unalloyed Gold Needle.
If you immediately go back to Gowry after this point you can unlock additional dialogue and unlock his shop. Alternately, if you reload the area and speak to Millicent in the church once again, the next time you visit Gowry's Shack Gowry will be absent and Millicent will be there in his place.
Caelid (Sellia, Town of Sorcery)
(Optional) After giving Millicent the Valkyrie's Prosthesis, return to Gowry and speak to him again. He will now have Pest Threads in his shop inventory. Purchase the spell to unlock additional dialogue about Millicent and Malenia.
Caelid (Sellia, Town of Sorcery)
Once Millicent arrives in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree, return to Gowry to hear additional dialogue. He will ask you help the sisters defeat Millicent.
Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree
Complete the final part of Millicent's questline, by using one of the summon signs to either aid Millicent or defeat her.
Caelid (Sellia, Town of Sorcery)
If you aided Millicent, Gowry will lament her decision to remove the Unalloyed Gold Needle. You may now permanently kill him to obtain the Flock's Canvas Talisman and Gowry's Bell Bearing.
If you killed Millicent in Elphael, Gowry will already be dead, and the Flock's Canvas Talisman and Gowry's Bell Bearing can be looted from his corpse.

Background:
A Sanguine Noble encountered in the cellar of Writheblood Ruins in Altus Plateau. This enemy guards a chest containing a Bloody Helice, the same weapon wielded by all Sanguine Nobles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Sanguine Noble at the Second Church of Marika will only spawn before or after the encounter with Bloody Finger Hunter Yura and Eleonora, Violet Bloody Finger. It will not spawn while they are present.
Sanguine Nobles wield a Bloody Helices in their right hand and a Reduvia in their left hand.
If blood loss is inflicted near them, they receive a damage boost similar to Lord of Blood's Exultation; they are highly vulnerable to suffering a bleed.
The Sanguine Noble Set is dropped by Sanguine Noble (Invader) in the Consecrated Snowfield. This is an NPC who does not have the same model or moveset as the Sanguine Noble enemy, and who dual wields Reduvias just like Nerijus.
Sanguine Nobles have black horns resembling Mohg's protruding from their necks. They also have horns growing downwards out of the soles of their feet, serving like high heels, and they also have long claws on their fingers and toes.
The nobles may be a late stage of the "cessblood" affliction used among the Bloody Fingers, as this seems to use Mohg's own blood.
Their internal name is "daemonbloodlaity."
Daemonblood, again, likely references them having been given the injection as per the initiation ritual.
A laity is non-ordained member of a religious organization; a layperson.

name: Scadutree
description:
The Scadutree (影樹, Eiju; lit. "Shadow Tree") is a colossal tree in, included in the expansion.

It is the shadow of the Erdtree which looms over the Land of Shadow, born of dark notions that bear no sense of Order, that twist and bend its stock, rendering it misshapen and brittle.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
The Scadutree is holy but its gold is veiled in shadow and covered in impenetrable thorns.

Like the Erdtree, the Scadutree can manifest avatars to defend itself and its offspring. Scadutree Avatars take the form of giant Shadow Sunflowers.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: The Scadutree is located at the northernmost point in the Realm of Shadow, found at the Scadutree Base.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
]]

The blessed sap of the Scadutree once fell like tears into the Scadutree Chalice, but it has since scattered, pooling deeply within the Furnace Golems.

Its splinters were collected, displayed, and prayed to in some Churches of Marika by the people of the Erdtree. Scadutree Fragments bestowed a Scadutree blessing of great power, although it has no influence outside of the Realm of Shadow. The remains of the warriors who perished in the realm of shadow were touched by the gold of the Scadutree, a blessing said to be the highest honor that can be afforded to the dead.

For those who abandoned the practice of incantations after devout faith rewarded them with only despair, the image of the misshapen Scadutree is an edict: “Spurn all that exists. Wound all that exists. For we have been abandoned. Denounce their ways. Do them harm. For they have abandoned us.”

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Director Hidetaka Miyazaki mentioned the title "" contains a secret: the Scadutree is the shadow of the Erdtree, and the shadow of its former self.
The Scadutree Grail holds six Red Relics, complimenting the Sacred Erdtree Grail's six yellow slots. When considering the nature of primordial gold, these Chalices indicate that the Scadutree is still imbued with the red power of life, containing the primordial form of the Erdtree.
The straight, leaning Scadutree trunk oozes a vast quantity of pitch (i.e., a sticky, protective resin secreted by conifers—pines, firs, spruces, cedars—when sick or wounded, different from the tree's internal sap), supporting textual evidence of the Scadutree's deterioration.
The Sealing Tree resembles one of the Scadutree's trunks.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: "Scadutree" (pronounced Schadutree) derives from "scadu" ([https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/sceadu#Old_English sċeadu), an Old English word for "shadow" or "shade"—meaning the Scadutree is literally named "Shadowtree".

name: Scarlet Rot
description: Scarlet Rot (朱い腐敗, Akai Fuhai) is a status effect in Elden Ring, inflicting damage over time to the player and serving as a more dangerous variant of the Poison status effect. The player's resistance to this status ailment is determined by their Immunity stat, which is increased by the Vigor stat.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.body: Scarlet Rot accumulates gradually and comes into effect once the threshold is reached. The higher the player's Immunity stat, the longer it will take for Scarlet Rot to become effective. Immunity can be increased by increasing the Vigor stat. Once effective, the player will receive continual damage over time until the effect wears off.

sections.heading: Environment
sections.body:
Swamps:

Rot swamps can be found in several locations throughout the Lands Between.
They generally comprise of bodies of filthy sludge that continuously build up Scarlet Rot as the player is standing in them. Rolling around in said sludge will also cover the player-character's body with the fluids, which will slowly yet consistently build up Scarlet Rot even if the player is no longer directly standing in the liquid itself or even tries to cure their Rot ailment with boluses. While these stains will gradually wear off over time, they can be removed immediately if it's raining, the player rolls around in clean water or uses Soap.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Despite the Antspur Rapier indicating that the Giant Ants can inflict Scarlet Rot, they don't in actual gameplay. This is either because it was fashioned from an ant that was infected with the disease (such ants are not encountered by the player) or Marais somehow modified it.
Despite being afflicted with Scarlet Rot, Starscourge Radahn does not spread the infection. 
"朱い" in the Japanese "朱い腐敗" is a spelling of the word "赤い" (red) which indicates the color vermilion, rather than scarlet. While both are bright, reddish colors, vermillion has a distinctly more orange hue than scarlet; an example of this is Malenia's flower.

description: Scholar's Armament is a spell in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Purchase: Limgrave / Liurnia of the Lakes / Academy of Raya Lucaria / Roundtable Hold
Sold for 3,000 Runes by Sorceress Sellen in any of her locations other than Witchbane Ruins.
Should Sellen die before purchasing this Sorcery from her, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Sellen's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
POWER: 75% SS

DURATION: 90 seconds.

An exceptional spell for a fighter-mage hybrid character; it adds raw Magic damage to your equipped melee weapon. The Power ratio is the damage added to every base strike. This added damage is also completely independent to how high or low the base damage of the original weapon is, so a strong boost to a normally weak-but-fast weapon could have quite a significant DPS effect.

Note that this spell explicitly forces an orientation on which hand holds what equipment. The melee weapon must be held in the right hand, the staff in the left, for this to be able to fire. It also cannot be used on another staff, Fist, or a bow/crossbow.

Also note, 2-handing the weapon after enchanting it does not appear to add the 50% damage multiplication to the magical part of the damage, only the base physical damage is affected.

NOTE, this cannot be cast on a weapon that already has a bonus elemental damage effect either naturally or through an Ashes of War.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Scorpion's Stinger was a relic of the ancient Rot god, defeated by the Blind Swordsman.
A carved Wolf, or shadowbound beast, decorates the pommel of the Scorpion's Stinger. Sensory bristles grow from its scarlet stinger.
Scales quite well with Dexterity, enough to be neck-and-neck with the Parrying Dagger and the Celebrant's Sickle and to only be substantially surpassed by the Wakizashi.
Has a unique, thrusting heavy attack compared to the standard dagger moveset. This trait is shared with the Glintstone Kris, Main-gauche, and the Miséricorde.
The locked skill, Repeating Thrust, is somewhat useful for applying the weapon's innate Scarlet Rot. However, it notably offers extra mobility beyond the usual Quickstep skill.

name: Scouring Black Flame
image: ER Icon Spell Scouring Black Flame.png
description: Scouring Black Flame is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Godslayer Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed Drop: Altus Plateau
Scouring Black Flame is received upon defeating the Godskin Apostle at Dominula, Windmill Village, on the Altus Plateau.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Create a small ball of Blackflame to throw, hitting with Fire Attack Power equal to 244% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting an effect that deals damage equal to 2% of target's maximum HP + 20, over the course of 2 seconds. 

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 300% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 29 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 38 points. 
Deals 9.25 Stance damage on hit. Charging the spell increases the Stance damage to 13.635. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged. 
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 23%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 41%. 
Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Godslayer's Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Generally outmatched by Black Flame due to its greater range and speed, while having the same damage. However, Scouring Black Flame is a bit more difficult to read and dodge due to the cast being somewhat hard to read and the spell sweeping upwards. 
Hits flying enemies easier due to said sweeping upwards. Small enemies, however, may require the player to unlock their camera and aim it more towards the ground so that it doesn't simply sweep over them. 
All bosses in are resistant to the percentage-based damage of Blackflame, only taking damage equal to 1% of target's maximum HP + 10 over 2 seconds. Messmer the Impaler, Bayle the Dread, and the Promised Consort are even more resistant to the effect, only taking damage equal to 0.7% of target's maximum HP + 7.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07: Increased stamina attack power against guarding enemies and increased poise damage when charged.
Stamina Attack Power against guarding enemies was increased from 65 to 150 for the uncharged version, and from 84 to 210 for the charged version.
Against players the Stamina Attack Power was instead increased to 187 for the uncharged version and to 262 for the charged version.
Stance damage for the charged version was increased from 12.025 to 13.635. 
Patch 1.04: Decreased FP cost and recovery time. Increased attack range and area of effect.
FP cost was decreased from 27 to 21.

name: Serosh
description: Serosh, Lord of Beasts, also known as the Golden Lion and Beast Regent, is a character in. He indirectly fights the player during the Godfrey, First Elden Lord boss encounter at the Elden Throne in Leyndell, Ashen Capital.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Serosh is a large lion with a dark gray coat and a silvery white mane, though it was once golden in his youth. The skin on his snout and lips are both colored black and his face is covered in scars, the most notable ones passing over his perpetually closed eyes—indicating his blindness. His largest wound was inflicted by the death blow that cleaved through the left side of his silver crown, before continuing across his forehead and over his right eye, ending at the bottom his right cheek.

Serosh wears silver platemail armor that covers his chest and shoulders, with matching, sharp-tipped gauntlets covering his paws. His broken crown resembles the Elden Lord Crown. While mounted on Godfrey's back, Serosh's body is translucent, with the lower half of his body not visible.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Serosh was a regal, golden lion regarded as the Lord of Beasts in ancient times. For the beastmen of Farum Azula, the presence of five fingers was celebrated as a symbol of the intelligence granted to their kind, with the five black nails of the Beastclaw Greathammer representative of Serosh.

The soul of Serosh was taken upon Hoarah Loux's back when the warrior vowed to become Godfrey, Marika's first Elden Lord, suppressing his ceaseless lust for battle. Serosh offered counsel and guidance to Godfrey and his Golden Lineage as their Beast Regent, his insignia becoming a longstanding symbol of their glory. General Radahn, captivated by Godfrey in his youth, wore armor depicting a golden lion, said to symbolize both Godfrey and Serosh.

Serosh remained with Godfrey even after he became Tarnished and was exiled from the Lands Between. After the Axe of Godfrey broke and the Long March came to an end, Godfrey divested his kingship, and became Hoarah Loux once more. Serosh and Hoarah Loux settled in the badlands, where they lived and died together as simple warriors. Following their deaths, the Guidance of Grace returned, restoring them to life and ushering them home. They reclaimed the axe and became Godfrey once more, crossing the Sea of Fog to claim the Elden Ring.

The pair arrive at the foot of the burning Erdtree after the player Tarnished commits the Cardinal Sin and defeats Maliketh, the Black Blade. They mourn the passing of Morgott, and Grace directs them to confront the player. When pushed to their limit, Serosh transitions from a spirit to a tangible, corporeal form, preparing to play an active role in the duel. However, Godfrey interrupts the process; he thanks Serosh for his service and violently kills him, drenching himself in the blood of his Beast Regent. He discards his axe to fight as Hoarah Loux, Warrior.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Serosh and Hoarah Loux's pairing most likely occured at the Gate of Divinity, as per the requirements for Marika returning from the other side. The Divine Beast Warriors who protect the Gate each wears a lion's head and allows a Divine Beast to control their actions, paralleling Godfrey and Serosh.
Serosh is often shown with his teeth sinking into Godfrey's arm or torso. This may be a means of keeping Godfrey's lust for battle in check.
Serosh and Elder Lions are the same color, but Serosh lacks horns.
Although the Talisman of Lord's Bestowal omits Serosh, his presence is indicated by Godfrey's stoic demeanor and Elden Lord Crown.

Loot: Can be picked up within the boss arena of Praetor Rykard, just after the fog gate.

This item does not re-spawn when the player has one in either their inventory or chest, even in NG+. However it will re-spawn (and thus can be picked up again) from the same location should the player discard it. This is to make sure that the player always have the means of fighting Rykard with it.

Because of this safeguard it is still possible to obtain duplicates of this weapon:
Requirements:
The player needs to not have a copy it in their inventory.
Rykard needs to still be alive.
The game needs to be in online-mode.
1) Stand outside Rykard's arena and attempt to connect to another player's world through any means necessary. 
(Tarnished's Furled Finger, Duelist's Furled Finger, Bloody Finger, Recusant Finger, Festering Bloody Finger or Blue Cipher Ring)
2) When the game has successfully found a world it can try to connect to, enter Rykard's arena and pick up the Serpent-Hunter before the Loading Screen appears.
3) Leave the multiplayer session either by completing your objective or using the Finger Severer.
4) When you re-spawn back in your own world, do not fast travel or rest at the Sites of Grace, instead enter Rykard's arena again and you'll see the Serpent Hunter is still there, available to be picked up again for a second time. 
(Traveling or resting at the site of grace will make the game check if the Serpent-Hunter is in your inventory before it decides if it'll spawn in a new one for you to pick up)
It's possible to obtain even more copies of this weapon if the player simply loops back to step 1 after finishing step 3.
