sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
]]
There was once an ancient religion based at Mt. Gelmir that worshiped a Serpent-God, offering sacrifices to it through a creature known as the God-Devouring Serpent, also refered to as the Great Serpent. The Serpent-Hunter was a weapon crafted and used in the distant past to kill a incarnation of the God-Devouring Serpent; but the Great Serpent is immortal, and has since been reborn by some means.

Age of the Erdtree:
The eldest child of Queen Marika, Messmer the Impaler, was born entangled by serpents. He was inhabited by the Base Serpent, a malevolent creature without light. However, two benevolent Winged Serpents were also present from birth. They served as his constant advisors during the Crusade and, more importantly, suppressed the abyssal serpent's influence.

The Erdtree regarded serpents as traitors. Even displaying their image was considered a curse. In Godfrey's age, Duelists adorned with bronze serpents fought in the Colosseums. Audiences took pleasure in seeing their effigies struck down.

The Shattering:
Disillusioned with the Golden Order and the state of the world the Shattering brought, Praetor Rykard, son of Rennala, swore to oppose the Erdtree. From his residence at the Volcano Manor atop Mt. Gelmir, Rykard spent time studying the ancient religion once based there. He discovered hexes the serpent worshipers had used and by applying his extensive knowledge of sorcery, natural to Carian Royal like himself, Rykard brought these hexes back into practical use, creating the Magma Sorceries.

After waging a bloody, undending war against the Erdtree, Rykard had since seemingly become obsesed with a young reincarnation of the Great Serpent. In an appalling act, Rykard fed himself, Great Rune and all, to the God-Devouring Serpent, and the birth of the unnatural Man-Serpents followed. With the power of Rykard's rune, and the sacrifices of many Recusant champions it has been fed, the Great Serpent has grown to an enormous size.

name: Shabriri
description: Shabriri is an NPC. He is a spirit that possesses the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, appearing after the player ascends the Grand Lift of Rold. Note that once Shabriri appears, Yura's questline will end regardless of how much progress has been made in it. It is not necessary to have started or completed Yura's questline for Shabriri to appear. If player visits the Three Fingers before reaching Shabriri, he will not appear. The Ronin's Set can be found on the ground where he would otherwise stand.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The most reviled man in all history, Shabriri was found guilty of slander long ago and sentenced to blindness. With his eyeballs completely gouged out, it is said that, in time, the Frenzied Flame came to dwell within his empty sockets. He believed that chaos should take the world and was regarded to be the origin of the sickness of Frenzied Flame. Following his death, Shabriri endured as a spirit capable of inhabiting the bodies of others.

Game Events:
The Tarnished encounters Shabriri in the Mountaintops of the Giants, where he is inhabiting the body of Bloody Finger Hunter Yura. The Tarnished, at the behest of Melina, is bound for the Forge of the Giants so she may set the Erdtree aflame. However, Shabriri advises the Tarnished to seek out the Three Fingers in the depths below Leyndell, revealing that their ascendency to the throne of Elden Lord would otherwise require Melina's sacrifice. He proposes an alternative path: the Tarnished may spare the life of Melina by inheriting the flame of frenzy and using their own body as kindling. Shabriri bids the Tarnished become the Lord of Chaos, burning the Erdtree to the ground and incinerating all that divides and distinguishes.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
Shabriri is found near the Zamor Ruins Site of Grace on the Mountaintops of the Giants.

Summon Sign:
Shabriri is a summonable cooperator for the Godfrey, First Elden Lord / Hoarah Loux, Warrior boss fight if the player has visited the Three Fingers and has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Shabriri can be attacked and killed at the Mountaintops of the Giants ( 3,107 HP).
Drops: 1,000, Iron Kasa, Ronin's Armor, Ronin's Gauntlets, and Ronin's Greaves.
The version of Shabriri at the Mountaintops of the Giants can cast one extra spell: Inescapable Frenzy.

Equipment:

sections.heading: Shabriri's Quest
sections.body:
Shabriri's questline intersects with the following NPCs: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, Melina

Quest Items:

Questline Steps: 
Mountaintops of the Giants
Shabriri can be found by the Zamor Ruins Site of Grace near the beginning of the Mountaintops of the Giants area. Exhaust his dialogue to unlock new dialogue from Melina when resting at a Site of Grace. 
Frenzied Flame Proscription
Travel to the Frenzied Flame Proscription through the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and Cathedral of the Forsaken. Remove all of your armor and interact with the door on the lowest floor for a cutscene in which the Three Fingers embrace you. This can be done regardless of whether you have met Shabriri already. Doing so will cause Shabriri to disappear from his previous location.
This will unlock the Lord of Frenzied Flame Ending. This will lock you out of achieving any of the other endings unless you obtain Miquella's Needle by completing Millicent's quest and defeating Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and using it in Dragonlord Placidusax's boss room.
(Optional) Leyndell, Ashen Capital
Shabriri will be available as a cooperator to assist with the fight against Godfrey, First Elden Lord at the Elden Throne if the player has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Shabriri and Bloody Finger Hunter Yura wear the same armor set and have the same face data and voice actor; however, Shabriri does not use Yura's Nagakiba or battle art, instead wielding an Uchigatana with Impaling Thrust.
Shabriri performs a unique gesture: he covers his eyes with both hands.
Shabriri was said to have gained the Flame of Frenzy from reading the message imprinted on the tomb of an ancient god by the Readerless Fingers.
The eyeballs of those afflicted with madness were called Shabriri Grapes. Lightseeker Hyetta, a blind maiden, is guided to the Three Fingers after consuming enough of them.
Shabriri most likely influenced Roundtable Knight Vyke to inherit the Frenzied Flame and spare his Finger Maiden. Festering Fingerprint Vyke invades near the body of his maiden and drops a Fingerprint Grape, which is a Shabriri Grape touched by the Three Fingers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Shabriri is voiced by Shaun Dooley, who also voiced Yura, Kaiden Sellswords, and the Fire Giant.
"Shabriri" (lit. "dazzling glare") is a demon associated with blindness in Jewish folklore and Talmudic demonology. It rests on uncovered water at night and blinds those who drink from it. In modern Hebrew, the literal translation for shabriri is "fragile".

questline: Shabriri's questline intersects with the following NPCs: Bloody Finger Hunter Yura, Melina

Questline Steps:
Mountaintops of the Giants

Shabriri can be found by the Zamor Ruins Site of Grace near the beginning of the Mountaintops of the Giants area. Exhaust his dialogue to unlock new dialogue from Melina when resting at a Site of Grace.
Frenzied Flame Proscription

Travel to the Frenzied Flame Proscription through the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds and Cathedral of the Forsaken. Remove all of your armor and interact with the door on the lowest floor for a cutscene in which the Three Fingers embrace you. This can be done regardless of whether you have met Shabriri already. Doing so will cause Shabriri to disappear from his previous location.

This will unlock the Lord of Frenzied Flame Ending. This will lock you out of achieving any of the other endings unless you obtain Miquella's Needle by completing Millicent's quest and defeating Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and using it in Dragonlord Placidusax's boss room.
(Optional) Leyndell, Ashen Capital
Shabriri will be available as a cooperator to assist with the fight against Godfrey, First Elden Lord at the Elden Throne if the player has not used Miquella's Needle.

sections.body: The caster throws a shadowy effigy that attracts humanoid enemies within a 15-meter radius for 3 seconds. It only affects medium or smaller foes and has no effect on those already engaged in combat.

sections.heading: Notes

Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.

The Shaman Village is situated in the eastern Hinterland of Scaduview, a secret area unlocked by solving a puzzle at the Shadow Keep. To access it, perform the O Mother gesture before a statue of Marika near the Shadow Keep, Back Gate Site of Grace and head southeast.

The road to the village is guarded by two Tree Sentinels in possession of a Blessing of Marika. The nearest Sites of Grace are Hinterland and Hinterland Bridge, though the village itself lacks a dedicated Site of Grace. The village is entered from the west, with a one-way path connecting to Scadu Altus in the southeast, where a cliffside descent reveals a secret area within Rabbath's Rise.

name: Shardbearers
description: The Shardbearers (破片の君主, Hahen no Kunshu) are special bosses that are key to progression in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Shardbearers were the inheritors of the Great Runes, the fragments of the Elden Ring, and were primarily among the Demigod offspring of Queen Marika the Eternal. Uniquely among the Shardbearers, Ranni the Witch cast aside her Great Rune. The mad taint of the power they acquired from their Great Runes precipitated the Shattering wherein most of them fought for control of the Lands Between. However, none succeeded in becoming Elden Lord, or the god of a new age.

Unlike the other Shardbearers, Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, is not a Demigod. She received her Great Rune of the Unborn from Radagon of the Golden Order long before the Shattering. This Great Rune was removed from the Elden Ring long ago and stored within the amber egg that was left by her former husband.

The Tarnished, upon their return to the Lands Between, were tasked by the Two Fingers to defeat the Shardbearers in order to claim their Great Runes, and use them to repair the shattered Elden Ring. Several Tarnished, such as Roundtable Knight Vyke and Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing, became shardbearers and earned a personal audience with the Two Fingers.

sections.heading: Facing the Shardbearers
sections.body:
Certain bosses or events must be completed before the shardbearers can be fought.
Godrick the Grafted (Stormveil Castle, Limgrave):
Defeat Margit, the Fell Omen and navigate Stormveil Castle
Mohg, Lord of Blood (Mohgwyn Palace, Siofra River):
Use the item given by Varre after completing his quest at Rose Church or take the waygate in the Consecrated Snowfield
Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon (Academy of Raya Lucaria, Liurnia of the Lakes):
Defeat Red Wolf of Radagon and navigate the Academy of Raya Lucaria
Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy (Volcano Manor, Mt. Gelmir):
Speak to Tanith at the Volcano Manor after completing all three of her contracts, or take the waygate after defeating the Godskin Noble in the Volcano Manor
Starscourge Radahn (Redmane Castle, Caelid):
Speak to Jerren at Redmane Castle after reaching Altus Plateau or defeating the Crucible Knight & Misbegotten Warrior duo

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
There are several demigods who are not known to be shardbearers. Namely, Godwyn the Golden, Godefroy the Grafted, and the Soulless Demigods carried in the Wandering Mausoleums.
Messmer the Impaler is not a shardbearer. He was sent on his crusade and forlorned in the Realm of Shadow prior to Radagon leaving Rennala.
Radagon was a shardbearer before he gave the amber egg to Rennala.
The Scadutree Avatar technically becomes a shardbearer after Miquella discards his Great Rune.
Both Patches and White Mask Varré allude to having gained an audience with the Two Fingers. Similar to other NPCs, they do not drop Great Runes upon defeat.
Melina receives the Rune of Death in the "Lord of Frenzied Flame" ending if she did not sacrifice herself at the Forge of the Giants.
Rennala also did not participate in the Shattering due to being locked inside Raya Lucaria Grand Library after the Academy's mages rebelled against the Carian Royals. 
When the Tarnished confronts Rennala, their battle is interrupted by Ranni the Witch, who conjures a phantom of Rennala in her prime from the amber egg, which the Tarnished defeats instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Localisation Notes
In Japanese, the shardbearers are rather called "Monarchs of Fragments" or "Sovereigns of Shards" (破片の君主, Hahen no Kunshu.)
The Sword Monument that reads "The First Defense of Leyndell / A sovereign alliance rots from within / Traces yet remain of bloody conspiracy" also uses the same kanji 君主 (Kunshu) to refer to the "sovereign alliance." This may indicate an alliance between the shardbearers before the First Defense.
In English, Enia calls the player a shardbearer after they acquire a Great Rune, however, in Japanese she simply calls them "Master of the/a Great Rune" (大ルーンの主, Dai Rūn no Omo.)
In English, Tanith refers to the shardbearers vying for power, however, in Japanese she uniquely calls them "Great Rune Monarchs" / "Sovereigns of (the) Great Rune(s)" / (大ルーンの君主, Dai Rūn no Kunshu.)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The default skill is good for dealing with enemies that are blocking, though it can also be used by simply switching to an empty right-hand slot or replicated by continuously attacking if the blocker isn't using a greatshield. 
Has an entirely unique heavy attack chain consisting of only thrusts. 
Since these attacks will reliably deal Pierce damage they pair well with the Spear Talisman for extra counter damage against attacking foes. Note that this works best with purely Physical infusions, as split Elemental damage (such as Magic or Lightning) will note benefit from the bonus to Pierce damage. 
Surprisingly decent for the Magic and Flame Art/Sacred affinities, placing it closer to the middle of the pack than the end for damage. 
When using its Keen affinity it actually has slightly weaker Dexterity-scaling for "bullet"-type (i.e. doesn't scale directly with the used weapon's damage) Skills with a Keen, Quality, Lightning, or Cold affinity, giving them usually about 2% less damage than they otherwise would have. This includes, as an example, the skills Beast's Roar, Storm Blade, Thunderbolt, and Hoarfrost Stomp (these skills however perform as normal on any affinity besides Keen).
Consistently the third weakest weapon in the type in terms of pure Attack Power (AP), outclassing only the Weathered Straight Sword and Cane Sword. 
Quite short, the shortest of its weapon type in fact. 
Wielded by Foot Soldiers.

Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

name: Siege of Caria Manor
description: The Siege of Caria Manor refers to the failed siege of Caria Manor, the home of the Carian Royal Family, by the Knights of the Cuckoo, the private army of the Academy of Raya Lucaria. It was the final battle in the Liurnian Civil War.

sections.heading: History
sections.body:
Prelude:
Main article: Liurnian Civil War

The Siege of Caria Manor was the decisive battle that occured towards the end of Liurnian civil war.

The head of the Carian Royal Family, Rennala, was left a grieving wreck after being abandoned by her husband, Radagon. The Academy of Raya Lucaria realised she was a champion no longer, and in her weakened state, they took the opportunity to attempt a restoration the long-restricted study of the Primeval Current that had been in place before Rennala became their governor. The Academy imprisoned Rennala in their Grand Library and, alongside their mercantile allies, the Knights of the Cuckoo, began a rebellion against the Carain royalist forces. This marked the beginning the Liurnian civil war.

Some members of the Academy who followed the Lazuli Conspectus chose to defend the Carians. Permitted, yet deemed heretical and shunned within the Acadamy itself, their study believed in equality between the moon and stars.

Siege:
The Knights of the Cuckoo launched a surprise attack against the Caria Manor. The Cuckoo leveled the family's forward defense at what became the Kingsrealm Ruins, swiftly moving on towards the Manor itself. From the design of their shields, specially made for magical defense, it is no secret that the Carians believed the Academy's treachery would one day come. Although they were caught off guard, the Carian's preparations meant their forces were scarcely weakened. The Carians also created an enchanted snare over the Manor as the fighting raged, which in turn ultimately ended the Cuckoo's advance. The Cuckoos caught in the snare had their souls trapped, being redeployed against their comrades as puppet soliders.

The Siege of Caria Manor was somewhat of a pyrrhic victory for the Carians, as they themselves had suffered a great number of casualties. While the battle was won, Rennala was still held captive by the Academy, With Rennala imprisoned, and her successors absent, the Carians fell into disarray. Despite the Cuckoo's defeat, the Academy had regained its independence.

name: Sir Ansbach
description: Sir Ansbach, also known as Pureblood Knight Ansbach, is a character in

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Formerly the feared commander of the Pureblood Knights in service of Lord Mohg, Ansbach is one of the compatriots of Needle Knight Leda who followed Miquella into the Realm of Shadow. A wise old man, Ansbach has dedicated himself to investigating Miquella's purpose by following the trail of crosses he left behind.

Game events:
As with the rest who followed Miquella into the Shadow Realm, Ansbach was under the influence of a charm, which breaks when the Empyrean abandons his Miquella's Great Rune. With his mind free of the charm, Ansbach recalls that he once challenged Miquella in an attempt to free Mohg of his enchantment, which resulted in him falling under the enchantment himself. 

With his faculties restored, Ansbach makes his way to the Specimen Storehouse within the Shadow Keep. There, he learns that Mohg's body has been taken to Miquella, and with the assistance of the Tarnished, discovers that Miquella intends to use Mohg's corpse as a vessel for his king consort.

Ansbach becomes one of Needle Knight Leda's possible targets, resulting in a duel in which the Tarnished may intervene on either side. Should Ansbach survive Leda's attack, he will aid the Tarnished against Leda, Dryleaf Dane, and their allies in Enir-Ilim. Ansbach will then be available to assist the Tarnished in their battle against Promised Consort Radahn, before which he admits that he knows the Tarnished was responsible for killing Mohg, but bears no grudge against them, viewing Mohg's death as an honorable one. After defeating Miquella and his consort, Ansbach dies before the Gate of Divinity.

sections.heading: Character Information
sections.body:
Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing is a boss encounter in Leyndell, Ashen Capital. He utilises both sorceries and incantations in combat, and learns new spells depending on whether you have defeated Rykard, Malenia, or Mohg. He only has seven memory slots, and knows six spells by default, meaning that the spells learned by defeating the aforementioned bosses can replace his default spells. If two of these bosses have been defeated, Gideon will lose Comet Azur. If all three have been defeated, he will lose Triple Rings of Light.

name: Sites of Grace
description: Sites of Grace are special locations in. They serve as resting points where players can fast-travel and manage various aspects of their character. Resting at these locations has multiple effects and provides options to customize and progress.

sections.heading: Using Sites of Grace
sections.body:
Resting at a Site of Grace has the following effects:
Restores the player's HP and FP to full and removes all Buffs and Status Ailments
Refills all charges for both Sacred Flasks
Sets the Site of Grace as the player's respawn point
Respawns Enemies killed throughout the game world (exceptions include Bosses, NPCs, and other foes)
Displays the Site of Grace menu

The Site of Grace menu offers the following options:

Pass Time: Advance time to morning, noon, or nightfall.
Level Up: Allocate Runes to improve character stats.

sections.heading: Acquisition

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: The caster floats up into the air and summons a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of blue flames, dealing Magic damage equal to 188% of Incantation Scaling up to 3 times (i.e. 564% of the same cumulatively) if the entire wave hits. Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 60 points of Stamina to cast, and another 60 points upon using the follow-up breath. 
Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion. 
Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max). 
Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used. 
This spell can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Glintstone Breath. 
Compared to Glintstone Breath, this spell deals 18% more damage but also consumes 40% more FP. 
Casting this spell until it stops costs 144 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*6 FP from keeping the spell running. 
Only 79 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless. 
This is the strongest "named" dragon breath attack, dealing 19% more damage than Ghostflame Breath and 18% more damage than Agheel's Flame, though vulnerability to Frostbite can make up the damage for the former and if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation is substantially lower than its Magic Damage Negation, the latter may deal more damage. 
Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased. 
The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

name: Smithing Master Hewg
description: Smithing Master Hewg is a character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A Scaly Misbegotten bearing aspects of the primordial Crucible, Hewg practiced the once-divine art of smithing. A spirit tuner with distinctive eyes helped him out in the distant past, though she died before he could repay her.

Long ago, Queen Marika cursed Hewg with an impossible task under her Golden Order: to create a weapon capable of slaying a god. Chained to the Roundtable Hold for eternity, he maintained the weapons of Tarnished seeking the Elden Ring.

Game events:
When he meets Roderika, he recognizes that her eyes share the same hue as those of his old acquaintance. Although reluctant at first, Hewg agrees to take Roderika under his wing at the insistence of the the Tarnished.

After the Tarnished sets fire to the Erdtree, the Roundtable Hold also begins to burn. Hewg's chains are broken, yet he insists on remaining in the hold, where he can continue to smith weapons to slay a god, despite Roderika's pleas for him to leave. As the Roundtable burns, Hewg's mental state deteriorates, causing him to slur his words and, eventually, to forget both Roderika and the Tarnished. Roderika decides to respect Hewg's decision to stay at the Roundtable, and resolves to remain with him. Her last request is for the Tarnished to use the weapons Hewg smithed to slay Queen Marika.

sections.heading: Hewg's Quest
sections.body:
Hewg and Roderika's questlines progress together.

Questline progression:
Smithing Master Hewg remains in a fixed location at the Roundtable Hold throughout the entire game.

Speak to Hewg
Once Roderika arrives at the Roundtable Hold, speak to Hewg and select the "About Roderika" dialogue option.
Return to Roderika and tell her what Hewg said.
Return to Hewg and select "About Roderika" again, followed by "Would you watch over Roderika?" and finally "It's what she wants".
Reload the area. Roderika moves, seated across from Hewg, now offers spirit tuning services.
Upon reaching the Forge of the Giants, return and talk for advice.
After burning the Erdtree, return to the Roundtable Hold and select "Let's talk a while". You may then select the dialogue option "Why are you still making weapons?"
After talking to Roderika and selecting "About Hewg", return to Hewg and select "What happened to her?"
After defeating the Godskin Duo, return to Roundtable Hold and speak to Hewg and select "About the god-slaying weapon".
After defeating Maliketh, the Black Blade, return to Hewg and select "About yourself".

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
He wears a brown smith's apron and wields a Hammer.
Although Hewg shares a model with fellow Scaled Misbegotten, he lacks a tail and hair, but has a beard.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Hewg resembles Dark Souls' Andre of Astora. Both are bearded, older, do not leave, wield hammers, upgrade weapons, are always hammering, and can be interacted with for dialogue and lore. They also share a pariah status in their settings, Hewg being a Misbegotten and Andre being an undead.
In an early prerelease version of Elden Ring, Hewg was found in Stormhill Shack, which at that time served as a character hub. Notably, this is now where Roderika is initially found.
Redeemer Guilbert advised the player to meet Hewg, wondering whether he held any unresolved grudges.

name: Smoldering Walls
description:
Smoldering Walls are perpetually burning stone walls found throughout Caelid. Constructed by the Redmanes after the Battle of Aeonia in an effort to suppress the spread of the Scarlet Rot. 

They are lined in several layers throughout the land, with several walls barricading the entrances to Fort Gael and Redmane Castle. One extremely long wall can be found crossing the entire midsection of the western countryside and across the southern edges of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Another smaller wall found west of Rotview Balcony, marking the border between Limgrave and Caelid and acting as an ominous warning to outsiders of the dangers lurking within the rot-infested land.

description: The snowy crone, also known as the snow witch, is an unseen character in. She was the secret mentor of Ranni the Witch.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The snowy crone was a heretical witch who practiced forbidden magic deep within the woods. She taught these cold sorceries to Lunar Princess Ranni in secret, and warned the young Carian to beware the dark moon.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The snowy crone was described as an elderly woman dressed in clothing as white as the snow itself. She wore a heavy cloak of gray furs and a frozen hat with a wide brim and pointed tip. The blue, four-armed doll inhabited by Ranni's soul was modeled after the crone's likeness.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Of the spells imparted by the old snow witch, three are obtainable in-game: Freezing Mist, Frozen Armament, and Glintstone Icecrag.
The icy, wide-brimmed hat and white robes Ranni wears once belonged to the snow witch.
After Ranni resumes her empyrean journey, the Snow Witch set may be found in Renna's Rise.
When initially encountered at the Church of Elleh, Ranni will introduce herself as Renna the witch.
The snowy crone may have a connection to the sorcery of the Zamor people.

sections.heading: Trivia

name: Sorcerer Rogier
description: Sorcerer Rogier is an NPC in. He is first encountered as an optional summon against Margit, the Fell Omen, and is later found within a church searching for knowledge in Stormveil Castle.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A Tarnished dedicated to investigating the fateful Night of Black Knives, Rogier familiarized himself with D, Hunter of the Dead and Fia, Deathbed Companion at the Roundtable Hold. He and Fia discussed at length the Black Knifeprints left by the Black Knife Assassin. He hasn't seen the Guidance of Grace for a long time.

He later left the Hold to search for clues at Stormveil Castle, where he offered to teach the Tarnished his magical combat arts, warning them of Godrick's Tarnished hunters. While exploring the lower reaches of the castle, Rogier discovered a cadaver of the Prince of Death and was infected with Death Blight. 

Back at the Roundtable and immobilized by his condition, Rogier imparted his knowledge of the plot and Those Lost in Death to the Tarnished. If Rogier receives a Black Knifeprint from the Tarnished, he deduces that the one who enchanted the assassins' weapons was Ranni the Witch. He urges the Tarnished to seek Ranni and enter her service in order to learn more. However, he soon succumbs to the Deathroot, leaving behind a note informing the Tarnished of the whereabouts of D's inseparable twin, Devin. 

Fia later summons Rogier as one of her Champions at the Prince of Death's Throne in Deeproot Depths.

name: Sorceress Sellen
description: Sorceress Sellen is a merchant NPC in. She is initially found in Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave and is eager to share her glintstone sorceries.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Sellen was considered to be the most promising glintstone sorceress to ever attend the Academy of Raya Lucaria. Her first teacher at the academy was the sorcerer Azur, one of the founding glintstone sorcerers and originator of the Karolos Conspectus. Azur, along with Lusat, was banished from the academy due to their study of the Primeval Current, a study Sellen wished to pursue. However, following accusations of unspeakable treatment of her fellow scholars under the name of the Graven Witch, Sellen too was expelled from the academy. Sellen had sought to restore the Primeval Current, desiring glintstone sorceries unbound by terrestrial taboos and the pedantry of the Carian Royal Family.

Sellen was also an acquaintance of Preceptor Seluvis, and a frequent visitor to his underground cellar, where he kept his collection of puppets. When Sellen was expelled, Seluvis helped her in some capacity, for which she owes him. 

At some point following her banishment, Sellen was imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins on the Weeping Peninsula, bound by the Academy's shackles. She managed to manifest a projection of herself in the Waypoint Ruins in Limgrave. It is here that she meets the Tarnished, who becomes her apprentice, learning glintstone sorceries from her. When she learns that the Tarnished has found Master Azur on Mt. Gelmir, she requests that they seek out Master Lusat, speculating that he returned to his home of Sellia, Town of Sorcery. The Tarnished discovers Lusat, in a near-inorganic state much like Azur, in Sellia Hideaway, and reports back to Sellen.

Freeing Sellen:

Much like Ranni the Witch, Sellen's fate is tied to the stars, and with the defeat of Starscourge Radahn, Sellen becomes dispossessed of her immortality. This makes her a target of Jerren, a friend of the Carian Royal Family who once made a promise to exterminate the witch. Sellen reveals to the Tarnished that the form they have been speaking to is a projection, and that her true body resides in Witchbane Ruins. The Tarnished meets with Sellen's true body, shackled in the ruin's cellar, and she asks them to remove her Primal Glintstone, beseeching them to look after it. Jerren arrives to find Sellen's previous body already perished. The Tarnished later places Sellen's Primal Glintstone into a puppet in Seluvis's basement, which bears a striking resemblance to Sellen's old body.

Sellen, now in her new, more youthful body, returns to the Academy and displaces Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon. She has the bodies of Azur and Lusat moved back to the Academy, so that she can finally hone the Primeval Current. She offers her support to the Tarnished in their mission to become Elden Lord, and requests that when the time comes, they illuminate her about the secrets of life which course the Elden Ring Before long, however, Jerren finally catches up to her. Should the Tarnished aid her in beating back Jerren, she will continue her research. When the Tarnished next sees her, she has transformed into a Graven Mass.

sections.heading: Quests
sections.body:
Quest items:

Questline progression:
Waypoint Ruins 
Sellen can be found in the cellar of Waypoint Ruins after defeating the Mad Pumpkin Head. Talk to Sellen and then select "I wish to learn glintstone sorceries" to receive the "Nod in Thought" Gesture, and to unlock her sorcery shop.
(Optional) If the Radahn Festival has not commenced, Sellen will have dialogue about it if you have Seluvis's Introduction in your inventory. This is obtained by progressing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline and speaking to Seluvis about Nokron prior to initiating the Festival.
Waypoint Ruins 
Find Primeval Sorcerer Azur, located beyond the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir, to obtain Comet Azur. Return to Sellen and select the "Show Azur's Sorcery" dialogue option. After listening to this dialogue, select the "Tell me your story" option, and then select "Let us journey together". Next, select "I have a favor to ask" to obtain the Sellian Sealbreaker.
The Sellian Sealbreaker can be used to open a sealed tunnel in Sellia Hideaway, behind which is Primeval Sorcerer Lusat. Interact with him to receive Stars of Ruin. It is now possible to select the "Lusat's location" dialogue option when talking to Sellen, which will reward you with a Starlight Shards. This option can be avoided until later in the questline.
Witchbane Ruins
After Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, talk to Sellen to learn that her true body is in Witchbane Ruins. Travel there and speak to the shackled Sellen to obtain Sellen's Primal Glintstone.
Reload the area and return to find Castellan Jerren. In order for him to appear, you must have spoken to him in Redmane Castle after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
Three Sisters
Travel to the Three Sisters and go to the ruined structure north-east of Ranni's Rise. Roll or attack the ground to reveal a hidden staircase leading to a basement full of immobile puppets. Pass through the illusory wall on the far end of the room to find a puppet duplicate of Sellen. Interact with the puppet to insert Sellen's Primal Glintstone, resurrecting Sellen in her new body.
Academy of Raya Lucaria 
There will now be two summon signs outside the door to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library; one red and one gold. To progress Sellen's questline, select the gold summon sign. You will be summoned as a co-operator to assist Sellen in defeating Witch-Hunter Jerren. Defeat Jerren to receive the Eccentric's Set.
This step can only be completed if Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon has been defeated.
Academy of Raya Lucaria
After defeating Jerren, Sellen can be found where Rennala is usually based. Speak to her to receive the Glintstone Kris. If you have not done so already, find Primeval Sorcerer Lusat in Sellia Hideaway and speak to Sellen to select "Lusat's location" and receive Starlight Shards.
It is also possible to obtain Azur and Lusat's armour sets by returning to their respective locations at this point.
Academy of Raya Lucaria
Reload the area after telling Sellen about Lusat. Sellen, now in the form of a Graven Mass, can be found to the side of the room. The Witch's Glintstone Crown can be obtained here. It is still possible to purchase sorceries from her and to offer her scrolls.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Portraits of Sellen are hung around the Academy of Raya Lucaria, notably the Debate Parlor.
Sellen may be summoned as a cooperator against the Red Wolf of Radagon if her Primal Glintstone has been inserted in the doll body from Seluvis's Cellar. Given that this requires both reaching the top of Mt. Gelmir and defeating Starscourge Radahn before you have made significant progress in the Academy of Raya Lucaria, this is rather unlikely to happen naturally.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Sellen's body in the Waypoint Ruins and the doll body in Seluvis's cellar have some differences, with the doll body having a smaller head as well as paler skin and its hair is brown instead of the original's black hair. 
Per the description of the Primal Glintstone Blade, sorcerers would slice open their hearts to imbue primal glintstone with their soul, killing them. As Sellen is already in possession of a Primal Glintstone, it is possible that she has already died, and that the body imprisoned in Witchbane Ruins is not her original body.
Both Sellens in Limgrave are protected by enemies that bring down a cascade of energy. The Miranda Blossom at Waypoint Ruins calls down Holy light, while the Graven Mass at Witchbane Ruins triggers a cascade of starry Magic.

|req = Received at the end of her questline, or by killing her.
Questline progression:
Waypoint Ruins

Sellen can be found in the cellar of Waypoint Ruins after defeating the Mad Pumpkin Head. Talk to Sellen and then select "I wish to learn glintstone sorceries" to receive the "Nod in Thought" Gesture, and to unlock her sorcery shop.

(Optional) If the Radahn Festival has not commenced, Sellen will have dialogue about it if you have Seluvis's Introduction in your inventory. This is obtained by progressing Blaidd the Half-Wolf's questline and speaking to Seluvis about Nokron prior to initiating the Festival.
Waypoint Ruins

Find Primeval Sorcerer Azur, located beyond the Hermit Village on Mt. Gelmir, to obtain Comet Azur. Return to Sellen and select the "Show Azur's Sorcery" dialogue option. After listening to this dialogue, select the "Tell me your story" option, and then select "Let us journey together". Next, select "I have a favor to ask" to obtain the Sellian Sealbreaker.

The Sellian Sealbreaker can be used to open a sealed tunnel in Sellia Hideaway, behind which is Primeval Sorcerer Lusat. Interact with him to receive Stars of Ruin. It is now possible to select the "Lusat's location" dialogue option when talking to Sellen, which will reward you with a Starlight Shards. This option can be avoided until later in the questline.
Witchbane Ruins
After Starscourge Radahn has been defeated, talk to Sellen to learn that her true body is in Witchbane Ruins. Travel there and speak to the shackled Sellen to obtain Sellen's Primal Glintstone.
Reload the area and return to find Castellan Jerren. In order for him to appear, you must have spoken to him in Redmane Castle after defeating Starscourge Radahn.
Three Sisters

Travel to the Three Sisters and go to the ruined structure north-east of Ranni's Rise. Roll or attack the ground to reveal a hidden staircase leading to a basement full of immobile puppets. Pass through the illusory wall on the far end of the room to find a puppet duplicate of Sellen. Interact with the puppet to insert Sellen's Primal Glintstone, resurrecting Sellen in her new body.
Academy of Raya Lucaria

There will now be two summon signs outside the door to the Raya Lucaria Grand Library; one red and one gold. To progress Sellen's questline, select the gold summon sign. You will be summoned as a co-operator to assist Sellen in defeating Witch-Hunter Jerren. Defeat Jerren to receive the Eccentric's Set.
This step can only be completed if Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon has been defeated.
Academy of Raya Lucaria

After defeating Jerren, Sellen can be found where Rennala is usually based. Speak to her to receive the Glintstone Kris. If you have not done so already, find Primeval Sorcerer Lusat in Sellia Hideaway and speak to Sellen to select "Lusat's location" and receive Starlight Shards.
It is also possible to obtain Azur and Lusat's armour sets by returning to their respective locations at this point.
Academy of Raya Lucaria

Reload the area after telling Sellen about Lusat. Sellen, now in the form of a Graven Mass, can be found to the side of the room. The Witch's Glintstone Crown can be obtained here. It is still possible to purchase sorceries from her and to offer her scrolls.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Strengthens Guard Counters from Piercing attacks by 15%. 

As the damage bonus for Guard Counters with Piercing attacks is already 30%, this stacks with that bonus for a total damage boost of 50%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
As with the regular Guard Counter damage bonus, this damage bonus is only applied if a target is attack in the middle of an attack animation. 
Note that the important bit is not that the attack made is a thrust, but that the damage it deals is Pierce damage. 
This leads to some seemingly unexpected synergy with the Lucerne, Pickaxe, Rusted Anchor, and Warpick as all their attacks deal Pierce damage despite not looking the part. 
Skills such as Giant Hunt deal heavy Pierce damage, giving synergy with the Shard of Alexander and the like, and many weapons also reserve their Pierce damage for their heavy attacks, giving some combination potential with the Axe Talisman.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Spellmachinist Rabbath was an innovative glintstone sorcerer who resided in Rabbath's Rise on the Scadu Altus in the Realm of Shadow. He is credited with the creation of Rabbath's Cannon, a jar cannon powered by glintstones that could imbue greatbolts with guiding magic and additional magical damage.

Rabbath's Cannon was most effective when paired with Rabbath's Greatbolts, specialized ammunition tipped with glintstone shards. Upon impact, these bolts caused a powerful magical explosion, making them one of Rabbath's most destructive innovations.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Rabbath's Rise is adjacent to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr and below the Shaman Village.
The puppet of Swordhand of Night Anna is found within Rabbath's tower.
Spellmachinist Rabbath is deceased.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Clasp hands in prayer and then raise them to create a sigil that explodes after a moment, with the explosion having Holy Attack Power equal to 160% of Incantation Scaling.

Continue channeling the incantation to keep the hands raised and send out more pillars, but with less delay between them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 14 points of Stamina per cast. 
Deals 3 Stance damage per hit. 
Attack Power is boosted by 20% per Spiraltree Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Has some vertical reach, enough to hit a Dragon's head when it's walking. 
Since there is a short delay between the sigil being created and the pillar erupting, it's very easy to miss foes moving quicker than a walking pace. 
Requires line of sight between the caster and the target, as the sigil is actually created by an invisible bullet sent out from the caster.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The terms used for Soul in the Japanese script generally refer to the animating consciousness which dwells within living beings and reincarnates upon death, while the term used for Spirit generally refers to the spectral presence left behind by the dead, more akin to a ghost. This distinction seems to hold in Elden Ring, with souls being reborn through the Erdtree and spirits lingering in the form of ashes and such.
An individual's body, soul, and spirit are connected but separate parts of one's identity.
The Deathbirds used ghostflame to separate spirits from ashes.
The Furnace Golems use a form of Messmerfire to burn bodies down to the soul.

Various types of unusual souls and spirits appear in the game.
Fia's Champions are manifestations of the warmth and vigor siphoned from the many heroes held by Fia, Deathbed Companion.
The Dung Eater binds his victims' spirits to his own body.
Like Ulcerated Tree Spirits, the Ancestral Spirits and their horned remains are fully corporeal. They gain new abilities and shine brighter after absorbing the spirits of animals.
Though Serosh is normally ethereal like a spirit, he can turn corporeal at will.
Puppets are usually corporeal, but sometimes appear as phantoms.
The short-lived Larval Tears that sprout from spiritgraves are neither flesh nor spirit; they are a unique form of life somewhere in between.
D, Hunter of the Dead and D, Beholder of Death are one soul with two minds and bodies.
Like Marika and Radagon, Miquella and St. Trina were two entities sharing the same body. When Miquella shed St. Trina, she gained an independent, physical body.
Divine Elements like Scarlet Rot and Messmerfire are able to inhabit and grant life to Putrid Corpses. Those Who Live in Death may function similarly.
Non-living things can be imbued with spirits or souls.
Primeval Sorcerers transfered their souls to primal glintstones.
Warrior Jars can harness the combined power of the champions they contain. When heroic Alexander, Warrior Jar finally cracks, Jar Bairn is selected to inherit Alexander's Innards and fighting spirit.
Golem Smiths read wrinkles in metal to grant souls to Molten Tears and Smithscript weapons.
The spirits of white banners appear over the sites of the major battles of the Shattering, including in the Altus Plateau, Capital Outskirts, and Wailing Dunes. The spirits of fiery red banners are present in the boss arena for Gladius, Beast of Night.
Many ancient gravestones on the Gravesite Plain turned into spiritgraves, the eldest of which have already faded away. Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon transforms her Juvenile Scholars into spiritgraves when she rebirths them with the amber egg.
Ashes of War are the essence of mighty techniques.

Sprites are drawn to holes, where they form nests. Conversely, spirits naturally are drawn to Grave Violets and Gloveworts Spirit Tuners use these to bolster spirits. Grave Keepers used Spirit Glaives to commune with spirits.

Spirits can be permanently destroyed by the Frenzied Flame.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
In Elden Ring, beasts, plants, stones, and even words can contain or become spirits. Animism is the belief that everything—even a word—is imbued with a spirit.
The Blue Dancer fairy can be interpreted as the spirit of the Siofra River due to its etymology.

name: St. Trina
description: St. Trina, also known as the saint of sleep, is an NPC character in:.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
A pale young girl, delicately swaddled within the nurturing petals of a motherly deep-purple flower, rests her cherubic head on folded arms as she slumbers within her tranquil garden. Purple blood seeps from an unhealed wound on the left side of St. Trina's head, and her plant-like lower body twists into a dark stalk that roots her to the earth. A silvery-white streak graces her flowing purple hair, and the sweet, poisonous nectar she secretes grants eternal rest to those who partake of it.

Her earlier form was that of an alluring young woman with two long braids, yet her destined adult form was considered unsettling. Crowned by a flower with eight petals, this cyclopean deity was expected to a awaken a third eye and eight wild braids of hair that coiled into eddy-like spirals.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: St. Trina is found in a small cave within the Garden of Deep Purple at the bottom of the Stone Coffin Fissure.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
An enigmatic and fleeting individual who held dominion over sleep, some say she is a comely young girl, others are sure he is a boy. The only certainty is that their appearance was as sudden as their disappearance. She was the other half of Miquella, the aspect of his love thanks to his Empyrean nature. The Empyrean and aspect inhabit the same body, much like Queen Marika and Lord Radagon. As Miquella they appeared a small, golden-haired boy; as Trina, a prepossessing young woman with silver, light-purple hair. 

St. Trina's love was boundless, offering gentle, intoxicating rest to those she visited in dreams. Some inhabitants of the Lands Between were so enamored that they formed a cult. Light-purple water lilies on the verge of wilting numbed the senses and prevented agitation, symbolizing faith in Trina. Seeking to find her again in their sleep, Trina's followers developed poisonous concoctions to elicit deeper slumber, and some priests were rumored to use sleep-inducing arrows for ritual purposes. Dolores the Sleeping Arrow and Thiollier were among her greatest devotees.

In the final act of the Shattering, Miquella and Malenia mustered an army of Cleanrot Knights and departed the Haligtree for Caelid to confront General Radahn regarding the vow. The ensuing Battle of Aeonia culminated in a duel between Radahn and Malenia, who snapped Miquella's Needle to break the stalemate, unleashing her first scarlet rot bloom. Although she gained wings of strength, fierce Malenia, Blade of Miquella, soon fell into a deep slumber.

Shadow of the Erdtree:
 wings.]]

During Miquella's pilgrimage through the Realm of Shadow, he stopped at the Cerulean Coast and traveled downward into the Stone Coffin Fissure. Deep underground, the Empyrean stood atop the largest stone coffin and divested himself of his love and adoring other self, casting Trina into the chasm's darkest depths. Liberated from his fate and eternal childhood, he sealed the Fissure and resumed his injurious path to godhood.

St. Trina survived her fall; wounded, flowers burgeoned where her nectar-like blood pooled. Her faint, light-purple slumber mists concentrated into an intoxicating deep-purple fog. Trina blossomed, manifesting deep-purple water lilies and forming her Garden of Deep Purple. The congealed, arcane putrescence of ancient heroes imbibed her poisonous nectar, received velvety eternal rest, and became her gallant Putrescent Knight.

Trina's love for Miquella never wavered, even after her abandonment. Unable to speak directly, her singular wish was to grant Miquella forgiveness in death, knowing that godhood would become his prison. If her wish is granted, Trina withers and dies, leaving behind a single harmless water lily.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
St. Trina was a young adult woman in the story trailer, but appears as a young girl in-game. Miquella was a boy during his flashback, but returns a young man at the Gate of Divinity.
Her roots are purple, but her eyebrows and eyelashes are white. 
The white in Trina's hair is reflected in Nectarblood Burgeon and St. Trina's Blossom
Trina's fall displays on-screen while Needle Knight Leda mentions Miquella abandoning his fate in the story trailer.
The woodland creatures that followed Trina into the Fissure received eternal sleep at the spot from which she fell, arranged in uniform rows, as if herded by Ancestral Followers.
Horned Owls drop Deep-Purple Lilies.
Fresh buds also sprout from blood shed by her siblings.
The path to Trina is protected by * Bloodfiends, Gravebirds, Sentry Stones, and Putrescent Skeletons. In addition to his seal, Miquella left behind the golden spirit of a Misbegotten Warrior.
The close relationship between Trina and Miquella was teased prior to the release of Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree:
St. Trina and Miquella are youthful and elusive figures with complementary water lilies: Miquella's Lily and Trina's Lily.
[[Fevor's Cookbook 3|Fevor's Cookbook [3]]] contains the recipe for Bewitching Branches. Blessed with an incantation of Unalloyed Gold, these twigs compel affection.
Guarding the approach to Miquella's Haligtree, Albinauric Archers in the Consecrated Snowfield have lily motifs on their Blue Silver Mail Armor and can drop St. Trina's Arrows. Latenna the Albinauric and her wolf companion, Lobo, rest at the Slumbering Wolf's Shack.
Cleanrot Knights can drop both Miquella and Trina's Lilies.
Slumbering Eggs foreshadowed the Cocoon of the Empyrean and associated nascency with sleep.
Sleep is often equated with Death.
St. Trina's unnerving adult form shares many traits with the cyclopian Fell God.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Trina is a feminine inflection of the Latin trīnus ("three" or "triple"), affirming her status as a triplet.
The unmarked location in Altus Plateau where the Amber Starlight is found is internally referred to as "St. Trina's Hideaway", and features a statue of Miquella and his twin, Malenia.
An additional voiceline was cut from Shadow of the Erdtree. If the player visited Trina and drank her nectar after defeating Promised Consort Radahn she would have thanked the player for their deed before finally withering.
Several early iterations of St. Trina were cut from Elden Ring during development. 
In the files, St. Trina of the Cradlesong sang a lullaby to the Nomadic Merchants, granting them succour by alleviating the Frenzied Flame and allowing them to sleep. After the singer vanished, the merchants left their prison, and soothed themselves by playing the song on their instruments. Later, Merchant Kalé asked the player to collect Slumber Fog with St. Trina's Crystal Ball so he could recreate the effect.
In a later version, Reeling Rico used Slumber Fog to produce Dreambrew, an alcoholic potion that revealed secrets. His questline would have concluded at the Cocoon of the Empyrean, where he would have discovered St. Trina was Miquella all along.
Intriguingly, the Network Test files lacked Miquella's Lilies to match Trina's Lilies, the Chinese and Korean versions of St. Trina's Torch describes her as active since ancient times, and there is no reference to apparent gender fluidity in Sword of St. Trina, suggesting that her textual connection to Miquella had yet to be implemented at this point of development.
Quella, a young boy whose emblem was a sacred tree, was the god of dreams in Dark Souls II.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
The Starfall Crater appears in eastern Limgrave, opening south of the Mistwood and west of Fort Haight.<!--
Unlike its sister cities, the nameless Eternal City lacks a false night sky. Its ruins sit at the edge of a tremendous chasm in the Deeproot Depths, far below the Erdtree, at the source of the Siofra and Ainsel Rivers. It is flooded and sinking into a bog of milky white liquid. Its streets are patrolled by the headless spirits of Mausoleum Knights and the last of the Ravaged Gargoyles keep watch over its empty towers. The city is home to a large Basilisk population, indicating the Prince of Death's Throne must be nearby.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: The nameless Eternal City was built by the Nox in a bygone age. It was protected by Valiant Gargoyles made with the Corpse Wax of fallen champions. It was destroyed by a falling star long ago after its inhabitants sinned against the Greater Will. Despite the Nox's deep knowledge of the fate foretold in the stars, Astel, Naturalborn of the Void appeared suddenly and devastated the city with bombardment of meteorites. The Eternal City was fully depopulated and buried deep underground, where it would again never see a true Night sky.-->

sections.heading: Acquisition

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums with a bell to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Has a 30% damage bonus against Gravity-affinity enemies.
Scales best with Strength until it reaches 54, where after Dexterity-scaling becomes more effective until it reaches 40. Intelligence-scaling is mostly irrelevant for weapon damage. 
Despite being paired weapon it still receives the 50% Strength-bonus from two-handing.
Average weight for a Colossal Sword, effectively allowing dual-wielding with half the weight and therefore with much less required Endurance. 
Two-handing replaces the light attack, including all its derivatives, with dual-wield attacks. Blocking also becomes available while heavy attacks remain the same. 
This means two-handed dual-wield attacks will deal more damage than heavy attacks, though the latter will still deal more Stance damage per hit. 
The skill has a special follow-up heavy attack. 
Only the first part of the skill counts as a roar attack and benefits from the Roar Medallion and Highland Axe.

Patch 1.09 increased the scaling values as well as the speed of guard counters.

name: Starscourge Radahn
description: , also known as General Radahn, the Red Lion General, and later as Promised Consort Radahn and Radahn, Consort of Miquella, is an optional Demigod boss and a mandatory God boss in:;.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Red-maned Radahn was the son of Radagon, a champion of the Erdtree, and Queen Rennala of the Full Moon, head of both the Carian royal family and Academy of Raya Lucaria, born after the Second Liurnian War. He had two siblings, Rykard and Ranni. Radahn inherited his father's flaming red hair and was fond of its heroic implications. From a young age, he was enamored with the Elden Lord Godfrey. Attempting to emulate his idol, Radahn adorned his armor with lions, the symbol of Godfrey and Serosh.

At some point, the first Elden Lord, Godfrey, was robbed of grace and hounded from the Lands Between. Radahn's father, Radagon, left Rennala to become Queen Marika's new consort and the second Elden Lord. Radahn and his siblings were thus raised to demigod status by their new step-mother, Marika.

In their youth, Radahn's Empyrean half-brother Miquella deeply admired him for his kindness and strength, seeing in him the qualities of a lord. When he decided to pursue godhood, he made a vow with Radahn that, upon his deific return, he would take Radahn as his consort. In return, Miquella would uphold some unspecified part of the vow.

Not wanting to abandon his scrawny but beloved steed, Leonard, Radahn studied gravitational magic in Sellia under a master who was an Alabaster Lord. Radahn befriended the Albinauric Gaius, a senior disciple of his teacher, and the two formed a competitive yet friendly rivalry. Radahn's step-brother Messmer the Impaler was also friends with Gaius, and the two became as elder brothers to Radahn.

Mastering gravitational magic allowed Radahn to manipulate the forces of gravity and challenge the stars themselves. During the Starscourge Conflict, Radahn saved Sellia by conquering the stars and arrested their cycles, delaying fate. Having earned himself the moniker "Starscourge," he engraved the gravity crest upon his blades.

Radahn's soldiers were known as the Redmanes for the red-maned lion raising a sword in the image of Radahn on their surcoats. The longest serving of the Redmane Knights was Ogha, who studied gravitational techniques alongside Radahn in Sellia. It was popularly said that the Redmanes knew no weakness. At an unknown period in time, Jerren, a guest of the Carian royals, became a guest commander for Radahn's armies, and they swore a mutual oath of honorable death. During his youth, Radahn witnessed the valor of a gladiator called Freyja, who he asked to become another member of his knights; an offer Freyja accepted.

The Shattering:

At some point following the Night of Black Knives, Queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring, and her offspring acquired the Great Runes. The maddening taint of their newfound strength led to the Shattering, a war between Marika's demigod descendants, each seeking to become the new ruler of the Lands Between.

From his stronghold of Redmane Castle in the Caelid Wilds, Radahn led his armies against the forces of the other demigods. Radahn tried to challenge Godrick the Grafted in Limgrave, but the latter hid in Stormveil Castle. 

By the end of the Shattering, only Radahn and his half-sister Malenia, Blade of Miquella were left standing. The two fought to a stalemate in the Battle of Aeonia, their duel ending inconclusively when Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot. As the Scarlet Aeonia flower blossomed, Malenia whispered in Radahn's ear, "Miquella awaits thee, O promised consort."

The Scarlet Rot ravaged Caelid and consumed Radahn from the inside, eating away at his psyche but failing to kill him. Following the Battle of Aeonia, Radahn roams the Wailing Dunes as a mindless beast who devours the flesh of friend and foe alike, howling at the sky. Without their commander, the Redmane Knights burned the crest on the left breast of their armor to indicate their resolve not to return home, and to serve as a bulwark against the spread of the rot in Caelid using fire.

Despite his madness, Radahn continues to ride his scrawny steed, as well as halt the motions of the stars. The Radahn Festival has been organized by his men in Castle Redmane to celebrate his last battle. It is a gathering of mighty warriors who might finally put the General out of his misery and claim his Great Rune for themselves. The festival serves as Jerren's way of fulfilling his oath of honorable death to Radahn.

Game events:
Upon the participation of a Tarnished Champion, the Radahn Festival is a success, and Radahn is freed from his tortured existence. His death causes the stars to resume their cycles, some of which come crashing down upon the Lands Between. One such falling star lands in Limgrave, opening the path to Nokron, Eternal City, and allowing the fate of Ranni the Witch to progress.

Shadow of the Erdtree:
Following Radahn's defeat, his soul met its end. However, Miquella sought to revive it, still desiring for Radahn to be his lord consort. Miquella successfully revived Radahn, placing his soul into a vessel made from the remains of Mohg, Lord of Blood, another Demigod slain by the same Tarnished who had defeated Radahn. The Tarnished encounters the newly-resurrected Radahn at the Gate of Divinity at the top of Enir-Ilim. Radahn stands guard as Miquella completes his ascension to godhood and battles the Tarnished once more. During the ensuing battle, Miquella steps out of the Gate of Divinity and embraces Radahn as his consort and fights the Tarnished with Radahn. The Tarnished triumphs over Radahn and Miquella, thus preventing Miquella's age of compassion.

sections.heading: First Encounter (Starscourge Radahn)
sections.body:
The fight against Starscourge Radahn only becomes available when the Radahn Festival commences. This requires the player to either activate a Site of Grace in Altus Plateau, talk to Blaidd the Half-Wolf about Radahn in Siofra River, or talk to War Counselor Iji about Jerren.

Torrent can be called during this fight and is useful for closing distance and evading Radahn's ranged attacks.

Multiple NPCs are available to be summoned during the fight, and their summons can be located throughout the arena. Six can be summoned at a time, and once a summon sign is used it will vanish, however each NPC has multiple summon signs that can be used.

The following eight champions are available:

Alexander, Warrior Jar
Blaidd the Half-Wolf
Castellan Jerren (phase 2 only)
Finger Maiden Therolina
Great Horned Tragoth 
Lionel the Lionhearted
Okina
Patches (disconnects after arrival)

Moveset:

Phase 1:
The player will spawn some distance away from Radahn, with the boss visible at the top of a dune in the distance. Immediately, Radahn will begin firing volleys of arrows which rain down from above, homing in on the player, as well as gravity arrows. The latter can be avoided by hiding behind the clusters of weapons dug into the ground, however the weapons will break when struck. Riding Torrent will make it easier to avoid the volleys. Summon signs can be found in clusters all around the arena, and can be used to summon NPCs to assist in the fight.

Once the player is close enough, Radahn will begin attacking using his swords. He is very mobile, using his horse to cover distance easily. He also uses a number of gravity-based attacks, such as Cragblade, gravity waves, and Collapsing Stars.

Phase 2:
Once his health is below 50%, Radahn will launch himself into the sky, disappearing for several seconds. He will then come crashing down in a ball of fire, dealing devastating damage to anyone caught in the impact. Radahn now gains the ability to raise four floating rocks, which will hover beside him and then launch at the player or their summons. He also gains the ability to float into the air and spin rapidly while charging.

Environment:
The Wailing Dunes is a very large arena consisting of many tall dunes, with Radahn initially standing at the top of the largest dune close to the centre of the area. Clusters of weapons can be found stuck in the sand, and can be used to hide from Radahn's arrows. Summon signs can be found throughout the arena, often in clusters of two or three.

Strategy:
During the first encounter, Radahn can be defeated by luring him to the cliffs in the far north, causing him to fall to his death. Alternatively, players can position themselves at the southern shore during his phase transition, leading Radahn to crash into the ocean upon descent.

sections.heading: Second Encounter (Promised Consort Radahn)
sections.body:
The second encounter with Radahn serves as the final boss of the Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree expansion. The first phase is Promised Consort Radahn and the second is Radahn, Consort of Miquella. 

Moveset List:

Phase 1:
Just like in the base game, players will spawn a distance away from Radahn. While retaining his gravity magic, and as his soul now possessed Mohg's remains, Radahn now employs Bloodflame, and seamlessly switches between the two elemental magics while in combat. To defeat him, it is always important to time your attacks in between Radahn's string of attacks or pull off counters at the very end of a combo. Because of his recovery time, this makes his boss battle complicated, as he can launch other attacks almost instantly after finishing a heavy attack. As a result, it is important to note that patience and appropriate timing are the keys to defeating Radahn. The optimal moment to attack is when he finished his basic sword combos, and would take a brief pause to recover. 

At the start of his boss battle, he will nearly always use a gravity attack to prevent players from summoning or buffs upon entry into the boss battle. Because of this, players are recommended to use buffs before accessing the boss and cast summons right after dodging the initial attack. During his first phase, Radahn will use a flurry of combos aside from special abilities such as a Bloodflame Slash and his Gravity attacks. After being reduced to 65% of his health, this will trigger a cutscene leading to Phase 2.

Phase 2:
In this phase, Radahn's previous attacks are improved and he gains new powerful abilities. Most of them are Holy-powered and have a wider AoE. Overall, while his attacks become more lethal, Radahn is now faster in speed, now capable of creating mirror images to attack and using strong Holy-based abilities, making the boss battle more difficult and challenging. However, despite gaining immense power, Radahn's health has already been reduced to 75%, allowing players to gain a slight edge. It is important to capitalize on the pauses of Radahn's combo attacks, as there are opportunities to strike. Constantly taking advantage of them can deplete his health and because Radahn's attacks can be very punishing if caught off-guard, you have to be prepared to switch between offensive and defensive at times.

While Radahn can still perform similar combos from Phase 1, they have an additional Holy damage explosion at the end. As Miquella is now mounted on his back, he can do a grab attack where he will glow and jump at the player in order to grab them. If successful, Radahn will bring them close to Miquella, who will then place the player under a charm. While this doesn't deal any damage, if Radahn successfully grabs the player a second time while they are charmed, this will ultimately result in instant death. Using Miquella's Great Rune will undo the charm. 

Environment:
The arena consists of a very wide area, with a rough white surface filled with gray-white decomposed corpses, which can be found sticking from the ground. At the other end of the arena, stands the Gate of Divinity itself, where Miquella will step out in divine aspect in the second phase.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
General Radahn and his foot soldiers engaged Margit, the Fell Omen during an undisclosed battle of the Shattering.
Starscourge Radahn's feet have been eaten away by the scarlet rot.
Promised Consort Radahn has Omen horns and casts Blood Oath Incantations because he inhabits Mohg's body.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Radahn is the only Shardbearer boss with no spoken dialogue or cinematic introduction immediately before his battle (excluding the cutscene triggered by speaking with Castellan Jerren) or during his phase transition.
Although Radahn remains silent in the DLC, unused voice lines suggest he once had an introductory monologue.
The description of the Longtail Cat Talisman referenced Radahn owning a pet cat, though this detail was later removed.
Hidetaka Miyazaki has cited Radahn's first battle as his personal favorite boss fight, praising the character's design and the duel's bittersweet tone.

sections.heading: Note
sections.body:
Most information about Stone Astrolabes is conjectural, based on its visual details and context.
The name "Stone Astrolabe" appears in the Messages system among a list of gameplay objects and landmark features. Although the nameless Starlight Shard collection basins don't meet the real-world definition for "stone astrolabe", they're the only recurring objects that fit the general description of an otherwise missing gameplay feature. Their Japanese name, 星見台 (Hoshimidai, lit. Star Viewing Pedestal) more accurately reflects their purpose.
Astrologers and Fire Giants being friends may be explained by the fact that both found common ground in the Sun, one group studying the star closest to the Lands Between with their sundials, the other looking at it through the lens of faith.

sections.body: Stone Astrolabes were inspired by real-world hemicycliums made from stone.

description: The Stone Coffin Fissure (石棺の大穴, Sekkan no Ooana) is a legacy dungeon located within the Realm of Shadow in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Stone Coffin Fissure accumulated many stone coffins over the ages. In ancient times, ghostflame cleansed the impure lives within these vessels, but their putrid remains eventually congealed into Putrescence.

After the Shattering, the Empyrean Miquella embarked on a self-sacrificial pilgrimage to the Land of Shadow to attone for the sins of his mother, Queen Marika the Eternal. Before his ascension to godhood, Miquella attempted to rid himself of his curse of nascency by casting off his other self, St. Trina, into the chasm. In doing so, he abandoned his ability to love, dooming his Age of Compassion.

At the bottom of the fissure, St. Trina's slumbering presence transformed the land into the Garden of Deep Purple, where Deep-Purple Lilies and Nectarblood Burgeon began to bloom. The leaking contents of the stone coffins imbibed her velvety nectar, achieving eternal rest and manifesting as the Putrescent Knight.

sections.body:
Found at an altar in either Fog Rift Catacombs, Ruins of Unte, or Ancient Ruins of Rauh. Since the altar in Fog Rift Catacombs is the most complicated to reach, it's recommended that the sword be taken there so that the later interactions with altars are less time-consuming. 
WARNING: Once either the Sword of Darkness or Sword of Light has been acquired, though the two forms can be freely switched between by traveling to their assigned altars, the Stone-Sheathed Sword itself cannot be reacquired until you enter the next new game cycle.
Fog Rift Catacombs: From the start, follow the path so that you pass the first and second falling-spikes roofs to the elevator. Continue to the third falling-spikes roof and get to the other side of the room (be wary of the pit in the second saferoom to the left). Use the raised platform at the end of the room to enter the hidden compartment in the falling roof, then ride it to a higher platform so you can stand on top of the falling roof. The altar is in the opposite right corner of the room, on the roof. 
Picking the sword up here means it turns into the Sword of Darkness at Ruins of Unte and the Sword of Light at Ancient Ruins of Rauh. 
Ruins of Unte: Found to the right inside the courtyard, blocked by a Furnace Golem (a Hefty Fire Pot can get it going again to open the path). 
Picking the sword up here means it turns into the Sword of Darkness at Fog Rift Catacombs and the Sword of Light at Ancient Ruins of Rauh. 
Ancient Ruins of Rauh: From Ancient Rauh Ruins, East Site of Grace, head across the bridge towards the west, then continue forward until a small body of water, and take a right. Take the Spirit Spring that is now straight ahead and jump forward (north-northeast on the map) to a ruin underneath the large cliff. Here is a body with the Greater Potentate's Cookbook 9 on a pile of rubble. Standing at the cookbook with the Spirit Spring directly behind you, turn to the right to see a tower and a "broken" bridge (actually just invisible) that can be crossed to reach the altar. 
Picking the sword up here means it turns into the Sword of Darkness at Ruins of Unte and the Sword of Light at Fog Rift Catacombs.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
While the locked skill, Square Off, is rather generic for a Straight Sword, it's still powerful due to the guard-breaking ability of its light attack version and the heavy Stance-breaking of its heavy attack version. 
A single sword switched between Sword of Darkness, Sword of Light, and Stone-Sheathed Sword forms always has the same level. 
This means that if the Stone-Sheathed Sword is upgraded to +3 before switching to Sword of Darkness, you will gain a Sword of Darkness +3. If it's then upgraded to +7, it will become a Sword of Light +7 when switched. 
Note that all swords currently held in one's inventory switch forms when the respective altar is interacted with. Thus, extra Stone-Sheathed Swords should be kept in the item box when interacting with the altars to switch between the Sword of Light and Sword of Darkness forms. 
There are a few reasons to keep the sword in this form, as it's a fairly weak weapon that is only barely stronger than the Cane Sword. 
It has one interesting quality, which is that it's a Straight Sword that inflicts Strike damage, which is strong against mechanical, armored, and skeletal foes. 
Its scaling is quite different from the Sword of Light and Sword of Darkness, with its Strength-scaling at +0 completely outstripping either other sword's Strength-scaling at +10, and its Dexterity-scaling also almost does the same, and it has no Faith requirement. In exchange, its Physical damage is lower, and it completely lacks Holy damage and Faith-scaling. 
Though this weapon technically gains the most Attack Power (AP) from a pure Strength build, a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build with a leaning towards Strength works better since it barely sacrifices one-handed Attack Power in exchange for a slightly greater amount of Attack Power when two-handed. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 459 AP, 60 Strength and 30 Dexterity grants 458 AP, and 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 443 AP. Two-handing grants 488 AP, 503 AP, and 493 AP, respectively.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Their battle with Lord Godfrey likely occured after the War Against the Giants.
The Storm Lord presumably ruled over Limgrave from Stormveil Castle during the era when the true storm raged at Stormhill.
A large portrait of Godfrey and Serosh hangs in the castle's main hall, which is patrolled by the Grafted Scion. A statue of Godfrey and Serosh also appears in the throne room.
This kingdom extended southward to Castle Morne on the Weeping Peninsula, which was likewise conquered by Godfrey.
Banished Knight Engvall served as castellan of either Stormveil Castle or Castle Morne at some point between the Long March and the First Defense of Leyndell.
The identity of the Storm Lord is unknown, though the Stormhawk King is the most likely candidate. However, both Dragonlord Placidusax and the Divine Beast are also associated with storms.
Kenneth Haight declares Nepheli Loux, Warrior—a presumed scion of Hoarah Loux, Warrior—the true heir to Limgrave after she accepts the ashes of the Stormhawk King.
She can only accept this item after the defeat of Morgott, the Omen King, another heir to Godfrey.
In an unused questline branch, Gatekeeper Gostoc or even Kenneth himself could have succeeded Godrick the Grafted as lord.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Found in the Chapel of Anticipation. After returning to the area via the portal at The Four Belfries, go through the previously locked door near the main entrance, and follow the staircase into the upper level of the chapel to find the ashes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Upgraded with Ghost Gloveworts.
Summons a brown Stormhawk. 
Deals Standard damage. 
Will immediately let out a war cry that functions as an Aura Buff to strengthen itself and its summoner by increasing all Physical damage, Stamina damage against blocking, and Stance damage by 20% for 60 seconds. This war cry will periodically be reused. 
While it has fairly low health, the evasiveness of its flying and its tendency to use divebomb attacks instead of simply hanging around in melee range causes Deenh to actually have pretty good survivability. 
This divebomb attack can actually deflect projectiles (if only very rarely) and will knock human-sized enemies over.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Localisation Notes
Rather than "unwanted child", the soulless demigod(s) of the mausoleum is referred to as Queen Marika's "ugly bastard" or "ugly spawn." (醜い落とし子, Minikui otoshi-ko.)
The verb used to describe the sun not being "swallowed" in Castle Sol is 蝕まれませ (Mushibama remase) which can mean "to be eaten by worms", or more generally "to spoil, to undermine, to gnaw at." This may be a play on words, as 蝕ま (Mushibama) is written with kanji that also denotes an eclipse, 蝕.
The souls outside the Limgrave Colosseum and the Divine Tower of Caelid both wear the cut Brave Set. The one in Caelid wears the altered version.
