sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The sun is typically depicted with eight, ten, or sixteen points.
The sun's movement across the sky doesn't impact the stationary moons. Rather than reflecting the light of the sun, they produce their own or reflect that of an unseen source in the east.
Sunwarmth Stones radiate the healing warmth of the gentle sun. They are made by imbuing Spiritgrave Stones with an ancient Erdtree incantation. They were introduced to the Shadow Realm by invaders faithful to Marika's Erdtree.
The weaker Warming Stones exude the warmth of the old Erdtree.
The Golden and Tarnished Golden Sunflowers all bloom facing the Erdtree rather than the sun, whereas the Shadow Sunflowers face the Scadutree.
The Eclipse emblem is available as a tattoo. It shows the color dripping from the sun in a way that resembles a sunflower.
A faded sunset was the last thing partakers of the original form of Dragon Communion saw with human eyes before becoming Ancient Dragons.
Castle Sol holds a Haligtree Secret Medallion (Left).
The Dryleaf Set worn by Dryleaf Dane was faded through exposure to the sun.
Abductor Virgins have sun-shaped wheels, or circular saws.
A swirling sun is etched into the Mask of Confidence worn by Radagon's Preceptors.

Speculation:
The sun is possibly synonymous with the polar star depicted on the Black Leather Shield.
The identity of the "sun realm" or the city once called the "Seat of the Sun" remains unclear. It may refer to one—or none—of the following locations:
Crumbling Farum Azula
Beast Skeleton Knights carry the Sun Realm Shield.
Ruin Fragments and Sanctuary Stones interact with light. Sanctuary Stones blessed with Two Fingers incantations become Warming Stones.
Farum Azula was destroyed by a meteor impact in time immemorial.
The sun remains fixed in place in the eastern sky when viewed from this location.
Enir-Ilim
It would nestle perfectly atop the Gate of Divinity.
A prominent sundial appears at the center of the ashen arena where Miquella's Followers are fought. The orientation of this clock holds importance as it is exactly as it appears in concept art for the area.
The sun never sets in this location.
Potent Sunwarmth Stones are made from Spiritgrave Stones harvested from the adjacent Gravesite Plain.
Several circular motifs above doorways may symbolize the sun.
Stormveil Castle
Like the Gate of Divinity, there is an intentional trough built into the two primary towers.
The warm sun variant may be—or may have once been—connected to the Fell God.
The Furnace Visage, depicting the fell god, resembles a sun. It appears on the Furnace Golems, where it sits high above the heads of Fire Giants depicted on their knees.
The sun medallion worn by the Dung Eater symbolized his guiding grace and his Mending Rune of the Fell Curse. Reddish hair strands grow from the excised horns on his Omen Armor.
Queen Marika's victory over the fell god coincided with the growth of the Erdtree, which once radiated the warmth of the sun.
An eclipse likely occured in the past, possibly giving rise to the soulless king Ensha.
The failure of the eclipse plan may have been a consequence of the Starscourge Conflict, when Starscourge Radahn halted the movement of the stars. It is also possible the revival was prevented by the Prince of Death setting the colorless eclipsed sun ablaze with his flames, spreading Death in the process.
Miquella finds a different way to summon the soul of Radahn into Mohg's body at the Gate of Divinity.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Before it was the scarlet rot Swamp of Aeonia, the heart of Caelid contained the Street of Sages, a western extension of Sellia, Town of Sorcery, where great sorcerers practiced Gravity Sorcery. Alongside peers Gaea and Gaius, young Radahn learned this potent form of magic from an ancient Alabaster Lord. However, it was fate that the stars would destroy Sellia. After learning all he could from his master, Radahn confronted the stars and prevailed. Following the Starscourge Conflict, the Red Lion was the renowned Starscourge.

The area was later known as the site of the last battle of the Shattering—the Battle of Aeonia. The Redmane forces of General Radahn clashed the invading cleanrot forces of Miquella of the Haligtree. The mightiest Demigods and greatest champions of the era—Starscourge Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella fought each other to a standstill. Unable to match Radahn's measure, Malenia snapped the Unalloyed Gold Needle that suppressed her curse, producing her first-ever bloom of her Scarlet Aeonia. She unleashed her Aeonian Butterflies and gained wings of strength.

In the aftermath, Miquella himself rescued Redmane Freyja, who was striken with rot. He drained the disease from her body, earned her loyalty, and vanished, abandoning Commander O'Neil, Malenia, and her Cleanrot army. Over time, the area was scarlet rot formed a vast red bog that gave rise to ancient Rot Disciples and contemporary Kindred of Rot. A great scarlet rotflower tree grew, and rot ate away at the land like a vicious plague. Later, young Scarlet Buds, offshoots of Malenia, were born of the rot. Sage Gowry cultivates them, taking care they blossomed into beautiful Scarlet Valkyries.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Localization Notes
The two Liurnian Wars and the Routing of the Ancient Dragons are referred to as 戦役 (Sen'eki), which can be read "military campaign" and "battle", as well as "war."
The second line in the First Liurnian War monument says less ambiguously "red-haired Radagon becomes a hero." (赤髪のラダゴン、英雄となる, Akagami no Radagon, eiyū to naru.)
The "siege" of Caria Manor is referred to as 防衛戦 (Kōjō-sen) meaning "defensive battle", the same kanji used to refer to the First and Second Defenses of Leyndell.
Radahn less ambiguously is called "protector of Sellia" (サリアの護り, Saria no mamori) in the second line of the Starscourge Conflict monument.
The second line of the Routing of the Ancient Dragons monument says less specifically that Godwyn the Golden fought bravely or desperately, rather than "to the last." (黄金のゴッドウィン勇戦し, Ougon no Goddowin yūsen shi)
The second line of the First Defense of Leyndell monument says that the sovereign alliance "collapses from within and becomes defeated" or "becomes a defeated army." (内から瓦解し敗軍となる, Uchi kara gakai shi haigun to naru.)
May be a reference to the Hill of Swords from Berserk.
Consequently may be a reference to Sverd i fjell in Norway.

image: ER Icon Weapon Sword of Darkness.png
description: The Sword of Darkness is a melee armament in, included in the expansion.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Take the Stone-Sheathed Sword or Sword of Light to an altar at either Fog Rift Catacombs or Ruins of Unte. 
WARNING: Once either the Sword of Darkness or Sword of Light has been acquired, though the two forms can be freely switched between by traveling to their assigned altars, the Stone-Sheathed Sword itself cannot be reacquired until you enter the next new game cycle.
See the page for the Stone-Sheathed Sword for all 3 altar locations.
If the Stone-Sheathed Sword was taken from Fog Rift Catacombs or Ancient Ruins of Rauh, the altar at Ruins of Unte should be used. If it was taken from Ruins of Unte, the altar at Fog Rift Catacombs should be used.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones.
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The unique skill, Darkness, sprays streams of Holy darkness in a rotating circle around the user. This takes about 4 seconds to cast and reduces the Holy damage negation for any enemies hit by 20% for 60 seconds. Since this casts quite slowly, taking about 4 seconds to complete, it's best used in an ambush to strengthen any Holy damage attacks used afterwards. 
The debuff inflicted does not stack with any other defence or attack debuff, except Frostbite. This includes the two moon sorceries Rennala's Full Moon and Ranni's Dark Moon, the Shriek of Milos of the Sword of Milos, Acid Spraymist, and the Soul Stifler skill of the Winged Greathorn.
Since the Sword of Light's skill, Light, works as a Body Buff, these two skills work well together to raise the damage of Holy attacks significantly.
Has identical statistics to the Sword of Light. Only their unique skills and appearances distinguish one from the other.
A single sword switched between Sword of Darkness, Sword of Light, and Stone-Sheathed Sword forms always has the same level. 
This means that if the Stone-Sheathed Sword is upgraded to +3 before switching to Sword of Darkness, you will gain a Sword of Darkness +3. If it's then upgraded to +7 it will become a Sword of Light +7 when switched.
Incredibly bad damage negation when blocking, even for a Straight Sword.
Note that all swords currently held in one's inventory switch forms when the respective altar is interacted with. Thus, keeping one sword in the item box allows for the dual-wielding of the Sword of Darkness and Sword of Light.
Scales the best with a pure Strength build but due to scaling becoming less effective when stats are leveled above 54 a hybrid Strength/Faith build performs almost as well. The second, hybrid build will also deal more damage with the skill. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 80 Strength grants 638 Attack Power (AP), and 45 Strength and 45 Faith grants 622 AP.
Note that the high levels of Faith required to wield the sword, a hybrid Strength/Faith build, effectively have 14 more levels to work with. These could either be put in other stats, such as Endurance for more Equip Load or Stamina, or Mind for more FP, but they could also be put into Strength and Faith for more AP. Doing this would put both stats at 52 and grant 642 AP.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
In a locked room at Caria Manor, Liurnia of the Lakes, which the Tarnished can jump into from above on the walkways where the Raya Lucaria Soldier puppets appear.

More specifically, starting from the Manor Lower Level Site of Grace walk out onto the stone walkways and take a left when they path splits in two. Follow the path as it turn to the right and look to the left when halfway across the last walkway. Search for a nearby roof to jump onto and then walk forward to find another roof further down. In one of the corners should be a ladder leading down into the inside of a tower with a chest containing the sword as well as a door leading outside.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
This weapon possess one of the strongest skills in the game, Night-and-Flame Stance. While holding the stance, the user is able to perform either a miniature Comet Azur with a light attack or a flame wave resembling the skill Flame of the Redmanes with a heavy attack. 
Since both Magic damage and Fire damage have specialized ways to increase their damage (their respective Shrouding Cracked Tear, as well as Terra Magica for Magic and Flame, Grant Me Strength for Fire) it may be best to think ahead and try to specialize if you are about to challenge a touch foe or boss. 
One of the main weaknesses of this weapon is the relative lack of other equipment that scales well with both Intelligence and Faith, which pretty much only the Golden Order Seal being a strong option. The Prince of Death's Staff (and the much harder to get Gelmir Glintstone Staff) has rather subpar returns for Sorcery Scaling when the two stats are below 60, making it only relatively good with Death Sorceries and rather bad with everything else. 
It's possible to invest primarily in only one of the two stats, but it's ill-advised to do this beyond the early and early-to-mid sections of the game. This is because, while doing so lets you potentially hyper-specialize in one of the attacks and more easily overcome flat defences early on, it will also lock you into one element, and both the sword's own damage and the skill's damage doesn't scales all that well past 54 in the associated stat. 
Just meeting the sword's requirements means that you will have the Intelligence to cast the Magic-boosting Terra Magic and the Fire-boosting Flame, Grant Me Strength, and just 1 more points in Faith will let the wielder cast the Golden Vow spell (which also boosts the skill since it's based of weapon Attack Power).

The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Despite the skill's description that the light attack follow-up casts Night Comet it actually casts Comet Azur. 
Patch 1.07 increased attack power, the attack direction may now be adjusted up and down when using a normal attack, added damage detection to the weapon part.
This is in regard to the skill. 
Increased the damage of the light attack follow-up from 100%, 150%, and 180% of weapon Magic Attack Power (1,180% in total) to 108%, 162%, and 194% of Magic Attack Power (1,274% in total). 
Increased the damage of the heavy attack follow-up from 700% of weapon Fire Attack Power to 800% of Fire Attack Power. 
Patch 1.03 decreased weapon skill, Sword of Night and Flame’s damage.

name: Sword of St. Trina
image: ER Icon weapon Sword of St Trina.png
description: Sword of St. Trina is a straight sword found in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Behind a Stonesword Key imp statue in the Forsaken Ruins, Caelid, visible directly below the ledge at the Rotview Balcony Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The skill, Mists of Slumber, is notable for being a strong tool for inflicting Sleep, both from the mist's 156 Sleep build-up per second and from the Weapon Buff it grants for 30 seconds, giving the sword another 70 Sleep build-up on top of its innate 66 Sleep build-up, 136 Sleep build-up total. 
In combination with the innate Sleep build-up, a buffed Sword of St. Trina can make the notoriously strong-but-sleep-vulnerable Godskin Noble fall asleep in two hits. This is quite valuable since it is a very easily accessible and reusable tool for inducing Sleep. 
Gains the most Attack Power from a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build or a pure Dexterity build. At the same time, the Intelligence-scaling is largely useless due to being the weakest scaling (maxing out at 36% versus Strength's 50% and Dexterity's 72%) and scaling the much, much weaker Magic damage. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 542 AP, 80 Dexterity grants 533 AP, and 45 Dexterity and 45 Intelligence grants 490 AP. 
While it can technically match the strongest Keen Straight Swords (Longsword and Broadsword) in terms of pure Attack Power, the fact that a considerable part of that is Magic damage (about 20% on a pure Dexterity build) hampers the damage a bit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The inwards-curled and flowery hilt, resembling two Trina's Lily, gives it a striking resemblance to a sword that is generally considered to be the sword Tizón (alt. Tizona), owned by the legendary Spanish folk hero, knight, and ruler Rodrigo Días de Vivar aka El Cid. 
Patch 1.06 fixed a bug where the effect added to the weapon upon using “Mists of Slumber” was lost when the player received an attack. 
Patch 1.04 increased cast speed Of the skill.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.body:
Defeating Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy at any point during Tanith's questline will cause all subsequent steps in the questline to become locked.#Upon entering Volcano Manor, Tanith can be found to the right of the Site of Grace. Speak to her and agree to join the family. Tanith will give you the Drawing Room Key.
Go into the corridor to the right of Tanith and open the first door on the left. Pick up the Letter from Volcano Manor on the table as well as the Recusant Finger.
Travel to the entrance to the colosseum in Stormhill and interact with the invasion sign to fight Old Knight Istvan. After defeating him, report back to Tanith to obtain Magma Shot.
Go back to the drawing room and pick up the Letter from Volcano Manor. Travel to Altus Plateau and find an invasion sign at the bottom of the gorge leading to Shaded Castle. Interact with the sign to fight Rileigh the Idle. After defeating him, talk to Tanith to obtain the Serpentbone Blade.
(Optional) If you have advanced Rya's questline and met her in serpent form, and rested at a Site of Grace in the main dungeon area of Volcano Manor, speak to Tanith to obtain the Tonic of Forgetfulness. This step will be locked if you kill Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood, before giving Rya the Serpent's Amnion.
Pick up the Red Letter from the drawing room, and travel to the Shack of the Lofty in the Mountaintops of the Giants. Interact with the invasion sign to fight Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood. Report back to Tanith to obtain the Taker's Cameo.
Tanith will now offer to send you directly to Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, bypassing the rest of the Volcano Manor. Defeat Rykard and return to Tanith and exhaust her dialogue.
Travel to the Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy Site of Grace to find Tanith eating the remains of Rykard.
(Optional) After obtaining the Dancer's Castanets from Patches in Shaded Castle, offer them to Tanith. There is no reward for doing so, however the Dancer's Castanets will be removed from your inventory.
(Optional) Attacking Tanith will cause her to die in a single hit. You will then be invaded by Tanith's Knight. Defeating the knight will reward you with Aspects of the Crucible: Breath and the Consort's Set.

name: Terra Magica
description: Terra Magica is a spell in.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Creates a large, stationary sigil inside of a circle, centered on where the caster stands that lasts for 30 seconds and grants a +35% (+20% in PvP) increase to all Magic damage dealt while standing inside of it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Since all Magic damage, not only that from Sorceries, is increased, other powerful sources of Magic damage such as the incantation Glintstone Breath and the unique skill Sorcery of the Crozier from the Watchdog's Staff Colossal Weapon benefit greatly from it. 

The buff is unique, meaning it stacks with any other buff used. Additionally, since the buff only matters at the time the damage is inflicted, the damage increase is granted even if the spell, skill, or consumable is used outside of the affected area as long as the caster stands in the sigil when it hits. 

Due to the limited area of effect where the buff is granted it can be difficult to make use of the effect except in ambushes and the starting moments of a fight.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The ground-bound sigil of this is Sorcery is the same as the one created when casting basic Glintstone Sorceries such as Glintstone Pebble and Glintstone Arc. 
This spell's name was Terra Magicus upon release but was changed to Terra Magica at a later date. 
The buffs is applied through what is basically an attack that deals 0 damage, as can be seen if the Golden Epitaph unique skill Last Rites is used in the vicinity of an already created Terra Magica. This is because the unique skill grants a small amount of flat Holy damage which Terra Magica thereafter applies on each attack.

variant.effect: Raises the magic strength of those within the sigil

sections.heading: The Night of Black Knives
sections.body:
During the Golden Age of the Erdtree, a fragment of the Rune of Death was stolen by Lunar Princess Ranni, who used it to forge godslaying Black Knives. These knives were used by the Black Knife Assassins who, one night, entered Leyndell and assassinated Godwyn the Golden. As the assassins fled the capital, an assassin named Tiche was killed protecting her mother Alecto, the leader of the assassins. 

Ranni slew body at the moment of Godwyn's death, causing the Cursemark to break into two half-wheels rather than form a circle. While Ranni died in the flesh, Godwyn's soul alone perished, sentencing him to live in death. His body was interred in the Erdtree's roots beneath Leyndell, where it mutated and warped. Later, the Rune of Death began to spread through the roots in the form of Deathroot, giving rise to Those Who Live in Death.

In preparation for the fallout of the Night of Black Knives, earlier that same night, Ranni met with her elder brother and co-conspirator, Praetor Rykard. She gifted him a slab of rock inscribed with traces of the Rune of Death, which was to serve as a last-resort foil to Maliketh, the Black Blade, in case a battle between Rykard and Maliketh came to pass.

sections.heading: The Shattering of the Elden Ring
sections.body:
The Night of Black Knives became the catalyst for the Shattering. In response to Godwyn's death, Queen Marika the Eternal used her hammer to shatter the Elden Ring. Elden Lord Radagon, her other half, attempted to repair the Elden Ring, but in vain. As punishment for her offense, Marika (alongside Radagon) was imprisoned within the Erdtree.

Consequently, the shattering of the Elden Ring corrupted the Golden Order, and led to a Great War that would leave the Lands Between in ruin.

sections.heading: The Shardbearers
sections.body:
The shards of the Elden Ring, known as Great Runes, were inherited by Marika's Demigod offspring. Tainted by the strength of the Great Runes, the Demigods warred, with the conflict becoming known as the Shattering.

Morgott, a Demigod of the Golden Lineage who was born as a graceless Omen, inherited a Great Rune known as the anchor ring which houses the base, proving his pedigree as a member of the Golden Lineage and as the Lord of Leyndell. Taking on the moniker of the "veiled lord", Morgott ruled over Leyndell, slaughtering countless champions in defence of the Erdtree under the guise of Margit, the Fell Omen.

Praetor Rykard, whose noble ambitions had turned to gluttonous depravity, fed himself to the blasphemous serpent after obtaining his Great Rune. His consort, Tanith, established the recusants of Volcano Manor, waging a war against the Erdtree in his stead.

Godrick, a distant relation of Marika whose blood was sorely diluted, escaped the capital by hiding amongst the womenfolk, bringing with him a multitude of treasures including the Mimic's Veil. He hid from General Radahn in Stormveil Castle, and later insulted Malenia, only to grovel for mercy after he himself was defeated at her hands. He turned to the act of grafting in order to attain power, so that one day he could return to the capital.

General Radahn, famed as the scourge of the stars, led the Redmane Knights during the Shattering. They were met in battle by Malenia, Blade of Miquella, and her undefeated army of Cleanrot Knights. They fought to a standstill, until Malenia unleashed her Scarlet Rot, ending the duel inconclusively. Radahn was driven mad by the rot and was forced to wander the battlefield as a mindless beast, devouring the corpses of those who died during the conflict, whether they be a friend or foe. Malenia, who became comatose, was carried back to the Haligtree of her brother Miquella by Cleanrot Knight Finlay, one of the few survivors of the battle.

Ranni, the instigator of the Night of Black Knives, is said to have cast aside her Great Rune, and its present whereabouts are unknown.

Mohg, known only as the Lord of Blood, began building his dynasty underground in secret. To this end he abducted Miquella from his resting place in the Haligtree, wishing to raise the Empyrean to full godhood and become his consort.However, Miquella never responded to Mohg, no matter how hard the omen tried, and continued to remain asleep in his cocoon.

sections.heading: Conflicts
sections.body:
The First Defense of Leyndell:
 march upon the Royal Capital|232x232px]]

The First Defense of Leyndell was precipitated by the deterioration of a sovereign alliance. Godefroy the Grafted was captured by Ancient Dragon Knight Kristoff during this conflict, earning the latter the honor of Erdtree Burial. The belligerents of said conflict are not confirmed; however, Godefroy's involvement may suggest that the remnants of the Golden Lineage were the attackers.

The Second Defense of Leyndell:

During the Second Defense of Leyndell, Morgott, in the guise of Margit the Fell Omen, slaughtered many heroes in his defense of the Erdtree and engaged in conflict with Radahn. 

Whether Morgott actually defeated Radahn is unclear, as his description as the mightiest hero of the demigods would suggest not. Regardless, while the walls of Leyndell did not fall, Radahn survived, and his forces were repelled. Alongside what were apparently Radahn's forces, soldiers of Godrick and Stormveil Castle also took part in the battle.

The Assault on Volcano Manor:
Said to have been the most appalling battle in the Shattering, the conflict took place on Mt. Gelmir, seemingly between Praetor Rykard's army and the forces of Leyndell. The squalid, the sick, and the blasphemous are said to have participated in this battle, which went on without end. The attackers brought the Jar Cannon to the assault; however, it was discovered that nobody knew how to use it. Most of the soldiers in Leyndell's army eventually became afflicted by Frenzy and seemingly resorted to cannibalism, consuming the bodies of the dead. Rykard's own men deserted him following this conflict, no longer able to abide the consequences of his blasphemy.
Godrick vs Malenia:

Scarcely deserving of being considered a balanced conflict on her journey to face Radahn in the Battle of Aeonia, Malenia and her Cleanrot Knights marched past Stormveil Castle, where Godrick the Grafted and his own forces had been cowering from the Red Lion general. Apparently, Godrick did something to insult Melania, sparking a fight between the pair. Godrick was defeated, and rather than choosing to die in battle, he begged Malenia for mercy. Godrick was spared, and Malenia pressed on to meet Radahn.

The Battle of Aeonia:

The final act of the Shattering was the Battle of Aeonia, a conflict between General Radahn and Malenia, Blade of Miquella. It occured in the area south of Sellia, Town of Sorcery in Caelid, in a region now known as the Swamp of Aeonia. Malenia and her army of Cleanrot Knights marched southward before arriving in Caelid, where they met Radahn's Redmane Knights in battle. The battle ended in a stalemate after Malenia unleashed her scarlet rot, driving the Redmane Knights to defeat. At the same time, their leader was infected with the rot, which drove Radahn into becoming a mindless beast.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.body: Ultimately, none of the Demigods succeeded in becoming Elden Lord, and they were abandoned by the Greater Will. Instead, the guidance of Grace was extended to the Tarnished, who were called to the Lands Between to claim the Great Runes, become Elden Lord, and restore the Golden Order.

sections.heading: ''[[Elden Ring Nightreign|Nightreign]]''
sections.body:
The events of the Shattering in the alternate timeline are likely the same, though the aftermath is entirely different in comparison. In the aftermath of the civil war, a primordial cataclysm known as simply the Night and its harbingers Heolstor and the Nightlords emerged and descended on the Lands Between. As Marika's shattering of the Elden Ring and the Shattering had destroyed order itself, the Night, through the Night's Tide, began plunging the Lands Between into darkness and chaos, drawing forth all manner of monsters and beasts from different realms and eras as perpetual rain threatened to wash away everything. 

As the world was alternated and consumed by the Night, the Golden Order ceased to exist. Queen Marika seemed to have disappeared completely from the Lands Between, as she and the Elden Ring are no longer prayed to, though a few churches remained standing. Meanwhile, the Erdtree itself had vanished entirely from the Lands Between, and its golden, radiant hues are no longer visible. Its disappearance, along with the Grace of Gold, prevented the Tarnished from being beckoned by its call to return. The fate of many of the demigods is unknown, but they presumably died out during the Shattering, while only very few, namely Morgott, Godrick and Mohg, were left alive. In response to the growing darkness, a group of warriors from other lands known as the Nightfarers chose to stay in the Limveld to slay the Nightlords and end the Night.

name: The Tarnished (Protagonist)
description:
The Tarnished is the protagonist and.

Compelled by the "Flame of Ambition", the Tarnished endeavors to brandish the Elden Ring and become Elden Lord. In their journey throughout the Lands Between, they encounter various demigods, bearers of Great Runes, as well as their fellow Tarnished.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
A Tarnished of no renown, called to cross the sea of fog to the Lands Between, having been blessed once more by the Grace once thought lost to their kind. Their origins are unknown, as are their accomplishments prior to their arrival in the Lands Between. 

Game events:

The Tarnished begins their journey in the Chapel of Anticipation, off the western coast of Limgrave, where they find only the corpse of a Finger Maiden slumped against a wall. After a brief encounter with a Grafted Scion, the Tarnished falls from the precipice and washes up in the Stranded Graveyard. Although death seems inevitable, they are found by a mysterious woman riding a spectral steed. The woman grants the Tarnished two flasks: one of crimson tears and the other of cerulean tears. With these blessings, the Tarnished emerges from the damp cavern into the grasslands of Limgrave.

The Tarnished is reunited with the woman once more, and she introduces herself to them as Melina. Seeing that the Tarnished is maidenless, she offers to play the role of a Finger Maiden, allowing the Tarnished to convert the Runes they collect from their enemies into strength. In return, she requests that the Tarnished bring her with them to the foot of the Erdtree. To aid them further, Melina grants the Tarnished a whistle which will allow them to call upon her spectral steed, whose name she reveals to be Torrent. Melina further explains to the Tarnished that she is searching for a purpose given to her by her mother inside the Erdtree long ago, and the reason she lives, despite her burnt and spectral state. She advises the Tarnished to seek the Great Runes: shards of the shattered Elden Ring, currently held by the Demigods.

Early in their shared journey, Melina extends the Tarnished an invitation to Roundtable Hold, the gathering place of Tarnished champions. Here, the Tarnished meets several of their fellow Tarnished, as well as Roundtable Hold's leader, Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing.

The Tarnished claims a Great Rune from one of the Shardbearers scattered throughout the Lands Between, and is permitted audience with the Two Fingers; envoys of the Greater Will, and Finger Reader Enia. Interpreting the words of the Fingers, Enia explains to the Tarnished that the shattering of the Elden Ring has left the land in ruins, and instructs the Tarnished to hunt down the Demigods, who have been renounced by the Greater Will. Gideon offers the Tarnished further advice, imparting his knowledge of the five Shardbearers known to Roundtable Hold.

On their journey, the Tarnished may encounter Ranni the Witch, a Demigod and the perpetrator of the Night of Black Knives. The Tarnished may choose to enter her service, aiding her as she treads the dark path of the Empyrean and attempts to establish her Order upon the world.

After claiming two Great Runes, the Tarnished makes their way to Leyndell, Royal Capital, the home of Morgott the Grace-Given. Melina regains the ability to govern her own movement and bids the Tarnished farewell, leaving them with Torrent and the ability to convert Runes into strength. The Tarnished proceeds to the Elden Throne and defeats Morgott, claiming his Great Rune, but when they attempt to pass through the door in the Erdtree's trunk they find the way obscured by impenetrable thorns. Melina appears before the Tarnished once more, and reveals that it is her purpose to help the Tarnished become Elden Lord. In order to do so, however, the Erdtree must be burned to remove the thorns. And so, the Tarnished begins a new journey with Melina, to the Mountaintops of the Giants, upon which rests the giant's forge, and a flame which may burn the Erdtree.

The Tarnished may encounter a being named Shabriri, who reveals to the Tarnished that Melina must offer herself as kindling so that the Erdtree can burn. Shabriri offers an alternative: the tarnished may take Melina's place as kindling and singe their own flesh instead. To this end, they must descend below the Royal Capital and meet with the Three Fingers, setting themselves upon the path to becoming the Lord of Chaos. Should the Tarnished accept this offer, they will make an enemy of Melina, who vows to hunt them down and kill them if they rise as Lord of Chaos.

Whether through Melina's sacrifice or the power of the Frenzied Flame, the Erdtree is set aflame, and the Tarnished is transported to Crumbling Farum Azula; an ancient temple in the sky said to have been crumbling since time immemorial. In Farum Azula, the Tarnished encounters and kills Maliketh, the Black Blade, releasing the Rune of Death upon the Lands Between. 

The Tarnished returns to Leyndell to find it coated in ash, the Erdtree glowing red above. The Tarnished makes their way through the ruined city, but their path is blocked by Gideon, who attempts to stop them from becoming Elden Lord. The Tarnished kills Gideon, who asserts with his dying breath his belief that a Tarnished cannot become a Lord, for a man cannot kill a god.

The Tarnished once again finds themselves at the Elden Throne. This time they find Godfrey, the First Elden Lord and former leader of the Tarnished. Godfrey reveals that he has come to once more be granted audience with Queen Marika, the goddess of the Lands Between The two Tarnished duel, and Godfrey is forced to tear the beast Serosh from his back and assume the role of Hoarah Loux. Nevertheless, the Tarnished defeats Godfrey and approaches the Erdtree.

Inside the Erdtree, the Tarnished find Marika hanging from a Rune, her body seemingly made of stone. Marika falls from the Rune and her body begins to warp as she assumes the form of Radagon of the Golden Order, the second Elden Lord. Radagon fights to protect the Golden Order from the Tarnished, but is bested. From his body emerges the Elden Beast, a vassal of the Greater Will and embodiment of Order that became the Elden Ring long ago. Despite its status as a god, the Tarnished fells the Elden Beast, and finally stands before the broken body of Queen Marika. Depending on the decisions they made on their journey, the Tarnished may now decide the fate of the Lands Between. They may repair the Elden Ring and rise as Elden Lord, go with Ranni on her thousand year voyage into the chill night, or become the Lord of Frenzied Flame and incinerate all that divides and distinguishes.

name: Theodorix's Magma
description: Theodorix's Magma is an incantation spell in. It is part of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Dragon Communion: Limgrave / Caelid / Jagged Peak
Acquired from the altar at the Church of Dragon Communion in Limgrave, the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid, and the Grand Altar of Dragon Communion on the Jagged Peak for 2 Dragon Hearts after defeating Great Wyrm Theodorix in Consecrated Snowfield.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: Creates a wyrm head to spit a ball of magma that remains on the ground. Can be cast again to immediately spit a second ball.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Damage is boosted by the Roar Medallion and by holding a Dragon Communion Seal in an active hand.
Can be cast midair but cannot be cast while mounted, unlike Magma Breath.
Compared to Magma Breath, this spell deals about 40% more damage but also consumes 50% more FP.
The leftover magma pools last for roughly 6 seconds and deal about 5% of the damage of a direct hit, less early on due to enemy flat defenses.
Pools are useful as traps against agile enemies such as Strays and Fingercreepers by forcing them to stagger a bit.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Patch 1.04 reduced the FP cost from 62 to 46, and Patch 1.07 further reduced it from 46 to 45.

sections.heading: Thiollier's Quest
sections.body:
Quest items:

Questline Progression:
WARNING: Coming too close to the entrance of the Shadow Keep will lock you out of the first step of his quest, and you will miss the Spirit Ash of Ancient Dragon Florissax.

Gravesite Plain
Speak with Moore outside Belurat, Tower Settlement. 
Find and speak with Thiollier at the Pillar Path Cross Site of Grace.
Speak with Moore again and he will give you Black Syrup for Thiollier.
Find Thiollier again and he will give you Thiollier's Concoction.
After all this is done, approach the Shadow Keep, and you will get an ominous message on the screen. Find Thiollier once more, and after exhausting his dialogue, reload the area, and he'll state he is heading south.
Stone Coffin Fissure
Make your way to the southernmost point of the Cerulean Coast, where you'll find a pit. When facing south towards the pit, turn to the right; there are steps leading into it. Follow the given path, and you'll come across the Stone Coffin Fissure. 
Beat the Putrescent Knight, a boss found at the end of this Legacy Dungeon, and in the corner of the arena, you'll find both the Garden of Deep Purple Site of Grace and Thiollier, in front of St. Trina. 
Exhaust Thiollier's Dialogue and then reset the area using the nearby Grace. Return and Thiollier will have new dialogue, exhaust it again, and then imbibe St. Trina's nectar, repeating this step (6 times) until St. Trina speaks to you.
Once that is complete, pass on St. Trina's words to Thiollier, who will be reluctant to believe these words, and choose to try passing on St. Trina's words again and exhaust his dialogue. 
After this, return to the Grace. Here you will immediately be invaded by Thiollier, so defeat him and enter St. Trina's garden. Speak to Thiollier, then imbibe St. Trina's nectar again until she speaks. Here you can tell Thiollier of what she has said and exhaust his dialogue.
Enir-Ilim
Thiollier will now be available to summon for the two final fights of the Shadow of The Erdtrees story, where his quest finishes.

name: Three Fingers
description: The Three Fingers (三本指, Sanbonyubi), also known as the Readerless Fingers, are a character in. As the maddening source of Frenzied Flame Incantations, the burnt Fingers bestow the Frenzied Flame so that a Lord of Frenzied Flame may rise to destroy the world and return the universe to its primal state before the Greater Will fractured the One Great. They only appear during a cutscene triggered when the player opens the charred door at the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: As their name implies, the Three Fingers resemble a disembodied humanoid hand with three finger-like appendages, similar to that of the Greater Will's Two Fingers. However, unlike their counterparts, the Three Fingers are burned and smoldering, as they embody the curse of the Frenzied Flame. They emit a frail light that can be felt at the back of the eyes of those who amass Shabriri Grapes. They sear their fingerprints onto the flesh and eyes of those they grasp.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Long ago, the Three Fingers inscribed their message on the great stone tomb of an ancient god. Shabriri, a blind man, was said to have been the first to contact the Fingers and receive the Frenzied Flame. Others would gain audience with the Three Fingers over the ages, though none possessed the strength required melt it all away as a true Lord of Frenzied Flame.

At some point, the Three Fingers were present in Midra's Manse. Among those they embraced was Sage Midra, whom they chose to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

During the age of the Erdtree, the Three Fingers were summoned beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital by a curse of despair chanted by the deeply unforgiving Great Caravan. The Fingers enthralled them and their nomadic descendants. After the Shattering, Roundtable Knight Vyke met the Three Fingers, but ultimately failed to rise as a Lord of Chaos.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
Three Fingers reside at the very bottom of the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, within the Frenzied Flame Proscription. The area is hidden behind an Illusory Wall located at the back of the Cathedral of the Forsaken, and is sealed until Morgott, the Omen King is defeated. Once there, the door can only be opened if the player removes all equipped Armor. The Three Fingers will be in a small chamber behind the door, appearing during a brief cutscene.

Lord of Frenzied Flame:

Interacting with the Three Fingers causes Melina to leave permanently, vowing to kill the player Tarnished. However, the player can now bypass her sacrifice by using the Fingers' flame as kindling to awaken the Flame of Ruin at the Forge of the Giants and commit the Cardinal Sin. The player can still meet the Three Fingers if they have already used Melina to burn the Erdtree. The Three Fingers do not clasp the player again if they cheat fate by inserting Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Tibia Mariners were skeletal boatsmen who navigated their spectral vessels through ghostly waters with alpine horns that, when blown, summoned and empowered Skeletons. The Tibia Mariners were the first of all grave keepers in the Lands Between, beckoning Those Lost in Death by blowing into their hollow oars. They guided the dead to the Gravesite Plain for an eternity, unbothered by their bones having long since crumbled to dust. Their secrets were inherited by future generations of grave keepers, such as the Servants of Death, who used their skulls as catalysts for summoning wandering spirits. Their boats, or recreations of them, were prominently displayed at the Shadow Keep. The importance of the oarsmen was recognized even amongst the living. 

The Tibia Mariners were suppressed when the Rune of Death was removed from the Elden Ring. In their absence, those without Marika's Grace who met a glorious end in battle were left to wander. The heroes of her Golden Order received Erdtree Burial, and had no need for the archaic ferrymen. When Godwyn the Golden was buried at the base of the Erdtree, he soon transformed into the piscine Prince of Death. The blight leaked from his body and infected the great tree roots, and manifested itself as Deathroot throughout the Lands Between. The Tibia Mariners slowly resurfaced, and Those Who Live in Death answered their call.

Gurranq the Beast Clergyman charges D, Hunter of the Dead, and the Tarnished to hunt down the Tibia Mariners and reap their Deathroot. He believes he can restore the sanctity of the Golden Order by absorbing the residual fragments of Destined Death.

Charo's Hidden Grave=
Charo's Hidden Grave:

If pushed further, he eventually retreats behind a large aggregation of gravestones where several strong skeletons await his call.

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.body:
While the Tibia Mariners themselves, curiously enough, are not counted as among Those Who Live in Death, their minions are, and the usage of specialized anti-undead equipment will make it easier to isolate the mariner.
In terms of combat ability, these enemies are pretty weak on their own, especially against ranged attacks. Their main threat comes from the allies they summon and the fact that they typically operate in large combat areas, periodically teleporting to different positions.
Given that they all fight among ruins, it can be challenging to locate them after they teleport, and the constant stream of summoned allies can become overwhelming. To counter this, your primary tactic should be to ignore the summoned allies entirely. Instead, use Torrent whenever possible to quickly locate the mariner, then hit them hard and fast before his friends have a chance to regroup.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
The seated Tibia Mariner uses an alphorn to paddle his incorporeal rowboat across ethereal, violet waters. His body is skeletonized, save for the wizened beard that clings to his slack mandible. A floral pattern decorates the white-laced chapel veil that rests upon his head and drapes over his bony frame. Attached to the veil are wide, golden hoops, each adorned with three large golden flower emblems inlaid with rubies. The mariner's forearms are wrapped in cloth, and several gold bracelets hang from his wrists. He wears the tattered remains of robes sewn from purple thread.

The mariner's transparent wooden rowboat shimmers with a faint purple hue. A chair is built into its deck, with a semi-circle cut into the backrest to create a depression at the top. Spiral patterns ascend its stile and backpost before transitioning into straight lines beaming upward. The backpost extends several feet higher than the chair and terminates in an upward concave arch reminiscent of Marika's Rune. Hanging ventrally from it is a small lantern alight with a purple ghostflame. The boat's exterior hull is highly decorated with intricate relief carvings. Two adjacent floral embellishments are encircled by spiral-containing rings and bound together with a sturdy knot. The gunwale trim above features a wavelength weaving over and under stars, possibly symbolic of the Primeval Current.

The mariner will sometimes whip up a grand torrent of water that carries his boat high into the air. When it reaches it apex, he extends his arm, and a bright red light emanates from a jewel in his palm. This light is said to beckon the lost spirits of those slain in battle.

The dry and metallic moans of the mariner eerily echo upon themselves as if uttered from deep within a dungeon. When he sounds his lengthy brass horn, a single clang of metal deeply reverberates like a tolling bell. When cast, his ancient Death magic produces a haunting noise, akin to the crashing of cymbals.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Soundtrack: Death's Kindred
The enemies summoned by Mariners vary by location. Some call Giant Skeletons or Royal Revenants, while others only field assorted Skeletons.
Their movement was not restricted to water when they appeared in the Lands Between.
They appear to be leaders among Those Who Live in Death, and each one carries Deathroot.
Only one non-boss Tibia Mariner can be encountered. They are in the Mountaintops of the Giants, north-west of the Snow Valley Ruins Overlook Site of Grace.
The Tibia Mariners lack of Holy damage vulnerability may be attributed to being part spirit.
In, the Tibia Mariner will appear at the end of a day, leading a large group of Those Who Live in Death.
Mariners are grave keepers who ferry lost souls across a sea in the spirit world.
The detailing on the external hull of the mariners' boats may be interpreted as an infinity symbol (∞) representative of an endless cycle of life and death.
Tibia's boats appear at the Shadow Keep. Each is a funeral pyre carrying a Messmer's Army standard, representative of Tibia ferrying the unsung heroes of Messmer's crusade.
The ancient mariners themselves were laid to rest amongst the crimson fields of Charo's Hidden Grave.
Tibia Mariner remain seated as if immovable like an Elder Albinauric or the giant maidens perched upon Eternal City chair-crypt.
The tibia also known as the shinbone or shankbone, is the larger, stronger, and anterior (frontal) of the two bones in the leg below the knee. The first generation of Albinaurics lost the use of their tibias, and are unable to walk on their own.
Some of the red Second-Generation Albinaurics at the Mohgwyn Palace blow into wooden clubs like horns to summon the mariners' Giant Skeleton.
The massive figures seated in the Chair-Crypts of the Eternal Cities vaguely resemble the Tibia Mariners. However, upon closer inspection, their outfits and chairs are quite different.
The Putrescent Knight also suffers this affliction.
It is unclear whether the Tibia Mariners played a role in delivering the Stone coffins now beached on the Cerulean Coast.
Usher of Death, Rosus fills a similar role, guiding the dead toward the catacombs and Erdtree Burial.
Crescent Moons are carved into the side of the boat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal Name: NightKingKenzoku, 夜の王の眷属 (Yoru no Ou no Kenzoku, lit. Lord of Night's Kin) The specific word "Kenzoku" isn't limited to someone who is related by blood, as it also includes those with similar goals, which is consistent with how "kindred" is used in-game.
The Tibia Mariners are psychopomps who deeply resemble Charon, the ferryman of the dead, and the titular character from The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.
The spectral boats piloted by the mariners are literal "ghost ships."

sections.heading: Strategy Guide Description
sections.body:
{| class = " mw-collapsible mw-collapsed article-table" style= " width:100%"!Elden Ring Official Strategy Guide Vol 2 - Shards of the Shattering
|-
| While they may perhaps appear as ferrymen for the souls of the dead, Tibia Mariners are not responsible for bringing those who have perished into the afterlife, but instead call upon Those Who Live in Death to slay the living and add them to their ranks. Tibia Mariners are generally encountered as Bosses, and can always be found in the overworld. meaning they can all be fought on foot or on horseback. Like necromancers, these enemies don't rely on their own offensive capabilities to battle their foes, but instead will raise nearby skeletons or summon skeletal giants to do their bidding. As such, Tibia Mariners can always be found in ruins and graveyards where Those Who Live in Death are abundant.

sections.heading: Preparation
sections.body: Tibia Mariners are always encountered in the overworld, in a variety of environments that are usually somewhat cluttered with ruins and gravestones, but are open enough for the terrain to not be much of a concern. Their attacks are fairly easy to evade, but if you prefer to rely on blocking, a 100% Physical damage negation shield is recommended. It can also be useful to have armor or a shield with good Magic damage negation for the few Magic damage attacks that the various skeletal minions may use against you. Weapons and spells with Strike and or Holy damage are very potent against Tibia Mariners, as well as the skeletons that can be found with them. Similarly, Holy Water Pots and Sacred Order Pots work well in fights with these enemies.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body:
Due to their generally slow speed, mobility shouldn't be much of an issue for you unless you get overwhelmed by the other enemies the Mariners summon to aid them. This means that fighting on foot or on horseback are both relatively easy approaches for fighting Tibia Mariners. For melee users, you can use hit and run tactics with the horse by riding up to the Mariner and using a charged Strong attack before running away and looping back to repeat the process. Alternatively, when on foot it's rather easy to run straight up to the Mariner and pummel them repeatedly with attacks, and simply back away when they begin to do an attack, or if you get crowded by other enemies. For spell and ranged combat users, the same principals apply, though it's generally easier to hurl spells at Tibia Mariners on horseback, while running around to evade anything they or their minions can throw at you, unless you're using spells with a very limited or melee range.

In terms of the enemies they have with them, the majority of skeletons will have melee weapons and can easily be taken down or evaded, and will often get hit by the Mariner's own attacks. The ones you'll need to be more mindful of are the Skeletal Militiamen with crossbows, the Skeletal Grave Wardens that cast Magic damage dealing homing skulls and the Giant Skeleton summons. The Giant Skeletons are summoned temporarily for individual attacks, specifically by the Tibia Mariner Boss found in the Wyndham Ruins in Altus Plateau, and the Strong enemy version found in the Mountaintops of the Giants. These skeletons are more easily evaded while on horseback, or simply by rolling under or behind them. While their slam attacks can be deadly, you'll need to watch out for their devastating beam attack, which they'll only use when you're a good distance away.

Holy Water Pots are a great tool for dispatching Mariners, regardless of your build and Faith.

sections.heading: Abilities

Besides allowing a player to get around relatively quickly, Torrent also doesn't appear to take fall damage from certain heights. This allows one to easily jump down from heights that'd normally kill the player as long as they're mounted on Torrent. That said, Torrent isn't immune to dying from jumping from too high of a height: even if a double jump is used to get to a lower level, if the starting point is too high up, Torrent will dissipate on landing and the player will die from the impact. 

Jumping again while in mid-air will cause Torrent to perform a second jump. This can only be done once until he touches the ground again and can be used to change direction at the moment of the second jump. 

Players can also fight from horseback against enemies, such as shooting arrows or casting spells. However, only one of the player's weapons can be used at a time as the left hand is constantly occupied holding Torrent's reigns, it is still possible to switch between the right-hand and left-hand armament while riding by using the same input the player uses to two-hand their weapons. 

Note that it is not possible to change from wielding a weapon one-handed to two-handed while mounted. It is however possible to get the bonuses of two-handing by performing the action before mounting up.

Spirit springs can be used by jumping while riding Torrent to reach higher altitudes. Landing on or close to a spirit spring will completely negate fall damage.

Torrent's HP can be restored by consuming Rowa Raisins, Sweet Raisins and Frozen Raisins. Using a Flask of Crimson Tears will also restore his health on top of the player's own, however only while the player is riding him. If Torrent is killed, using the Spectral Steed Whistle will bring up a prompt to expend a single charge of the Flask of Crimson Tears to revive him.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body: Torrent cannot be summoned in Dungeons, Legacy Dungeons, and the Abyssal Woods, or during online multiplayer sessions.

name: Traitorous Straghess
description: Traitorous Straghess, also known as the Dreglord, is one of the Nightlord bosses included in the expansion for. When its health is depleted, it gains a second health bar by transforming into Pure Impulse Straghess.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Traitorous Dreglord Straghess is a large, staff-wielding humanoid boss formed from discarded corpses. The fight opens with slow, clearly telegraphed attacks, allowing consistent windows for evasion and counterattacks. At roughly 50% health, Straghess enters its second phase. It begins using attacks and spells that inflict Scarlet Rot and control space or block movement, sharply increasing the difficulty. Straghess also summons Putrid Corpses and Rotmounds that impede and trap the players.

Upon depletion of its health bar, Traitorous Straghess gains a second health bar and transforms into Pure Impulse Straghess, initiating the third and most demanding phase. Still applying Scarlet Rot, it becomes a markedly agile and erratic melee attacker, punishing players who overextend or fail to adjust to the faster tempo. Pure Impulse Straghess frequently disengages before re-entering with high-speed lunges and unrelenting attack combos, making sustained pressure difficult to maintain. It enters the fourth phase at approximately half health, at which point it summons pillars of flesh throughout the arena. These obstructions conceal its approach and allow it to trigger a wide explosive attack, forcing players to track its position while remaining constantly mobile.<!--

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Possessed of great strength and abundant Grace, Queen Marika's mounted Tree Sentinels met little resistance as they charged down her enemies. Heavily-equipped and blessed with old Erdtree incantations, very few were permitted to join their nigh unbreakable ranks. They were resolute in their commitment toward protecting that which deserved protection, becoming the gold standard to which all defenders of the Erdtree measured themselves. Their gallantry influenced the practices of the Leyndell Knights, who similarly put the shield before the sword.

After the Ancient Dragon Gransax attacked Leyndell, some of the Tree Sentinels adopted characteristics of the Ancient Dragons. These knights became Draconic Tree Sentinels to better protect the Erdtree.

A few Tree Sentinels embarked on Messmer's crusade, later safeguarding the path to the Shaman Village, Queen Marika's former home.

King Morgott distributed special, invisibility-revealing torches to the Tree Sentinels following his rise to power, hoping to prevent a second Night of Black Knives.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: An imposingly sturdy knight chained to the saddle of a large horse. The Tree Sentinel wears golden filigreed plate with intricate vine and floral motifs, inlaid with crimson and viridian jewels, and a dark ochre cape depicting a sacred tree. Their helm features red false eyeslits and a small, decorative tree with yellow-green growth in place of a plume. The knight carries a massive golden halberd imbued with Holy energy. Their steed is covered head-to-hoof in barding of golden plate over layered black armor. Its ornate chamfron (faceplate) has vented blinkers and a spiral unicorn horn embellishment.

sections.heading: Variants
sections.body:
Shield: A Tree Sentinel who wields a Golden Halberd and an Erdtree Greatshield. The shield allows them to dispel oncoming sorceries, countering with a golden beam that deals Holy damage.
Torch: A Tree Sentinel who wields a Golden Halberd and Sentry's Torch that deals Fire damage on hit. They always appear alongside the Shield variant.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
Altus Plateau, two guard the main road to the Capital Outskirts. Drops Erdtree Greatshield and [[Hero's Rune 1|Hero's Rune [1]]].
Limgrave, one patrols near the Church of Elleh and Fringefolk Hero's Grave. Drops Golden Halberd.
Scaduview, two patrolling the Hinterland near the Shaman Village. They each drop one Blessing of Marika.

A duo of Tree Sentinels found in the Hinterlands of Scaduview, guarding the path to the Minor Erdtree incantation.

name: Trees
description: This page lists Trees in,, and.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Trees held deep symbolic and spiritual importance to the people of the Lands Between and the Realm of Shadow, particularly to groups like the Woodfolk. The greatest of these trees were suffused with profound holiness, bestowing sacred blessings in the form of soaring grace, Golden Dew, and blessed sap, which dripped from their boughs and hardened into Crystal Tears and treasured amber. These great trees typically grew from potent sources of life energy. For example, Queen Marika used the Crucible to create her Erdtree, and Miquella watered the doomed Haligtree with his divine Empyrean blood. Certain trees manifested stylized avatars to protect themselves and their offspring in times of need. The Erdtree could rebirth or renew its followers through esoteric death rites like Erdtree Burial.

Some individuals gained the power of trees by channeling aspects of the Crucible or by entering pacts with great trees. For example, the Tree Guardians received eternal life to defend the Erdtree and its offspring; the end of their service was said to approach when their buds bloom into blood-red flowers, beginning their slow transformation into trees.

However, the all-female, blind shamans—spirited-away denizens of another world—and their descendants, the Numen, inherently possessed the greatest arboreal affinity in all the Lands Between. Their founding Grandmother formed a small yet significant tree at the Shaman Village, Marika's home, long ago. The flesh of shamans was later prized for its ability to graft and meld harmoniously with that of others. Many maidens were dismembered to create jar saints, while others bulged from inside trees around Enir-Ilim.

Feminine forms likewise manifested in other trees related to Marika or her people, including the motherly womb at the Haligtree Roots and the praying maiden bound by a Cord End inside a blossom sealed within Limveld's secret cave. Just as dried prunings from the Erdtree were snapped in lieu of death, the Cutting-Gifted Tribe atoned for learning the original sin by offering up their young maidens to become Sacrificial Twigs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Many trees on the Mountaintops of the Giants have become spirits.
The bodies and souls of warriors who receive Erdtree Burial are absorbed by the Erdtree. Art in the catacombs suggests this practice causes new or reborn life to later sprout from the Erdtree.
There is a unique "root tree" in the courtyard of the Shadow Keep, Church District.
Bleached willow trees are commonly found throughout the realm of shadow, especially in areas associated with the hornsent.
Birch trees, such as those found in Altus Plateau, can regrow their bark once peeled off. The Secret Rite Scroll, which details the Gate of Divinity's workings, was recorded on birch bark.
Fallen red oak and maple leaves blanket the land at Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree and the Scadutree Chalice.
Fallen oak leaves litter the Deeproot Depths, especially around the hollowed-out tree guarded by Crucible Knight Siluria.
The Cutting-Gifted Tribe converted their maidens to Sacrificial Twigs to atone for learning the Erdtree's Original Sin. The bound figure in Limveld's secret room is possibly connected to the divine Spirit Shelter.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Loot: Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree
Found in a treasure chest in a room locked by an Imp Statue located at the lower level near the Prayer Room Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Throws out 3 wide rings of light in a 90-degree arc that has Holy Attack Power equal to 155% of Incantation Scaling and pierces through enemies, stopping upon hitting an object. They still cause damage when stopped and return to the caster 2 seconds after stopping, having the same amount of Attack Power on the returning hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast. 
Deals 3 Stance damage per hit, for up to 9 Stance damage if all hits land. 
Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%. 
Effectively has Attack Power equal to 310% of Incantation Scaling per ring since it will very often hit the main target on the way back.
Can potentially hit with Attack Power equal to 465% of Incantation Scaling if the target is also standing at the incantation's maximum range or at a hit object (or hit ground).
Note that the rings share hit registration, meaning an enemy can only be hit up to 3 times: once when the ring is thrown out, a second time when it's stopped, and a third possible hit when the rings return. 
Several rings can be out at the same time, making the spell very spammable.
If casting the spell sequentially, the first set of rings will start to return as the second set is being thrown out. 
Pairs decently well with the Erdtree Greatshield's skill Golden Retaliation and the Ash of War: Carian Retaliation since the timing of the returning ring is very predictable and will trigger the spell-parry-into-projectile part of those skills.
The caster takes a short step forwards each time the spell is cast. While many steep falls prevent a character from stepping over them from movement caused by Skills, Spells, and Weapons, it's still good to be a bit careful.
Though it goes through all enemies, it will not ignore the damage reduction from an enemy that is keeping its guard up if they are guarding in the direction it's flying from.
Note that it will still fly through said guarding enemy and will hit their unprotected back when returning unless said enemy turns around in between the two hits.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 increased casting speed.
Patch 1.04 increased damage.
Attack Power was increased from 134% of Incantation Scaling to 155% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: Prevents the loss of Runes upon death for 3 minutes (except for deaths caused by Death Blight).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Like the Sacrificial Twigs, since it prevents you from dropping a Bloodstain with your runes upon death it will also prevent it from replacing your previous one and therefore gives you another chance to grab it.
This is especially useful around large drops since it makes the consequences around fall damage deaths much smaller. 
Especially useful for jumping puzzles, such as the one that is found as a side path at the start of Raya Lucaria Crystal Tunnel and the one that covers almost the entirety of Frenzied Flame Proscription at the bottom of Subterranean Shunning-Grounds. This is of course presuming you are carrying a worthwhile amount of runes. 
Keep in mind the time limit, as while 3 minutes is a fair amount of time it's still a limited amount of time and it may run out at the worst of times in an area.
Usually best saved for a run through or fight against dangerous enemies, or just before starting a section with falls.
Can be used to transport out a bunch of Runes stuck inside of a boss room, especially when combined with quitting out to the main menu to reset the character to just outside of the boss room's fog wall.

name: Twinbird
description: The twinbird was an unseen character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The twinbird once made its nest in the Lands Between, long before the Erdtree grew. The twinbird's offspring were the deathbirds who burned all manner of Death in their ghostflame kilns. Vengeful spirits were released by the ancient death hex as the deathbirds raked the smoldering ashes with barbed bone pokers. Even the putrescent sludge interred within the monolithic stone coffins received these final rites.

The servants of Death venerated the violent Deathbirds as evil deities, symbolically invoking them during sacrificial rituals. Meaningful death was valued, as those who faced death with valor were granted a glorious end. Other worshippers preserved their lives in hopes of making a greater sacrifice in the future. 

Over time, the influence of the twinbird waned. Some priests pledged their spears to protect the Deathbirds, entering the rite of Death in exchange for a promised, distant resurrection. Later, Gravebird golems were created in the Deathbirds' likeness to guard the spiritgraves on the Gravesite Plain. Although a few hexes continued to be practiced in the tower of Enir-Ilim, the importance of the ghostflame diminished, and its secrets were eventually forgotten.

When the Prince of Death spread his Deathroot through the roots of the Greattree, the Golden Order collapsed. Soon, the Deathbirds returned to the world as Those Who Live in Death. A few were rumored to descend from above under the cover of night in places where crumbled ruins have fallen from the temple in the sky.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The twinbird is believed to persist in some form or capacity.
Some speculate that the two-headed bird relief in Crumbling Farum Azula depicts the twinbird.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The twinbird bears a striking resemblance to the imperial banner of the Holy Roman Empire (800–1806 C.E.).
Due to its clear associations with fire and life after death, the twinbird is often thought to resemble a phoenix.
The twinbird embodies the concept of duality, a theme echoed in the contrasting flower fields of the Cerulean Coast and Charo's Hidden Grave, as well as in the lights of Rosus and Tibia Mariner, among other places.
Similar to Marika and Miquella, the twinbird may qualify as a Rebis.
The twinbird on the blue side of the shield is bright and warm. Its twin appears as a black bird against a red sky. These twinbirds may be symbolic of the sun before and during a solar eclipse. Additionally, the Deathbirds are described as having black feathers.

name: Two Fingers
description: The Two Fingers are a set of NPC characters in. Seven pairs of Two Fingers can be found throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: The Two Fingers are a large, hand-like creature with a slight indentation in its palm and twinned phalange-like appendages, hence their name. When standing upright, these fingers resemble heads with long and wispy white hair. Bowed with age, the Two Fingers are in a state of decay, with exposed flesh and lesions covering their ancient bodies.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Two Fingers are the children of Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and serve the Lands Between as divine envoys of the Greater Will. They are responsible for selecting Empyreans, granting them shadowbound beasts, and guiding them toward godhood and inheriting the Elden Ring. They are the source of the Baleful Shadows and all Two Fingers incantations and possess the ability to restore blessings to Great Runes atop the ancient Divine Towers. They communicate in a cipher-like language of light composed of intangible symbols that hang in the air, which are perceived and translated by attending Finger Readers. In the past, the Fingers were masters of oration, their wisdom attracting champions from far and wide, establishing missionary churches in foreign realms beyond the Sea of Fog. However, their guidance became skewed long, long ago when their mother was damaged and consequently lost direct contact with the Greater Will.

In a prior age, a pair of Two Fingers deemed Marika an Empyrean and granted her Gurranq, Beast Clergyman. Under their guidance, she wove the Erdtree into existence from a Golden Seed and the primordial Crucible of life. They also selected Ranni, Malenia, Miquella, and the Gloam-Eyed Queen to be gods of the new age. After no clear victor emerged from the Shattering War, the Two Fingers abandoned the Demigods. Their favor was instead granted to the Tarnished, to whom the Grace of Gold had returned, issuing their instructions from the Roundtable Hold. Though most Tarnished follow their teachings, others doubt their judgment and have lost faith. They believe the Two Fingers to be corrupt and senile, having been broken along with the Erdtree long ago. The Two Fingers grant Darkness to confessors who hunt down these enemies.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.body:
The first pair of Two Fingers can be found in Roundtable Hold, behind a set of doors that remain closed until the player Tarnished acquires their first Great Rune. They will be at the back of the chamber with Finger Reader Enia sitting close by. Five are found atop Divine Towers; however, each is dormant and lifeless. The seventh chose Ranni the Witch, and is concealed beneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes. She slays it with the Fingerslayer Blade during her questline to fully free herself from its control.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The Two Fingers can only be harmed by the Fingerslayer Blade when wielded by someone destined with that fate. The Two Fingers cannot be attacked or killed through any means during normal gameplay.
The individuals known to have been named Empyrean by the Two Fingers include Malenia, Miquella, Ranni, the Gloam-Eyed Queen, and Queen Marika herself.
Many characters distrust the Two Fingers:
Count Ymir believes that the Fingers are themselves flawed, that the instructions they give do not come from the Greater Will but instead from the Fingers' belief in what the Greater Will says.
Patches ridicules the Fingers.
Sir Gideon Ofnir, the All-Knowing believes the purpose for the Two Fingers was lost long ago.
White Mask Varré views the Two Fingers in a poor light, believing they had fallen into madness and lost their purpose after the Greater Will abandoned the Lands Between.
Tanith, Volcano Manor Proprietress considers them dogmatic, and their favor burdensome.
Their cipher inscriptions could be fashioned into weapons such as the Cipher Pata and the Coded Sword.
In a bid to become Fingers themselves, finger-weavers harvested and consumed hallucinogenic Finger Mimic mushrooms, which they called the "stillborn of the Two Fingers."

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: The Two Fingers are each a literal Finger of God.

name: Unalloyed Gold
description:
Unalloyed Gold is a type of metal in. It was produced and employed by the demigod and empyrean, Miquella, the Unalloyed.

After observing that Golden Order Fundamentalism could not alleviate his sister's sickness, Miquella began pursuing other means of treating her condition. One of these pursuits leading to the creation of Unalloyed Gold, a substance that Miquella would make into a primary design element in the equipment of his army and closest companions.

Repeatedly used as a medium to compel affection and raise faith, one of the primary inventions that enforced the pursuit of this metal were the many prototypes of Miquella's Needle. An artifact that when inserted into ones flesh, had the ability to ward away the meddling of the outer gods. However, even the latest and most advanced model of these needles are still considered incomplete, and could only accomplish this fully if inserted into the flesh while standing in a location that has been untouched by time, the only currently known location being the heart of the storm found in Farum Azula.

name: Urgent Heal
description: Urgent Heal is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Two Fingers incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Equipped:
Urgent Heal is a starting spell for the Confessor origin.

Purchase: Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
Urgent Heal is sold for 1,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn.
Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation from him, the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price, after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body: The caster bows in prayer, healing HP equal to 115% of their Faith-based Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 16 FP per cast.
Costs 30 Stamina per cast.
Requires 1 Memory Slot to be equipped.
Restores HP equal to 7.19% of Incantation Scaling for each FP spent.
The caster can walk slowly while casting, though the overall duration matches that of other direct healing incantations.

Strategies:
Urgent Heal is the weakest direct healing incantation and is generally outclassed by Heal, which restores twice as much HP for nearly the same cost and provides additional benefits.
Although it only requires 8 Faith, most seals have a minimum requirement of 10 Faith, making 10 the practical threshold for most playthroughs.
While the Frenzied Flame Seal has no attribute requirement, its healing output is reduced due to its scaling being split across multiple attributes.
This spell synergizes well with Bestial Vitality, a health regeneration spell.
It may help reduce FP wasted on overhealing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Urgent Heal is tied with Heal for the lowest healing effectiveness per FP spent.
It is the only health restoration spell that does not heal nearby allies
One of two healing incantations that do not damage Revenants and Revenant Followers.
