name: Usher of Death, Rosus
description: is an unseen character mentioned in. Rosus Statues are two sets of interactable objects that emit Rosus' Light.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
Bowed with age, Rosus is a long-necked, near-skeletal humanoid with a pronounced hunchback and stooped posture. A stoic frown forms on his eyeless face, which is striated like tree bark, and a row of dead twig-like horns grows from his forehead in a regal manner reminiscent of a crown. His hands feature five clawed fingers, but his feet bear only four digits, including a dewclaw. He wears a robe with drooping sleeves and a pin that resembles an eight-spoked wheel.

Statues of Rosus around in the overworld hold a small dish with a black candle in their right hands that, when ignited, produces a trail of blue light not unlike the golden Guidance of Grace. Rosus statues found in Hero's Grave dungeons lack the candle and instead hold a scepter-like torch with both hands that can project a gold Erdtree Burial spell sigil onto the ground by shining light.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body: Rosus was the Usher of Death, a psychopomp who guided Those Lost in Death back to the roots for Erdtree Burial. Statues in his likeness appeared across the entire Lands Between, revealing the path to the catacombs with a trail of spectral light. However, it is unclear whether Rosus was a real character or a personification used for religious iconography.

sections.heading: Rosus Statues
sections.body:
Rosus Candle Statues:

Rosus Statues in the overworld display a message and create an arrow-like trail of blue Rosus Light when activated, ushering the player towards the entrance of a nearby catacombs. If the location is undiscovered, marker icons for the Rosus Statue and its Rosus Light appear on the Lands Between map.

Rosus Scepter Statues:

A limited number of Hero's Graves contain "shades"—shadowy enemies that are invulnerable until they are given form by Rosus's gold Light, which projects golden Erdtree Burial sigils onto the ground. Several of the statues must be located and activated before they can shine their light from their scepters.

Statues of Rosus with scepters that emit gold light can be found in the following Hero's Graves:

Auriza Hero's Grave
Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave
Sainted Hero's Grave

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Rosus' Axe is locked behind an Imp Seal in the Black Knife Catacombs. Its unique Skill, Rosus's Summons, is a variant of Tibia's Summons, which also manifests Those Lost in Death.
Rosus cranes his neck like Deathbirds and Gravebirds.
Rosus serves a role similar to those of Tibia Mariners and lamplight.
Rosus Statues with blue light have a similar gameplay function as the spectral Candletrees that lead the player to Caves and other points of interest.
Disabled Rosus Candle Statues litter the ground near the entrances to Darklight Catacombs, Fog Rift Catacombs, and Scorpion River Catacombs in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: Rosus is a Latin word, the perfect passive participle of rōdō (“gnaw, eat away.”). An appropriate English translation would be one who has been eaten away.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body: A pair of Valiant Gargoyles encountered at the Siofra Aqueduct in Siofra River. One wields a Greatsword and Halberd, whilst the other wields a Great Axe and Twinblade. The latter emerges from the waterfall when the former falls below half its health. They are unable to perform Beast's Roar, instead coughing out a poisonous mist from their bodies.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: The Valiant Gargoyle duo is found at the Siofra Aqueduct, located east of Nokron, Eternal City and the Ancestral Woods. They protect one of two entrances to Deeproot Depths.

sections.body: Moveset:

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.body:
Since the second one only drops in from the cliffs above once the second gets low on health, it is best to draw the first Gargoyle to the entrance so that it takes a few seconds longer for them to gang up on you. 

The poison breath is very hard to see and also quickly causes Physical damage, but it only affects a conal area in front of the gargoyle, so it can be avoided by quickly heading behind it, running away a bit if close enough. 

The Putrid Corpse Ashes are very useful for this fight, as even upgraded to just +4, they will keep the attention of the second gargoyle, provided that they are summoned around at around 60% health of the first gargoyle. They are quite tanky, draw aggro very well, and will be summoned at the summoning monument instead of at your side, meaning they will be in the perfect spot to distract #2. 

Be wary that the summoning zone doesn't quite cover the entire arena, and as such, standing too close to the entrance of the arena may cause any summoned Ashes to disappear.

image: ER Icon Weapon Velvet Sword of St. Trina.png
description: Velvet Sword of St. Trina is a melee armament and straight sword in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: From the Fissure Cross Site of Grace in Cerulean Coast, head north and drop down two stone platforms to a cliff lower down. Inside a Putrescent Rotmound-infested cave to the south is the sword, furthest in.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with Somber Smithing Stones. 
Cannot have its Affinity and Skill changed. 
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
The skill, Mists of Eternal Sleep, has two parts. The first is a fine, purple mist that inflicts 112 Eternal Sleep build-up per second for two seconds, that is also paired with a swing of the weapon. The second is a Weapon Buff that increases the sword's innate Eternal Sleep build-up by 15 for 30 seconds. 
Since both of these parts happen simultaneously, hitting both the sword and the mist on an enemy immediately causes 169 Eternal Sleep build-up. 
Similar damage and scaling as the Sword of St. Trina, and since they both inflict Sleep buildup, they pair quite well together for dual-wielding. 
Scales best with Dexterity, but unlike with the Sword of St. Trina the Strength- and Intelligence-scaling isn't far behind, and its base Magic damage is far greater. This means that the sword deals roughly equal amounts of damage on a hybrid Strength/Dexterity build, a pure Dexterity build, and a hybrid Dexterity/Intelligence build. 
For comparison (unmentioned stats are at the minimum required level): 45 Strength and 45 Dexterity grants 534 AP, 80 Dexterity grants 534 AP, and 45 Dexterity and 45 Intelligence grants 522 AP.
The hilt features a St. Trina carving.

name: Volcano Manor
image: ER Volcano Manor Guest Hall Roof Panorama.png
description: The Volcano Manor (火山館, Kazan-kan) is a subregion in. It is a legacy dungeon located on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.body:
The Volcano Manor is one of the game's most complex locations. It can be reached in multiple ways and you can progress through from different directions.

The fastest, but most gimmicky way to reach it is by letting the Abductor Virgin at the bottom of the Raya Lucaria Academy grapple you to death. You will still drop your runes, but be respawned right within the Volcano Manor area. From here there are two paths that are each a point of no return. One leading to the rest of the manor, the other brings you to the Abductor Virgin duo bossfight and back to the Altus Plateau. For the Abductor Virgin boss, search for the cave with multiple drop-down platforms. To progress deeper into the manor, jump down the lava waterfall. If you die here before reaching a grace, you will be respawned where the Abductor Virgin dropped you within Volcano Manor. From here you can explore the area, defeat the Godskin Noble and either make it back to the manor entrance with Lady Tanith and the other npcs, or skip their quests and head straight to the gateway portal leading to Praetor Rykard.

The regular paths to enter the manor are either on foot/horseback across Mt. Gelmir, or to be teleported right to the Volcano Manor entrance grace by Rya once reaching the Altus Plateau. You won't be able to reach the bosses or explore the rest of the area from here unless you accept Lady Tanith's offer to get the Drawing-Room Key. If you join the manor, a list of NPCs become available there: Bernahl, Patches, Rya, Diallos Hoslow. To get all the content out of the manor, you have to wait with fighting Rykard until reaching the Mountaintops of the Giants, so that you can do all of the following NPC invasions for the manor: Old Knight Istvan, Rileigh the Idle, Great Horned Tragoth, Vargram the Raging Wolf + Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood. After defeating Juno Hoslow, Tanith offers to send you to Rykard, where you can then start the boss fight. Remember to complete Rya's quest before defeating Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood, otherwise you'll be locked out of Tanith's dialogue regarding Rya.

name: Vyke
description: Vyke the Dragonspear, also known as Roundtable Knight Vyke and Festering Fingerprint Vyke, is a character in. He acts as an Invader and a Boss.

sections.heading: Encounters
sections.body:
Festering Fingerprint Vyke (Invader)=
Festering Fingerprint Vyke  (Invader):

A dark spirit who invades in Liurnia of the Lakes, on the path leading to the Church of Inhibition.

Vyke will use Vyke's War Spear along with several Frenzy Flame spells. Like other humanoid invaders, he will heal with a Flask of Crimson Tears if needed.

Roundtable Knight Vyke (Boss)=
Roundtable Knight Vyke  (Boss):

This mini-boss version is found at the Mountaintops of the Giants in the Lord Contender's Evergaol, close to the First Church of Marika (just west of it) on a hill that you can jump up to.

Uses Ancient Dragon Incantations, has a Flask of Crimson Tears, and uses a unique jump attack with his spear. His movements are usually slow and easy to predict, although his abilities can easily kill anyone with low lightning protection. Unlike his Festering Fingerprint form, Vyke does not use any Frenzy abilities during this fight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Vyke has no dialogue.
Finger Reader Enia mentions that "Only once before [has she] seen two Great Runes together". This is probably a reference to Vyke, since he is the only one who ever got close to be Elden Lord. Nevertheless, not any other details are given about the situation and Vyke isn't ever mentioned anywhere as having had runes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Vyke is the mascot for Elden Ring. He appears prominently on the box art and in marketing materials.
The maiden corpse at the Church of Inhibition is identical to the the character named [133600 Vyke's Finger Maiden] in the game's files.
Roundtable Knight Vyke was an NPC in an earlier build of Elden Ring. He was introduced at Stormveil Castle, where he was a possible Cooperator against Godrick the Grafted. His questline intersected with those of Gatekeeper Gostoc and Redeemer Guilbert.
Unused audio files within the game warn the player about a knight with melted armor; most probably Vyke.

name: Vyke's Dragonbolt
description: Vyke's Dragonbolt is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Guaranteed Drop: Mountaintops of the Giants
Vyke's Dragonbolt is acquired from the defeat of Roundtable Knight Vyke in the Lord Contender's Evergaol.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
A bolt of red lightning strikes down on the caster's weapon, granting them a Weapon Buff that gives Lightning Attack Power equal to 75% of Faith-based Incantation Scaling and a Body Buff that increases maximum Equip Load by 15% but lowers Lightning Damage Negation. 

Both buffs last for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast. 
The Weapon Buff and the Body Buff are separate effects, meaning that the Body Buff remains active if the Weapon Buff is deactivated and vice versa. 
The effective change to current Equip Load depends on how high the Equip Load was beforehand. To compare, someone at 30% Equip Load would have it lowered to 26.1%, someone at 70% Equip Load would have it lowered to 60.9%, and someone at 100% Equip Load would have it lowered to 87%. 
This spell can only be cast if the wielded right-hand weapon can be buffed by spells, though the Body Buff can still be taken advantage of by keeping a light, buffable weapon such as a Dagger or Caestus in an extra weapon slot. 
Lightning damage is fairly rare outside of Leyndell, Royal Capital and Crumbling Farum Azula, making the downside of the Body Buff often irrelevant unless fighting other players. 
The Weapon Buff portion is equally as strong as Electrify Armament. 
Outmatched by Lightning Grease and Skill: Lightning Slash below 114 Incantation Scaling and by Dragonbolt Grease below 160 Incantation Scaling. 
Though they cast much quicker and last for a shorter duration, Drawstring Lightning Grease is stronger below 147 Incantation Scaling while Drawstring Dragonbolt Grease is stronger below 180 Incantation Scaling. 
Lightning Slash has the advantage of also being usable for weapons with the otherwise unbuffable (not counting other skills) Lightning and Sacred Affinity weapons.

name: Wakizashi
description: The Wakizashi is a dagger found in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body:
Found on a corpse inside a locked cell in Gaol Cave, located in Caelid. The cave requires one Stonesword Key to access. 

From the lever that unlocks all the cages it can be found by taking a right then a left, and then it's one of three items in the second cage on the left.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Overall is slightly stronger on Dexterity-scaling affinities. 
Counts as a Katana for the purpose of dual wielding and as such cannot be paired with another dagger except for a second copy of itself. 
Its attacks deal 15-28% more damage when dual wielded with a Katana in the right-hand slot and dual wield attacks cost 20% less Stamina, at the cost of bad reach. 
Useful for granting access to the skill Parry when dual wielding Katanas. 
Also uses the Katana dual wield moveset when wielded alongside another Wakizashi, though this will not cause the damage increase for the Wakizashi in the left-hand slot. 
Consistently the strongest dagger damage-wise for all affinities despite its often only average scaling, in large part due to its high base damage. However, it effectively lacks access to the powerful Daggers dual wield moveset and the one for Katanas is much slower and as such will have much worse status build-up. 
The innate Blood Loss build-up pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult). 
While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.

sections.heading: Upgrade Information
sections.body:
Upgraded with regular Smithing Stones.
Can have its Affinity and Skill changed.
All non-physical Affinities lower all types of guarded damage negation by 5%, except for the associated element where the damage negation increases by 25% and another element also increases by 15%.
Magic negation receives the secondary 15% negation bonus on Sacred and Cold affinities, Fire negation gets the increase on Lightning affinity, Lightning negation gets the increase on Fire and Flame Art affinities, and Holy negation gets the increase on Magic affinity.
The upper number in the Atk column denotes Physical base damage while the lower, colored number in the Atk column denotes elemental base damage: red for Fire damage, yellow for Lightning damage, orange for Holy damage, and cyan for Magic damage. 
See the Weapon Scaling page for what the scaling values mean.

name: War Against the Giants
image: Mountaintops of the Giants Giant Corpse - MENU Load 00008.png
description: The War against the Giants, refers to the conflict in the Lands Between between the forces of Leyndell and the Fire Giants.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Long ago, the red-haired Fire Giants had made the northern Mountaintops their lands, after chasing away the ice dragons who were the former lords of the region. The Giants worshiped the God of Fire, whose one-eyed visage manifested upon their chests, and continued to borrow its power and practice smithing as a form of divine ritual, and even the Trolls, their descendants, wielded hammers as ceremonial tools for smithing, crafted with the same pattern of the fell god's eye.

Meanwhile, Queen Marika the Eternal, the Empyrean that become the vessel of the Elden Ring, had planted the Golden Seed that would become the Erdtree under the guidance of the Two Fingers and had begun to establish her reign over the Lands Between. The Flame of Ruin posed a threat to the burgeoning Erdtree, as it was capable of burning it, and thus needed to be neutralized for her Order to truly start. And so, Queen Marika and her consort Godfrey, First Elden Lord, marched upon the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.body:
The War against the Giants, was led by Godfrey himself. When the king of the battlefield and his warriors left the Altus plateau and reached into the Mountaintops they joined forces with the Knights of Zamor, who had been historical and mortal enemies of the Fire Giants, having challenged them many times in the past thanks to the power of their ice storms. 

From the town of Zamor the allied forces marched through the Mountaintops, carving winding paths to reach the higher, western summit on the other side of the cliff walls.. The fighting continued, with the Giants using their bellowing roars to trigger avalanches and whip up storms of flame, and facing a Fire Giant was seen as a horror, thanks to their dreadful visages and the power of the flames they wielded. 

Enormous, crushing weapons were deployed to counter their onslaught, and the heroes of the Erdtree strengthened their arms using semi-vitrified smithing stones mined in the cold, northern regions. The priest of the Erdtree would devise a fire incantation to protect the warriors of Godfrey from the Giants' flame. However this defense was created through that same fire, thus requiring for priests of the Erdtree to have faith in the Fell God they were fighting 

After traversing the great lake of the Mountaintops, now closer the the Forge of the Giants, Queen Marika issued a proclamation to Godfrey and his warriors, commanding them to put the Giants to the sword and confine their flame, so that the Age of the Erdtree could begin. 

At some point, the Trolls, the descendants of the Giants, betrayed their ancestors and switched sides to fight on behalf of the Erdtree and were furnished with gilded swords to commemorate their fealty.

Despite the initial odds, the champions of the Erdtree prevailed over the Fire Giants that were massacred in the fields before their Forge, leaving the battlefield littered with their impaled corpses. Queen Marika herself supposedly fought against the one-eyed fell god, and she was believed to have been slain them.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.body:
Although the Giants had been defeated, it became apparent that the Flame of Ruin would never die and the fell god was still lurking within the last Fire Giant.. Seeing this, Queen Marika marked the lone surviving Fire Giant with a curse, compelling him to tend to the flame for eternity. 

With the flame sealed away, the Fire Monks and Flame Guardians were appointed to watch over its smoldering remains.. Wearing armor emblazoning with a depictions of the fell god of the Giants to imprint the idea of taboo through fear these priest warriors also continued to make use of Giants' Flame Incantations that required faith in it through Giant's Seal depicting the god of the Giants. The Fire Prelates kept the Fire Giant incantations hidden and the Chief Guardian Arghanthy kept the legendary Flame of the Fell God incantation drawing directly from power of the fell god a secret After many years of watch, the Fire Monks would later succumb to the allure of the flame,

The Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave was built to give Erdtree Burial to the champions that fought in the war, even becoming the resting place of dozens of Trolls that fought alongside the Erdtree's warriors.

The knights of Zamor earned great renown for their actions during the war and were hailed as heroes. Some of them would leave from their ancestral home to continue to fight under the Erdtree, their devotion showing even centuries later as some of them would defend the Hero's Graves of the War against the Giants and the Ancient Dragons The Trolls, despite their own efforts in the war, did not receive such recognition and were instead merely integrated into the army as war beasts and would end up used as menial labor, working in mines, or dragging great coffin carriages when their intelligence degraded. 

The end of the war marked the dawn of the Erdtree's era, presided over by Queen Marika and Godfrey. The Erdtree itself would go on to become the embodiment of Order and its blessed sap dripping from its boughs would start an Age of Plenty.

Although the flame of ruin was sealed, the burning of the Erdtree was considered to be the first cardinal sin. Prophets would occasionally glimpse the flame of ruin in their faith, envisioning the ruin that it would bring. Those who had such visions would be banished, forced to wear shackles around their necks to warn passersby against listening to them.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
The War against the Giants could be the conflict in which Commander Niall offered his leg in exchange of the lives of his defeated soldiers and his would be Banished Knight would lose their lands. 
For the armies of Godfrey to reach the lands of the Fire Giants they would first need to cross the region controlled by Castle Sol.
The path between Leyndell and the Grand Lift of Rold, the Ancient Snow Valley Ruins, before the Stargazers' Ruins, and on the path between Castle Sol and the First Church of Marika is littered with Banished Knights' weapons.
The path between Castle Sol and the frozen lake is covered by graves, in the greatest concentration found through the Lands Between.
The Fire Giants and the knights of Castle Sol could have been allies by virtue of their conflict against ice dragons.
Six Giant Skeletons are buried among those that fell close to Castle Sol.
The Troll Theodorix became a hunter of dragons on the Mountaintops even after his kind's alliance with the Erdtree and the end of the war.
The Briars of Sin were used to impale the corpses of the Fire Giants.
Those who would become the Black Knights and Fire Knights may have participated in the War Against the Giants, as both drop [[Smithing Stone 7|Smithing Stone [7]]].

name: War Counselor Iji
description: War Counselor Iji, also known as Smithing Master Iji, is a character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
War Counselor Iji is a wise and kind-hearted Troll who smithed weapons for the Carian royal family and their enchanted knights. He has known Ranni and Blaidd since they were children, and they would let him join in when they played. Along with Blaidd, he swore allegiance to Ranni when she renounced her flesh and chose the dark path of the Empyrean. 

He made weapons for Radahn during the Shattering but now counsels and aids Ranni the Witch in her opposition to the Greater Will.

Game events:
Iji maintains a smithing post near the Kingsrealm Ruins and warns the player to beware Caria Manor. If the played joins Ranni's followers, Iji welcomes them with open arms.

Jerren recalls that the weapons Iji smithed were blunt, yet did not decay when faced with Scarlet Rot. Jerren may also offer a vital clue regarding Ranni's fate, which helps Iji to come to the realisation that General Radahn must be killed in order to release the stars and Ranni's own fate.

Iji is also shown to care for Blaidd, however he also harbours some reservations. Fearing that, as her sworn shadow, Blaidd will go mad and become a curse for Ranni for resisting the Two Fingers, Iji imprisons Blaidd in the Forlorn Hound Evergaol. Later, after Blaidd breaks free of his imprisonment and gives his life in defence of Ranni, Iji admits that he misjudged Blaidd's loyalty, and senses that he will soon join Blaidd in death. Later, he can be found dead, his body ablaze with black flame, with the corpses of Black Knife Assassins nearby.

|I am Iji. A blacksmith who once served the Carian royals…
|An old codger who refuses to retire his rusty hammer.
|So, here I am, still quietly plying my trade, on this spot.
|Perhaps you'd like a display? These bones are old, but still able.
!If talked to again
|Well, it's kind of you to speak to me again.
|Then I presume these old bones served their purpose, more or less?
!Generic greeting
|Brave Tarnished. Here to put my old bones to work again?
!"Talk"
|Brave Tarnished. A word of warning, if you please.
|This territory once belonged to the Carian royal family. Their manor lies not far beyond this point.
|When the Raya Lucaria Academy turned on the Carians, the Knights of the Cuckoo descended on this tract.
|After leveling it, they carried on to the manor.
|The Carians were taken off guard, but their strength had not waned, and they repelled the knights' onslaught...
|By conjuring an enchanted snare that remains potent to this day.
|That is why I say, Tarnished. Don't go near the manor.
|Unless you wish to lie with the corpses of the heedless Knights of the Cuckoo.
!"Please take care"
|Oh, watch out, there.
|When I'm absorbed in my smithing, I lose sight of all else.
|If you come too close, I'm apt to cause you harm.
|I am, after all, terribly large compared to you, Tarnished.
|You don't know how hard it is not to break anything while I work.
!Generic greeting
|Something else for you?
!"About advice"
|I've explained the peril.
|Of the enchanted snare that remains at the royal Carian Manor.
|Whatever you do, brave Tarnished, stay away from that deathtrap.
!"Blaidd sent me"
|Blaidd actually did that, did he?
|Quite a rare occurrence, for such a guarded soul as he.
|Perhaps he sensed something unusual about you.
|At any rate, if you're friendly with Blaidd,
|I've something else that might suit you.
!Ranni's Rise (if previously met)
|Oh, so you were the one. Lady Ranni has explained everything.
|Again, I am Iji.
|The Carian royal family's dedicated blacksmith, and Lady Ranni's war counsellor.
|I am told that you are searching for Nokron with Blaidd.
|I will give you whatever guidance I can. And pray, for your success.
!Ranni's Rise (if warned about Caria Manor)
|My apologies for the misleading words of warning.
|I never imagined that an audience, let alone service to Lady Ranni was in your fate.
|I, for one, should have seen it, but I did not.
|Do forgive me, my fellow.
|Let us give all that we can of ourselves.
|Together, for Lady Ranni.
!If talked to again
|Let us give all that we can of ourselves.
|Together, for Lady Ranni.
!Ranni's Rise (if not previously met)
|Oh, then you must be the one. Lady Ranni has explained everything.
|The pleasure is mine. I am Iji.
!Ranni's Rise (if Radahn has already been defeated)
|Oh, so you were the one. Lady Ranni has explained everything.
|You've defeated General Radahn, unlocking the stars.
|A grand reward, justly procured by any measure.
|Again, I am Iji.
|The Carian royal family's dedicated blacksmith, and Lady Ranni's war counsellor.
|I welcome one of your calibre. A fellow champion in service of Lady Ranni.
!"About Nokron"
|I take it you've heard of the Eternal City of Nokstella?
|Well, it has a twin, known as Nokron. The other Eternal City.
|After years of expeditions, we've determined the location of Nokron.
|By going underground through the well in the Mistwood of Limgrave, you can see Nokron up above.
|Only, we've failed to find a path leading to the city.
|Blaidd's made a good go of it, but I'm afraid this has him quite stumped.
|To be honest, I'm not sure where to go from here...
!"About Blaidd"
|Blaidd is Lady Ranni's stepbrother.
|Ranni's mother, Queen Rennala, approved of him, and they played like siblings from childhood.
|They were always happy to have me tag along, as well.
|When Lady Ranni renounced her flesh, and chose the dark path of the Empyrean,
|Blaidd and I swore allegiance as vassals,
|but none of us will ever forget our earliest days together.
|Promise to look after Blaidd for me, will you?
|The man is honest to a fault. But fortunately, now he has you.
!"About Jerren"
|Jerren. Now, that's a name I haven't heard for a while.
|Before taking up the banner of General Radahn, he was a guest of the Carian royal family.
|An expert swordsman, to be sure, but ever the eccentric.
|No surprise he'd get wrapped up in some festival.
|Oh, no, wait...
|How did I not see it before!
|I ought to retire as war counsellor for such a gross oversight!
|Let me explain. The fate of the Carian royal family is guided by the stars.
|As is the fate of Lady Ranni, first heir in the Carian royal line.
|But General Radahn is the conqueror of the stars.
|Who stood up to the swirling constellations, halting their movement in a smashing victory.
|And so, if General Radahn were defeated, the stars would once again resume their movement.
|As would Lady Ranni's destiny.
|Perhaps, even, revealing the elusive path. That leads to Nokron.
!"Go to the festival grounds"
|Go with Blaidd to the festival grounds.
|Should General Radahn be defeated, the stars would once again resume their movement.
|Perhaps revealing the elusive path to Nokron.
!After defeating Radahn
|Ah, you've finally come. Blaidd told me everything.
|You've defeated General Radahn, unlocking the stars.
|The General was blighted by scarlet rot and driven to madness, but not long ago he was hailed as the mightiest demigod of them all.
|There is no parallel to your achievement. Nor to Lady Ranni's acute judgement of character.
|Thanks to you, Lady Ranni's fate once again stirs, and the path to Nokron has opened.
|Descend underground where the fallen star struck Limgrave.
|And make it yours. The precious treasure of Nokron.
!"Talk" (after defeating Radahn)
|Oh, Blaidd wanted me to tell you.
|Not to bother waiting for him, and head straight to Nokron.
|Blaidd has been given an important task.
|Apparently, a matter of great urgency.
!"About Blaidd"
|You need not await Blaidd.
|Descend underground where the fallen star struck Limgrave.
|And make it yours. The precious treasure of Nokron.
|So that Lady Ranni may tread the dark path of the Empyrean.
!"Talk" (if Radahn was defeated before entering Ranni's service)
|Thanks to you, Lady Ranni's fate once again stirs, and the path to Nokron has opened.
|Descend underground where the fallen star struck Limgrave.
|And make it yours. The precious treasure of Nokron.
|So that Lady Ranni may tread the dark path of the Empyrean.
!Generic greeting
|Well, my fellow. How may I serve you?
|As war counsellor, or as blacksmith?
!Generic greeting
|Greetings, my fellow. How can I help?
|Generic greeting
|Something else for you?
!"About Jerren" (if not previously talked to about Jerren before the Radahn Festival)
|Jerren. Now, that's a name I haven't heard for a while.
|Before taking up the banner of General Radahn, he was a guest of the Carian royal family.
|An expert swordsman, to be sure, but ever the eccentric.
|It's funny how things happen.
|Jerren and I parted ways long, long ago, yet here he is, playing his part in Lady Ranni's fate.
|I'm afraid I never saw it coming. And I thought myself a capable war counsellor...
!"About Jerren" (after Radahn Festival)
|Now the festival is over, and General Radahn is defeated...
|Jerren's duties are finally fulfilled.
|Though we served different masters, I could see he was truly adept in his role.
|Now the time has come to remind him of an old promise made.
|With the stars of fate set into motion, a certain sorceress is dispossessed of her immortality...
|Finally, we can be rid of a longstanding Carian weed...
!"Why is Blaidd in the evergaol?"
|I presume you've spoken with Blaidd?
|Very well. There is something you should know.
|The Two Fingers gave Blaidd to Lady Ranni, as a faithful follower. Her very shadow, incapable of treachery.
|But if Lady Ranni, as an Empyrean, resists being an instrument of the Two Fingers,
|the shadow will go mad, transforming from a follower into a horrid curse.
|But such is his destiny. In such matters, Blaidd's own thoughts hold no weight.
|It pains me so, but he must be neutralised. For Lady Ranni's sake.
!"About Blaidd" (after killing Blaidd at Ranni's Rise)
|Unthinkable, how could Blaidd...
|How did he break free from his cell?
|No, more importantly...
|Blaidd became a curse that plagued Lady Ranni, yet even in madness, gave himself to her.
|I've made a grave misjudgment. And I thought myself a capable war counsellor...
|I'll catch up with you soon enough, Blaidd.
|When I do, I only hope you'll accept my apology.
!After giving Ranni the Fingerslayer Blade
|Oh, there you are. Good of you to drop by.
|Have you heard? Lady Ranni has departed on her journey.
|Along the dark path of the Empyrean, from Renna's Rise, as she calls it.
|It would not have been possible without you.
|As Lady Ranni's war counsellor, and moreover, her childhood warden, I express my deepest gratitude.
|You, and only you, were Lady Ranni's true champion.
!"Talk"
|My purpose is nearing its end.
|I've served Lady Ranni for as long as I can remember...
|It has been a long and wondrous journey.
|Now Lady Ranni is in your hands.
|I pray that you serve her well, unto the very end.
!If talked to again
|Lady Ranni has departed on her journey.
|Along the dark path of the Empyrean, from Renna's Rise, as she calls it.
|Now Lady Ranni is in your hands.
|I pray that you serve her well, unto the very end.
!If attacked (before entering Ranni's service)
|Ngh!
|Enough of that, Tarnished.
|There is no fight without a foe.
!If attacked until he disappears (before entering Ranni's service)
|If that's the cloth you're cut from,
|don't ever show your face again.
|Not to me. And not to my liege.
!If attacked (after entering Ranni's service)
|Agh.
|Cease this treachery at once.
|Lady Ranni will be devastated.
!If attacked until he disappears (after entering Ranni's service)
|This is a true shame.
|Don't ever show your face again.
|Not to me. And not to my liege.

|本当に素晴らしい、長き旅でした

|貴公、ラニ様をよろしくお願いしますぞ
|どうか最後まで、彼女に仕えてくだされ
!If attacked (before entering Ranni's service)
|ぐっ
|やめなされ、褪せ人の方
|匹夫の勇、何の意味もないことです
!If attacked until he disappears (before entering Ranni's service)
|…くだらぬ輩だ
|もう二度と、会うことはありませんな
|私にも、我が主にも
!If attacked (after entering Ranni's service)
|ぐっ

|裏切りなど、ラニ様が悲しまれる
!If attacked until he disappears (after entering Ranni's service)
|…残念です、貴公
|もう二度と、会うことはありませんな
|私にも、我が主にも

name: War of the Ancient Dragons
description: The War of the Ancient Dragons, refers to the conflict in the Lands Between between the forces of Leyndell and the Ancient Dragons.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
During the reign of Queen Marika the Eternal and Godfrey, the first Elden Lord, at some point after the end of the Age of Plenty the royal capital of Leyndell was attacked by Ancient Dragon Gransax. 

The immense dragon wielding a giant golden spear managed to fell the walls of Leyndell for the first time in recorded history and wreck havoc upon the city until it was finally defeated, his massive corpse left lying between the Fortified Manor and the lower city. Gransax's assault marked the beginning of the War against the Ancient Dragons. 

For the battles to come, the priests of the Erdtree would develop incantations to protect the knights of Leyndell against the lightning of the dragons.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.body:
The dragon's attack on the capital caused some among the Tree Sentinels, the guardians of the Erdtree, to have an epiphany; According to them, the only way to protect the Erdtree was to become dragons themselves. Thus, some of the Sentinels began to emulate the Ancient Dragons in order to provide proper protection for the Erdtree against the new threat. They adorned their armor with dragon imagery and wielding weapons and shields imbued with red lightning, crafted whittling from the claws of great dragon that fell on their city. From then on, these grotesque Tree Sentinels are referred to as Draconic Tree Sentinels. 

The last battle of the war happened in the Altus Plateau, outside the outer walls of Leyndell. Godwyn the Golden, the son of Queen Marika and Lord Godfrey, engaged in conflict against Ancient Dragon Fortissax, who had stood out during the war for its usage of twin red lightning stakes and was known as the "mightiest boulderstone".

Fighting with courage, Godwyn triumphed over Fortissax before eventually befriending him and sparing his life. This event marked the end of the war against the Ancient Dragons and their integration into the Golden Order.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.body:
Through his friendship with Fortissax, Godwyn learned to channel golden lightning. and their bond gave rise to the Ancient Dragon Cult in Leyndell. The dragon cult worshiped the ancient dragons and their incantations channeled lightning instead of the power of the Erdtree, but these practices were sanctioned by the Golden Order, as lightning and the Gravel Stones of the dragons were imbued with gold. 

The cultists devotedly worshipped the Ancient Dragons and prayed for their golden lightning incantations thus adding another great power to Leyndell's arsenal, although the red-hued incantations remained a secret of Farum Azula, as its prayerbooks never reached the rest of the Lands Between.

Ancient Dragon Lansseax, the sister of Fortissax, assumed a human form and became the priestess for the Dragon Cult of Leyndell to interact with its knights. Only those loved by the dragons could receive the blessing of their lightning and survive their lightning, with Vyke the Dragonspear being the most favored by Lansseax and able to imbue his body even with red lightning.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
It is possible that during the war, battles between Leyndell forces and Dragons happened even in Crumbling Farum Azula.
The Golden Lightning Fortification incantation used during the war is obtained from a scarab rolling the ashes left on the ruined city
Golden Runes from 9 to 12, those of people born at the foot of the Erdtree and those of people that first served it, can be found on the ruined city.
Two Crucible Knights can still be found fighting Beastmen in the ruined city.
It is possible that, in the last battle of the war, Demigods or nobles closely affiliated with the Golden Lineage fought and died.
The Sainted Hero's Grave, built close to the site of the last battle, implies that champions of holy status were buried in the catacomb.
The banners found on the Sainted Hero's Grave display the symbol of the Golden Lineage.
Godwyn was the first Demigod to die in "recorded history".

Note that while the first heavy attack in the chain will always hit twice, charged or not, the second one will only hit twice if charged, and once if not.

name: Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia
description: The Weapon-Bequeathed Harmonia, also known as the Balancers and Salvation's Standard-Bearers, are one of the Nightlord bosses in, included in the expansion.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.body:
The Balancers are pallid maidens wielding victorious weapons. Their armor resembles white flowers. Their faces are similar to Trina's and have white clothes as wings.

However, Everdark Harmonia is drenched in blood. Their clothes are red rather than white, while the wings are very rose-like and bloody. In their final form they emerge as a giant worm-like creature drenched in blood. The worm has the corpses of balancers all over its body, with one in the middle of its face that has a spear.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Young Harmonia fled into the forest to seek help when ruthless marauders terrorized her small farming settlement. The village girl prayed to a statue of a guardian deity with a weapon raised overhead, and was granted great power. By the end, the village was steeped in red and settled in silence. Harmonia, drenched in blood, stood with a vacant stare and a heroic weapon in her grip.

She became the Balancers, seven white-winged valkyries of the heavens, sent to purify chaos and restore balance to the world.

+0% indicates that a boss is neutral to that damage type.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.body:
The Sleep status effect is Harmonia's greatest weakness. It is easily inflicted on the valkyries, causing them to fall into a deep slumber that lasts for an extended duration, comparable to that of Godskins. This serves as a means to control their numbers, tipping the scales. Sleeping Balancers are also vulnerable to Critical Attacks.
Parrying is a valid strategy for Wylder against Harmonia because most of her attacks can be Parried.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Internal names.
Valkyries: AngelsDaughters.
Harmonia's Tree Spirit form (ID: 4641) is a modified Ulcerated Tree Spirit (ID: 4640).
When resurrected, the Harmonia are held up by their weapons in a manner akin to puppets.
Harmonia is fully modeled beneath their armor. Their sleeping, cherubic faces strongly resemble St. Trina's, whose eyelids also appear to be bruised.
Salvation Harmonia's cranial cavity houses a dark seed surrounded by six glowing sprouts—one for each of her clones—during Phase 3. It blossoms into a magnificently red bloodflower during Phase 4, transforming Harmonia into a Tree Spirit in full bloom.
Miranda and Malenia, Goddess of Rot also share Harmonia's ability to duplicate and bloom.
Harmonia's name and botanical nature tacitly imply a Numen Shaman lineage: "The flesh of shamans was said to meld harmoniously with others."
They may be connected to the Formless Mother, since the Lord of Blood is one of her Night 2 bosses. Her Standard-Bearer armor is identical to Varré's Bouquet.
Their screech attack uses the same sound as the Grafted Scion.
Salvation Harmonia's grand bloodflower bloom unfurls in the divine "eight around one" pattern.

Localization:
In Japanese, their title is written as 英雄武器の娘たち, which roughly translates to "Daughters/Girls of Heroic Weapons". The term used for them as a group coincides with their young faces.
In Brazilian Portuguese, their boss name is rendered Harmonia, Arma Legada, roughly meaning "Legacy Weapon Harmonia". Here, the title makes it seem that the name refers to the weapons and not the valkyries.

moveset: | Purifying Light || Channels light through the spear, sending a linear ground wave that sprouts erupting spears. Dodge or strafe sideways to exit the line and punish recovery.
| Circle of Purification || Casts an outward-expanding ring of spears. Sprint outward, then dodge toward the Balancer as the ring erupts for a safe punish.
| Spear Swipe || Teleports, leaps, and performs a horizontal landing swipe. Roll toward the leap and counter once or twice.
| Spear Thrust || Rushes forward with a straight thrust, sometimes twice. Side-roll and circle behind during recovery.
| Double Spear Swipe || Executes two wide horizontal swipes. Roll toward the first to slip behind, or roll back to disengage.
| Purity of Lightning (Phase 2) || Floats with a glowing left hand, then dives for a long-range lightning grab that impales on hit. Roll toward the dive to evade.

| Harmonious Smite (Phase 2) || Sequential individual dives leaving delayed explosive trails, followed by a coordinated dive and a spear barrage from above. Sprint out of trails and dodge early to avoid explosions.
| Dancing Spear (Phase 2) || Gliding multi-slash sequence followed by airborne crescent projectiles. Out-run the first flurry; roll toward incoming projectiles.
| Smite (Phase 2) || Leader signals synchronized dives that leave explosive trails, followed by Purity of Lightning. Reposition early and roll through the final grab.
| Purifying Blast (Phase 2) || Leader vanishes; a light ray marks an impending explosion. Sprint from the ray or roll through it to counter safely.
| Absolution (Phase 2) || Teleports Balancers, kneels, and releases four expanding spear-waves while gaining attack buffs. Time forward rolls into each wave.
| Pouncing Combo (Phase 2) || Purifying Light → airborne retreat → pounce and thrust-flurry with diving finisher. Side-roll the Light, widen distance, and dodge the pounce and final hit.
| Pulverizing Slams (Phase 2) || Repeated empowered spear-slams, upward slash, and a final explosive fissure. Roll the opener, stay behind until the slash, then dodge the fissure.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Produces a spiraling stream of fire with a Fire Attack Power equal to 96% of Incantation Scaling. It can hit up to 4 times and pierces foes (though not Guarded Damage Negation). 

Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 121% of Incantation Scaling and doubles its range.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 19 FP per cast.
Costs 26 Stamina per cast. Charging increases the cost to 34 points. 
Costs 1 Memory Slot to equip.
Deals 1.85 Stance damage per hit (7.4 if all hits land). Charging increases Stance damage to 2.8 per hit (11.2 if all hits land). 
The spell can pierce through multiple enemies but is blocked by walls and other solid obstacles.
If it hits a Guarding foe the damage will be lowered by Guarded Damage Negation but will still hit enemies behind the first one. 

Boosting:

Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 26%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 45%.

Strategies:
Effective for hitting multiple enemies due to its piercing effect.
Large or immobile enemies are much easier to hit multiple times, as they are much more unlikely to move out of the way of the fire stream. 
Deals very low Stamina damage to Guarding enemies, as it will only deal 52 Stamina damage to an enemy Guarding with a 50 Guard Boost shield and all 4 hits land.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Update 1.07: Reduced FP consumption. Increased stamina attack power against guarding enemies. Increased ability to stagger enemies.
FP cost was reduced from 21 to 19. 
Stamina Attack Power per hit was increased from 15 to 20 for the uncharged version, and from 20 to 26 for the charged version. 
Against players the Stamina Attack Power per hit was increased from 15 to 25 for the uncharged version, and from 20 to 32 for the charged version. 
Stance damage per hit was increased from 1 to 1.85 for the uncharged version, and from 1.85 to 2.8 for the charged version. 
Update 1.04: Increased damage, decreased recovery time. 
The Attack Power of the uncharged version was increased from 91% of Incantation Scaling to 96% of the same, and from 106% of Incantation Scaling to 121% of the same for the charged version.

Limgrave (The First Step)

As he moves at the entrance of the Rose Church after speaking with Enia, talk to him, selecting They didn't seem right, and exhaust his dialogues to receive Festering Bloody Finger x5.

Interact with the invasion sign of Magnus the Beast Claw, found at the Writheblood Ruins south-west of the Site of Grace, and either defeat him or simply invade him three times. Invading actual players with the Festering Bloody Fingers three times is also enough to progress Varré's questline.

Killing Irina of Morne or, if already deceased, Lightseeker Hyetta at any of their locations.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body: When mixed into the Flask of Wondrous Physick and used, greatly increases the user's equip load by 450% for 3 minutes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
A 450% increase in equip load is effectively the same as multiplying maximum equip load with 5.5. 
Potentially very useful in that it let's the Tarnished combine their heaviest armor with their heaviest armaments while still keeping at a medium load, but also carries the danger of getting stuck in Heavy Load - or worse, Overloaded - should it run out at an inopportune moment.
Even with the Prophet Origin's low Endurance of 8 this will boost its maximum equip load from 45 to 247.5, and therefore increase the thresholds for its light and medium loads from 13.5 and 31.5 to 74.25 and 173.25. This makes it possible to carry the heavy Bull-Goat Set and its 63 weight while still keeping a light load and its much longer rolls, if not with a lot of weight to spare. 
Be wary that unless equip load is kept under 15.6% of the maximum while under the effect of this tear, its effect expiring will send the user straight into heavy load. Additionally, being above 22.2% of maximum equipment load while under the tear's effect leads to being overloaded when it ends.

name: Winged Sword Insignia
description: Winged Sword Insignia is a talisman in.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.body: Obtained from Stillwater Cave in southern Liurnia of the Lakes, by defeating the Cleanrot Knight boss.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Increases attack power for every 3 hits landed, with the bonus increasing further for every 3 hits after that for an overall bonus of 3%/5%/10%. Bonus decreases by 1 "tier" every 1.5 seconds that pass without getting a point. 

Light attacks count as 1 hit towards this buff and heavy attacks count as 2 hit towards it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Mainly works for melee weapons, with only certain Sorceries (Adula's Moonblade, Gavel of Haima, Carian Greatsword, Carian Piercer, and Carian Slicer) and certain Incantations (Aspects of the Crucible: Tail, Aspects of the Crucible: Horns, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive). 
These spells counts as a heavy attack, i.e. they count as 2 hits if they land. 
For spells with a melee component and a ranged component, progress is only granted if the melee component hits. These spells are Adula's Moonblade, Black Blade, and Lansseax's Glaive. 
For Skills it only works if they can hit using the weapon, such as with Skill: Sword Dance, Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade, or the melee part of Skill: Blood Blade. Melee range skills that nonetheless don't directly hit with the weapon, such as Skill: Black Flame Tornado don't count. 
Can be worn together with the Millicent's Prosthesis to stack the effect, but not with the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia. 
Light or heavy attacks that hit several times per input counts as hits each time they hit an enemy. 
An example of this is the unique heavy attack shared by the Black Knife, Blade of Calling, and Erdsteel Dagger, which hits twice and therefore can count as either 2 or 4 hits depending if it manages to hit once or twice. 
This also counts for some skills that use heavy attacks and can hit several times, such as the heavy attack follow-up to the Stamp (Sweep) skill and the altered heavy attacks granted by the Barbaric Roar skill.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body: At some point between an unknown Patch and Patch 1.03.3, this talisman was apparently bugged, with the buff that is applied to attack power both increasing and decreasing with successive attacks. That is, in some scenarios, performing an additional attack within a sequence would cause attack power to decrease, rather than increase. This could be observed when using the Dagger and Short Sword weapons. This effect could be observed for the Rotten Winged Sword Insignia as well.

name: Witch of the Wheel
image: ERN Character Witch of the Wheel (1.1).png
description: The is a character in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
The Witch of the Wheel was a practitioner of ancient magic who once dwelled in the Deep Woods beyond the Lands Between. Known for her cunning and deceit, she relied upon guile as both weapon and shield. She was an old companion of the Recluse, sharing in the same arts and knowledge, and in time became the nurse of the Infant summoned by her counterpart. The newborn being devoured without end, and the Witch was tasked with appeasing its insatiable hunger.

During a later clash of armies, the two witches unleashed the Infant as a weapon. The monstrous creature overran the enemy but soon turned upon its summoners. The Recluse failed to offer comfort or embrace to the frightened child, and the Witch of the Wheel was slain in the chaos. Her shadow was shorn away and her essence subsumed, leaving behind a lifeless body.

The Witch of the Wheel was later restored to life at the Roundtable Hold through the power of the Nightlord. In this state, she attacked the Iron Menial and locked him in the crypt, taking his likeness to move freely within the Hold. Her activities drew the suspicion of the Recluse, who eventually detected the Witch’s magic within the Vestige of Night. The Witch's old companion sought her out to atone for her death.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body:
The Witch of the Wheel appears in the Realm of Remembrance at the Shrouded Roundtable Hold during the third chapter of Recluse's Remembrance Quest. She has disguised herself as the Iron Menial, and is polishing a sword at the Sparring Grounds. Attack and slay the puppet, prompting her to mimic the Recluse's appearance.

She appears again after defeating Heolstor the Nightlord. Visit the bed area where the Vestige of Night was in the ashen Roundtable Hold and embrace the crying Infant. Return to the bed area after the ending. The Witch of the Wheel thanks the Recluse for choosing to love their infant Night.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Wears the Recluse's Remembrance Garb
The Witch of the Wheel's magic binds the Night Aspect.

If the player sided with Sorceress Sellen, then the Witch's Glintstone Crown will be on the floor beside her following her transformation.
If the player sided with Witch-Hunter Jerren, then Sorceress Sellen drops the crown upon defeat.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Slot: Head
Sell value: 500 runes
Part of the Witch's Set, which also includes the Raya Lucarian Robe, Sorcerer Manchettes, and Sorcerer Leggings.
Worn by Sorceress Sellen at Waypoint Ruins and Witchbane Ruins.
The Witch's Glintstone Crown appears to be based on Sorceress Sellen's face, which cannot be viewed during normal gameplay. A portrait of Sellen can be found in the Schoolhouse Classroom at the Academy of Raya Lucaria.
It is the only glintstone crown whose face is feminine, featuring neither glintstone eyes nor a gaping mouth.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Armor ID: 834000
Short description: "Stone mask of a Green Glintstone Sage"

The variant with the large green crystal (ID: 834100), worn by Sorceress Sellen's second body, is unobtainable. Although it features an unbroken glintstone, its item description mentions a shattered one: " Stone mask of a Green Glintstone Sage. This mask is broken, its glintstone fractured." (Short description: "Broken stone mask with fractured Glintstone".)
Patch 1.07 increased the Poise from 3 to 6.

description: Wrath from Afar is an incantation spell in. It is one of the Erdtree Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Loot: Shadow Keep

sections.heading: Effects
sections.body:
Throws out a vertical ring of light with Holy Attack Power equal to 100% of Incantation Scaling and a 2 meter effect radius on impact.
Charging the spell increases the Attack Power to 120% of Incantation Scaling and the radius to 3 meters.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 18 FP per cast.
Costs 24 Stamina per cast. Charging the spell does not increase the cost.

Sends human-sized enemies flying if they are hit.

Boosting:
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 20%, wearing the talisman increases charged Attack Power by a total of 38%.

variant.effect: Fires a golden shockwave that knocks back foes

sections.heading: Acquisition

Loot: Altus Plateau
Found in a treasure chest in the cellar of Woodfolk Ruins. The cellar is located in a cluster of ruins in the southeasternmost quarter of the forest.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.body:
Quickly lets loose a golden shockwave, with Holy Attack Power equal to 350% of Incantation Scaling and affects enemies within a 4-meter radius of the caster.

Charging the spell increases Attack Power to 420% of Incantation Scaling and the attack radius to 5 meters.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.body:
Costs 44 points of Stamina to cast. Charging the spell increases the cost to 57 points of Stamina.
Deals 12 Stance damage when not charged and 17 Stance damage when charged.
Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 20%, wearing the talisman increases charged Attack Power by a total of 38%.
Can be cast while riding Torrent.
Sends human-sized enemies flying if they are hit, even when the incantation isn't charged.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.body:
Patch 1.07 increased stamina attack power against guarded enemies.
This increased the Stamina damage against guarding enemies from 221 to 240 for the uncharged version and from 251 to 290 for the charged version.
This patch also split the Stamina damage against guarding enemy players, increasing it to 300 for the uncharged version and to 362 for the charged version.

name: Yuri
description: Yuri was a character mentioned in.

sections.heading: Background
sections.body:
Yuri, the treasured son of a renowned sorcerer, died at a young age and was laid to rest in the quiet cemetery beside the Cathedral of Manus Metyr. Despite his passing, his grief-stricken father, Count Ymir, continued to speak of him as though he still ran about the church grounds. Ymir believed a rotten, tangled mass haunted Yuri’s dreams, and often visited his grave to soothe the nightmares. 

Consumed by loss, Count Ymir sought Yuri’s rebirth, attempting to replicate the power of Metyr, Mother of Fingers. Should Ymir become a Mother of Fingers, he ultimately fails in his efforts to restore Yuri’s life.

sections.heading: Location
sections.body: Yuri's grave is found in the small graveyard attached to the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, assemble via the cathedral entrance near Jolán, Swordhand of Night.

sections.heading: Notes
